input: Best place for salads! I go there every time I'm in town for lunch. It's fast and veggies are always fresh.
Help me polish this: Looking for the perfect place to indulge in some refreshing salads? Look no further! This hidden gem is my go-to spot whenever I'm in town for lunch. With its swift service and consistently crisp and flavorful veggies, it never fails to impress.

Help me polish this: On September 26th, 2015, my parents and I embarked on the Oak Alley and Laura Plantation tour. input: We have been here twice for brunch and have enjoyed it immensely. Everything we have tried has been delicious, particularly the grits with scallions and sour cream. But the room is always freezing so be sure to bring a sweater!
Help me polish this: We have had the pleasure of visiting this place for brunch not just once, but twice, and it has truly left us delighted on both occasions. input: Love this place...best hot dogs and chili dogs around...i go here as many times as i can..yum
Help me polish this: I absolutely adore this place! They serve the most mouthwatering hot dogs and chili dogs in town. I find myself visiting as frequently as possible because the food is just irresistible. Every bite is a true delight. Yum!

input: Sweet spot in the Waterline. Came for some live music with friends on Saturday. Very cool. Best local beer in town by far. Seems like the concept is a few notches up from Fig Mountain. Definitely prefer Topa. Even cooler is that you can order incredible food from the Nook Restaurant, and walk two feet into Lama Dog which is part of the Waterline. I love it!!
Help me polish this: I had a great experience at the Sweet Spot in the Waterline this past Saturday when I went with some friends to enjoy some live music. What made it even better was the convenience of being able to order incredible food from the Nook Restaurant and simply walk a few steps into Lama Dog, which is a part of the Waterline. This combination of great music, delicious food, and excellent beer made for an amazing experience. I absolutely love it!

input:
Great customer service! We were a little out of their pick up area but they were very accommodating and came and got our group of 7. When we got there we realized we were billed for 8 instead of 7. I called and he refunded my money for the extra ticket in minutes!

The tour itself was SO much fun! We were laughing and smiling and our tour guide was funny! We saw lots of alligators! From babies swimming in the water to full grown ones! We saw turtles and birds too! Our tour guide had a baby alligator we could hold that he's raising until it's a little bigger since it was a late hatch that would have died because of when it was born. The ride back was fun too because we went fast and the guide did some "tricks" with the boat! I highly recommend this tour!!!
Help me polish this:
Outstanding customer service! Despite being slightly outside their designated pick up area, they gladly accommodated our group of 7 and came to fetch us. Upon arrival, we noticed that we were charged for 8 instead of 7 tickets. However, a quick phone call resulted in the refund of the additional ticket within minutes!

Now, let's talk about the tour itself... It was an absolute blast! We couldn't stop laughing and smiling throughout the entire experience. Our tour guide was incredibly entertaining and kept us captivated with his humor. The abundance of alligators we encountered was extraordinary - from adorable baby alligators frolicking in the water to majestic, fully grown ones. We even had the opportunity to hold a baby alligator that our guide is nurturing until it grows a bit more, as it was born late and wouldn't have survived otherwise. On top of that, we were treated to sightings of turtles and various species of birds. The return journey was just as exciting, as we sped through the water while the guide performed thrilling maneuvers with the boat. I cannot recommend this tour enough! It was an unforgettable experience that exceeded all expectations.

input: Westfall replaced our roof in April. We could not be more pleased with the entire process. Quality roof, excellent communication and excellent follow up. Very happy we chose this company to replace our roof.
Help me polish this: Westfall completed the replacement of our roof in April, and we are truly delighted with the entire experience. input: Good food, reasonably priced, and nice staff. Not ideal for eating in, but since they are going for a fast food approach to vegan food, that makes a lot of sense. I know the buffalo bella is the dish that they push the hardest, but for my money the Cheesesteak is the way to go. And pro-tip: Get the sweet potato fries.
Help me polish this: This place offers delicious food at affordable prices and has a friendly staff. And, as a pro-tip, don't miss out on their mouthwatering sweet potato fries.

input: The ramen is okay, nothing spectacular. Service is okay. Good place for a quick stop but wouldn't go if there were other choices. Been here twice, will continue to go.
Help me polish this: The ramen is decent, but not particularly remarkable. The service is satisfactory. It's a suitable place for a quick bite, but I wouldn't choose it over other options. I've visited twice already and will probably continue to do so.

input: A menu that satisfies everyone's cravings! Clean, trendy, and delicious! I definitely recommend going early (before 9 am) as the wait tends to get longer after 9 am! But honestly, it is soooo worth the wait. You will leave there feeling so incredible satisfied!
Help me polish this: Indulge in a menu that caters to your every craving! Our offerings are not just delicious, but also clean and trendy. input: We stayed at The Saint last year for a girl's trip. The lobby is lovely, they have a cool bar and restaurant that you can't help but to "ohh and ahh" over when you walk in.  All the things I'm accustomed too when I stay at a hotel anywhere...ambiance, a little sexy but not overkill! Everyone is so friendly, etc.  I'm thinking "oh shhhh this is going to be a great weekend!"  I checked in a few hours before my girl arrived because I had a ton of work i needed to do. So I set up my laptop ordered some room service and worked for about 4 hours straight. Left out to buy a bottle and get a mani/pedi.  My girl arrives...its about to be some trouble in NOLA... the two of us and no supervision...we pop out for dinner, come back in giggling as usual and we see it...a HUGH flying roach.  I'm freaked out.  I literally walk right out of the room down to the front desk.  I CANNOT!!!! They tell me they're sending a maintenance worker to handle it.  NOT GOOD ENOUGH! If there's one that's bold enough to show itself, he has other cohorts that prefer to live behind the scenes. They give us another room but tell me they can't do more until 8am.  No the room the move us too also has small spiders and other dead small bugs in the corners of the window. The TV doesn't work and one of the lamps doesn't have bulbs in it! COME ON!  At this point its about 3am and I know I'm not staying here past 8:15am. I dont want to sit my purse let alone my luggage in this hotel! I go online to my normal go to hotel, The W and book us there for the rest of the trip! 8am comes and goes no manager comes to our room. I go down and demand to see someone immediately.  This younger gentlemen comes out and apologizes.  I thank him for his apology and politely request ALL of my money back immediately.   He obliged and asked if  I would consider coming back after changes have been made! Bless his heart. NO dear!
Help me polish this:
Last year, we chose to stay at The Saint for our girl's trip, and initially, we were quite impressed. The lobby had a charming ambiance, and the bar and restaurant were undeniably cool, making us "ohh and ahh" as soon as we stepped in. The hotel staff were friendly, which added to the overall positive experience. It seemed like we were in for a fantastic weekend.

However, I arrived a few hours before my friend and decided to get some work done. I set up my laptop, ordered room service, and dedicated four straight hours to work. Afterwards, I left to buy a bottle and treat myself to a mani/pedi. When my friend joined me later, our excitement quickly diminished as we discovered a massive flying roach in the room. I was utterly horrified and immediately walked out to the front desk. I couldn't stay in a place like this!

The staff assured me they would send a maintenance worker to handle the issue, but I felt that was inadequate. If one bold roach dared to make an appearance, it was fair to assume there were others hiding behind the scenes. They offered us another room, but it turned out to have small spiders and other dead bugs lurking in the corners of the window. Moreover, the TV didn't work, and one of the lamps lacked bulbs. It became clear that this hotel was not up to par.

By this point, it was 3 am, and I knew I couldn't stay here past 8:15 am. I didn't want to risk keeping my purse or luggage in this subpar hotel. Without hesitation, I decided to book us a room at my go-to hotel, The W, for the remainder of our trip. When 8 am came and went without any visit from the manager, I marched down to the front desk, demanding immediate attention.

A young gentleman finally emerged and apologized for the inconveniences we had faced. I accepted his apology graciously but made it clear that I wanted a full refund immediately. Surprisingly, he obliged and even asked if I would consider returning once they had made necessary changes. Bless his heart, but there was no chance I'd ever consider going back to that place after such a disappointing experience.

input:
Oh Chickie's and Pete's, you are the perfect place to watch some sports and indulge. 

No doubt this is not the best food I've ever had but, if you can get a seat, grab some beer with mussels red and crab fries, there's no way not to thoroughly enjoy this place during a game or any time you're down by the stadiums. 

My favs are the crab fries, mussels red (white is overloaded with garlic that I can't always take it), the spicy pull and peel shrimp, steamers, and if the mood is right the blue crabs (it's a lot of work but tasty). This place also makes getting down and dirty with your food easy. There are sinks all over so you can rinse the mess off your hands once you're done....good touch.

To sum it up, Chickie's and Pete's is a Philadelphia institution and always a good time. I strongly suggest going at least once to enjoy the experience. 

Please note: Make sure to remember two things before coming during major sporting events. 1. You'll never get a table and 2. You'll deal with a ton of drunk people. I've absolutely been one of these people before and we can get annoying unless you're in the right frame of mind. :)

input:
I'm giving this joint 4 stars because they have earned it, but they are definitely 5 star material, if they work out a few kinks. Granted, they just opened, so some of the errors I've experienced (I work in the area, so I've been there several times) will probably get worked out and they are more than willing to make corrections and accommodations when they mess up. 

But over all, the food is REALLY good. Unlike my fellow Yelp-ers, I would say that ther pizza is not their strong suit - its kinds greasy and not sure if they use 100% mozzarella - tastes like its cut with something cheaper. However, so far I've had:  

The Quaker (Chicken version) - Delicious. They make their chicken steaks with the chunky chicken, which I like much more than the shredded version. They could season the chicken more, but the cheese was melted perfectly and the veggies were fresh. 

The fries - crisp and flavorful. I didn't even need ketchup, and I always eat ketchup on my fries

The onion rings - a little greasy, but very tasty and crisp. The onions stayed in the breading and didn't slide out when you bit them (which I hate). 

Spanakopita - mine was a little over cooked, but the flavors were really good

Baklava - VERY GOOD! 

Signature Salad - The veggies they use are very fresh which will make or break a salad. Their balsamic is great too!

The (turkey) Greek Burger - one of the best turkey burgers I've ever had! The patty was moist and flavorful all on its own, but then they top it with what must be homemade tzatziki. I could eat a bowl of that stuff! My burger had romaine instead of the advertised arugula, but it was very fresh, so I didn't mind as much. I also asked for feta, which I didn't get, but that sauce made me forget all about it. 

Overall, this place is great! Provided they don't stray from the high quality standard they are setting, I will keep going back.
Help me polish this:
I'm giving this establishment 4 stars because they have certainly earned it, although they have the potential to be a 5-star experience once they address a few minor issues. It's worth noting that they recently opened, so it's likely that the errors I've encountered (as a frequent visitor due to working in the area) will be resolved as they continue to improve. They are also very accommodating and willing to make corrections when they make mistakes.

However, putting those minor hiccups aside, the food is truly exceptional. Unlike some reviewers on Yelp, I personally feel that their pizza is not their strongest dish - it tends to be a bit greasy and I suspect that they might not use 100% mozzarella, possibly opting for a less expensive alternative. Nonetheless, the other menu items I have tried so far have impressed me:

- The Quaker (Chicken version) - Absolutely delicious. The chicken steaks they use have a chunky texture, which I prefer over the shredded variety. To enhance the flavors, they could consider seasoning the chicken a bit more, but the melted cheese and fresh veggies make up for it.

- The fries - Crisp and bursting with flavor. Surprisingly, I didn't even find the need to add ketchup, which is unusual for me.

- The onion rings - They were slightly oily, but incredibly tasty and had a satisfying crispiness. I especially appreciated that the onions remained intact within the breading when bitten into, as I find it unpleasant when they slide out.

- Spanakopita - While mine may have been slightly overcooked, the flavors were still outstanding.

- Baklava - Exceptionally good!

- Signature Salad - The freshness of the vegetables they use here is crucial in determining the success of a salad, and they definitely deliver on that front. Additionally, their balsamic dressing is fantastic!

- The (turkey) Greek Burger - This is hands down one of the best turkey burgers I have ever had! The patty itself was moist and packed with flavor, but the real star of the show is the homemade tzatziki sauce they generously top it with. I could easily devour a bowl of that stuff! Although my burger came with romaine instead of the advertised arugula, the freshness of the lettuce made up for it. It is worth mentioning that I requested feta and unfortunately didn't receive it, but the incredible sauce made me forget all about that minor oversight.

Overall, this place is excellent! As long as they maintain their commitment to maintaining high-quality standards, I will gladly continue to be a loyal customer.

input: Stayed here three nights on business.  The property is located very close to the airport but you really don't hear it.  The rooms are standard TownePlace Suite rooms with a refrigerator, stove, etc..  The area in which the hotel is located is quiet with a combination of other hotels and office buildings.  It's about a 20 minute drive to the downtown or university area.  About 5-10 minutes from Pima Air Museum.  There are not too many restaurants close by but there are some fast food options and a sandwich place called Baggins that was really good and within walking distance.  The staff of the hotel was really friendly and helpful.  The breakfast is standard continental with a couple of hot options. They also have a reception on weekday evenings.  My only complaint is that the food and drink go quickly so get there early.  You could use this as a dinner if you wanted.  I got there about 45 minutes after it started and although there was food left there were very few soft drinks left (no diet).  They could improve by keeping the area stocked throughout the period.  Anyway, the rooms are nice, beds are comfortable and area is safe.
Help me polish this:
I stayed at this property for three nights during a business trip. Despite its proximity to the airport, the noise was not a disturbance at all. The rooms are standard TownePlace Suite rooms equipped with convenient amenities such as a refrigerator and stove. The hotel is situated in a quiet area, surrounded by a combination of other hotels and office buildings. It takes about 20 minutes to drive to the downtown or university area, and only 5-10 minutes to reach the Pima Air Museum.

While there aren't many nearby restaurant options, there are some fast food choices available and I highly recommend trying out Baggins, a sandwich place within walking distance that offers excellent food. The hotel staff were genuinely friendly and helpful throughout my stay. The breakfast provided is your typical continental fare with a couple of hot options, and they also hold a weekday evening reception. However, one downside is that the food and drinks at the reception deplete quickly, so it's advisable to arrive early. If you're in need of a dinner, the reception could serve as a suitable option. During my visit, I arrived 45 minutes after it started and although there was still some food left, there were very few soft drink options remaining, with no diet choices. I believe the hotel could enhance their service by consistently restocking the area throughout the event. Nevertheless, the rooms were pleasant, the beds comfortable, and the overall area felt safe.

We got diverted to Tampa and decided to make the drive to Orlando but first we needed somewhere to eat. Wanting to avoid chain restaurants, yelp steered us towards this little local gem!

The ladies had the 7 oz. Tampa strip and the gents both had a 14 oz. ribeye. They grill their steaks over oak and citrus Wood and the smoky flavor is to die for! We are big fans of our smoker back home and cook our steaks this way as well, it's rare to find steak cooked over woodsmoke in most places and this was worth the side trip!  Sides were veggies and sweet potatoes. The wines on offer were so reasonably priced- most under $20 a bottle but a decent selection. They just don't mark them up 5x like most places! 

Our waitress Lisa also made great recommendations and her service was welcoming, friendly, and excellent. We are so glad we went local instead of to a chain. Bookmarking this place for a return trip next time I am in Tampa for sure!

Complementing our main course were delectable sides of fresh veggies and sweet potatoes. input:
I've been wanting to try Trust Me BBQ for over a year now.  I stopped in there about 3 months ago and waited in line for 10 minutes with no service and left.  After reading reviews, I figured I'd give it a chance again just to see what all the fuss is about.  The food was 50/50 but the service was horrible so I'll likely never return.  The gentleman behind the counter didn't speak, smile or engage with us at all, I felt like I was at a vending machine.  Once we finally ordered, he didn't even listen to the order and put the wrong sides in our meals, we had to correct him while he was serving.  All in all, I will just stick with Down to the Bone BBQ

Pros:  BBQ Sauce is delicious, macaroni salad was different and interesting, "pulled" pork was moist.

Cons:  Chicken was more dry than a sheet of paper, inedible even with the BBQ Sauce.  Mac & Cheese was served from a pan that has probably been on the steam table for 2-3 days.  Collard Greens were very mildly flavored.
Help me polish this:
I have been eagerly anticipating a visit to Trust Me BBQ for well over a year now. However, my initial attempt three months ago left much to be desired. Despite waiting patiently in line for a grueling 10 minutes, I was disappointed to receive no service and ultimately left empty-handed. Seeking some reassurance, I decided to give it another shot after reading various reviews praising this establishment. Unfortunately, the experience was once again underwhelming. While the food had its moments, with the BBQ sauce being particularly noteworthy and the macaroni salad offering a unique twist, the overall service was abysmal. The individual behind the counter seemed devoid of any interest in engaging with customers, wearing a permanent scowl throughout our interaction. I was left feeling like I was a mere inconvenience rather than a valued patron. To make matters worse, our order was mishandled, resulting in incorrect side dishes being served initially. We had to intervene and correct the mistakes as the food was being handed to us. All in all, this experience has solidified my decision to stick with Down to the Bone BBQ.

On the bright side, the BBQ sauce at Trust Me BBQ is undoubtedly delicious, and the "pulled" pork managed to retain its moisture, demonstrating some skill in preparation. However, the negatives should not be overlooked. The chicken, despite being slathered in the tasty BBQ sauce, was drier than a sheet of paper and incredibly difficult to consume. The mac & cheese, unfortunately, appeared to have been sitting in a pan on the steam table for far too long, resulting in a lackluster and uninspiring dish. Lastly, the collard greens, while mild in flavor, failed to impress and left a lot to be desired.

Taking all aspects into account, my overall impression of Trust Me BBQ remains unsatisfactory. The lackluster service and inconsistent food quality leave little reason for me to consider returning in the future.

input:
This small little donut bakery is located in one of Hermitage's oldest shopping centers! 

I can imagine baking donuts is a hard job, let alone running the business...it's one of those jobs that starts in the wee hours of the morning so that the donuts are freshly made daily!

Yeu, the owner, serves not only your common popular donuts, but he also serves donuts with bacon on top, apple fritters, pigs in a blanket, breakfast pastries, and  kolaches....in addition to these yummy treats...he makes doughssants....they are what seems to be a scandalous marriage of a donut and a croissant...!!!!!!!! Need I say more? Yeah...you heard me. A doughssant! Worth the trip just to eat one of these! 

Prices are considerably cheap! The doughssants are only $1.99 each! The regular donuts are about $.60 each! 

These sweet donuts are my favorite treats to buy for my kid's school teachers...and they love them! 

Coffee also served here!
Help me polish this:
Welcome to this charming little donut bakery nestled in one of Hermitage's historic shopping centers. Baking donuts is no easy feat, but the dedicated owner, Yeu, rises early every morning to bring you freshly made delights!

Yeu not only offers the classic favorites you know and love, but he also surprises customers with unique creations like bacon-topped donuts, mouthwatering apple fritters, pigs in a blanket, breakfast pastries, and delectable kolaches. And let me tell you, the doughssants he bakes are an irresistible fusion of a croissant and a donut. A truly scandalous treat, if you ask me!

What's even better is that the prices here are surprisingly pocket-friendly. Treat yourself to a doughssant for just $1.99 or enjoy a regular donut for a mere $0.60. These sweet delights have become my go-to treats when it comes to showing appreciation for my kids' teachers, and they absolutely adore them!

On top of all the tempting treats, this little haven also serves coffee, complementing the donuts perfectly. So why not make a trip to indulge in a doughssant and savor a cup of quality coffee?

input:
Went here based on the high ratings and raves from people.  The entire experience was underwhelming from start to finish.  Their website which is fairly useless if you want to figure out the menu before going, you have to pick your location choice out of 3 locations and then drill down to the bottom to see the weak descriptions of their menu offering, no explanations and no price, just this

    Roast Beef
    Roast Beef Combo
    Roast Pork
    Roast Pork Combo
    Baked Ham
    Baked Ham Combo
    Roast Turkey
    Roast Turkey Combo
    Broccoli Rabe
    Broccoli Rabe Combo


No explanation of whats in a combo (its just where they add cheese by the way)

The table placecard (instead of menu) had a more detailed description than the website.  

When I walked in, its more bar than restaurant, no big deal, but there were tables.  Since I couldnt decide and the sandwiches werent too expensive at $6.85, I got the roast beef and roast port combos.

I got my two sandwiches fast enough, but the roast beef was cold and the roast pork was hot.  Not sure how a cook (for lack of a better word) could serve 2 things at the same time with such a temperature differential, one was obviously sitting for awhile.  I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef while I finished the roast pork, and supposedly it was reheated, since it was warmer, but it was still cold-ish compared to my roast pork I had just finished.  The waitress did offer to replace it when she inquired, but I was in a hurry and didnt really care for a hot version of this sandwich.

The sandwiches were very skimpy on meat, but they "made up for it" by adding too much gravy to make it overly messy and the bread was disintegrating.  The menu place card mentions the "wet meat" option where you get less gravy, I strongly recommend you get it that style, especially if the gravy overpower the meat and structural integrity of the sandwich.
Help me polish this:
I decided to visit this place due to its high ratings and the enthusiastic reviews from other customers. However, the entire experience turned out to be quite disappointing. Firstly, their website is unhelpful if you're trying to determine the menu beforehand. You have to select one out of their three locations and scroll all the way to the bottom to find weak descriptions of their menu items, without any explanations or prices, just a list of options.

For instance:
- Roast Beef
- Roast Beef Combo
- Roast Pork
- Roast Pork Combo
- Baked Ham
- Baked Ham Combo
- Roast Turkey
- Roast Turkey Combo
- Broccoli Rabe
- Broccoli Rabe Combo

There is no clarification on what a "combo" entails, except for the fact that they add cheese. Surprisingly, the table place card displayed more detailed descriptions than their website.

When I entered the establishment, I noticed that it felt more like a bar than a restaurant, which wasn't a big issue. They did have tables available. Since I couldn't make up my mind and the sandwiches were reasonably priced at $6.85, I ordered the roast beef and roast pork combos.

Although I received the two sandwiches promptly, the roast beef was cold while the roast pork was hot. I couldn't understand how the cook managed to serve two items with such a significant temperature difference, indicating that one had been sitting for quite some time. I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef while I finished the roast pork. Supposedly, it was reheated, but it still remained somewhat cold in comparison to the roast pork I had just consumed. The waitress did offer to replace it when she inquired, but I was in a hurry and not particularly interested in a hot version of the sandwich.

To make matters worse, the sandwiches were lacking in meat, but compensated for this by drowning them in excessive amounts of gravy, which made them incredibly messy. Additionally, the bread was falling apart due to the abundance of gravy. The menu place card mentioned a "wet meat" option with less gravy, and I strongly suggest opting for that style, especially since the gravy overpowered the meat and compromised the structural integrity of the sandwich.

input:

Well..... when I go back I'll have a hard time NOT getting another burger. Oh, they also have a decent beer selection and the wait staff/bartenders made me feel very welcomed too.  My food was prepared exactly as I ordered and was served quickly.  The restaurant has a nice atmosphere and the restrooms were clean.  All in all I was very happy!
.
Help me polish this: I stopped by for dinner and a drink, and I must say, I was thoroughly pleased with my experience! Typically, I don't order burgers when dining out because I believe I can make them easily at home. However, I might have a hard time resisting another burger when I return to this place. Additionally, their beer selection is quite decent and the wait staff and bartenders made me feel incredibly welcomed. Not only was my food prepared exactly as I ordered, but it was also served promptly. The restaurant boasts a pleasant atmosphere, and the restrooms were impeccably clean. Overall, I left extremely satisfied!

input:
Too big, too expensive and too far from Downtown.  

I was here for a conference, which seemed like an awesome idea. It wasn't.  I'm in Direct Sales and (like most people at this conference) don't have tons of extra money to spend on mediocre meals when I'm traveling.  $10 for a slice of generic pizza, small side salad and a soda for lunch.   I understand it's a hotel but there weren't any options close by.  Just getting your car from valet was a hassle and took a lot of time.  Being such a big property, it made getting to restaurants off the property really time intensive.  Since you're so far out of Nashville (out near the airport), the good little holes you find when you're in a city are pretty nonexistent.  

The property itself was great.  The hotel is HUGE but really pretty.  I enjoyed walking around but was really happy when I found what I didn't know existed...a shortcut between my room and the Convention Center.  It took my 10-15 minute walk down to about 3 minutes!  BONUS!  Like I said, this place is ginormous.  

Room: Our room was great.  I shared a wonderful suite in the Garden Conservatory with 2 other girls.  We were under a group rate and my friend was quoted $200/night, which is awesome for the space we had.  We had a large room (probably used as a hospitality suite for groups) for socializing.  It had a great bar area set-up and a nice big fridge and lots of drawer space.  Our bedroom was separated by doors that could be locked from either side (like an adjoining room), so it looked like the hospitality suite could be reserved without reserving the room.  It was different than what I was expecting, but whatevs.  It was fine.  So, I wasn't there at check-in.  The girl who reserved the room checked in a couple days earlier than my friend and I.  So, Sunday comes, and the bill was waiting for us when we woke up.  Our friend was charged $1200 for one room (I'm guessing the suite) and $1400 for the other room.  YEP.  She reserved what she thought was a 2 room suite for $200.  The bedroom door was closed when she got there and she asked them to open it up. It was all arranged by the bellman.  She was never told that the bedroom wasn't included....kind of necessary if you're staying over for 6 nights, dontcha think???  So, she's being charged $2600 for what was supposed to be $1200.  Last I heard, the Gaylord's legal department was investigating what she was told, what she wasn't told and if they should charge her the entire amount.  

Checkout:  A FREAKING NIGHTMARE.  Between the money situation, which was not resolved as of late this week, and the 45 minute wait for a cart (in a hotel that holds thousands of people, you'd think they'd be plentiful and they aren't) and a 25 minute wait for the car, my friend and I decided to sweat it out and schlep our goods to the door where our car would be delivered to us.  It was not a short walk and we had a TON of stuff, which meant multiple trips.  UGH.

I'm sure I'll be back for another conference (I am pretty sure my company has booked this for at least one more year....) but I'm not going to be happy about it.  I might even consider driving down, staying in a hotel somewhere downtown and driving out to the Conference stuff.
Help me polish this:
The hotel was too large, too expensive, and too far from Downtown. Attending the conference seemed like a great idea at first, but it turned out to be disappointing. As a Direct Sales professional, I, along with many others at the conference, couldn't afford to spend a fortune on average meals while traveling. Paying $10 for a slice of generic pizza, a small side salad, and a soda for lunch seemed excessive. I understand it's a hotel, but the lack of nearby dining options made it even more inconvenient. Simply retrieving my car from valet took a lot of time and effort due to the property's immense size. Exploring restaurants off-site also became time-consuming because of the hotel's location far from Nashville's city center. Unfortunately, this meant missing out on the charming local spots usually found in a city.

Despite these downsides, I must admit that the property itself was impressive. The hotel, though colossal, possessed a stunning aesthetic. Although navigating around was challenging, I stumbled upon an unexpected shortcut between my room and the Convention Center, significantly reducing my walking time from 10-15 minutes to a mere 3 minutes - a definite bonus. To reiterate, the hotel was undeniably enormous.

In terms of accommodation, our room was excellent. I shared a delightful suite in the Garden Conservatory with two other ladies. We received the benefit of a group rate, with my friend quoted an incredible $200 per night for the spacious suite. The suite itself served as a socializing area, featuring a well-equipped bar, a large fridge, and ample drawer space. There was also a separate bedroom with lockable doors, giving the illusion that the hospitality suite could be reserved independently from the bedroom. It wasn't what I had anticipated, but it sufficed. Unfortunately, I wasn't present during check-in as my friend handled those arrangements a few days prior. To our surprise, upon waking up on Sunday, we discovered a bill waiting for us. Our friend had been charged $1200 for one room (possibly the suite) and $1400 for the other. Yes, you read that correctly. She had assumed she reserved a two-room suite for $200, only for the bedroom to be closed off upon arrival. She requested that staff open the door, but no one informed her that the bedroom wasn't included - a crucial detail considering our six-night stay. Consequently, she now faces a bill of $2600 instead of the initial $1200. As far as I know, the Gaylord's legal department is investigating the situation, evaluating what our friend was told and not told, as well as determining whether they should charge her the full amount.

The checkout process was a complete nightmare. Coupled with the unresolved billing issue and a 45-minute wait for a luggage cart (despite the hotel accommodating thousands of guests, carts were inexplicably scarce), my friend and I decided to endure the physical strain and transport our belongings to the door where our car awaited. It was a lengthy trek, especially considering the substantial amount of items we had to bring, resulting in multiple trips and considerable effort.

Although I'm certain I'll be attending another conference here in the future (my company has likely booked it for at least one more year), I cannot say I look forward to it. Perhaps opting to drive down and stay at a downtown hotel, while driving to the conference location, may be a more satisfactory alternative.

input:
This was my first time dining at Ava and I enjoyed most of it. We ordered the Ricotta cheese & toasted bread and although the flavor was excellent, I thought the bread to cheese ratio was off quite a bit. The ricotta came in a tiny ramekin typically reserved for flavored butters, so I expected more for an appetizer. 

The two pizzas split among a couple of people were the sausage and the potato with rosemary. They were both tasty but I think they forgot the Rosemary on ours. Still yummy, tho! Another entree was the grouper w/Israeli couscous. Scrumptious!

Dessert was a must and the zeppoles, or sugared donuts, were amazing. The cherry tart a little less so, but one person at our table loved it, so maybe it was just not my cup of tea. The cherries were a sort of candied cherry-interesting, but sweet with a very dense crust. Again, just not my personal fave. 

I will definitely return to try other menu items that looked great-like the pastas made in-house daily...that's next!!
Help me polish this:
This was my first dining experience at Ava, and overall, I thoroughly enjoyed it. One highlight was the Ricotta cheese & toasted bread appetizer. The flavor was excellent, although I did find the bread to cheese ratio to be a bit imbalanced. The ricotta came in a tiny ramekin usually reserved for flavored butters, which left me expecting a larger portion for an appetizer.

We also ordered two pizzas to share among our group, the sausage pizza and the potato with rosemary. Both were delicious, although I believe they might have forgotten to include the rosemary on ours. Nevertheless, they were still quite enjoyable. Another standout dish was the grouper with Israeli couscous, which was truly scrumptious.

For dessert, we couldn't resist trying the zeppoles, or sugared donuts, which were absolutely amazing. However, the cherry tart fell a little short for me personally. Although one person at our table loved it, perhaps it just wasn't my cup of tea. The cherries had a candied flavor and the crust was dense, resulting in a sweetness that didn't quite align with my preferences.

Overall, I will definitely be returning to Ava to explore more of their enticing menu options. I'm particularly excited to try their house-made pastas, which are prepared daily. That will definitely be my next culinary adventure!

input: 1st time eating here. Very clean, nice folks and very good sushi.  Would and will go back. Service was spot on, sushi was very fresh and reasonably priced .
Help me polish this: First time dining at this restaurant and I was thoroughly impressed. The atmosphere was clean and the staff were incredibly friendly. As for the sushi, it exceeded my expectations - fresh and flavorsome. I will definitely be returning in the future. The service provided was exceptional and the prices were reasonable. Overall, a fantastic experience.

input: This place is just the best. If you really have to ask why it's all in the name itself. If u don't like chicken then don't come here bc their birds are fly! Don't forget to try their fried corn on the cobs. It's dank!
Help me polish this: This place is unquestionably the best, and the reasons are evident in its name. If you're not a fan of chicken, then this may not be the ideal place for you, as their poultry dishes are exceptional! Additionally, make sure not to miss out on their delicious fried corn on the cobs. It's truly outstanding!

input: REALLY below average food.  Akin to waffle house.  I wanted this to be good based on the reviews but not so.  The pancakes tasted like a frozen processed version, "homemade" maple syrup was watery/sugary with fake flavoring.  Trees make authentic syrup, not people.  The hash browns were greasy and fairly tasteless. The bacon overcooked, hard and chewy.  Obviously had been sitting awhile. Overall, very uninspired food.  Unfortunately, this is one of those places that is living on an outdated "must go" reputation.  There are much better offerings in Nashville.
Help me polish this: Extremely subpar dining experience. Comparable to a Waffle House setting. As much as I hoped for a delightful meal based on the positive reviews, I was sorely disappointed. The pancakes tasted akin to processed, frozen ones, lacking any authentic flavor. The so-called "homemade" maple syrup was nothing more than a watery, overly sweet concoction with an artificial aftertaste. Authentic syrup comes from trees, not from a bottle. Additionally, the greasy and bland hash browns did not leave a lasting impression. The bacon was severely overcooked, rendering it tough and chewy, clearly having been left sitting for quite some time. Overall, the uninspiring dishes fell far below expectations. Regrettably, this establishment seems to rely on a reputation that is no longer deserved. When it comes to dining in Nashville, there are far superior options available.

input: Excellent.  Went there for lunch (the budget option).  Prix fixe menu was tempting.  Wife had the prime rib po'boy with the soup of the day (tomato fennel).  Both were excellent (the po'boy being an upscale interpretation, with gruyere and a really good horseradish sauce).  I had the seafood jamabalaya and seafood gumbo, also excellent (probably the best I've had).
Help me polish this: Great choice! We decided to check out this place for lunch, opting for the budget-friendly option. The prix fixe menu immediately caught our attention. My wife went for the prime rib po'boy, accompanied by the tantalizing soup of the day - tomato fennel. Both dishes exceeded our expectations, with the po'boy boasting an upscale twist featuring gruyere cheese and a delectable horseradish sauce that really elevated the flavors. As for me, I indulged in the seafood jambalaya and seafood gumbo, and let me tell you, they were absolutely outstanding. Hands down, the best I've ever had.

input:
We recently used Pure Design for a large event in a nearby hotel. Pure staff met with me to discuss my budget and offered beautiful, unique flower and arrangement selections. Their estimate came in well within my budget. Their staff was always professional and their expertise was obvious. The day of the event, they created such a gorgeous space with all the beautiful arrangements - our guests raved about them, even days after the event was over! I was also able to take home/give away the arrangements, which is not always the case with other florists. And the flowers lasted several days after the event.

I would highly recommend Pure for a large event.
Help me polish this:
We recently had the pleasure of working with Pure Design for a major event held at a nearby hotel. From the moment we met with their staff to discuss our budget, we knew we had made the right choice. They presented us with a range of stunning and unique flower arrangements that perfectly aligned with our vision.

Not only were their offerings exquisite, but their estimate also pleasantly surprised us by fitting comfortably within our budget. Throughout the entire process, Pure Design's staff was consistently professional, displaying their undeniable expertise in every interaction.

On the day of the event, we were blown away by what Pure Design had accomplished. They transformed the space into a breathtaking haven with their incredible arrangements. Our guests couldn't stop raving about the flowers, even days after the event concluded! What's more, unlike other florists, we had the privilege of taking home or giving away the arrangements. It's another testament to Pure Design's dedication to providing value and service to their clients.

Even beyond the event, we were impressed with the longevity of the flowers. They remained vibrant and fresh for several days, exceeding our expectations.

If you are in need of exceptional floral design services for a large event, we wholeheartedly recommend Pure Design. Their talent, professionalism, and ability to work within your budget make them an outstanding choice.

input: My husband and I are not "spring chickens", but we love to Par-Tee. The server immediately welcomed us and asked about our drink preferences.  He was very knowledgeable and helpful. The beer selection was wonderful, the liquor selection divine.  The bar food, even though it was a small selection, was excellent. I had never wanted to try pork bellies (the name turned me off.) Dan ordered it, I tried it,and we now have a convert.  WE highly recommend their pork belly sliders! I hope they continue to add a few more delicious tapas.  These folks have it together and are very engaging.  We'll be back often.
Help me polish this:
My husband and I may not be young, but we still know how to have a good time. That's why we were thrilled when we discovered this fantastic place to Par-Tee. From the moment we walked in, the server made us feel right at home, inquiring about our drink preferences with genuine interest. Not only was he incredibly knowledgeable, but he also went out of his way to help us choose the perfect beverages. The beer selection was impressive, offering a wide variety of options to suit any taste, while the liquor selection was nothing short of divine.

Despite the limited options on the bar food menu, we were pleasantly surprised by the quality of the dishes. I had always been hesitant to try pork bellies, as the name didn't exactly spark my appetite. However, encouraged by my adventurous husband, I decided to give it a shot. And boy, am I glad I did! The pork belly sliders were absolutely phenomenal, and I can't recommend them enough. If there's one thing I wish for, it's that they expand their tapas selection to include more delectable options.

Not only does this place have amazing food and drinks, but the staff also knows how to make you feel like a valued customer. Their friendly and engaging manner added an extra layer of enjoyment to our visit. Needless to say, we will definitely be frequenting this establishment in the future. We highly recommend it to anyone seeking a memorable Par-Tee experience.

input:
Average or slightly above, despite the hype.  On the expensive side.  For $10 or $12 you should get fries with your burger, not a large to share for $8.  I had a bison burger. that was the only reason I went there.  Seems we had 1 beer, 1 iced tea, 1 burger, 1 bison burger and split a large fry, for about $37.  Rather ridiculous. And they try to hard to be different or interesting, but ruin a good meal.  The bison burger was tainted with unnecessary slaw and BBQ on it to call it a Carolina bison burger.  Not worth $12 on its own.

Been there.  Done that.  No reason to go back.  Next...
Help me polish this: Average or slightly above, despite the hype. On the pricey side. You would expect to receive fries with your burger for $10 or $12, not a large portion to share priced at $8. The only reason I visited was for the bison burger, which turned out to be disappointing. They put unnecessary slaw and BBQ on it, trying too hard to make it different or interesting but ultimately ruining the meal. Considering we had one beer, one iced tea, one regular burger, one bison burger, and split a large fry, the total came to about $37, which is rather ridiculous. I've been there and done that, and there's no reason to go back. Next...

input:
Before I share the main issue, I want to share the reason I give any stars is because of our awesome server, LaToya. She was thoughtful and engaging! 

The black bean burger was dry. Sweet potato fries were good. 

Today while at lunch with a group of colleagues the most disturbing thing happened. I noticed the manager in a green sweater lingering around the entrance and then two cop cars with lights flashing pulled up and 3 officers rushed in walked to the table next to us that the manager was pointing to and one of the officer's proceeded to pull out their handcuffs and tell the guy delivering food to put food down at the table and hands behind his back. They escorted him near the front door and had him sit down for a moment before taking him outside in freeZing cold with no jacket where he stood for a few minutes while cops came in and out of restaurant. 

This entire thing was poorly handled, disturbing and unsettling not only to the customers but the other staff. They should have had the cops walk back away from where customers were and deal with it there. Then all the managers disappeared not available to talk to any of the customers let alone apologize or acknowledge people being unsettled. 

No one needs to know why the arrest happened but there needed to be more care for customers and staff in how it was handled. 

Not ok!!!
Help me polish this:
Before I address the main issue, I want to express my appreciation for our outstanding server, LaToya. She was considerate and engaging throughout the meal!

Unfortunately, I had a negative experience today while having lunch with my colleagues. The most unsettling incident occurred, leaving a lasting impression. I observed the manager, easily identifiable by their green sweater, loitering near the entrance. Shortly after, two police cars, lights flashing, swiftly arrived at the scene. Three officers entered the restaurant, directed by the manager's gestures, and approached the adjacent table. To my surprise, one of the officers promptly pulled out handcuffs and instructed the food delivery person nearby to stop what they were doing and place their hands behind their back. The individual was then escorted to a seat near the entrance before being led outside into the freezing cold, without even a jacket. The whole scene was distressing and poorly handled, causing discomfort not only among the customers but also the staff. Ideally, the police should have taken the situation away from where patrons were seated and handled it discreetly. Moreover, it was disheartening that none of the managers seemed available to address the concerns of the customers or even offer an apology for the unsettling experience. 

While the details of the arrest are not necessary to disclose, it is essential to emphasize that greater consideration should have been given to the well-being of both customers and staff in handling the situation. This was simply unacceptable.

input: Fantastic sliders!! Perfect size that you can try more than one!  Fried chicken slider, BLT slider, monte cristo and Cuban were all fantastic!  Now for Donuts to go!!
Help me polish this: Delightful sliders! They are perfectly sized, allowing you to indulge in more than just one. The fried chicken slider, BLT slider, monte cristo, and Cuban options were all truly amazing! And now, it's time for some delicious donuts to take away!

input:
They reopened up derived new management.. this was our 3rd time there. They have daily specials, which is a pretty good price, $7.95 for a plate, ice-tea and soup. Todays (Friday)special, they had Carne Asada with rice n beans, fried fish plate and 2 chicken enchiladas with rice n beans, all come with tea n soup. 

We both had the Carne asada plate but they let me substitute my rice n beans for a salad. Steak was pretty good. 

I think their specials are different everyday. So for the most part it was good all around. Oh service was good n attentive.
Help me polish this:
They recently reopened with a new management team, and this was our third visit to the restaurant. They offer daily specials, which are reasonably priced at $7.95 for a plate, ice-tea, and soup. Today's (Friday) specials included Carne Asada with rice and beans, a fried fish plate, and two chicken enchiladas with rice and beans. All of these options came with tea and soup.

We both decided to have the Carne Asada plate, but I requested a substitution for a salad instead of rice and beans. The steak was delicious and cooked to perfection.

It seems like their specials change every day, which adds variety to the menu. Overall, the food was good, and the service was prompt and attentive.

input: Love this little shop so much for so many reasons. First off, whenever I'm on my way to Sweet Divas, I can smell the spices wafting from this little, inviting shop. Second, they have such a large range of spices that you can smell, taste a little, and purchase. Yes, there's a large overwhelming variety of spices, but fear not! Their knowledgeable staff is available and more than happy to assist you in finding the right spice you are looking for all your cooking needs. Over the years I've purchased many items from here and I can attest that they do last a long time (about a year, year and a half, including some stuff I use often!). I see all kind of specialty salts for example (onion salt, celery salt) as well as sugars and powders (lavender vanilla sugar, vanilla bean powder). Their products even seem to taste fresher (I can taste a difference between their cinnamon and nutmeg and what I can get at a dollar store, for example). The prices aren't too bad and they last long. My three bottles pictured cost about $19, but that will last a good year, so its worth it to me.
Help me polish this:
I absolutely adore this charming little shop for numerous reasons. Firstly, as I make my way to Sweet Divas, the delightful aroma of spices wafts through the air from this inviting establishment. Secondly, their extensive selection of spices allows you to sample and purchase to your heart's content. Though the array of choices may seem overwhelming, rest assured that their knowledgeable staff is always on hand, eager to assist you in finding the perfect spice for all your culinary endeavors.

Throughout the years, I have frequented this shop and can confidently affirm that their products have remarkable longevity. Some items I have purchased from here have lasted up to a year and a half, even with regular usage. They boast an impressive range of specialty salts, including onion salt and celery salt, as well as sugars and powders such as lavender vanilla sugar and vanilla bean powder. Comparing their offerings to those of a dollar store, for instance, I can discern a distinct freshness in their spices, particularly in their cinnamon and nutmeg.

Thankfully, their prices are fairly reasonable considering the quality and durability of their products. The three bottles displayed in the accompanying image, for instance, cost me approximately $19, yet I know they will last me for a significant span of time. In my opinion, this makes the investment well worth it.

input: Steve & his partner are the best! Love that he'll do a bunch of demo racquets! Great prices with lots to choose from. If you're a player this is the place to go!
Help me polish this: Steve and his partner are absolutely amazing! I love the fact that they offer a wide range of demo racquets at great prices. It's a paradise for players with so many options to choose from. If you're a player looking for the perfect racquet, this is definitely the place to go!

input: We went around 6 and it was more packed than I expected. I knew it would be busy but I was surprised. The staff was amazing. We waited in line for about 8 minutes regardless of it being a huge line going out side. Found a table and had our food in less than five minutes. Even with the amount of people they had, it ran so smoothly. One sandwich was messed up but it was very loud in there so I don't think she heard me correctly but someone came to our table and had a new correct sandwich almost immediately. I love that they made time to go around asking if we needed refills and how the food was. So glad to have a chick fil a in Reno. They upheld the chick fil a standards even with all the chaos of opening day.
Help me polish this: We arrived around 6 o'clock, and to my surprise, it was even more crowded than I had anticipated. Although I knew it would be busy, the number of people inside was overwhelming. Nevertheless, the staff provided exceptional service. Despite the long queue extending outside the restaurant, we only waited for about 8 minutes. Once we found a table, our food arrived in less than five minutes, which was impressive considering the crowd. Even with the large number of patrons, they managed to keep things running smoothly. Although one of our sandwiches was prepared incorrectly, it was difficult to communicate the error due to the loud noise inside. However, a team member promptly noticed the mistake and brought us a new, accurate sandwich. I appreciated that they took the time to check on us, ask about refills, and ensure the quality of our dining experience. Having a Chick-fil-A in Reno is a great addition, and I am pleased to see that they maintained the high standards of the brand, even during the chaos of opening day.

input: Great, beautiful spot to do wine tasting. I loved all the wines I tried, great prices as well as service. I had a good
Help me polish this: time and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a fun and enjoyable wine tasting experience.

input:
A wee bit pricey for the portions they serve. I come to Beck's for their gator gumbo over jambalaya. The whole thing is just so savory and the spices are just right. It's not overly spicy and not too salty as well. It's a great meal. The gator is in a sausage form. All chopped up into the gumbo. During this visit, I had to order their pasta. Chicken alfredo, for my 2 year old son. It was alright. The whole pasta tasted a bit dry. It's something I wouldn't get twice.

Verdict - Gator gumbo, end of story.
Help me polish this: The portions at Beck's may be a tad expensive considering what they serve. However, I specifically visit for their incredible gator gumbo which is far superior to their jambalaya. The gumbo is bursting with flavor, perfectly seasoned without being too spicy or salty. The gator, shaped in sausage form, adds a delightful texture to the dish. On this particular occasion, I had to order the chicken alfredo pasta for my 2-year-old son. Unfortunately, it was only passable, as the pasta itself was quite dry and lacked appeal. Therefore, my final verdict is clear - go for the gator gumbo and forgo anything else on the menu.

input: I was a little worried about seeing the reviews but everything. Was great! Not long wait time. Staff was nice from walking in the lobby and asking which way to the office, to the office staff.
Help me polish this: I initially had some concerns after reading the reviews, but my worries quickly dissipated as everything turned out to be great. The wait time was not long at all, and every staff member I encountered, from the welcoming lobby personnel to the office staff, was incredibly nice and helpful.

input: Hipsters unite!  I've never had a good time at The Taint, despite several people's attempts top tell me otherwise.  I'm not impressed by the apathy here, or the dirty-headed Garden District crapfest of regular clientele.  Boo.
Help me polish this: Calling all hipsters! I've yet to experience a great time at The Taint, despite numerous assertions from others. The prevailing apathy and the lackluster crowd in the Garden District just don't impress me. Here's to hoping for something better.

input:
Yea! Another Chick-fil-A!

Just happened to be driving down (up?) Bloomingdale looking for a new spot to eat, and saw this. OK, it's not new food, but it is a new location (opened yesterday).

The parking lot is crazy, like many in FL, but the staff outside kept the drive-thru lanes flowing. I was in line for less than ten minutes. *Every* last employee I talked to, and I talked to six, were pleasant and welcoming, just like every Chick-fil-A I've ever been to.

The food was good of course, although the fries could have been cooked a bit longer. Chick-fil-A sandwhcih was on poojnt, and so was the sweet tea.

Welcome to Bloomingdale CFA!
Help me polish this:
Yay! Another Chick-fil-A has arrived!

I was driving along Bloomingdale, searching for a new dining spot, when I stumbled upon this gem. While it's not a new food discovery, it is a brand new Chick-fil-A location that just opened its doors yesterday.

The parking lot was packed, as is often the case in Florida, but the efficient staff members outside managed to keep the drive-thru lanes moving smoothly. I spent less than ten minutes waiting in line. Every single employee I interacted with, and I spoke to a total of six, was incredibly friendly and welcoming, just like every other Chick-fil-A establishment I've visited.

As for the food, it was as delicious as ever. Though I must admit, the fries could have used a bit more time in the fryer. However, the Chick-fil-A sandwich was spot-on, and so was the sweet tea.

Welcome to Bloomingdale, Chick-fil-A! We're glad to have you.

input: Cute lil spot on Germantown Ave. I came in craving something sweet and they did not disappoint. There was an array of cookies and bars to choose from, if my memory serves me right. Behind the display of goodies there was a table with clear plastic cups filled with yumminess, labeled "cake scrapple" I was intrigued. They were different kinds of cakes and icings, most likely left over from a bake. There were about 5 different flavors to choose from and I went with my favorite Red Velvet with cream cheese frosting. I also ended up with an M&M cookie, my other fave! It was a nice day so I sat outside on their bench and had a couple bites of goodness! The cookie was great, soft & chewy with those hard candies for texture. The cake was also delicious and moist!
Help me polish this:
Cute little spot on Germantown Ave, this place exceeded my expectations when I was craving something sweet. As soon as I walked in, I was greeted with an enticing display of cookies and bars that made it difficult to choose just one. However, what truly caught my attention was the table behind the goodies, adorned with clear plastic cups filled with a delectable treat labeled "cake scrapple". Intrigued, I couldn't resist exploring this unique offering.

To my delight, the table boasted an array of different cakes and icings, most likely leftovers from a recent bake. With five distinct flavors to choose from, I followed my instincts and opted for the timeless Red Velvet with rich cream cheese frosting. Additionally, I couldn't resist indulging in an M&M cookie, an all-time favorite of mine.

Choosing to enjoy the pleasant weather, I settled on their inviting bench outside to savor these delectable treats. The M&M cookie exceeded my expectations, with its perfect balance of softness, chewiness, and the delightful crunch of the candy-coated chocolates. As for the Red Velvet cake, it did not disappoint either, boasting a moist and flavorful crumb that melted in my mouth with every bite.

In conclusion, this adorable establishment on Germantown Ave has certainly won me over. With a wide variety of tempting treats and an undeniable flair for delicious flavors, I highly recommend this spot to satisfy any sweet tooth cravings.

input:
Let me preface by saying that I have been getting my hair cut by a guy in Austin for seven years, even though I've lived in other cities for half that time. He is that good. The couple of times that I've strayed, I have been severely disappointed in the outcome. But I wasn't planning a trip back to Austin for a while and badly needed a cut, so I decided to bite the bullet.

My friend walks in a few weeks ago with *srsly* the cutest short hair cut. And so I ask her who and where, and she says Rodney Mitchell. I figured that this place would be too expensive, but she corrected my thinking on the matter. So I called to make an appointment with her guy (whose name I sadly cannot remember at the moment) and Rodney answered the phone. Turns out the guy my friend had seen didn't do morning appointments and all my afternoons were filled, so Rodney said "look, I'm the owner, I can absolutely vouch for Allison who has several openings in the next few days." So I thought, alright, he's the owner so he knows his stuff--I'll do it.

Allison absolutely did not disappoint. First off, she's a total sweetheart, but not super chatty (I appreciate stylists who can be content to both hold and not hold a convo while working) so there was no pressure there. I came in with my laptop and several photos I'd found that approximated what I wanted in a haircut, as I couldn't find exactly the right one. We talked about it a bit, discussed front and back length, bangs, etc. and she said alright and went to it. What she gave me was the cutest damn shaggy bob that I never thought possible. I seriously can't wait to go back.

One of the other awesome things about RMS is that they give you a discount for your first visit and I believe they have some kind of discount for students and teachers. They also will give you *another* discount when you refer people. So I got my friend a discount, and then referred a friend, so I'll get another discount when I go back for my next cut. All good things when you're trying your best to be a frugal  grad student.

input:
So much to like about this place--the beautiful Mercer Building location, the spaciousness, the lovely, friendly baristas. But there are a couple of important cons for me. Biggest being, the music is constant and too loud, ruining everything you go to a coffee shop to do: read, work, reflect, or enjoy a good conversation. When I asked for it to be turned down, they told me they can't--it just plays at one level all the time, and the speakers  are everywhere so you can't get away from it. It sucks.

Secondly, if you're a tea drinker, you're out of luck. They don't serve the tea in pots, but huge, sloppy individual filters--it makes your beverage totally ungainly, hard to drink and is really off putting.

Pros: gluten free goodies and yummy Italian sodas. I'd love to spend more time here, but the music usually drives me out after 10 minutes.
Help me polish this:
There are many aspects of this place that I truly appreciate - the captivating location of the Mercer Building, the ample space it offers, and the genuinely warm and friendly baristas. However, I have encountered a few significant drawbacks that greatly affect my overall experience. 

First and foremost, the incessant and excessively loud music becomes a hindrance to fully enjoying the purpose of visiting a coffee shop - whether it be reading, working, reflecting, or engaging in a pleasant conversation. Despite my polite request to lower the volume, I was informed that they are unable to adjust it as the music plays at a fixed level throughout the establishment, with speakers positioned inescapably everywhere. This aspect is undeniably frustrating.

Furthermore, if you happen to be a tea enthusiast, you may find yourself rather disappointed. Instead of delightfully served pots of tea, the tea is served using large, untidy individual filters. This method renders the beverage awkward to drink and presents a rather discouraging experience.

On a positive note, they do offer a delightful selection of gluten-free treats and delicious Italian sodas. Although I would genuinely enjoy spending more time at this place, the overpowering music typically forces me to depart within a mere 10 minutes.

The restaurant doesn't have great seating  in the store, so I will take food to go next time. The owner served us and he was very nice, but I don't think people eat in the restaurant very often.

As a newcomer to nihari, I was pleasantly surprised by its tantalizing taste and can't wait to indulge in it again.

While the seating arrangement within the restaurant may not be the greatest, we found the option of taking our food to go superb. The owner, who personally attended to us, was exceedingly amiable. Having known that the previous owners of 'Indian Food' were behind this new venture, our anticipation soared, and Spice n Grill undoubtedly lived up to our expectations. If you ever find yourself hankering for mouthwatering take-out, I wholeheartedly recommend paying them a visit.

input:

But, if you're not too concern about natural vs powder flavor then this place could be good for you. They ask what level you would like you sweetness and any additional add-ons you would like. I always get boba but sometimes the grass jelly is pretty good too! I'd recommend you try. 

This is also a good place to catch up, talk, play board, card games and even do homework. I know it's always busy with students from the U of A and being told from them it's a nice area to just hang out, that's a pretty good sign. 

Maybe I'm just too picky, but I think it could be better.

They give you the option to choose your desired sweetness level and any additional add-ons. Personally, I always get boba, but I have to admit that their grass jelly is pretty good too! I recommend giving it a try.

This place is also great for catching up with friends, having conversations, playing board or card games, and even doing homework. It's always busy with students from the University of Arizona, and hearing from them that it's a nice area to hang out is a promising sign.

Maybe I'm just overly particular, but I believe there is room for improvement here.

"See it, taste it, Yelp it"

input:

input:
Underrated burger alert!!

Randomly came into Pag's during a stroll around Doylestown. The menu wasn't super appealing, actually, so I just went with a cheeseburger. Legitimately, one of the best cheeseburgers I've had in a while! Tasted like a quality Big Mac! Patty wasn't too thick, bun didn't overshadow the burger and whatever sauce they used - YUM.

We were in the wine bar section - ambiance is really nice; def not very kid friendly (we had our son with us.) but staff was friendly and accommodating.

We will totally be back next time we are in the mood for a good burger!
Help me polish this:
Underrated burger alert! Prepare to be pleasantly surprised at Pag's in Doylestown. While the menu may not have initially caught my attention, I decided to give their cheeseburger a try. And boy, am I glad I did! This cheeseburger ranks among the best I've had in quite some time. It had all the makings of a quality Big Mac, with a perfectly sized patty, a bun that complemented the burger, and a delicious sauce that left me wanting more.

We found ourselves in the wine bar section, which had a wonderful ambiance. However, I must note that it may not be the most kid-friendly establishment (we had our son with us), but the staff was friendly and accommodating.

Rest assured, we will definitely be returning to Pag's the next time we're craving a fantastic burger.

input: Absolutely wonderful food & service! Go there for lunch/dinner with my boyfriend at least once every two weeks. Prices are very much reasonable. Weekends get pretty packed so may have to wait a little bit but that's never an issue for us. Always get the Indian Pancake & the Hainanese Chicken or Curry Chicken. Other dishes are delicious as well. Never get tired of it!
Help me polish this: The food and service at this restaurant are absolutely phenomenal! My boyfriend and I make it a point to dine here for lunch or dinner at least once every two weeks. The prices are very reasonable, making it even more enjoyable. Although it can get quite busy on weekends, we don't mind waiting a bit because the experience is always worth it. Our go-to orders are always the Indian Pancake and either the Hainanese or Curry Chicken, both of which are incredibly flavorful. However, the other dishes on the menu are equally delicious. We never tire of the outstanding dining experience this restaurant offers!

input: Pretty slow service and the waitresses aren't very kind. I guess I was expecting something different at a diner with high ratings but I understand it's in the middle of a tourist area. However, service should be a priority. Something that really bothered me was how much trash was left on the floor of the outside deck- it all has the potential to blow right into the ocean. NOT OKAY. I had to stand up several times to grab straw wrappers and napkins before they blew into the water. If you're going to have a waterfront/beach front business, be responsible about it. It would be a very easy fix-just a screen on the bottom of the fence. The food was good but I won't be back.
Help me polish this: The service at this diner was disappointingly slow, and the waitresses lacked kindness. Considering its high ratings, I had higher expectations. I understand that being in a tourist area can impact service, but it should still be a priority. What really bothered me was the excessive trash left on the floor of the outside deck, posing a threat to the ocean. This is simply not acceptable. I found myself constantly having to stand up to pick up straw wrappers and napkins before they blew into the water. If you choose to establish a waterfront or beachfront business, it is crucial to be responsible about maintaining it. A simple solution would be installing a screen on the bottom of the fence. While the food was decent, I have no plans to return due to these issues.

input:
I recently had the pre fixe meal for $22 and I enjoyed the combination of tastes on my plate. The chicken was moist my veggies were tasty but a little too greasy....overall is was a great meal. 

I also use them for take out/delivery. I have always enjoyed the way the package their food, in plastic containers that I use over and over again until they look too worn out and I recycle them. I hate take out places that use so much boxes and cups and card board - it's extremely eco-unfriendly. 

The food here is never spectacular but is a good standby you will always come away enjoying. The prices seem a little steep but the restaurant atmosphere is contemporary, the service has always been splendid and the food is dependable.
Help me polish this:
I recently enjoyed a pre fixe meal for $22 at this restaurant, and I was delighted by the harmonious combination of flavors on my plate. The chicken was incredibly moist, while the veggies offered a delectable taste, although slightly greasy. Overall, it was a truly satisfying dining experience.

In addition, I often opt for their takeout or delivery services. One aspect I particularly appreciate is their environmentally conscious approach to packaging. They utilize reusable plastic containers, which I happily use until they become too worn out, and then I recycle them. It's refreshing to support a restaurant that actively minimizes its use of boxes, cups, and cardboard, as it aligns with my eco-friendly values.

While the food here may not be exceptionally exceptional, it serves as a dependable go-to option that consistently pleases. Though the prices may seem a bit steep, the contemporary restaurant ambiance, splendid service, and dependable cuisine make it worth the cost.

input: It's no different than any other Chinese place. Same menu, etc. this place does have some good lunch specials though, and the food is always ready when I go to pick it up.
Help me polish this: This Chinese restaurant is fairly typical, offering the same menu as many others in the area. However, it does have some standout lunch specials that are worth trying. One notable advantage is that the food is consistently prepared on time for pick-up.

input: Finally got to eat here last night. Eclectic foodie menu. I had their onion tart as an app and Kerry had the veal meatballs with sauce on polenta, very delicious. The red gravy tasted like my own. We both ordered the special of citrus short ribs with fat noodles and brussel sprouts, peas. couldn't finish we will be back to try other interesting items. Small crowded but great friendly atmosphere
Help me polish this:
We finally had the opportunity to dine at this amazing restaurant last night. The menu offered a diverse selection of delectable dishes for food enthusiasts like us. As an appetizer, I decided to try their onion tart, while my dining companion, Kerry, opted for the veal meatballs with a delectable sauce served on a bed of polenta. Both dishes were absolutely delicious, and the red gravy from the veal meatballs reminded me of my own homemade recipe.

For the main course, we couldn't resist ordering the chef's special: citrus-infused short ribs served alongside fat noodles, brussel sprouts, and peas. The flavors were truly sensational, but the portions were so generous that we unfortunately couldn't finish the dish. However, this just gives us another great reason to return and explore the other intriguing items on the menu.

Despite the small and crowded nature of the restaurant, the atmosphere was vibrant and friendly, adding to the overall dining experience. We were thoroughly pleased with our visit and can't wait to come back for more culinary adventures.

input: Last night we tried to get into the oldest Italian Restaurant in South Philly. Thankfully, they couldn't fit us in, so our son said lets try Angelina's  so we walked around the corner and into a small Italian Restaurant.  Immediatly we felt at home.  Angelina is cooking in the front of the resaurant and her husband is servicing. There were 3 of us and we started off with Eggplant and roasted pepper appetizer.  One bite and we were hooked.  We ordered the Veal Osso Bocca, Carbonara and lasagna.  Everything was absolutly DELISH!!  Can't wait to go back!!!

input: The food is average. Drink specials are great but the place is rarely crowded. Last time I was there it was a Friday night at 10 pm. There were maybe 3 other parties at the bar.
