input:
You think Value City, you think cheap value, right? Wrong! 

Think Rothman prices with Ashley Furniture pieces. Not a Broyhill in sight. 

Negatives:
- Entertainment centers and TV stand selection is small, and over priced selection.
-Their "Clearance" section is laughable and not much of a sale. No one is going to pay $299 for a nicked up coffee table that was originally $350. Go lower. 
- Sectionals by themselves average around $1,000 by brands I've never heard of. 
- The staff hangs out like a clique chatting in the middle of the store rather than helping customers. 
-Dining sets are nothing special and overpriced as well. I've seen the same selection everywhere else at a lower price. 
-5% military discount? Ooooh you're going to knock $20 off my sofa! 

Only Positive:
-They have a few modern pieces. 

Overall:

I think they're high for low quality-mediocre furniture. Shop around town. Or if you do find something you must have here, wait for a holiday sale.
Help me polish this:
Revised:

When you think of Value City, you may assume it's all about cheap value, right? Well, you couldn't be more wrong!

Picture Rothman prices combined with tasteful Ashley Furniture pieces. You won't find a Broyhill item anywhere in sight.

However, there are a few drawbacks:

1. The selection of entertainment centers and TV stands is limited and the prices are on the higher side. It's difficult to justify paying top dollar for these items.

2. Their "Clearance" section leaves much to be desired. Their so-called sales don't offer much of a bargain. Who would pay $299 for a scratched coffee table that was originally priced at $350? The prices should be reduced further.

3. Sectionals from unfamiliar brands typically average around $1,000. It's hard to have confidence in the quality when you've never heard of the manufacturers.

4. The staff tends to hang out together, engaging in idle chatter in the middle of the store, rather than assisting customers. It's not the most customer-friendly approach.

5. The dining sets are neither exceptional nor reasonably priced. You can find the same selection elsewhere at a lower cost.

On the positive side:

- They do offer a few modern pieces that are worth considering.

Overall, I feel that Value City offers overpriced, low-quality to mediocre furniture. It's advisable to explore other furniture stores in town. In the event that you do find something you truly desire at Value City, it's best to wait for a holiday sale to make the purchase.

input: I really like Franzone's. The owner is typically around, super friendly, and seems to really care about the product. input:
Finally had the chance to stop by Bab Cafe...what took us so long!  Both of us being Asian food fanatics, we are so happy to have Bab Cafe part of our ever expanding culinary experience here in Reno.

Located conveniently downtown, Bab Cafe offers the flexibility of dine-in, takeaway, or even delivery through UberEats. We can't wait to return and continue our culinary journey at this remarkable establishment.

input: First meal in New Orleans. I had the $15 lunch special, a seafood stew (with oyster meat, crab claws, shrimp, and redfish) that came with a surprisingly thoughtful salad. Yeah, it's weird: I'm not even a fan of seafood and, to be honest, I wasn't even really that hungry. Still, before I knew what I was doing I had wolfed down the entire thing. Help me polish this: First meal in New Orleans? Absolutely unforgettable. input:
Ichicoro Ane gets lots of things right and the best part about it is the combination of the ambiance with the food choices and whiskey selection. I'm very happy with this location and the servers I have encountered so far have been helpful and pleasant.

The katsu is great and I highly recommend it to people looking for a more filling dish on the menu. The bao buns were also good for a lighter fish. I haven't had anything I really regretted trying, but definitely ask your server about the portion sizes of each dish since they vary across the menu.

The cocktail selection is excellent. I even had a special Japanese Old Fashioned last time which was a little expensive, but well worth it for some quality Japanese whiskey. 

I'm looking forward to exploring the menu little by little. The best way to experience this is in a group setting so you can try more things and it really reminds me of Izakayas or Japanese pubs I visited in Japan and Korea.
Help me polish this:
Ichicoro Ane excels in many aspects, but what truly stands out is the seamless combination of its inviting ambiance, delectable food choices, and extensive whiskey selection. My experience at this establishment has been nothing short of delightful, and the servers have consistently displayed helpfulness and friendliness.

One dish that truly stands out is the katsu, which I highly recommend to those seeking a more substantial option from the menu. For a lighter fare, the bao buns are also a fantastic choice. Personally, I have yet to taste something that I regretted ordering. However, it is advisable to consult your server regarding portion sizes as they do vary across the menu.

The cocktail selection at Ichicoro Ane is excellent. During my last visit, I indulged in a special Japanese Old Fashioned which, although a little pricey, was well worth the expense for the exceptional quality of Japanese whiskey.

I am eagerly anticipating the opportunity to gradually explore the menu more extensively. The best way to fully appreciate the diverse offerings is to visit with a group, allowing you to sample a wider array of dishes. This communal dining experience reminiscent of Izakayas or Japanese pubs I have visited in Japan and Korea truly enhances the overall enjoyment.

input: Love this bakery!! Great breakfast sandwiches, coffee, and donuts! My friend and I love coming on weekend mornings

input: There is a great selection of whiskey/bourbon to suit anyone's taste. We had burgers with the fried egg on it and it was soo good and probably one of the best burgers I've ever had. input: Very cozy place to have a drink with friends.  The drinks were tasty and were served in very pretty glasses reminiscent of those some of our grandmothers had in their china cabinets. On the downside, all of the drinks seemed to have some combination of ginger, lime, and honey with the main difference being the kind of liquor you wanted in your drink.  So the choices felt limited.  I ordered the bacon wrapped dates, and have to admit that I was choking them down because I was hungry.  They tasted like they were double dipped in sugar.  Also, once another 10 or so people came in, it was very hard to hear each other because the noise level skyrocketed, which is surprising with so much fabric in the room.  The servers were nice and left us alone except to check on us every so often.  I don't recall being offered a second drink when my glass was taken away.
Help me polish this:
This place is incredibly cozy and perfect for catching up with friends over drinks. The drinks themselves were not only delicious but also served in beautiful, vintage-like glasses that reminded me of my grandmother's china cabinet. However, one drawback was that the menu seemed to have a limited variety as most of the options were combinations of ginger, lime, and honey, with the only difference being the choice of liquor. 

I decided to order the bacon-wrapped dates, but unfortunately, they were a bit of a disappointment. I had to force myself to finish them because I was quite hungry, and they appeared to be overly sweet, almost as if they had been double-dipped in sugar. 

As the night went on and more people arrived, the noise level rose to a point where it became difficult to have a conversation without shouting. This was surprising considering the abundance of fabric in the room, which I assumed would help absorb the sound. 

On the positive side, the servers were friendly and gave us space to enjoy ourselves, only checking on us occasionally. However, I do not recall being offered a second drink when my glass was taken away.

Although there are countless little Mexican places below Washington Avenue, I never get sick of them and always look forward to trying the new kid on the block. This time it was El Sabor Poblano on Federal, which could not look less special if it tried.

I liked that there were 3 fish tacos on the menu.  I picked the fried and battered version, though the tortilla chip covered fish could have been awesome. I was instantly impressed when I opened one of my three and found that El Sabor puts an entire filet of fish in each taco! The flakey meat had no fishy taste. These tacos came with the more American toppings of lettuce and, tomato, and cheese. I bet I could have gotten cilantro and onion if I asked. The sole staff member in the place seemed happy to accommodate us- well, we were the only ones dining in.

Another taco filling option that comes with more traditional toppings is the super crispy chorizo, only $8 for 3. There was no detectable gristle here, something I have often come across at this little places.

As unassuming as it looks, this particular South Philly Mexican place is worth stopping by.

Although I couldn't help but wonder how the tortilla chip coated fish would taste, the generous serving of an entire filet of fish in each taco was impressive. The fish itself was incredibly flaky and lacked any unpleasant fishy taste. Accompanied by the more American toppings of lettuce, tomato, and cheese, I suspect I could have requested cilantro and onion if desired. The sole staff member at the restaurant was more than happy to accommodate us - not that there were many other diners at the time.

For those looking for a more traditional taco option, the super crispy chorizo is a fantastic choice at just $8 for three tacos. Unlike many other similar establishments, El Sabor Poblano managed to eliminate any trace of gristle in their chorizo, which was a refreshing surprise.

Despite its unassuming appearance, this Mexican spot in South Philly is definitely worth a visit.

You would think from the size of the place it would be good for groups, but in my experience with 9 people on Saturday at 11am it was about a very hungry, tiring wait to get a seat. 

We tried to make reservations, but they do not take them. And I think we were too small to be put in the side meeting room. So hangry we stood, hoping for just the right table to leave.

The manager was nice enough to offer to fill cups of coffee for us while we waited. But I thought it was odd that they just didn't refill the pot for everyone who was waiting. 

Now for the food...They have these 1/2 and 1/2 combos. Which I love! I got a turkey Reuben and salad. I asked for lots of sauerkraut, and they charged $0.50 for it.. Which is no biggie but I'd expect a lot of kraut. Sadly there was not a lot of it.. But it was still a delicious sandwhich.  :) My friend got the sunrise chile rellenos. If I come back with a smaller party, that is what I would get.
Help me polish this:
Despite its size, the restaurant proved to be quite challenging for our group of nine people on a Saturday morning at 11am. The wait for a seat was incredibly long and tiresome, leaving us famished and impatient. We attempted to make reservations, but unfortunately, the restaurant does not accept them. Additionally, we were deemed too small of a party to be accommodated in the side meeting room, further complicating matters.

In an effort to appease our hunger, the manager kindly offered to fill our cups of coffee while we waited. However, it struck me as odd that they didn't simply refill the pot for everyone in the waiting area.

Despite these setbacks, the food itself was quite enjoyable. The menu offers enticing 1/2 and 1/2 combos, which I particularly liked. Opting for a turkey Reuben and a salad, I requested extra sauerkraut, for which they charged an additional $0.50. Although I had hoped for a generous amount of kraut, I was slightly disappointed by the portion. Nevertheless, the sandwich was still delicious. On the other hand, my friend ordered the sunrise chili rellenos, which was outstanding and definitely something I would consider getting on a future visit with a smaller party.

input: Terrace Lounge appears to want to have a great cocktail venue, but they fall short.  One bartender didn't even know there was a new cocktail menu.  The cocktail was weak and watery, and the liquors they have here and throughout Peppermill are the most unfortunate corporate types.  The service is also very spotty.  It confounded me how four bartenders could not seem to handle about 45 customers.  They didn't have any bar areas, so they all floated around the circle, but then they'd stop, often just short of me and go to the waitress stations to fill their orders.  You can't really build up any rapport with four bartenders floating around trying to serve everyone.  I also hated the people there.  Sorry, but many were your run-of-the-mill casino gamblers.  Why don't you just sit at a machine and play?  You didn't come here for the drinks or to smooze with the bartenders, so seriously, go sit at a machine.  One just sat next to me and lite up a cancer stick and the smoke just blew in my face.  Look, if I walk into a bar and sit next to someone, it's their turf.  They can smoke, fart, vomit on themselves, if I don't like it I can leave.  But if I'm there, it's my turf.  Don't come sit next to me and smoke, fart, or vomit all over yourself.  Or at least be frickin thoughtful and if you see your smoke wafting in my face, put your cancer stick and tray on the other side of the bar so it wafts in your face.  Oh, you don't like smoke in your face???  Me neither moron.  Your life revovles around throwing away your pension money in a mindless electronic game of cards and killing yourself with carcinogens and toxins, well go kill yourself in private, seriously.  You don't see me walking up to a bar and slitting my wrists and burning my money.  It's gross.  I probably just realized this, but I really enjoy Cin Cin not only because they have the best cocktails in town, but they have no machines at the bar.  Peppermill, if you want to create a cool cocktail bar, ditch the machines, train your staff, or hire bartenders with better service skills, and buy some independent liquors.
Help me polish this:
The Terrace Lounge falls short of being a great cocktail venue for multiple reasons. Firstly, one of the bartenders was unaware of the new cocktail menu, displaying a lack of knowledge and attention to detail. The cocktails themselves were disappointing, as they were weak and watery. Furthermore, the liquor selection at Terrace Lounge and throughout Peppermill was limited to unfortunate corporate brands.

In addition to the underwhelming drinks, the service provided was inconsistent. Despite there being four bartenders on duty, they struggled to handle just 45 customers. The absence of designated bar areas led to a chaotic atmosphere, with the bartenders constantly moving around to serve customers or fulfill orders at waitress stations. This made it difficult to establish any rapport or connection with the bartenders.

Another deterrent was the clientele at Terrace Lounge. Many of them resembled typical casino gamblers, which detracted from the overall experience. It was disheartening to see individuals mindlessly playing slot machines while disregarding the quality of the drinks and the opportunity to interact with the bartenders. Moreover, one particular individual even sat next to me and began smoking, with the smoke blowing directly in my face. This lack of consideration was highly unpleasant and made me question why people would engage in such unhealthy habits in public spaces.

On a positive note, I recently discovered a venue called Cin Cin that I thoroughly enjoy. Not only do they offer the best cocktails in town, but they don't have slot machines at the bar. If Peppermill truly aspires to create a cool and memorable cocktail bar experience, I suggest they eliminate the presence of machines, provide comprehensive training to their staff, hire bartenders with exceptional service skills, and invest in a diverse selection of independent liquors. This would greatly enhance the overall atmosphere and quality of Terrace Lounge.

input:
Thank you for a lovely morning!  I was in NJ early and decided to stop in for a delicious diner breakfast.  I got a taylor ham, egg, and cheese and a short stack of blueberry pancakes (I simply couldn't decide between sweet or savory, plus leftovers are never a bad thing).  

The egg sandwich was fantastic.  I was nervous when they said they didn't have kaiser rolls so I went with a hamburger roll.  It was an excellent decision.  The roll was excellent - not just an average cheap hamburger roll.  They layered the cheese on the sandwich, which to me is a must for a true egg sandwich.  It was served with home fries, which were sauteed with large slices of peppers and onions.  I'm not the biggest breakfast potatoes fan, but these were great and I appreciated that they didn't clearly just scoop some food from a huge pile of pre-cooked home fries.

The pancakes were great and fluffy.  My one gripe was their use of smuckers pre-packaged syrup.  I realize that if they put syrup in a container, it probably wouldn't be real maple syrup, but I sort of wish I didn't know that they were giving me sub-par syrup.

The server was friendly and very attentive.  The coffee refills were constant, and the coffee was actually good (so many diners fail at coffee).  Bonus points for the server agreeing not to judge my decision to get two breakfasts.

All around, I loved this place and hope to go back soon.  Long live the Jersey diners!
Help me polish this:
Thank you for a wonderful morning! I found myself in NJ early and couldn't resist treating myself to a delightful diner breakfast. Indecisive as always, I opted for a taylor ham, egg, and cheese sandwich alongside a short stack of mouthwatering blueberry pancakes (because who says I have to choose between sweet and savory? Plus, leftovers are always a plus!).

The egg sandwich surpassed my expectations. Though I was initially apprehensive about the lack of kaiser rolls and settling for a hamburger roll, it turned out to be a fantastic decision. The roll itself was far from ordinary—definitely not your average cheap hamburger roll. They generously layered the cheese, which in my opinion is an absolute must for a truly satisfying egg sandwich. The dish also came with home fries, sautéed to perfection with large slices of peppers and onions. As someone who isn't the biggest fan of breakfast potatoes, I was pleasantly surprised by how enjoyable these were. It was evident that they weren't simply scooped from a pile of pre-cooked home fries, and I truly appreciated the attention to detail.

The pancakes were simply divine, light and fluffy as can be. My only minor complaint was the use of pre-packaged Smuckers syrup. While I understand it's unlikely to find real maple syrup in a container, I would have preferred not to be made aware of the fact that I was being served a sub-par syrup.

The server was friendly and extremely attentive throughout the meal. They kept my coffee cup full, which is a rarity in many diners, and the coffee itself was surprisingly good. It's quite uncommon for diners to get coffee right, but they definitely succeeded. Bonus points for the server graciously accepting my decision to indulge in two breakfasts without any judgment.

All in all, I absolutely adored this place and already have plans to return soon. Here's to the enduring legacy of Jersey diners!

input:

Maybe I'm biased, because I love the service here. They've always been very nice, and came over to check in with me and just make some small conversation when they heard I had a peanut allergy (even though they had no peanuts in any of the dishes I ordered; I think it was Han's sister?). Note though, that the different branches have different specialties. I heard the dan dan mian in Olde City is the best, but the one in UC isn't so good (I wouldn't know since it has peanuts). Overall, I think it;s okay food wise, still not spicy enough as with the other branch. But I like the layout and atmosphere a lot more.

Help me polish this:
The new Han Dynasty has replaced the old Mid-Atlantic restaurant, which had an unchanging menu. Personally, I prefer this Han Dynasty location over the one in Olde City, even though I would rate both of them with 4 stars. Perhaps I am biased because of the exceptional service I receive here. The staff has always been incredibly kind and attentive, going as far as checking in with me and engaging in small conversation when they learned about my peanut allergy (even though none of the dishes I ordered contained peanuts; I believe it was Han's sister who took the initiative). Additionally, if you visit during lunchtime, you can request lunch portions, which are smaller than the dinner portions but offered at half the price on the menu! This makes it an excellent choice for lunch, whether you're dining alone or in a group of two or three people.

input: Husband and I made a mistake and came here on a Lenten Friday. The wait was forever. But since we were already there, might as well suck it up and see what's it all about. input:
im going to have to give this place one star for its horrible customer service:

i called in to ask about the 50% off for tulane students they were advertising, the woman assured me if i came with an id it would be half off and made an appointment for me, only once i got there did they tell me it's only on certain days, "it says it right on the sign," i was perturbed by the inconvenience and said so you're not going to honor it even though you just made an appointment with me and told me it would be 50% off, they said no flat out at first even though the error was blatantly on their side, after my nagging, she eventually called john jay himself and he told the woman that he would not honor what i was told even though i had been inconvenienced by someone in HIS staff because it might cause a 'domino effect,' i said how will there be a domino effect unless you continue to give people incorrect information, there will be no other 'dominoes' as long as you remember what day it is from now on... they began to treat me somewhat patronizingly as i explained that usually businesses make concessions when they are the one at fault, that the customer is supposed to always be right, yadda yadda yadda, i left pretty upset and with ~45 minutes of my life having been wasted - empty handed but for a lame excuse from someone who owns at least 3 businesses over 10 dollars...

i have not received a haircut from them so if you're one of those people who ONLY cares about the product and you think you'll get a good cut go right on ahead, but if you're like me (principled) and you don't like handing profits to people who care nothing about their customers this is a good place to skip next time you need a cut
Help me polish this:
I have to give this place one star for its extremely poor customer service experience. 

I called in to inquire about the 50% off discount that they were advertising for Tulane students. The woman on the phone assured me that if I came in with my student ID, I would receive the discount. She even went ahead and made an appointment for me. However, when I arrived at the salon, they informed me that the discount was only applicable on specific days, as "it says it right on the sign."

I was frustrated by the inconvenience, especially after being told otherwise and having made an appointment based on that information. I expressed my disappointment, questioning why they wouldn't honor what was promised to me. Initially, they flat out refused to honor it, despite the clear mistake on their part.

After persistently bringing up the issue, the woman eventually reached out to the owner, John Jay himself. Shockingly, he too decided against honoring what I was told, citing a potential "domino effect" as his reason. I challenged this claim, arguing that there wouldn't be a domino effect unless they continued to provide incorrect information. All they needed to do was remember what days the discount was applicable in the future.

Throughout our conversation, they began treating me with a patronizing tone. I tried explaining that businesses typically make concessions when they are at fault and that the customer is supposed to be right. However, they seemed dismissive of my concerns.

I left the salon feeling upset and disappointed, with almost an hour of my time wasted and nothing to show for it except for a feeble excuse from someone who owns multiple businesses, all over just $10.

I must mention that I did not actually get a haircut from them. So, if you're solely focused on the end product and believe you'll receive a good haircut, you can proceed at your own risk. However, if you prioritize principles and dislike giving your business to people who show no regard for their customers, I strongly recommend skipping this place the next time you need a haircut.

We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life."

All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. 

I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.
Help me polish this:
My friend and I recently embarked on a trip to Tampa for a concert. However, our experience took an unexpected turn when, just moments away from the Atlanta airport, he realized that he had mistakenly purchased tickets for the wrong day. Despite this setback, we were determined to make the most of our plans and decided to pay the same-day price for airfare, amounting to an additional $800. As my friend later remarked, "It was a costly mistake, but completely worthwhile because it led me to the most incredible sandwich I have ever tasted."

How did we stumble upon this culinary gem, you may ask? It was all thanks to a random selection from Yelp: the Bricks of Ybor. While I cannot vouch for their peanut butter or meatless options, the meat sandwiches we savored were nothing short of extraordinary. Personally, I indulged in the pulled pork, infused with the flavors of ponzu and generously served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was an unforgettable meal, surpassing my culinary expectations by a long shot.

While enjoying our culinary delights, we spent a few hours relaxing and unwinding at the restaurant. To our surprise and delight, Brian, the owner, kindly approached us and engaged in an amiable conversation. He graciously treated us to a complimentary drink and even allowed us to sample his latest appetizer creations, all free of charge. Brian's warm hospitality made us feel truly welcome and added an extra layer of warmth to our dining experience.

Throughout our time at the Bricks of Ybor, I couldn't help but observe the diverse array of patrons frequenting the establishment. From hipsters to geriatrics and even families with young children, it seemed to attract a wide range of individuals. To me, this serves as a testament to both the restaurant's diverse menu and the inviting atmosphere it exudes. In fact, we returned to the Bricks for pre- and post-concert drinks, despite the bustling crowds. Remarkably, the outstanding quality of both the food and service remained unwavering even amidst the hustle and bustle.

Without hesitation, I wholeheartedly recommend this remarkable establishment to anyone visiting Tampa. It will undoubtedly be the first place I revisit upon my next trip to this vibrant city.

input: So worth the wait! The crepes are amazing! I also loved the grits, which is rare. Tried my hubby's pancakes....awesome!
Help me polish this: Absolutely worth the wait! The crepes were absolutely amazing, I couldn't get enough of them! Surprisingly, I even found myself loving the grits, which is something quite rare for me. And let's not forget about my husband's pancakes - they were absolutely awesome!

input: My sister-in-law and I visited this restaurant on 8/28/15 mid afternoon.  We were seated after requested 3 times that the hostess speak a little louder because we couldn't even hear her with the background music.  We were seated in a booth with a never ending Larry King vitamin commercial on the TV - really?  Our waitress introduced herself and a new trainee and then we never saw her again.  Two other wait staff seemed to be sharing our table, but no idea who was responsible for our table.  We got our drinks and ordered, but food took forever considering there was not more than 15-20 filled tables in the entire restaurant.  Burgers were not bad - I ordered the blue cheese burger and it would have been better with less blue cheese, way too much!  Fries and onion sticks were very good.  But no one came to see if we were satisfied, needing anything, etc and took two requests and waiting to get a carry out box.  There was a family seated across the aisle from us when we arrived and we assumed they had finished their meal and were "hanging out".  Only after we received our food did we understand they had already ordered and still did not have their food!  I doubt I will return to this restaurant in the future.
Help me polish this:
My sister-in-law and I visited this restaurant on August 28th, 2015, in the mid-afternoon. Despite requesting three times, the hostess spoke so softly that we couldn't even hear her over the background music. Eventually, we were seated in a booth with an incessant Larry King vitamin commercial playing on the TV. It was quite baffling.

Our waitress introduced herself along with a trainee, but her presence was scarce throughout the meal. Two other wait staff members seemed to be sharing our table, yet it was unclear who was responsible for attending to our needs. Although we received our drinks and placed our orders, the wait for our food felt incredibly long, even though there were only 15-20 filled tables in the entire restaurant.

The burgers we ordered were decent, although my blue cheese burger would have been better with less blue cheese. It was quite overwhelming in quantity. On the positive side, the fries and onion sticks were delicious. However, the lack of attentiveness from the staff was disheartening. It took two requests and an extended wait to receive a carryout box, and no one bothered to check if we were satisfied or needed anything else.

To add to the lackluster experience, there was a family seated across the aisle from us when we arrived. Initially, we assumed they had finished their meal and were simply "hanging out." However, we later realized they had already placed their order and were still waiting for their food. This further highlighted the delays and disorganization within the establishment.

Considering everything, I highly doubt I will choose to return to this restaurant in the future.

input:
In short, the food was decently good, but completely overpriced.  The guacamole and my Mojito were probably the highlight of the meal. I had the peach pork medallions, which were nicely cooked, but lacked flavor. I tried the corn cakes with Barbacoa and that was pretty good.  

The atmosphere was inviting with a hip feel if that's what you're looking for.  What was really annoying was the parking situation. For a place with price points such as these and limited parking spaces, a valet service should be provided either at a cost or complimentary.  Don't even try and park in the back of the building, it's tight and dangerous even getting there and back.  I ended up parking three blocks away and broke a sweat walking in the dead of summer to the front entrance.
Help me polish this: In summary, the food was decent, but overpriced. The guacamole and Mojito were the standout items. The peach pork medallions were well-cooked but lacked flavor. The corn cakes with Barbacoa were enjoyable. The atmosphere was trendy and inviting. However, the parking situation was extremely frustrating. Considering the high prices and limited spaces, a valet service should be provided, even if at a cost. Attempting to park in the back of the building is difficult and potentially dangerous. Personally, I had to park three blocks away and walked in the sweltering summer heat to reach the front entrance.

input: Had dinner Saturday night for the first time at rusty pelican. Called ahead and made a reservation and requested a table next to the window overlooking the water. Hostess went to seat us away from the window, when we questioned her she huffed off and left us staying in the middle of the dining room!! She did return and sat us by the window. The rest of the evening was great, drinks, food and wait staff was excellent. Liz was our server and went above and beyond. Still have to say the hostess was very disappointing!
Help me polish this:
I had the opportunity to dine at the Rusty Pelican for the first time on Saturday night. Prior to our visit, I made a reservation and specifically requested a table by the window, offering us a beautiful view of the water. Unfortunately, upon our arrival, the hostess initially tried to seat us away from the window. Confused, we questioned her decision, which led to her huffing off and leaving us standing in the middle of the dining room. Thankfully, after some time, she returned and eventually seated us by the window as requested. 

Despite this initial disappointment, the rest of our evening at the Rusty Pelican was exceptional. The drinks, food, and wait staff were all superb, and our server, Liz, truly went above and beyond to ensure we had a memorable experience. However, it's important to note that the hostess' behavior left a lasting negative impression on us.

input:
This was a tough one!   On the merits of the wine, fairly average... I understand that the winery has more than one lable and other label is their premium wines.  I look forward to when that is available (I went two weeks ago so maybe it already is)     Location..   what's not to like?  On the pier!  A wonderful outdoor patio,  couldn't have a nicer setting to enjoy your tasting....   The staff were super, super nice,  I would give them an A+!  

So why only three stars?  It is because of the wine club!  Very expensive for the quality of the wines and stingy as HELL with the benefits to the members..   Most wine clubs will give you a free tasting every time you come in (after all, we are your best customers... we are the ones who buy your wine time and time again).  Some wineries will give their members a complimentary glass in leau of a tasting (Carr).   Most wineries allow you to bring guests which is how you get new wine club members.   This system works folks!  The way this wine club works is that you are given a very limited number of passes per quarter, five as I recall.   If I come with my wife once a month we wouldn't even be covered... let alone if we bring a guest!   

So go to this winery if you want to enjoy a tasting in one of the most beautiful settings on earth.   But avoid the wine club!  For that you can pretty much go to any of the other wine tasting rooms on the Urban wine trail.
Help me polish this:
This was quite a challenging experience! In terms of the wine itself, it was fairly average. I understand that the winery has more than one label, and their premium wines are something I look forward to trying in the future (I visited two weeks ago, so maybe they're already available). 

Now, the location was absolutely amazing! Who wouldn't love a winery on the pier? The outdoor patio was truly delightful, providing an idyllic setting to enjoy your tasting. The staff deserves special commendation as they were incredibly friendly and deserving of an A+!

So, why did I only rate it three stars? It's primarily due to the wine club. The prices were quite high considering the quality of the wines, and the benefits for members were disappointingly stingy. Most wine clubs offer a free tasting every visit (since we are, after all, their most loyal customers). Some wineries even provide a complimentary glass instead of a tasting (such as Carr). Furthermore, many wineries allow members to bring guests, which in turn helps acquire new wine club members. This kind of system works wonders, folks! However, this particular wine club only provided a very limited number of passes per quarter, if I recall correctly, it was just five. Even if I were to visit with my wife once a month, it wouldn't suffice, let alone if we bring a guest!

In summary, I recommend visiting this winery if you want to enjoy a tasting in one of the most gorgeous settings imaginable. However, I strongly advise against joining the wine club. Instead, you can find better options on the Urban wine trail, where you'd have a more satisfactory experience.

input:
I got a cheap haircut in NY for next to nothing and what do you know. it looks like some crazy chimp chewed up my hair and spat  it back on my raw scalp.

Since I'm going for job interviews, I needed to look better and went to Domenick's. The guys were great, Robert cut my hair and did a clean job. Bill came out to $35. I'd give it a 4, but it was a little pricy for my taste, but I look human again. Don't know what you guys in Philly normally pay for a haircut.
Help me polish this: After getting a remarkably cheap haircut in NY, I was disappointed to discover the unsatisfactory result that resembled a chaotic mess on my scalp. Considering I had important job interviews coming up, I decided to improve my appearance by visiting Domenick's. The experienced barber, Robert, skillfully transformed my hair into a neat and polished style. Although the service cost me $35, which was a bit steep for my liking, I am pleased to say that I now appear presentable and ready for professional endeavors. I am unsure of the average haircut expenses in Philadelphia, so I would appreciate any insight from you all.

input: Very unhappy, you lost a valued customer. We had a problem where Monro Muffler underfilled our engine by 3 quarts of oil and caused damage to the engine. Monro's insurance company said they would pay for damages if we brought to the dealer, we were frequent customers of Bergeys so we brought it here. They discovered the timing chain needed to be replaced, a chain that lasts the life of the car unless you don't change the oil or have low oil pressure the tensioner can lock and stretch the chain. Joe the service associate that took the car in specifically said I told the insurance company as little as possible and told them he couldn't tell if it was from the oil and there was no way to tell. And on top of that, was extremely rude and unprofessional to my wife bringing her to tears the way he spoke to her. My wife and I just bought a house in the area, only 26 years old and you lost a life long customer. Over the past year we spent about $7000 in repairs here, and Joe went out of his way to be unhelpful and leave us in a terrible spot. I brought it to another mechanic who was able to help us prove more it was from the oil and do what Joe told us and the insurance company they could not do. So on top of losing a service customer, I'm on the market for a new car and can tell you for sure where I will not be getting it.
Help me polish this:
I am extremely disheartened to inform you that due to a significant incident involving Monro Muffler, we have decided to terminate our long-standing relationship with your establishment. Our unfortunate experience began when Monro negligently underfilled our engine with 3 quarts of oil, leading to severe damage. In an attempt to address the issue, Monro's insurance company promised to cover the damages if we had the repairs done at a dealership. Considering our loyalty to Bergeys as valued customers, we trusted in your expertise and brought the vehicle to your premises.

To our dismay, during the examination, it was discovered that the timing chain, which typically endures for the entire lifespan of a car, required replacement. The service associate named Joe, who handled our case, made a deliberate effort to downplay the role of the oil in causing this damage. More distressing than his uncooperative stance, Joe exhibited an unacceptable level of rudeness and unprofessionalism towards my wife, reducing her to tears. Considering our recent purchase of a house in the vicinity, our experiences with your establishment have left an indelible negative impression. We were loyal customers, having spent approximately $7000 on repairs over the past year, but Joe's deliberate lack of assistance has now pushed us to reconsider our loyalty.

Fortunately, we sought assistance from another mechanic who not only managed to provide evidence supporting the connection between the oil issue and the timing chain damage but also fulfilled the requirements set by Joe and the insurance company. The unfortunate combination of losing a valuable service customer and the current need to purchase a new vehicle will unequivocally guide us away from considering your establishment for future automotive endeavors.

Please understand the gravity of this situation, as it represents a significant loss for your business. We sincerely hope that you address the issue at hand and take the necessary steps to ensure that other customers are spared from similar ordeals.

input:

Homemade breakfast tarts and chicken pot pies .
All sweets looked well beyond beautiful and delish.
I felt some of the items were a tad pricey considering the sizes being on a smaller size. But I know premium quality costs more ..

Help me polish this: Help me polish this: This beautiful shop is incredibly clean and offers a wide variety of delicious treats, from homemade breakfast tarts to flavorful chicken pot pies. Every sweet treat in the shop is not only stunning but also incredibly delicious. However, I did find that some items were a bit on the pricey side considering their smaller sizes. Nevertheless, I understand that premium quality often comes with a higher cost. It's a fantastic spot for locals and definitely worth a visit for anyone traveling from center city and beyond. input: Definitely get in line before 8:30am. We waited about 30 minutes. Pancakes were fine. My friends got the raspberry pancakes, the sweet potato pancakes and the san antonio. I got the sugar and spice pancakes. All were well and fine, a bit dry. I don't understand the hype, but if the line isn't too long it's not bad for normal breakfast food. If the line is longer I would highly recommend skipping this place and heading down the street to Fido - insanely good coffee and great breakfast food.
Help me polish this: Definitely be sure to join the queue before 8:30am; we waited for approximately 30 minutes. The pancakes we ordered were satisfactory, though a tad dry. My friends opted for the raspberry, sweet potato, and San Antonio varieties, while I chose the sugar and spice pancakes. While they were all decent, I fail to comprehend the excessive hype surrounding this place. However, if the line isn't too lengthy, it's acceptable for a typical breakfast. On the other hand, if the wait is considerably longer, I would highly recommend skipping this establishment and instead heading down the street to Fido. They serve incredibly delicious coffee and offer a fantastic breakfast menu.

input: They have the WORST service advisors! Used to be good before Kelly and her team left. Unfortunately, it's convenient to work if I need oil change before I can make it to another Honda dealer.
Help me polish this: The service advisors at this place are absolutely terrible! They used to provide great service until Kelly and her team departed. Sadly, it's the only convenient option for me to get an oil change if I can't make it to a different Honda dealer.

input:
The best soon-dubu in the city!  This place is tucked away and once you walk in, it's like you've stepped into a Korean home.  Very welcoming, warm and inviting.

It's very vegetarian friendly!  The soft tofu is stewed and put into the dol sot pots which each and every stew feels like it's custom made for you. 

You can select from beef, seafood or mixed meats (seafood & beef), mushroom, and just plain.  They can adjust the spice as needed too.  I always get the extra hot with the hot temperature, can't beat it.  The rice also comes in a dol-sot which is great if you leave it in for a while, it burns the rice into a nice crispy shell.  DROOL.

Just thinking about this place makes my mouth salivate!  

If you're not into tofu, they also offer korean bbq meats (cooked in the back), with other soup/stew items.

Love this place!!!
Help me polish this:
Experience the best soon-dubu in the city at this hidden gem! As soon as you step inside, you'll feel like you've entered a cozy Korean home, with its welcoming and inviting atmosphere.

What sets this place apart is its vegetarian-friendly options. The soft tofu is simmered and beautifully presented in dol sot pots, giving the impression that each stew is tailor-made just for you.

You have a variety of choices including beef, seafood, mixed meats (seafood & beef), mushroom, or plain. Don't worry about spice levels, as they can adjust it to your preference. Personally, I always go for the extra hot with a high temperature, nothing beats that intensity. And let's not forget about the dol-sot rice, which develops a delightful crispy shell if left in for a while. Prepare to indulge!

The mere thought of this place makes my mouth water! But, if tofu isn't your thing, fear not, as they also serve delicious Korean BBQ meats cooked in the back, alongside other tantalizing soup and stew options.

I absolutely adore this place and highly recommend it to all food enthusiasts!

input:
As motels go this one is very nice for the rate. Clean, comfortable and well-managed. You get what you pay for so the breakfast buffet is just OK. The pool is too small to swim laps (disappointing). The lobby area is spacious and comportable. 

If you are looking for a moderately priced place to sleep that is clean and comforable this will suit you just fine.
Help me polish this:
This motel is an excellent choice considering its rate. It is clean, comfortable, and efficiently managed. However, keep in mind that the breakfast buffet is just average, but it fulfills its purpose. The pool, unfortunately, falls short when it comes to size as it is not suitable for swimming laps, which may be disappointing for some. On the bright side, the lobby area is pleasantly spacious and comfortable.

If you are seeking a reasonably priced accommodation that guarantees cleanliness and comfort, this place will certainly meet your expectations.

input:
The only reason I mentioned the media or attorney was out of frustration after he would not provide the owner's contact info so I could appeal to her about keeping the area clean and cleaning or painting the columbarium.  That older area that is out of sight has been that way for years but we finally got tired of it and complained.  He never admitted it could be cleaned up.  As for the vase, I didn't demand just one for my Dad.  I stated he should replace the cheap plastic vases on ALL the niches as they were falling off and disintegrating.  There are not very many of them. I simply thought it would be the right thing to do.  

If there was empathy, I did not hear it.

My intention was to appeal to the owner directly about the need to keep the area clean and to address the issues with the columbarium, which had been neglected for years. Unfortunately, he never acknowledged the need for cleaning or maintenance.

Regarding the vases, I did not demand a replacement solely for my father's niche. Instead, I expressed that it would be appropriate for him to replace the cheap plastic vases on ALL the niches, as they were falling off and deteriorating. I believed it was the right thing to do considering there were only a few of them.

Sadly, I did not perceive any sense of empathy from him throughout the conversation.

input:
From the second you walk in the door, you're greeted by the adorable woman at the counter. It seems if you come in here more than once a week, she'll know you're name but I haven't been so lucky since my visits are a bit more sporadic.

My most recent discovery are the vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, which are served all day! I particularly enjoy veg. sausage w/ havarti on an everything bagel. I could actually go for one right about now... I've also had the veggie club sandwich and my other half has enjoyed the chicken cheesesteak hoagie and the chicken salad on a croissant. Everything always taste fresh, they are priced really well  (I think my favorite bagel sandwich I mentioned is $2.09-2.99- cheaper than wawa!). The people at the deli are super helpful, offering menus if you can't read the one on the wall and will make great suggestions and accommodations to your needs and want.

Don't forget to grab a really great snack too while you're there- they have amazing chocolate bars, an incredible drink case, tons of chip varieties and those addictive hi-chew candies in every flavor.

I know i'll be back here, who doesn't like fast / delicious / attentive service?
Help me polish this:
From the moment you step through the door, you'll be welcomed by the charming woman behind the counter. If you're a regular visitor, she'll remember your name, although I haven't been fortunate enough to experience that since my visits are somewhat sporadic.

My latest revelation has been their vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, available all day long! Personally, I find the veggie sausage with havarti on an everything bagel absolutely delightful. In fact, I could really go for one right now... I've also tried their veggie club sandwich, while my partner thoroughly enjoyed their chicken cheesesteak hoagie and chicken salad on a croissant. Every item tastes incredibly fresh, and the prices are very reasonable (even cheaper than Wawa, with my favorite bagel sandwich priced at $2.09-2.99). The deli staff are extremely helpful, even providing menus if you have trouble reading the one on the wall. They always offer fantastic recommendations and are more than willing to accommodate your dietary preferences.

Oh, don't forget to pick up a fantastic snack on your way out! They have an amazing selection of chocolate bars, an incredible array of drinks, a wide variety of chips, and those addictively delicious hi-chew candies in every imaginable flavor.

It's safe to say that I'll definitely be returning here. After all, who can resist fast, delicious, and attentive service?

input: We stopped in for brunch and we weren't expecting the food to be so delicious.  The 3 meat hash was amazing, as was the turkey sandwich and bagel/salmon.  The employees were very friendly and accommodating.  A little pricey, but well worth.  We will visit again if in the area.
Help me polish this: We decided to have brunch at this place without any high expectations, but to our surprise, the food turned out to be absolutely delicious. The 3 meat hash was particularly outstanding, along with the mouthwatering turkey sandwich and the scrumptious bagel topped with salmon. Additionally, the employees were exceptionally friendly and accommodating throughout our visit. Although it may be a bit on the pricey side, the quality and taste of the food make it well worth the cost. If we find ourselves in the area again, we would definitely return for another visit.

input: Nice little bar located at the very far end of Terminal E and Tampa International. The airport recently added several new restaurants with a "local vibe" and this is one of them. There isn't a ton of seating but it also isn't close to the TSA area so it's a bit hidden. Hey have TVs if you wanna catch a game while you wait for your flight. Food is very reasonably price for the portion size. Appetizers run from $5-$10 and majority of sandwiches are $12. I didn't order any food but it looked amazing! Drinks are tasty and Prices are not terrible. Think 22oz Jai Alai for $8.50. You cannot take alcoholic beverages into the terminal (Columbia does this I think). I had a Manhattan for $11 and it was very tasty. Staff is attentive and friendly. I know my new spot when I'm waiting on a Delta flight!
Help me polish this: Located at the far end of Terminal E in Tampa International Airport, this cozy little bar is a hidden gem among the recently added "local vibe" restaurants. Despite its limited seating, it offers a quiet respite away from the bustling TSA area. With TVs available, it's the perfect spot to catch a game while waiting for your flight. The food here is reasonably priced, with appetizers ranging from $5 to $10 and sandwiches priced around $12. Although I didn't try any myself, the food looked amazing. The drink options are also impressive, with the delectable 22oz Jai Alai priced at just $8.50. While you can't take alcoholic beverages into the terminal (unlike Columbia), the bar serves a delicious Manhattan for $11. The attentive and friendly staff make it a pleasant experience overall. Personally, I've found my new go-to spot for waiting on Delta flights!

input: The depot burger is so delicious along with the shishito peppers! Perfect food, perfect atmosphere, perfect drinks!
Help me polish this: The Depot Burger is an incredibly delicious dish, and when paired with the flavorful Shishito Peppers, it creates a perfect culinary experience. The combination of delectable flavors, combined with the inviting atmosphere and superb drink selections, make it an exceptional dining experience in every way.

input: Quality of this store has gone downhill over the past few years. In the past,  I was able to easily choose from a wide selection of food at reasonable prices any time of day. I have noticed recently that the produce is not as fresh, but more expensive,  and the prices of the organic foods are more expensive than Whole Foods. This morning I debated on going to Wegmans or going to this store. I only had to get a few items so I decided on this Giant since it was closer. Big mistake. I have seen on average at least 3 or 4 people shopping around 5 a.m. In the past but today just me. They had all of the store roped off where it was impossible to get to certain aisles and very difficult to get to the register. In my frustration I went under a rope to get soup.  I was then berated by a number of people who were supposed to be cleaning the floors but some were just standing around doing nothing. I couldn't even walk out of the closest door because that was blocked off. If they needed to clean the floor they should have closed the store for a few hours. It would have taken less time at Wegmans which is where I will shop for now on.
Help me polish this:
The quality of this store has significantly deteriorated over the past few years. Previously, I used to have no trouble selecting from a wide range of food options at reasonable prices, at any time of the day. However, lately, I've noticed that the produce is not as fresh and comes at a higher cost. Moreover, the prices of organic foods here are even higher than Whole Foods. 

This morning, I was torn between going to Wegmans or this store. Since I only needed a few items, I chose Giant due to its proximity. This decision turned out to be a big mistake. Contrary to previous experiences where I would see at least 3 or 4 people shopping around 5 a.m., this time it was just me. To add to the frustration, the entire store was sectioned off, making it impossible to access certain aisles and extremely challenging to reach the register.

In my desperation, I had to go under a rope just to get a can of soup. As a result, I faced a barrage of criticism from individuals who were supposedly cleaning the floors, although some were simply idling around. Adding insult to injury, even the nearest exit was blocked off. If the store management deemed it necessary to clean the floors, they should have temporarily closed the store for a few hours. It would have taken less time to complete my shopping at Wegmans, which is where I will exclusively shop from now on.

input: This place is a hidden gem.  It is located in a strip mall, but this restaurant is anything but a strip mall restaurant.   My husband took me here for my birthday and I was blown away with the whole experience.  It's a very modern, romantic atmosphere.  The food is excellent.  I was shocked by the Fois gras-amazing.  I had the prix fixe menu and I loved ordering 3 courses.  The short ribs were great, but I want to try something new next time.  The desserts were awesome.  I usually take caramel, but there was a caramel tart that was to die for.  Can't wait to go back!!!!
Help me polish this:
This place is truly a hidden gem, tucked away in a strip mall, but don't let its location fool you. This restaurant breaks all expectations of your typical strip mall eatery. My husband surprised me with a birthday dinner here, and I was absolutely blown away by the entire experience. The ambiance is both modern and romantic, setting the perfect mood for a special occasion. 

Now, let's talk about the food. It was truly excellent. I was pleasantly shocked by the superb Fois gras, it was simply amazing. Opting for the prix fixe menu, I had the pleasure of indulging in three courses. While the short ribs were undoubtedly delicious, I am eager to explore new dishes on my next visit. And let's not forget about the desserts - they were simply awesome. As a caramel lover myself, I typically lean towards that flavor, but their caramel tart was definitely the highlight that I can't stop raving about.

Without a doubt, I am eagerly anticipating my return to this wonderful establishment. I can't wait for the opportunity to explore more of their enticing menu and bask in the incredible dining experience once again!

input:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I rarely write reviews, but this honestly was one of the worst group dining experiences I've ever had. It was objectively a horrible experience, even without comparing it to the hype it receives, and ruined what was supposed to be a nice birthday dinner celebration. 

We had a group of 8 that had a reservation made well in advance. Short wait, but not too bad. Keep in mind, it seemed like a normal Friday night, but weren't super busy or at-capacity.

It was a birthday dinner, so I told the hostesses that it was her birthday, and asked if they could bring out something for her at the end of the meal, which was acknowledged. Pretty standard stuff, whether at a Applebee's or the French Laundry. We were sat at a booth right next to the Maitre D' stand, and next to all the wait staff's home base, so pretty much no excuse for not getting any attention. 

After getting us waters, it took them a LONG time to even come by and acknowledge us. Didn't get one of the tables facing the windows, but still had great views of the sunset and city by night. Again, multiple choices for the three courses, but I chose to start with the crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto [balls]. Main course was the Butcher's Filet (braised short rib + Steuben bean chili, potato/farm veg slaw and basil), which was quite heavy since there was also meat in the chili as well. The dazzling dessert to finish it off was the milk chocolate + hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel and coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. A bottle of wine for the table as well. Food was great, waiter was awesome (making sure to warn me that the risotto came in ball form rather than a bowl, for instance), very classy experience.

Our second stop for Center City Restaurant Week was R2L, a luxurious restaurant/lounge located on the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place. This elegant establishment offers a breathtaking bird's eye view of the city. After a long day of meetings, our group decided to dine here together. Although we weren't seated at one of the tables facing the windows, we still enjoyed magnificent views of the sunset and the city at night. 

The three-course menu provided numerous options, and for my starter, I opted for the delightful crisp peas and ham garlic risotto balls. For the main course, I indulged in the Butcher's Filet, which consisted of braised short rib, Steuben bean chili, potato and farm vegetable slaw, and basil. The dish was quite substantial due to the addition of meat in the chili. To top off the extraordinary dining experience, I savored the mouthwatering milk chocolate and hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel, coffee to melt the chocolate, and accompanied by candied almonds on the side. To complement our meal, we also enjoyed a bottle of wine shared among the table. The food was exceptional, and our waiter was outstanding, even taking the time to inform me about the unique presentation of the risotto balls. input:
I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago.  Everybody here raves about the restaurants, but I have yet to find many that deserve five stars, or even four.  This is the best restaurant I have eaten in in Philadelphia.  

Tahini and bread  arrived at the table, and I thought, hum, plain but I'm hungry.  They must put crack in that Tahini.  I wanted to lap it out of the bowl like an uncouth dog.  The bread is excellent too.

I love a menu with many organic meat choices.  How often can you order an organic beef shishkabob?  It was superb.  The meat done perfectly, the onions nearly caramelized but not quite so they still had some substantive crunch.  The purslane salad tasted like I was eating a plant in the middle of a garden.  It is not often that I dream about a salad but I do dream about this one

My husband had a chicken dish with black eyed peas and green peas and fantastic rice.  I won't begin to describe the flavoring; it is beyond my culinary vocabulary.  We asked what spices they use, and in addition to traditional zatar, they use their own blend of spices.  I don't even need to know what is in it just so long as we can keep coming back and ordering it again and again.

I was so full but ate dessert none the less, which I usually don't do.  But when a diner is this good, I had a feeling the desserts would be too and I just needed to find out.  Pistachio creme brulee.  It could have come out over the top, but no indeed.  It was pure pistachio heaven in s super light yet rich custard.  Heaven. Heaven.

Our service was superb.  The squeezed us into a last minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to get through our dinner in an hour and 15 minutes in order to accommodate a reservation made prior to us.  Given the time constraints they never made us feel rushed and timed the meal perfectly.  Then my husband left to go to the restroom, the waiter picked up his napkin and refolded it nicely on the table.  Do I care about the napkin placement in the middle of a meal?  Not really, but it is a sign that the waitstaff is incredibly attentive and extremely well trained.  

My eating out plan for Philly might just be to skip eating most everywhere most of the time so I can frequent this expensive, though appropriately priced restaurant.  Kudos to the chef.

I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia more than a year ago, and while everyone here raves about the restaurants, I haven't come across many that I believe deserve five stars, or even four. However, I can confidently say that this place is the best restaurant I have eaten at in Philadelphia.

As soon as tahini and bread were brought to the table, I thought they appeared plain, but my hunger took over. Little did I know, that tahini had some sort of addictive quality to it. I had an urge to slurp it out of the bowl like an uncouth dog. The bread was also exceptional, adding to the entire experience.

One thing I adore about this restaurant is their extensive selection of organic meat options. How often do you come across a place where you can order an organic beef shishkabob? The dish was outstanding, with the meat cooked to perfection and the onions almost caramelized, yet still maintaining a satisfying crunch. The purslane salad tasted as if I was consuming fresh greens straight from a garden. It's not often that I dream about a salad, but this one has managed to invade my dreams.

My husband opted for a chicken dish that was accompanied by black-eyed peas, green peas, and a phenomenal rice. Describing the flavors would be impossible for me; they transcend my culinary vocabulary. When we asked about the spices used, we discovered they incorporate a blend of their own in addition to the traditional zaatar. I don't even need to know the specific ingredients – as long as we can keep coming back and ordering it repeatedly, I'm content.

Despite feeling incredibly full, I couldn't resist trying their desserts, something I rarely do. However, this exceptional dining experience had me convinced that their desserts wouldn't disappoint. And I was right. The pistachio creme brulee was heavenly. It had the potential to be overwhelming, but instead, it delivered a delicate, pistachio-infused custard that was both light and indulgent. Pure bliss.

The service we received was superb. We managed to secure a last-minute Friday night reservation, with the condition that we would need to finish our dinner within an hour and fifteen minutes in order to accommodate a prior reservation. Despite the time constraints, we were never made to feel rushed, and our meal was perfectly paced. When my husband excused himself to use the restroom, the waiter even took the time to refold his napkin neatly on the table. While I don't particularly care about napkin placement in the middle of a meal, it speaks volumes about the attentiveness and exceptional training of the waitstaff.

Considering my experience, I think my dining plan for Philadelphia might just involve skipping out on most other establishments in order to frequent this expensive, yet appropriately priced restaurant. A big kudos to the talented chef who has created such an extraordinary culinary experience.

input:
I love trying fresh seafood on piers, wharfs and seaside markets. Most of the time, it is a disappointing experience but this place is not. The food is legitimately fresh and prepared well. The gorgeous view is just a cherry on top of nature's beautiful sundae. I have been here before but ordered the "wrong" thing (cioppino). That wasn't very good when I had it a couple of years ago here. 

We came for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4pm,  there was a wait! We waited about 25 minutes and got a table outdoor. While it wasn't ideal that we sat right in the sun with no shelter other than our sunscreen and sunglasses, the view was worth it. 

We got the local crab special which was a steamed 3-lb. crab served with a salad and soup for $26. I thought this was quite the steal because the crab was huge, delicious and meaty. The garden salad was fresh as simple as it was. The lobster bisque we got was pretty good. (The other options were Caesar salad and clam chowder). They topped off the crab with a couple of onion rings and cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Yum!

We also got the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari and scallops for $12.95. It came with cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce and cocktail sauce. As greasy of a meal as this made, it was one of the better fried platters I've had anywhere. The seafood was just really fresh including the sometimes-feared fried oyster. :)

The ice in our iced teas melted away in the sun. Our waitress was so cool and brought us lots of extra ice and an extra iced tea in case we needed it (we did because it was hot out!). She was just friendly and good at her job - five stars for her!

By the time we left at about 6, there were so many people waiting. Make sure you sign up for a seat on the clipboard right when you get there. The restaurant is the last one at the very end of the pier. Parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes but it looks like a drive that will upset tires. I parked in the large lot south of the pier and walked 15 minutes up and onto the pier. It was free on a Monday late afternoon.

input:
I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday.

Arrival: I already read plenty of reviews about no signs marking the location therefore, I looked for Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi business complex. I went inside to find a guard at a desk that said we have been contracted to hand guests their keys and room number and nothing more. He advised me there was a phone that was on the wall that I could make a call to someone if I needed to. He also stated that the very few parking spots in front were free* only on the weekend.

The Room: This wasn't a room, this was an apartment and I absolutely loved it. It was very spacious and had everything I sought* after for that weekend, such as: fully stocked kitchen, a desk, lots of space, king bed, huge table, nice living room, lots of closets. My only complaint is that I could not open any windows for fresh air...they are nailed/screwed shut. There was also a small welcome bag w cookies and water and papers letting you know where all the food delivery locations and numbers.
There wasn't maid service knocking loudly or trying to barge in early in the morning. This place is more of a long term setting and I'm sure the maids come around during the week Monday-Friday if you desire. I was only here for 3 days and I was fine with that. I went shopping at Shoprite and filled my fridge with water and breakfast to cook.

Overall: This place is awesome, I had a huge living room to entertain my guests when they visited, and a nice desk to study my Anatomy notes. I forgot to mention how quiet** this place is. I loved it. I felt as if no one was there except me. Very quiet* which worked for me on Sunday bc I had lots of studying to do and two TV's to watch The Walking Dead on. Lol!  I would most definitely stay here again. Very spacious and updated. Loved it!

input: I had the worst experience of my life and it's not over yet.  I made a mistake in purchasing a vehicle that is out of my budget on a Friday afternoon. He stated he would speak with his manager and call me back.  At 3:30 after no return call, I called him again, no answer. I left a voicemail and still no call at closing time.  Monday morning I arrived at the dealership as they were opening.  I asked Stephen, the salesman what they determined.  He instructed me to have a seat and he would talk to his management team.  One hour + later, I was called into a cubicle and told my loan had been funded and the title had been changed.  Therefore, I would have to sell the car back to the dealership as a used car.  I would lose a lot of money in doing this.  This morning, Bill head of finance advised that the bank had questions about funding the loan.  I received a call from the bank stating the loan had NOT been funded and they would be unable to okay the loan.  I have left numerous messages with the dealership and have yet to receive a callback.  I contacted an attorney and per his review I again called the dealership and asked for a time to return the vehicle and take back my trade.  Still no response!  These people will lie to your face, avoid this dealership!!

Upon reviewing my finances on Sunday, I quickly realized that I couldn't afford the car. In a panic, I immediately called the salesman at 11:30am to explain my situation. He promised to speak with his manager and get back to me, but by 3:30pm, I hadn't received any response despite multiple attempts to reach him.

On Monday morning, I decided to go to the dealership as soon as they opened. I approached Stephen, the salesman, and inquired about the outcome of my situation. To sum it up, the way this dealership has handled my situation has been extremely deceitful. They have continuously lied to my face and have shown a complete disregard for customer care. I strongly advise against doing business with this dealership.

input:
I have been a patron of Desi Village in West Philly for years.  After moving the suburbs, we saw the KOP Desi Village and finally tried it.  We were skeptical having also tried Mood Cafe (owned by the W.Philly folks), and it wasn't as good. But the KOP location is actually very comparable to the West Philly location.  

There is no ambiance or atmosphere here.  The strip mall where it's located is pretty depressing.  Desi Village may be the only active store in it.  And its decor is tired and old.  It is a big space and it appears they do a big lunch buffet but I'm curious if it's ever full.  So don't go for the ambiance.

But the food is good.  We ordered some Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani.  All of it was really good.  Perfectly seasoned, not too oily, and appropriately spicy.  I have a nut allergy and made them aware of that and they did not screw it up (most Indian restaurants do).  So we'll definitely be back.  It would be great if they moved into nicer digs but the food is what is most important.

Admittedly, the strip mall where Desi Village is situated lacks ambiance and atmosphere, making it quite unappealing. It appears to be quite desolate, with Desi Village being the only active store. Therefore, if you are seeking a cozy or aesthetically pleasing dining experience, this may not be the best choice.

The flavors were perfectly balanced, with just the right amount of seasoning, minimal oiliness, and appropriate levels of spiciness. As someone with a nut allergy, I appreciate that they took my dietary restrictions seriously and ensured that there was no mix-up (something that unfortunately happens at many Indian restaurants). Despite the lackluster ambiance, the quality of food alone will make us frequent visitors. It would be wonderful if they could relocate to a more inviting space, but ultimately, it is the food that matters most.

What an AMAZING occurrence that we ended up here after another barbecue place ran out of food!

Super bummed and still in the mood for barbecue, we started wandering around Mid City and my trusty Yelp app guided me to this place. We were greeted by the super nice woman working the counter and she explained the whole process.

I decided to get the one-meat plate with "wet" pulled pork, grits and potato salad, I also got a medium mac and cheese, because I can. My boyfriend got the two-meat plate with brisket and pulled chicken with potato salad and fries. The food blew us both away! It was delicious from beginning to end. The pulled pork was perfect and had the perfect amount of sauce without being drenched. I could tell that if I hadn't ordered it wet it still would have been able to stand on it's own. The mac and cheese was incredible, and after the pork, was my favorite part of the meal. The stone ground grits had a different type of flavor (almost smoky) that I enjoyed and the potato salad was served cold and had that nice crunch that I like in potato salad,

We both agreed that the food was excellent, and a good deal to boot, and that we would both make the trip back out to Earhart, just to have more of this delicious food. The owner himself was bringing the food out to folks and he was really friendly and made sure that we were happy with everything. I like when the owners take the time to make sure that everything is okay. The atmosphere is casual and comfortable and the entire process was a breeze. I will definitely return to LA Smokehouse and I'll be adding it to my "BBQ Favorites" list for future reference.

input:
After today's lunch, Iris has moved to the top of my New Orleans favorites lists--no small feat in a city where restaurants are numerous and culinary competition is fierce. Iris excels in every area: food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music and overall graciousness. I made the reservation for 10-15 people, not knowing exactly how many in my party would show up. Iris pulled out all the stops to make sure everyone had comfortable seating and even prepared an overflow table for us. At no time did we feel jostled or rushed, which is a common fine dining concern. 

The layout of the restaurant allowed diners to move freely to and from the table and to exchange seats as needed. The music selection was fun and unique, ranging from the Magnetic Fields to Johnny Cash. It was also quiet enough to be enjoyed while allowing conversation to flow unimpeded. Our waiter had excellent timing and anticipated our every need. 

Though they don't have a full drink menu for lunch (I hear they have an amazing mixologist for the dinner hour) they do offer a selection of martinis and wines. One of the guests has accounts with several high-end bars in the Quarter, and the drink list passed his muster. Our table settled for Chardonnays, Perseco and chilled shots of Chartreuse, though I hear they have several types of absinthe as well. 

Our group began with slices of warm, heavenly bread that Iris bakes in house. We continued with an assortment of salads--I had the Hollygrove arugula with warm goat cheese, niçoise olives and balsamic vinaigrette. It was fresh perfection. A few of us opted for the mussels, which I heard were delicious. For my main course, I had a wonderful drum with onions prepared in a tangy soy reduction, which was an elegant complement for the fish. I also heard rave reviews about the gnocci and chicken. 

All the entrees were creatively arranged and selected, and at no point did I feel overwhelmed or that any fuss or pretense had gone into the food. I also appreciated that the portions were European-sized (it always makes me laugh when other Americans list too-small portion size as a complaint even when the food is well-prepared!). Iris prepares a lot of their basic ingredients in-house, and I appreciate that the kitchen makes a point of incorporating gulf fish and produce purchased from local, farmer-friendly markets. 

We settled on the prix fixe menu, which was $20 a person for appetizer, main course and the dessert of the day (the best strawberry sorbet I have had yet). With the added drinks and tip it came out to under $35 a person, which is an excellent price for such a delicious white-linen lunch. No matter the size of my group, I will definitely be returning!

input:
