input:
Awefull!!!! 
If I could give zero or negative stars I would!
I've never wrote a review before, but I am going out of my way to say that I had the absolute worst dining experience at the Sake House!! 
And esp families, stay clear! 
So first off, I decided to take my 15 month old son out on a sushi date. We arrive at the Sake House at 4pm. There is only one other table and they were closing out. We sit down, and I immediately ask for a simple ice water with lemon. Waiter comes back 20 minutes later (no water). I order a simple roll for my son, to get him started  and a cold Sake. I said I will wait to order mine to get him settled. Another 30 min later, still no water, no food. Waiter comes back with hot Sake, instead of cold. 20 minutes later, the roll for my son (not how I asked) finally some cold Sake, then I have to request water, and then only one cup for my son, no lemon. When I see 2 going on a third table had come in and ordered, and a "to go" order is being placed, all with food and water, I became perturbed. The waiter never came back to see what I wanted. Never came back to check on the order. Finally after  nearly 2 hours of waiting and trying to deal with my antsy son, who waited so long to be served, and seeing one chef trying to make everyone's order I decided it was time to go. Finally after waiting another 5/10 minutes I had to walk up and ask for my check , which was only a $6 drink. Which I reluctantly paid. After being in the hospitality industry for years, I know what to expect, and I know what to forgive. I also know that English being a second language must be tough...BUT since he was able to wait in other tables i know that wasn't the issue. After 2 hours of waiting, and dealing with a fussy/hungry toddler as a single mother I feel like the least they could have done is offer a free drink, to say "we understand we couldn't accommodate you, but we tried." It's principal above all else. ...I just waisted 2 hours! And had to leave and take my baby somewhere else. Time is money! And I waisted 2 hours here! 
Time that is rare and I had to plan being a busy mother.
I should have listened to the other reviews about the shitty service here. 
Don't waste your time or money!!!
Stay away! Any other place is better than here!
Help me polish this:
Terrible Experience at the Sake House - Stay Away!

I felt compelled to write this review after the absolutely dreadful dining experience I had at the Sake House. If I could give zero or negative stars, I definitely would. Families, especially, should steer clear of this place.

To start with, I decided to take my 15-month-old son out for a sushi date and arrived at the Sake House around 4pm. At that time, there was only one other table occupied, and they were wrapping up. We sat down and I immediately asked the waiter for a simple ice water with lemon. However, the waiter disappeared for 20 minutes and never brought me any water.

I proceeded to order a simple roll for my son and a cold Sake for myself, with the intention of ordering my own food later once my son was settled. Another 30 minutes passed, and we still had no water or food. When the waiter eventually returned, he brought me a hot Sake instead of the cold one I had requested. Finally, after 20 more minutes, my son's roll arrived (not as I had asked), and only then did I receive the cold Sake. I had to request water again, and they only brought one cup for my son without any lemon.

It was infuriating to see two, and then a third, table come in after us and place their orders, all while they received their food and water promptly. The waiter never returned to see if I wanted to order my food or even checked on our order. After waiting nearly two hours, trying to keep my antsy son calm, and witnessing only one chef struggling to prepare everyone's orders, I couldn't take it anymore. I decided it was time to leave.

To make matters worse, I had to wait another 5-10 minutes just to request my bill, which was only for a $6 drink. Reluctantly, I paid it. Having worked in the hospitality industry for many years, I understand what to expect and what can be forgiven. I also understand that English being a second language can be difficult, but since the waiter managed to attend to other tables, I knew that wasn't the issue.

After waiting for two hours and dealing with a hungry and fussy toddler as a single mother, I believe the least they could have done was to offer a complimentary drink as a token of goodwill, acknowledging that they couldn't accommodate us properly. It's a matter of principle above all else. I wasted two precious hours here and ultimately had to go somewhere else with my baby. Time is money, and I wasted valuable time that I carefully planned as a busy mother.

I should have heeded the warnings from other reviews about the abysmal service at this place. Save yourself the trouble and avoid wasting your time and money here. Any other place would be a better choice.

input:
The only good part.... 

Their stage is really cool! Raised up, lights that move around, good sound system, a fog machine, and a pretty big dance floor. 


But their food service.... crappy both times Ive been there. 

The last time I was there I walked in, hadn't been greeted by anyone at the empty front podium, and just found a table. I figured once I sat down Id wait for an employee to get back to the menus and go up and ask for one. So I saw a lady working up at the front and went up and asked her.  She said that they stopped serving food at...... I cant remember if it was 9 or 10 pm.... but she gave me a certain time that the kitchen closed. I went back to my table and looked at the time. It was 10 minutes before the time she told me the kitchen closed. I thought that was kinda dumb, but oh well.... maybe they stopped taking orders 10 minutes ahead or something. The next thing I see the SAME EXACT LADY seat four people RIGHT NEXT to our table and give them menus. Then she takes their order, and brings out their food. All I wanted were some freakin french fries and I had to sit there and watch the people who got there long after me eating french fries instead. RUDE!
Help me polish this:
The only positive aspect of the place is their impressive stage setup. It's raised up, complete with moving lights, a top-notch sound system, a fog machine, and a spacious dance floor.
 
However, I can't say the same for their food service. On both occasions that I've been there, it was disappointingly subpar.

During my last visit, I walked in and found the front podium empty, without anyone acknowledging my presence. I decided to find a table and wait for a staff member to provide me with a menu. After spotting a lady working at the front, I approached her and politely asked for a menu. To my surprise, she informed me that the kitchen had stopped serving food at a certain time, which I can't recall if it was 9 or 10 pm. I glanced at the time and realized that it was only 10 minutes before the time she mentioned. I couldn't help but find this policy rather absurd and frustrating. However, my frustration reached its peak when I witnessed the same lady seating and serving four people right beside our table, offering them menus, taking their orders, and ultimately delivering their food. All I wanted was a simple order of French fries, but instead, I had to endure the sight of people who arrived well after me enjoying their fries while I sat there feeling overlooked and disrespected. Absolutely rude!

input:
Would it be weird if I wanted to move in and permanently live here!? The style of this salon is impeccable. The color palette and decor they chose makes it feel like you're in a Restoration Hardware magazine...in France...surrounded by heirloom antiques. I didn't know what to expect when arriving but I was pleasantly surprised with their upscale polish options like Chanel and many others I actually didn't know I needed in my life until I arrived. 
Service was prompt and I especially enjoyed the extended massage. Most importantly the tools she used were brand new/ had been sterilized. I watched her open the fresh package up, that made me feel good about cleanliness and safety. I don't know if all nail salons have cute gold tips on their nail trimmer tools but now I want them for my own collection. 

I picked a gray color for my toes and did OPI Funny Bunny gel on my nails. So far I'm loving both! 
So nice to see a high end nail salon finally making its way to Nashville. I've gone to others in Nashville that seem to be high end, but it just ends up like a VIP club on the Vegas strip with loud music and sparkles just waiting for a Justin Bieber song to come on. 
CURED was not only high end, but it was classic. Like The Hamptons type of classic but with a comfortable low key brunch with girlfriends mimosa type of vibe. I think it would be amazing for a bridal party with so many photo opportunities. I felt comfortable with their prices, competitive to anywhere else I've gone in Nashville worth mentioning. 

I didn't know where to park so I parked on the side in a random parking lot. Looks like there's a lot of up and coming businesses beside them under construction. So I'm assuming once those are complete, parking will be pretty straight forward? 

When my Mom & Sister come into town next I'm going to take them here & go to Local Honey for lunch since it's so close. 

Can't wait to go back. Welcome to the neighborhood!
Help me polish this:
Would it be strange if I expressed my desire to move in and permanently reside here? The aesthetic of this salon is absolutely flawless. The choice of color palette and decor gives off a vibe of being in a Restoration Hardware magazine...in France...surrounded by exquisite heirloom antiques. I didn't have any expectations upon arriving, but I was pleasantly surprised by their upscale polish options, including Chanel and other brands that I didn't know I needed in my life until now.

I witnessed the technician opening a fresh package, which reassured me about the salon's commitment to maintaining a safe and hygienic environment. I'm not sure if all nail salons have cute gold tips on their nail trimmers, but now I absolutely need them for my personal collection.

For my nails, I opted for a sophisticated gray color on my toes and OPI Funny Bunny gel on my nails. I am already loving both choices!

It's truly refreshing to see a high-end salon like this emerge in Nashville. I have visited other supposedly upscale salons in the area, but they felt more like a VIP club on the Vegas strip with loud music and excessive glitter, waiting for a Justin Bieber song to play. CURED, on the other hand, exudes a timeless elegance reminiscent of The Hamptons, combined with a comfortable and relaxed atmosphere perfect for a leisurely brunch with friends, complete with mimosas. I can imagine it would be an ideal venue for a bridal party with numerous photo opportunities. The pricing is also reasonable and competitive compared to other nail salons worth mentioning in Nashville.

Parking was a bit confusing for me as I ended up parking in a random lot on the side. However, it seems that there are many upcoming businesses under construction nearby, so once they are completed, I anticipate parking will become more straightforward.

When my mom and sister visit town next, I am definitely bringing them here and then treating them to lunch at Local Honey since it's conveniently close by.

I cannot wait to return to this salon. Welcome to the neighborhood!

input: This has fast become one of my favorite New Orleans gems! The path stretches about a 1.25 miles from close to Elysian Fields over to the area near the old Navy installation. Along the way are various art installations, a dog park, and a wonderful walk along the mighty Mississippi River. If you time it just right, you might catch one of the spectacular sunsets. A beautiful way to end any day in NOLA!
Help me polish this:

If you time your visit just right, you might even be lucky enough to witness one of the most spectacular sunsets you'll ever see. It truly is a picturesque way to end any day spent exploring the vibrant city of NOLA.

The only minor hiccup was with the bathroom door lock and handle, which were initially confusing to use. Nonetheless, this didn't overshadow the positive aspects of our visit.

Overall, I would highly recommend this place for a delightful lunch experience.

input:
4-5 stars, this is just after one visit so far, worth a try if you're a thai fan. I liked the food, but you always have to have the first visit to see "how they do things" and figure out what your preferences will need to be.

I did use their living social deal so I brought my dad in when he came in from out of town to try it out with me. I like the set up, the quaint house is cute (and well, quaint), but I can see how it wouldn't be ideal it if was jam packed. I imagine you could potentially do family style for some of the pub height tabletops. I did call ahead to make sure that I didn't need to print out the coupon and it could be used from my ipod and to make sure they were open, as the website said to just double check.

We started with shrimp spring rolls, probably the best I've had, the ingredients seemed fresher, and crispier. No shredded lettuce here. Simple and loosely wrapped, but you could taste the individual components. The peanut sauce was tasty too, though they don't have sirracha (spelling?) to add to it, just dried pepper flakes. 

We then got the tom yum (gai?) with shrimp. I know it is hot (because of the name, duh), I usually prefer it a little less spicy (I am white), though I still got a good sour flavor (for instance at Thai chili it's too hot for me, I don't taste any sour). I usually get my tom yum without meat or seafood because I feel the meat gets dried out, but the server assured me the shrimp wouldn't be overcooked, and they weren't. I think they are making sure to use fresh ingredients, but I do prefer straw mushrooms (I think they are usually canned) over the button mushrooms they used. Next time I am probably going to try out a veggie version (i love the soup with the cabbage, and broccoli). The owner did tell me they are trying to be authentic and so maybe button mushrooms and less veggies is more authentic?

We then got shrimp pad thai and chicken pad keo mao (drunken noodle) minus the red pepper. Both were tasty, the portions were probably a little less than other places in Reno (not sure if just lunch sized portion now that I think about it).

Like Ernie said, the pad thai noodles were a little soft, overdone, and its not the 'orange-y' sauce like other pad thai's, but there was still flavor there. The shrimp were also tasty in this dish. The drunken noodles was done exactly how I like them, lots of baby corns and the noodles covered in the sauce and of course spicy. 

My dad and I talked outside for a while and the husband did come out and talk with me about the food, and asked if I was happy (we were outside a while). I hope the living social deals bring in some business, and I do plan on coming back, it is just hard because I don't live in the area. I also asked about the cooking classes (they are a steal at $65), and on facebook it said they are looking to improve and give some focus to that side of the business. The owner did say that they use just a regular kitchen so no woks or anything like that (meaning what they teach us can actually be done at home), I wonder if that is why the pad thai noodles are that way? Regardless, they seem to pride themselves on authentic and quality food and service.

I did include pictures. Oh I did try a thai iced tea for the first time too, pretty tasty, reminded me of chai tea. 

I didn't get to see the bill closely, but it was $24 and some change after the living social deal (takes $20 off), I didn't think that was too bad for 2 for lunch (the total cost), with an appetizer and soup and a drink.
Help me polish this:
Rating: 4-5 stars

After just one visit, I would highly recommend trying this restaurant if you're a fan of Thai cuisine. The food was delightful, but it's important to have the first visit to understand their unique approach and discover your personal preferences.

I took advantage of their Living Social deal and brought my dad along when he visited from out of town. The cozy and quaint house setup added to the charm, although it may not be ideal if it gets overcrowded. For larger groups, they do offer family-style dining options with pub height tabletops. Prior to visiting, I called ahead to confirm that the coupon could be redeemed from my iPod and to check their operating hours, as indicated on their website.

To start, we ordered the shrimp spring rolls, which were hands down the best I've ever had. The freshness and crispiness of the ingredients were apparent, and the rolls were delicately wrapped, allowing the flavors to come through. The accompanying peanut sauce was flavorful, although unfortunately, they didn't have sriracha available, only dried pepper flakes.

Next, we tried the tom yum soup with shrimp. While it lived up to its spiciness (as implied by the name), it had a good balance of tanginess. As someone who prefers milder flavors, I found it a bit too spicy for my taste, although I appreciated the bold sourness. At other Thai restaurants I've been to, such as Thai Chili, the heat tends to overpower the sourness. Despite my usual preference of having the soup without meat or seafood to avoid dryness, our server assured us that the shrimp wouldn't be overcooked, and they truly weren't. The restaurant is clearly dedicated to using fresh ingredients, but I personally prefer straw mushrooms (typically canned) over the button mushrooms they used. Perhaps on my next visit, I will try the vegetarian version with cabbage and broccoli, as I particularly enjoy those additions. The owner mentioned that they strive for authenticity, and it seems that using button mushrooms and fewer vegetables may align with that vision.

For our main courses, we ordered the shrimp pad Thai and the chicken pad keo mao (drunken noodles) without red pepper. Both dishes were delicious, though the portions appeared slightly smaller compared to other places in Reno (it could have been the lunch-sized portion).

As Ernie mentioned, the pad Thai noodles were slightly overcooked and lacked the characteristic orange sauce that other pad Thai dishes have. Regardless, there was still great flavor, and the shrimp was cooked perfectly. The drunken noodles, on the other hand, were exactly how I like them, with plenty of baby corn and a satisfying level of spiciness.

My dad and I spent some time chatting outside after the meal, during which the husband came out and engaged with us about the food, ensuring our satisfaction. I hope the Living Social deal attracts more customers, as I plan on returning myself, despite not being a local resident. I also inquired about their cooking classes, which seemed like a fantastic value at $65. Their Facebook page mentioned their intent to enhance that aspect of their business, and the owner informed me that they teach cooking in a regular kitchen setup, making it practical to replicate the recipes at home. I wonder if this approach explains the texture of the pad Thai noodles? Nevertheless, their commitment to authentic and high-quality food, as well as exceptional service, remains evident.

I included some pictures in my review, and I must mention that I also tried a Thai iced tea for the first time, which was surprisingly delicious and reminiscent of chai tea.

I didn't closely examine the bill, but after subtracting the $20 discount from the Living Social deal, the total came to around $24. Considering we had an appetizer, soup, drink, and two main courses for two people, I found this to be quite reasonable for a lunch outing.

input:
Yes, it's a little pricey, but it was darned near worth it. 
It certainly didn't seem a priority to get us our menus, but once they did, the service was pretty on point. The bread was good. I ordered a chopped salad and a crab cake, and the hub got a crab cake sandwich with fries. We had water to drink, no appetizers-walked out for $45 with tip. The food came quickly.  My food was great-and I'm no salad eater. The crab cake was quality, fries were good. 
Another drawback is that we had to sit in the bar area bc it was after 9. The table was the size of a chair, 3 plates were too much.

P.S. i used my bank card, and noticed that I was charged significantly more than I agreed to, so I called the restaurant. The manager said it's a banking glitch, and should correct itself before the money comes out of my account... It better.
Help me polish this:
Yes, it was a bit pricey, but it was nearly worth every penny. Admittedly, the staff didn't prioritize serving us our menus promptly, but once they did, the service was commendable. The bread was delicious. For our main courses, I opted for a chopped salad and a crab cake, while my partner chose a crab cake sandwich with fries. We only had water to drink and skipped appetizers, yet the bill still amounted to $45 with tip. Despite that, our food arrived promptly. To my surprise, the salad exceeded my expectations - and I'm not a huge fan of salads. The crab cake was undeniably of top-notch quality, and the fries were quite good too.

One downside worth mentioning is that we were seated in the bar area due to it being past 9. The table we were assigned was incredibly small, barely enough space to accommodate three plates.

On a side note, I paid with my bank card and noticed that I had been charged significantly more than the agreed-upon amount. Concerned, I immediately contacted the restaurant and spoke with the manager. According to them, it was attributed to a banking glitch and assured me that the discrepancy would resolve itself before the funds were deducted from my account. I sincerely hope they are right.

input:

input:
i enjoyed the experience eating here and will definitely go back.

first of all, there are vegetarian options on the menu. we started with the veggie spring rolls which were hot, crisp, and delicious. my husband had the duck and rice vermicelli soup which we both agreed was great in a yummy, savory broth. i had the beef pho which i didn't care for because the meat was a bit grisly and i'm not a fan of tripe. i've not eaten a lot of pho and wasn't sure what to order, though. they offer several different beef cuts and i should have picked a different one. next time. also, the regular serving size was way more than enough. i don't think either of us could have come close to finishing the largest bowls.

the restaurant was clean and quiet with a sparse, yet very 80s decor. the server was quick and attentive.
Help me polish this:
I thoroughly enjoyed my experience dining here and I am eager to return. Firstly, I was pleased to find that they offer vegetarian options on their menu. To start, we ordered the veggie spring rolls which were served hot, crispy, and packed with delicious flavors. My husband opted for the duck and rice vermicelli soup, and we both agreed that the savory broth added a delightful touch to his dish.

input:
3.5 stars.

I appreciate the sound booth in the sky, as it means that (admittedly bad) music is played during the commercials, along with special themes for Eagles fans. And, the place seems to be smoke free.

But, I am not impressed by the famous crab fries, which are crinkled, lightly fried, and seasoned with garlic, chili pepper, and salt. Something about the congealed cheese sauce detracts from the entire experience, and I also prefer my fries to be piping hot. However, there are towers of beer available (complete with taps), which is pleasantly tacky. 

With loads of space, booming sound, cute servers, and rowdy fans, Chickie's and Pete's is a perfect place to catch a game.

On a positive note, the towers of beer available, complete with taps, add a fun and slightly kitschy element to the bar.

input:
A quasi political rant and a store review all wrapped in one, so enjoy. 

Ever since Target hit the scene I really have to ask, "Who even goes to Kmart anymore?" I asked this to myself out loud the other day as I had to get my meds filled due to a sinus infection. No one looked at me odd, as there seemed to be several people talking to themselves. I now go here because of the stolid contractual war between Express Scripts and Walgreens. Thanks you two....idiots.....qausi-political rant over.

This store is harshly bright, rather dingy, and the selections, especially in the electronic section, are on the cheaper end.  On top of that, I've found the mainstream DVD and Blu-Ray movies are overpriced.  I laughed at the men's area, especially the young man's department, as they had a tv with music videos playing. I laughed because it just seemed a lame attempt to be cool and creating a shopping experience that you will find at a department store like Macy's or Dillard's. This is hard to create when everything is whitewashed. You will feel like you are in that August Burns Red's "Whitewashed."  The best WTF moment is discovering the opportunity to purchase Joe Boxer male thongs. Who knew that Kmart cared about male panty line?

One great tip is you can find patio furniture cheap during the off season and clearance days. I bought a great patio table for under $50. So, keep that in mind.

The extra star is for the pharmacy, as they filled my prescription out efficiently and with the greatest of ease. The hours are little later than Target.  No problems there and credit when credit is due!

The later 80s quote, "K-Mart sucks", remains as true as ever and who knows, you may even bump into someone who still dresses from that Tom Cruise era who cares about male panty line. One never knows?
Help me polish this:
Since the debut of Target, I often wonder why anyone still goes to Kmart. This thought crossed my mind recently while I needed to fill a prescription for a sinus infection. Interestingly, nobody gave me a strange look for talking to myself, as it appeared that several people were engaged in self-conversations. It's all thanks to the obnoxious dispute between Express Scripts and Walgreens that I find myself patronizing this place now. Thank you, idiots. Quasi-political rant concluded.

The store itself is glaringly bright, somewhat rundown, and offers products that lean towards the cheaper end, especially in the electronics section. Moreover, the prices for mainstream DVD and Blu-Ray movies are exorbitant. I couldn't help but laugh at the men's department, particularly the young men's section, where they had a television playing music videos. This feeble attempt to create a "cool" shopping experience reminiscent of Macy's or Dillard's seemed laughable to me, especially when everything is so bland and unwelcoming. It feels like being trapped in August Burns Red's "Whitewashed" music video. However, I must admit, stumbling upon Joe Boxer male thongs on their shelves was a definite "WTF" moment. Who knew Kmart cared about male panty lines?

One notable tip: you can score affordable patio furniture during the off-season and clearance events. I managed to purchase a fantastic patio table for under $50. So, bear that in mind.

I'll give an extra star to the pharmacy, which efficiently and effortlessly filled my prescription. Their operating hours are a bit more convenient than Target's. Credit is due where credit is deserved.

The quote from the late 80s, "K-Mart sucks," remains as accurate as ever. Who knows, you might even run into someone still donning fashion from the Tom Cruise era who happens to be concerned about male panty lines. Anything is possible, I suppose.

input:

input:

input:
Despite it's great reviews by other Yelpers, I was not that blown away by Nippon Tei. 

My roommate and I were craving sushi and were recommended to come here by Yelp and a friend so we decided to give it a shot. 

First off, they get bonus points for serving FREE edemame as an appetizer. I usually pay $4 to $5 for it at other sushi restaurants. The mango sake drink I have was alright, but not worth the price I paid for it. 

On to the main event...SUSHI! We had the philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and california roll. They were all yummy, but I would have to say I have had better. Actually, out of the hand-full of sushi restaurants I have tried, this was the worst sushi I have tried, but I cannot say the sushi was bad by any means. Don't get me wrong, it was still tasty. 

The other big thing was that the rolls were actually falling apart. I have never had this happen. Therefore, I can say that the presentation and the ability to get the sushi from the plate to my mouth without falling apart did make me unhappy. 

I am willing to come back to Nippon Tei, but I have to say I already have my other favorites. The prices were average compared to other sushi bars, so that won't really help them out either when it comes to bringing me back. We will see!
Help me polish this:
Although Nippon Tei has received rave reviews from other Yelpers, it unfortunately did not meet my expectations. Highly recommended by both Yelp and a friend, my roommate and I decided to give it a try as we were craving sushi.

To start off on a positive note, I must commend them for graciously serving complimentary edamame as an appetizer. Other sushi restaurants typically charge $4 to $5 for this dish. However, I was not fully satisfied with my mango sake drink, as I felt that it was not worth the price I paid.

Now, onto the main event - the sushi. We ordered the philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and california roll. While they were enjoyable, I have to admit that I have had better sushi elsewhere. In fact, among the handful of sushi restaurants I have tried, Nippon Tei unfortunately falls at the bottom of the list. That being said, I cannot label the sushi as bad in any sense; it was still flavorful.

One major disappointment was that the rolls were prone to falling apart. This is something I have never experienced before, and it did affect my overall satisfaction with the meal. The presentation and ability to enjoy the sushi without it unraveling did detract from my dining experience.

Although I am open to revisiting Nippon Tei in the future, I can confidently say that I already have my preferred go-to sushi spots. Additionally, the average pricing of the restaurant compared to other sushi bars does not significantly incentivize me to return. Only time will tell if I give it another chance.

input: Went to see Star Wars Rogue One yesterday in 3D.  Buying the tickets was a breeze, and the atmosphere was inviting.  Found the comfortable seats with no problem and ordered right away before the movie began.  I ordered pretzel sticks - food was hot, prompt & delicious.  I was excited for the movie to begin.  Once the advertisements were done and the movie started, that's when I noticed something wasn't right.  The entire screen was so dark that I was not able to make out the faces of the actors on the screen.  I kept lifting up the 3D glasses to see if it made a difference - nope.  The two people seated next to me were noticing the same and complaining.  I thought that maybe this is how the movie was filmed?  Then it got worse.  Even with the 3D glasses on, the shadows in the background on the screen were double and there was no discerning most actors' faces at all.  I got up and went to the lobby and asked for the manager.  The gentleman wore a blue shirt, middle age with a beard, said that this was the 3D experience, it was a "closed-system" and there was nothing he could do.  I simply asked him to come with me into the theater to see with his own eyes how dark it was.  He would not and did not.  I suspect this wasn't the first time he's heard this from a customer.  I've seen normal movies at this location before, but this was my first, and last experience with their 3D in room #1.
Help me polish this:
Yesterday, I went to see Star Wars Rogue One in 3D and overall, the ticket purchasing process was smooth. The inviting atmosphere of the theater instantly set the mood for an enjoyable experience. I easily found comfortable seats and promptly placed my order for pretzel sticks, which turned out to be hot, delicious, and served without delay. Excitement filled the air as the movie was about to begin.

However, as the advertisements ended and the movie commenced, I couldn't help but notice a glaring issue. The entire screen appeared excessively dark, making it impossible to discern the faces of the talented actors. I repeatedly lifted my 3D glasses to see if they were the cause, only to find that the problem persisted. To my dismay, the two individuals seated next to me shared the same observation and were also complaining about it. In an attempt to rationalize the situation, I wondered if this was an intentional artistic choice by the filmmakers.

Unfortunately, matters only worsened when the shadows in the background of the screen became doubled, rendering most actors' faces indistinguishable despite the 3D glasses. Frustration grew within me, prompting me to take action. I decided to step out and approach the lobby to speak with the manager. 

Upon encountering the manager, I noticed he possessed a middle-aged appearance and sported a beard, clad in a blue shirt. Expressing my concerns, I implored him to accompany me inside the theater to observe the darkness firsthand. Regrettably, he declined my request, citing that this was how the 3D experience was intended to be, referring to it as a "closed-system." Feeling disappointed, I simply wished for him to witness the issue directly, realizing that this may not have been the first time he had encountered such complaints. Although I had watched regular movies at this particular location previously, this incident marked my inaugural and final encounter with their 3D theater, specifically room #1.

input: Overpriced for average food served warm (not hot) by servers who had trouble saying the names of the dishes and seemed in a rush to give us our bill when the place was more than half empty (on a Saturday night). When one of the servers came over to check on the $23 pork chop (which was not listed in the menu - $18 price was), my spouse commented there was a lot of fat....she seemed baffled by his comment, then walked away! Help me polish this: The prices were overly expensive considering the average quality of the food, which was served lukewarm instead of hot. Additionally, the servers had difficulty pronouncing the dish names and appeared rushed to bring us the bill even though the restaurant was not busy on a Saturday night. When my spouse commented on the excessive fat in the $23 pork chop (which was not listed on the menu), the server seemed confused and walked away without addressing the issue. Although the "ropa vieja" dish was satisfactory, it was served in a small portion for its high price. Furthermore, the menu prices did not match the overall ambiance of the restaurant, with random plastic containers placed on a nearby table and a sagging knitted item hanging over our table, as if there should have been a lamp present.

input: Should have listened to other reviews--we were kind of disappointed.  The layout of the restaurant is interesting in that it's made to look sort of like the inside of a chicken coop (made for people).  However, the food was overpriced and underwhelming.  We ate from the Sunday brunch menu--only decent value on the menu is the chicken strips and fries.  My wife ordered the seasonal salad, which was comically small and was way short on the actual lettuce (and not cheap either).  Chicken was good, but nothing better than Raising Canes in my opinion.  Service and food seemed on the slow side, especially with the small crowd.
Help me polish this: I wish I had taken heed of the other reviews as our experience left much to be desired. While I found the layout of the restaurant intriguing, with its chicken coop-inspired design for human diners, the food was both disappointing and expensive. We opted for the Sunday brunch menu, and the only item that offered decent value was the chicken strips and fries. My wife decided to try the seasonal salad which turned out to be comically small and lacking in lettuce, despite its steep price. Although the chicken was satisfactory, it didn't surpass the quality of Raising Canes in my opinion. To make matters worse, both the service and food were noticeably slow, despite the small number of customers in the restaurant.

input:

input:

input: awesome place.  good food. nice people.  rotating specials.  all home made.  what else do you want?  Chicken salad is a great pickup to make sandwiches at home.

input: I'm rating this based on the service and not the food. I am a sales administrator at a hotel. Typically, many places offer a hospitality discount because we do refer guests different places. Front desk told me I should try this place as they give a decent discount. I called to place my order and wasn't really able to say what I liked b/c the girl who answered would cut me off to finish my statement.(she wasn't in the best mood) We get to the end of the order and she asks me am I a guest or an employee. I told her an employee. She asked my title. I told her. She gives me a total and I asked her about the discount. She says it's only for front desk. I'm shocked that this is a departmental thing 1 and 2 I'm thinking to myself, "I'm in sales. I get groups of people here. They ALWAYS asked for recommendations." I said well should I hang up and have front desk place my order? She huffed and puffed and then said "well i'll give it to you this time but please dont abuse it." I was so shocked at how rude she was. So when I finally got my food, I tipped the driver and gave him their menus back and said we will no longer be doing business with you guys. She didnt know SALES is in charge of who the front desk can recommend. Her name was Neisha.The food was good though.
Help me polish this:
I have based my rating solely on the service, not the food. As a sales administrator at a hotel, it is common for us to receive hospitality discounts from various establishments as we frequently refer guests to different places. The front desk recommended this particular place to me, mentioning that they offer a decent discount. 

When I called to place my order, I encountered some difficulties expressing my preferences as the girl who answered the phone kept interrupting me before I could finish my statement. She seemed to be in a rather bad mood. Despite that, we managed to reach the end of the order, at which point she asked if I was a guest or an employee. I honestly informed her that I was an employee and even mentioned my job title. As I inquired about the discount, I was surprised to learn that it was only applicable to the front desk. Firstly, I found it disappointing that this was limited to one department, and secondly, I couldn't help but think about my role in sales, where I frequently bring groups of people to this hotel who often ask for recommendations.

I asked if I should hang up and have the front desk place the order instead. She seemed irritated and reluctantly granted me the discount, cautioning me not to abuse it. I was taken aback by her rudeness. Consequently, after receiving the food, I tipped the driver and returned their menus, letting him know that we would no longer be doing business with their establishment. She seemed unaware that the sales department has the authority to determine which places the front desk recommends. Her name was Neisha. 

Despite the unpleasant service experience, I must admit that the food itself was enjoyable.

input: Always the sweetest ladies! Appointments never take forever and barely any wait time!
Help me polish this: Always the most delightful ladies to deal with! Appointments are never a hassle and there's hardly any wait time!

input: We won't be back. We got the Brussel sprouts and they tasted like pure salt. Our server sent them back and we got another batch and they tasted exactly the same. Help me polish this: We will not be returning to this restaurant. Our experience with the Brussel sprouts was extremely disappointing as they tasted overwhelmingly salty. Despite sending them back, the replacement batch had the same issue. Similarly, the fries that accompanied my husband's burger were also excessively salty. It seemed as though the cook for the night had a heavy hand with the salt. While the flank steak I ordered was decent, it did not impress me enough to warrant any future visits. On a positive note, our cocktails were enjoyable and the atmosphere of the restaurant was nice. Unfortunately, the overall disappointment with the food overshadowed these positives.

input: I love going to Phillies games sooo much and this stadium definitely adds to the experience. I was never a big baseball fan until about a couple of years ago, when my bf introduced me to the wonder that is the Phils- instant love. Sure,my first Phils game was the 10, 000 loss but whatever. The places has a open feeling, and never feels clausterphobic. The only time i've felt that I had bad seats was when we sat right under neath the scoreboard, and I had to keep on looking up.  I like how you can wander about and watch the game from the lower levels, and that despite it's a sold out game, it never feels cramped or you're really aching to get around the stadium. Go Phillies!
Help me polish this:
I absolutely adore going to Phillies games! The atmosphere at this stadium truly enhances the overall experience. It's funny how I wasn't a huge baseball fan until my boyfriend introduced me to the amazingness of the Phils a couple of years ago. It was love at first sight!

Sure, my initial game happened to be the 10,000th loss, but hey, no big deal. The stadium itself has this open and airy vibe, which prevents it from ever feeling claustrophobic. The only time I can recall feeling like I had less than ideal seats was when we sat directly beneath the scoreboard, and I found myself constantly looking up.

One of the things I really appreciate about this stadium is how you can wander around and catch glimpses of the game from the lower levels. Even during sold-out games, it never feels overcrowded or like you're desperately trying to navigate through the masses. Plus, they offer an abundance of delicious food options with great variety. And let's not forget about the cleanliness – the facilities are always on point and I never find myself waiting in long lines.

Baseball season is sorely missed, and I'm counting down the days until April! Go Phillies!

input: My boyfriend and I decided to stop by for lunch yesterday, and I am so glad we did. I ordered a side of beans, chips and salsa, and guacamole. He ordered two steak tacos and a side of rice. The beans are hands down my favorite I've had from a mexican restaurant.  My only complaint is that, unfortunately you do not get a very big portion. The salsa is so fresh tasting and delicious-very cilantro forward, and the chips were nice, thick and crunchy without being oily at all. Take note though, chips and salsa are not included with your purchase and must be bought separately. Now let me get to the best part-the made to order, chunky guacamole. The hardy chips would definitely withstand this heavy duty guac, but I opted instead for tortillas as my vessel to stuff it with along with my beans and salsa. The hot sauces were anything but, though admittedly my tolerance to spices may be higher than the average persons. While I had a great eating experience, my boyfriend did not. He said the meat was of low quality and quite flavorless. He did say he would give it another shot though!
Help me polish this:
My boyfriend and I spontaneously decided to grab lunch yesterday, and I'm so thankful for that decision. We had an amazing meal at the restaurant. I personally ordered a side of beans, along with some chips and salsa, and guacamole. On the other hand, my boyfriend went for two steak tacos and a side of rice. Without a doubt, the beans were absolutely phenomenal and the best I've had from any Mexican eatery. Though, my only slight complaint would be that the portion was a bit small. The salsa was incredibly fresh and had a delicious, prominent cilantro flavor. Moreover, the chips were thick and crunchy, providing a delightful texture without any excessive oiliness. It's worth noting, however, that the chips and salsa are not included with your order but must be purchased separately.

Now, let's talk about the highlight of the meal - the made to order, chunky guacamole. The sturdy chips would certainly hold up against this robust guac, but I decided to use tortillas as a vessel instead, along with some beans and salsa. As for the hot sauces, they were milder than expected, but I should disclose that I have a higher tolerance for spiciness than most people. In summary, I had a fantastic dining experience, though unfortunately, my boyfriend didn't share the same sentiment. He found the meat to be of low quality and lacking flavor. Nevertheless, he is willing to give it another chance in the future.

input: I love this place. It's been in La Cumbre Plaza for I don't know how long now. If you are looking for a good sandwich look no further. Help me polish this:

As a Santa Barbara native, being raised just down the street, I've been a loyal customer for many years. I've had the pleasure of trying more than half of their sandwiches, and each one has been exceptional. It's so difficult to choose a favorite because they are all that good.

I must also mention their incredible selection of sodas. It's absolutely fantastic! With every visit, I find myself unable to resist trying something different. While you won't find anything overly fancy or exotic, like a roasted duck pastrami sandwich, Plaza Deli is perfect for locals and those passing through who just want a fantastic sandwich made with fresh, top-notch ingredients. Swing by and grab a bite, you won't be disappointed!

input: A small aquarium that is interesting mainly for kids.  They have a shark feeding show and stingrays that you can pet and buy food to feed.  It is not the first place i would go in Tarpon Springa, but it is ok, small children seem to like it.
