input:
I visited Jake's for the first time after learning that the small diner I used to go to in Delaware as a kid had become a franchise. I was so excited to experience the delicious burgers and fries that I craved as a kid.

I walked into the establishment and was frankly unimpressed by the ambiance. The restaurant was moderately clean and very open. The menu actually reminded my of a Five Guys. You get to choose your own toppings (all free) to put on 1, 2, or 3 patties.

I ordered the regular cheeseburger with a ton of toppings and a regular size french fry to share with my boyfriend. The burgers were delicious. The bread was soft and tasty and the burgers were succulent and juicy. The fries were disappointing. McDonalds fries taste better and usually aren't even as cold as Jake's were.

Man oh man, Jake's. I'll go back for the burgers, maybe, but I definitely will stick to the original location for a better experience.
Help me polish this:
I was thrilled to finally visit Jake's after discovering that the small diner from my childhood in Delaware had expanded into a franchise. The thought of relishing the mouthwatering burgers and fries that I had longed for since my youth filled me with excitement.

Upon entering the establishment, I couldn't help but feel a twinge of disappointment regarding the ambiance. While the restaurant was reasonably clean and had an open layout, it lacked a certain charm. The menu reminded me somewhat of Five Guys, with the option to personalize your burger by choosing from a variety of toppings, all at no additional cost. 

Opting for the regular cheeseburger adorned with an abundance of toppings, and accompanied by a regular-sized serving of french fries to share with my boyfriend, I had high hopes. The burgers exceeded my expectations, with the soft and flavorful bread perfectly complementing the succulent and juicy meat patties. However, I found the fries to be underwhelming. Surprisingly, even McDonald's fries managed to surpass them in taste and temperature, as the ones at Jake's were disappointingly cold.

Though Jake's still holds a special place in my heart for its delectable burgers, I believe I will continue to frequent the original location for a more fulfilling overall experience.

input: This place was cute and was in a great location!  It is one block up from the beach and wharf, two blocks over from State Street.  Parking was convenient, and our room was a King overlooking the courtyard and spa on the ground floor.  If there were people in the spa, they could be heard, but the noise didn't bother since the spa closed at 9pm.  The room was clean with a nice couch to lounge on, a refrigerator, a nice fireplace, ample closet and counter space, and a nice bathroom.  The wine and cheese at 5 was a nice touch as well.  Although this place didn't have a lot of extras, it was a pleasant stay, friendly and helpful staff, a good price, perfect location, and suited our needs just fine for a place in Santa Barbara.  My only complaint was that the room got a little stuffy, but was fine once we opened the windows and used the ceiling fan to air it out.  Would consider staying here again.

While this place may not offer a plethora of extra amenities, it still provided us with a pleasant stay, thanks to the friendly and accommodating staff, reasonable price, perfect location, and overall suitability to our needs during our stay in Santa Barbara.

If I had to nitpick, my only complaint would be that the room tended to get a little stuffy. However, this was easily remedied by opening the windows and utilizing the ceiling fan to quickly air it out. Overall, I would definitely consider staying here again.

input:
I've been to Mirna's about four times over the past few years and never been disappointed. The portions are HUGE, especially for the modest price tag. Do yourself a favor and get a pasta dish, I can assure you that you'll be glad you did. I've had fish there too, which wasn't bad by any means, but the pasta plates are definitely their specialty. A couple of the times I've been there they treated us to free hummus and pita, which is always a plus. BYOB!

Only knock on the place is that it's pretty small, so make sure to call ahead to reserve a table or check for a wait.

input: While I generally support independent restaurants over chain places,I still don't buy into the overpriced center city Phila hype. Help me polish this: While I generally prefer independent restaurants over chains, I must admit that I am not entirely sold on the overpriced center city Philadelphia hype. However, there seemed to be a lack of coordination between the bus help and the waiter, as they were clearing our plates just as the waiter was presenting the dessert options. input: The Tater-Tots were good but not anything I haven't  had before. Burger was satisfactory.  Quick stop for lunch.  Staff was helpful with providing directions to local attractions.

input:
As a frequent customer who has come since the place opened, I had previously rated this place higher, based on a recent experience decided to downgrade.

input:

input: I had chicken BBQ burritos with all kinds of stuff that I like. I love the it ! Good place to sit down with family & had a meal. I wish they had a place for kids to play that would be even better !

input: We stopped here for my Chai and Hubby's coffee and caffeine mania. The line went quite fast, they're quick with the service especially not a lot of people at the time. input: Very impressed with this place, particularly the menu (amazing) and the food. We ordered the fruit bruschetta (yum, what an awesome idea!) and the Popeye skillet and the Roadhouse sw. Great food, creative options! Couple areas of critique: it was FREEZING (every woman had a sweater on in July) and lack of ambiance. The latter could be easily remedied with some decent background music, and better lighting? (Overhead office lighting is a drag, but large windows a plus) Customer service was good not great, tad disconnected...but it was a holiday weekend. Overall, a keeper. I'll def be back!
Help me polish this:
I was extremely impressed with this place, especially the outstanding menu and the fantastic food. We had the fruit bruschetta (such a brilliant idea, and it tasted amazing!) as well as the Popeye skillet and the Roadhouse sandwich. The food was truly exceptional, and they offered a variety of creative options. 

However, there were a couple of areas that could use improvement. Firstly, the temperature inside was uncomfortably cold (to the point where every woman had to wear a sweater in the middle of July). Secondly, the ambiance was lacking. However, this issue could easily be resolved with the addition of some pleasant background music and better lighting. The overhead office lighting was a bit dull, but the large windows were definitely a positive aspect.

In terms of customer service, it was good but not outstanding. There seemed to be a slight disconnection, but I understand that it was a holiday weekend, so it might have been a bit busier than usual. Despite these minor flaws, I still consider this place a keeper. I will definitely be returning!

input: I can't recall the day I went but it was a memorial resturant experience.  I was greeted by an incredibly nice cashier. I can't recall the exact day I visited, but it was an unforgettable dining experience at a memorial restaurant. Upon entering, I was warmly greeted by an incredibly friendly cashier. After much contemplation, I finally settled on ordering the Devils' Delight. To my surprise, the cashier, who had a cute nickname "Devil Dev," explained that the burger was actually called "Dev's Delight," named after herself as it was her creative idea. It didn't take long for the staff to serve my meticulously prepared medium burger and truffle fries. Even before taking my first bite, the aroma alone had my mouth watering. The classic beef patty, paired with mozzarella cheese, tomato, basil, and a savory portobello mushroom, created an innovative twist on a traditional burger.

Nevertheless, I firmly believe that every penny spent was well worth it. Without a doubt, I will be returning as a satisfied customer.

input:
this place was awful. the first time my mother and I went we were very excited because everyone had been talking about it and we want to support local business. The day we went it happened to be pouring raining. So we are standing there at the hostess stand cold and wet waiting to be seated. Not only was the hostess not there, no one even acknowledged that we were there. The bartender who was right next to he stand was on his blue tooth and only looked our way to flirt with me. My mom was so annoyed we just left. 

The second time we went was because we were going to be in the area and we decided to give it a second try. We were seated right away and the music was really good. The waiter could have cared less about our table. he acted like we were doing him a favor by even coming to the table. The menu was thin and nothing to really choose from. when he eventually brought the food it was decent. My mom hated her salmon cakes because they were overly breaded and poorly season. it honestly looked like two pieces of bread. 

It was overpriced for what we had. I WOULD NEVER RECOMMEND THIS PLACE. The take out makes great dog food though.
Help me polish this:
This place was absolutely terrible. The first time my mother and I visited, we were filled with excitement and anticipation because everyone had been raving about it, and we genuinely wanted to support a local business. Unfortunately, our enthusiasm quickly turned sour. To make matters worse, it happened to be pouring rain on the day of our visit, and we stood there at the hostess stand, cold and drenched, waiting to be seated. Not only was the hostess nowhere to be found, but no one even bothered to acknowledge our presence. The bartender, who was conveniently positioned right next to the hostess stand, paid more attention to his phone conversation, occasionally glancing our way only to flirt with me. This disregard for our presence and comfort was too much for my mother, and we promptly left the establishment in utter frustration.

Despite our terrible first experience, we decided to give this place a second chance. We found ourselves in the area again and thought maybe our initial visit was just an anomaly. We were promptly seated this time, and the music playing in the background was surprisingly enjoyable. However, our optimism was quickly squashed when our waiter displayed zero interest in serving our table. He acted as if we were burdening him by simply being there, barely acknowledging our existence. The menu offered limited options, and nothing truly appealed to our taste buds. When the food finally arrived, it was passable at best. My mom was particularly disappointed with her salmon cakes, which were excessively breaded and poorly seasoned - they honestly resembled two slices of bread. The overall experience did not justify the exorbitant price we paid. I unequivocally declare that I would NEVER recommend this place to anyone. On the bright side, their takeout proved to be a suitable option for dog food.

input: Service was good. Mesquite wings are very good  best to share or save some don't be greedy like me and try.and go back to work. Only downside was the weak lemonade. It was the weakest I ever had.

input:
I don't know how I lucked out with having this taqueria in our neighborhood, but this is the best Mexican food you'll get in New Orleans.

We discovered Taqueria Guerrero after finding that burrito joint down the street was packed, had a line wrapping around the buidling (you know which one!).

After finding street parking near the mattress store, we plopped down and ordered the 3-taco plate (al pastor, mmmm) with beans and rice on the side and a burrito (barbocoa). I am a creature of habit and order the same tacos, but the bf has ventured out to get other dishes such as the fajita plate or the really spicy shrimp (camarones del diablo?). All very tasty.

The rest is history. It's embarrassing how often I suggest this place when we want to go out/get take out.
Help me polish this:
I can't believe how fortunate we are to have Taqueria Guerrero in our neighborhood. This place undoubtedly serves the finest Mexican cuisine in all of New Orleans.

Our journey to discover this gem began when we were craving Mexican food and the popular burrito joint down the street was swarming with customers. It seemed like there was an endless line wrapping around the building (you know the one I'm talking about!).

After securing a street parking spot near the mattress store, we eagerly entered Taqueria Guerrero and promptly ordered their outstanding 3-taco plate. My personal favorite is the al pastor, and it never fails to satisfy my taste buds. Of course, we couldn't resist adding a side of beans and rice and also indulged in a delectable burrito, specifically the barbacoa.

Although I tend to stick to my beloved tacos, my boyfriend has been adventurous and explored other dishes from the menu, such as the succulent fajita plate and the intensely spicy shrimp known as camarones del diablo. Each and every dish has exceeded our expectations and left us craving for more.

The undeniable truth is that Taqueria Guerrero has become our go-to spot for dining out or grabbing some takeout. I must admit, I find myself suggesting this place embarrassingly often whenever we plan to go out or enjoy a delicious meal in the comfort of our own home.

input:
Came here with a group of 15 people on a Tuesday night. We had reserved a space in advance. 
While the food was good, what was lacking was good service and cleanliness. We sat down at our table and it was sticky, and there was a dirty and also sticky fork still on it...so the assumption was that the table simply hadn't been wiped down all the way. Yuck. 
We ordered and the food took a fair amount of time, understandable because of such a large party. Problem was, when the food came out, no server knew what we'd individually ordered, so it became a huge mix up with people eating others' food. 
I ordered the pork belly tacos which had a great caramelization on the outside and tender inside. I also ordered the spicy beef pho, which was perfectly balanced with flavor after adding the accompanying bean sprouts and limes. 
The wait for the check and processing payment was long and arduous, a problem again because we had a Lyft driver waiting outside for us. 
All in all, go for the food, not for the service.
Help me polish this:
I came here with a group of 15 people on a Tuesday night, after making a reservation in advance. While the food itself was good, there were some areas in which the restaurant fell short, particularly in terms of service and cleanliness. When we sat down at our table, we immediately noticed that it was sticky, and there was a dirty, sticky fork left behind, suggesting that the table hadn't been properly wiped down. This lack of cleanliness was off-putting. 

We placed our orders, but the wait for the food was quite long, which was understandable considering the size of our party. However, when the food finally arrived, it became apparent that no server knew what each individual had ordered, resulting in a mix-up where people ended up eating each other's dishes. This mishap was disappointing and made the dining experience less enjoyable. 

On a positive note, I personally ordered the pork belly tacos, which had a delicious caramelized exterior and a tender, flavorful interior. Additionally, I tried the spicy beef pho, which was well-balanced in terms of flavor, especially after adding the accompanying bean sprouts and limes. The food itself was definitely a highlight.

Unfortunately, the wait for the bill and payment process was lengthy and cumbersome, which was problematic since we had a Lyft driver waiting outside for us. This further added to the overall dissatisfaction with the service.

In conclusion, if you decide to visit this establishment, I would recommend going primarily for the food rather than expecting exceptional service.

input: Unfortunately, I'm NOT happy after coming to this salon yet again. I got a message from the owner saying he'd like to have me come in to receive a FREE service because they previously ruined my hair. So, I thought since he's the owner my hair would turn out good but I was wrong. I'm really unhappy with this whole experience. I showed him multiple photos on google of what I wanted done to my hair which was a lot of blonde. I told him I do not want any ORANGE in my hair as I wanted a "white blonde". He said you won't have any orange in your hair. I have a message from him the OWNER saying I would receive a FREE service if I deleted my previous review. He should of NEVER offered a free service if it wasn't really free! So, I said how much because I thought I was getting my hair done for free. He said since your hair is long and thick you'll have to pay for the hair color and "medicine" but he won't charge me for his time. I said ok how much he said $80. He said it would cost me $180 if he didn't give me a discount which is very pricey. He put a lot of highlights on my hair and worked quickly as he seemed to want to rush on my hair which I do not like. My hair is important to me, I don't want my hair to fall out. He said this medicine he's gonna put on my hair is $50 for a treatment and that I needed it because of the blonde going on my hair which I know any coloring is damaging and blonde is very damaging but he said he charges everyone who gets hair color for this so called medicine which they mix into the color you dye your hair. You can purchase the entire set online (3 bottles) for $75 which is supposed to give you like 15 applications so he's definitely charging a lot of money! He only put No.1 on my hair and not No.2 or No.3. He also had a lady (the receptionist) wash out my hair? Ok, even though she was nice why would he have her do that when she said she knows nothing about hair because I asked if she's styling my hair and she said she doesn't do hair and I wouldn't want her to do my hair. As I was waiting there was a lady next to me, she got her hair cut and a perm. She was done but she wasn't happy, she told the lady she didn't like the hair cut and she had her style it more and trim off a little more but the lady still wasn't happy. The girl told the client when she washes her hair it will be better.. um how? I know she left very unhappy! Also the lady behind me was getting her hair cut and when he (the owner) was done cutting her hair she looked in the mirror and wanted it different and styled different so that made me have to wait longer but 2 clients were not happy and also myself. That's not a good look TJ nail and spa! I had a towel on my head and waited about 30 mins just to get my hair blow dried because he was cutting another clients hair. I seen orange roots, I was mad!!! He finally came over and I said I don't like the orange color on my roots, can you put a toner on my hair and he said it's not orange it's the lighting. The lighting?! It wasn't the lighting! He proceeds to blow dry hair and then starts straighten it without asking me if I wanted it straightened or curled, you are supposed to pick how you want your hair styled. At that point I knew my hair wasn't what I wanted and it wasn't gonna be fixed even if I wanted it too. I just sat there in the hair, mad and yet again very disappointed! I looked in the mirror and seen my hair damaged and brittle, orange and brassy and not even close to what I wanted. There goes my money down the drain, yet again. I will not be back to get my hair ruined and he made me delete my previous review which was also 0-1 stars before I left his salon but I had to write this one, this is real, this is honest, beware of getting your hair completely ruined and nothing close to what you want! Like I said I showed the OWNER multiple photos and I stated I did NOT want any orange on my hair but I did have orange on my hair, I didn't get what I wanted like he said, he said he doesn't mess up, he's been doing hair for years. As a salon owner I think he should take the time to really do what the client wants and achieve what the client wants done to their hair, if the workersowner would do that then there shouldn't be any bad reviews but there is so that shows you they do not care, not even the owner cares. They just want to rush and get done to get paid, they don't care if the customer is happy or not. There are more bad reviews from people going to this salon and having horrible experiences but he is bribing people to delete their bad reviews because he told me the bad reviews is hurting his business which is why people do reviews, to let people know this place is awesome or this place is horrible, beware, stay away. I do reviews to let people know the good, the bad and the ugly. I do reviews anywhere and I'm always 100% honest. So, if bad reviews hurt his business that is all on him and his employees not me or anyone else.
Help me polish this: Unfortunately, I am extremely dissatisfied with my experience at this salon once again. Despite receiving a message from the owner offering me a free service to make up for the previous hair mishap, my expectations were not met. I specifically showed the owner multiple photos of the blonde hair I desired and emphasized my preference for a "white blonde" without any orange tones. He assured me that there would be no orange in my hair. Additionally, the owner promised me a free service in exchange for deleting my previous review, which should have been honored without any hidden costs. However, when I inquired about the price, I was told that I would need to pay for the hair color and additional "medicine" due to the length and thickness of my hair. The owner's rushed approach and lack of attention to detail during the highlighting process made me uncomfortable, as my hair is important to me and I want to avoid any damage. He insisted that I needed a $50 treatment to counteract the damage caused by the blonde color, even though such treatments can be purchased online for a significantly lower price. Furthermore, I found it questionable that a receptionist with no experience in styling hair was tasked with washing my hair. While she was kind, I would have preferred a more qualified individual for this task. During my wait, I observed two other clients who were also unhappy with their haircuts. One client's dissatisfaction persisted even after the stylist attempted to rectify the situation. It became evident to me that the salon's professionalism was lacking. After waiting for approximately 30 minutes with a towel on my head, I finally asked for my hair to be blow-dried. Upon seeing orange roots, I expressed my displeasure to the owner and requested a toner. However, he dismissed my concerns, attributing the color to the lighting. I was not given a choice regarding how I wanted my hair styled, as the owner began straightening it without consulting me. At that point, I realized that my hair would not be fixed, regardless of my desires. Looking in the mirror, I saw damaged, brittle, and brassy hair that was far from the desired result. Unfortunately, my money had been wasted once again. I will not be returning to this salon to risk further damage, especially since the owner coerced me into deleting my previous review. This review serves as a genuine and honest warning to others. The owner was shown multiple photos, and my explicit request to avoid any orange tones was blatantly disregarded. Despite his claims of being an experienced stylist, he failed to prioritize customer satisfaction. It is essential for a salon owner to take the time to understand and achieve the client's hair goals. The disregard for customer happiness is evident not only in my experience but also in the numerous other negative reviews regarding this salon. It is apparent that the owner values financial gain over ensuring a positive and satisfactory experience for clients. Despite attempts to bribe customers into deleting negative reviews, it is important for people to know the truth about this place. I provide honest reviews in order to inform others about the positives, negatives, and potential drawbacks of various establishments. If negative reviews are negatively impacting the owner's business, it is his responsibility to address the concerns and improve the quality of service provided by both him and his employees.

input:
I am so glad we had our wedding here!!! I cannot say enough what a pleasure it was to work with Breanna, the venue manager and Eli, the food and beverage director. Our wedding here was a destination wedding, so we were very concerned about making sure all of our family and friends that travelled a long way to get to our wedding had a good time. Being a couple straight out of grad school, we were also very concerned with keeping the cost manageable. Everything worked out on all accounts! 

We first picked the venue for two reasons: the price was right and the venue is GORGEOUS. The pricing was very straightforward, which we really appreciated, and when looking at other options in the Santa Barbara area, the Riviera mansion was pretty comparable with other venues which are not all inclusive (ones where you have to find your own caterer, rent linens, etc etc). Planning a wedding without a coordinator and from across the country, it was also definitely worth it for us to go with a venue that minimized the amount of details we would have to think about.

The looks and layout of the place are what sold us though. With people coming from the east coast and middle of the country, we wanted something that would really showcase Santa Barbara's cool architecture and vibe. The mansion is exactly that.  The layout is also pretty perfect for a multigenerational wedding. We were able to enjoy the California weather for our ceremony and cocktail hour outside, then go inside for dinner, avoiding the cooler night air. Later, we could turn up the party in the bar/dance floor area, while the older folks talked and relaxed on the couches in the living room. It really has something for everyone.

What I didn't realize when we picked it was how absolutely awesome all the staff would be to work with. Breanna was super helpful, answering all my questions promptly and pleasantly, and accommodating my sometimes short notice visits to the area. When we did our walkthrough a couple of days before the wedding, Breanna and Eli paid attention to every detail and made sure we were taken care of, as they did the day of the wedding too. Eli was incredibly attentive and easy to work with! My dad is in the restaurant industry and was in charge of setting up desserts (we had family make some traditional desserts, as well as got some cupcakes from Enjoy Cupcakes- also a great idea!). Eli worked with him to get whatever he needed, risers, tablecloths, etc and was really sweet about it. 

The attention to bartending at the Riviera Mansion deserves a paragraph of its own. Breanna worked with me and the bartender (who's name I forget but has worked there for 20 years and is also incredibly awesome) to create a peach moscow mule as our signature drink (our colors were peach and green) and get it to taste just right. She even arranged it so we had fresh peaches! At the wedding, everyone raved about them, even guests who usually prefer something more manly sounding. The staff had all drinks ready to go for our cocktail hour, and also passed trays of drinks, so there was never a line at the bar (something guests also specifically mentioned that they appreciated). Hell, Eli even followed me with my drink for a couple of minutes around dinner since my hands were full of other things! Really spectacular and attentive service.

Five stars all around. It was absolutely a joy to have our wedding here.

input:
Yeah, I know what you're thinking. One Wawa store is pretty much the same as another, so why even bother writing a review? But I think we have a winner here.

When this Wawa store opened for business, gas prices at gas stations all along Concord Pike fell by 30 cents per gallon just to compete with them. Sure, this Wawa store could've followed the general pricing in the area and lowered prices just a few cents, keeping the bulk of the profit. But no, they'll have none of that. I love a store that is on the side of my wallet!

Secondly, I love the automatic start/stop digital air pump. So far, I've only seen that at BJ's Wholesale and Sheetz. It's a snap to use and I get the exact tire pressure every time.

Instead of just lowering prices slightly to keep the majority of the profit, this Wawa store went above and beyond. They truly have their customers' wallets in mind, and that's something I truly appreciate.

Additionally, they have a fantastic automatic start/stop digital air pump. It's a feature I've only seen at BJ's Wholesale and Sheetz thus far. Using it is a breeze, and I always get the exact tire pressure I need.

In terms of service, the staff here are friendly and reasonably efficient. The store's layout follows the new style that I first saw in Newark, which I find convenient. input:
For a seafood restaurant at the edge of pear expectations should be set high. My wife and I have come here 3 times now and ordered different plates off the menu each time. This last time we ordered cioppino, clam chowder, and a crab salad sandwich;
*Good - clam chowder (excellent flavor and consistency) would order again.
*Not great - cioppino (lacked flavor & a variety of sea food/lack there of) would not order again
*Pass - crab salad sandwich (lacked flavor, mayo was overpowering, crab flavor was almost non-existent, side of onion rings too greasy) - would not order again 
The overall experience is okay, better if seated outside right on the pear overlooking the ocean, inside is very small. Service is good but be prepared to wait a bit to be seated. 
Is it worth a visit? Yes, but be selective of what you order as the menu tends to be a hit and miss.
Help me polish this:
For a seafood restaurant located on the edge of a pier, high expectations should be set. My wife and I have dined here three times now, trying different dishes during each visit. During our most recent visit, we ordered cioppino, clam chowder, and a crab salad sandwich. 
The clam chowder was a highlight, boasting excellent flavor and a perfect consistency. We would definitely order it again. 
However, the cioppino fell short, lacking in flavor as well as a variety of seafood. We would not recommend ordering it again. 
As for the crab salad sandwich, it was disappointing. The flavors were lackluster, the mayo overpowered the dish, and the crab flavor was nearly nonexistent. Additionally, the side of onion rings was greasy. We would not recommend ordering this dish either. 
The overall dining experience was okay, especially if you are fortunate enough to secure an outdoor seating overlooking the ocean. However, the indoor seating area is quite small. The service was good, although there may be a wait for a table. 
Is it worth a visit? Yes, but we suggest being selective with your order as the menu tends to be hit or miss.

input: Chef Kevin Sbraga knows fried chicken. My first exposure to his succulent birds was the hot chicken at The Fat Ham. Lo and behold, his lavender honey fried chicken tops its spicy cousin. The chicken is brined in buttermilk, dredged in seasoned flour and sits for ten minutes. It's then coated with a second round of flour and dropped into the fryer. The chicken (breast, wing, thigh, drumstick) is drizzled with lavender honey and sprinkled with salt and ground pink peppercorns. It comes with a buttermilk biscuit, whipped honey-thyme butter, and red bliss potato salad. It is some of the best fried chicken I've eaten in a long time. Crunchy, crispy coating on the outside with a juicy, moist inside. The sweet honey glaze is truly outstanding and finger lickin' good. The biscuit is awesome. I would definitely order this dish again and again. I got the salty but delicious fried smelts with chili pepper aioli as an appetizer. My friend Chris W got the filet mignon and butter poached king crab surf and turf. For dessert, I had a slice of salted pecan pie and he had the ice cream sundae. Every dish at Juniper Commons was top-notch. Chef Sbraga does it again!
Help me polish this: Chef Kevin Sbraga, renowned for his expertise in fried chicken, continues to impress with his latest creation - the lavender honey fried chicken. After indulging in the hot chicken at The Fat Ham, I couldn't resist trying this even more tantalizing option. The chicken is first brined in buttermilk, then coated in seasoned flour and left to sit for ten minutes. A second round of flour is added before it takes a dip into the fryer. The result? A succulent combination of breast, wing, thigh, and drumstick, drizzled with lavender honey and garnished with salt and ground pink peppercorns. Served alongside are a delectable buttermilk biscuit, whipped honey-thyme butter, and red bliss potato salad. It's safe to say that this is some of the best fried chicken I've had in ages. The exterior boasts a crunchy, crispy coating, while the interior remains juicy and moist. Not to mention, the exquisite sweet honey glaze beckons you to lick your fingers clean. The biscuit alone deserves praise - it's truly awesome. Undoubtedly, I would order this dish again and again. As an appetizer, I couldn't resist the salty yet delectable fried smelts, which were perfectly complemented by the chili pepper aioli. My companion, Chris W, opted for the filet mignon and butter-poached king crab surf and turf, which did not disappoint. For dessert, we indulged in a slice of salted pecan pie and an ice cream sundae. Every dish at Juniper Commons exceeded expectations. Kudos to Chef Sbraga for yet another culinary triumph!

input:
I really wanted to like Casselli's, but it wasn't in the cards. Maybe I just caught them on a bad night, but I didn't really enjoy much about my visit. The waiter was very unpleasant - was banging down the plates and glasses on the table when he delivered them. Maybe he was having a bad day, but I still would have expected better. 

We had mixed experiences with the food. Mine and our friends' was OK, but my wife's baked ravioli would have been more use to a hockey team for use as pucks. They were really overdone - woefully overdone. 

The worst part was that our table was next to the opera singer guy. He was singing extremely loudly and it was nigh impossible to maintain a conversation - especially coupled with how close we were to the table next to us and their attempts to speak over Opera Guy.

Part of me wants to give them another chance (since I hate writing bad reviews) and the other part is annoyed over the waiter's attitude. I probably will not go back. There are so many good Italian restaurants worth visiting that the opportunity cost of returning to Casselli's seems too high.

On the upside, they have somewhat convenient parking in the lot behind the restaurant (near the Shawmont School).

Note: cash-only.

input:
Amazing food!! and  the whole experience is great there every time. I suggest going there with a  group of about 6 people so it doesn't totally break the bank but if you've got the money then who cares! Have fun!

First you enter in and select the wine you would like. The staff is helpful and knowledgeable about their stock. (And if for some reason at the end you didn't  finish your bottle they will cork it back up for you to take.) Then select your cheese platter. Lots of yummy stinky cheese to select  from and prosciutto. I wish they had more cured meats but it's all yummy anyway. You pay for the wine and cheese there. Which in a large group one or two people can take care of this  part. 

Then going to get a seat can be difficult but just be patient. There's outdoor seating that's very nice and always a live band playing. Inside upstairs is nice as well. Once you're all set with your wine and group it's time to order. Go to the window and play your order. Definite things you must get.... the bacon wrapped dates stuffed with chorizo and the goat cheese and mushroom dish....AMAZING! Although everything I've ever had here is great. 

Then just wait for your cheese platter, food and enjoy!
Help me polish this:
The food at this place is absolutely amazing! The overall experience is always fantastic. I recommend going with a group of about 6 people to keep the cost reasonable, but if you're willing to splurge, then go for it! Have a great time!

Upon entering, you get to choose your wine from a great selection. The staff is incredibly helpful and knowledgeable about their collection. And if, by chance, you don't finish your bottle, they'll kindly cork it for you to take home. Next, you can select your cheese platter, which offers a variety of delicious and aromatic cheeses, as well as some prosciutto. It would be nice if they had more cured meats, but everything is still yummy. Payment for the wine and cheese can be handled by one or two people in a larger group to make it easier.

Finding a seat might be challenging, but just be patient. The outdoor seating is beautiful, and there's always a live band playing. The upstairs indoor seating is also lovely. Once you're settled with your wine and your group, it's time to place your order. Head to the window and make your selections. There are a couple of must-try items - the bacon wrapped dates stuffed with chorizo and the goat cheese and mushroom dish. They are absolutely amazing! However, everything I've ever had here is great.

Now, all you have to do is wait for your cheese platter and food to arrive, and then enjoy!

input:
I find it hugely ironic that WF is trying to reposition itself as a 'value' food store right now when others (i.e. Trader Joe's up the street) have been doing that for years.  For value, go elsewhere.  For pretty food, lovely store displays and a feeling of smugness, check out Whole Foods.

Despite my snark, I have to admit that it's nice to see an enormous, clean and well stocked yuppie market in Reno finally.  Now that this town has been rated by National Geographic as a top outdoors place to live in, it needs the retail to support that (and I don't mean another REI).  For myself, I'm too cheap to look seriously at this place for my regular shopping needs, but for lunch and the odd stopover, it's awesome.   Beautiful produce, drool inducing cheese selections and a bakery that would break my budget if I bought everything that struck my fancy.

Plus it's proximity to the freeway (for those of us who do our shopping based on distance from the 395 or 80) makes it an ideal stop to/from the airport.
Help me polish this:
I find it incredibly ironic that Whole Foods is attempting to position itself as a 'value' food store right now, especially considering that others like Trader Joe's have been successfully doing so for years. If you are looking for value, I would suggest looking elsewhere. However, if you are in search of beautifully presented food, delightful store displays, and a sense of smugness, then Whole Foods is worth checking out.

Despite my sarcastic remark, I must admit that it is refreshing to see a large, clean, and well-stocked upscale market like Whole Foods finally appear in Reno. With National Geographic rating this town as one of the top outdoor places to live in, it's about time we have the retail infrastructure to support it (and I'm not just talking about another REI). While I personally find it too expensive for my regular shopping needs, it is perfect for grabbing lunch or making the occasional stop. The produce is stunning, the cheese selections are mouthwatering, and the bakery is simply irresistible, even though it could easily exceed my budget if I gave in to every temptation.

Moreover, the convenience of its location near the freeway (for those of us who prioritize shopping based on proximity to the 395 or 80) makes it an excellent choice for a quick stopover before or after a trip to the airport.

input:
Monthly lunch with my fellow colleagues the other day and the person assigned to get lunch ordered from Fresh and had it delivered. 

My selection was the Chopped Italian salad. The salad consists of mixed greens, salami, smoked turkey, tomato, garbanzo beans and parmesan cheese served with the house vinaigrette. The salad was lacking for me. I think such a salad would be so much better with a few more Italian-esque ingredients in it, perhaps a little more anitpasto like. I know, it's not advertised as antipasto but c'mon....this salad was boring.  Throw in a couple of olives, some artichoke hearts, some sliced pepperoncinis. Maybe my tastebuds were having an off day but the salami wasn't very flavorful either. Charge a couple dollars more for a more inventive salad. Please!

I do want to give them another chance since so many reviews on here are glowing. Maybe I need to stick with a panini or something but I really do love salads for summer lunches.
Help me polish this: During our monthly colleague lunch, we decided to order delivery from Fresh. I opted for the Chopped Italian salad, which includes mixed greens, salami, smoked turkey, tomato, garbanzo beans, and parmesan cheese, served with the house vinaigrette. However, I found the salad to be somewhat lacking. In my opinion, it could benefit from the addition of more Italian-inspired ingredients, such as olives, artichoke hearts, or sliced pepperoncinis. Adding these antipasto elements would truly elevate the flavor profile. Furthermore, the salami itself was not as flavorful as I had hoped. I would gladly pay a couple of dollars more for a more innovative and flavorful salad option. Despite my disappointment, I am willing to give Fresh another chance, as I have noticed many positive reviews. Perhaps I should consider trying one of their paninis instead, though I genuinely enjoy salads for my summer lunch choice.

input:

Unfortunately, the shop was damaged by a fire in the next door laundry mat and they've been closed for a few weeks, but I can't wait for their doors to open again soon. I miss the lunch special, 2 slices and a self serve soda for $3.99.   Best local pizza you'll find in the Hatboro area.

input:
If you are going for the food, I would give it 5 stars, but since this is a brewhouse, I only gave it 3. 

I ordered the light flight since we went for lunch and I wasn't looking for a heavy meal. The beer was OK at best. It was bland, a little strange in after taste and uninspired. Light beers dont have to equal tasteless. My boyfriend had a "hoppy beer with citrus undertones". He could taste neither the hops or the citrus  (disclaimer - we are from VT and are used to very hoppy beers!)  

Now the food - that was great. We went at lunch time and was able to get a soup and salad for 8.95. We both had the same thing - Chicken Bruchetta salad and French Onion Soup. The portion was fantastic for a lunch size and the soup really flavorful! 

For a lunch downtown it was great, but I would go for the brews...
Help me polish this:
If you're looking for great food, I would give this place 5 stars. However, since it's a brewhouse, I can only give it 3 stars. 

I decided to go for the light flight since I wanted a lighter meal for lunch. Unfortunately, the beer was just okay. It lacked flavor, had a strange aftertaste, and overall seemed uninspired. I expected more from a light beer. My boyfriend tried a "hoppy beer with citrus undertones," but couldn't taste either the hops or the citrus. (Disclaimer: We're from VT and used to very hoppy beers!)

But let me tell you, the food was a different story. We both ordered the Chicken Bruschetta salad and French Onion Soup for 8.95, and it was fantastic. The portion size was perfect for lunch, and the soup had amazing flavor.

Overall, it's a great spot for a downtown lunch, but I wouldn't come here specifically for the beer.

input:
This place just opened up near rivers edge apartments. It's a boutique style taqueria with a menu that anyone can enjoy. The head chef was nominated for a James Beard Award and it shows in his flavorful and diverse menu choices! The restaurant has both an outdoor and indoor setting with double doors that allow access to both, with a bar around the corner. 

I personally have tried every taco on the menu as well as the appetizers! Each taco uses fresh local ingredients with an option for vegetarians and meat eaters like myself. My two favorites are the mushroom taco and the short rib taco, both have unique and fantastic flavors. But I would recommend trying them all, you will not be disappointed! Overall a great place for lunch or dinner! I will definitely be going back soon!
Help me polish this:
There is a new establishment called "Taco Haven" that recently opened near Rivers Edge Apartments. This unique taqueria offers a boutique-style experience with a menu that appeals to everyone. The head chef, who has been nominated for a prestigious James Beard Award, has crafted a diverse and flavorful selection of dishes that truly showcase his culinary expertise.

Upon entering, you are greeted with the option of indoor or outdoor dining areas. The establishment seamlessly blends both settings with its double doors, allowing easy access between the two spaces. Additionally, there is a well-stocked bar conveniently located around the corner.

Having personally sampled every item on the menu, including the enticing appetizers, I can confidently attest to the high quality of the tacos served at Taco Haven. Each taco is meticulously prepared, using only the freshest local ingredients. Whether you are a vegetarian or meat lover like myself, there is an option that will surely satisfy your taste buds. Personally, the mushroom taco and the short rib taco stand out as my absolute favorites, boasting unique and exquisite flavors. Nevertheless, I encourage you to explore the entire menu as each offering is a delightful culinary adventure. Rest assured, you will not be disappointed by the taste and quality of the food at Taco Haven.

For those in search of a memorable lunch or dinner experience, Taco Haven is an excellent choice. With its delectable dishes and inviting ambiance, it is definitely a place worth revisiting. I, for one, am already eagerly anticipating my next visit.

input: Originally, our little group headed to Franklin Fountain and the line was around the block-- Capofitto was only a few steps away with no line (and bonus--cheaper/better dessert treat!). We only popped in for gelato, but I would love to come back for the pizza! It looked and smelled really good. Gelato was amazing, as capogiro gelato always is. Highly recommend chocolat scurio and pera as a combo--it was perfect!
Help me polish this:
Originally, our small group decided to visit Franklin Fountain. However, upon arrival, we were met with an incredibly long line that extended around the block. Fortunately, Capofitto was just a few steps away, and to our delight, there was no line. Not only that, but their dessert treats were also cheaper and of superior quality!

Although we only intended to have gelato, the smell and appearance of their pizzas were incredibly tempting. I couldn't help but crave a slice. The gelato itself was exceptional, as expected from Capogiro gelato. I highly recommend trying the combination of Chocolat Scurio and Pera flavors - trust me, it's the perfect blend!

Overall, our experience at Capofitto was fantastic, and I am eager to return specifically for their delightful pizza.

input: This hospital is by far the best for families on the East Coast. They make seeing multiple MDs on the same day very easy and the quality of care is incredible. The renovated wing is fantastic with good accommodations for caregivers and friendly and attentive staff. I wholeheartedly recommend A.I. DuPont and will continue to travel from NY for my child's care.
Help me polish this: I highly recommend A.I. DuPont as the top hospital for families on the East Coast. Their exceptional services make it easy to schedule appointments with multiple MDs in a single day, ensuring convenience and efficiency. The quality of care provided is truly extraordinary. The recently renovated wing is remarkable, offering excellent accommodations for caregivers. The staff members are welcoming, attentive, and friendly. As a parent, I wholeheartedly endorse A.I. DuPont and have no hesitation in continuing to journey from New York to seek my child's care at this exceptional facility.

input: I highly recommend this place! This was our first "Chef Tasting"! It was exquisite!! We had 9 courses and all were truly delicious. Wine was amazing. If you are in Philly, I highly recommend Vetri.
Help me polish this: I highly recommend Vetri in Philadelphia! My experience there for their Chef Tasting menu was truly exquisite. We were treated to nine courses, each of them incredibly delicious. The wine selection was also amazing. If you find yourself in Philly, do not miss the opportunity to dine at Vetri.

input:
I'm pretty sure this place has been open since before I was born and it's no surprise as to why. 

The absolute classic of an American diner, polite and attentive waitresses and most of their food made entirely from scratch. I would definitely say their fried chicken is the best I've had before, and fresh! Bottomless coffee too, for $1.75 which I think is quite reasonable. Nice pie, too :)
Help me polish this:
This place is undoubtedly a true gem that has stood the test of time, and it's not hard to see why. It embodies everything you expect from a classic American diner, complete with courteous and attentive waitresses, and a menu that is painstakingly crafted from scratch. 

When it comes to their fried chicken, I can confidently declare it the best I've ever tasted. The chicken is not only incredibly delicious but also amazingly fresh. And if that's not enough, they offer bottomless coffee for a mere $1.75, a truly reasonable deal. Oh, and don't even get me started on their delightful pies!

input: Don't go here. They gave me grief over the groupon then didn't bother to actually change my oil filter or tell me that they hadn't changed it so I drove 5k miles on an old filter. Crappy customer service, rude attitude, find somewhere better.
Help me polish this: Avoid this place at all costs. Not only did they give me grief over using a Groupon, but they also failed to change my oil filter and neglected to inform me about it. As a result, I ended up driving 5,000 miles with an old filter. Their customer service is absolutely terrible, with a rude attitude to top it off. Save yourself the hassle and find a better place to take your business.

input: I attended the #welldoneTBO tweet-up at Anthony's Coal Fired Pizza last week and had a great time. The folks at Anthony's were amazing with the customer service. We got to try so many menu items, and all were amazing. The Philly Cheesesteak Pizza was my 10 year old's favorite. I loved the Cauliflower pizza...so buttery and garlicky and delicious (vegetarian). We also got to try the carmelized onion-smothered wings which were out of this world. Also tasted: meatballs, ribs, salad...all very good. We ordered off the menu a half and half pizza with pepperoni, sausage and mushrooms. So good. If they had liquor on the menu I would have given them five stars (I'm just not a beer or wine person). Thanks for a great evening Anthony's! We'll be back.
Help me polish this:
I had an incredible time at the #welldoneTBO tweet-up held at Anthony's Coal Fired Pizza last week. The exceptional customer service provided by the staff at Anthony's truly stood out. Throughout the evening, we had the opportunity to sample a wide variety of items from their menu, and each one was fantastically delicious.

The Philly Cheesesteak Pizza received high praise from my 10-year-old, who couldn't get enough of its flavors. Personally, I was captivated by the Cauliflower pizza, which was not only vegetarian but also had a delightful buttery and garlicky taste. Additionally, we had the pleasure of trying the caramelized onion-smothered wings, which were simply out of this world. Our taste adventure also included dishes like meatballs, ribs, and salad, all of which were right on point.

For our main course, we ordered a half and half pizza with pepperoni, sausage, and mushrooms. The combination was a mouthwatering blend of flavors that left us craving for more. If only Anthony's had liquor on their menu, they would have earned a perfect five-star rating from me. Unfortunately, I am not fond of beer or wine.

Thank you, Anthony's, for an amazing evening. We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves and cannot wait to return for another culinary adventure.

input: Awesome service and food.  Served with a dry ice fog thing that add a layer of coolness to the whole experience.
Help me polish this: Exceptional service and delectable cuisine make the dining experience truly unforgettable. To further elevate the ambiance, the addition of a captivating dry ice fog creates a mesmerizing and ultimately cool atmosphere.

input: Come here for delicious, home style New Orleans cuisine. We went in the afternoon, and although it was full, we were lucky and a table was ready right away. We did the a la carte as opposed to the buffet. It was our favorite meal of the trip!
Help me polish this: Indulge in scrumptious, authentic New Orleans cuisine at our establishment. During our visit in the afternoon, we were pleasantly surprised to find the restaurant bustling with patrons, yet fortunate enough to be seated immediately. Opting for the a la carte menu instead of the buffet, we were treated to a gastronomic delight that quickly became the highlight of our trip.

input: A great restaurant to take people visiting from out of town. Very popular for breakfast/brunch on the weekends. Should expect to wait at least an hour any time after 9:30 AM and service takes a little while. But great menu options and delicious food. Also a great bakery, coffee and gelato counter that offers instant service or items to enjoy while waiting to get called.
Help me polish this:
Looking for an exceptional restaurant to bring your out-of-town guests? Look no further! This establishment is renowned for its breakfast and brunch, particularly on weekends. However, be prepared for a wait of at least an hour after 9:30 AM, as it tends to get immensely crowded. The service might also take a little longer, but trust me, it's well worth it.

This delightful eatery boasts a diverse menu with numerous delectable options that will tempt any palate. Whether you're a fan of classic breakfast staples or crave more adventurous dishes, this place has got you covered. The flavors served here will leave you longing for more.

Furthermore, while waiting for your table, you can enjoy the convenience of a superb bakery, coffee, and gelato counter. This counter not only offers instant service, but also provides delightful treats to savor as you eagerly anticipate your turn to be seated. 

Overall, despite the slight wait and service duration, this restaurant is truly worth the visit. Its exceptional menu options, delectable flavors, and the added bonus of a delightful bakery, coffee and gelato counter guarantee an unforgettable experience for both you and your out-of-town guests.

input:
The food is really good!! The service is less than average; I felt very rushed, unimportant, and cheated. Was shocked that the waitress withheld my coins when she gave me my change! Do they withhold change from all of their customers?!! Very disappointed.  Would she have done that to a well known food critic?

Will probably go back one more time eventually but will have lots of change with me to pay the EXACT amount! When it came time to give her tip, I applied the coins she withheld from me -they became part of her tip. Also, her tip dropped from my standard 25% to 15%. Flabbergasted.
Help me polish this:
The food at this place is absolutely wonderful! However, I must say that the service received was quite disappointing. I felt hurried, unvalued, and even deceived. To my surprise, the waitress held onto my change when she gave me my total! I couldn't help but wonder if this is a common practice for all customers. This particular incident left me feeling thoroughly let down. I couldn't help but ponder whether she would have treated a well-known food critic the same way.

Despite my disappointment, I do plan on giving this place another chance in the future. However, I will make sure to have the exact change with me when paying. When it came time to leave a tip, I factored in the coins that were kept from me. Consequently, her tip was reduced from my usual 25% to 15%, which truly astonished me.

input: Their sushi is pretty good. Mesa rolls are my fav here. They would be 4stars if they gave better estimations for pick ups. It is typical that they lag a lot and they seem to make it after you show up.
Help me polish this: Their sushi is absolutely delicious, and I particularly love their Mesa rolls. If only they could improve their estimation system for pick-ups, they would easily earn a solid 4-star rating. It's quite frustrating that there's often a significant delay, with the order not being prepared until after you arrive.

input: If you want The Best burger in Philly, this is the right place to come. The bread was fresh, meat was nothing but juicy, service was a amiable, price was descent and affordable to everybody!
Help me polish this: If you're craving the best burger in Philly, look no further than this place. Our bread is always fresh, our meat is perfectly juicy, and our service is amiable. Plus, our prices are not only reasonable but also affordable for everyone!

input: Great hangout for wine, cheese, and some music outside.  Tried some of the food - bacon-wrapped dates & brussel sprouts - all unmemorable.  Also tried the sardines which smelled and tasted past their prime - sent back.
Help me polish this: "Seeking a delightful spot to unwind with wine, cheese, and live music outdoors? Look no further. However, my recent experience at this establishment left much to be desired. The food options, including bacon-wrapped dates and brussel sprouts, failed to leave a lasting impression. Moreover, the sardines, with their pungent smell and off-putting taste, clearly had surpassed their prime and had to be returned."

input:
Excellent tasting Po-Boys but it could have had mire catfish, pretty skimpy.
Service, very good.
Help me polish this: The Po-Boys had excellent taste, but it would have been even better if there was more catfish. The portion size was a bit skimpy. However, the service was very good.

input:
Define the worst Mediterranean food I have ever had.  The hummus appeared to have a good texture, that is the little bit I could see under the ocean of olive oil.  The pita bread was burned- not just over toasted, but black on the majority of the wedges.  I went home and was sick the rest of the evening from the amount of oil it had in it. 

The manager was probably the worst of the experience. He told my gf he would "upgrade her hummus for no charge, because normally it's $1.00" but said it as if he was doing us this huge favor.  He then continued to yell at us from across the restaurant after we sat down  (instead of coming up to our table and actually having a conversation) and says, "please let me know how your food is because that's the only way I can know if we are doing a good job or not is when customers tell me."  But we agreed that the vibe he gave off would not be that of open mindedness and gratitude if we were to say anything about his plate of olive oil, er I mean hummus.  There is also a sign that advertises the "cleanest bathroom in town".... Ehhhh ok, good to know for our next road trip.
Help me polish this:
Let me help you polish your text:

Describe the worst Mediterranean food experience I've ever had. The hummus had a seemingly good texture, but it was difficult to tell as it was submerged in an excessive amount of olive oil. The pita bread was not just over toasted, but completely black on most of the wedges. The excessive oil content made me sick for the entire evening after consuming it.

The manager truly worsened the experience. He condescendingly offered my girlfriend a "free upgrade" on her hummus, as if it were a generous favor, stating that it normally cost $1.00. Instead of approaching our table to discuss the issue, he resorted to yelling at us from across the restaurant, demanding that we inform him of our food's quality because it was the only way he could gauge his restaurant's performance. However, his demeanor gave us the impression that he wouldn't be receptive or grateful if we were to mention the excessive oil in the hummus. Adding to the strangeness, there was a sign boasting about having the "cleanest bathroom in town" - an irrelevant detail for our visit.

This incident will surely be remembered on our next road trip.

input: Great bagels!  I wish they stayed open later in the day though.  Staff not very friendly but the bagels are worth it!
Help me polish this: The bagels here are fantastic! My only wish is that they would stay open later in the day. While the staff isn't the friendliest, the incredible taste of their bagels makes up for it!

input:
This hotel was fantastic. I was in town for a week, working at my company's PA office in Wayne. Great location and easy to get in and out. Hotel staff was very friendly. Room was immaculately cleaned and very spacious for just one person. Kitchenette was fully stocked with dishes, silverware, utensils, a small dishwasher and a full size fridge. Windows surrounding the king size bed were great- lots of natural light. I liked that opting out of housekeeping got me a $5 credit at the restaurant. 

The pool is small but no one was there the two times I went to use the hot tub. The bar has a decent drink selection, although I was bummed they were out of mint and couldn't make a mojito (which was on the drink menu). Burger was okay. Dessert was mediocre (but free with my $5 credit, so nbd). Omelet station was a nice touch in the AM. Coffee frequently had coffee grounds in it/was very weak, but the breakfast spread overall was nice.
Help me polish this:
This hotel was absolutely fantastic. I stayed here for a week while working at my company's PA office in Wayne, and I couldn't have asked for a better experience. The location was perfect and it was very convenient to get in and out. 

The hotel staff was incredibly friendly and accommodating. They truly went above and beyond to ensure my stay was comfortable and enjoyable. 

The room itself was exceptional. It was immaculately cleaned and surprisingly spacious for just one person. I particularly loved the kitchenette, which was fully stocked with dishes, silverware, utensils, and even a small dishwasher and a full-size fridge. It made it so convenient to prepare my own meals during my stay. 

One aspect I really appreciated was the windows surrounding the king-size bed. They allowed for an abundance of natural light, creating a bright and welcoming atmosphere. 

Another perk of staying at this hotel was the option to opt-out of housekeeping in exchange for a $5 credit at the restaurant. It was a great way to save some money while still enjoying a delicious meal. 

The pool was on the smaller side, but luckily, there was never anyone using the hot tub during the two times I went. It provided a relaxing way to unwind after a long day. 

The hotel's bar had a decent drink selection, although I was a bit disappointed they were out of mint and couldn't make a mojito as advertised on the drink menu. However, the burger I ordered was still enjoyable. The dessert, while mediocre, was free with my $5 credit, so it wasn't a big deal. 

In the mornings, I loved the omelet station at the breakfast spread. It was a nice touch and allowed for personalized and fresh breakfast options. The only downside was that the coffee frequently had coffee grounds in it and was on the weak side. However, the overall breakfast offerings were satisfying.

input: Decent falafel wrap...but not exactly cheap. And the cave-like sitting area was cold and uninviting. There are better choices in Manayunk.
Help me polish this: Although the falafel wrap was decent, it cannot be considered cheap. Additionally, the sitting area with its cave-like atmosphere was cold and uninviting. With better options available in Manayunk, it would be advisable to explore different dining choices.

input: This place was awesome! I am driving cross country and hit a busted tire on the road and something came off the bottom of my car.  I called and Brian told me to come in and he would take a look.  They put my car up right away and patched things up. He was really nice and had me on my way in less than 30 minutes.  Definitely recommend this place.
Help me polish this: This place was absolutely amazing! While driving cross country, I unfortunately encountered a flat tire and some damage to the bottom of my car. In my moment of distress, I reached out to Brian and he graciously invited me to bring my car in for inspection. The team at this establishment swiftly attended to my car, promptly fixing the issues at hand. Not only was Brian immensely kind, but his efficient service ensured that I got back on the road in less than 30 minutes. Without a doubt, I highly recommend this exceptional place for all your automotive needs.

input: Friday, July 22 we decided to give this eatery a try.  It is definitely in a great location especially if you want to explore the Quarter afterwards.  We were a party of 8 people and out of the 8 dishes ordered only 2 were really good --the jambalaya and file gumbo were very tasty.  The other dishes --red beans/rice,  meatloaf, Mac and cheese,  shrimp po boy, and chicken wings were bland and a waste of money.  The staff was nice but overall the food was mediocre.
Help me polish this: On Friday, July 22, we made the decision to try out this eatery. Located in a prime spot, it is perfect for anyone eager to explore the Quarter afterwards. With a group of 8 people, we ordered a variety of dishes, but unfortunately, only 2 stood out as really good—the jambalaya and file gumbo were incredibly tasty. The remaining dishes, including red beans and rice, meatloaf, Mac and cheese, shrimp po boy, and chicken wings, were disappointingly bland and felt like a waste of money. The staff was friendly and accommodating, but overall, the food was mediocre.

input: According to my experience, there is just one place in Tokyo at the fish market where you get your seafood a little fresher. Here in Santa Barbara, it does not get any fresher. Right from the fish tank in the cooking pot on your plate. Don't expect a fancy restaurant with a nice ambiance because this is not the reason you come here (though the outside seating has a nice ocean/harbor view). It is the variety of fresh shellfish prepared according to your appetite and taste buds. The wait can be long during peak hours but it is worth it. Put your name down and take a walk on the peer to free-up some extra room in your stomach - you'll need it!
Help me polish this: Based on my experience, there is only one place in Tokyo's fish market where you can find seafood that is slightly fresher. However, here in Santa Barbara, you won't find anything fresher than what we offer. Our seafood goes straight from the fish tank to the cooking pot and onto your plate. While we may not boast a fancy restaurant ambiance, that is not why people come here (although our outdoor seating does offer a stunning view of the ocean/harbor). It's all about the variety of fresh shellfish we have, prepared to satisfy your cravings and taste buds. The wait can be long during peak hours, but trust me, it's worth it. Just put your name down and take a leisurely stroll on the pier to make some extra room in your stomach - because you'll definitely need it!

input: I've always had good experiences here. The food is creative and tasty and the house wines are decent. Their cocktails are well made but small. I've never had a problem with service but also haven't been here during a super busy time. The patio is a great spot to hang out with friends.
Help me polish this: I've consistently had wonderful experiences at this place. The food is both inventive and flavorful, while the house wines are of a satisfactory quality. Their skillfully crafted cocktails, albeit on the smaller side, never fail to impress. I've personally never encountered any issues with the service, although I must note that I haven't visited during peak hours. Additionally, the patio area makes for an excellent gathering spot to spend quality time with friends.

input:
tldr; Huge plates of food. Cheap. Delicious. Get the banana pecan pancakes.

Skyway Jacks is now Skyway Cafe. Same great food and service. I love the bovine decor. It really makes it feel homey. This is the kind of place that you think about when you imagine a local diner (at least my opinion of one). Everything I've eaten has been awesome. The service is good and the coffee keeps coming. 

They have a morning breakfast deal between 7 and 830 am. $2.89 for 5 different combinations such as 2 eggs, pancakes and sausage (when you buy a beverage). I might have to start grabbing a little breakfast before work!

Seriously, though.... get the banana pecan pancakes. You can thank me later.
Help me polish this:
Skyway Jacks has recently rebranded as Skyway Cafe and continues to offer the same great food and service. The charming bovine decor adds a homely touch to the diner experience, making it a perfect representation of a local diner in my opinion. Every dish I have tried at Skyway Cafe has been delicious, and the service is top-notch with a constant flow of coffee. 

One of the highlights of this diner is their morning breakfast deal available from 7 to 8:30 am. For just $2.89, you can enjoy various combinations including 2 eggs, pancakes, and sausage when you purchase a beverage. It's definitely worth considering grabbing a quick breakfast here before heading to work!

However, the standout item on the menu that I highly recommend are the banana pecan pancakes. Trust me, these are absolutely delightful, and you won't regret trying them.

input:

Help me polish this:
My worst experience ever!!!!

input: Good luck finding anyone to help you.  Poor poor customer service.
Help me polish this: I'm sorry to inform you that you'll have a difficult time finding someone to assist you. The customer service provided here is severely lacking.

input:
On my first day in New Orleans, I walked to Fair Grinds for a caffeine boost. It was a beautiful afternoon, and a handful of people were scattered around the shop and the outdoor seating area, working on laptops and visiting with friends. 

I ordered a small cold brew with vanilla, easy on the ice. I added a hunk of gluten free zucchini bread (the bread butt; the best part!) to my order and paid with a credit card. They have a fancy touchscreen register that lets you add tip to your card purchase. 

I topped off my drink with whole milk -- which in itself was a real treat. It's so rare to see whole milk at the mixing station! 

Before leaving, I asked what else they had in the way of a GF offering, and the young man behind the counter said "just the zucchini bread." That's a real bummer; the zucchini bread is great but I'd love to have more than one option. 

My drink was smooth and had a perfect flavor. I was happy with my choices. 

If I lived in the neighborhood, I'd be here all the time. I like the hipstery feeling of this place, and everything I've ordered has been delightful.
Help me polish this:
On my first day in New Orleans, I strolled over to Fair Grinds for a much-needed caffeine boost. It was a stunning afternoon, with a charming scattering of people working on their laptops or engaging in friendly conversations at both the indoor and outdoor seating areas.

Craving a refreshing pick-me-up, I decided to order a small, vanilla-infused cold brew, with just the right amount of ice. To complement my drink, I couldn't resist adding a delectable slice of gluten-free zucchini bread – the coveted bread butt, known for its unrivaled deliciousness! Opting for convenience, I smoothly paid for my order using a credit card at their state-of-the-art touchscreen register, which conveniently allowed me to include a tip as well.

To my surprise, Fair Grinds offered a rare delight – the option of whole milk at their mixing station! It's not often that one encounters such an indulgence, and I eagerly topped off my drink with the creamy goodness.

Before bidding adieu, I enquired about any other gluten-free offerings they might have. Unfortunately, the response was disheartening – the young man behind the counter informed me that the zucchini bread was their sole gluten-free option. While I thoroughly enjoyed this particular treat, I couldn't help but feel a pang of longing for a more varied selection.

Nevertheless, as I took my first sip, I was met with sheer satisfaction. The cold brew was impeccably smooth, boasting a flavor profile that was simply perfect. With contentment in my heart, I relished the choices I had made.

If I were fortunate enough to call this neighborhood home, Fair Grinds would undoubtedly become my go-to spot. There's something captivating about its hipster ambiance, and every order I've placed thus far has been an absolute delight.

input: This place is so lovely! I went for a sweet and was amazed at the variety. The gooey butter cookies were awesome and the German chocolate cupcake simply amazing!
Help me polish this: This place is absolutely delightful! I decided to try their sweets and boy, was I blown away by the incredible variety they had to offer. The gooey butter cookies were absolutely awesome, and I can't even find words to describe how mind-blowingly amazing the German chocolate cupcake was!

input:
Decent frozen yogurt with a lot of options for toppings. They have about 8 different froyo flavors to chose from. Lots of possible combinations. However, it can get expensive pretty quickly when you weigh the cup. 

There's not a lot of seating inside. Staff is friendly but not very active. I do want to try their bubble tea, but j wasn't very impressed.
Help me polish this: This frozen yogurt place offers a great variety of flavors and toppings, allowing for endless combinations. However, the cost can escalate rapidly when the cup is weighed. The limited seating inside might be inconvenient. While the staff is friendly, they are not particularly attentive. Although I was curious to try their bubble tea, I found it to be underwhelming.

input:
I loved this place!  We drove down from Tahoe just to eat here!  The 90 miles round trip was worth it!  The food was that good!  The Chicken Basil was the best!  And they have good Boba Tea!

Don't believe the nay-sayer about this place.  The food was pretty authentic Taiwanese.  Try it and see for yourself!
Help me polish this:
I absolutely adored this place! We made a special trip all the way from Tahoe just to dine here, and I must say, the 90-mile round trip was completely justified. The quality of the food was exceptional, surpassing our expectations. The Chicken Basil dish stood out as an absolute gem, bursting with incredible flavors. Additionally, their selection of Boba Tea was excellent. 

I implore you to disregard any negative opinions you may have heard about this establishment. The food genuinely reflected the authentic Taiwanese cuisine I have experienced before. Give it a try and judge for yourself - you won't be disappointed!

input:
Cru is such a cute quaint wine bar! In the front is a wine store and in the back ins the wine bar. The wine bar area is small but had a very modern atmosphere.

I started off with the Vina Vino wine flight and my friends ordered The Bold and the Beautiful. Both came on a cute wood/chalkboard board with the wine written in chalk. All the wines were very tasty but the Vespucci  Primitivo and the Il Fauno di Arcanum were my favorite.

We then ordered the fig jam and prosciutto, bleu cheese, arugula flatbread. A little heavy on the blue cheese for my liking but overall was really good. We also ordered the Farmers Platter. You can choose anything from 1-7 items and build your plate from a variety of cheese and meats. We selected the Brillat-Savarin, Cypress Grove "Purple Haze", Blue Brie, Spressata and the Italian Speck. The farmers plate also came with jam, mustard,  caramelized nuts and crostini. The Farmers plate by far was my favorite!

Overall I really liked CRU. Its cute, quaint and cozy. Can't wait to come back!!

To begin our evening, I opted for the Vina Vino wine flight, while my friends chose The Bold and the Beautiful. These delightful selections were beautifully presented on a cute wooden chalkboard board, with the names of the wines elegantly written in chalk. Accompanied by an array of condiments such as jam, mustard, caramelized nuts, and crostini, the Farmers Platter stole the show and became my absolute favorite!

In conclusion, I thoroughly enjoyed my experience at CRU. Its charming, quaint, and cozy environment was a delightful setting to relax and unwind. I'm already counting down the days until I can return for another visit!
