input:
First impression:

Home Wine Kitchen's "No Menu Monday" is a must-try for anyone interested in the St. Louis fine dining scene or good food more generally.  We came prepared with reservations, but the restaurant actually began quieting out while our delicious meal was ramping up; the tables offer more elbow room than the photographs online belie.  As the name of the evening suggests, no menu is in play here; you'll let your friendly server know if you have any food allergies or particular preferences, and before long watch your customized meal unfold.  That's a three-course meal, $30, plus $12 for three half-glass wine pairings.

As starters, we were served lamb meatballs -- likely the favorite of the night -- and goat cheese-stuffed poblano peppers.  The peppers had a good bit of spice offset by the chalkiness of the goat cheese, making an excellent pairing for my Soave (white wine).  The mains were a corvina fish delicately cooked in wax paper and a swordfish steak served over asparagus with homegrown tomatoes and "love sauce."  The corvina came out on the rarer side, perhaps a little too complex for this Midwesterner's palate, but the hearty swordfish was some of the best seafood I've tasted in Missouri.  Dessert comprised a champagne gelatin and a chocolate tart, both of which were topped by fluffy homemade whipped cream and quickly eaten.

The staff at Home Wine Kitchen made our visit pleasant, acting casual yet professional during our meal.  The restaurant patrons seemed to be largely industry types that oohed and aahed about the cuisine (perhaps a trifle self-importantly, but this Yelper is no saint himself).  I was surprised to note that other diners were served the same courses as we were (albeit in different configurations), when I was under the assumption there would be a little more variation; however, I can only imagine the challenge such an endeavor would pose to the talented kitchen.  The interior, lighting, and volume here were all very good.

By the end of the evening, we realized that putting yourself in the hands of the chef is not for the faint of heart, as evidenced by one conversation near us during the meal that all but stopped when a beautiful whole fish was served to the table.  Leaving the restaurant, I was glad that I had tried No Menu Monday, but did wonder what the meal would have been like had I ordered off the menu.  I guess that calls for a return visit, don't you?

input:
Went here with a few friends as the place to have our reunion dinner. We hadn't seen eachother since elementary school and got reacquainted through Facebook so this was a pretty special dinner. 

The restaurant is very swanky and the prices show this. I do think the food was worth the price although all of my party thought it was very expensive. I ordered the lobster bake which was delicious. It was not fantastic and there wasn't alot of seafood but it was adequate for me. I also ordered a Neopolitan Old Fashion which was made perfectly. 

My friends ordered the fritters, carpaccio, crab cake and fries. Plus 2 shots of tequila, a lemonade and 2 more old fashions. Bill was $170 which is not bad but some of my friends weren't expected it. 

And I must say something about our waiter. Unfortunately, I didn't remember his name but he was fantastic! Very attentive, nice and even bought out a dessert because it was also one of my friend's bday. He was just real cool. 

5 stars for service
3 stars for food
4 stars for ambience 
2 stars for price.  

But I was satisfied.
Help me polish this:
I recently visited this restaurant with a few friends for our long-awaited reunion dinner. We hadn't seen each other since elementary school and reconnected through Facebook, so this dinner was incredibly special for all of us.

The restaurant had an upscale and sophisticated atmosphere, but the prices were quite high in line with that. While all of my friends felt that the food was expensive, I personally found it worth the price. I opted for the lobster bake, which was undeniably delicious. Although it lacked a generous amount of seafood, it was sufficient for my taste. Additionally, I ordered a perfectly crafted Neopolitan Old Fashioned cocktail, which further enhanced my dining experience.

Among my friends, the ordered dishes included fritters, carpaccio, crab cake, and fries. Along with these, we also had 2 shots of tequila, a lemonade, and 2 more Old Fashioned cocktails. The total bill amounted to $170, which I personally considered reasonable, but it did catch some of my friends off guard.

Now, I must take a moment to express my gratitude towards our waiter. Unfortunately, I cannot recall his name, but he provided exceptional service throughout the entire evening. He was incredibly attentive, pleasant, and even surprised us with a complimentary dessert in celebration of my friend's birthday. Truly, he was a remarkable and memorable part of the dining experience.

In terms of rating, I would give 5 stars for service, 3 stars for the food, 4 stars for the ambience, and 2 stars for the price. However, despite the slightly higher price range, I left the restaurant feeling satisfied with my overall experience.

input: My first trip to Susanna Foo was at 6 months old when the restaurant was still a hole-in-the-wall takeout joint owned by Susanna's parents. My parents have been taking my brother and I ever since. I have many fond memories of Susanna fashioning dolls for us out of the linen napkins and preparing Chicken with Cashew Nuts when we refused to eat anything else. The food has always been reliable, but now that I am an adult, I find it lacking excitement. The service is always impeccable and I have never been disappointed by the overall decor or ambience. I'd like to see Susanna improve upon some of her traditional recipes by either adding new flavors or perhaps returning to her Chinese roots with a more ethnic menu. I'm hoping there will be a revitalization and that I will come to love Susanna Foo as much as I did as a child.
Help me polish this: My very first visit to Susanna Foo was when I was just six months old. Back then, it was a cozy little takeout joint owned by Susanna's parents. Since then, my parents have been bringing my brother and me there regularly, creating countless cherished memories. I can still recall how Susanna used to craft dolls for us using linen napkins, and how she would whip up her famous Chicken with Cashew Nuts whenever we were stubborn about eating anything else. The food has always been consistently good, but as I've grown into an adult, I find myself yearning for something more exciting. However, I must admit that the service has always been impeccable, and I have never been let down by the overall ambiance and decor of the restaurant. In order to rekindle my love for Susanna Foo, I hope to see her experiment with new flavors or even explore her Chinese heritage by introducing a more diverse and ethnic menu. My wish is for a revitalization that will bring back the enchantment I felt as a child, and make me fall in love with Susanna Foo all over again.

input: I am from California and was looking for something besides the hotel dining room to have dinner at.  I usually use the Yellow Pages to find restaurants and judge them by the size of their ads.  Spiro's jumped out at me, not because of the size of their advertisement (small) but Greek food just sounded good to me tonight.  I wasn't disappointed at all.  The Greek lemon soup was excellent and I liked the Moussaka, although the waiter suggested the Sea Bass.  All in all, the dinner was terrific and if I am back in this area, I will head to Spiro's again.  Thanks Neil for the wonderful service!

Typically, I would turn to the Yellow Pages to discover restaurants, often judging them solely based on the size of their advertisements. input: I'm a Barbecue judge and this ain't barbecue.  Not in Texas, not in the southeast.  Not in KC.  An earlier reviewer nailed it perfectly.  The brisket is fatty pot roast.  No evidence of smoke.  Mushy texture like long braised  meat.  My sandwich was 75 percent fat.  Big meatless chunks of fat.  Either the owner doesn't care or he's left the place in the hands of employees who don't know any better. Sorry.  But you can do much better elsewhere.
Help me polish this: As a Barbecue judge, I must express my disappointment in the barbecued offerings at this establishment. Whether in Texas, the southeast, or Kansas City, this does not meet the standards of authentic barbecue. Another reviewer accurately described it, and I concur, that the brisket resembles fatty pot roast rather than the beautifully smoked meat we expect. The lack of smoky flavor further adds to the disappointment. The texture is overly tender, akin to meat that has been braised for an extended period. Regrettably, my sandwich consisted of an alarming amount of fat, with sizable meatless chunks. It appears that either the owner does not prioritize quality or they have entrusted the operation to employees who lack the necessary expertise. I apologize for the negativity, but I believe there are far better barbecue options available elsewhere.

input:

The music is lively, as are the patrons. Don't expect to swim in the water, it's a rocky beach, not much sand. Have been taking our boys since they were babies...are fifteen now. The food and drinks don't make an impression either way, it's the view and atmosphere that draws you in. 

Never disappoints.

Let's refine this:

One of the highlights is joining the crowd in applauding as the sun gracefully disappears below the horizon, providing a magical end to the day.

With a vibrant ambiance and lively music, this place is always buzzing with cheerful patrons. Although the beach may not be ideal for swimming due to its rocky terrain and lack of sand, it has been our go-to spot to bring our boys since they were infants, who are now fifteen. The food and drinks may not leave a lasting impression, but it's the breathtaking view and inviting atmosphere that truly captivate.

No matter how many times we visit, this place never fails to meet our high expectations.

input: I decided to stop by since I was in the area and craving some authentic Mexican cuisine. I was literally by myself (late lunchtime on a tues) and really excited to try the pazole!! Help me polish this: I decided to stop by this restaurant since I was in the area and had a craving for some authentic Mexican cuisine. I believe it's made with pork and includes hominy, lettuce, radishes, onions, and they even provide a small container of dried oregano. The lettuce tends to wilt a bit, which I'm not a big fan of, but adding some hot sauce really makes it a satisfying meal on its own. The service provided by the sweet lady was amazing, and everything served seemed very fresh. Although I wasn't the biggest fan of the sweet salsa, I must admit that it was a matter of personal preference. Nonetheless, I highly recommend trying their pineapple water. Despite not being a fan of pineapples, I read some great reviews and decided to try it, and I'm glad I did. It's a must-try. I'm already looking forward to coming back to try their burritos, especially since this restaurant is conveniently close to Costco, where I often shop. input:
by 3 stars, i really mean 3.5-

white brick walls, cool rustic furniture, seasoned, attractive employees. and the lighting is lovely.. nay, PERFECT. probably good for a blind date.  and service is good and timely.

but 3.5 could've been 4 if it wasn't so expensive for what i'm getting. and if the kitchen was more accommodating.

the first time i ever ate there, (around when it first opened), i ordered ravioli and received 3 or 5 pieces for $11-13.  another time i visited, i tried substituting a salad for fries with my burger. and my server said, "no, sorry, the kitchen won't do that." 

are you $^%ER@# kidding me??? it wasn't a super modification. it's not as if i asked for a burger with only one bun, no tomato, half piece of lettuce, two onion rings, and love. it wasn't like i wanted to substitute lobster for fries!!! needless to say, this is the first time i've been unable to substitute. i'm usually really easy to please, but this is the first time i've ever felt difficult. at least in my head. is this in my head?

unforgivable.
Help me polish this:
By 3 stars, I really mean 3.5-

With its white brick walls, cool rustic furniture, seasoned, attractive employees, and perfect lighting, this place seems ideal for a blind date. The service is also commendable, with good and timely assistance.

However, I must admit that the rating could have been higher if it weren't for the prices being on the expensive side for what I received, and the lack of flexibility from the kitchen.

During my initial visit, around the time of its opening, I ordered ravioli and was surprised to receive only 3 or 5 pieces for $11-13. On another occasion, I attempted to substitute a salad for fries with my burger, only to be told by my server that the kitchen wouldn't accommodate the request.

Are you kidding me? It wasn't a major modification. I didn't ask for a burger with numerous specific alterations; I simply wanted to exchange fries for a salad. It's not like I was requesting lobster instead of fries! Needless to say, this was the first time I've encountered such refusal to substitute. Normally, I'm quite easygoing, but this experience made me question my own reasonableness. Is this all in my head?

To me, this lack of flexibility is unforgivable.

input: I would eat here again, but mostly because it is an interesting destination in a town with a lot of bad restaurants. Great decor, noisy atmosphere, and funky vibe. Help me polish this: Overall, I would consider dining at this establishment again, although my decision is mainly driven by the lack of decent options in the town. input:
So, I went back to El Arado on Monday with a group of six people. The staff seemed shocked about our 6 pm arrival, and "sanitized" a large table for us quickly. Yes, the table smelled like dirty sanitized rags, ugh, but, once you got buzzed on...I mean beyond, the smell, your waiter will appear and take your drink orders. 

We got beers and margaritas. The margarita drinker in the group declared that it "was good."  The prices for drinks weren't that bad.  ($2.95 for Mexican beers). 

We all ordered our food, which was brought out at a good time, fresh, and hot. Everyone snarfed - it was good and tasty and all our needs were met attentively by the quiet waiter. 

All of us were let satisfied, and our specific requests (i.e. "no beans" "light on the cheese") were met by the kitchen staff with no problems. We left with full bellies then went to the Red Garter for a mind-numbing strip club experience. 

What a way to wrap up a review..

El Arado has gotten a bad wrap - but, the staff is decent, the food wasn't too shabby and the drink prices are cheap. A good place to start out for affordable and filling eats before a night out in Fountain Square (or to strip clubs).
Help me polish this:
On Monday, I revisited El Arado with a group of six people. Surprisingly, the staff appeared taken aback by our 6 pm arrival but quickly prepared a large table for us. Admittedly, the table had a slight unpleasant odor due to being recently sanitized, but once we overlooked this minor issue, our waiter promptly took our drink orders.

We opted for both beers and margaritas. The margarita enthusiasts among us declared that the drinks were satisfying. What pleasantly surprised us was that the prices for the drinks were quite reasonable, with Mexican beers priced at $2.95.

After placing our orders, our food arrived promptly, fresh and piping hot. We all eagerly dug in, thoroughly enjoying the delicious and flavorful dishes. The attentive and unassuming waiter ensured that all our requests, such as having no beans or a light amount of cheese, were met without any hassle.

Leaving the restaurant with satisfied stomachs, we decided to continue our evening at the Red Garter for an unforgettable strip club experience.

So, to sum it up, El Arado deserves a fair review. Despite its questionable reputation, the staff is courteous, the food is more than decent, and the prices for drinks are surprisingly affordable. It's a great spot to grab a filling and affordable meal before venturing into Fountain Square or even heading to nearby strip clubs.

input:
I could say that this is a touch of Italy in a strip mall, but even I recognize that is a little too precious. Stepping into the dark, cool interior of Sapore made for a refreshing change after the sweltering July heatwave. It was no problem for our party of three to be seated; the fact that we had a reservation helped, I am sure. We started out with drinks--bellinis for my two dinner companions and a classic vodka martini for me. I appreciated being able to customize my drink with a blue-cheese-stuffed olive and an anchovy. I would never have thought to put an anchovy in a martini, but it looks like this will be a new obsession for me. 

On to the food. We opted to skip the appetizers and go straight to soup/salad and entrees (all the better to save room for dessert). My mom went with the Italian soup and my other dining companion and I split the Caprese salad, a solid presentation that did not blow me away, but certainly does not provide grist for anything like the negative reviews of this establishment that I have seen on yelp. I didn't know what to expect in terms of pasta portions here, so I went with the Chicken Marsala. It might have been nice to have pasta to pick up some of the sauce, but I appreciated that the dish was hot by temperature and I even had enough for leftovers (to which I added pasta, in the comfort and convenience of my home).

The dessert selection was excellent. We went with the tiramisu. I understand Sapore also has an excellent cannoli which I would like to try on a future visit. I would be tempted to come back, if only for another excellent martini, appetizers, and another run through the dessert menu.
Help me polish this:
I could describe this place as a taste of Italy tucked away in a strip mall, but that might be a bit too exaggerated. Stepping into the cool and dimly lit interior of Sapore provided a welcome reprieve from the scorching July heatwave. Fortunately, our party of three had no trouble finding a table, thanks to our reservation. We started off the evening with some refreshing bellinis for my dinner companions and a classic vodka martini for myself. What impressed me was the opportunity to customize my drink with a blue-cheese-stuffed olive and an anchovy. Putting an anchovy in a martini was a surprising revelation for me and it seems like I've found a new obsession.

Now, let's talk about the food. We decided to forego appetizers and dive straight into soups, salads, and entrees, all in order to leave room for dessert. My mother chose the Italian soup while my other dining companion and I shared the Caprese salad. The salad was decent, nothing mind-blowing, but definitely not deserving of the negative reviews I've seen on Yelp about this place. As for the portion sizes of pasta, I wasn't sure what to expect, so I went with the Chicken Marsala. It would have been nice to have some pasta to soak up the delicious sauce, but I appreciated that the dish was served hot. Plus, I even had enough leftovers to enjoy at home with some pasta added in for the ultimate comfort and convenience.

The dessert selection at Sapore was outstanding. We opted for the tiramisu, but I've heard their cannoli is also excellent and I plan to try it on a future visit. To be honest, I may be tempted to return just for their fantastic martinis, appetizers, and another round of exploring their dessert menu.

They are truly outstanding, not greasy and finished with paresan cheese. The metaphorical cherry-on-top was the chocolate milkshake (which actually had no cherry on top). The shake was nothing fancy, but perfectly made, creamy, not too sweet or over-chocolatey. 
If you want your upscale burger experience but still want your burger-fries-shake holy trinity, come here.

The regular fries alone are a delicious treat, but once you try the truffle fries, you'll be truly impressed. These fries are remarkably outstanding, boasting a non-greasy texture and a finishing touch of Parmesan cheese. To top off your meal, indulge in their metaphorical cherry-on-top: the chocolate milkshake, which, despite its lack of an actual cherry, is perfectly crafted. Creamy, balanced in sweetness, and not overly chocolaty, it truly hits the spot. If you're seeking an elevated burger experience without sacrificing the classic burger-fries-shake trifecta, this is the place to be.

input: Maybe I just had bad luck at this property but I am a SPG gold member... quickly approaching platinum and made a reservation at this property. I payed a good amount for my room and when I asked for a larger room they told me they where all the same. I asked did every room have adjoining doors and was told yes. I then told the front desk clerk that I could hear EVERYTHING going on next door including sneezing and even AC talking on CNN 360 very clearly. He told me to come down and get a new key and move to a room there was nobody in. They did not offer to bring me a key or help me move. When I got to the lobby the line was at least 10 people deep and there was only ONE person there. I just gave up and dealt with the noise and a few hours later they finally turned off the TV and I could sleep.  There is nothing fancy about this hotel and the service for sure needs improvement!
Help me polish this:
Perhaps I simply had an unfortunate experience at this particular property, but as a dedicated SPG gold member on the verge of reaching platinum status, I expected a higher level of service. input:
Its a hotel and you can stay there.

After a couple of stays here I find it is not bad. 

Its definitely more of a business traveler kind of place than a tourist kind of place.

Pros
The rooms have the essentials. The beds are quite comfortable.
The cafe isn't bad although it is a little foggy as to what comes with the room. Apparently its one entree and one beverage. Not a bad deal.

Help me polish this:
I have stayed at this hotel a couple of times now and overall, it's not too bad. 

I would say that it caters more towards business travelers rather than tourists.

Here are some positives of the hotel. Firstly, the rooms are well-equipped with all the essentials. Additionally, the beds are quite comfortable, ensuring a good night's sleep. 

The cafe at the hotel is decent, although it could use some clarification on what is included with the room. From my understanding, it offers one entree and one beverage, which is a decent deal.

However, there are a few downsides to consider. The hallways could use some maintenance as they appear a bit shaggy. However, this didn't really bother me since I didn't spend much time in the hallway.

Unfortunately, the room cleaning service let me down during my last stay. While the room itself was clean, I discovered a bag from Burger King in my mini fridge, which was definitely not a pleasant surprise.

Overall, despite its flaws, the hotel provides a satisfactory experience, particularly for business travelers.

input:
I recently moved in a few blocks away from Henry's and was looking forward to having a neighborhood coffee spot not far from my house. So, on a beautifully humid August morning I walked over to check it. 

1) The atmosphere is pretty standard. Open space with the coffee bar in the back left corner and ordinary tables and chairs scattered throughout. No college coffee shop couches or armchairs but no industrial airbnb chic vibe either. Lacked uniqueness. 

2) The name Henry reminds me of Thomas the tank engine. Was there a train named Henry on there or not? If so, was he chill or not. Could add one star for chill train association. 

3) The coffee was not good. I got an iced coffee (STFU) and it was super bitter. The amount of ice in it wasn't obscene so it had that going for it but other than that idk.

I'm coming back to try some hot coffee or espresso on a cooler day but damn Henry :((( not a great first impression.
Help me polish this:
I recently moved just a few blocks away from Henry's and was excited about having a convenient neighborhood coffee spot near my house. So, on a beautiful, humid August morning, I decided to walk over and check it out.

1) The atmosphere at Henry's is quite standard. It's an open space with the coffee bar located in the back left corner, and the tables and chairs are arranged in a typical fashion. While it doesn't have the cozy couches or armchairs you might find at a college coffee shop, it also doesn't have a trendy, industrial Airbnb vibe. It lacks a bit of uniqueness.

2) The name "Henry" reminds me of Thomas the Tank Engine. I'm uncertain if there was a train named Henry on the show, but if there was, and if he was a chill character, it could add a star to the overall appeal for me. A subtle nod to childhood nostalgia is always a plus.

3) Unfortunately, the coffee at Henry's left much to be desired. I ordered an iced coffee (STFU), which turned out to be overly bitter. The amount of ice in it was reasonable, but other than that, I wasn't particularly impressed.

Despite this disappointing first impression, I'm open to giving Henry's another chance. I plan to return on a cooler day and try their hot coffee or espresso. Perhaps that will provide a different experience. But for now, Henry, I must admit, you didn't leave the best impression on me.

input:
We were thoroughly impressed with this hotel! Upon arriving, you are immediately welcomed with the scent of fresh baked cookies. Walking up to the desk we were greeted by Valorie who informed us that cookies and water were complementary to guests and that we were more than welcome. Across from the desk we noticed a book shelf. This is not the kind of book shelf where rejected leftovers were placed but rather, a wide range of books by well known authors. The name of the program was called Read it and Return. In essence, you can borrow a book for the duration of your stay and if you don't finish it you can return it the next time you stay at the hotel at any of the Carlson hotels who have the same program! ( what!?! Cookies and books!?! YES!) Right off the bat, we felt like we were right at home.

   Arriving at our room, we noticed that everything was extremely clean and there was a refrigerator (with a small freezer) , a microwave, a coffee maker, and a well working A.C. (you know, the kind that you don't have to yell over to have a conversation). The bathroom was stocked with brand name shampoo, conditioner, and lotion.

  Our next stop was the smoking area. Normally, smokers feel as though they have been marooned to a small place behind the dumpster...but not here! Provided was 2 sets of swinging benches; set far enough away so that it did not disturb the guests in rooms around the area but no a 10 mile hike for those adults who enjoy the pleasure. Did I also mention they have smoking rooms available?

In the morning, feel free to partake in a complimentary breakfast (NOT CONTINENTAL)-I mean a real breakfast which changes daily; anything from fresh made waffles to eggs, sausage, and bacon! Also, cold cereal, juices, and coffees have options! Coffee is available 24/7 as well! 

The hotel also has a pool and hot tub which I personally observed them clean daily!

On our last night we got back late and I was going to ask the desk for a late check out, but there was no need! Their check out time is 12:00 Pm as opposed to the hotel usual of 11:00 Am. That worked out well for us.

At checkout we were asked if there was anything we would change about the hotel or our stay. I made small suggestions which I thought would help them, but definitely nothing major. The desk person wrote down what I said and said she would pass it on! I was impressed with that, because we've been asked about our stay at other places, but it seemed more out of routine than actual interest. Here, she seemed genuinely interested. We don't usually do reviews, so I'm sorry for the long review. However, we wanted you to get a real feel for this wonderful hotel and hope that you enjoy it as much as we did! Thanks for reading and safe travels. J & Niki.

input: Let me start by saying buying a car is an intimidating process. I feel like I am playing poker with someone who can see all of the cards while I can only see my cards. I felt well prepared and needed to use all of my preparation to get what I considered to be a fair deal (time will tell whether I really got a fair deal) on a used (pre-owned is what they like to say) car. Do your homework (KBB.com, Edmunds.com etc) As long as the car performs like I expect it to over time, I will be happy. Sam Ladd was the salesman who always treated me courteously and let me drive lots of cars while I was deciding what vehicle I wanted. I drove everything from subcompacts to full sized SUVs. I visited many dealerships I chose Toyota of Santa Barbara because they ultimately had the vehicle that I wanted. I bought what I believe will meet my families needs. The negotiation process was business like and I believe that Frank Flores the sales manager was up front with me and answered my concerns. Be prepared and stick to your position throughout the process.

input:
3 separate reviews:

CITY TOUR: 1 STAR -Not worth the time or money. We never got a confirmation email when booking over the phone. Then during the tour we had to wait and be hassled over payment that was already cleared on our account. Don't do this tour if you get carsick easily. It was full and we had to sit in the back. You can't see anything on the tour through the tinted windows and you only stop at two places that I never would have stopped at on my own. 

The only intriguing part was the Katrina history during the visit the the 9th ward. Do yourself a favor and take the green street cars, save your money and REALLY see things on your own time. We couldn't get pictures of anything and wish we would have done a walking tour instead or tried the red bus tours.

PLANTATION TOUR: 5 STARS! Our driver Stacie gave us a history of the surrounding area and a lot of cool information on our way to the plantation. Laura Creole plantation had an amazing history. Our guide there was Ethan and he did a really good job explaining about the owners journey to this land and how the slaves were treated and also their journey. We felt that it was a balanced historical view of the plantation in general. After that tour we went to the Oak Alley plantation. The grounds alone are worth the trip. The tour guides really focus on the landowners and not so much on the lives of the slaves living there. But you have some time after the tour to visit the  slave quarters on your own. But we wished that there would have been a more balanced explanation of both experiences like at the Laura Plantation. The buses are big and you can recline and take a nap on your way back to the hotel. (No car sickness) 

SWAMP TOUR: 4 STARS and we didn't even see any alligators! This would have been a five-star tour if we would have seen alligators. But our guide Henry was very thorough and explained a lot of great details about the surrounding area. We got to see some boars, raccoons, and birds. It started to rain with thunder and lightning so we did not see any alligators because we had to go back for safety reasons. We did try to see some alligators but they don't come out if it's cold. Don't book your tour if it's cold or storming and I'm sure it will be a 5 star tour for you.  The buses are big and you can recline and take a nap on your way back to the hotel. (No car sickness)
Help me polish this:
CITY TOUR: 1 STAR - This tour was a disappointment and not worth the time or money. We encountered multiple issues, starting with the lack of a confirmation email after booking over the phone. During the tour, we had to endure unnecessary delays and payment hassles, despite already clearing our account. Sitting in the back of the full bus added to our discomfort and made it impossible to see anything through the tinted windows. Furthermore, the tour only made two stops, neither of which were places we would have chosen to visit on our own. The only redeeming aspect was learning about the history of Katrina during our visit to the 9th ward. Save yourself the trouble and opt for the green street cars instead to explore the city at your own pace. We regret not choosing a walking tour or the red bus tours, which would have provided a much better experience.

PLANTATION TOUR: 5 STARS! Our driver, Stacie, added an extra layer of enjoyment to the tour by sharing interesting historical facts about the surrounding area during the journey to the plantation. Once we arrived at Laura Creole plantation, our guide, Ethan, did a commendable job in providing us with a comprehensive understanding of the owner's journey to the land and the treatment of the slaves. It felt like a well-balanced historical view of the plantation. Our next destination was Oak Alley plantation, and the impressive grounds alone made the trip worthwhile. However, we wished the tour guides focused more on the lives of the slaves in addition to the landowners, similar to the approach taken at the Laura Plantation. Nevertheless, we appreciated that we had the opportunity to explore the slave quarters independently. The spacious buses allowed for a comfortable return journey to the hotel, and we even had the luxury to recline and have a nap. Plus, there were no concerns about car sickness.

SWAMP TOUR: 4 STARS - Unfortunately, we didn't have the chance to see any alligators on this tour, hence the missing star. However, our guide, Henry, made up for it with his extensive knowledge of the area, providing fascinating insights along the way. Instead of alligators, we encountered boars, raccoons, and various bird species, which was still enjoyable. Due to adverse weather conditions, including rain, thunder, and lightning, we had to prioritize safety and were unable to witness alligators. It's advisable not to book this tour during cold or stormy weather if you're hoping to see alligators. Otherwise, it would undoubtedly be a five-star experience. The comfortable and spacious buses allowed for a relaxing journey back to the hotel without any concerns about car sickness.

input: Never been to this location before, never had a problem with any other location. It was almost full but there were a handful of tables open. Our waitress mentioned that our food was almost ready, but we expressed that we didn't want to wait any longer. She kindly informed us that we didn't need to pay for our drinks, and we left. There was no apology offered, and it left me wondering if our waitress had forgotten to enter our order or if the kitchen staff simply didn't prioritize the timeliness of food preparation. Despite the lack of visible chaos in the kitchen, I can't pinpoint the exact issue. This experience has compelled me to not return to this establishment, as it felt like a waste of our time.

My husband went for the chocolate dipped cannoli with the original filling, and it was pure delight. As for the Italian wedding cookies, they had the ideal balance of crunchiness and delicacy, with just the right amount of Anise flavor. And let me tell you about the dark chocolate florentine cookies - they were absolutely scrumptious! Even though I'm not a fan of coconut, the combination of chocolate and coconut in these cookies was perfect. Needless to say, we will most definitely be returning to this bakery again and again.

input:
So it is a good friends birthday today and we all met up here. This place has a great, homey feel. It wasn't crowded at all. 

The service was prompt and friendly, my burger was good, not great. Menu said it's charbroiled...seemed more like pan fried, and the meat was well done / dry. Oh well. My buds and I were all having a good time.

Went down to the river and actually found some water!

Good times on Paradise road.
Help me polish this:
So today is my good friend's birthday, and we all decided to meet up at this wonderful place. The ambiance here is cozy and inviting, giving off a homely vibe. Surprisingly, the place wasn't crowded at all, which made our gathering even more enjoyable.

The service we received was prompt and friendly, no complaints there. Now, about the food. I ordered a burger, and while it was good, I wouldn't say it was incredibly amazing. According to the menu, it was supposed to be charbroiled, but it tasted more like it was pan fried. Additionally, the meat was a bit too well done for my liking, rendering it slightly dry. Nevertheless, it didn't damper our spirits as my friends and I were all having a great time.

After our meal, we decided to take a stroll down to the nearby river and, to our surprise, we actually found water! It was such a pleasant surprise and added an extra touch of enjoyment to our day.

All in all, it's been a wonderful time here on Paradise Road, filled with good company and memorable experiences.

input: I read at least 30 reviews before I decided to eat here. The only thing that was good was the oysters because it's raw. Everything else was dry and tasteless. The space is cramp. We had people on our backs coughing on us while sitting at the bar trying to enjoy it. Let's just say the 2 half and half baskets that my boyfriend and I ordered was not worth $60.
Help me polish this: After thoroughly researching through 30 reviews, I ultimately opted to dine at this establishment. However, the only aspect that truly stood out was the oysters due to their raw freshness. Unfortunately, the remaining items on the menu lacked flavor and were disappointingly dry. Furthermore, the limited space was cramped, and we were constantly disturbed by individuals coughing behind us while attempting to savor our meal at the bar. Regrettably, the 2 half and half baskets that my boyfriend and I ordered were highly overpriced at $60 and did not meet our expectations in terms of value.

input:
Dearest Reader,

Please allow me to hereby confirm the rumors: Village Whiskey does, in fact, have the best burger in Philadelphia. And, I should note, some of the best bartenders. 

As my wife and I sat at the bar waiting for our friends to arrive, I marveled at the infinite selection of whiskeys and bourbons. I decided that this, self, is the day you will begin liking whiskey. So I petitioned the bartender to "make me something awesome with whiskey in it." "What kind of drink do you want?," he inquired. "I have no idea, good sir. You see, I am a neophyte, a tyro, and fledgling when it comes to spirits such as these." (Perhaps my banter wasn't quite at this level at the time; I was already a few drinks in from my visit to Franklin Mortgage, but this is how I remember it going.) So, he thought about it for a while and proceeded to mix up the craziest drink I had ever seen -- it had whiskey, orange bitters, an egg white, Portuguese red wine, and other stuff in it! The verdict: delicious. I also had the "The Commodore" off the drink menu, and it was very good, too. The drinks are a little pricey here, and they will set you back around $11 or $12 each.

When our friends arrived, we were seated outside and I got to try to village burger and the short-rib and cheddar duck-fat fries. The burger, which comes with an artfully restrained dollop of homemade thousand island dressing, was unbelievable. The applewood bacon and the dressing served the elevate the already-incredible taste of the meat. I can't wait to come back and order another one. As for the fries, they were very good, but I think next time I will stick with the plain duck fat fries. Our friends ordered those, and they were super crispy and delicious.

Warning: this place gets insanely busy, so you might have to wait a pretty long time for a table. 

All in all, the drinks were great, the food was delectable, and the staff was very knowledgeable and personable. I would totally come back.

Still dreaming of that burger,
Chris M.

input:
I find it hard to believe there are so many people with such low standards when it comes to the Daily Bread.

It is a ripoff of St. Louis Bread Co/Panera Bread, which in of itself I don't mind at all.  I have eaten multiple times at the Daily Bread and have yet to have an enjoyable experience.  The food is so-so at best.  Their sandwiches are basic and lack any real flavor.  I also tried the BBQ Chicken pizza and it was okay.  

I certainly wouldn't steer anyone away from this place based on the food.  The food is basic and simple, not bad but also nothing great.

My biggest qualm with the Daily Bread is the service.  The majority of the workers seem utterly uninterested in helping out.  There was a line of about 6 people and one person at the register.  There was no sense of urgency to help any of the customers in line.  We waited for a good 5-6 minutes to put an order in.  After receiving our cups to get our drinks we looked for a clean place to sit and eventually settled on a table top that was the least dirty of the tables available.  There were plenty of open spots but it just appeared as though there was lots of trash left behind.  Does anyone bus these tables?

I anticipate that people are responsible for cleaning up after themselves, but it appeared as though the tables hadn't been effectively cleaned in a while.  There was also some trash on the floor that hadn't been addressed as well.

The order number was called and the order was only halfway completed.  When we asked which sandwich was ours, we were basically ignored as the girl put up two more orders.   After another few minutes the rest of the order came up and we began to eat.  I tried both items and as I stated before, both were okay.  The problem is that the food was just unable to make up for the lack of organization, the slow speed at which we were served, or the cleanliness of the restaurant.

After 3 attempts, I'm writing the Daily Bread off and won't return.  I'd rather go to St. Louis Bread Co, get the same level of food, but in a clean environment and a timely setting.

I ordered delivery online through Yelp, and the food took about 45 minutes to get to my door.
The delivery driver was friendly.
I ordered a bbq chicken pizza and it was really good. They spread the good stuff out over top of most of the crust which was awesome. I also ordered mozzarella sticks, and they were not really what I was expecting--they weren't breaded, they were deep fried. They were good, just not what I was expecting. They also gave me two free cookies with my order and I have to say they were SO good. They were a little undercooked so they were perfectly chewy and they were almost the best part of my meal (and a nice little surprise). The price was fair and I would order here again for sure, although the wait was a little long.

I placed an online delivery order through Yelp, and it took approximately 45 minutes for the food to arrive at my doorstep. Despite the wait, the delivery driver was very friendly and courteous.

I opted for a BBQ chicken pizza, and I must say it was delicious. The toppings were generously spread across most of the crust, which was absolutely awesome. However, I also ordered mozzarella sticks, and they weren't quite what I expected. Instead of being breaded, they were deep-fried. While they were still tasty, they didn't meet my initial expectations.

To my surprise, the restaurant included two complimentary cookies with my order, and they were outstanding. Despite being slightly undercooked, they had the perfect chewy texture and were arguably the highlight of my meal. It was a delightful bonus and added to my overall satisfaction.

Considering the pricing was fair, I would definitely order from this establishment again, even though the delivery time was a tad long.

input: This is a fabulous gym.  Considering the cost, it provides a lot of fitness opportunities. I look for a gym that has a lot of classes at various times so that I can fit in exercise before or after work. As my work start and end times change from day to day, though, I need a gym that has classes at various times throughout the early morning and mid to late afternoon.  I found that the class schedule here meets that need. The trainers are excellent.  The spin and row teachers are really exceptional.  Try the We-Fit class, but expect a huge challenge, even if you are fit.  The facility is very clean, but this is a new enterprise, so time will tell if the business will continue to keep things clean and fresh.  I love that the women's locker room contains a blow dryer and extra hair ties.  These little things make a huge difference. Thanks for thinking of them.

With my ever-changing work schedule, it's crucial for me to find a gym that accommodates early morning and mid to late afternoon classes, and fortunately, this gym's class schedule perfectly meets that need.

The trainers at this gym are remarkable. The spin and row teachers, in particular, are exceptional and truly master their craft. I highly recommend trying the We-Fit class here, but prepare yourself for a serious challenge, even if you consider yourself fit. 

What sets this gym apart is its exceptional cleanliness. Although it is a new establishment, I have high hopes that they will continue to maintain their impeccable standards in the long run. Keep up the great work, and I look forward to enjoying this fabulous gym for years to come.

input:
If you are in a hurry and don't have time to read my entire review, here's the bottom line:  this place is FANTASTIC!

After my 3 month old car got rear ended TWICE inside of TWO weeks at the end of October, I took my dealership's recommendation and ended up bringing it in to Prestigious for repairs.  I am really glad I chose them.

First off their place is really clean and professional, you feel more like you are in a bank or a business office than a body shop.  I don't mind the typical "shop" feel of most of these places, but the experience at Prestigious is a notch above that and I appreciated it.

Next off, they assigned a specific advisor, Juan Mendez to work with me from start to finish through my repair.  He was really knowledgeable and provided detailed information to me about how they were going to diagnose everything and ensure that all of the various components of the damage were fixed correctly.  There was an added challenge in my case because I was hit in nearly the same place by two different drivers:  one submitted a claim through insurance and the other asked to pay outside of insurance.  I explained all of this to Juan and he came up with a forensically defensible way to determine the value of the damage caused by each of the accidents so that the costs could be assessed fairly and accurately.

Juan set up my rental for me and kept me updated regularly throughout the repair process, which in my case took a while due to the insurance company requiring additional evaluations etc. and the Thanksgiving holiday.  Detailed updates, and the fact that these came to me without me having to ask for them, made it a lot less stressful during the time my car was in the shop.  Juan (and I believe all the other staff who hold similar positions over there) also clearly understands all of the procedures, and deviations that can occur from these procedures, that are related to processing insurance claims and he was always able to answer any questions I had.

I got the vehicle back yesterday and the quality of the work is 1st class.  There is no way to tell that anything ever happened to the back of my car...it looks exactly as it did when I purchased it in late July.  I was particularly concerned about paint matching because all of the exterior damage was to the bumper (a plastic part) which had to be matched to the car body panels (metal parts).  Anyone who knows anything about paint and body work knows that it is a challenge to match paints on different substrates, and most body shops, even Prestigious, have disclaimers about this that are plainly visible in their offices.  I told them up front I was really concerned about this, and they said not to worry.  They were right....they did a dead-perfect color match in my case.  I have mild OCD and I notice even the smallest differences and defects in things, and I was 100% satisfied with the paint match, as well as the gap tolerances etc. on my repair.  If a place can meet my standards, it is going to far surpass most people's standards.

It sucked to get hit twice in two weeks, in a brand new car....but I am thrilled that I found this place as part of the deal.  I would take my vehicles here from now on and recommend them to anyone who wants a top quality job with serious attention paid to fit and finish.

input:
I stopped in for lunch one day after years of, 'I really need to try that place.'  I really like their layout.  They have an uncrowded floor of tables and booths and a lunch counter along one side.  The counter faces the cooks' area, which I like because the bustle of multiple grills, fryers, and prep areas serves as a good distraction, not to mention you get frequent interaction with the staff.  They were busy and getting everything done, but they weren't rude or frazzled, and I had a real sweet waitress.

I ordered the fried shrimp po boy dressed, and asked for a side of rebbeans instead of fries.  I almost had second thoughts on that because the burgers that they were cooking right in front of me looked and smelled so good.  I really have a difficult time resisting the grill.

The food was average and is what you would expect in a tourist spot in the Quarter.  They may get another star if I go back for one of them burgers.

input:
This place was definitely the best dining experience I had in NOLA during my week-long trip! My husband and I walked in without reservations during their Sunday Jazz Brunch. We waited about 40 minutes, but we had the music and ambience to keep us occupied. 

Despite the place being ridiculously busy, our server didn't rush us at all. He encouraged us to take our time browsing the menu and placing our orders- definitely one of the friendliest servers I've encountered. 

The food here was absolutely amazing! The complimentary bread and butter was very nice. My husband and I started off with the seafood gumbo, and it was delicious! Both of us had a sea bass entree and it was definitely the best fish I've ever had. The fish came with a side of green beans and this DELICIOUS sauce that could make anything taste great. We finished off with chocolate orange ice cream and creme brûlée for dessert. The next table over was raving about their bread pudding, so I'm guessing dessert is usually a hit all around at this place. 

The coolest bit about my experience here was that my husband and I got seated where Ronald Reagan sat on his two visits to Mr. B's (far left corner)- Reagan just so happened to visit on my birthday! 

Our bill came out to be $100+ but it was worth every penny. If I'm in NOLA again, I'm definitely revisiting Mr. B's.

input:
If you are visiting Indianapolis, I highly suggest this hotel. My boyfriend and I went just for one night and used his AAA discount which saved us a lot. They have a parking structure attached to the hotel for $20 a night. Starting at the garage they had such cool urban art that continue throughout our stay. The check in was an easy process and the service was amazing. Everywhere you turn there is another interesting piece of art work to look at. Our room was very nice, keurig coffee machine,large luxurious shower, comfy robes, and comfortable california king. We had tickets to the Pacers game which worked out perfectly. We had drinks and dinner before the game at Plat 99 which is in the hotel- again more great decor. They had a whole timeline of cocktails and complementary truffle popcorn. (they also had a really cool outdoor rooftop seating area for the bar, but was too cold and snowy to go out on) Bankers Field house was maybe 1 minute away walking. After the game we came back and got some drinks at Plat 99 again, it was pretty crowded, fun environment. For breakfast we ate at the Market Place downstairs, it was one set price for a buffet and had a lot of good food.

We checked out at 11am- very easy and the concierge was friendly and helpful. Before we left we spent about 30 minutes just walking around the hotel looking at all the art work, it is like a modern art museum. 

Overall we loved this hotel, for a quick getaway to Indianapolis, especially if you are going to a Pacers or Colts game, is was fantastic. Next time I go back to Indianapolis I will be staying here again.
Help me polish this:
If you are planning a visit to Indianapolis, I highly recommend this hotel. During our one-night stay, my boyfriend and I took advantage of his AAA discount, which saved us a significant amount of money. One of the perks of this hotel is the attached parking structure, available at a rate of $20 per night. Right from the start, we were captivated by the stunning urban art displayed throughout the garage and continued throughout our stay.

We had a seamless and hassle-free check-in process, with exceptional service from the staff. The hotel is a treasure trove of interesting artworks at every turn. Our room was exquisite, featuring modern amenities such as a Keurig coffee machine, a spacious and luxurious shower, cozy robes, and a comfortable California king-sized bed.

We had tickets to attend a Pacers game, and the hotel's location couldn't have been more perfect. Before the game, we enjoyed pre-game drinks and dinner at Plat 99, an incredible restaurant within the hotel that stood out for its impeccable decor. The bar offered an extensive cocktail menu with a fascinating historical timeline and served complimentary truffle popcorn. Although we couldn't experience it due to the cold and snowy weather, the rooftop seating area at the bar seemed like a fantastic spot to unwind.

The Bankers Fieldhouse, where the Pacers game took place, was just a one-minute walk away from the hotel. After the game, we returned to Plat 99 for more drinks. The lively atmosphere and bustling crowd made it an enjoyable experience. 

For breakfast, we dined at the Market Place downstairs. It offered a buffet with a diverse selection of delicious food, all for a fixed price.

Check-out at 11 am was a breeze, and the concierge was friendly and accommodating. Before leaving, we spent an additional 30 minutes exploring the hotel and admiring the art collection – it felt like being in a contemporary art museum.

All in all, our experience at this hotel was exceptional. Whether you're looking for a quick getaway to Indianapolis or attending a Pacers or Colts game, this hotel is the perfect choice. We are already looking forward to our next visit, where we will undoubtedly stay here again.

input:
Cashier was trying to put a beer on my to go order and I did not get the fish taco I ordered.

They have nice setting and the establishment seems to be fairly nice, it has got tvs, a bar, a number of tables in various sizes, and a downtown street patio complete with fire heaters for cold nights.

I had the sonoran dog and received two beef tacos that I did not ask for.  The tacos has scraps of beef with cilantro and onion.  They also have the regular styled tacos with tomatoes and lettuce.  The dog was the last one sitting the bin and a bit soggy.  Compared to truck dogs, it does not compare.  The tacos were simply bits of beef with onion and cilantro, nothing impressive and nothing like what is seen in the pictures.

Perhaps, my disappointing experience was due to how the place was packed, had a line out the door by the time I left, and was somewhat loud, but that is no excuse for the terrible eating experience.  They were starting to run out of the beef and dog that I ordered when I got in at the end of a fairly short line, i would hate to think how much worst if I came in a bit later for the dinner rush.
Help me polish this:
The cashier attempted to include a beer in my to-go order, disregarding my request. Additionally, the fish taco that I had ordered was missing from my order.

Despite the restaurant's attractive ambiance, with its TV screens, bar area, ample seating options in various sizes, and a charming downtown street patio complete with fire heaters for colder evenings, my dining experience was lackluster.

I opted for the Sonoran dog but was presented with two beef tacos instead, which I had not requested. These tacos consisted of scraps of beef accompanied by cilantro and onion. Alternatively, the menu also offered traditional-style tacos with tomatoes and lettuce. Unfortunately, the Sonoran dog I received was the last one remaining and had become soggy. It was quite underwhelming compared to the quality typically found in food trucks. The tacos themselves were simply small portions of beef with onion and cilantro, lacking any impressive features and failing to resemble the appetizing presentation depicted in the menu pictures.

Perhaps the disappointing nature of my visit can be attributed to the establishment being exceptionally crowded, evidenced by a line extending out the door by the time I departed. The noise level was also quite high, further detracting from the overall dining experience. Merely being busy, however, does not excuse the subpar quality of the food. It was evident that they were starting to run low on the beef and Sonoran dogs I had ordered, despite my arrival towards the end of a relatively short line. I shudder to think how much worse my experience would have been had I arrived during the dinner rush.

input:
When I was preparing to write this review and give Sam's a particular number of stars, I encountered a dilemma.  Should my star rating be based upon comparing Sam's to all Sports Bars in which I have ever been?  Or, should it be a comparison to Nashville Sports Bars?

I chose the former:  compared to everywhere - because if you're from out of town that only seemed fair.  The sad news is that for a vibrant southeastern city where we have two professional sports teams, our sports bars kinda suck.

Sam's is honestly one of two great sports bars in the city.  I really like Sam's and I really like the patio in Spring, Summer, and early Autumn.  But, when compared to so many sports bars across the country in other cities of comparable size with their own sports' teams... Sam's is just mediocre.  

The service is always a toss up, and the ladies dressed in those referee outfits - could you not find some attractive Southern women to put on those booty shorts and v-cut referee shirts?  Some of the regular old-time employees who have been there since I was in undergrad - a decade ago - really should not be wearing tight clothes.  Wow.  That was just really mean.  I'm sorry.

The food is on the better side of bar fare.  But their beer selection could want for some better beers and a wider variety of selection.  The mixed drinks tend to be a bit weak, in my opinion.

But, hey, it's a bar.  It has lots of TVs and they play the game commentary over the speakers throughout the bar.  All and all, if you want to watch sports at a bar, then I would recommend Sam's.
Help me polish this:
When I sat down to write this review and assign a specific star rating to Sam's, I found myself faced with a dilemma. Should my rating be based on comparing Sam's to all the sports bars I've ever been to, or should it be a comparison specifically to Nashville sports bars?

After considering this, I decided on the former approach - comparing Sam's to sports bars in general - as I wanted to be fair to those who may be visiting from out of town. Unfortunately, the disappointing reality is that our city, despite being home to two professional sports teams, lacks quality sports bars.

Sam's, however, stands out as one of the two great sports bars in this city. Personally, I really enjoy Sam's, particularly its patio during the spring, summer, and early autumn. However, when comparing it to sports bars in other cities of comparable size with their own sports teams, Sam's falls into the category of being just mediocre.

The service at Sam's can be hit or miss, and I can't help but wish they had found some attractive Southern women to wear those referee outfits instead of the ones I often see. I apologize for my harsh comment earlier; it was uncalled for.

As for the food, it leans towards the better side of typical bar fare. However, the beer selection could use improvement, as they don't offer a wide variety of options or particularly interesting beers. In my opinion, the mixed drinks tend to be on the weaker side as well.

But hey, it's a bar. They have plenty of TVs and play game commentary over the speakers throughout the establishment. Overall, if you're looking to watch sports at a bar, I would recommend Sam's.

input: Great location, great food, and friendly staff! There are only a few seats and the store gets pretty crowded with people waiting for their food. I saw a lot of online order ready to go at the counter and think that would be the smart move the next time I want to come during a weekday lunch rush. Weather permitting, it's great to grab some HCV and eat it in Rittenhouse Square across the street! I've come a few times with friends and coworkers and no one has complained about their choices (vegetarians and meat eaters alike)!
Help me polish this: Fantastic location, delectable cuisine, and an incredibly friendly staff! Although the venue has limited seating and can become quite crowded during peak hours, observing multiple online orders prepared for pickup at the counter gave me the insight to opt for that convenient method during future weekday lunch rushes. If weather permits, indulging in their heavenly culinary delights and savoring them in the serene ambiance of Rittenhouse Square just across the street is an absolute delight! I have visited this establishment numerous times with both friends and coworkers, and without fail, everyone, be they vegetarians or meat lovers, has been thoroughly satisfied with their menu choices.

input: Absolute garbage company. Trying to get from Indy to Chicago and they are more than an hour late, did not inform me of the delay, and their entire customer policy (feel free to read it on the website) consists of "we cannot be held responsible for anything." Sitting at a bus stop with 20 people whom are all having their time wasted with absolutely no recourse.
Help me polish this: This company is an absolute disaster. I was trying to travel from Indy to Chicago and they have not only made me wait for over an hour, but they also failed to inform me about the delay. It's evident from their customer policy (which you can find on their website) that they refuse to take any responsibility for their actions. I'm currently stuck at a bus stop with 20 other frustrated individuals, all of us having our precious time wasted with no options for resolution. input: I'm glad that Michael & Lucy found a way to open up another family restaurant after years at Tony's on Linden (now closed following an ugly family dispute). The food is good and the prices are reasonable (ask about the slice and salad special). The Tuscany design is pleasant as are the owners (Lucy is always sweet and friendly). They have local beer on tap (Figueroa, Island Brew and others), 3 HD sports TVs inside, one HD sports TV outside for patio diners, a TV dedicated to surf videos and a TV dedicated to kids shows (and a classic old family friendly Ms Pac-Man game that was a hit with 2 kids when I was there). It's a tough location but I hope they make it work. Santa Claus Lane seems to be having a bit of a Renaissance after many years of being known mostly for outdated kitschy roadside attractions. Good luck!
Help me polish this:
I'm delighted to see that Michael and Lucy have successfully opened a new family restaurant, following their time at Tony's on Linden (which unfortunately closed due to a family dispute). The quality of the food is excellent, and the prices are very reasonable (be sure to inquire about the slice and salad special). The restaurant's Tuscany design creates a pleasant atmosphere, in line with the friendly nature of the owners themselves (Lucy is always sweet and welcoming). 

In addition to the great food and ambiance, the restaurant boasts a selection of local beers on tap, including Figueroa and Island Brew, among others. For sports enthusiasts, there are three high-definition TVs indoors, and an additional one outdoors for those enjoying the patio area. In a thoughtful touch, one TV is dedicated to surf videos, while another is dedicated to kids shows. Moreover, there is a classic and beloved family-friendly Ms Pac-Man game, which proved to be a hit with the two kids I saw during my visit.

Although the location is challenging, I sincerely hope that Michael and Lucy are able to thrive. Santa Claus Lane seems to be experiencing a revitalization after numerous years of being primarily known for outdated and cheesy roadside attractions. Best of luck to them in their new endeavor!

input: Don't let the shopping center location deter you! Amazing place and even a more amazing staff. Curtis is the true epitome of great service. Loves his job and wants nothing more than for you to enjoy your dining experience. Try the scallops small plate, you won't regret it, but the whole dining experience is top notch.
Help me polish this: Don't let the fact that it is located in a shopping center discourage you from visiting this hidden gem! It is an incredible place with an even more incredible staff. Curtis, in particular, embodies the essence of exceptional service. He genuinely loves his job and strives to ensure that you have a truly enjoyable dining experience. Be sure to try their scallops small plate, as it is simply unforgettable. However, I must say that the entire dining experience is truly top notch.

input: Awesome! Loved this place. Great little breakfast joint easy walk south of route 90. Easy walk from French Quarter and surrounding areas. We got the bananas foster and it was incredible. Great decorations and colorful setting that feels like how you'd expect New Orleans to feel. Highly recommend.
Help me polish this:
This place is absolutely amazing! I couldn't have asked for a better breakfast experience. It's a charming little breakfast joint located just a short walk south of route 90. The best part is, it's also within easy walking distance from the French Quarter and surrounding areas.

We ordered the bananas foster and it was out of this world. I can't even put into words how incredible it tasted. The flavors were divine and the presentation was stunning. 

The restaurant itself is beautifully decorated with vibrant colors and a lively ambiance that perfectly captures the essence of New Orleans. From the moment you step inside, you'll feel like you've walked right into the heart of the city. 

I can't recommend this place enough. If you're looking for a fantastic breakfast spot with a true New Orleans vibe, this is the place to go. Trust me, you won't be disappointed!

input:
Great birthday cakes...I mean it.
  BUT: The cupcakes and cookies out front tend to be stale at times...although when I have complained they made good on everything. 
  I will go back!
Help me polish this: Great birthday cakes...and I absolutely mean it, the quality is outstanding! The great thing is that whenever I have voiced my concerns, the staff has promptly resolved the issue and made it right. This level of customer service has definitely impressed me, and because of that, I will definitely be returning for more.

input:
Service was a bit slow for Saturday lunch but not unacceptable. Understandable as a new place gets its feet under it. I tried to go Friday night and it was a total mess. Long line and nobody taking names. We left. 

The margarita was great. I had the cilantro chicken enchiladas. Also great! The outdoor seating area was very pleasant under the umbrellas on a lovely Saturday afternoon. 

Overall, I liked it. They just need a bit more time to figure out the flow. I'm thrilled to see something affordable move into my neighborhood. The prices are very reasonable and this place isn't trying to be "casual fancy" like the last two train wrecks that occupied this space.

Hope Loco thrives for years to come!
Help me polish this:
The service during Saturday lunch was slightly slow, but not to the point where it was unacceptable. It's understandable since the establishment is still finding its footing as a new place. However, my experience on Friday night was chaotic. There was a long line and no one was taking names, so we decided to leave.

On a positive note, the margarita I had was excellent. I also thoroughly enjoyed the cilantro chicken enchiladas. The outdoor seating area was delightful, especially on a beautiful Saturday afternoon with the umbrellas providing shade.

In general, I liked the place. They just need a little more time to work out the kinks in terms of their service flow. I'm delighted to have an affordable option in my neighborhood, as the prices are very reasonable. Unlike the previous two disastrous attempts at occupying this space, this place isn't trying to be overly fancy yet manages to maintain a casual atmosphere.

Here's to hoping that Loco thrives for many years to come!

input:

input: A definite go-to place if you're in Treasure Island! Love the char-grilled oysters!  Great staff!  Big outdoor seating area and best yet, it's pet friendly so bring your pup!!!  Coming from Austin where pets are accepted everywhere this is a real bonus for me!
Help me polish this: If you find yourself in Treasure Island, this place is an absolute must-visit! I cannot recommend their char-grilled oysters enough – they are simply divine! And the best part? It's completely pet-friendly, so don't forget to bring your furry friend along! input: Lots and lots of mostly fried seafood. Surprisingly expensive for a working class joint. It's the kind of place a dock worker would take his family for a fancy meal and not feel out of place. And it's definitely a New Orleans sort of experience. But the food isn't that great.
Help me polish this: Indulge in a diverse selection of deep-fried seafood at our establishment, accompanied by an unexpected, higher price point for a working-class joint. This charming eatery caters to families seeking a special dining experience, where even a dock worker can bring their loved ones and feel right at home. Embracing the essence of New Orleans, our restaurant offers an authentic taste of the city. However, regrettably, the culinary delights here may not meet the same high standards as our ambiance and atmosphere.

input: This place came highly recommended from some family that has been here many times. Service was fast and friendly even though they were extremely busy. Food was very tasty with mostly basic fare for breakfast.  The Cajun tasso omelet was fantastic. Not too spicy but just enough. Hash browns were fluffy and delicious. Other food at the table was French toast and eggs over medium. Everybody left satisfied and full. Will def come back for more next visit.
Help me polish this: This place comes highly recommended by some family members who have been here numerous times. Despite being extremely busy, the service was fast and friendly. The food itself was incredibly delicious, offering mainly basic options for breakfast. Notably, the Cajun tasso omelet was fantastic - not overly spicy, but just enough to add a kick. The hash browns were just as impressive, being fluffy and delicious. Additionally, others at the table enjoyed dishes such as French toast and eggs over medium. Everyone left feeling satisfied and full. I will definitely be coming back for more during my next visit.

input: I came here with a group of four and had a great experience. There are tons of interesting appetizers to try--we had dumplings with corn and mushrooms, wings, and some specials that are escaping me. Each of us also got an order of noodles. These are not chinatown noodle house portions, but they also aren't chinatown noodle house ingredients. Interesting, fresh, and tasty. Plus its a great deal and BYO to boot. Great addition to 10th street!
Help me polish this: I visited this place with a group of four and had an extraordinary experience. Their menu offers a wide variety of appetizers that are worth exploring. We indulged in delectable dumplings with a delightful combination of corn and mushrooms, alongside some delicious wings and tempting daily specials that I unfortunately can't recall. Additionally, we each savored a serving of noodles, which stood out for their unique and fresh flavors. The portion sizes are not as generous as those typically found in a Chinatown noodle house, but the quality of ingredients is far superior. The food was not only interesting but also incredibly tasty. The best part? It offers excellent value for your money and allows you to bring your own beverages. This establishment has definitely made a valuable addition to 10th street.

input: Best sandwiches in St.Louis! Could eat here everyday. Always a very friendly crowd when I come and eat here.
Help me polish this: Discover the unparalleled sandwich experience offered in St. Louis! Indulge in these delectable creations which are so incredible, you'll find yourself returning day after day. Not only do these sandwiches surpass all expectations, but the warm and inviting atmosphere, combined with a consistently friendly crowd, makes your dining experience truly unforgettable.

input:
A great lunch or dinner stop in Reno, NV.  

We've had some fine meals in this establishment......Tyler (manager) does a great job with his staff, and it shows in the overall results.

They are also a pub, so its got a great selection of beers and wines too!
Help me polish this:
Looking for a fantastic lunch or dinner spot in Reno, NV? Look no further than this exceptional establishment! We have had the pleasure of enjoying numerous delightful meals here. Credit goes to Tyler, the manager, who consistently excels in leading his capable staff. The outstanding service and culinary expertise are evident in every aspect of the experience.

Additionally, for those who appreciate a good drink, this place doubles as a charming pub. They offer an impressive selection of beers and wines to complement your meal perfectly.

input:
As a childless woman I wasn't sure how I was going to enjoy my experience here but I give the good folks at Chuck E Cheese credit....they do run a fairly tight ship. There are lots of staff running around both on the floors and behind the counters so whether you need to order another sample platter or get a refund after a machine ate your token you will never be stuck waiting too long. There is also staff at the door and they do stamp the kids to make sure they don't wander away on their own or with somebody they do not know.

I like that all the games here are just one token. There are also quite a few different types of games available from Arcade style to games of chance. One thing I did notice is that the game area is larger then the play area which means your kiddo's are more likely to want to spend their time here and your likely going to be reaching for your wallet on more then one occasion.

There was a decent amount of food sent to our birthday party table and even with six kids and five adults there was still pizza left over. I did find the birthday area to be a little crowded and we did on more then one instance accidentally back our chairs into people from the neighboring party table. 

The staff here were great and very attentive making sure all the special birthday rock stars were well looked after. I don't know how many times I would really need to come into a place like this as I don't have that many friends with kids but it was great to see them enjoying themselves as well as reliving some fond memories from my own trips to Chuck E Cheese as a little girl.
