input:
Very cool bar attached to the Alexander Hotel. Several vintage cocktails from pre-prohibition are on the menu. None cooler than "The Elephant in the Room" a bourbon cocktail which comes in its own decanter filled with cherrywood smoke. You decide how long to let it infuse. Lots of comfortable seating and when it warms up a touch a large beautiful deck with seating and heating overlooks the street life. As an added bonus you can relax and watch people work out through the glass of the new CityWay YMCA. 
And yes the truffle oil and sea salt popcorn that greets every patron is as good as it sounds. Get a beer and start collecting bags, once you start you can't stop.
Help me polish this:
Introducing a remarkably trendy bar, conveniently connected to the Alexander Hotel. Our bar features a delightful assortment of vintage cocktails from the pre-prohibition era. Among them, "The Elephant in the Room" stands out as the ultimate bourbon cocktail. Served in a decanter filled with cherrywood smoke, you have the freedom to decide how long you want it to infuse, making it a truly personalized experience.

Our venue offers a plethora of comfortable seating options, ensuring a relaxing atmosphere for all our guests. Additionally, as the weather turns warmer, you can take advantage of our spacious and stunning deck, complete with seating and heating elements, providing a beautiful view of the lively street life.

As an extra treat, you have the unique opportunity to unwind while observing people exercising in the brand-new CityWay YMCA through the glass windows. It's an intriguing sight, allowing you to combine relaxation with a glimpse into the world of fitness.

Oh, and let's not forget about the delectable truffle oil and sea salt popcorn that awaits every visitor. Trust us when we say that it’s even better than it sounds. Grab a beer, and be ready to become a popcorn connoisseur as you won't be able to resist collecting bag after bag once you start.

input:
This hotel is a gem in the heart of Philadelphia.

It's a cozy, quaint, and charming property. The rooms are spacious, modern and gorgeous. 
The decor is chic and attractive: big wooden desk, hardwood floors, couches and throw pillows: Looks more like a friend's apartment than a hotel. 

Free breakfast is always a plus for those of us with limited time. It's not a hot breakfast (I've had so many mass-produced bad ones, so I'm not complaining) but greek yogurt, a huge croissant, an orange and some cranberry juice hits the spot! They leave it at your door though, instead of ringing your bell to wake you. So if you ask for it to be delivered at 7 a.m., check outside your door; by 7:01 it WILL be there. 

Coffee, a variety of teas, cold and hot water, as well as ice and a bowl of assorted fruit are available 24/7 in the lobby. There are doorbells for each room, and the hotel can only be accessed after hours if you have a key card. Floors are acessible with a keycard as well, for extra protection. The staff is very polite: one of the few places in Philly where someone will actually say "good morning" to you (No, seriously. I lived there for 5 years, so trust me on that). They're also extremely helpful. When I checked in the night before, the gentleman at the reservation desk called to make sure I had a cab waiting for me at 8:15 the next morning so that I could make my speaking engagement on time. While I was getting my clothes ready, my iron was making more wrinkles than it was taking out, so I asked them for a new one and within 30 seconds, I had a brand new model with all the bells and whistles.

I've read a few reviews talking about the noise level of this place. My room was closest to the reception desk and I never heard a peep. There were people out and about, but I didn't hear a thing. And I'm a very light sleeper...

A few things to note:
Its location on a tight, one way street can cause a little difficulty if you're traveling solo, but if you have one person to unload the car while someone else parks, you should be fine. The parking garage they use is about half a block from the hotel, but you have to drive in a big rectangle to get there. 

There's a stand-up shower instead of the traditional bathtub/shower combo. It fits one comfortably enough... provided that you're not too far from average height and build. (My boyfriend is 6'2 with a football player build and he made out okay.)

Don't expect much of a view. The view from our room was of the side of another building. But that's what the city is for... go out there and see something!

Overall, this was an excellent trip and a great find. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone.
Help me polish this:
This hotel is truly a hidden gem nestled in the heart of Philadelphia. From the moment you step inside, you'll be greeted with a cozy, quaint, and charming ambiance that sets it apart from other properties. 

The rooms are not only spacious, but also exude a modern and stunning aesthetic. The chic decor, featuring a large wooden desk, beautiful hardwood floors, plush couches, and throw pillows, creates an atmosphere that feels more like a friend's stylish apartment than a traditional hotel. 

One of the standout amenities is the complimentary breakfast, which is a real plus for those of us with limited time. While it may not be a hot breakfast, the offerings of Greek yogurt, a delectable croissant, an orange, and refreshing cranberry juice are just what you need to start your day off right. Not to mention, the hotel delivers the breakfast right to your door, ensuring a convenient and prompt service.

In addition, the lobby is available 24/7 for guests to enjoy a variety of beverages including coffee, teas, cold and hot water, as well as ice and a bowl of assorted fruit. The hotel's security measures, such as keycard access to both the entrance and floors, provide an extra level of safety and peace of mind.

Beyond the physical aspects, the staff at this hotel truly goes above and beyond to ensure a memorable stay. Politeness is their strong suit, with friendly greetings and genuine interactions. The staff is also extremely helpful, always ready to assist with any requests or needs. Whether it's arranging transportation or promptly replacing an iron, their attention to detail and responsiveness is truly commendable.

Despite a few concerns mentioned in other reviews regarding noise levels, my experience in the closest room to the reception desk was pleasantly quiet. Although the hotel was fully occupied, I was undisturbed and enjoyed a peaceful night's sleep. Even as a light sleeper, I didn't hear a peep.

There are a couple of things worth noting. The hotel's location on a tight, one-way street can pose a slight challenge for solo travelers. However, with a second person to assist with unloading the car, this inconvenience can easily be overcome. The parking garage, located about half a block away, requires navigating through a slightly convoluted route, but it is a minor inconvenience in comparison to the overall experience.

Another slight deviation from the norm is the stand-up shower included in the rooms instead of a traditional bathtub/shower combination. While it comfortably accommodates one person, those who are taller or have a larger build might find it slightly cramped. Nonetheless, this is a minor consideration in the grand scheme of things.

As for the view, it may not be the hotel's strong suit, as some rooms offer views of neighboring buildings. However, with the vibrant city of Philadelphia right outside your door, there is no shortage of attractions to explore and sights to see.

In summary, this hotel exceeded my expectations and proved to be an excellent find. I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone seeking a memorable and delightful stay in Philadelphia.

input:

I got the oxtail soup (Sancocho) with extra rice and plantains to see how it would differ from the Korean-style stuff I was used to at home. Aside from a thicker, stew-like broth and beefier potatoes, it was just as delicious. My friend got a flat steak (Carne Asada) that I think he ate in just under 10 seconds. 

Remember Yelp, you're missing out on a lot if you don't visit NE philly once in a while, especially this place.
Help me polish this:
Today, I was brought here by a Colombian friend who had a craving for something inexpensive yet delicious. This place instantly reminded me of Nanzhou, a beloved establishment on Yelp, because of the generous portions you receive without breaking the bank.

Curious to compare it to the Korean-style dishes I usually have at home, I opted for the oxtail soup (Sancocho) with extra rice and plantains. To my delight, the only notable differences were the broth's thickness and the heartier potatoes, making it just as satisfying. input:
One of my most favorite Indian restaurants. Nothing fancy but absolutely delicious meals.

Never an issue being seated promptly. A casual dining experience awaits. Service is pleasant. Ambience a bit blahh but still enjoyable.

Now onto the real reason to come here... the FOOD:
Naan is soft. Garlic is tasty but I usually like the original best.  Regardless of your entree of choice, you really cannot go wrong. And although it does not appeal to my level of spiciness preferred (I like it HOT HOT HOT), it has great flavor and is great for the average spicey food eater. My recommendations are the Masala or Vindaloo (Chicken, Shrimp, Lamb... option is yours). Room for dessert? Order the Rice Pudding  and Gulab Jaman, mix together and enjoy the creamy sugary treat.
Help me polish this:
One of my absolute favorite Indian restaurants, this place may not be fancy, but it undoubtedly serves up some incredible meals.

When it comes to finding a table, you'll never have an issue being seated promptly. The dining experience here is casual, offering a laid-back atmosphere that is still enjoyable despite its somewhat bland ambiance. However, it's the food that truly steals the show.

The naan at this restaurant is always beautifully soft and fluffy. While the garlic naan is tasty, my personal preference lies with the original naan. Regardless of what entree you choose, you really can't go wrong. Each dish is bursting with flavors that satisfy even the most discerning palate. Although it may not appeal to my preference for fiery spiciness, the food here has a fantastic flavor that caters perfectly to those who enjoy a moderate level of spice.

If you have room for dessert, I highly recommend trying the Rice Pudding and Gulab Jamun. Indulge in the creamy and sugary treat by mixing the two together – it's a delightful combination that will leave you craving more.

Overall, this Indian restaurant is a hidden gem, serving up delicious meals that are sure to satisfy your culinary cravings.

Help me polish this:
To the other reviewers,

I would like to offer some constructive feedback regarding the stadium rather than focusing on personal biases and irrelevant details. 

- The food options at the stadium are limited, and the number of vendors is insufficient. This can be inconvenient, as you may have to leave your seat to purchase snacks or drinks.
- The quality of certain food items, such as the "Hoagies," is disappointing. Considering Philadelphia's reputation for delicious sandwiches, one would expect better. The french fries are also subpar, being overly greasy and lacking crispness.
- The stadium's small, blurry TVs make it challenging to enjoy the game while waiting in line for your food.
- It is unfortunate to witness empty beer containers scattered around even in the early innings of the game.

While not directly influencing my evaluation, it is essential to warn others about the behavior of some Philadelphia fans. They can be rude, intoxicated, and may disrespectfully intrude upon your personal space, regardless of team affiliations or gender.

In conclusion, I regret to say that this stadium does not provide a satisfactory experience. If visiting, be prepared for relatively easy home runs due to the stadium's design favoring hitters. It would be wise to bring your own food and be cautious of the behavior exhibited by certain fans.

Please note that these observations are meant to be helpful and not to disparage anyone or perpetuate negative stereotypes.

input: Good menu, solid ingredients, but these folks are not sandwich artists.  I had a Turkey and Brie Wrap one day and the Spinach Florentine Wrap the next.  Both "wraps" could have more fittingly been called "crumples" because that's how they were assembled.  While watching the sandwich line I kept thinking, "Thank god they're not trying to fold burritos!"  Everyone in the sandwich line either looked befuddled by anything other than a plain bagel or like they were supposed to be somewhere else ten minutes ago.  Also, can we please hang a few signs like "order here", "pick-up here," "pay-here" to direct traffic instead of the east coast "If you don already know, then leave!" attitude?
Help me polish this: The menu is great, the ingredients are high quality, but unfortunately, the staff lacks the skill of making sandwiches. One day, I ordered the Turkey and Brie Wrap, and the next day, I tried the Spinach Florentine Wrap. However, both of these "wraps" were poorly assembled and should have been called "crumples" instead. I couldn't help but imagine the chaos that would ensue if they ever attempted to fold burritos. The individuals working at the sandwich line seemed either confused by anything beyond a plain bagel or as if they wished they were somewhere else ten minutes ago. It would be greatly appreciated if some signs could be put up, such as "order here," "pick-up here," and "pay here," to help direct traffic. The current "If you don't already know, then leave!" approach is rather unwelcoming and off-putting.

input:
This place is absolutely amazing. A cute little bakery and the employees are super attentive. I walked in and was bouncing around from one dessert to another deciding if I should make a purchase. The employee offered me a sample of the banana puddings - definitely try some! And you know how sometimes when they give you so small of a sample to taste, you can't really make a proper judgment because there isn't enough to judge from? Not the case here!

I got the salted caramel banana, the strawberry banana pudding and the upside pineapple cake.

Thoughts: OMG!! I never crave banana pudding and never really thought anything of the dessert. But man after this, I wanted to go home and make my own banana pudding (Although I highly doubt that I could make it half as good)! Their desserts are crafted perfect - three/four layers depending on what you get. The bottom layer the the pudding, second layer is the nilla wafers or they might even use some sort of pound cake(whatever it was - it was AMAZING), third layer, the strawberry and then the top layer is pudding with a nice whipped creme and topping. The creme has so much flavor and the texture is so smooth. Everything just comes together so nicely! 

The upside pineapple cake was BOMB. the cake wasn't too fluffy but was dense to the perfect amount to Taste like what it's suppose to. The pineapple flavor isn't overwhelming but just right. My only problem was that the pineapple bottom got a little too carameliZed with brown sugar and was a bit hard to chew.

Definitely go to this place! I was so sad that there was no option to leave them a tip. (They use an iPad to ring you up). The service/help was so great and I would have left a tip but I had no cash. Any ways, highly recommend this place for desserts!!
Help me polish this:
This place is absolutely amazing! It's a charming little bakery with incredibly attentive employees. As soon as I walked in, I couldn't help but bounce around from one dessert to another, struggling to decide what to purchase. The friendly employee even offered me a sample of the banana puddings, which I must say, you should definitely try! I ended up getting the salted caramel banana, the strawberry banana pudding, and the upside pineapple cake. Let me just say, OMG!! I never crave banana pudding and never really thought much of the dessert, but after trying these, I wanted to rush home and try making my own banana pudding (although I highly doubt it would come close to theirs)! Their desserts are crafted to perfection - with either three or four layers, depending on what you choose. The bottom layer is the pudding, the second layer is either nilla wafers or some heavenly pound cake (whatever it was, it was AMAZING), then there's the third layer of strawberry, and finally, the top layer is pudding with a delightful whipped cream and topping. The cream has so much flavor, and the texture is wonderfully smooth. Everything comes together so nicely!

As for the upside pineapple cake, it was absolutely BOMB. The cake itself wasn't overly fluffy but had the perfect density to capture the true essence of the flavor. The service and help I received were exceptional, and I would have gladly left a tip if I had cash. Anyways, make sure to check out this place for an incredible dessert experience!

input: I made my Yelp account for the soul purpose of reviewing this place; I think that very much speaks to how I enjoyed the experience. I also appreciated the dog-friendly policy but that's definitely a personal preference and isn't right for everyone. The location is also great, being situated in the French quarter. My only complaint is that I could only visit once on my trip to New Orleans.

input:
oh Millers, how i wanted to like you.  You are close to my house, have ample parking, and large spacious tables.  you even have a fireplace in the back for a little ambiance. 

friends and i tried to come here 2 or 3 times for a quick/inexpensive* bite to eat and every time there was a 30-60 minute wait. we thought this must mean they are really good.  perhaps it just means that people in Springfield are willing to settle for a less than average dining experience.  *side note- this place is not inexpensive. 

hubby and i ordered apps- he got zinger boneless wings, and i got the guacamole. portion size was ENORMOUS on the guac - it could have served 8 people, seriously.  flavor was meh. apparently the wingz were good.  hard to tell what hubby enjoyed more, the wingz or the scantily dressed hostesses. 

our server was great, attentive and pleasant.  When something went wrong she did her best to fix it. That was much appreciated.   Side salad came out wilted and gross. management offered to take it off the check, would have rather had a decent salad in the first place but i digress.  Dinner was not very flavorful - at all - and portion sizes were okay. i got the quesadilla appetizer (which was plenty for an entree) but it was very sloppily put together and had no seasoning at all.  I have had food that is presented better and tastes better at fast food restaurants, where i am happy to pay $5 for a meal.  

At the end of the meal, i badly wanted dessert but didnt want to risk another poorly flavored dish.  Not to mention, all the dishes were like lunch tray plastic, and i felt that a $50-60 dinner for two was at least worth a nicer presentation. who knows, it may have even made up for the bland flavors. 

perhaps i was let down by the fact that there always seemed to be a wait and i had over hyped it in my head.  Never have i wanted to send back everything i ordered at a restaurant before this night.  i will never be back.  my husband says he will order the wings, but takeout only. no more dining in at this place.
Help me polish this:
Oh Millers, how I had hoped to enjoy you. You are conveniently located near my house with ample parking and spacious tables. I was even impressed by the cozy fireplace in the back, adding a touch of ambiance.

On multiple occasions, my friends and I attempted to grab a quick and affordable bite to eat here, only to be met with a frustrating 30-60 minute wait each time. Initially, we assumed that such a long wait must indicate exceptional food. However, it seems more likely that the people of Springfield are settling for a less-than-average dining experience. Additionally, I must clarify that despite its reputation, this place is not inexpensive.

My husband and I ordered appetizers; he opted for the zinger boneless wings, while I chose the guacamole. The portion size of the guacamole shocked us as it could easily serve eight people. Unfortunately, the flavor was lackluster. On the other hand, the wings seemed to be the highlight for my husband, although I couldn't help but notice his appreciation for the scantily dressed hostesses.

Our server was excellent, displaying attentiveness and a pleasant demeanor. She promptly addressed any issues that arose, which we greatly appreciated. However, the side salad arrived wilted and unappetizing. While the management offered to remove it from the bill, I would have preferred a decent salad from the beginning. The main courses were disappointingly bland, with portion sizes falling into the realm of average. I ordered the quesadilla appetizer, which was substantial enough for an entree, but it was sloppily assembled and completely devoid of seasoning. It was disheartening to realize I've had better-tasting and better-presented meals at fast food establishments, where I pay a fraction of the price.

By the end of the meal, I desperately craved dessert but was unwilling to risk another disappointing dish. Moreover, the plastic dishes used for all the courses added to the feeling that a $50-60 dinner for two deserved a more elegant presentation. Perhaps I had set my expectations too high due to the consistently long wait times. This particular evening marked the first time I've ever contemplated sending back every item I ordered at a restaurant. Needless to say, I will never return. My husband insists that he may order the wings for takeout only in the future, but no more dining in at this establishment.

input:
I am sort of a simple man, so I had never been to a liquor bar before. I have been to The Libertine twice and had a good experience both times. They use fresh ingredients all the way down to the crushed ice, which they crush with a mallet right at the bar. 

The biggest problem I ran into was figuring out which restroom was the men's. You have to look at the hair on the dimly lit pictures that indicate which is which, all the faces look the same.
Help me polish this:
As someone who considers myself to be quite simple, I had never visited a liquor bar until recently. I've had the pleasure of visiting The Libertine twice now, and on both occasions, I've had nothing but positive experiences. One aspect that truly impressed me is their commitment to using fresh ingredients, down to the meticulously crushed ice, which they prepare right at the bar using a mallet.

However, I did encounter a slight predicament during my visits - determining which restroom was designated for men. The establishment's dim lighting and the hair-centric pictures used as indicators posed a challenge, as all the faces on the signage appeared very similar in appearance.

input: Came with the family based on a recommendation and was not disappointed.  I consider myself to be a bit of a Pizza connoisseur and this was right up there.  The staff was friendly and the food came out quick.  Solid experience across the board.  I would come back and recommend it to others.
Help me polish this: I arrived with my family based on a recommendation and I must say, I was beyond satisfied. As someone who prides themselves in being a Pizza connoisseur, I can confidently say that this place truly impressed me. The staff greeted us warmly and the food was served promptly. Without a doubt, every aspect of our experience was top-notch. I would undoubtedly return and highly recommend it to others.

input: We tried these at the Collingswood Art Festival this weekend. they are a bit pricey, but worth it. The flavor is perfect. they aren't greasy. I will be seeking them out. Once you try them... you will want to have them again. they are a light cheddar curd, battered and friend. You don't taste grease or batter. the flavor of the cheese is delicious, and so stringy and melty. The sauces are a delicate compliment to the curd. Well worth the splurge.
Help me polish this:
We had the pleasure of trying these delectable treats at the Collingswood Art Festival this weekend. Although they may be a bit more expensive, trust us, they are absolutely worth every penny. The flavor is simply impeccable and they are surprisingly not greasy at all. After experiencing these, I can guarantee you'll be on the lookout for them. 

These delightful morsels consist of light cheddar curds, which are then delicately battered and fried to perfection. What's even better is that you won't even notice the presence of grease or batter in each bite. The flavor of the cheese itself is undeniably delicious, with its irresistible stringiness and melt-in-your-mouth texture. Paired with the carefully crafted sauces, these curds receive a delicate compliment that adds to their overall incredible taste. Trust us, indulging in these curds is worth every bit of splurging.

input:
Yats rocks. You walk in and they've got 4-6 cauldrons full of your choices...which are written in sidewalk chalk on a blackboard. There's always something vegetarian, and a plate full of any of it costs five fitty. Add a buck and you can get a split plate of 2 delectable cajun creations with rice. But the best part is the ridiculously awesome garlic bread...which you can get a bowl of for like a buck.

Not only is the food awesome, but the owner (Joe Vuskovich) is a local celebrity. He's a famed restaurateur from New Orleans that sells his secret spice to restaurants everywhere. Everybody in town knows him (despite the fact that there are two other locations) and he's highly supportive of local bands and kids that most older people stay away from.
Help me polish this:
Yats is truly a gem. As soon as you step inside, you're greeted by the sight of 4-6 cauldrons brimming with delectable dishes, their names playfully written in sidewalk chalk on a charming blackboard. What sets this place apart is that there's always a vegetarian option available, catering to all palates. The best part? You can savor a generous plate of any of these mouthwatering creations for a mere five fitty. And if you're feeling a little adventurous, for just an extra dollar, you can indulge in a split plate with two tantalizing Cajun delicacies accompanied by flavorful rice.

However, Yats' allure doesn't stop at the food. Meet Joe Vuskovich, the renowned owner and local celebrity. A celebrated restaurateur from New Orleans, he has even shared his secret spice with restaurants far and wide. Despite having two other locations, everyone in town knows Joe. What truly sets him apart is his unwavering support for local bands and the younger generation that many older people tend to shy away from. 

But the pièce de résistance at Yats is undoubtedly the ridiculously amazing garlic bread. Be prepared to be blown away by its perfection. And the best part? You can enjoy an entire bowl of this culinary masterpiece for just a buck.

input:
Today after our Ethiopian food fiasco (see Selam review), we literally RAN into Pi after waiting hours to be served at the prior restaurant. We must have looked like a pack of hungry wolves so we told the hostess what had just happened. She seated us right away and sent us two orders of garlic bread (which we later found out were comped!). 

We ordered two pizzas and scarfed it all down. Pi has been consistently good on every visit I have made since I've moved to STL. Service is always excellent. Both the deep dish and thin crust are amazing every time.
Help me polish this:
Today, following our unfortunate Ethiopian food experience (as mentioned in the Selam review), we coincidentally stumbled upon Pi after enduring an extended wait at the previous restaurant. Our ravenous hunger was unmistakable, prompting us to share our predicament with the compassionate hostess. Without hesitation, she promptly seated us and surprised us with two complimentary orders of garlic bread, which we later discovered had been graciously comped.

With voracious appetites, we eagerly indulged in two pizzas from Pi, savoring every last bite. Remarkably, Pi has consistently impressed me during every visit since my relocation to STL. The exceptional service remains unwavering, and the quality of both the deep-dish and thin-crust offerings never fails to astound me.

input: I went here to get my wisdom teeth out and they did a great job. The only complaint I have is that I never see the same dentist. I've been going here for 5 years.
Help me polish this: I visited this place specifically to have my wisdom teeth extracted, and they did an excellent job. However, one aspect that has been consistently disappointing is that I have never had the same dentist attending to me. Despite being a loyal customer for the past five years, this inconsistency in dentists has been a drawback.

input:
After hearing about this place from a fellow Yelp Elite, my SO and I decided to try this place! We were warned of possible waiting times so came here on a Saturday around 10:45, and a line was already forming! 

For apps, we ordered the takoyaki and fried octopus. The takoyaki are delicious-an order comes with 5 balls that were perfectly cooked and topped with sauces. Takoyaki are little circular doughs with squid in the middle, topped with sauces and squid flakes (?). I definitely recommend this app. As for the fried octopus, it was just fried without sauces on top and came with mayo on the side, but it didn't come with enough mayo to dip the octopus in.

For ramen, I got the red spicy tonkotsu ramen and my SO got the black garlic tonkotsu ramen. For both ramen, the thin noodles were mushy/overcooked and just didn't quite fit with the ramen. That was the flaw with the dishes, and it tasted like the noodles were overcooked in a pot of flour-y water so it wasn't as clean (which explains the mushy feeling). They should use more bouncy noodles for this.

Now let's talk about the broth. The broth is flavorful, but the red chili broth was a bit too spicy for me and covered up the depth of the broth. I prefer the black garlic tonkotsu broth for that reason.

Overall, delicious food and pricing is reasonable. The decor is very nice as well, but screaming kids that were running around didn't make our meal pleasant.
Help me polish this:
After receiving a recommendation from a fellow Yelp Elite, my SO and I decided to give this place a try. We were aware of potential waiting times, so we arrived on a Saturday around 10:45 am, only to find a line already forming.

For appetizers, we ordered the takoyaki and fried octopus. The takoyaki was absolutely delicious, with each order containing five perfectly cooked balls topped with flavorful sauces. Takoyaki are small dough balls filled with squid, garnished with sauces and squid flakes (?). I highly recommend this appetizer. On the other hand, the fried octopus was simply fried without any toppings, and it came with mayo on the side. However, the amount of mayo provided wasn't sufficient for dipping the octopus.

As for the ramen, I chose the red spicy tonkotsu ramen while my SO opted for the black garlic tonkotsu ramen. Unfortunately, both dishes suffered from overcooked and mushy thin noodles that didn't quite complement the overall flavor. It seemed as though the noodles had been boiled in starchy water, resulting in a less clean texture. Using more springy noodles would greatly improve these dishes.

Now let's discuss the broth. It is undeniably flavorful, but the spiciness of the red chili broth was a bit overwhelming, masking the true depth of the flavor. Personally, I found the black garlic tonkotsu broth to be more favorable due to this reason.

In conclusion, the food was delicious and reasonably priced. The decor of the restaurant was also quite appealing. However, the presence of screaming kids running around greatly diminished the pleasantness of our dining experience.

input: Hands down best breakfast in Philly!  I've only been here for four months, but I have tried nearly every "Best of" spot in town.  I'm a breakfast fanatic so I get little over critical.  However, this small cafe has managed to create incredible flavor while keeping their dishes fresh and simplistic.  While the actual space is "cozy," this menu could easily keep a place as big as Parc overflowing with patrons.
Help me polish this: Undeniably the finest morning meal in Philadelphia! Despite my relatively short time here of only four months, I have diligently explored the city's reputed breakfast joints. As a devoted breakfast enthusiast, I tend to be overly discerning, but this charming café has mastered the art of infusing extraordinary flavors into their dishes, all while embracing a fresh and unfussy approach. Although the cafe might be on the smaller side, their exceptional menu could easily draw crowds to a grand establishment like Parc.

input: If I could give this place 6 stars I would. Don't let the looks deceive you, great diner food. Biscuits and gravy were incredible. Portions were more than I could eat.
Help me polish this: If I had the option, I would gladly give this place 6 stars. Don't be fooled by its appearance; it offers exceptional diner food. input:
This place is hip.  Perhaps too hip for many over 35 but if you can tolerate the boisterous and extremely casually attired youth--I haven't worn a suit in 20 years either but even 20 year olds should have something besides skinny jeans and T-shirts with borderline obscene slogans in their closets--the food is worth it and the staff copes well.   

I had a 6:00 reservation (obtained the day before) but the sky seemed threatening a downpour so I came early to avoid it and was seated 20 minutes or so before the appointed time.  I often don't even make reservations and have no trouble getting seated at popular places by being there when they open or, for those open all day, coming before the popular dinner hour, but that didn't work the day before at Lüke.  Even at 4:30 the place was packed so I did make one for the following day.

My meal started with the crispy Brussel Sprouts.  Even if you hate Brussels sprouts (I like them), don't be afraid to try this dish--if no one told you you might not know what you were eating.  They are in some sort of sweet/sour sauce/dressing and fried both slightly blackened and crispy as advertised . . . tossed with almond slices, small bits of jalapeño and sprinkled with shavings of cheese on top.

Then I had pork schnitzel and "pommes frites" (that's shoestring fries to the Galliphobes).  It came with whitish gravy in a pitcher, I suppose to make it "Southern".  The gravy was good but I skipped eating it, doing that the usual way with a squeeze of lemon.  It was excellent and the fries were fine too.

I finished with some excellent decaf and a glass of Kahlua--I had had iced tea with the meal so some alcohol was not an excess.

A lady who was some sort of hostess dropped by my table while I was eating to make sure everything was OK and when told I needed ketchup (for the fries), went and got me some (in a dainty little single-serve Heinz bottle).  My waiter also checked several times but didn't hover.

I am giving it 4 stars.  The 5th star is withheld because of the crowded dining room and noise level . . . nothing to do with the food which I greatly enjoyed.
Help me polish this:
This place is incredibly hip, although it may be a bit too trendy for individuals over the age of 35. However, if you can handle the lively and extremely casually dressed younger crowd (even though I haven't worn a suit in 20 years either, I believe even 20-year-olds should have more variety in their closets than just skinny jeans and t-shirts with borderline obscene slogans), the food is absolutely worth it, and the staff handles the chaos quite well.

I had made a reservation for 6:00 (obtained the day before), but the weather seemed ominous, so I arrived early to avoid any potential downpour. Thankfully, I was seated approximately 20 minutes prior to my reservation time. Normally, I don't bother making reservations and have no trouble finding seating at popular establishments by arriving when they open or, for those open all day, coming in before the popular dinner hour. However, this strategy did not work the previous day at Lüke. Even at 4:30, the place was packed, so I made a reservation for the following day.

To start my meal, I ordered the crispy Brussels sprouts. Even if you despise Brussels sprouts (I happen to enjoy them), don't be apprehensive about trying this particular dish. If no one informed you, it would be difficult to identify them. The sprouts are coated in a delightful sweet and sour sauce/dressing, fried to a slightly blackened and crispy perfection as advertised. They are then tossed with almond slices, small bits of jalapeño, and sprinkled with shavings of cheese on top.

Next, I indulged in the pork schnitzel and "pommes frites" (which are essentially shoestring fries, for those who aren't fond of the French). The dish came with a whitish gravy in a pitcher, presumably to give it a Southern touch. Though the gravy was delicious, I opted not to consume it as I usually prefer a squeeze of lemon instead. The schnitzel was outstanding, and the fries accompanied it perfectly.

To conclude my meal, I savored a cup of excellent decaf coffee and a glass of Kahlua. Since I had already enjoyed iced tea with my meal, treating myself to a small amount of alcohol felt appropriate.

During my dining experience, a lady who appeared to be a hostess stopped by my table to ensure everything was satisfactory. Upon learning that I needed ketchup for my fries, she promptly fetched a dainty little single-serve Heinz bottle for me. Additionally, my waiter checked on me multiple times throughout my meal, but never intrusively.

Overall, I am awarding this establishment 4 stars. The fifth star is excluded solely due to the overly crowded dining room and the high noise level, which has nothing to do with the food itself that I thoroughly enjoyed.

input: Beers were amazing! I got the porter, the double IPA and the table gutt and they were all fantastic. Food was also killer if you like Russian cuisine. They had a special when I went with a sausage and sauerkraut which was tasty. I also got the pickled everything appetizer, great choice. This place rules.
Help me polish this: The beers at this place were absolutely amazing! I tried the porter, the double IPA, and the table gutt, and all three of them were fantastic. If you're a fan of Russian cuisine, the food here is also killer. During my visit, they had a special featuring a sausage and sauerkraut dish which was absolutely tasty. Additionally, I ordered the pickled everything appetizer, and it was a great choice. Overall, this place definitely rules.

input: There are a ton of good sushi places in Reno and I have tried them all, but it always seems like Rickshaw has the freshest fish. I'm not a big fan of rolls and sauces, and opt mainly for Nigiri or sashimi. You can get some dressed up roll anywhere, hell you can buy them in the store, but if you are a true fan of sushi, just fish is where its at and Rickshaw has some of the freshest in town.
Help me polish this: There are numerous exceptional sushi restaurants in Reno, and having explored them all, I can confidently say that Rickshaw consistently serves the freshest fish. Personally, I prefer Nigiri or sashimi over rolls and sauces, and Rickshaw truly excels in offering raw fish at its finest. While one can find elaborately prepared rolls almost anywhere or even purchase them at a store, true sushi aficionados know that the pure essence lies in the fish itself, and Rickshaw undeniably delivers some of the freshest seafood in town.

input: This was my 1st visit here.  Overall, not that impressed!  To start with parking was really bad!  There are good choices of beer on draft.  The food was ok.  We split a few appetizers.  The fried olives were very tasty & different!  The rest of the appetizers were ok: the blue cheese chips, calamari, & meat/cheese platter.  I would try this place again, but overall not thrilled!
Help me polish this: This was my first visit here, and overall, I wasn't very impressed. The parking situation was really bad, which was already off to a rough start. On the positive side, they do have a good selection of beer on draft. As for the food, it was just okay. We decided to split a few appetizers, and out of all of them, the fried olives stood out as being very tasty and different. However, the rest of the appetizers like the blue cheese chips, calamari, and meat/cheese platter were just average. While I would be willing to give this place another try, I can't say that I was thrilled with the overall experience.

input: Really not sure what the hype was when it opened. It's fine, the ambiance was nice, but the menu is limited and food is nothing to write home about. They are in a nice location so at least if you decide to wait, then you have things to see...
Help me polish this: I fail to see what all the hype was about when this place first opened. Sure, the ambiance is pleasant, but the menu is disappointingly limited and the food itself is rather underwhelming. Thankfully, the restaurant is situated in a desirable location, so if you do end up waiting, you'll have at least a few things to see.

input:
This place was amazing! I only tried their ice cream I really wanted to try the hot chocolate but didn't get a chance :(. Well the ice cream was great! The first night I came here I got a brownie sundae all for myself, brownie on the bottom and three scoops of ice cream topped with whipped cream and nuts. I finished it all happily! I chose pumpkin cake flavor which was delicious and smooth. I also got pralines and cream that was better than other praline ice creams. The Tennessee fudge was vanilla with fudge swirled it was good not too special. 

The next time I came I got nutter butter ice cream that was really good had cookie pieces in it! I got the hot fudge topping over it and that was a great combination. 

The service was great the workers were really nice and patient with me haha indecisive! They would joke around with me and let me sample all I wanted. Also no judgement for eating all the brownie sundae alone :) lol
Help me polish this:
This place was absolutely amazing! Although I only had the chance to try their ice cream, I was really longing to taste their hot chocolate. Unfortunately, I didn't get the opportunity to do so. Nevertheless, the ice cream here was beyond delicious! On my first visit, I indulged in a mouthwatering brownie sundae, which consisted of a delectable brownie as the base, three scoops of heavenly ice cream, and a delightful combination of whipped cream and nuts on top. I devoured every last bit of it with pure satisfaction! The pumpkin cake flavor that I chose was both delicious and incredibly smooth. Moreover, their pralines and cream flavor surpassed any other praline ice creams I had tried before. As for the Tennessee fudge, it was a vanilla-flavored ice cream with a tantalizing fudge swirl, which was definitely good, but not exceptionally unique. 

During my next visit, I decided to try the nutter butter ice cream, which turned out to be absolutely fantastic! It had generous amounts of cookie pieces blended in, giving it an irresistibly crunchy texture. To enhance the experience, I opted for the hot fudge topping, and the combination was truly divine.

One aspect that made my experience even more enjoyable was the exceptional service provided by the staff. They were incredibly friendly and patient, even in the face of my indecisiveness. They would playfully banter with me and gladly allowed me to sample as many flavors as I desired. Their non-judgmental attitude towards my indulgence in the entire brownie sundae alone was also a pleasant surprise. Overall, my time at this place was simply wonderful!

input:
My dad and I were here for lunch and after reading some of the reviews, I was excited to check out this restaurant located where an O'Henry's once stood.

The place was fairly empty at 1 on a Friday and we were lead upstairs. Honestly, there's not much going on up there and it was a bit warm, but we decided to stick it out. Everything on the menu looked great and I decided to get the Catfish Acadian, which is catfish topped with crawfish and sauce with a side of vegetables. My dad got the pork chop.

My dish was great! I have no idea what was in the sauce but it was delicious and it was a perfect pairing with the fish. The vegetables were also really good; they were nicely cooked and fresh. My dad wasn't overly blown away by his pork chop, so if you find yourself here you might want to stick to the seafood.

Bria was our waitress and she was wonderful! She was attentive, kept the fresh iced tea coming and she was extremely personable. She was probably the highlight of the visit.

I'm not sure if I would go back. The food was good, but the atmosphere left something to be desired and I feel like I can get good catfish at plenty of places without going out of my way. I might go back at dinner, when the weather is cooler, and sit on the balcony outside as Harry suggested.
Help me polish this:
My dad and I decided to have lunch here, and after reading some positive reviews, I was excited to try out this restaurant that now stands where an O'Henry's used to be.

Arriving at 1 o'clock on a Friday, the place was fairly empty, and we were guided to the upstairs area. I have to admit, there wasn't much happening up there and it was a bit warm, but we decided to stay. Glancing at the menu, everything looked enticing, and I ultimately settled on the Catfish Acadian, a dish that features catfish topped with crawfish and a flavorful sauce, served with a side of vegetables. My dad opted for the pork chop.

I thoroughly enjoyed my dish! The sauce had a tantalizing flavor, and it paired perfectly with the fish. The vegetables were also well-prepared and tasted fresh. However, my dad wasn't overly impressed with his pork chop, so if you visit, sticking to the seafood options might be a safer bet.

Our server, Bria, deserves special acknowledgement as she provided excellent service! She was attentive, always keeping our glasses filled with refreshing iced tea, and her friendly and warm demeanor truly enhanced our dining experience.

As for returning to this restaurant, I'm a bit uncertain. While the food was satisfying, the ambiance left something to be desired, and finding good catfish elsewhere without going out of my way seems possible. However, I might consider giving it another chance for dinner when the weather is cooler, taking advantage of sitting on the recommended balcony outside by Harry.

input:
Well, well.... Where do I start with this place? First time experience, went in with my partner.

Walking in at about 7:30 on a Friday night (st paddys day weekend even)  and the  place had about 4 customers. That should have been my first clue as to what our experience was going to be like.

We seated ourselves and the waitress, an older gal maybe mid to late 40's who had greasy stringy unwashed hair and rotting teeth came up and took our drink order. My girlfriend got a Dr. Pepper and I got a water. She brought out Coke instead of DP. No biggie. We let it go, assuming it was an honest mistake. After about 10 minutes she returns and we order a 12 piece "jumbo" wing basket ($11.99), a 6 piece($7.99), and a beer batter sampler($11.99). 20 minutes pass and finally here comes our appetizer. The waitress throws the basket of appetizers on the table  and says "here's your food." Very flat with a big attitude and walks off. The beer battered mushrooms were doughy and undercooked. We had a single half full ranch cup to share between us for the big platter and she avoided our table when she saw we needed more.
***let me note that this waitress is giving the customers at the 3 tables surrounding us WAY better customer service. Even brought their food out in a timely manner with no attitude whatsoever.
I decide to let the mushrooms slide for the moment. I used to work in a restaurant and I understand that mistakes happen, however this far into the experience I'm being mighty generous since it's a first time experience.
We finish our appetizer and we wait and wait and wait and finally she comes by and takes the platter returning 10 minutes later with our wings. She makes no inquiry about the broken open, clearly undercooked, mushrooms still sitting on the platter.
I got the 12 piece with a single half full ranch. Again. Food on the table, doesn't ask if we need anything else which is something she is doing for other customers. at this point we have been here for about 40 minutes.

I got half regular and half thai flavor. The wings were NOT jumbo. They were puny. The flavor was good for the thai, and the waitress even stopped by to check up on us, though I wouldn't consider walking by quickly and saying in your flat attitude tone "youguysdoingalright?okaycool." Really all that helpful since she came and went so fast it took me a second to understand her. I had to reiterate for my girlfriend.  When I started on the regular I bit into my drumstick and had to fish a feather out of my mouth. DISGUSTING. It was that point that the entire experience was completely and thoroughly unacceptable.  The wings were soggy because they batter them or something on top of all that.  At first I had no plans other than to pay for the meal and leave the waitress 2 pennies and be on my merry way. But when the waitress came and asked if we needed a box I said no with 6 wings still on my plate, OBVIOUS SOMETHING WAS WRONG, again. She was going to take my stuff and make no inquiry to right the situation. I asked for the manager. Took a minute but finally the manager came over (mind you it is still pretty dead, what are these people doing I wonder?) I explained the food issues but blew off bringing up our treatment by the waitress. Normally I give the benefit of the doubt on this one but it was blatantly obvious that we were being treated differently with a different attitude than other patrons because we are a same-sex couple. Like our table had a contagious disease that prevented us from getting food in a timely manner, and getting drink and condiment refills too, regardless of the *empty* cups on the edge of the table. It wasn't like we were off in the distance. She had to walk by our table every time to communicate with the surrounding tables.

Anyways. The manager experience wasn't the greatest, but I wasn't going to pay for that meal after the feather thing, and she comped everything. BUT only after slightly arguing with us about the undercooked mushrooms, which by the way come frozen which  makes the fact that they weren't cooked all the way acceptable I guess? Don't know. Don't care. I WILL NOT BE GOING BACK!!!

2 stars because they did comp the meal, the waitress got lucky. If I would have had to pay for anything she wouldn't have gotten a tip due to the attitude but we left her $4 anyway since we didn't have to pay for the meal.  THAT IS THE ONLY REASON.
1 star though for the overall experience. Same-sex couples, steer clear. You aren't welcome there and it's obvious.
Help me polish this:
Well, well... Where do I even begin with this place? It was our first time visiting, and we went with my partner.

Upon walking in at around 7:30 on a Friday night (even during St. Patrick's Day weekend), we noticed that there were only about four customers present. In hindsight, this should have been our first warning sign for what our experience would be like.

We found a table and were greeted by a waitress, who appeared to be in her mid to late 40s. Unfortunately, her appearance was not the most pleasant, as she had greasy stringy hair and rotting teeth. She took our drink order, and my girlfriend requested a Dr. Pepper while I asked for a water. However, she mistakenly brought out a Coke instead of the Dr. Pepper. We shrugged it off, assuming it was an honest mistake. After about 10 minutes, she returned to take our food order. We ordered a 12-piece "jumbo" wing basket ($11.99), a 6-piece wing basket ($7.99), and a beer batter sampler ($11.99). 

We waited for about 20 minutes until our appetizer finally arrived. The waitress carelessly threw the basket onto our table without any courtesy and simply said, "Here's your food," before walking off with an attitude. The beer battered mushrooms in the sampler were doughy and undercooked, and we only had one half-filled ranch cup to share between the two of us. When we tried to ask for more, the waitress purposely avoided our table.

I tried to overlook the undercooked mushrooms, understanding that mistakes happen in the restaurant industry. However, at this point in our experience, I felt like I was being exceedingly generous since it was our first time there. It also didn't go unnoticed that the waitress seemed to provide much better service to the customers at the surrounding tables.

We finished our appetizer and waited patiently for our wings. After what felt like ages, the waitress finally came by and took away the platter. She returned 10 minutes later with our wings, and without acknowledging the issue with the undercooked mushrooms still sitting on the platter.

To my disappointment, the 12-piece wings I ordered came with only one half-filled ranch cup again. The wings themselves were far from "jumbo" - in fact, they were quite small. The Thai flavor was enjoyable, but the waitress only briefly stopped by to ask if we were okay, speaking quickly and disinterestedly. It almost felt like she wanted to rush past our table without actually caring about our experience. I had to repeat her question to my girlfriend since she spoke so fast. 

As I began eating the regular wings, I bit into a drumstick only to find a feather in my mouth. It was absolutely revolting and truly made the entire experience completely and thoroughly unacceptable. On top of that, the wings were soggy, possibly due to them being battered or something similar. Initially, I had planned to pay for our meal and leave the waitress a meager tip of 2 pennies, but when she came to ask if we needed a to-go box without addressing the obvious issues with our food, I requested to speak with the manager.

It took a bit of time, but eventually, the manager arrived at our table. While I explained the food problems, I chose to overlook our mistreatment by the waitress. However, it was abundantly clear that we were being treated differently and with a colder attitude compared to other customers simply because we were a same-sex couple. It almost felt like our table was plagued by an invisible barrier preventing us from receiving timely service, refills on our drinks, or even basic condiments, despite the empty cups clearly signaling our need for them. Our table was not secluded, and the waitress had to walk by us every time to serve the surrounding tables.

The manager's response left much to be desired, but I made it clear that I wouldn't pay for the meal after the incident with the feather. After a slight argument over the undercooked mushrooms, which apparently come frozen (as if that makes the undercooking acceptable), she finally decided to comp our entire meal. However, this did little to salvage the overall experience.

I reluctantly gave the establishment 2 stars solely because they did comp our meal. The waitress was lucky to receive a $4 tip from us, even though her attitude would have warranted no tip at all if we had actually paid for the meal. This rating is solely based on the fact that we didn't have to pay for our meal. However, I must give the experience 1 star overall due to the mistreatment and obvious discrimination toward same-sex couples. I strongly advise other same-sex couples to steer clear of this establishment, as it is evident that they are not welcome there.

input:
Don't let the outside fool you-this place is much cuter and nicer inside than you would expect! 

Food is good and reasonably  priced. We ordered papaya salad, triple flavor duck, and king tofu soup. Papaya salad is always refreshing, but this place overdoes it on the fish sauce. Help me polish this: Do not be deceived by the exterior, as this establishment boasts a charming and delightful interior that exceeds expectations! Moreover, the food offered here is both delectable and reasonably priced. During our visit, we indulged in the papaya salad, triple flavor duck, and king tofu soup. While the papaya salad was undoubtedly refreshing, the abundance of fish sauce used was slightly overwhelming. Opting for anything labeled "triple flavor" proves to be a reliably delicious selection. input:
I feel so comfortable with the Mazzoni Center.  I, and many others, am incredibly lucky and grateful that these services exist.  Going through all sorts of life challenges can be painful and frightening when you know you're assumed to be a certain way.  Here, there are no assumptions.  They know who they're working with, and they are sensitive without the need to pry for information.  If you're in need of gynecology and you're not a woman, for example, they know exactly how to handle your needs while prioritizing respect for your identity.

My biggest concern is the physical space in which the Mazzoni Center clinic exists.  I feel sort of exposed in the waiting room.  I hope that they someday have the funds to upgrade to a larger, more private space.

If you visit during youth drop-in hours rather than making an appointment, you will probably wait a very long time to see someone.  This is completely understandable, in my opinion.  They'll advise you regarding what time you should show up if you call.

Occasionally, I've noticed lapses in communication; I have been kept waiting in the exam room before with no one around and no idea how much longer I would have to wait.  This is not a common issue, and I find that, overall, I receive more attentive service here than at any other clinic I've visited.

Be aware that the doctor you want to speak with may not always be available over the phone.  Don't be afraid to leave messages with reception.  You'll always receive quick assistance.
Help me polish this:
I feel incredibly comfortable and grateful for the exceptional services provided by the Mazzoni Center. When facing various life challenges, it can be painful and intimidating knowing that others might assume things about you. However, at the Mazzoni Center, there are no assumptions made. They display a deep understanding of their clients and approach sensitive topics without prying for unnecessary information. 

One aspect that concerns me is the physical space of the Mazzoni Center clinic. I sometimes feel exposed in the waiting room, and I hope that in the future, they will have the means to upgrade to a larger and more private space. 

If you decide to visit during youth drop-in hours rather than scheduling an appointment, please be prepared for a potentially lengthy wait time. However, this is completely understandable, in my opinion. If you call, they will advise you on the best time to arrive. 

On rare occasions, I have experienced lapses in communication. There have been times when I was left waiting in the exam room without any staff present, and uncertain of how much longer I would have to wait. Nevertheless, this is not a frequent occurrence, and overall, the level of attentive service I receive at the Mazzoni Center surpasses that of any other clinic I have visited.

It's important to note that the doctor you wish to speak with may not always be immediately available over the phone. However, don't hesitate to leave a message with reception as you will always receive prompt assistance.

input:

input:
Really great place for wine!

Came here with my dining group, there was about 20 of us on a Friday, for their Happy Hour. Excellent wine happy hour where all glasses are $5 or you can take $5 off any bottle of wine, which is a great deal if you're sharing with a few people...great way to try a few bottles.

The food was also great! Cheese plates are the way to go here! Excellent selections! Several of my foodie friends ordered sandwiches, which looked & smelled amazing! They all raved about them!

The ambiance is very warm and inviting! They do a great job decorating, especially around the holidays! My favorite space is the enclosed patio area, adjacent to the main dining area. Super warm and romantic on those cold winter evenings! 

The service is great as well!
Help me polish this:
Came here with my dining group of about 20 on a Friday, and we were blown away by the fantastic wine selection and affordable prices during their Happy Hour. All glasses were only $5, or we could take $5 off any bottle of wine. It was the perfect opportunity to try a few different bottles, especially when sharing with friends.

Not only was the wine exceptional, but the food exceeded our expectations as well. The cheese plates were an absolute hit, featuring an impressive variety of top-notch options. Some of our foodie friends couldn't resist ordering sandwiches, and they were not disappointed. The sandwiches looked and smelled amazing, and everyone raved about their flavors.

The ambiance of the place is another highlight. The warm and inviting atmosphere, especially during the holiday season, simply adds to the overall experience. Personally, I fell in love with the enclosed patio area, right next to the main dining space. It is a cozy and romantic spot, perfect for those chilly winter evenings.

Lastly, the service was top-notch. The staff made us feel welcome and provided excellent attention throughout our visit.

input: Rude staff. Can't even get a salad order right. Overpriced by the slice. When we sat down to wait for our food I thought wow this is taking a long time given the fact we were the only people in there. I guess it should stay that way. Don't waste your money.

input: Really good, really authentic! This is some of the BEST Mexican cuisine I've tasted since my nana cooked for me; I'm from California so I would know. The enchiladas w/mole are awesome and the carne asada tacos remind me of Rosarito Beach, yummy!
Help me polish this: This is truly an exceptional and genuine culinary experience! Having grown up in California, I can confidently say that this is one of the finest representations of Mexican cuisine I have come across since my nana's homecooked meals. The enchiladas with mole are absolutely outstanding, perfectly capturing the flavors that I cherish from my childhood. Likewise, the carne asada tacos transport me back to the delightful taste of Rosarito Beach. Simply delectable!

input:

input: I had the carrot cake.... Very disappointed tasted like licorice and baking soda cooking powder. It's too bad because everything looks so delicious :( also didn't like the chocolate chips in it either.

input: You can't beat the prices for the unlimited food, but I've had better. The sushi is delicious, the salad was subpar and the crab Rangoon was probably the worst I've had. I've been twice and would definitely go again.
Help me polish this: The attractive aspect of this place is undoubtedly the unbeatable prices for unlimited food; however, in terms of overall experience, I have had better options elsewhere. Despite these drawbacks, I have visited this place twice and would still consider going again in the future.

input: Best chicken you could ever hope for in bourbon st. The chicken is good. The sauce is good. Everything is goof
Help me polish this: Indulge in the most exceptional chicken experience on Bourbon Street. Our chicken is beyond compare, and the accompanying sauce takes it to the next level. input:
Reviewing the food.
Hard to justify $16 for a burger and fries BUT wowow this burger was so delicious. I'm not sure if I was just starving but ordered the Lama burger and the patty size is quality. They also have random ingredients thrown in that you probably haven't seen before like gruyere stuffed in a pepper on your burger. Fries came out nice and crisp vs. soggy and the bun on that burger was great. You order inside by the Nook and then can sit around. They have tons of craft beer to choose from and I could see this place getting packed on the weekends.
Help me polish this: It's quite challenging to justify spending $16 on a burger and fries, but let me tell you, this burger was absolutely worth every penny. I can't exactly pinpoint whether it was my hunger talking, but the Lama burger I ordered had a substantial and high-quality patty that left quite an impression. The addition of unique elements, like gruyere stuffed in a pepper on the burger, really elevated the flavor profile. Thankfully, the fries were perfectly cooked - crisp, not soggy - and the bun used for the burger was delightful. The ordering process takes place inside The Nook, and after that, you can find a cozy seat. Moreover, the wide selection of craft beers available here is sure to please any beer enthusiast, and I anticipate this spot becoming jam-packed on weekends.

input: Favorite place in Nashville for breakfast!! This is a must go to spot!! Near Vandy and always busy...park in the back lot and be sure to get the parking ticket from the machine so you won't be charged...its free parking for a specified amount of time. My favorite is banana pancakes...think banana bread only in a pancake!! Perfection!!!! I don't leave Nashville until I go here to eat my pancakes!
Help me polish this:
Looking for the ultimate breakfast spot in Nashville? Look no further than this must-visit gem! Located near Vanderbilt University, this place is always bustling, so make sure to arrive early or prepare for a short wait. Don't worry about finding a parking spot, just park in the back lot. Remember to grab a parking ticket from the machine to avoid any charges. The best part? It's completely free for a designated amount of time!

Now, let's talk about the real star of the show - the banana pancakes. Imagine the irresistible taste of banana bread, but in pancake form. It's pure perfection! Trust me, I never leave Nashville without indulging in these delectable pancakes.

input:
Yes, there are vegan options in University City, you just have to know where to look for them. MexiCali has a number of great options.

Many options here can be made vegan by holding the cheese. I absolutely adore the marinated tofu burrito. The tofu has a wonderfully chewy texture, and along with the black beans, the meal packs a protein-filled punch that will leave you full well past dinner-time, should you choose to finish it.  The sweet potato and plantain burrito is purportedly dairy-free, and it's another delicious, filling vegan option. The veggie tacos come with a spicier version of the sweet potato, the marinated tofu and some cabbage on doubled corn tortillas. The tacos are not as filling as the burritos, but they're a delicious lighter option. Finally, a fourth option for vegans: the guacamole burrito. They homemade guac is to-die-for delicious. 

I end up at MexiCali about once a week. I've been going since they were just a lunch truck 8 years back. There's often a line at the restaurant, but this place has been around for years and they have a great system to get you your burrito in a very timely manner.
Help me polish this:
Yes, there are definitely vegan options available in University City if you know where to find them. MexiCali is a fantastic spot that offers a variety of delicious options.

Many of their menu items can be easily made vegan by simply omitting the cheese. Personally, I absolutely love their marinated tofu burrito. The tofu itself has a delightful chewy texture, and when paired with the black beans, it creates a protein-packed meal that will keep you satisfied long after dinner. If you're looking for something a little different, their sweet potato and plantain burrito is also dairy-free and incredibly tasty. It's another great vegan option that will leave you feeling full and satisfied.

For a lighter alternative, their veggie tacos are a fantastic choice. Made with a spicier version of the sweet potato, marinated tofu, and topped with cabbage, these tacos are served on double corn tortillas. While they may not be as filling as the burritos, they still deliver plenty of flavor and are a great option for those looking for something a bit lighter.

Another must-try vegan option at MexiCali is their guacamole burrito. Their homemade guacamole is simply to-die-for, and when paired with other fresh ingredients, it creates a truly delicious and satisfying meal.

I personally frequent MexiCali at least once a week and have been a loyal customer since they were just a lunch truck eight years ago. Despite the occasional line, the restaurant has perfected their system to ensure that you receive your burrito in a very timely manner. MexiCali has been a staple in the area for years, and their consistent quality and efficiency prove why they continue to be a local favorite.

input:
Great breakfast fare and all. Eggs provençale was pretty good; all kinds of herbs and seasonings, but cooked inconsistently. Tomato on the side was awesome.

Omelets were executed well, and the pastries were pretty impressive.

But the coffee was horrendously bad. And without good coffee, what's the point of breakfast?

And I still can't trust restaurants that have misspellings on their menus. Even if the misspelling is from another language.
Help me polish this:
The breakfast options were great, especially the eggs provençale with its flavorful blend of herbs and seasonings, although it was cooked inconsistently. The tomato served on the side was absolutely delicious.

The omelets were expertly cooked and the pastries were surprisingly impressive.

However, the coffee was exceptionally poor. It's difficult to fully enjoy breakfast without a good cup of coffee.

Furthermore, I find it hard to trust restaurants that have misspellings on their menus, even if they are in another language.

input: Another Yelper hit it -- this is a noisy, crowded restaurant with big screen TVs.  I wouldn't call it a sports bar.  Nothing wrong with the place.  Cool location, good beer selection.  The food - delicious, but eliminates itself as a "sports bar". My sons and I wanted to catch some pub grub and the hockey game.  Got the game.  The grub-- eclectic.  Do go here if you want a busy, bustling, energetic, tasty, flavorful, thumping music-beat experience.  Don't go here if you want  a burger, a beer and a hockey game amidst sports conversation.
Help me polish this: Another Yelper nails it: this restaurant is definitely not your typical sports bar. Yes, it's noisy and crowded, complete with big screen TVs, but the ambiance doesn't scream sports bar. However, that doesn't mean there's anything wrong with the place. In fact, it's conveniently located and boasts an impressive beer selection. Now, let's talk food. Delicious? Absolutely. But here's the catch: it's a bit too eclectic to fit the bill of a traditional sports bar. My sons and I were hoping for some classic pub grub while catching a hockey game, and while we got the game, the menu proved to be quite diverse. So, if you're seeking a lively, vibrant atmosphere filled with tasty and flavorful dishes accompanied by thumping music, this is definitely your spot. However, if your ideal sports bar experience revolves around enjoying a burger, a cold beer, and engaging in sports conversation while watching a hockey game, this might not be the place for you.

input: Fabulous, quick, stress free windshield repair. .. didnt cost a penny out of pocket. I would definitely use this company again and would recommend to anybody!!
Help me polish this: Experience a truly fabulous, efficient, and hassle-free windshield repair with absolutely no out-of-pocket expenses.
