input: I was so excited about this meal, I came home to review it immediately. The service was outstanding and the food I'd say was some of the best in New Orleans. Even the freshly made bread was piping hot and delicious. We started with the oysters good enough, which were four fried oysters with bearnaise sauce and Benton's bacon- a must get. Then we both got scallops and swine with a butternut squash purée and balsamic vinegar. All of the entrees sounded phenomenal, but we both couldn't resist getting that dish. The best part I have to say was the dessert. We got cafe au lait panna cotta with mini glazed donuts, which reminded us of beignets at cafe du monde. Finally, I sampled their house made 'cellos, including ginger and limecellos, and they were unique and delicious. An amazing experience!
Help me polish this:
I was incredibly thrilled about this meal, so much so that I came home immediately to share my thoughts. The service was truly outstanding, and I must say the food exceeded all expectations, placing it among the finest in New Orleans. The freshly baked bread was an absolute delight, arriving at our table piping hot and irresistibly delicious.

To kick off our dining experience, we indulged in the "oysters good enough" - four delectable fried oysters accompanied by a delightful bearnaise sauce and succulent Benton's bacon. This appetizer is an absolute must-have and left us wanting more.

For our main course, we both opted for the scallops and swine, served alongside a velvety butternut squash purée and drizzled with a tantalizing balsamic vinegar. Although all the entrees sounded exceptional, we simply could not resist the allure of this particular dish. And let me tell you, it did not disappoint.

The highlight of our entire dining experience had to be the dessert. We savored the cafe au lait panna cotta, perfectly paired with miniature glazed donuts that transported us back to the unforgettable beignets at cafe du monde. It was a delightful treat to conclude our meal.

To complete our remarkable culinary journey, we sampled their house-made "cellos," including the ginger and limecellos. These distinctive creations were absolutely incredible, offering a unique and delicious twist on traditional liqueurs.

Overall, our experience at this restaurant was nothing short of amazing. From the exceptional service to the extraordinary food, every aspect of our visit was exemplary.

input:
Absolutely amazing!!! My girlfriend and I went on a Wednesday night for Restaurant week and didn't know what to expect but we were overly satisfied. We ordered blood orange margaritas and they were strong and delicious. For our appetizers we had meatballs and let me tell you they weren't your average meatballs. They were veal and beef meatballs that melted in your mouth. Our other appetizer was some sort of grilled cheese that was amazing as well. For our entree we had the fishermen stew that was full of flavor and well balanced. Initially I did not think I was going to like it but it was to die for. Every element of the stew had it's own flavor and it was properly cooked. My girlfriend ordered the steak that came with cauliflower puree and a vegetable medley that was delicious as well. This was the first time we had ever ordered our steak to be medium-well and ever since we've been hooked. The steak was so juicy, tender and seasoned so eloquently and the puree was seasoned beautifully as well. 
The service there was amazing!! I forget the waitors name but he was great with the menu. He helped us order and came back frequently to check on us. 
Overall I think BARRA is amazing. It's not expensive and it is very intimate.  If you are looking for good food and great service at a reasonable price, BARRA is the place to go!!!!
Help me polish this:
It was an absolutely amazing experience at BARRA! My girlfriend and I decided to go for Restaurant Week on a Wednesday night, not knowing what to expect. However, we were pleasantly surprised and left overly satisfied. To start, we ordered the blood orange margaritas which were both strong and delicious. Our appetizers consisted of veal and beef meatballs that melted in our mouths, and a grilled cheese that was simply amazing. The flavors were unique and exceptional.

Moving on to our entrees, we opted for the fishermen stew and a steak with cauliflower puree and a vegetable medley. The fishermen stew was surprisingly flavorful and well-balanced. Each element had its own distinct taste, and the stew was cooked to perfection. Furthermore, the steak, cooked medium-well, was juicy, tender, and seasoned with utmost finesse. The cauliflower puree complimented it beautifully with its exquisite seasoning.

The service at BARRA was outstanding. Although I can't recall the waiter's name, he was extremely knowledgeable about the menu and assisted us in making excellent choices. He frequently checked on us, ensuring our satisfaction throughout the evening.

Overall, I must say that BARRA is truly amazing. It offers delectable food and impeccable service at a reasonable price. The intimate ambiance adds to the overall experience. If you're seeking a place that offers great food, outstanding service, and affordability, BARRA is a must-visit!

input:
We went here hoping for a good breakfast,  and we weren't disappointed.  We went on Valentine's Day, not because we wanted to, but because we had to.  In doing so,  we knew the wait would be long, which it was (an hour and a half), though i hear there's always a wait. 

The place is buzzing with servers and busboys. The tables around the edges of the room are a bit close to one another,  so seating is tight.  The service was though, considering how busy it was.  I ordered the famed cornmeal pancakes with a side of hash browns and a fried egg.  My girlfriend ordered the banana pancakes with a side of bacon.  Everything was amazing.  The pancakes were hearty but fluffy... The side of bacon only comes with three pieces which is disappointing,  but it was cooked to her liking.  The cornmeal pancakes had just the right amount of everything... Bacon,  peppers... Salsa, sour cream,  syrup... Yes,  all of that.  If you're looking for good coffee,  this is not the place, which was surprising. 

The only question is do you go with the homemade syrup or the maple.... Or both
Help me polish this:
We decided to try this place in search of a satisfying breakfast, and we were not let down. Despite visiting on Valentine's Day out of necessity rather than choice, we were aware that the wait would be long – and indeed it was, lasting an hour and a half. However, I understand that this is a typical occurrence at this establishment.

Upon entering, we were met with a bustling atmosphere full of servers and busboys. The tables around the periphery of the room were spaced a bit closely together, resulting in limited seating. Despite the busy environment, the service was commendable. Moving on to the food, I opted for their famous cornmeal pancakes accompanied by hash browns and a fried egg. Meanwhile, my girlfriend chose the banana pancakes accompanied by a side of bacon. The dishes surpassed our expectations; the pancakes were both filling and fluffy. However, it was disappointing that the bacon portion only consisted of three pieces. Nevertheless, they were cooked to perfection according to her preference. The cornmeal pancakes were a harmonious blend of flavors, incorporating bacon, peppers, salsa, sour cream, and syrup – all in just the right amounts. Remarkably, this place did not live up to our expectations in terms of coffee quality, which came as a surprise to us.

Now, the ultimate question arises – should one opt for the homemade syrup, the maple syrup, or perhaps both at once?

input: My husband son and I went in for dinner last Friday night. Upon entering we were greeted by a friendly hostess. As we stood there waiting for her to grab the menus I couldn't help but to notice a strong dirty mop water stench. Thankfully when we left the entry way it didn't carry into the dining room. The remodel is impressive looking. We were sat at a booth. Looking over the menu I was surprised at how limited it was. As long as you make what you offer well no biggie. I ordered the mushroom swiss burger and a beer. My husband ordered the "knuckle sandwich", ( tri-tip sandwich served French dip style). My son ordered the chicken strips and we all got French fries as our side. Jesse, our server was nice enough but in the loud dining room you couldn't hear a word he said. I was more annoyed that he didn't take the initiative to speak up than about the noise. The beer came out, although tasty it wasn't cold enough at all. The food came out within a reasonable amount of time. My husband's "Knuckle Sandwich" was delicious! That is what the two stars are for. My burger was shockingly small and probably the blandest burger I have ever eaten. My son's chicken strips tasted like they floured them...and that was it... also, no hint of seasoning. The fries are your run of the mill freezer to fryer. I hope they step it up and are successful.
Help me polish this:
Last Friday night, my husband, son, and I decided to go out for dinner. When we entered the restaurant, we were warmly welcomed by a friendly hostess. However, as we waited for her to bring us menus, I couldn't ignore the strong odor of dirty mop water. Fortunately, this unpleasant smell did not extend into the dining area.

The restaurant's remodeling was quite impressive, and we were seated at a comfortable booth. As I perused the menu, I was surprised to discover its limited offerings. Nonetheless, I believed that as long as the food was prepared well, it wouldn't be a major issue. I opted for the mushroom Swiss burger and a beer, while my husband chose the "Knuckle Sandwich," a tri-tip sandwich served French dip style. My son, on the other hand, ordered chicken strips, and we all decided to have French fries as our side dish.

Our server, Jesse, was decently friendly, but due to the loud atmosphere, we couldn't hear much of what he said. Although I found it a bit bothersome that he didn't make an effort to speak up, the noise was more aggravating than his soft-spoken manner. Our beer arrived, and while it had a good taste, unfortunately, it wasn't cold enough. Thankfully, our food promptly arrived.

To my delight, my husband's "Knuckle Sandwich" was absolutely delicious, hence the two stars I'm giving in this review. However, I was disappointed with the size of my burger, which was shockingly small, and it lacked any notable flavor. Furthermore, my son's chicken strips seemed to be only coated with flour, devoid of any seasoning. The fries, as expected, were average and appeared to be straight from the freezer to the fryer.

Ultimately, I hope the restaurant can step up its game and find success despite these shortcomings.

input: I had a delicious breakfast at Tuttini a few months ago.  I went back for lunch recently and was excited by their sandwich offerings, however, I was not served. Besides, I wanted to have a few minutes to relax in the cozy restaurant and enjoy my sandwich, not gulf it down on the street, so I left. input:

The seafood was ok. It's not their fault; it's Tucson so you know you really can't get fresh seafood. That's why I took off a star. They have 1 type of sauce with mild, medium, hot spiciness. It's similar to angry crab's "trifecta" or boiling crab's, "the whole shabang" but with an Asian twist. It was good in my opinion.

Lastly, if anyone has ever gone to angry crab, hot n juicy, boiling crab, should know that the price range is similar. Heck, if anyone has ever bought raw seafood at the store should know that it is on the expensive side. Expensive? Yes. Overpriced? No. I have been to many seafood places similar to this and it's a decent price for what you get. My advice for the Dungeness crab, since it did happen to me at other places and I saw a review on it here, is to share it or get their other selections that they can measure out. The dungeness crab is a full crab so finding a 1 lb dungeness crab is not common. 

Would recommend and go again.

I've only dined at this restaurant twice, and my overall experience has been great. On my first visit, they had just opened, so there were a few minor issues, but nothing worth complaining about. A nice bonus was that they were playing Star Trek, Hunger Games, and Iron Man, offering a fun selection of movies.

In terms of the seafood, it was okay. However, it's not the restaurant's fault, as fresh seafood is hard to come by in Tucson. Due to this limitation, I deducted one star from my rating. They offer one type of sauce with varying levels of mild, medium, and hot spiciness. It's somewhat similar to Angry Crab's "Trifecta" or Boiling Crab's "The Whole Shabang," but with an Asian twist. Personally, I found it quite tasty.

Lastly, I'd like to address the price range. If anyone has ever dined at Angry Crab, Hot n Juicy, Boiling Crab, or purchased raw seafood from the store, they would know that the prices here are similar. input:
I moved to Philadelphia from the midwest as a wide eyed 19 year old full of wonder. Yuengling lager was the first beer I've ever truly enjoyed and remains in my top five favorites of all time. Smooth, sweet, cheap, it's like me in a bottle. I love that the bottlecaps can be rusty, I like that the taste varies per batch, I even like its relatively low alcohol content. 

The tour was pretty great, the British tour woman was funny in a non canned way. She took a shine to my grandpa and was constantly begging him to sell her his hat (signed, sports, I haven't a clue). I was amazed at how close they let you get to the active equipment, I could've spit in the mash and no one would've been the wiser. The whole facility reminded me of St. Pete Catholic High, 50's cinderblock with a residue of toil clinging to the walls. 

The tasting, that's what you came for right? Fantastic. They were out of Lord Chesterfield, but who drinks that? I "tasted" the shit out of the lager, probably 6 times. It makes sense, the bar is next to the gift shop and I went a bit insane in there. 

The fact that Dick Yuengling made it a point to hire back the laid off workers after the last closure bumps it up a star. This is a family business, one that deserves support as Inbev has encroached upon everything else.
Help me polish this:
I moved to Philadelphia from the midwest as a wide-eyed 19-year-old, filled with wonder. Yuengling lager was the first beer I truly enjoyed and it remains among my top five favorites of all time. Smooth, sweet, and affordable, it's like a bottle that captures my essence. I appreciate that the bottle caps can have a rustic charm, and I even enjoy the slight variation in taste from batch to batch. Its relatively low alcohol content is also a bonus.

The tour itself was quite enjoyable. Our British tour guide had a great sense of humor that felt genuine. She took a liking to my grandpa and couldn't resist asking him repeatedly if she could buy his signed sports hat (although I have no idea which sport it was from). I was impressed by how close we were allowed to get to the active equipment, almost as if we could've spit in the mash without anyone noticing. The whole facility had a nostalgic feel, reminiscent of my old high school, St. Pete Catholic High, with its 50s cinderblock structure and a lingering sense of hard work.

Of course, the highlight of the tour was the tasting. And boy, did it live up to expectations. Unfortunately, they were out of Lord Chesterfield, but who drinks that anyway? I made the most of the lager and must have tasted it at least six times. Admittedly, the proximity of the bar to the gift shop may have played a role in my enthusiasm.

What sets Yuengling apart, and earns it an extra star in my book, is the fact that Dick Yuengling made it a point to rehire the laid-off workers after the last closure. This is a true family business, one that deserves our support in a world where Inbev seems to be taking over everything else.

input:
I have visited the brewpub several times now, and I'm finally ready to write up a review.  I really like the decor here.  It's old-school brewpub with lots of games for children.  The beer is pretty good.  I wish they would do some more adventurous offerings, but I can still get a good beer here.  
The food can be a mixed bag.  I had a small pizza that was a gooey mess (mushrooms and hearty toppings need a thick crust for stability).  I love all the scotch egg offerings (you can get it on a pizza or burger here), but they are so salty.  The burgers are good. The desserts are great (please get the frangipane).  It's also great to get the ploughman's plate and a beer, and just relax for a bit.
Help me polish this:
After frequenting the brewpub multiple times, I am finally prepared to provide a thorough review. The establishment's decor truly captivates me with its charming old-school atmosphere. Additionally, they have an abundance of games available for children, which adds to its appeal. As for the beer, it is of decent quality, although it would be wonderful if they ventured into more adventurous offerings. Nonetheless, I always manage to find a good beer to enjoy here.

Regarding the food, it can be a hit or miss experience. I distinctly recall ordering a small pizza that unfortunately turned out to be a gooey mess. With mushrooms and hearty toppings, a thicker crust would have provided better stability. On a brighter note, I am absolutely enamored by the various scotch egg options provided (they even offer it as a topping on pizza or burgers); however, they tend to be excessively salty. Fortunately, the burgers prove to be enjoyable. Furthermore, the desserts are exceptional, especially the irresistible frangipane. A personal recommendation would be indulging in the ploughman's plate accompanied by a delicious beer, allowing yourself to unwind and relax for a while.

input:
I think if I could, I would give Zen Yai a 3.5 stars, but alas, c'est la vie. 

The prices for their curry are excellent, at less than $12. Zen Yai is a tiny place, which is both good and bad. Good if you don't have to wait, because it is nice and cozy, but bad if enough people eat here on a given evening -- because you may just have to wait a while.

I like the decor a lot, and the use of colors. The tables and plates are full of refreshingly bright colors. 

The service was fine, and the food was at our table in no time.

My Pineapple curry was excellent! And the rice is served in the shape of a pyramid, which is fun. 

All that being said, my girlfriend had a less than pleasurable experience. She is a seasoned green curry lover, and was disappointed with their green curry offering.
Help me polish this:
I would give Zen Yai a solid 3.5 stars, if I had the option, but alas, c'est la vie.

The prices for their curry are simply excellent, at less than $12. However, it's worth noting that Zen Yai is on the smaller side, which can be both a positive and negative. It's great if you're lucky enough to avoid a wait, as the cozy atmosphere is quite inviting. However, if the restaurant is crowded, you might be in for a bit of a wait.

One aspect I really enjoyed was the delightful decor and clever use of colors. The tables and plates are adorned with refreshingly vibrant hues.

As for the service, it was perfectly fine and our food arrived at the table promptly.

Personally, I had a delightful experience with my Pineapple curry. It was absolutely delicious! I also found the pyramid-shaped rice to be a fun touch.

On the other hand, my girlfriend, who considers herself a seasoned green curry lover, wasn't as pleased. She found their green curry offering to be lacking and somewhat disappointing.

input:
Having stayed here several times, it is my favorite hotel. The staff is excellent. Really exceptional. Everyone from housekeeping to front desk staff to valets.

Rooms are clean, heating and AC are quiet, beds are very comfortable and they make it feel special.

Special K is awesome. I cannot say enough about how wonderful and helpful he has been over all of our visits. One of the best reasons to visit this hotel. Did I mention the exceptional staff?

Turn-down service is Sucre chocolates on your pillow. Sweets for the sweet dreams.

The bathroom wasn't as slippery this time. 

This was the first time we used the valet service and it worked great. No more than a 10 minute wait for the car. You can text them from your phone and they text back with how long it will take.

They also hosted a Gold Status reception. We made a brief appearance on our way to a Mardi Gras ball.

Our only glitch was a mini-bar charge on our bill. We didn't consume any of their food or drink and they happily removed it from the bill.

We will be back. Note to hotel: please put Louis back in the elevator.
Help me polish this:
After having stayed here multiple times, I can confidently say that this hotel is my absolute favorite. The level of service provided by the staff is truly exceptional, surpassing all expectations. From the diligent housekeeping team to the friendly front desk staff and valets, every member of the staff goes above and beyond.

The rooms are meticulously clean, and the heating and AC systems are whisper-quiet, allowing for a peaceful and comfortable stay. The beds are incredibly comfortable, further adding to the overall experience and making it feel like a special treat.

Speaking of exceptional staff, I have to give a special shout-out to Special K. He has been amazingly wonderful and helpful throughout all of our visits, making him one of the top reasons to choose this hotel. I cannot thank him enough for his outstanding service. And did I mention the rest of the staff? They are equally remarkable.

During turn-down service, they leave Sucre chocolates on your pillow, providing a sweet touch to end your day and ensure sweet dreams.

I must note that this time, the bathroom was not as slippery as before, showing that the hotel takes guest safety seriously.

We decided to use the valet service for the first time, and it was a great decision. We never had to wait longer than 10 minutes for the car, and the convenience of being able to text them from our phone for updates was fantastic.

Additionally, the hotel hosted a Gold Status reception, which we briefly attended on our way to a Mardi Gras ball. It was a nice and unexpected perk.

The only issue we encountered was a mini-bar charge on our bill. However, the staff promptly and happily removed it upon our request, as we had not consumed any of their food or drink.

Without a doubt, we will certainly be returning to this exceptional hotel. And as a friendly note to the hotel management, please consider putting Louis back in the elevator.

input: Great rolls and sake. We sat in the bamboo room, which definitely added to the experience, if you are able and agile.
Help me polish this: Enjoy incredible rolls and sake in the mesmerizing bamboo room, an authentic and immersive setting that truly enhances the dining experience, especially for those who possess grace and flexibility.

input: First, I love that they offer food delivery! Second, THAT is a gyro! I got one delivered with fries, and actually I didn't need the fries! The gyro was so big I had to save half.  Both the fries and the gyro were very tasty. The tzaziki was spot on and the meat tender. I'll be back!
Help me polish this: Firstly, I absolutely love the fact that they provide food delivery services! Secondly, let me just say, their gyro is absolutely phenomenal! I recently had one delivered along with a side of fries, but to my surprise, the gyro itself was incredibly generous in size. It was so substantial that I ended up saving half for later. The flavors of both the fries and the gyro were incredibly delectable. The tzaziki sauce was perfectly balanced, and the meat was incredibly tender. Needless to say, I will definitely be returning for more!

input: I stopped in to order take out and get a drink while I waited since it was happy hour. I am usually a beer drinker but I decided to step out of my comfort zone and ordered the dragonberry iced tea which was refreshing but not obnoxiously cocktail-ly, very pleasant. I had lemongrass chicken and crab rangoon, the lemon grass chicken and rice was fantastic. I do wish the crab rangoon had a little more filling but the dipping sauce was great. I've been here a few times and I have never been disappointed in the food or the service.
Help me polish this: I stopped by to place a take-out order and decided to grab a drink while waiting, taking advantage of the happy hour. As someone who typically sticks to beer, I took a leap and chose the dragonberry iced tea - it turned out to be a refreshing choice that wasn't overly cocktail-like, quite enjoyable. For my meal, I went with the lemongrass chicken and crab rangoon. The lemongrass chicken alongside rice was absolutely fantastic. While I would have preferred a bit more filling in the crab rangoon, the dipping sauce made up for it. Having visited this place multiple times before, I have never been let down by either the food or the service.

input: Consistent quality and service.  Love the #1 Deluxe.  Props to Amanda for excellent customer service, above and beyond!
Help me polish this: Consistent quality and outstanding service define our brand. The #1 Deluxe dish has gained a reputation for being a customer favorite. We want to extend a special shout-out to Amanda for providing exceptional customer service that truly goes above and beyond our expectations.

input:
*note* I wrote a similar review on tripadvisor.
I really wanted to like this hotel- it was charming and in a great location, with cute, unique rooms. It was just my style. Unfortunately, some blood-sucking insects ruined that.
Yup- bed bugs. We found them the morning we were leaving, because they normally come out very early in the morning (we were up at 530). Bleck! The management let us stay as long as necessary to take care of the issue (ie throwing away a bunch of our stuff and bagging the rest in ziplocks to be boiled) but it didn't change the fact that it was gross and a huge inconvenience. I threw away about $300 worth of clothing, shoes and luggage and I'm still worried that we brought the creatures back to our house with us. 
I would never stay here again, and I would urge you to think twice about it. Without seeing every carpet and mattress in the place replaced, there's no way I'd trust that the bugs were gone.
Help me polish this:
I had high hopes for this charming hotel, as it was wonderfully located and boasted cute, unique rooms that perfectly matched my style. However, my experience was marred by the presence of blood-sucking insects that completely ruined my stay.

To my great dismay, we discovered bed bugs on our last morning at the hotel. This distressing encounter took place early in the morning (around 5:30 am), as these pests tend to be most active during that time. It was, without a doubt, a disgusting and highly inconvenient situation. The management kindly allowed us to stay as long as necessary to address the issue. This involved throwing away a significant portion of our belongings and bagging the rest in ziplock bags to be sanitized. Despite their efforts, the grossness of the situation and the inconveniences caused remained. Regrettably, I had to discard approximately $300 worth of clothing, shoes, and luggage. Furthermore, I am still concerned that we may have inadvertently brought these creatures back to our own home.

Given what I have experienced, I cannot in good conscience recommend this hotel to anyone. I strongly advise you to think twice before considering a stay here. Unless every carpet and mattress in the hotel is replaced and the issue is entirely resolved, I cannot trust that the bed bugs have truly been eradicated.

input: Still running on EST, we arrived @8:30 on a Saturday to find no wait to be seated OR helped, ordering up the sweet potato pancakes with cinnamon cream syrup (good topped with excellent) with some borderline awful hash browns (really, people??). Can't say I'd return even without a wait, though; would prefer to just buy a jar of the syrup and apply it at home. Ended up at $24.43 pre-tip; no paper towels in the restroom and the day had barely started, so that was probably a dogshow.
Help me polish this: Arriving at 8:30 on a Saturday and still running on EST, we were pleasantly surprised to find no wait to be seated or helped. We decided to order the sweet potato pancakes with cinnamon cream syrup, which were deliciously topped with excellent flavors. However, the hash browns were disappointing, bordering on awful - truly a letdown. Unfortunately, this experience left us doubtful about returning, even without a wait. Perhaps it would be better to simply buy a jar of the syrup and enjoy it at home. The bill came to $24.43 before tip, which seemed reasonable. It was unfortunate to note the absence of paper towels in the restroom, especially considering the day had barely started - definitely not the best start to the day.

input:
There never seems to be a crowd at this Marsh store...getting in and out is always easy.  I agree with the other reviewer on the state of red baskets...ick.  Fix please!

I like that they opened up aisles so you don't have to walk all the way to one end to go to the next (prob happened a long time ago but I just noticed today).  And always seems like they are one cashier short here.

Very good selection of products (as always) from Marsh.
Help me polish this:
I have never encountered a crowd at this Marsh store, making it incredibly convenient to navigate and complete my shopping quickly. However, I must agree with the previous reviewer regarding the unsatisfactory state of the red baskets. It would be greatly appreciated if this issue could be addressed.

On a positive note, I recently noticed that the store has reorganized its aisles. This change allows customers to easily move from one section to another without having to traverse the entire store. It may have been implemented a while ago, but I only just noticed it today.

Nevertheless, it is worth mentioning that this particular Marsh location consistently appears to be understaffed at the cashier stations. Having one cashier fewer than necessary can result in longer wait times for customers.

Despite these observations, I must commend Marsh on their excellent product selection. As expected, they offer a wide range of high-quality items that meet my needs effectively.

input: Creative food and good. We get coffee or tea while we wait to be seated and even that is a cut above.  We love their Bloody Marys too.  Always interesting and an adventure.
Help me polish this: Exceptional food and creativity at its finest. From the moment we step foot inside, we are treated to a delightful experience, starting with a refreshing cup of coffee or tea as we await our table. Even this small detail surpasses expectations. And let us not forget their extraordinary Bloody Marys, which always leave us craving for more. Every visit to this place is an opportunity for an exciting culinary adventure, with captivating dishes that never fail to surprise and delight.

input: Wonderful atmosphere, great selection of beers.  We ordered the Asian chicken salads and the Cajun pasta and both were excellent. We will return again.
Help me polish this: The atmosphere was absolutely fantastic, creating an incredible dining experience. The beer selection was extensive, offering a wide range of options that catered to all tastes. We couldn't resist trying the Asian chicken salads and Cajun pasta, and they surpassed our expectations with their exquisite flavors. We were so impressed that we will definitely be returning in the future.

input: Love this place introduced almost 25 years ago when I enrolled at the UD and have loved ever since. For longest time it was basically just a Delaware treat but so happy it is so many more places now. Just want to know when you are coming to the Huntsville AL area. Sorry this review is not about this specific location but if it is half as good as others I have been to it will be great!!! This location has plenty of seating was real clean and playing good tunes as I waited. About only negative is it doesn't have Herrs chips like the Delaware locations but that is not really a problem.
Help me polish this: I fell in love with this place almost 25 years ago when I enrolled at the UD, and my love for it has only grown since then. Initially, it was a beloved Delaware treat, but I am overjoyed to see that it has expanded to many other locations. I can't help but wonder when this amazing establishment will make its way to the Huntsville, AL area. I apologize for veering off-topic with this review, but if this location is even half as impressive as the others I have been to, it will certainly be exceptional! The abundance of seating and the cleanliness of the restaurant, coupled with the delightful tunes playing in the background, provided a pleasant atmosphere while I waited. The only minor downside I can mention is the absence of Herrs chips, which are a staple in the Delaware locations. Nonetheless, this does not pose a significant issue.

input: At first I thought the prices here were pretty decent, but then I realized that they charge for every add on- chips/salsa, rice and beans, etc. I would be fine with this if the food was exceptional, but it is subpar. Both times I've been here, my side order of rice has been hard and dry, and burritos sad and limp. Additionally, the waitress we've had the two times going there had a horrible attitude. The only thing that saves this place is the guac, and the strong margaritas. Their strategy must be to get people drunk enough to not care about what they're eating and the rude service.
Help me polish this: Initially, I believed the prices at this establishment were reasonable. However, it soon became evident that they charge for every add-on item such as chips/salsa, rice and beans, and more. This practice would have been acceptable if the quality of the food was exceptional, but it is rather subpar. On both occasions that I have visited, the side order of rice was hard and dry, and the burritos lacked flavor and were disappointingly limp. To add to the dissatisfaction, the waitress we encountered on both visits displayed a consistently unpleasant attitude. The only redeeming qualities of this place are the delicious guacamole and the flavorful margaritas. It seems as though their strategy is to intoxicate customers enough to overlook the mediocre food and rude service.

input: My boyfriend and I have lived in trolley square for about three months now and tend to stick to the same restaurants.  We went out the other night planning on El Diablo and decided to try this cute little Italian restaurant. We are so glad we did! First off, the waiter was awesome, so friendly and on top of it.  He told us the history of the restaurant and gave us some good suggestions. The food was some of the best Italian food I have had in a long time. You can tell everything is made fresh.  The bread was delicious and a new recipe the owner received from his brother who lives in Sicily. We started off with the prosciutto wrapped Shrimp with a yummy sauce. I ordered the Penne Alla Vodka and my boyfriend ordered the traditional spaghetti and meatballs. The sauce in both dishes was excellent! The portions were a decent size with plenty of leftovers for my lunch the next day.  Finally, the cannoli was the best I have ever had! My boyfriend has been to Italy and said it was just as awesome as the ones he tasted there. I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a delicious Italian meal for a good price.  The special he night we went was order two entrees and get any appetizer for free! Check this place out!
Help me polish this:
"My boyfriend and I have been residents of Trolley Square for approximately three months now, and we have developed a habit of frequenting the same restaurants. However, the other night, we decided to break our routine and give a cute little Italian restaurant a try - and we are so delighted that we did! Firstly, our experience with the waiter was exceptional. Not only was he incredibly friendly, but he was also highly attentive. He shared with us the captivating history of the restaurant and provided us with some fantastic recommendations.

Without a doubt, the food we savored there was some of the finest Italian cuisine we have had the pleasure of tasting in a long time. The freshness of the ingredients was evident in each bite. Additionally, the bread served was simply divine; the owner had recently acquired a new recipe from his brother residing in Sicily. To begin our culinary journey, we opted for the prosciutto wrapped shrimp paired with a delectable sauce. For our main courses, I ordered the Penne Alla Vodka, while my boyfriend went for the traditional spaghetti and meatballs. The sauces in both dishes were truly remarkable, bursting with flavor. Furthermore, the portion sizes were generous, leaving us with ample leftovers for my next day's lunch.

Lastly, we were pleasantly surprised by the cannoli, which turned out to be the highlight of our meal. In fact, my boyfriend, who has visited Italy before, deemed this cannoli to be on the same level of awesomeness as the ones he had tasted there. I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone in search of a scrumptious Italian feast at a reasonable price. On the night of our visit, there was even a special promotion where ordering two entrees earned us a complimentary appetizer. Do yourself a favor and give this place a visit; you won't be disappointed!"

input: 3.5 stars because they don't serve alcohol (and I was in dire need of a drink after a veryyyy long week). Get the margherita pie - it is delicious and fresh. Also ordered the Greek salad for an appetizer which was filled with yummy veggies. Yum.
Help me polish this: I would rate this place 3.5 stars because unfortunately, they do not serve alcohol (which was something I really needed after an extremely long week). However, I highly recommend trying their margherita pie as it is absolutely delicious and made with fresh ingredients. Additionally, we ordered the Greek salad as an appetizer and it was filled with flavorful and tasty veggies. Overall, the food was satisfying and appetizing. Yum!

input: I love Mr. Wizard's because they offer frozen yogurt which is a  lot healthier than frozen custard. I like that they offer some pre-select combinations or you can create your own. The only part that sucks is that there is only outside seating so if it's cold outside, plan to eat in your car.
Help me polish this: I am a big fan of Mr. Wizard's because they provide a delicious frozen yogurt alternative that is much healthier compared to frozen custard. One aspect that I particularly appreciate is the option to choose from their pre-select combinations or even create your own personalized yogurt treat. However, it's worth mentioning that their lack of indoor seating can be inconvenient during colder weather, requiring patrons to enjoy their yogurt inside their cars.

input:
Not sure the significance behind the name and logo of the restaurant.  Unless it was three guys putting their money together to form this business 
The food was great/ staff friendly/ huge menu from breakfast /lunch/dinner to dessert.   Open 24 hours will definitely be back next time in town
Help me polish this: I'm not entirely sure about the meaning or symbolism behind the restaurant's name and logo, unless it represents the collaboration of three individuals pooling their resources to establish this business. Nonetheless, the overall dining experience was exceptional. The food surpassed my expectations, and the staff was incredibly friendly and accommodating. The extensive menu offered a wide range of options from breakfast to lunch, dinner, and even dessert. Another notable aspect is that the restaurant operates round the clock, which adds to its appeal. I'll definitely make it a point to revisit next time I'm in town.

input: I went to Spasso the other night with some friends. All four of us were SO pleased with our experience and our meals! We each had something different. I had the special for the evening, which was seafood (jumbo shrimp and jumbo lump crab) over pappardelle with tomato and asparagus. it was to die for, and my leftovers the next day were just as tasty :) service was amazing and wine was perfect. I live on state street and can't wait to visit again very soon!!
Help me polish this: I had the most fantastic experience at Spasso the other night with a group of friends. We were all absolutely delighted with our meals! Each of us ordered something different, and I must say, I made an excellent choice. The special for the evening was a mouthwatering seafood dish consisting of jumbo shrimp and jumbo lump crab served over pappardelle alongside a delicious blend of tomato and asparagus. It was truly divine; I couldn't help but savor every bite. Even the leftovers the following day were just as delectable! The service was exceptional, and the wine selection perfectly complemented our meals. Being a resident of State Street, I am already looking forward to my next visit to Spasso.

input: Returned to get a fill and pedicure a week after getting a gel polish change, once I discovered the cost would be over $85 I canceled the pedicure and only wanted a fill. Originally the owner was very nice and attentive but when she sensed I refused to pay their ridiculous price, she turned her attention completely off of me and showed absolutely no regard. She no longer cared for my business and she had no problem showing it. She even reassigned the nail tech to someone else bc I refused to be over charged for service. I asked why the original nail tech was no longer doing my fill, I got no answer. I looked over and saw the owner catering to customers that had just walked in. I sensed flaky business so I ultimately walked out without being serviced. Horrible customer service from the owner. I understand they use quality products but not everyone is looking to spend hundreds of dollars in a nail salon regardless of how "high end" it's self proclaimed to be!
Help me polish this: I went back to the salon to get a fill and pedicure a week after having a gel polish change. However, upon learning that the cost would exceed $85, I decided to cancel the pedicure and only receive a fill. Initially, the owner was friendly and attentive, but as soon as she realized I was not willing to pay their unreasonable price, her attitude completely changed. She displayed no regard for my business and seemed to no longer care. To my astonishment, she even reassigned the nail technician to someone else because I refused to be overcharged. When I inquired about this change, I received no explanation. I observed the owner promptly attending to new customers who had just walked in, further confirming the inconsistent and unreliable nature of the salon's business. Frustrated by the poor customer service from the owner, I made the decision to leave without being serviced. While I understand that they use quality products, it is unreasonable to expect every customer to spend exorbitant amounts at a nail salon, regardless of its proclaimed "high-end" status.

input:
Ice cream wasn't the best, and definitely not for the price. But it was there when I was passing through Belmawr, and it hit the spot when I needed to satisfy my sweet tooth! 

The service was friendly, albeit a little slow. And the place has a cute, quaint charm about it with the decor. If I lived in the area I'd probably return, but I wouldn't make any special trips to go back here.
Help me polish this:
The ice cream was mediocre at best and certainly not worth the price. However, when I happened to be passing through Belmawr, it provided a satisfying option to satiate my sweet tooth.

Though the service was friendly, it could have been more efficient as it was a bit slow. Nevertheless, the establishment exuded a charming and quaint ambiance with its delightful decor. If I were a local resident, I might consider returning, but I wouldn't go out of my way to make a special trip here.

input: Best auto body shop in Philadelphia in my opinion. My Honda Fit had accumulated all sorts of nicks, dents, scratches, and even some really ugly lime deposit stains on the hood of my car. I took it to Devlin's to get touched up, and what I got back was a car that looked like it just rolled off the assembly line. Honestly, if I told you my car was 3 years old and had gone through a few scrape-ups, I don't think you'd be able to tell. Ed Devlin is a miracle worker, and he does his magic at a super affordable price... I was shocked at how inexpensive the bill came out to be.
Help me polish this: In my opinion, Devlin's is the best auto body shop in Philadelphia. When I took my Honda Fit to them, it was covered in nicks, dents, scratches, and unsightly lime deposit stains on the hood. However, when I got my car back, it looked brand new as if it had just rolled off the assembly line. The expertise of Ed Devlin, the owner, is truly remarkable. Even though my car is 3 years old and has been through a few scrape-ups, you wouldn't be able to tell. On top of that, the price for his exceptional work was surprisingly affordable.

input:
Even though theres nothing ostensibly stand-out about 45, I spend quite a bit of time here. This is definitely a "Cheers" bar, where everybody knows your name. If you can make out their face through the haze of cigarette smoke, that is. Personally, the smoke doesn't bother me, though i have plenty of friends who refuse to go here for that reason. 

I just love the laid back, dive-y vibe. On game days, theres always a spread of food to help yourself to, which is such a nice tradition that you rarely see in bars now. During baseball season, well, I hope you're a Red Sox fan. If not, keep your allegiances quiet, lol. And theres often a food truck parked out front. Yum! A great pre or post show stop if you're seeing music at Tipitinas, which is just down the street.
Help me polish this:
Even though there's nothing particularly outstanding about 45, I find myself spending a significant amount of time here. It's undeniably a quintessential "Cheers" bar, where everyone knows your name, that is if you can recognize them through the dense haze of cigarette smoke. Personally, the smoke doesn't bother me, but I have numerous friends who adamantly refuse to join me here for that very reason.

What I truly adore about this place is its laid-back, dive bar atmosphere. On game days, they always lay out a spread of food for patrons to enjoy, which is a delightful tradition that seems to be fading away in most bars nowadays. During baseball season, it's practically a prerequisite to be a Red Sox fan, so it's best to keep any other allegiances quiet, just to be safe! Another perk is the frequent presence of a delicious food truck parked right outside. It's an appetizing bonus, especially if you're heading to or from a live music show at Tipitinas, which conveniently sits only a stone's throw away.

input: Please note: the coffee is excellent! However, you have to ask for cream and sugar. I find this pretentious and intimidating. It's coffee. I want it how I want it. It shouldn't be such a big deal.
Help me polish this: Please take note: the coffee served here is absolutely excellent! However, it is important to mention that if you prefer cream and sugar with your coffee, you will need to kindly request it. I must admit that I find this particular aspect somewhat pretentious and intimidating. After all, it's just coffee, and we should have the freedom to enjoy it exactly as we prefer. It shouldn't be made into such a significant ordeal.

input:
Is it okay to say this is my favorite brunch spot even though all I've ever had here is their grits? I would definitely try one of their other courses and I'm pretty sure they're amazing, but it is so hard to not get my favorite thing off their menu! Their portion is so huge, i usually share it with another person (if I'm not being greedy)! You can literally top anything onto your dish and they vary from .50 cents to 1.00 dollar.  I love to add on avocados, red bell peppers, bacon, cheddar, and mushrooms! Their grits are incredible, it is not grainy nor watery. It's just perfect. I can go on and on. but I'm pretty sure you get the point! 

Eventually, i will try their other dishes, but for now, it's all about their grits.
Help me polish this: Can I still claim this as my favorite brunch spot even though I've only ever tried their grits? I'm dying to sample their other menu items, which I'm certain are amazing, but I just can't resist ordering my all-time favorite dish. The portion they serve is so generous that I often end up sharing it with someone else (if I can manage not to be selfish!). What makes it even better is that you can customize your grits by adding on various toppings, ranging from just 50 cents to a dollar. Personally, I love loading mine up with avocados, red bell peppers, bacon, cheddar, and mushrooms. Trust me, their grits are beyond compare - neither grainy nor bland, just pure perfection. I could go on and on singing their praises, but I hope you get the picture! While I promise to eventually explore their other offerings, for the time being, my heart belongs to their delicious grits.

input:
Great staff.  Nothing is ever disappointing - chili cheese etoufee is the BOMB.  It's a 4 instead of 5 stars because it's CASH ONLY.  But I love that you can also sit outside on nice evening.  

Don't forget the garlic sauce!
Help me polish this: The staff is exceptional, consistently delivering an amazing experience. The chili cheese etoufee is absolutely incredible and could be considered the epitome of flavor. The only reason it falls short of a perfect 5-star rating is due to its cash-only policy. However, the added bonus of being able to enjoy your meal outside on a pleasant evening is a definite perk. And of course, don't leave without trying their amazing garlic sauce!

input: Nice view from outside tables. It has typical beach food and typical beach service, but nice place to grab a drink with a view.
Help me polish this:
Enjoy a mesmerizing view from our charming outdoor tables, where your dining experience will be complemented by a delightful beach ambiance. input: Large menu. Clean restaurant and restroom. Friendly staff. They were fairly busy in the middle of the day when we visited. input: This place had fantastic donuts! They were very well priced and so soft. We tried the blueberry cake donut and apple fritter. We will definitely be going back.

input:
I really had a wonderful experience at the Nashville location, and we found out that New Orleans had one now and should go to it. Last night we got there kinda late around 10pm. input:
Allegro's is great. The pizza is really cheap, and lightning fast. My favorite was the sicilian, followed by the, uh, meaty kind, followed in a close third by anything stuffed (sometimes the centers were cold). They also sell beer, but I can't comment much on that because when I lived in Philadelphia I was under 21.
The only downside is the service (occasionally rude) and the constant crazies that hang out there talking to themselves.
Help me polish this:
Allegro's is absolutely amazing. Not only is their pizza incredibly affordable, but it's also prepared at lightning speed. Among their delicious options, the Sicilian pizza definitely stands out as my all-time favorite. Close behind is their meaty variety, and a closely-contested third place goes to any of their stuffed options, although on some occasions, I did find the centers to be a bit cold. While I can't provide much input on their beer selection since I was underage during my time in Philadelphia, they do offer it as well.

Unfortunately, the only downside to Allegro's is their occasional lackluster service, with instances of rudeness. Additionally, the constant presence of eccentric individuals who often engage in conversations with themselves can be a bit overwhelming.

input:

On my last visit I stayed for free for 3 out of the 4 nights, and on top of that they gave me $120.00 of free play. The Peppermill is rated the casino with the loosest slots in casino. The rooms were clean,  the bathroom smelled great, and there weren't any bed bugs in our bed. The casino reminds me of old casino, when they relied on millions of lights bulbs, neon signs, and the smell of argon in the air. Happy hour everyday from 4-6 , you get mini apps and 3 dollar martinis at the fireside lounge. Also the Fish bar is awesome to go and relax, since they have a 40 foot aquarium that wraps around two of the walls. They have some excellent restaurants in the casino, that you don't even have to leave to satisfy any food craving you might have. The staff is extremely friendly and that is the top reason I keep coming back to this casino in Reno.
The only thing about this place is that the lights in the casino can really discombobulate you! Just remember that they key sleeve they give you has a map, so keep that in your pocket !
Help me polish this:
This place truly exceeds expectations from the moment you step inside. I make it a point to stay here every time I visit Reno, and I am constantly impressed by the consistently improving service. During my last stay, I was delighted to discover that I received a complimentary stay for three out of the four nights, along with $120.00 of free play. The Peppermill is renowned for being the casino with the loosest slots, adding to the allure.

The rooms are always impeccably clean, and the bathroom emits a pleasant fragrance. It's worth noting that we had absolutely no issues with bed bugs. Stepping into the casino transports me back to a bygone era, reminiscent of classic casinos adorned with bright bulbs, neon signs, and the unique aroma of argon. 

One of the highlights of my stay is the daily happy hour from 4-6, offering delectable mini apps and $3 martinis at the fireside lounge. Additionally, the Fish Bar provides a serene ambiance with a stunning 40-foot aquarium spanning two walls. The casino boasts a variety of excellent restaurants, satisfying any food craving one might have without ever needing to leave the premises. However, the standout feature for me is the remarkable friendliness of the staff, which continually brings me back to this casino in Reno.

The only minor setback is that the casino lights can be disorienting at times. Thankfully, they provide a key sleeve with a handy map, so be sure to keep it in your pocket for guidance.

input: Two very good experiences.  Excellent burger and very good pulled pork.  Wife loved her egg white and goat cheese omlette.  Solid beer list and a good spicy bloody Mary.  Also had great service and an ecclectic play list.

input:

Not  the way to treat someone who helped you out. 

I will not be going back to Peppermill.
Help me polish this:
One of their guests unleashed a sudden onslaught, ruthlessly assaulting innocent individuals, and even causing one to collapse on the ground. input:
IF YOU ARE ON A STUDENT BUDGET, READ ON:

This is a 5 mile wide/long convention center. It has up to 2,000 guestrooms.  The conference I went to had 6,000 attendants. Of course I booked late and I didn't want to spend $200+/night on these hotel rooms! Otherwise this place is ginormous. The service (shuttle), lunch/drinks were really well done.  This place is immaculate; I do not know how many workers they staff.  

The food of course is overpriced (I had lunch/dinner at Wasabi. My bento box was $25.  Overpriced right?)  I also had lunch at the pizza place Paisano (forgot the name).   

If you decide to stay at the hotels across the street from the convention center (it is only 1 mile away - across from the McGovick Pwky).  They have Cracker Barrel, Apple Bees, Chillis?, McDonalds there.  The hotel I stayed in (being on a student budget) was crappy but I can't complain for $55/night.  It was Days Inn. It was walkable to shuttle pick up stop at Marriott Hotel (walk ~0.3 miles).  

They have Finleys pub, FUSE (night/club), STAX burger, Jack Daniels and more restaurants inside this convention center.  

I posted some photos.
Help me polish this:
Attention students on a budget:

If you're looking for affordable accommodations and a convenient location, keep reading!

The convention center I stayed at was massive, spanning 5 miles wide and long, with a capacity for up to 2,000 guestrooms. Although the conference I attended had a staggering 6,000 attendees, I didn't want to break the bank by booking a hotel room for over $200 per night. Nevertheless, the convention center impressed me with its impeccable service, including a shuttle and well-executed lunch and drink options. I can only imagine the number of staff required to maintain such high standards.

The only downside was the food, which was quite pricey. For instance, I had a bento box at Wasabi for $25—definitely overpriced. I also grabbed lunch at a pizza place called Paisano, but unfortunately, I forgot its name.

If you're open to staying at hotels across the street from the convention center—about a mile away, near McGovick Parkway—you'll find affordable dining options like Cracker Barrel, Applebee's, Chili's, and McDonald's. On my student budget, I chose to stay at the Days Inn, which was, to be honest, a bit rundown. But for $55 per night, I can't complain. Plus, it was within walking distance (approximately 0.3 miles) to the shuttle pick-up stop at the Marriott Hotel.

Inside the convention center itself, there are additional dining options such as Finley's Pub, FUSE (a nightclub), STAX Burger, Jack Daniels, and more. Check out the photos I posted for a glimpse of the convention center.

input: I took an 8 year old and a 14 year old for the lunch special pizza.  We have done this on several occasions, and the kids love that they each get their own personal pizza, made the way they like.   They both ordered their pizza with 2 items and wanted BBQ sauce as the base instead of tomato sauce.  (this is the only way they enjoy pizza).   I was told that they could only get tomato sauce, not BBQ sauce.   I explained that we have gotten it this way several times before.   We were told that they don't offer it this way any more.   I see that some of the pizzas offer BBQ sauce and pointed it out, but again was told that it couldn't be made this way for them.   I asked if I could pay additional to have it made with BBQ sauce, but once again told it was not possible.   Sadly, we left the restaurant and chose a different nearby restaurant for lunch.  I'm sorry to say I won't be able to take the kids here anymore.

I regret to say that due to this experience, I won't be able to bring the kids to this restaurant anymore.

input: Excited to have this place in Reno! Delicious matcha and ube flavors! Like authentic. Friendly staff, looking to get better but what they have as a base is solid. Soft serve, cake and the sauces aren't overly sweet.  Hoping they add more flavors!

input: Delicious. So happy I Yelped for a restaurant closer to home and stumbled upon this. It's small and pleasant inside with some decent hip hop setting the mood. The menu is small, but packed a punch. We ordered the Duck Fries, which were heaven. Fries smothered in smoked gouda,  shredded duck, and scallions. For 8 bucks came a pretty large bowl that I couldn't stop picking at. I ordered one of the specials, the scallop and foie gras  tacos...wow...so good (then I read the origin of foie gras and hated myself, but aside that...). The person I was with ordered the pork roll burger, which I tried of course. It was incredibly juicy and cooked perfect. I will definitely come back here. Definitely.
Help me polish this:
Absolutely delicious! I am beyond thrilled that I decided to use Yelp to find a restaurant closer to home and stumbled upon this hidden gem. The moment I walked in, I was greeted by a cozy and inviting atmosphere accompanied by some captivating hip-hop music that set the perfect mood. Despite having a limited menu, this place did not disappoint - each dish packed a powerful punch.

Our first choice, the Duck Fries, left me in utter culinary bliss. Imagine fries smothered in a heavenly blend of smoked gouda, tender shredded duck, and just the right amount of scallions. For just 8 bucks, you'll receive a generously sized bowl that you won't be able to resist picking at.

Next, I decided to indulge in one of their specials - the Scallop and Foie Gras Tacos. These tacos exceeded all expectations and brought me to foodie heaven. However, I must admit that upon learning the origin of foie gras, I couldn't help but feel a touch of remorse - but that's an entirely separate matter. Moving on, the person accompanying me opted for the Pork Roll Burger, and of course, I couldn't resist taking a bite. The juiciness and perfect cook of this burger left me in awe.

Without a doubt, I will be returning to this amazing establishment. The experience was so memorable that I can confidently say this will become a regular haunt for me.

input: Went to Three Muses our first night in New Orleans. The plates are tapas style, small and meant for sharing. Between the four of us we got the blue cheese stuffed dates, the crawfish egg rolls, steak and cake, lamb sliders, feta fries and fish tacos. Everything was really good,i could have done without the tacos, but the lamb sliders and the steak and cake were AMAZING. The goat cheese paired with the lamb was to die for. And the crab cake was the best I have ever had.
Help me polish this: On our first night in New Orleans, we had the wonderful opportunity to dine at Three Muses. Serving tapas-style plates, perfect for sharing, the restaurant offered a delightful culinary experience. With a party of four, we indulged in an array of dishes including the delectable blue cheese stuffed dates, the flavorful crawfish egg rolls, the enticing steak and cake, the succulent lamb sliders, the mouthwatering feta fries, and the satisfying fish tacos. Overall, the food was exceptional, though I found the tacos to be the least impressive among the selection. However, the lamb sliders with their exquisite pairing of goat cheese were truly outstanding, as were the crab cakes that surpassed any I had previously tasted.

input: Great ambiance!  Loved the trendy and modern decor.  The presentation of the dishes was also great.  The food was just okay though. I would also like to try their lunch. Service was excellent.
Help me polish this: I thoroughly enjoyed the fantastic ambiance of this place! The trendy and modern decor added a touch of elegance to the overall dining experience. Unfortunately, the potatoes were undercooked and the pancakes were a tad greasy. Despite this, I would be willing to give this place another chance, particularly to try their delectable-looking French toast and omelette. Moreover, I am eager to sample their lunch menu. input: This place is awesome the food is dynamite . Super friendly service. And the. Coup de grace was the flan made in house fresh and believe me I've tried flan everywhere, there's is exceptional. input: Had breakfast with the family after a quick stopover. Great food and service (thanks Jonathan!), definaelty a good find that was busy but had no wait on a Saturday.

input: During the parents' visit,  dad wanted some southern food. We tried Willie Maes, but the line was long and they weren't crazy about the area.  So we waited a bit and went down to The Praline Connection. Dad was in heaven. He's been talking about the food since we left. Dad got the taste of soul platter pictured below. He said the fried chicken was the best he's had and he had not tasted red beans and rice like that since he was a kid and my granny used to make em. Mom got the meatloaf with cabbage and lima beans. I got the ribs with potato salad and mac and cheese. My ribs were good but hard to cut the meat off the bone. I could've ate em with my hands but I didn't want a BBQ face. The potato salad was good but my mac & cheese was a little bland. The cornbread was great.  I'm going back next time for the fried chicken!
Help me polish this:
During my parents' visit, my dad had a craving for some traditional southern food. We initially tried going to Willie Maes, but the long line and the area didn't appeal to them. So, we decided to wait a bit and headed down to The Praline Connection instead. Let me tell you, my dad was in complete heaven! He hasn't stopped talking about the food since we left.

Dad ordered the legendary taste of soul platter, which you can see pictured below. According to him, the fried chicken was hands down the best he has ever had, and the red beans and rice brought back memories of his childhood when my granny used to make them. As for my mom, she chose the meatloaf with cabbage and lima beans, which she really enjoyed.

I decided to go for the ribs with potato salad and mac and cheese. While the ribs were flavorful, they were a bit tough to separate from the bone. I debated eating them with my hands, but I didn't want a BBQ-covered face. The potato salad was tasty, but I found the mac and cheese to be a bit on the bland side. However, the cornbread was fantastic.

All in all, I'm definitely planning on revisiting The Praline Connection solely for their fried chicken. It easily exceeded all expectations!

input:

This particular location is in Hyde Park Village. The benefit is that parking is free. The down side is that seating is limited. The store is also extremely cold, so it is uncomfortable to sit and socialize for very long. You may be better off getting your coffee to go and walking around Hyde Park Village instead.

Buddy Brew, a trendy coffee shop nestled in Tampa, offers a delightful coffee experience with its rich flavors and exquisite presentation. Conveniently located in Hyde Park Village, this particular Buddy Brew location provides the added perk of free parking. However, it's important to note that seating options are somewhat limited. input:
A really nice place to get your hair did with as much of an edge as you want.  

In the East Loop, across from the Pageant, might be one of the most underrated salons in the city.  I first went into this place as a walk-in, and keep on going back.  Yes, I'm a guy, and since my hair is pretty coarse, grows weird, and I want a bit of style to it, I go to hair salons.  At V Vegaz I've never been dissatisfied with my cut. 

When you walk in you realize how spacious the place is, with a bit of a slightly modern, slightly baroque interior design.  There's a nice vibe there too amongst the employees, and you can see that the stylists are happy with the work situation.  Of course, happy stylists, to me, mean better haircuts.

I go to Callie, since that first walk-in, and keep on going back.  Yes, she's real friendly, which is a nice touch, but she's also a great stylist.  I'm a bit wishy washy when I look for a cut, usually changing what I want most of the time.  Callie's sensitive to that, and really understands how my hair grows and where it's going to move.   I think the biggest compliment to her is that, as I'm a once a month haircut kinda guy, my brother and sister told me they really my hair a full month after I had it cut with Callie.  So that's really a testament to her skills.

I've not gotten color there, but it is a full service salon, and not just a turn and burn place.  

I highly recommend this place.
Help me polish this:
Looking for a top-notch salon that offers a unique touch to your hair? Look no further than V Vegaz, located across from the Pageant in the East Loop. This hidden gem is one of the city's most underrated salons, and once you step foot inside, you'll understand why.

The salon boasts a spacious interior with a tasteful blend of modern and baroque design elements, creating a visually appealing atmosphere. What sets this place apart is the positive vibe among the employees, which translates into exceptional haircuts. Happy stylists mean better results, and at V Vegaz, satisfaction is guaranteed.

From the moment I walked in, Callie has been my go-to stylist. Her friendly demeanor adds a personal touch to the experience, but it's her talent that truly shines. As someone with coarse and unruly hair, I am quite particular about the style I desire. Callie understands my ever-changing preferences and works magic with my hair's growth pattern.

What truly speaks volumes about Callie's skills is the lasting effect of her cuts. Despite being a once-a-month haircut kind of guy, my brother and sister complimented my hair a full month after Callie worked her magic. This testament to her expertise speaks for itself.

While I haven't tried their coloring services yet, V Vegaz is a full-service salon, not just a "turn and burn" establishment. The range of services they offer reflects their dedication to providing a comprehensive experience for their customers.

If you're in search of a hair salon that can meet your needs and add an edge to your style, I highly recommend V Vegaz. Don't miss out on the opportunity to discover this well-kept secret in the heart of the East Loop.

input:

input:
Late one Saturday night, some friends and I made the mistake of trying to get drinks at Plough and the Stars and left very quickly. We were walking around trying to find somewhere else to go, noticed this unmarked bar and decided to check it out. We were so excited to see that there were so many great beers on tap, and there was a decent crowd there so we stuck around. It was a fun night! And after a few weeks of wondering where we had gone, we were able to find the Irish Pol on Yelp :D

I went back for happy hour recently and it wasn't exactly as I had remembered. It was pretty dark and dingy looking inside,  and the few people there were much much older. It just had a weird vibe. The beer was still great of course. The happy hour special was $3 drafts, but most of the beers I wanted weren't included. I won't be back for happy hour, but I would definitely stop in on a Saturday night!

input: Great pizza! The place is beautiful and the atmosphere is truly inviting. The service is very nice and fast.

input:

We sat outside on the patio which was just lovely. Even if you sat inside, like other restaurants in the French quarter, every door and windows are open, so fresh breezes flow throughout. Really nice experience.

I opted for the French toast with a side of fruit and an a la carte fried egg. Unfortunately, they accidentally dropped my egg when it was being served, but they quickly brought me a replacement. Additionally, I enjoyed a delicious vanilla latte that required no additional sweeteners.

Overall, it was a truly enjoyable experience.

input:
We were early for church and wanted to grab a quick bite to eat. The atmosphere was really inviting and everyone on staff spoke to us at least once! 

The food was good, but not great. I had quiche and my guest had a croque madame. The crust of the quiche wasn't done and the bread on the croque wasn't that great. Otherwise these two dishes would have been perfect. The fruit was fresh and the coffee was great!

I will definitely return.
Help me polish this:
We arrived at church ahead of time and decided to grab a bite to eat. The ambiance of the place was incredibly inviting, and each and every staff member took the effort to interact with us.

While the food was satisfactory, it fell short of being outstanding. I opted for the quiche, but unfortunately, the crust wasn't fully cooked. Similarly, my companion ordered a croque madame, and the quality of the bread didn't impress. Nonetheless, had these minor issues been resolved, both dishes would have been perfect. Thankfully, the fruit served was refreshingly fresh, and the coffee exceeded our expectations.

Considering my overall experience, I can confidently say that I will be returning to this establishment in the future.

input:
Stayed here for a bachelorette party. This place got the job done. Unfortunately, all the hotels in Santa Barbara are pretty freaking pricey. A lot of the other hotels started at $400+ /night.  This ain't Vegas where you can get something pretty cushy for $250. This seemed like a decent option on the lower end. Our rooms were about $250 a night. A lot of the other hotels in the area were already booked for the weekend or required more than one night to book. 

Pros: 
-decently priced
-clean and cozy rooms
-charming exterior and grounds
-relatively comfortable beds
-bath and body works shampoo, body wash etc
-free water bottles and fruit waiting for you in the room

Cons:
-dated decor 
-toilet issues: The hook inside kept coming undone. I guess we decided not to get maintenance because we temporarily fixed it, but it kept coming undone so it wouldn't really flush. We were checking out that day, so we decided just to deal with it. 
- door was difficult to open without using a certain technique
-no hair dryer, so bring your own
-no complimentary breakfast
-a bit noisy in the morning, but I slept fine. I guess the window in the bathroom was open or something for some ventilation.

Overall, I still don't think I would've chosen to stay anywhere else in Santa Barbara, so BW Pepper Tree Inn was still a good choice based on the location of the bachelorette and price range.
Help me polish this:
I stayed at BW Pepper Tree Inn for a bachelorette party and it served its purpose well. Unfortunately, the hotels in Santa Barbara are quite expensive. Most of the other options started at $400 or more per night. Unlike Vegas, where you can find luxurious accommodations for $250, Santa Barbara was more limited in terms of affordable options. Our rooms at BW Pepper Tree Inn were priced at around $250 per night, which was relatively more reasonable. However, many other hotels in the area were already fully booked for the weekend or required longer stays.

Pros:
- The hotel offered reasonably priced rooms.
- The rooms were clean and cozy.
- The exterior and grounds had a charming appeal.
- The beds were relatively comfortable.
- The provided Bath and Body Works shampoo, body wash, etc., added a nice touch.
- We were pleasantly surprised to find free water bottles and fruit waiting for us in the room.

Cons:
- The decor seemed a bit outdated.
- We encountered issues with the toilet's hook constantly coming undone, causing flushing problems. Since we were checking out that day, we opted not to contact maintenance and temporarily fixed it ourselves. However, it continued to come undone.
- Opening the door required a specific technique, making it somewhat difficult.
- It would be wise to bring your own hair dryer as it was not provided.
- There was no complimentary breakfast included.
- The mornings were a bit noisy, possibly due to a slightly open bathroom window for ventilation, but it did not disrupt my sleep.

Overall, despite the mentioned drawbacks, I still would not have chosen to stay elsewhere in Santa Barbara. BW Pepper Tree Inn proved to be a fitting choice considering the location of the bachelorette party and our desired price range.

input: In my book you can never go wrong having a good old-fashioned meal a Johnny Rockets. I had their recent promo which was a barbecued pulled pork burger. input:
I still love this place just as much as I ever did, and here's why:

1) Super friendly and knowledgeable staff 
2) Roomy, with lots of outlets and enough space to accommodate mid-sized groups (like the recent Yelp Office Hours)
3) Delicious tea, of course!

I've always loved their "Awake" Fizz Tea, but I've also broadened my horizons to include Pearl Tea (aka bubble tea). The taro flavor rocked my socks off. It did take a little getting used to though, as I had a mini anxiety attack every time I took a sip. Because I got it warm, it was in a paper cup and I never knew when a pearl was making its way into my mouth. As a result, I spent half my drink wondering "is there one in my straw?" It's totally worth the suspense, though.

The only thing that still troubles me is the music. It's just...not right. In fact, sometimes it's pretty distracting. It's easily avoided, however; just bring headphones and your own musical selection and all is well.

input: Yah Man was yah man! Go here and enjoy the atmosphere, the personal service and delicious Caribbean fare. The beef pie was yummy as was the chicken and island sampler plates. input:
Favorite place to go in New Orleans. Chill backyard bar with great local music options.

Smaller groups are better- seating can get tight. The wine and cheese bar up front services the live music venue in back. You can pick 3 or more cheeses and they put together a lovely cheese and accoutrements tray for you. You can also choose a wine to open up in the back. Wines have a great selection, mid-range price (almost all winces over $10-20 a bottle).

Great place to spend the night and have a wonderful time away from the packed tourists hot spots. (Mind you, this place is well known and a hot spot itself).
Help me polish this:
Experience the ultimate New Orleans oasis at my favorite spot in the city - a charming backyard bar with an inviting ambiance and an unbeatable local music scene.

This hidden gem is ideal for smaller groups, as the seating can get a bit snug. As you enter, you'll first encounter a delightful wine and cheese bar. This front area caters to the vibrant live music venue located in the back. Enhancing your evening, the staff happily assists you in choosing from an impressive selection of three or more cheeses. From there, they expertly curate a picturesque cheese and accoutrements tray for your enjoyment. To elevate your experience, you can also select a wine from their extensive collection. With a multitude of options available, you'll find that the prices are reasonable, with most bottles falling between $10 and $20.

Escape the hustle and bustle of the tourist-filled hotspots and instead revel in the intimate atmosphere this establishment offers. Although this place is itself a popular destination, it remains a well-kept secret that guarantees a memorable evening away from the crowds.

input: Had a great lunch here. I ordered a chicken Caesar and my dining companion ordered a custom salad. Waitress had a great personality and did not rush us at all. Allowed us to linger. Great space which is hidden from the outside.

I am completely let down, especially given the fantastic experiences I have had here in the past.
