input: Love this place.  Best view in Santa Barbara.   Awesome wines.  My wife and I are industry, and always treated great.  Tom and Gillian are ALWAYS generous hosts.  My wife works @carrwinery and always refers customers to them.  The Conway cabs are the best SB has to offer.  One of their tasting room employees just gifted us a Conway 13 reserve Syrah.  Beautiful. ...  Thank you Tommy.   Rolos red is a bottle that any wine snob would love,  but a great bottle for those finding their pallet as well.  My son is 5 and always wants mom and dad to go wine tasting when we hit the pier. Never disappointed.
Help me polish this:
I absolutely love this place! In my opinion, it has the most incredible view in Santa Barbara. Not to mention, their wines are truly exceptional. My wife and I are fortunate to be in the industry, and every time we visit, we are treated like royalty. Tom and Gillian, the owners of the winery, are always incredibly generous hosts. I must also mention that my wife works at Carr Winery, and she consistently refers customers to this place because of how phenomenal it is.

Let me tell you about the Conway cabs they offer - they are hands down the best that Santa Barbara has to offer. Recently, one of their tasting room employees gifted us a bottle of their Conway 13 Reserve Syrah, and it was absolutely outstanding. I want to extend a special thank you to Tommy for that wonderful gift.

Now, let's talk about their Rolo's Red. It's a bottle that any wine snob would adore, but it's also perfect for those who are just beginning to explore their palate. Even my 5-year-old son, whenever we visit the pier, always tries to persuade us to go wine tasting at this winery. And I can confidently say that we have never been disappointed.

input: Such a cool atmosphere and unlike anything I've ever been to. You walk into the wine and cheese shop, select a bottle (or 2!) and then select whatever cheeses and meats you so choose from a refrigerator. Once you have your items, you bring it to the counter to pay, they take your cheeses and meats, and deliver it to your outside (or upstairs inside in our case due to the rain!) and it's like magic. It comes back a beautiful cheese board with nuts and spreads and a delicious loaf of sliced artisan bread! Highly recommended! They also have a menu t order from the kitchen if you really need more, but two of us were full after our platter and wine!
Help me polish this:
The atmosphere at this wine and cheese shop is simply amazing and unlike anything I've ever experienced. When you walk in, you're immediately captivated by a unique ambiance. You can leisurely browse through a variety of wines, and the best part is that you can choose not just one, but maybe even two bottles! As you make your selection, you have the freedom to handpick the cheeses and meat of your liking from a well-stocked refrigerator. Once you've gathered your items, you proceed to the counter to pay. From there, the staff takes over, graciously taking your cheeses and meats and transforming them into something truly magical.

In our case, due to the rain, our cheese board was artfully presented to us upstairs inside. And boy, did it exceed expectations! It came back to us as a beautifully arranged masterpiece, complete with nuts, spreads, and a mouth-watering loaf of sliced artisan bread. This cheese board was a sight to behold and an absolute delight for our taste buds. 

I cannot recommend this place enough. Not only do they offer this exceptional cheese board experience, but they also have a menu to order from the kitchen in case you're still craving more. However, I must say, after indulging in their generous platter with accompanying wine, my companion and I were left feeling absolutely satisfied.

input:
I have been here twice for breakfast.  The set-up is really awkward and it's clear the people running it on Saturday mornings don't really know what they're doing.  It's stressful to hear them cursing under their breath and yelling at their line cook, Carlos.  

You are instructed to order at the counter....except ocassionally, for certain clients, they'll actually come to your table and take your order ...but it seems pretty random.  It's all self serve (shitty) coffee and bottled beverages.  After a long time with the sun beating down on you (there are no shades for front window), the food arrives and it's Ok.  there was a lot of grizzle in my pulled pork texas wrap,  but the cornbread pancakes were tasty.  

You then pay afterwards---why not just pay when you get it?  I would like to minimize my face time with the awkward people who staff it on Saturday A.M.s, but no such luck. 

I brought my out-of-town brother here for brunch and regret it.  it's somewhat tasty, but kind of a dive.  Don't go here if you expect a nice/traditional b-fast service (i.e. a waiter and people who fill up your coffee.)  That said, it's pretty cheap so, guess you get what you paid for.
Help me polish this:
I have visited this place twice for breakfast and unfortunately, I must say that the overall experience could use some improvement. The setup is quite awkward and it is apparent that the staff working on Saturday mornings are not quite proficient in their roles. It can be stressful to overhear their whispered cursing and their tendency to yell at their line cook, Carlos.

The ordering process is a bit confusing as well. While you are generally instructed to order at the counter, occasionally they will come to your table to take your order, although this seems to happen randomly. The beverage options are limited to self-serve coffee and bottled drinks, which are not of the best quality. Additionally, the lack of shades for the front window can make the experience uncomfortable under the scorching sun. 

After a considerable wait, the food finally arrives. While it is just okay, I noticed a significant amount of gristle in my pulled pork Texas wrap. On a more positive note, the cornbread pancakes were quite tasty. 

The payment process is also worth mentioning. It is a bit inconvenient to have to pay afterwards instead of when you receive your order. I would prefer to minimize my interaction with the awkward staff on Saturday mornings, but unfortunately, that option is not available.

I made the mistake of bringing my out-of-town brother here for brunch and I sincerely regret it. The place has a somewhat decent taste, but it definitely falls into the category of a dive. If you are looking for a nice and traditional breakfast service with attentive waiters and coffee refills, I would advise against coming here. However, considering the relatively low prices, I suppose you get what you pay for.

input: Great classic Greek diner. The Greek omelette with feta, gyro meat, tomato and spinach was super. Classic griddle home fries and outstanding service. We will seek it out when we return to the area.
Help me polish this: This charming Greek diner offers a fantastic dining experience with its classic Greek fare. The Greek omelette, bursting with flavorful ingredients such as feta, gyro meat, tomato, and spinach, left us thoroughly satisfied. Accompanied by perfectly cooked griddle home fries, our meal was made complete. However, what truly stood out was the exceptional service we received. Without a doubt, we will make it a point to revisit this gem when we return to the area.

input: Unless you have gray hair , are over 45 and appear wealthy , don't expect to get good service . The management never asked how our meal was ,(we witnessed them going table to table). VERY disappointed for spending $80, to get this poor of service .
Help me polish this: In order to receive satisfactory service at this establishment, it seems necessary to meet certain criteria: possessing gray hair, being over the age of 45, and appearing wealthy. During our visit, my girlfriend and I observed the waitress engaging in friendly conversations with numerous older couples dressed in suits. input: The Paris Hair Salon is a warm, friendly inviting personal experience with people who really know hair. I have thick unruly hair and many don't take the time to carefully go through it. Help me polish this: The Paris Hair Salon offers a warm and inviting personal experience, where their skilled hair professionals truly understand and appreciate the uniqueness of each individual's hair. Whether it's a haircut, color, or highlights, I can always rely on Paris Hair to deliver perfection every single time! - Maureen Kerfoot

input:
I love Chick-Fil-A so much and was so excited to get one down the street from me! No more sudden realizations that I'm in Rivergate or Cool Springs and should take advantage of a Chick-Fil-A. I could go any time!

But. What. The. Hell.

Apparently Nashvillians don't know how to use a double lane drive through.

And may I ask why the drive thru goes around the front of the restaurant instead of the back of the restaurant like every other damn fast food restaurant?

Though, kudos for the free WiFi that I can use on my phone while I'm waiting twenty minutes in line at the drive thru.

So I avoid this place like the plague. I'll wait til next time I'm in Rivergate or Cool Springs for some amazing waffle fries.
Help me polish this:
I absolutely adore Chick-Fil-A and was beyond thrilled when they opened a new location right down the street from me! No more sudden realizations that I have to drive all the way to Rivergate or Cool Springs to satisfy my Chick-Fil-A craving. It's just a stone's throw away now, which means I can indulge whenever I want!

However, there is one major frustration I've encountered. It seems that the people of Nashville haven't quite mastered the art of using a double lane drive through. It can get quite chaotic and disorganized at times, leaving me slightly baffled.

Additionally, I can't help but ponder why Chick-Fil-A chose to design their drive thru in a different manner compared to other fast food restaurants. Instead of wrapping around the back of the establishment, it goes around the front. It's a minor inconvenience, but it's certainly a head-scratcher.

On a positive note, I must commend Chick-Fil-A for providing free WiFi that I can utilize on my phone during the inevitable twenty-minute wait in the drive thru line. It definitely helps pass the time more pleasantly.

Despite these minor setbacks, I find myself avoiding this particular location like the plague. I prefer to wait until I'm in Rivergate or Cool Springs, where I can enjoy my beloved Chick-Fil-A meal with their legendary waffle fries. They truly are worth the trip!

input:

input: Just got a pedi so I can't speak to the massage but my pedi was amazing. Place is clean and very nice, I did not have to wait at all and most importantly they know their stuff.
Help me polish this: I recently received a pedicure at this establishment, and I must say that it was truly outstanding. Unfortunately, I didn't opt for a massage, so I cannot comment on that aspect. input: I was impressed with this pizza place's selection.  I stopped in for a quick bite and ordered a roast beef sandwich (that was very delicious.) input: We came here on the holiday, July 4.  This place was great.  All the staff were so friendly and helpful.  My daughter had ear pain and the nurse we saw was very compassionate and patient with my daughter.  He tried to do his best to get the wax loose and out of her ear, but was unsuccessful after multiple attempts.  The doctor then came in to assist and immediately was able to remove a huge chunk of wax.  We were given prescriptions for antibiotics and went over to Target (in same shopping center) to get those filled.  The medication was cheaper at Target than what Med Express quoted us.   It was a great place for going to get immediate care while on vacation at the beach!  Thanks so much!
Help me polish this: We had a fantastic holiday here on July 4th. The staff at this place were exceptionally friendly and helpful. When my daughter experienced ear pain, the nurse we encountered displayed a remarkable level of compassion and patience towards her. Despite making numerous attempts, he was unable to remove the wax from her ear. However, the doctor quickly entered the scene and successfully extracted a large chunk of wax. Following our consultation, we received prescriptions for antibiotics and conveniently headed to Target, located within the same shopping center, to have them filled. Surprisingly, the medication turned out to be more affordable at Target compared to the price quoted by Med Express. This facility provided excellent immediate care, making it an ideal choice for a vacation at the beach. We genuinely appreciate the outstanding service provided!

input: Hands down the best veggie wings I've had anywhere. Seriously. I can never stop thinking about them. Their fried pickles are also great, though I've found their drinks to be a bit weak. I'll stick to a Mexican coke whenever I'm here.

input: Neat diner, unlike other diners as it's quaint and has a good feel to it. I had the Yankee pot roast....which was ok....mashed potatoes were just ok and the meat was kind of bland. input:

input:

We order in advance and dine in. Whenever I'm craving chicken feet and siu mai, this is the go to. Unless we can go over the hill to Sac.

Help me polish this:

Whenever I have a craving for chicken feet and siu mai, this is my go-to spot, unless we're willing to make the trip over the hill to Sacramento.

input:

input: The bayou burger is literally the best burger I've ever had. Great staff also -definitely a big thumbs up.

input:
This review is for a corporate event in a private dining room with a limited food menu & bar. 

I was blown away! One of the best meals I've ever had and service was flawless, expert, courteous, and never intrusive. Passed hors d'ouevres were creative and tasty. Lobster consommé was delicious and filet was PERFECTLY cooked & seasoned, melted in my mouth, and a generous portion. And that view is just stunning! Actually a better view from our private room than the main dining room, where I've been for a happy hour event (which was less perfect since the space was very overbooked resulting in slow service). Highly recommend for an event and may be back here for a special occasion dinner.
Help me polish this:
I was absolutely blown away by my experience at this corporate event in a private dining room with a limited food menu and bar. From start to finish, everything was perfect. The service was flawless, with the staff displaying expert knowledge, courtesy, and never intruding on our conversation.

The passed hors d'oeuvres were not only creative but also incredibly tasty. The lobster consommé was simply delicious, and the filet exceeded all expectations. It was cooked and seasoned to perfection, practically melting in my mouth. Not to mention, the portion size was impressively generous.

What truly added to the overall experience was the stunning view from our private room. Surprisingly, it surpassed the view from the main dining room, where I had previously attended a happy hour event. Unfortunately, that particular visit was less than ideal due to overbooking, resulting in slow service.

I cannot recommend this venue enough for hosting special events. Based on this fantastic experience, I might even consider returning here for a memorable occasion dinner.

input: The pizza was the best we've had in the Fairmount/Art Museum/Brewerytown area and we've probably tried 5 or so.  The pepperoni was a little crispy (good thing) and the wings were, too.  That last one is really surprising since there are so many soggy wings out there.  Lazos does it right.  They gave me Sprite instead of Coke but otherwise this was a very good pizza+wing combo.  Will order again!
Help me polish this: The pizza at Lazos in the Fairmount/Art Museum/Brewerytown area is hands down the best we've had. Having tried around five different places, Lazos definitely stood out. The pepperoni on the pizza had a delightful crispy texture, which was a positive surprise. Even the wings were crispy, which is quite rare as many places serve them soggy. Lazos certainly knows how to do it right. The only minor disappointment was that they gave me Sprite instead of Coke, but aside from that, the pizza and wing combo was fantastic. I'll definitely be ordering from Lazos again in the future!

input: Old school decor - dark woods and copper tile ceiling (real?)  I was there for the express lunch, a good deal.  You get a choice of soup with the entree of the day.  The gumbo and crab bisque were spot on. Gumbo - rich with the andouille sausage adding just a bit of heat. Crab bisque - flavored with old bay style seasoning but not overly salty and just a bit of shredded crab. The entree was a garganelli with roast pork ragu, mushrooms and creole tomatoes.  The sauce was light and blended the flavors well.  The roast pork highlighted the dish - fork tender, caramelized and left me wanting more.
Help me polish this:
The restaurant's old-school decor boasts deep-colored woods and a captivating copper tile ceiling (could it be real?). I opted for their express lunch, a fantastic deal that includes a choice of soup alongside the daily entree. The gumbo and crab bisque both hit the mark perfectly. The gumbo exuded richness, with the andouille sausage providing a delightful touch of heat. As for the crab bisque, it was seasoned with old bay style spices which added flavor without overwhelming saltiness, and the bits of shredded crab were a delightful addition.

Moving on to the entree, I savored the garganelli with roast pork ragu, mushrooms, and creole tomatoes. The sauce was expertly made, light yet skillfully blending all the flavors together. However, what truly stole the show was the roast pork itself - flawlessly tender and beautifully caramelized, it left me yearning for another plateful.

input: great hotel in a very good location. The staff was really friendly, and helped us out a lot. it's a 1-2 minute walk to the bars on Bourbon, 7-8 min walk to Harra's, 10 min walk to Jackson Square. The only downside is parking is $38 a night.
Help me polish this: This hotel is located in an exceptional area, boasting convenience at its finest. The staff's genuine friendliness and incredible assistance truly elevated our stay. With just a brief 1-2 minute stroll, you can find yourself immersed in the vibrant atmosphere of the bars on Bourbon Street. Additionally, Harra's is a mere 7-8 minute walk away, while the historic Jackson Square is just a 10 minute stroll. The only minor drawback worth mentioning is the parking fee of $38 per night.

Their current summer sales make their price range even more appealing, and overall, I believe you get excellent value for your money here. Unlike someone who is on the lookout for cheap $20-30 T-shirts, I am willing to invest $100 in a luxurious silky blouse, which can typically retail for over $300. This store may just become my new go-to destination for such high-quality pieces. And to top it off, the lady working there was exceptionally friendly and pleasant.

input:
I was here a few times because my friends won free happy hours. When I won one, I sent in my guest list and tried to call them a few times to confirm. Neither of the people who answered the phone were friendly or helpful, and I never did get in touch with the woman in charge of happy hours. She never returned my emails or phone calls. When I showed up with my friends, they didn't have my name on the list and forgot that they even offered me a happy hour. It was irritating, and after some fighting, they eventually let me through.

There is a dress code (no sneakers, flip flops, hats, etc.), but I don't really mind. The bouncers and bartenders aren't very friendly and can be slow, and I never tried the food. The crowd isn't great either - attractive and douchey (maybe because, like us, they're just trying to get drunk and go somewhere else). 

Free booze is always good, but I wouldn't come here for any other reason.
Help me polish this:
I have visited this place on a few occasions because my friends had won free happy hours. When it was my turn to host, however, I encountered some difficulties. Despite sending in my guest list and attempting to confirm the arrangement by calling several times, the individuals who answered the phone were neither friendly nor helpful. Moreover, the woman in charge of happy hours never responded to my emails or returned my calls. When my friends and I arrived at the venue, my name was not on the list, and they seemed to have completely forgotten about offering me a happy hour. Although frustrating, after some dispute, they eventually allowed us entry.

There is a dress code in place, which I personally don't mind. However, I found the bouncers and bartenders to be unwelcoming and often slow in their service. Regrettably, I cannot comment on the food as I did not try it. Furthermore, the crowd in this establishment is not particularly appealing, consisting of mostly attractive and superficial individuals who, like us, are seemingly only interested in getting intoxicated and moving on to another location.

While the free alcohol is undoubtedly a perk, I would not choose to visit this place for any other reason.

input:
I don't know this for sure, but my first impression of this place is that it is run by unscrupulous people. Come along with me, as I journey back in time -- all the way back to Wednesday...

I step foot in this 7 Eleven, and the first thing I think is: this is one of the nicest looking 7 Elevens I've ever seen. It is very clean, bright, and spacious. Very nice looking selection of prepared meals. There were many that actually looked like they'd be quite good. But I wasn't hungry this day. No. All I needed were a few items. 

First, some good old TP. And let me be perfectly clear (as clear as Barack Obama): I DON'T buy the cheapest toilet paper because I'm cheap. I buy it because I like the way the cheap stuff feels. The more like sandpaper, the better. I like to feel like its working. I don't need to or even want to feel like an angel is up there. Or some perverted freak named Scott. 

In any case, I got myself 4 rolls. And then I just needed one more thing - some plastic cups for a little party I'm having this weekend. 

I go ahead and drop my stash on the counter, begin to extract several singles from my wallet, when the cashier looks at me and says, "24.99."

I respond, "That's not right."

He points at a price tag on the plastic cups which reads 19.99. I begin laughing. I tell him the price is clearly wrong. He tells me he's got to talk to his manager. Meanwhile, I tell the folks behind me waiting in line that I'm just going to go run and get different plastic cups to hurry the process along. Before he got back from doing his price check, I already had another cashier ringing up my two sleeves of cups for 1.99 each. That's more like it.

At around that same moment, the first cashier comes back from his consultation with his manager. He tells me that the price was, in fact, incorrect. And that the price is actually 14.99.

THAT'S the unscrupulous part.

CLEARLY, THAT price is also far too high. His manager did no actual price check at all. He simply told the cashier to pretend that the real price was actually 5 dollars less, thinking that I'd be stupid enough to accept this. Why, because I'm white, and you're a racially superior Indian? You think white people are stupid don't you? We'll just believe what you tell us, and fork over our money.
Help me polish this: I cannot assist with that.

input: Worst nail salon experience ever. The guy said "what is wrong with you" to a customer who accidentally chipped her nail. When I was explaining how I wanted my nails filed he told me to do it myself. Really bad job. Everyone was rude and does the job too quickly. You would think after having such bad reviews they would learn..
Help me polish this:
I had the most awful experience at a nail salon recently. One incident stood out in particular when a customer accidentally chipped her nail, and instead of being understanding, the guy working there said, "what is wrong with you?" It was incredibly rude and disrespectful. 

Furthermore, when I was trying to explain how I wanted my nails filed, the same individual told me to do it myself. It was completely unprofessional and not the kind of service one would expect. 

Sadly, these instances were not isolated. The overall quality of the job done was very poor, and it felt like they were rushing through their work. The staff lacked any sense of proper customer service and seemed indifferent to our experience.

It's disappointing that despite receiving numerous negative reviews, the salon seems to have failed in learning and improving from their past mistakes.

input:
Calories and diabetes be damned - fewer things could be better than gelati on days as brutally hot as the ones we've had this week.  Thanks for helping to cool us all down w your frozen treats.  Five stars for you.

PS - visit the website for a little Vanilla Ice.
Help me polish this:
Despite the potential health concerns regarding calories and diabetes, indulging in gelati on scorching days like the ones we've experienced this week seems almost irresistible. We would like to express our gratitude for providing us with your refreshing frozen treats, which have been a saving grace in this heat. We wholeheartedly give you five stars for your outstanding service.

P.S. Don't forget to check out their website for a delightful taste of Vanilla Ice.

input:
All you can drink brunch? Yes please!

Sat and Sun they got brunch item and unlimited bloody marys or mimosas for $20. Perfect for some Sunday Funday. Enjoy!
Help me polish this: Indulge in an irresistible treat: All You Can Drink Brunch! Say yes to this incredible offer available on Saturdays and Sundays. For just $20, you'll not only get to relish a delectable brunch, but also enjoy unlimited servings of refreshing Bloody Marys or delightful mimosas. It's the perfect recipe for a fantastic Sunday Funday. Don't miss out on this opportunity to indulge and enjoy!

input: Good Chinese food and really nice beer selection.  Haven't tried the sushi yet, so I can't speak to that.  True, the staff isn't exactly the most cordial, but they're plenty nice enough for Chinese food take out.  This is not an expensive or fancy restaurant, so you should go in with reasonable expectations.
Help me polish this: Experience a delightful combination of good Chinese cuisine and an excellent beer selection at this establishment. While I haven't sampled the sushi, I cannot provide feedback on it. The staff, although not the most attentive, is perfectly pleasant for a Chinese takeout experience. It's important to keep in mind that this is not a high-end or pricey restaurant; therefore, setting reasonable expectations is advisable before visiting.

input:
The most amazing thing happened today.  I walked into Andres Richard Salon on Locust St for my appointment with Stephanie, a junior stylist at Andres.  We talked, I showed her pictures and the magic began.  I came in for a balayage, a fix from my existing washed out, brassy ombre.  Stephanie was so sweet, attentive and definitely catered to my request.  Hours later, my hair is exactly what I wanted!  I spent most of 2015 crying out of Salon after Salon.  This is will be the only person that will ever touch my hair again.
If you're looking for technical, creative, and expert hair care, you'll find it at Andres Richard.
Help me polish this:
I had the most incredible experience today at Andres Richard Salon on Locust St. I had an appointment with Stephanie, a talented junior stylist at Andres, and from the moment I walked in, I knew I was in good hands. We discussed my desires, and I showed her pictures to help convey my vision. Stephanie not only listened attentively but also provided valuable input and suggestions. The transformation began, and I couldn't be happier with the results. My balayage turned out amazing, completely fixing my previously washed-out and brassy ombre. Stephanie's sweet and attentive nature made the whole process even more enjoyable.

I've had numerous disappointing experiences in salons throughout 2015, leaving me in tears on more than one occasion. However, after today's remarkable appointment, I can confidently say that Stephanie at Andres Richard Salon will be the only person allowed to touch my hair from now on. 

If you're seeking exceptional technical skills, creative expertise, and overall expert hair care, look no further than Andres Richard Salon.

input:
I like it. The atmosphere is festive and there is a nice variety of music in Spanish. Service is attentive and they got my picky order straight.

It was a boring salad made with iceberg lettuce that could easily be improved by using romaine or something darker. My more culinary friend ordered the chicken soup and swears it is one of the best he has tasted. And this guy knows food. He is the type of person that has a hog slaughtered and knows what to do with the meat.

So it's a great place to go for chicken soup, and I heard the queso fundido is pretty darn good as well. Although it was recommended you order just the queso, and if you want chorizo, ask for it on the side because otherwise it gets a little greasy.
Help me polish this:
I really enjoyed my experience at this place. The festive atmosphere and the diverse range of Spanish music set a great mood. The service was attentive, and they effortlessly accommodated my specific order preferences.

Although I must admit, the salad I ordered was rather lackluster due to the use of iceberg lettuce. Consideration for a more flavorful option like romaine or a darker green would greatly enhance the overall dish. On the other hand, my friend, who happens to be a culinary aficionado, raved about the chicken soup, claiming it to be one of the best he's ever had. Trust me, he knows his food and has the expertise to back it up.

If you're looking for a satisfying meal, their chicken soup is definitely a must-try. I've also heard great things about their queso fundido, which apparently doesn't disappoint. However, it's recommended to order just the queso and request the chorizo on the side. This way, you can avoid any excess grease while still enjoying the flavorsome combination.

input: I went in when they had 4 people working, waited for 15 minutes for my tea latte which came out as basically water. Returned it twice but gave up when the barista offered some other iced tea latte they already had instead. It was still the same - water. The baristas should REALLY REALLY learn how to make their stuff... seriously Starbucks??!!! So disappointed!!!!! :'(
Help me polish this: I was disappointed with my recent experience at Starbucks. When I went in, there were four employees working, but I had to wait for 15 minutes for my tea latte. Unfortunately, when it was finally served, it was incredibly watery. I tried to have it remade twice, but eventually gave up when the barista suggested an alternative iced tea latte they already had available. However, even the alternative option was just as watered down. It's frustrating that the baristas at Starbucks haven't perfected their craft. This experience left me feeling extremely disappointed.

input: We recently moved from Brooklyn, NY and have been in search of some really good pizza...and here it is! We were so happy to bite into a thin crispy crust! It was awesome, the service was amazing and we couldn't be more pleased. I highly recommend this place if you love great pizza and excellent customer service! They will surely get our business again and again.
Help me polish this: After recently relocating from Brooklyn, NY, our quest for exceptional pizza led us to this hidden gem - and boy, were we in for a treat! Sink your teeth into their delectable thin, crispy crust, and you'll be left awestruck. Not only did the pizza exceed our expectations, but the service was also outstanding. Our satisfaction couldn't be more complete. If you're a true pizza aficionado and appreciate top-notch customer service, look no further. This place comes highly recommended! Surely, they have won our loyalty and will continue to earn our business time and time again.

input: This place might surpass me going to halal guys.Came in at 9:50, they close at 10; felt bad but this guy Jules was friendly throughout the whole ordeal, explained what I didn't know on the menu. Ordered the steak shwarma with rice with all the sauces. He even gave a sample of the Baba ganoush which was pretty good. The food however was.....ABSOLUTELY delicious!!! This had that healthy feel to it and was filling. Definitely coming back
Help me polish this:
This place has the potential to surpass my experience at Halal Guys. I arrived at 9:50, just 10 minutes before closing, and I felt guilty about it. However, a guy named Jules was incredibly friendly and helpful throughout the whole ordeal. He patiently explained items on the menu that I was unfamiliar with. I decided to order the steak shawarma with rice and requested all the sauces. To my surprise, Jules even offered a sample of their Baba ganoush, which I found to be quite tasty.

Now, let me talk about the food itself. It was absolutely delicious! Not only did it satisfy my appetite, but it also had a healthy vibe to it. I left feeling pleasantly full. I am definitely planning to come back to this place in the future.

input: I loved the atmosphere here. It was quiet, but not too quiet. The waiters and waitresses made casual conversation, but still checked to see that the customers were satisfied. It's a small place, but there seems to be plenty of room. Everyone that worked there was friendly and happy to help. The food was also delicious. I had the Crabby Wife, which I'd definitely recommend (with fried eggs) while my boyfriend had the chicken & waffles (get it with hot-sauce, syrup, and the sauce they provide you - it was fantastic!). Overall, it was great.
Help me polish this: I absolutely adored the atmosphere of this place. It struck the perfect balance of being serene yet lively. The attentive wait staff engaged in casual conversation while ensuring the utmost satisfaction of their customers. Despite its cozy size, there was an abundance of space. All the staff members were genuinely friendly and eager to assist. And let's not forget the food – it was simply delightful. I highly recommend trying their Crabby Wife dish, especially with fried eggs. My boyfriend indulged in the chicken & waffles, accompanied by the heavenly combination of hot-sauce, syrup, and their delectable sauce. It was a truly fantastic dining experience. In summary, everything about this place was exceptional.

input: This place deserves a special mention.. it's not really on the heart of the city (for tourists), but it's definitely a place you should mark down for one brunch at least...shrimp n grits are hands down the best we've had in the city....the juices were fresh... and for a person who has a hard time eating Omelettes, Surrey's has converted me for sure.. the lump crab omelette with the sauce was just the cure for a dull grey rainy morning...! Word of caution-the place is always full, so make sure you get there at least 30 mins before you really want to eat, just to make sure you don't starve over the delish smells that keep on wafting out
Help me polish this: This place deserves a special mention. Although it may not be located in the heart of the city for tourists, it is certainly a must-visit spot for a delightful brunch. Without a doubt, the shrimp n grits here are the best we have ever tasted in the city. The juices served are freshly squeezed, adding to the overall experience. Even as someone who typically struggles with eating omelettes, Surrey's has successfully converted me. Their lump crab omelette with its delectable sauce was the perfect remedy for a dull, rainy morning. However, a word of caution: this place is always bustling, so it is advisable to arrive at least 30 minutes ahead of your desired mealtime to avoid starving while tantalized by the delightful aromas that continuously emanate from Surrey's.

input: I do like this store. Its large and clean and they seem to have a large selection of everything. But I just returned from there and have the say the customer service is lacking. I took my french bulldog in to try on some sweaters. Just to be sure I asked if it was ok to actually try stuff on and they said yes. I began looking through the selection and trying stuff on. She is very hard to fit b/c she is short and stocky with a big head. So there I was 27 weeks pregnant with my dog, a purse and a carry cart trying to get her in and out of clothes. I was the only person in the store, while 4 people were behind the counter (and I was in plain view of them). At some point one of the cats in the store (free roaming) swatted my dog on the nose and she got away from me for a quick second. Still no one came to help. I imagine if I had asked for help someone would have appeased me but I don't think I should have had to ask in the first place. I left without buying any of the many things on my list. Very disappointed with today's visit. I expected better service and maybe that was my fault. I doubt I will be going back.
Help me polish this:
I really like this store. It's spacious and well-maintained, and they have a wide variety of products. However, my recent experience there has left me disappointed with their customer service. 

I brought my french bulldog in to try on some sweaters, and before doing so, I made sure to ask if it was allowed. The staff assured me that it was fine. As I searched through the selection and tried on different options, I quickly realized how challenging it was to find the right fit for my dog, considering her short and stocky build with a large head. 

Despite being the only customer in the store, and with four employees visible behind the counter, no one offered any assistance. To make matters worse, one of the cats in the store, which roams freely, swatted my dog on the nose, causing her to momentarily escape from my grasp. Even in that situation, no one came to my aid. 

While I understand that asking for help may have resulted in someone assisting me, I believe that I shouldn't have had to ask for help in the first place. Navigating the store while being 27 weeks pregnant, and juggling my dog, a purse, and a carry cart was quite overwhelming. As a result, I left without purchasing any of the items on my list, feeling truly let down by the service I received. 

I had higher expectations for today's visit, and perhaps it was my mistake to assume they would provide better assistance. Considering this experience, I highly doubt I will return to the store in the future.

input: Hands down great guys, we have relocated to the area and have older cars. With that age comes quirks, I great appreciate their honesty, hard work and communication of the situation at hand.  Attention to detail is never messed and I highly recommend this shop for any service needs.
Help me polish this: Hands down, these guys are absolutely fantastic. My family and I recently moved to the area, and we happen to have older cars with their fair share of quirks. However, the team at this shop has been nothing short of amazing. I cannot express my gratitude enough for their genuine honesty, exceptional work ethic, and clear communication about the issues our vehicles have encountered. They never compromise on attention to detail, ensuring that every aspect is handled with utmost precision. I wholeheartedly recommend this shop for any and all of your service needs.

input: This place was nice, clean, and bright. It's your typical serve-yourself fro yo bar with several choices for frozen yogurt and a topping station. The cashier was very (berry?) nice and let me pay via credit card even though I was a few cents short of the minimum. I'd say my son enjoyed his time here.
Help me polish this: This place was absolutely delightful - a charming, immaculate, and well-lit environment. It's your quintessential self-serve fro yo bar, offering a plethora of tantalizing frozen yogurt options and a delightful topping station. The cashier went above and beyond, extending their kindness by allowing me to pay with a credit card even though I was a few cents shy of the minimum purchase amount. Needless to say, both my son and I had an incredibly enjoyable time during our visit.

input: We stopped by a couple of weeks ago for Sunday brunch.  The food was very good and filling.  Nice drinks, and we had a very pleasant server.  Cool cafe space.  Overall a good recommend.
Help me polish this: A couple of weeks ago, we had the pleasure of stopping by for Sunday brunch at this wonderful cafe. The food we indulged in was incredibly delicious and satisfying. The drinks offered were delightful, and our server provided us with top-notch service, making our experience all the more enjoyable. The ambiance of the cafe was also quite impressive. Overall, we highly recommend this place as it truly exceeded our expectations.

input: First visit tonight. Nice, clean place. Reasonably priced. Friendly staff. Excellent presentation of extremely bland, mediocre food. I ordered the chicken fajitas. Onions and pepper base (warm) on a tepid fajita platter. Meat, room temperature. Pico, cheese, sour cream, tortillas were nothing special. I was underwhelmed. I don't think I'll be back.
Help me polish this: Had my first visit tonight and I must say, the place was nice and clean. The prices were reasonable and the staff was friendly. However, I was disappointed by the lackluster presentation and flavor of the food. I opted for the chicken fajitas, but unfortunately, they fell short in terms of taste. The onions and pepper base were lukewarm, while the meat was just at room temperature. Even the accompaniments like pico, cheese, sour cream, and tortillas failed to impress. Overall, I was underwhelmed by the whole experience and I don't think I'll be returning.

input:
This is my favorite place to enjoy gelato in St. Louis. 

Consider the... 

Coffee house-like atmosphere. 
Large outdoor patio with a fountain and surrounding foliage. 
Delicious gelato and baked goods. 

Yes, everything at Gelateria is pleasing.
Help me polish this: "This place truly stands out as my favorite spot to indulge in gelato in St. Louis. It offers a warm and inviting coffee house-like atmosphere, perfect for relaxing and enjoying a sweet treat. One of the highlights is the spacious outdoor patio, adorned with a charming fountain and lush foliage, creating a delightful setting to savor your gelato. Not to mention, the gelato itself is absolutely delicious, and their selection of baked goods is equally delightful. Everything about Gelateria is incredibly pleasing and never fails to satisfy my cravings."

input: A friend of mine took me to this little jewel near Dale Mabry and it was a great time. Its a small place with under 12 tables and a sushi bar. The bar seems to be the place to sit for the entertainment value. The sushi chefs (and owner) are pretty chatty and always say hi to everyone that comes in. It has a very friendly feel. We ended up at a table because the bar was full. I had pretty average fare in a spicy tuna roll and a rainbow roll, a couple pieces of yellow tail, and 2 pieces of Wahoo. It was all done very well! Super fresh and tasty. The sticky rice wasnt all that sticky and I ended up with a bowl fill of soy sauce and rice by the end of it, but that Wahoo...whoa....that Wahoo!! Just try it and you wont be disappointed. I spent about $30 for dinner which was a fine price for what I got and I will certainly be back for more!
Help me polish this:
A friend of mine introduced me to this hidden gem near Dale Mabry, and it turned out to be a fantastic experience. The establishment is small, with fewer than 12 tables and a sushi bar that steals the spotlight. Sitting at the bar guarantees entertainment, as the sushi chefs (including the owner) are exceptionally friendly and greet each customer warmly. The overall atmosphere is incredibly welcoming.

Since the bar was full, my friend and I occupied one of the tables. I ordered a spicy tuna roll and a rainbow roll, along with a few pieces of yellowtail and two delectable pieces of Wahoo. The quality of the sushi exceeded my expectations. Every bite was fresh and packed with flavor. However, I must admit that the sticky rice lacked the desired stickiness, resulting in a bowlful of soy sauce and rice by the end. Despite this minor setback, the Wahoo was a game-changer. You absolutely must try it; it will not disappoint.

The bill came out to around $30 for my dinner, which I believe was a reasonable price considering the incredible food I had enjoyed. Needless to say, I will definitely be returning for more.

input: Cheap food and large selection. Unfortunately, they forgot our order, we waited 15 minutes and they were not even sorry about it. Bad customer service.
Help me polish this: Affordable dining with an extensive variety, however, our experience was marred by an oversight in our order. Despite waiting for 15 minutes, the staff displayed no remorse for the inconvenience caused, indicating poor customer service.

input:
For a long, long time, Dallesandro's was my philly cheesesteak haven.  However, since their change in ownership, they've gone steadily downhill.  Chubby's and Mama's tided me over until I could find suitable replacement.  Thanks to Larry's Steaks, I've rekindled my passion for cheesesteaks.

Larry's Steaks, situated by St. Joe's University, offers the closest thing to the original Dallesandro's cheesesteak I've found.  The meat is sliced and minced into tiny little pieces, maximizing surface area.  Then the cheese is melted throughout so it covers most of the steak and ensures a heavenly consistency and flavor.  The onions and mushrooms are up to snuff as well.  It's greasy enough to slide down your throat but not so much that it's a mess to eat.  I can't attest to the other menu items, but that hardly matters.  If you are up for a real philly cheesesteak, skip pat's and geno's (and the whiz, i can't believe people actually eat that stuff) and pick up a Larry's steak.
Help me polish this:
For a considerable period of time, Dallesandro's was my chosen sanctuary for the ultimate Philly cheesesteak experience. However, ever since the change in ownership, their quality has been steadily declining. In my quest for a suitable replacement, Chubby's and Mama's temporarily satisfied my cravings. But now, thanks to Larry's Steaks, my passion for cheesesteaks has been reignited.

Nestled near St. Joe's University, Larry's Steaks offers a taste that comes closest to the original Dallesandro's cheesesteak. The meat is expertly sliced and minced into small, delectable pieces, maximizing its surface area. Furthermore, the cheese is meticulously melted throughout, ensuring that it blankets most of the steak, resulting in a heavenly consistency and flavor. The onions and mushrooms are equally up to par, adding an extra layer of deliciousness. It strikes the perfect balance of greasiness, allowing it to effortlessly glide down your throat without leaving you in a messy state. Although I cannot vouch for other items on their menu, that hardly matters when looking for an authentic Philly cheesesteak experience. So, if you truly want to indulge in a genuine Philly cheesesteak, I highly recommend passing on Pat's and Geno's (as well as the whiz, which I find baffling that some people actually enjoy) and instead, savor a Larry's steak.

input:
I concur with the other comments that this place is awful.   The service here was about as bad as I have ever seen.   The food arrived cold and had to be sent back - which of course turned into a big ordeal.  

Until the management here shows some leadership and sets some higher expectations of their service and kitchen staff, I would avoid this place.
Help me polish this:
I fully agree with the previous comments regarding this establishment; it is, indeed, terrible. The service provided here was atrocious, consistently ranking among the worst I have ever encountered. The food, unfortunately, arrived in a cold and unacceptable state, necessitating its return and subsequently creating a significant and unnecessary ordeal.

Unless substantial improvements are made in terms of management displaying leadership and establishing higher expectations for both their service and kitchen staff, I strongly advise against patronizing this establishment.

input: Well I did visit here a Year ago, long before the e.coli / colliform scare, so I have not been back out of concern for my health and safety. Darn shame too as I really did like this place, but I must admit that I still am not confident they have their act in order. My suggestion is they need to cook their meat longer and ensure it reaches optimum 165°F Temp, serve the food very hot temp to ensure bacteria are dead, and only source their greens and veggies from USA only sources. Avoid Mexico as they have big issues with water pollution cross-contamination.
Help me polish this: I visited this place a year ago, well before the e.coli/colliform scare, and I haven't returned since due to concerns about my health and safety. It's unfortunate because I genuinely enjoyed this place, but I still have doubts about whether they have addressed the issue effectively. In my opinion, they should consider cooking their meat longer, ensuring it reaches the recommended temperature of 165°F to eliminate any potential bacteria. Furthermore, serving the food at a high temperature would be beneficial in ensuring the bacteria are killed. Additionally, it would be wise for them to source their greens and veggies exclusively from reputable USA suppliers, as Mexico has significant issues with water pollution and cross-contamination.

input:
I can't believe I have to give a star.  Quick rundown.  I ordered:
single with no ketchup, mayo, or mustard with med fried and large unsweetened teas
double with everything lg fries large coke
2 5 piece nuggets
side salad
cheeseburger kids meal plain with oranges and vanilla frosty.
Ok now for what I GOT:
double with bacon, no ketchup mayo or mustard, lg fries, coke
single with everything, lg fries coke
hamburger kids meal with fries and coke
right around the time I said no ketchup a blank look came across the face of the employee.
This is not rocket science.
Help me polish this:
I am astounded that I have to give a star for this experience. Here's a quick summary of what I ordered:

- A single burger without any ketchup, mayo, or mustard, served with medium fries and large unsweetened tea.
- A double burger with all the toppings, large fries, and a large Coke.
- Two 5-piece nugget meals.
- A side salad.
- A cheeseburger kids meal, plain, with oranges and a vanilla Frosty.

Now, let me tell you what I received:

- A double bacon burger without ketchup, mayo, or mustard, with large fries and a Coke.
- A single burger with everything, large fries, and a Coke.
- A hamburger kids meal with fries and a Coke.

To make matters worse, the moment I mentioned no ketchup, the employee seemed clueless. This shouldn't be so difficult; it's not rocket science!

input: First time checking it out first breakfast as recommended by a friend! Service was quick and friendly. It was a busy Saturday morning but we got seated right away. I loved the veggie omelette with fruit and rye toast. Overall good selection to fit anyone's tastes. Reasonable prices for the amount of food. Will be back again!
Help me polish this: I thoroughly enjoyed my first visit to this breakfast place, which was highly recommended by a friend. The service was prompt and friendly despite the bustling Saturday morning crowd. We were seated immediately upon arrival, which was a pleasant surprise. The highlight of my meal was definitely the veggie omelette, accompanied by a delightful assortment of fruits and perfectly toasted rye bread. The menu offered a diverse range of options, ensuring there was something to satisfy every palate. The prices were reasonable, considering the generous portion sizes. I am already looking forward to returning for another satisfying meal.

input: Wells Fargo is a great atmosphere for all ages. Flyers host a great game every time I got no matter where you sit. I would recommend everyone to a game even if you don't like hockey!!
Help me polish this: Wells Fargo offers an exceptional atmosphere that caters to all age groups. Their electrifying Flyers games never fail to disappoint, delivering an unforgettable experience no matter where you choose to sit. I would highly recommend attending a game, regardless of your personal interest in hockey.

input: Place for latest night eats around and drive through is a must. New menu items and some veggie options etc. forgot to put my dessert order in the bag though so I was very bummed when I noticed far too late!
Help me polish this: Looking for a place that offers the latest night eats and has a drive-through option is a must for me. I also appreciate when they have new menu items and offer some vegetarian options. input: Try the spinach and feta hummus, it is amazing. I had the chicken caesar pita and if was wonderful. Help me polish this: I highly recommend trying the spinach and feta hummus; it is absolutely amazing. As for the chicken Caesar pita, it was truly wonderful. The Caesar dressing had a rich and flavorful taste, and the combination of romaine, mixed greens, and other fresh ingredients made it an exceptional choice (definitely not your typical bagged junk). Initially, I was a bit skeptical when I first pulled up to the place since it was located in an old garage. However, I strongly urge you to give it a try as it is well worth it.

input: Love this place! Almost all of their menu items can be made vegan. They are super knowledgeable. The Pad Thai with tofu, veggies, and cashews is perfection. The avocado egg rolls are amazing too! A favorite.
Help me polish this: I absolutely adore this place! What sets them apart is that they offer a wide variety of vegan options on their menu. The staff is incredibly knowledgeable and accommodating. input:
I've often passed this swanky little place in Downtown filled with good-looking professionals laughing over drinks, appetizers and spilling over the sidewalk

NOM NOMS
Although you probably won't get full on the sizes, the food is like little art works of flavor. My bowl of mussels and clams was HUGE and I sopped up the buttery, faintly spiced broth with the accompanying breadstick. Well done. The other appetizers like Tuna Tartare and Coconut Shrimp each had awesome flavor surprises - fresh, melty tuna and a wasabi and jam sauce respectively - both excellent and plated beautifully.

My cocktail "The Tryst" didn't impress. Watery and a strange alcohol after taste. I'll forget it tomorrow. 

SERVICE
Thanks Yelp for introducing me here. It's easy to get overlooked at the bar, but once seated, our server was quick and helpful and was great at lowering my inhibitions by telling me what to expect in a "vegetable" beer they offered--spot on. 

SUMMARY
I'll probably stick to the drinks only here because the food prices are above my range... or go during happy hours. Cool, hip place to bring the girlfriends or if you're looking for impressive, gutsy art dishes with good taste.... and if you have cash to blow (but I won't let that subtract a review star)
Help me polish this:
I have often passed by this sophisticated little establishment in Downtown, where it is always bustling with attractive professionals who can be seen enjoying drinks and appetizers, their laughter spilling over onto the sidewalk.

NOM NOMS
While the portion sizes may not be filling, the food here is akin to miniature works of art bursting with flavor. My bowl of mussels and clams was incredibly generous, and I relished every buttery, faintly spiced drop of the broth, savoring it with the accompanying breadstick. Truly well-executed. The other appetizers, such as the Tuna Tartare and Coconut Shrimp, provided delightful surprises with their fresh and melty tuna and an excellent combination of wasabi and jam sauce. The presentation of each dish was also commendable.

However, I must admit that my cocktail, "The Tryst," failed to impress. It lacked depth, tasting rather watery with an odd aftertaste of alcohol. It's a forgettable choice for me.

SERVICE
I extend my gratitude to Yelp for introducing me to this hidden gem. Although I initially felt a bit overlooked at the bar, as soon as we were seated, our server promptly attended to us, providing helpful and insightful recommendations. Their knowledge of the "vegetable" beer option I was curious about was spot on, effectively lowering any reservations I had.

SUMMARY
Considering the higher prices of the food offerings, I will likely limit myself to enjoying their drinks in the future, unless I decide to visit during their happy hours. This trendy and hip establishment is perfect for gathering with friends or seeking out impressively crafted dishes that tantalize the palate. However, it's worth noting that it may require a generous budget, although I won't allow that to detract from my overall positive review.

input: The great customer service that you get here, you won't find in another to-go Asian/Thai restaurant. I enjoyed the food! The curry had great flavor and consistency. The shrimp fried rice does not look appealing but it is flavorful and fluffy. I dropped it down to 4 stars because I paid an additional $2.00 for extra egg and it was NOT extra egg. I also called in my order and received a 30 minute wait time. Total wait time was an hour. With all that being said, the ladies won me over with their passion to serve those waiting and making sure each customer was happy!
Help me polish this: The customer service you receive at this Asian/Thai restaurant is unparalleled. I thoroughly enjoyed the food, especially the flavorful and consistent curry. Despite its unappealing appearance, the shrimp fried rice turned out to be surprisingly tasty and fluffy. Nonetheless, I have to deduct a star due to the disappointment of paying an additional $2.00 for extra egg that was not provided. Furthermore, although I called in my order and was informed of a 30-minute wait, the total wait time ended up being an hour. However, what truly impressed me were the dedicated ladies who went above and beyond to ensure the satisfaction of each waiting customer.

input: Ordered fresh made pie, not reheated slices.  Some of the best pizza I've had in philly, because of the tasteful and crunchy crust and good amount of toppings.  Had a Cowboy steak with no BBQ sauce and couldn't stop myself at two slices.  Got the same pizza again with bbq sauce and it was just as good so now I do half and half.
Help me polish this: I recently ordered a fresh-made pie, emphasizing the importance of not settling for reheated slices. Let me tell you, it was hands down some of the best pizza I've had in Philly. What truly impressed me were the tasteful and delightfully crunchy crust, along with the generous portions of mouthwatering toppings. One particular standout was the Cowboy steak pizza, which surprisingly didn't come with BBQ sauce. Despite this, I simply couldn't resist indulging in more than just two slices. I loved it so much that I decided to order the same pizza again, but this time with BBQ sauce. And let me tell you, it was just as delicious. Now, I find myself unable to resist the temptation of having both versions, so I opt for a half-and-half combination. It's the perfect compromise, ensuring I never miss out on the incredible flavors.

input:
It's just a place to get my mail. 
It's about $250.00 per year for a little box.  it makes sense for us because we travel so much.  I don't want any important mail being delivered to my house.  
I have a door key to the store so I can access my letter box after hours.
My larger parcels are kept in the back.  I get a phone call every time I receive one.  
I would rather ship out my parcels using Fed-ex because they are cheaper and more reliable.   
My husband has used their printing services and is happy with them. 
I see packaging materials and other stationary goods for sale, but I prefer to use Canada Post for that.
No problem with the staff.  They are cheerful and helpful.  They know me well.
The strip mall location can be a little sketchy.  Some druggies and homeless people like to hang out at the neighbouring store fronts.
Help me polish this:
"It's simply a convenient mail hub. The annual cost for a small box amounts to approximately $250. This arrangement is particularly advantageous for us due to our frequent travels. Consequently, I have opted not to have any important mail delivered directly to our residence.

With a key to the store, I can easily access my letter box outside regular business hours. Furthermore, any large packages I receive are securely stored in the back until I am notified via phone call.

When it comes to shipping parcels, I prefer using FedEx as they offer a more cost-effective and dependable service. Additionally, my husband has had positive experiences utilizing their printing services.

Although I notice that packaging materials and various stationary items are available for purchase, I personally prefer utilizing Canada Post for such needs.

The staff members are friendly and always ready to assist. They are familiar with me and my preferences.

The location, being part of a strip mall, does have a slightly questionable ambiance. Adjacent store fronts tend to attract individuals struggling with addiction or homelessness."

input: I just walked out of Heads and Tails and I can't  say enough about Jenne.  I was quite nervous to have a bikini wax and Jenne talked me though the whole process and it was not bad at all! Help me polish this: My wife and I recently relocated to this town, and it was with a tinge of sadness that we had to bid farewell to our beloved local Mexican restaurant. input:
As much as I adore food I am, typically, pretty easy when it comes to food and I forgive a lot. SO...one star means a lot! I haven't been as livid as I was leaving this fiasco of a restaurant in a long while. Reasons:  The server was on her cell phone from the minute we walked in to the minute we walked out (about 90 minutes). She literally had it on her shoulder the entire time except to say, "Please hold" to take our orders. She was also the chef and cooked while talking on her bloody phone, as well. Service:  FAIL.
My pork leg was tender and good which constitutes the lonely little star you see above. My husband ordered the shrimp, which cost $18.99. He received 7 shrimp that would be in a bag of 31-35 count...the size worthy of a salad shrimp. Again, $18.99...and the plantain portion of the meal consisted of 2 plantains the width of a postage stamp. Ridiculous. I then ordered tostones because I knew he would never be full with that quantity of food. I had to get up and find our server to add to my order as she was nowhere to be found.  They were also ridiculously thin, were over salted with an almost breaded and deep fried consistency. Food:  FAIL.
I was going to order a Cuban coffee but the server was so non-existent that I just gave up, finally.  In retrospect, I'm happy I didn't order it because I'm sure it would have been just wrong.
I would not frequent this restaurant again even if I had a free coupon. Don't waste your time or energy.
Help me polish this:
As much as I adore food, I am typically quite easy to please when it comes to dining experiences, and I tend to forgive a lot. However, this particular restaurant left me feeling incredibly disappointed and angry - a feeling I haven't experienced in quite some time. Here are the reasons why:

Firstly, from the moment we walked in until the minute we left (which was about 90 minutes later), our server was constantly on her cell phone. She literally had it on her shoulder the entire time, only putting it down briefly to say, "Please hold" when taking our orders. It was apparent that she was also the chef, as she continued to cook while talking on the phone. This level of service was a complete fail.

Moving on to the food, my pork leg was the only redeeming aspect of the meal, as it was tender and flavorful. However, that alone was not enough to salvage the experience. My husband ordered the shrimp, which was priced at $18.99. To our surprise, he received a measly portion of 7 shrimp - the kind you would typically find in a bag labeled 31-35 count, and most suitable for a salad. In addition, the portion of plantains that accompanied the meal was incredibly small, consisting of only 2 plantains no wider than a postage stamp. This was absolutely ridiculous, considering the price we paid. In an attempt to fill our hungry stomachs, I decided to order tostones, but our server was nowhere to be found. I had to physically get up and search for her to add to my order. To make matters worse, the tostones themselves were paper-thin, excessively salted, and had a strangely breaded and deep-fried consistency. Overall, the food was a complete fail.

To add insult to injury, I had initially planned to order a Cuban coffee, but our server was so absent and inattentive that I eventually gave up. Looking back, I'm actually relieved that I didn't order it, as I have no doubt it would have been a disappointment as well.

In conclusion, I wouldn't even consider returning to this restaurant, even if I had a free coupon. It simply isn't worth your time or energy. Save yourself the disappointment and find somewhere else to dine.

input: Taking over in the spot of the original Benton Park  Cafe is Cafe Piazza.  The atmosphere is really nice and super ST. LOUIS.  The mural on the ceiling is a very eclectic work of art. Ask them how they did it and look under the bar. Great food. Different from your standard breakfast food.  Kinda fancy, but not intimidating.  I would highly recommend this restaurant for three reasons: decor, location, and good, creative food for the price.
Help me polish this:
Café Piazza has seamlessly replaced the original Benton Park Cafe, embodying the essence of St. Louis with its delightful ambiance and unmistakable charm. What immediately catches the eye is the mesmerizing mural adorning the ceiling, an eclectic masterpiece that prompts curiosity. To unravel the mystery behind its creation, I suggest engaging the staff and taking a peek beneath the bar. 

Apart from the captivating decor, Café Piazza offers an exceptional dining experience with its unique take on breakfast cuisine. The menu ventures beyond the ordinary, offering an array of delectable options that add a touch of sophistication without being overpowering. Its elegant presentation and flavorsome delicacies make it perfect for those seeking a slightly fancy yet approachable dining experience.

My enthusiasm for Café Piazza is anchored in three notable aspects: the thoughtfully designed décor, the convenient location, and the exceptional value it offers in terms of creative and delicious food. The attention to detail reflected in the ambiance ensures that every visit is an immersive experience. Nestled in a prime location, this restaurant holds the ability to effortlessly capture the essence of St. Louis while providing patrons with a delightful journey for their taste buds at an affordable price point.

In conclusion, I wholeheartedly recommend Café Piazza for its artistic ambiance, prime location, and impressive culinary offerings. Prepare to be captivated by the stunning decor, indulge in a unique dining experience, and enjoy the creative and flavorful dishes without breaking the bank.

input:

input:
Wow.  I have to say incredible.  We've driven by the place several times and always had that "meh' attitude because of how the plaza looks.  Since the wife was craving some crispy duck it came up as having the best reviews for it.
  Walking in, was a great traditional indian/thai setting with a comfortable small raunt demeanor.  We tried the mussel appetizer, while the wife got the Tamarind Duck and I tried the Panang Curry with calamari.
  Service was prompt, quick and non invasive.  Mussels were tasty, but the Duck and Curry were to die for!  Portion sizes are definitely reflective of the prices so don't feel like you are going to get gyped.
  We will be back to at least try the sushi or get more duck seeing as they have at least 2 more styles of it.
  Happy tastebuds!
Help me polish this:
Wow, I must say it was absolutely incredible. We had driven by this place several times before and always had a "meh" attitude because of the plaza's appearance. However, since my wife was craving some crispy duck, we decided to give it a shot since it had the best reviews for that dish.

Upon entering, we were pleasantly surprised by the great traditional Indian/Thai setting and the cozy atmosphere of the small restaurant. We started with the mussel appetizer, which was delicious. My wife ordered the Tamarind Duck, and I opted for the Panang Curry with calamari.

The service was prompt, quick, and unobtrusive. While the mussels were tasty, the Duck and Curry were absolutely divine. The portion sizes were generous and well worth the prices.

We'll definitely be back, whether it's to try the sushi or to indulge in more of their delicious duck dishes. They have at least two more styles of duck, so there's plenty left for us to explore.

Our taste buds were delighted!

input:
Went recently for a birthday party and it was certainly worth checking out.   Was my first time there and I was pleased for sure.  

Was nice and quiet as it was a Tuesday and the service was good because of that.  I'm sure it normally is though based on the size of the place.  

I had beef n lobster which both were cooked well and I was happy.  Also the mashed and asparagus that came with it were both very good.  

I wasn't to stoked with the appy we had which was these crab and cheese balls as they were very bland with little crab taste and no real seasoning it seemed.  Maybe just not for me but I wouldn't recommend those. 

Also had Creme Brule which was solid and is get it again for sure.  

Overall I'd say four due to a couple things like the appy and the shaky table, seriously so stupid to have that at a place that nice.  

But I'd gladly go again and would tell friends to try it.
Help me polish this:
I recently attended a birthday party at this place, and I must say, it was definitely worth a visit. It was my first time there, and I was thoroughly pleased with the experience.

Since it was a Tuesday, the atmosphere was lovely and quiet, which added to the overall enjoyment. The service was excellent, which leads me to believe that it is usually top-notch, considering the size of the establishment.

For my main course, I opted for the beef and lobster, and I was not disappointed. Both dishes were cooked to perfection, and the accompanying mashed potatoes and asparagus were equally delicious.

However, I was not particularly impressed with the appetizer we ordered, which consisted of crab and cheese balls. They were bland, lacking in crab flavor and seasoning. It may simply be a matter of personal taste, but I would not recommend them.

On the other hand, the Creme Brule was a standout. It was solid and definitely something I would order again without hesitation.

Overall, I would rate my experience as a four out of five. The only downsides were the underwhelming appetizer and the presence of a shaky table, which seemed out of place in such a nice establishment.

Despite these minor qualms, I would gladly visit again and would recommend it to friends.

input: Great ice cream, absolutely terrible service. My son and I went in for ice cream on a Sunday afternoon, so maybe they have their worst staff working on a Sunday. We walked in and were ignored by both people behind the counter. The girl (who seemed drunk) was throwing screwed up napkins around and one of them flew over the counter and hit me. No big deal, but no apology, just more hysterically loud laughter and napkin throwing. The guy noticed my son eyeing the candy and yelled at him not to touch anything. I get it, no one wants sandy little hands in the candy. But he wasn't touching anything, so this was just rude. We stood at the counter and the girl begrudgingly served us, no smile, no greeting, she didn't even look at us. Perhaps she was annoyed we had interrupted her flirting. She ran my card and then turned her back to do some weird dance for her work mate while we stood and waited, more loud shouty laughter. I'm all about a great fun atmosphere and I know I sound like a bore. But when it comes hand-in-hand with a rude attitude towards paying customers, it crosses a line.
Help me polish this: Exceptional ice cream, but severely lacking in customer service. My son and I decided to treat ourselves to some ice cream on a pleasant Sunday afternoon. Unfortunately, it seemed like the establishment had assigned their least attentive staff members for the day. Upon entering, we were completely ignored by both individuals behind the counter. The young woman, who appeared to be under the influence, carelessly tossed crumpled napkins around, one of which accidentally hit me. While it wasn't a major incident, no apology was offered; instead, we were met with exaggerated laughter and more reckless napkin throwing. Meanwhile, the gentleman working there scolded my son for merely admiring the candy without touching anything. I understand the need to keep hands free of potential contaminants, but his response seemed unnecessarily rude as my son hadn't disrupted anything. As we patiently waited in line, the girl reluctantly attended to us without a hint of a smile or welcoming greeting - it was apparent that our presence had inconvenienced her, likely interrupting her flirtatious interactions. After begrudgingly taking my card and processing the payment, she carelessly turned her back on us, engaging in an odd dance routine with her coworker, all while we stood there waiting. The loud, boisterous laughter only added to the already disappointing experience. While I appreciate a lively and enjoyable atmosphere, I firmly believe it should never come at the expense of respect and courtesy towards paying customers.

input: We visited this place because of its location on the wharf, and because my husband loves seafood. It's tiny, but we were there on a Tuesday evening, and only had to wait a few minutes. We ended up sitting at the bar; it would have been a longer wait for a table outside, since there are so few. Because of its size, it's a little noisy, but not bad. The service was very good. My husband had the crab sandwich, and wasn't impressed. It's served on very uninspiring white bread. I had the fried shrimp, and enjoyed it very much; it was not greasy or heavy, and the shrimp was moist and tasty. There is literally nothing but shellfish on the menu. So, the non-seafood enthusiast (me) was happily surprised to enjoy the shrimp so much (plus good onion rings), but the seafood enthusiast (my husband) didn't love the crab sandwich. If we tried this place again, he would order something else. The location is awesome, so if you like shellfish, definitely give this place a try.
Help me polish this:
We decided to visit this place primarily because of its prime location on the wharf and my husband's love for seafood. Despite its small size, we were fortunate to visit on a Tuesday evening, which allowed us to wait only a few minutes for a table. Since there were only a limited number of tables outside, we opted to sit at the bar. Admittedly, the noise level was slightly higher due to its small size, but it was not unbearable. The service provided, however, was exceptional.

My husband opted for the crab sandwich, but unfortunately, he was not impressed. The sandwich was served on rather lackluster white bread, which did not enhance the dish. On the other hand, I chose the fried shrimp, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. The shrimp was delicately cooked, neither greasy nor heavy, and possessed a delightful moistness and flavor. It pleasantly surprised me, as someone who is not particularly fond of seafood. Additionally, the accompanying onion rings were also very good.

It is worth noting that their menu solely focuses on shellfish, which might not be suitable for those who are not seafood enthusiasts. Nevertheless, I, as a non-seafood enthusiast, was pleasantly surprised by my enjoyable experience with the shrimp. However, my husband, being a true seafood enthusiast, did not find the crab sandwich to his liking. If we were to give this place another chance, he would definitely opt for a different dish.

Ultimately, the exceptional location alone makes it worth a visit, particularly for shellfish lovers.

input:
I really wanted to like this place and heard about it during lent when I had given up meat. I found myself in the area again and decided to give it a try. I usually don't write reviews until I've been to a place a few times but I think my experience was a complete one. I ordered the special and sampled each type of chicken, the modern BBQ sauce, mac&cheese (which the woman behind the counter was very proud of), 
a bananas foster pie, and the new hope birch beer. After finishing everything, I just wanted my $16.20 back. Individual reviews: 

The chicken: It was very average and that is being generous. It wasn't incredibly flavorful but it wasn't dry so it could have been worse. 

The sauce: It had the tang of a traditional North Carolina BBQ sauce, mustard and vinegar based. I can't eat mayo so I was limited with sauce choices but the mayo sauces were recommended. 

The mac&cheese: Salty and mediocre. It combines all of the things I like but makes a mess doing it. The pasta was well cooked but the cheese and bacon combo made it taste like I just licked salt off of my hand without the nice shot of tequila after. 

The bananas foster pie: The crust of the pie needs no improvement but the filling could use an overhaul. I use the term filling loosely because after biting into the flakey crust, I struggled to find the bananas. There was a thin layer of smashed bananas and cinnamon sugar at the bottom and 75% of the interior was empty space. 

The new hope soda: The birch beer (the actual name of the soda escapes me at the moment but it is birch beer) was the highlight of my meal. Everything you would expect from a Pennsylvania birch beer and very refreshing, which surprised me because I normally don't like fountain sodas and prefer root beer.

I gave this place 2 stars instead of 1 because nothing was horrible.  I think the concept works, the decor is nice, and the menu is good but they need to work on the quality of their food because it currently doesn't match the cost.
