input:
Spot on!

I got "the veg" and the spicy fries.  "The veg" is a portabella burger, with grilled mozzarella, picked veg, arugula, and gauc.  Wholly non-cow is this thing spectacular for a bella burger!  The bella is on bottom, then the mozzarella is directly fused on top of that.  I actually thought the cheese was halloumi at first because it wasn't super melted (a good thing). The gauc and pickled veg are slightly citrusy and vinegary, but are contrasted by the bitterness of the arugula.  There's a nice bun to contents ratio, and for bonus points it's a potato bun.

Wasn't sure what to expect with the spicy fries going in - are they hot sauce fries, etc?  Turns out they are of the crab-fries variety with some subtle other spices added in.  Nice portion - not too big.

The atmosphere kind of reminds me of a dive bar - I think that's the best way to describe it.  It's pretty small, so I wouldn't choose to ever eat in most likely.

Spot on!

This burger is truly exceptional, especially for those who prefer a vegetarian option. The juicy portabella is placed at the base, with the mozzarella fused directly on top. At first, I mistakenly thought the cheese was halloumi due to its slightly melted state, which turned out to be a pleasant surprise. The guacamole and pickled vegetables offer a subtle citrusy and vinegary flavor, nicely balanced by the bitterness of the arugula. The bun-to-ingredients ratio is spot on, and to add an extra touch, it is served on a soft and delicious potato bun.

Initially, I wasn't quite sure what to expect with the spicy fries. I wondered if they would be coated in hot sauce or have other fiery seasonings. However, they turned out to be more similar to crab fries, subtly seasoned with a few additional spices. The portion size is just right, not overwhelmingly large.

The ambiance of the place reminds me of a cozy dive bar, and I believe that is the best way to describe it. As it is quite small, I personally wouldn't choose to dine in, but that doesn't take away from the overall experience.

Jay Fatimo or something like that, said he was very busy, as were the other service writers, so he handed me his card, and said to just email him with what I needed.  Sounded like a good plan, I wasn't in a big rush.  So I did just that, sent a picture of my vin, and the appropriate RPO codes to know what part I needed, and emailed it all to him.  I never got a response.  I tried again about a week or so later, still nothing.  Made sure it is his email at the dealership, etc.  

I guess I have a hard time with taking my car in or trusting a place to do such repairs (3000 dollar job according to Winkel GMC) if they can't even respond to an email.  He knew I would email that day, and I did.  

I guess the GMC dealer right next door gets my money instead.

input:
This tour is one to take when you want to have a lazy day, but you want to do a passive activity.  Me & my friends didn't wan the lunch, we just wanted to take a tour of the Mississippi.  The cost was average - around $28.00.  Con:  Remember it is a tour, so they have the typical tourist traps - photographer - me and friends declined that option.  

I would suggest if you aren't going to eat - to pull out your smartphone and research the Natchez Native American Tribe who inhibited the area prior to the colonization of the New Orleans area - interesting "tid bits of rituals", so that made the boat ride more fun because I became the secondary tour leader to my group.  If you are in the mood-go get a drink and this will comfort you as you learn more about the area on a steamboat.  Not a bad way to spend a few hours.

This tour is perfect for a leisurely day when you're looking for a low-effort activity. My friends and I didn't feel like having lunch, but we still wanted to experience a tour of the Mississippi. The price was reasonable, averaging around $28.00. However, it's important to note that since it's a tour, you'll encounter the typical tourist traps, such as photographers. My friends and I politely declined that option.

If you're not planning on having a meal, I recommend taking out your smartphone and researching the Natchez Native American Tribe who previously inhabited the area before the colonization of New Orleans. You'll come across fascinating tidbits about their rituals and traditions, which can add an extra layer of enjoyment to the boat ride. In fact, I ended up becoming the unofficial tour guide for my group, sharing interesting facts as we sailed along. 

If you're feeling in the mood, grab a drink during the tour. It can enhance your experience as you learn more about the area on a delightful steamboat ride. All in all, this tour is a great way to spend a few relaxing hours.

input: Just visited The Fat Ham with my girlfriend about an hour ago. The place is small, but the vibe is nice. Music isn't too loud, the staff welcomed us and the whiskey display is impressive. We couldn't get a table, so we took the two empty seats at the bar. The bartender, Dan, greeted us immediately. Dan was effecient, quick and friendly. Great service. My girlfriend ordered a margarita, which was reasonably priced and tasty. To eat, we ordered the pimento cheese, skillet cornbread, shrimp & grits and the hot chicken. Everything was delicious. The pimento cheese had some heat, and the country bread it is served with gives it a nice touch of salt. The mollases butter on the cornbread was "to die for". The shrimp & grits was my favorite dish. Creamy grits, perfectly cooked and seasoned shrimp. As for the chicken, they do not lie to you. It is hot. The brioche and ranch dressing compliment it well. For desert, we ordered the raspberry cobbler and a coffee. The cobbler was underwhelming. It wasn't bad - just not as great as the previous plates. Elixr coffee was spot on. Overall, I'll be back. Decent price point, high end comfort food and great service.
Help me polish this:
Just visited The Fat Ham with my girlfriend an hour ago, and we had a great experience. Despite its small size, the restaurant had a pleasant vibe with nice background music that wasn't too loud. We were warmly welcomed by the staff, and the impressive whiskey display caught our attention.

Unfortunately, we couldn't secure a table, but we happily settled for two empty seats at the bar. That's when we met the bartender, Dan, who immediately greeted us with efficiency, quickness, and friendliness. We were impressed with his service.

My girlfriend ordered a reasonably priced and tasty margarita, while I indulged in the pimento cheese, skillet cornbread, shrimp & grits, and hot chicken. Every dish we tried was absolutely delicious. The pimento cheese had a satisfying kick of heat, and the country bread it came with added a nice touch of saltiness. We couldn't resist the molasses butter on the cornbread— it was truly heavenly. However, my personal favorite was the shrimp & grits. The creamy grits and perfectly seasoned shrimp were an absolute delight. I must admit, the hot chicken lived up to its name, and the brioche and ranch dressing that accompanied it were a perfect complement.

For dessert, we ordered the raspberry cobbler along with a coffee. While everything else surpassed our expectations, the cobbler was a bit underwhelming. It wasn't bad, just not as extraordinary as the previous dishes. On the bright side, the Elixir coffee was excellent and provided a satisfying end to our meal.

Overall, we had a fantastic experience at The Fat Ham and will definitely be returning. With its decent price point, high-end comfort food, and exceptional service, it's a place worth revisiting.

input: When this place first opened we went. We loved the Greek salad and gyros. It was very fresh tasting and the place was cute. My salad had one bite of potato salad and two items in the salad - tomato and pepper tasted off. I had to spit them out. My daughter got a fajita bowl with chicken. Her tomato was also gross and the chicken was cooked into charred rubber. We ordered baklava and it was stale. I hope they clean and go back to the quality it was when they first opened. It was yummy and clean.

The flavors were incredibly fresh, and the charming ambiance of the place added to our overall dining experience. However, our recent visit was quite disappointing. The tables were all dirty, and the lamps were covered in dirt and dead bugs, which left us feeling somewhat disgusted. Unfortunately, the decline in cleanliness wasn't the only issue. The quality of the food had noticeably diminished. My salad had only a small portion of potato salad, and the tomato and pepper tasted off-putting, causing me to spit them out. To make matters worse, my daughter ordered a fajita bowl with chicken, and the tomato was also unpleasantly flavored, while the chicken had unappetizingly transformed into a charred rubbery texture. As if that wasn't enough, even the baklava we ordered for dessert was stale. It is our genuine hope that the establishment takes immediate action to address these concerns and returns to the exceptional quality it once had when they first opened. input:
This was our first time here. I had a coupon so I thought I would try it out. Pulling into the parking lot I noticed it was very busy. I was worried that I would have to wait a long time. I pulled up to the attendant and asked how long it would be for a reg wash. She said each wash takes about 15 minutes. I was surprised since they were busy. I left the car there and proceeded inside. 

The building is huge inside. One side is all windows so you can watch your vehicle move through. They even have a "soap gun" the kids can use to shoot their car. That was a huge hit. 

The cashier greeted me as I walked up to the counter. She took my coupon and handed me a receipt. I walked around while I was waiting. They have drinks she snacks for purchase. They sell lots of greeting cards for every occasion. They have gifts and accessories for your car. The building was cool inside which was great because it was hot the day we came in. I waited about 10 minutes and walked outside. They have a large covered area to wait under. It has some seating so you can sit and wait. After just a few minutes they yelled out my car make to say it was done. I handed the attendant my receipt and tip and I was on my way. Total time was 18 minutes which I think is fair considering they were packed when I arrived. 

The car was clean and vacuumed. Overall they did a great job. The only thing they missed was the front window. It had that haze on it that you notice when the sun hits its. I wiped it off myself. I'm sure they would have fixed it if I noticed before I left. Also, they don't offer free air freshener with the wash like most other places. 

This place was fast and they did a great job. The price was fair and the staff was friendly. I will be coming back soon.

input:
Trying to find a restaurant in The Big Easy that serves vegetarian is not an "Easy" feat

We've encountered many the restaurant who would tell us time & time again that they did not have or *would* not make something to accommodate veggie needs & it was such a letdown.....to this day I still remember 1 guy saying "Vegetarian?  Aww, you gotta get out earrrrrly for *that*".  We still laugh about it....

Well, over the last few years, we're noticing more & more places recognizing veggies like to eat Southern / Cajun comfort food & they are starting to open up their menus to us! ( YAY)

Seeing that Muriel's Jackson Square had such an offering, we made rezzies to ensure we veggies got fed - you'll want to do this too - veggie or not!  They were packed & quoting 2 hr waits & this was at 9pm!

Started w/ drinkys at the bar - Sazerac for the Mr & I had the uber-delish Honey Child cocktail: honey-infused vodka & muddled blackberries.  The Mr liked mine so well that he ordered 1 too, to go w/ dinner & just to be nice, I had another as well so he wouldn't have to drink alone

Their veggie appie had eggplant, of which I'm not a fan so we asked the waitress if they could make their Goat Cheese Crepe, veggie & she said sure.  Since the description said it was topped w/ crawfish, we thought, this would be easy..... but unfortunately, the roulade sauce was made seafood stock. ACK!  Wished you had told us this!  The Mr however, said the crepe was nice & plump, the goat cheese was creamy & smooth & he liked it, barring the sauce

Mains consisted of their Veggie Soiree - this was a sampling of little dollops of veggie tastes - some you'll find on their side dish offerings & some not

Divine beets & roasted acorn squash

Polenta topped w/ chickpeas & a basil sauce - flavorful though those beans were crunchy & could have used a bit more time in the cooker.... same w/ the crunchy wild rice

Yams were very flavorful & had lots of ginger - the Mr got to indulge in both our dollops of chard - I tried a bite & it triggered my dislike for cooked greens

Too full for dessert, we left w/ happy tummies & thankfulness for a nice veggie night out.  A-OK night!
Help me polish this:
Trying to find a vegetarian-friendly restaurant in The Big Easy is no easy task. We have encountered numerous restaurants that either did not have vegetarian options or were unwilling to accommodate our needs. It was disappointing, and we still remember one guy saying, "Vegetarian? Aww, you gotta get out early for that." We still laugh about it.

However, things are changing, and we have noticed more and more places recognizing that vegetarians enjoy Southern/Cajun comfort food too. These establishments are starting to include vegetarian options on their menus, and it's something to celebrate.

When we discovered that Muriel's Jackson Square offered vegetarian dishes, we made reservations to guarantee that we would be able to enjoy a meal there. Whether you are a vegetarian or not, we highly recommend making reservations, as the restaurant was packed and quoting two-hour waits, even at 9 pm.

We started our evening with drinks at the bar. The Mr. had a Sazerac, and I had the incredibly delicious Honey Child cocktail, made with honey-infused vodka and muddled blackberries. The Mr. enjoyed mine so much that he ordered one for himself, to accompany dinner. And just to be kind, I had another one so he wouldn't have to drink alone.

For the appetizer, we initially ordered the veggie option with eggplant, but since I'm not a fan of eggplant, we asked the waitress if they could make their Goat Cheese Crepe vegetarian. She happily obliged. However, we were disappointed to find out that the roulade sauce contained seafood stock, which was not mentioned on the menu. It would have been helpful to know this beforehand. Despite the sauce, the crepe itself was enjoyable, with its plump texture and creamy, smooth goat cheese.

For the main course, we ordered their Veggie Soiree, which consisted of small portions of various vegetable dishes, some of which were also available as side dishes. We particularly loved the divine beets and roasted acorn squash. The polenta topped with chickpeas and basil sauce had great flavor, although the beans were a bit crunchy and could have used more cooking time. The same went for the crunchy wild rice. The yams were very flavorful, with a generous amount of ginger. Unfortunately, I'm not a fan of cooked greens, so the Mr. enjoyed both our dollops of chard.

Despite being too full for dessert, we left with satisfied tummies and a gratefulness for having a pleasant vegetarian dining experience. It was a fantastic night overall.

input:
I ate at Puckett's yesterday for lunch, and I have to say it was some mighty tasty food for an old-fashioned meat-and-three.  But I actually had a meat-and-two!  Definitely check out the squash casserole.  it was quite the tasty dish.  I'd also recommend their meatloaf, which is what I had.

My only complaint--and it's a minor one--is that they advertise cornbread.  Yes, it's cornbread, but not a slice of cornbread like you typically think of it.  People in the North would call it a corn fritter.  Being from KY, I'd call it a hoe cake.  It's cornbread but more like a cornbread pancake.
Help me polish this:
I dined at Puckett's yesterday for lunch and I must say, their old-fashioned meat-and-three offered some mighty tasty food. However, I opted for a meat-and-two instead. One dish that you definitely shouldn't miss is their squash casserole; it was absolutely delicious. Another recommendation would be their meatloaf, which is what I had.

If I had to nitpick, my only complaint would be regarding their cornbread. While they advertise it as cornbread, it's not the typical slice you would expect. In fact, it resembles more of a corn fritter, or as us Kentuckians would say, a hoe cake. It's a slight deviation from the traditional cornbread, more like a cornbread pancake.

What I thought was a courtesy extend turned out to be bait a D switch.  They gave e me a 'courtesy room' with the understanding that upon my return,  I would get the suite I booked.

Although the hotel staff offered insincere apologies, it was clear that they were not willing to go the extra mile to rectify the situation. I left feeling dissatisfied and knowing that I would never choose to stay at a Hilton property again.

input:

Spotless restrooms and the service is top notch.

input:
This place is top notch, with phenomenal service and such fantastic ambiance- how can you go elsewhere? All of the food looked and smelled amazing. I love how creative everything was.
I CANT STOP DAYDREAMING ABOUT THE FOOD. Hands down, best brunch experience of my life. I don't even like french toast usually and theres was by far the most delicious food thats ever entered my mouth. I am literally drooling while writing this.

Help me polish this:
This place is truly exceptional, offering impeccable service and an unbeatable ambiance that sets it apart from any other. From the moment I walked in, I was captivated by the amazing array of food that looked and smelled absolutely divine. The creativity infused in every dish was simply remarkable.

input: I'm so happy we came upon this place randomly. They have a happy hour 3-8pm everyday:  Half off all beers, $3-$4 glasses of wine & $8 hookah! Their hookah on non-happy hour is $13. They have a wide selection of shisha flavors and even options of an ice chamber or smoking from a fruit bowl (extra charge). They do have a food menu, but I didn't try anything from it. But the plates I saw coming from the kitchen look pretty good. Overall, a really chill place to come and relax with friends. It was definitely an enjoyable experience.
Help me polish this: I'm delighted that we stumbled upon this place by chance. They offer a fantastic happy hour from 3-8pm every day, where all beers are half off, glasses of wine range from $3 to $4, and hookahs are only $8! Outside of happy hour, their hookahs are priced at $13. What sets them apart is their wide variety of shisha flavors, and they even provide the option of adding an ice chamber or smoking from a fruit bowl for an additional charge. Although I didn't try anything from their food menu, the plates I saw coming out of the kitchen looked tempting and delicious. All in all, it's a truly laid-back spot to unwind and hang out with friends. Our experience there was undeniably enjoyable.

input:
I absolutely love this hotel. It is certainly one of my favorites. Upon walking into the building, to your right you will enter the lobby. The lobby is adorable with eclectic decorations and 1 million places to sit that are very comfortable. They serve wine every day from 5 to 6 PM, it's nice to relax down in the lobby with a glass of wine and friendly staff..

Speaking of the staff, they are amazing. Checking in is fantastic, Jasmine and Kayla are the ones I dealt with and they are both wonderful. The hotel concierge Roshid is a very friendly and knowledgeable concierge, they are very lucky to have him on staff. The housekeepers are great, the rooms are immaculate. What I love most about this hotel are the fantastic bathrooms, I'm not sure about the regular rooms, but if you get a king spa room, the bathrooms are absolutely amazing. You have a freestanding tub, and a large shower and you can jump in between the two should you be so inclined ha ha. The decor is so attractive, incredible wallpaper, beautiful rugs, everything seems brand new and they keep it in perfect condition. This hotel is a must for anyone visiting Philadelphia. They make you feel right at home at the moment you step in the door. The pictures that you can get from inside the rooms are enough to make up your whole trip to Philly LOL. But if you want to get out and explore Philly you're only steps away from the Liberty Bell and a historical museum. Right in Center City or the old downtown area, you'll find lots of historical information about Philadelphia.  Definitely stop in and stay at the Monaco, you won't regret it!
Help me polish this:
I absolutely adore this hotel, as it has become one of my absolute favorites. The moment you step into the building, the lobby greets you on the right with its charming and eclectic decorations. The abundance of comfortable seating options adds to the overall appeal. Furthermore, the daily wine service from 5 to 6 PM creates the perfect atmosphere to unwind and relax, complemented by the warm and friendly staff.

Speaking of the staff, they are truly exceptional. Checking in was a breeze, thanks to the outstanding service provided by Jasmine and Kayla, both of whom were absolutely wonderful. One highlight of the hotel is the knowledgeable and affable concierge, Roshid. His presence adds immense value to the guests' experience. Moreover, the housekeeping team ensures immaculate rooms, a testament to their attention to detail.

While I cannot speak for the regular rooms, the king spa rooms boast stunning features that capture my heart. The resplendent bathrooms, in particular, are simply breathtaking. Complete with a freestanding tub and a spacious shower, one can effortlessly transition between the two for a luxurious experience. The attractive decor, including exquisite wallpaper and beautiful rugs, adds to the overall allure of the rooms. It is evident that the hotel takes great care in maintaining everything in pristine condition.

This hotel truly epitomizes the essence of a home away from home. From the moment you enter, you are enveloped in a sense of warmth and familiarity. The captivating views from within the rooms alone are enough to make your entire trip to Philly worthwhile! However, should you wish to explore the city, you'll be delighted to know that the hotel is conveniently located just steps away from significant landmarks such as the Liberty Bell and various historical museums, nestled in the heart of Center City or the old downtown area. Philadelphia's rich history is showcased in abundance in this area.

In conclusion, I wholeheartedly recommend a visit to the Monaco. Your decision to stay here will not disappoint, as this hotel surpasses all expectations. It truly encapsulates the essence of Philadelphia and ensures you feel like a cherished guest throughout your stay.

input: Love, Love, LOVE this store!!!  I admit, I'm an addict. But where else can you get a Bebe top, a Banana Republic skirt and a BCBG skirt for $4.13?????  The savings are ridiculous!
Help me polish this: I absolutely adore this store - I am head over heels in love with it! I must confess, I'm completely hooked. It's mind-blowing how I can score a Bebe top, a Banana Republic skirt, and a BCBG skirt all for just $4.13. The level of savings here is absolutely absurd!

input: It is what you expect in an Acme, the only thing I found a little different with this one is that it seemed the aisles were a little narrower than in other stores. Store is a little smaller than others so not as wide of a variety, but was fine, looks like they've upgraded some areas like the frozen/refrigerated food sections. Service was fine.

input: We're new to the area, so we're exploring restaurants every weekend. My wife has already proclaimed The Roost her favorite, and that's based on many years of breakfast dining, not just in this area. They bake all their own breads and pastries. Try the raisin bread or sugar-cinnamon toast. Yum! The cornbread casserole is another dish my wife and I highly recommend. And the service was prompt, attentive and very friendly. Enjoy!
Help me polish this: We are newcomers to the area and have been spending our weekends exploring different restaurants. Recently, my wife discovered a gem - The Roost. With years of breakfast dining experience, she instantly declared it her favorite spot, not only in this area but overall. One of the things that sets The Roost apart is that they bake all their breads and pastries in-house. If you have the chance, don't miss out on their delectable raisin bread or mouthwatering sugar-cinnamon toast - they are absolutely delicious! Another must-try dish is their cornbread casserole, which received high praise from both my wife and me. Furthermore, the service we received was top-notch - prompt, attentive, and exceptionally friendly. Don't miss the opportunity to enjoy a wonderful dining experience at The Roost!

input: Small, crowded and hectic but boy the food was good and plentiful. Wait staff was right on top of the chaos. Great breakfast place.
Help me polish this: This small eatery may be crowded and hectic, but trust me, the food is worth it! The ample portions and delicious flavors make it an absolute delight. Despite the busyness, the wait staff handles the chaos flawlessly, providing attentive and efficient service. It's truly a fantastic spot to enjoy a scrumptious breakfast.

input: Finally went in after walking by so many times. Glad we did. Small place but IR is pleasing to the eye. One wall cover with wood palates and subtle two tone gray walls. Started with the prosciutto fig arugula Parmesan flatbread appetites. Enough for two people and delicious. Nice mix of flavors. Main dishes were a burger grass fed beef with fries coated with truffles dusting. Burger was humongous!  Looked good smelled good and tasted good. I had a seafood soup with fish ( not sure what it was) shrimp and mollusks in a  coconut/ curry broth. Deliciously spicy but not enough to kill your taste buds. Overall I would recommend this place. We went early as we heard it gets crowded and they do not take reservations.  BYW great wine and craft beer selections
Help me polish this:
Finally, we decided to give it a try after passing by numerous times, and we were not disappointed. Despite its small size, the interior of the restaurant is aesthetically pleasing. One wall is adorned with wooden palates, and the two-tone gray walls give off a subtle yet stylish vibe.

To start our meal, we ordered the prosciutto fig arugula Parmesan flatbread appetizer, which proved to be both generous in portion size and incredibly delicious. The combination of flavors was expertly balanced, and it was more than enough to satisfy the appetite of two people.

Moving on to our main dishes, we opted for the grass-fed beef burger with truffle-dusted fries. The burger was not only massive in size but also visually appealing and had an enticing aroma. Fortunately, it tasted just as good as it looked and smelled. Additionally, I had the pleasure of trying their seafood soup consisting of fish, shrimp, and mollusks in a delightful coconut curry broth. The spiciness of the soup was just right, adding a flavorful kick without overpowering the taste buds.

Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant. It would be wise to arrive early, as it tends to get crowded, and be aware that they do not accept reservations. Lastly, their wine and craft beer selections are excellent, adding to the overall dining experience.

input:
Reading the reviews, I cannot agree with the others which tout the quality of the food. I had the dinner buffet and the food was mediocre at best. The selection was fine, though they do charge a higher price if you want crab legs. BTW- neither Easy Buffet nor Ginger Buffet charge extra for crab legs. The flavors were there, but the meats were dried out, concentrated, and fried foods soggy and tough as if the they hadn't been turned over in hours and were just sitting on the steam table.  

Service was very nice but slow, especially since there were only 3 tables going the whole time we were there.  I think they had him responsible for too many things other that waiting tables.  

There is a slim chance I'll come back since there are 3 other Chinese buffets in the area that I prefer over Dragon.  Perhaps if I do, there will be more guests to turn over the food and I can update my ratings.
Help me polish this:
After reading the reviews, I cannot agree with the positive comments regarding the food quality at Dragon Buffet. In my experience, the dinner buffet was mediocre at best. While the selection was satisfactory, it is worth mentioning that they charge an additional fee for crab legs, unlike Easy Buffet and Ginger Buffet. 

Although the flavors were present, the meats appeared to be dry, overcooked, and the fried foods were soggy and tough. It seemed as if they had been sitting on the steam table without being turned over for hours. This significantly impacted the overall enjoyment of the meal.

While the service was friendly, it was noticeably slow, especially considering the limited number of tables occupied during our visit. It appeared that the server had a multitude of responsibilities beyond waiting tables, which likely contributed to the delay in service.

Given the existence of three other Chinese buffets in the vicinity that I personally prefer, the likelihood of me returning to Dragon Buffet is slim. If I do decide to give it another chance, I hope to encounter a larger guest turnout, ensuring a quicker turnover of food and allowing me to potentially reevaluate my ratings.

input: This is our "go to" place! The food is consistently good and we always have friendly attentive waiters to sometimes help with our decisions. One of our favorites is the pasta pockets with pear filling. Really delicious! It's also byob which is always a plus. This is a great restaurant with a real cozy, family atmosphere. Highly recommend.
Help me polish this: This place is hands down our favorite! The food is consistently amazing, and the attentive and friendly waitstaff are always there to assist us in making the right choices. Personally, we can't get enough of their delectable pasta pockets filled with pear. They are truly mouthwatering! Oh, and did we mention that it's BYOB? That's definitely an added bonus. input: To sum it up, it's an average bar with ties to a very well-known TV show - but that fact doesn't make the food or much else better. When I went they had $4 White Rascal's and on top of that I had the normal gravy fries. $11 for fries, steep to say the least. They were steak fries, covered in gravy and mozzarella cheese and while pretty damn good, I would be hesitant to say that they're worth the price. When I visited, they were offering $4 White Rascal beers and I opted for their standard gravy fries, which were priced at a rather steep $11. Although these fries consisted of steak fries smothered in gravy and mozzarella cheese and were quite tasty, I had reservations about whether they justified the price. The service was generally satisfactory, albeit occasionally a bit slow, but the staff remained friendly throughout.

input: I went here based on the Yelp reviews and found everything to be true. The staff is extremely helpful and willing to answer all questions. I will continue to bring my bike repair/maintenance needs here.
Help me polish this: I decided to visit this place after reading the positive Yelp reviews, and I have to say that everything written is absolutely true. input: A very nice hotel and a good value. ($175/night) The king bed was primo, the room tastefully furnished. The  rotating Carousel bar is fun and the pool at the top of the building is a great way to cool off on a 95 degree day.We stay there given the great location in the French  Quarter, but our room facing Royal St. was very loud, especially on Friday night. Try for a room not facing the street if you are there over a weekend. Make sure they remove the extra $60 per night they tack on to your room charge for incidentals.
Help me polish this:
This hotel is a gem, offering both luxury and affordability at just $175 per night. The king bed in our room was incredibly comfortable, and the overall decor was tastefully elegant. One of the standout features was the rotating Carousel bar, which added an extra element of fun to our stay. Additionally, the rooftop pool provided a refreshing escape from the scorching 95-degree weather. The hotel's prime location in the vibrant French Quarter is definitely a major advantage.

However, one minor drawback was that our room facing Royal St. was quite noisy, especially on Friday night. If you plan on staying over the weekend, I would recommend requesting a room that doesn't face the street to ensure a quieter experience. It's also worth noting that an additional $60 per night was added to our room charge for incidentals. Make sure to double-check that this charge is removed before finalizing your bill.

input: the handmade orangina is delicious-better than the bottled version! and the croissant sandwiches are amazing!

input:

input: I had a most-delicious bagel sandwich this morning - pork roll, egg and cheese on an everything bagel. The price was very fair - $4.23 - and the bagels are made on site each day. They seem understaffed so hopefully they get some more staff to keep up with the crowds.

input: Warning, if you come here on a Sunday there is a set tasting menu.  We were a party of two, they served us with one plate, "family style".  The only problem is the woman next to us was a party of one and had the same size servings.  They are claiming family style but giving the same portions they give to one person to multiple people. Help me polish this:
Please be aware that if you visit this establishment on a Sunday, they only offer a set tasting menu. During our visit as a party of two, we were served with a single plate in a "family-style" manner. However, we noticed that the woman next to us, dining alone, received the same portion sizes. While they claim to serve family style, it seemed as though they were providing the same portions to both single diners and larger parties. 

My suggestion is to explicitly request individual plates if you prefer to be served as a single person. Although the food itself was delicious, I found this approach to be unacceptable from a business standpoint. As a result, I do not plan on returning.

input: Wonderful place, if you haven't checked it out!  Went there for a pizza making class. input: Overpriced and underwhelming.  Had the sausage/egg:cheese sandwich this morning on whole grain $4.89. Sausage was cold and the sandwich was about 1/2 the size of the picture on the menu. Help me polish this:

The sausage was served cold and the sandwich itself was only about half the size depicted on the menu. input:
I came here because of the higher rating and they accepted my insurance. My initial visit went well, no complaints on the staff or the doctor at that time. 

They switched my brand from Acuvue to Air Optix and about 2 weeks after using the contact I started to experience pain, redness and irritation. I took my contacts out that evening and had red rings around both of my eyes. I tried contacting them via telephone and left a message as well as email, I failed to hear back from them in a timely manner so I reached out to them again and got ahold of them. I simply wanted my contacts switched back to Acuvue and they tried to tell me that it was allergies causing my problems and were insisiting on me keeping Air Optix. Eventually I did get them to agree to switch my contacts back to acuvue. 

In march I had another eye irritation and I went to Vanderbilt Eye Institue, they told me it was a continued reaction to the Air Optix lenses because I did not give my eyes enough time to heal before applying my new contacts - which was I was not educated on by Music City Optical when I got my new set of contacts. I then reviewed them on facebook at that time. 

Today (8/30/16) I recieved a response to my review on facebook and a corresponding email stating that I was being slanderous and lying, which was not the case at all. I was simply explaining my experience with Music City Optical.
Help me polish this:
I chose to visit Music City Optical based on their high rating and the fact that they accepted my insurance. During my initial visit, I had no complaints about the staff or the doctor.

However, after switching my brand of contact lenses from Acuvue to Air Optix, I began experiencing pain, redness, and irritation about two weeks later. Worried, I promptly removed the contacts and found red rings around both eyes. I tried contacting Music City Optical through phone and email, but did not receive a timely response. After reaching out again, I was finally able to speak with them. My only request was to switch back to Acuvue, as I believed the Air Optix lenses were causing the issues. Despite their insistence that it was allergies, I eventually convinced them to make the switch.

In March, I experienced another eye irritation and sought help from Vanderbilt Eye Institute. They informed me that it was a continued reaction to the Air Optix lenses because I had not allowed enough time for my eyes to heal before using the new contacts - something I had not been educated on by Music City Optical. As a result of this experience, I decided to share my feedback on Facebook at the time.

Recently, on August 30, 2016, I received a response to my Facebook review and an accompanying email, accusing me of slander and lying. I want to clarify that I was simply sharing my personal experience with Music City Optical and did not intend to defame them in any way.

The Naan with peach chutney was amazing.
The Lamb Korma was perfect. Perfect amount of spice (too many Indian restaurant set your mouth on fire and you can't enjoy the taste). Not too much, not too little.

The Lamb Korma was a delight. It had just the right amount of spice, not overpowering like some other Indian restaurants. The balance was just right, allowing me to savor every bite without being overwhelmed.

Beyond the food, the decor of the restaurant is impressive. Those chairs in the front add a touch of elegance. The staff members are extremely friendly and provide excellent service. I was pleasantly surprised at how quickly my order arrived. 

I'm actually relocating to Tampa, but I can already see myself making the drive back here multiple times. The quality of the food and overall experience make it well worth it. 

Without a doubt, I highly recommend this place, even if it means driving a bit. The exceptional food, friendly staff, and inviting atmosphere make it a must-visit spot for any Indian cuisine enthusiast.

input:
Brother Rabbit you are young, hip, and tasty!

Met friends for drinks and an early dinner. I was the first to arrive so I sat at the bar and ordered the house cider which is great and I followed that with the Oban 18 which is phenomenal so try it while you're there. 

Our dinner kicked off with the most amazing house biscuits and butter that will have you begging for the recipe.

The rest of our dinner was comprised of several selections from the First course menu. We had the daily oysters which were great. Followed by the Brussels sprouts, delicious but the crispy chicken skins were a bit of a let down, they needed more flavor. 

The smoked tuna tartar is great but the sweet chips can overwhelm the dish. Definitely get the marinated shrimp and jalapeño jus it is a wonderfully fresh and bright dish. 

To close thing up we had the dobeger cake with lemon curd and chocolate ice cream, as if that wasn't enough they pour this amazing chocolate sauce on it when it arrives that will have you just dying as you wait to dig in.

Overall Compere Lapin is a great addition to the New Orleans food scene, great for groups or date night with your significant other.
Help me polish this:
Brother Rabbit, you embody youth, style, and irresistible flavor!

I recently had the pleasure of meeting up with friends for drinks and an early dinner. As the first one to arrive, I decided to take a seat at the bar and treat myself to the extraordinary house cider, which did not disappoint. I followed it up with the absolutely phenomenal Oban 18, a must-try if you find yourself there.

Our dining experience began with a bang as we indulged in the most incredible house biscuits and butter. I guarantee they will leave you begging for the recipe.

For the main course, we opted for various selections from their First course menu. The daily oysters were excellent, and the Brussels sprouts were delightful. However, the crispy chicken skins fell a little short in terms of flavor, lacking that extra punch.

Next up was the smoked tuna tartare, a dish that did not disappoint. However, take note that the sweet chips could overpower the overall taste. I highly recommend trying the marinated shrimp and jalapeño jus. It's a dish that bursts with fresh and vibrant flavors.

To end our meal on a decadent note, we couldn't resist indulging in the dobeger cake with lemon curd and chocolate ice cream. And as if that wasn't enough, they pour a heavenly chocolate sauce over it when it arrives at your table, leaving you impatiently waiting to dig in.

All in all, Compere Lapin is a fantastic addition to the vibrant New Orleans food scene. Whether you're gathering with a group of friends or planning a romantic date night with your significant other, this is the perfect spot.

input:
Here for convention and Imo's was suggested as "The Best" St. Louis Style pizza by hotel staff. 

I opted for delivery which was good and efficient. The food arrived still hot. I ordered a medium pepperoni and an order of toasted ravioli. 

Now, I knew the cheese on the pizza was provel so it would taste different. I was really not impressed. It may just be a matter of taste preference. It was hard to separate each piece of pizza too.  Like, it wasn't cut all the way through. Not really a fan. So thumbs down on the pizza. 

What bumps the stars up are the T-Ravs!  I was hoping for cheese ravioli but the staple is a meat mixture. Boy...do they do it justice. They were the bomb!  The sauce with it was too watery but still tasty. I would order just the ravioli next time!
Help me polish this:
During my visit to St. Louis for a convention, the hotel staff recommended Imo's as the ultimate St. Louis Style pizza experience. Taking their advice, I decided to have it delivered to my room. I was pleasantly surprised by the quick and efficient delivery, as the food arrived still piping hot.

I ordered a medium-sized pepperoni pizza along with a side of toasted ravioli. Knowing that St. Louis Style pizza features provel cheese, I anticipated a unique taste. However, I must admit that I was not impressed. Perhaps it simply didn't align with my personal preferences. To add to the disappointment, the pizza was unevenly cut, making it challenging to separate the slices. All in all, I wouldn't consider myself a fan of Imo's pizza, so a thumbs down from me in that regard.

Fortunately, the highlight of my order turned out to be the toasted ravioli. Although I was initially hoping for cheese-filled ravioli, the meat mixture provided by Imo's was truly exceptional. It surpassed my expectations and left me thoroughly satisfied. The accompanying sauce, while slightly watery, still managed to be delicious. If I were to reorder, I would opt for just the ravioli alone, as they were the true stars of my meal.

input: Okay, so it's a dance club. It's trendy and offers higher-end cocktails and beers while still offering your run-of-the-mill wells and domestic bottles. If you're on the patio, you can chat...but if you're inside it's (not shockingly) too loud to really talk. If you're in the CWE and you're looking to dance, at least give the Mandarin a shot; it's not going to be for everyone, but it's pretty great if you're in the mood for it.

Okay, so this place is a sleek dance club catering to a fashionable crowd. On the patio, you'll have the opportunity to engage in conversation, but inside the club, the volume is cranked up (not surprisingly) making it difficult to have a meaningful conversation. If you're in the Central West End and seeking a place to dance, the Mandarin is worth a try. input:

smoked hanger steak w/ chimichurri sauce on toastones - tasted much better than it looked - $4 HH price
lobster eggrolls w/ sweet chile lime sauce - $8 - didn't look promising but it was tasty
Hopitoulas - $4.5

Help me polish this:
Another hidden gem on Frenchmen Street, we managed to secure a coveted spot at a tall corner table just in time. As we settled in, the soothing melodies from the piano player filled the air, setting the perfect ambiance.

The bar staff was attentive and efficient, allowing us to order our food and have it promptly delivered to our table. Here's what we enjoyed:

- The pork pot stickers were a delightful surprise, boasting a flavorful filling and priced at a reasonable $4 during happy hour.

- The smoked hanger steak with chimichurri sauce on toastones exceeded our expectations, as its presentation didn't do it justice. At a happy hour price of $4, it was an absolute steal.

- Despite initially appearing unpromising, the lobster eggrolls with sweet chile lime sauce turned out to be quite delectable. Priced at $8, they were well worth the indulgence.

To accompany our meal, we opted for the Hopitoulas and UFO beers, both priced at $4.5 during happy hour. The selection was diverse and appealing, catering to a range of tastes.

It's worth noting that one of the owners/chefs has a Korean background, which explains the inclusion of Asian-inspired dishes on the menu.

If you're looking to make the most of your visit, take advantage of their happy hour specials, available daily from 4-6:30pm. During this time, you can enjoy their tantalizing tapas for just $4, complemented by $5 wines and $3 beers.

Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed our experience and have no doubt that we will be returning to this establishment.

input:
Four of us had dinner at the Sockeye Grill this weekend.  Service was terrible.  Super slow.  Salads were warm and tasteless.  Dressing was watered down. 

Salmon was excellent.  Nachos were okay. Finger steaks were mushy and drab. 

Waitress  knew her beer. The dark lager was excellent.  The lighter beers we had were too warm. 

Looks like this restaurant need some fine tuning.  The atmosphere was like a warehouse, more like being in a barn than a restaurant. 

Tvs everywhere but the news was on. Huh? How depressing is that? 

We won't be back.
Help me polish this:
Four of us had dinner at the Sockeye Grill this weekend, and unfortunately, the overall experience fell quite short. The service was incredibly slow, leaving us waiting for extended periods of time. Moreover, when our salads finally arrived, they were disappointingly warm and lacked any discernible taste. To make matters worse, the dressing seemed watered down and lacked the vibrant flavors we had hoped for.

Fortunately, the salmon dish we ordered was a saving grace. Cooked to perfection, it offered a delightful burst of flavors that helped redeem our dining experience somewhat. Similarly, the nachos were passable but failed to leave a lasting impression. On the other hand, the finger steaks in our party were mushy and lacked the desired texture and taste.

Credit should be given to our waitress, who displayed a commendable knowledge of beers. The dark lager she recommended was excellent, only adding to the disappointment when the lighter beers we tried were served too warm, significantly dulling their flavors.

Unfortunately, the restaurant's ambiance left much to be desired as well. The atmosphere resembled more of a warehouse than a welcoming dining establishment, inadvertently diminishing our enjoyment. Additionally, while the numerous TVs scattered around the venue were noticeable, it was baffling that the news channel was playing, bringing a sense of gloom to the already underwhelming experience.

Considering the overall poor experience we had, we regrettably cannot see ourselves returning to Sockeye Grill in the future. It seems that significant improvements and fine-tuning are necessary for this establishment to provide a satisfying dining experience.

input:
Beer service was lackluster. The first beer I ordered had an off flavor (sour). I ordered a taste of another similar dark beer to see if the problem was endemic but it wasn't. I would have appreciated it more if the bar tender looked into the off flavor when I sent my beer back. This tells me the bar tender doesn't know beer. I assume that particular draft line needs to be cleaned but maybe the problem was with the keg. 

Another thing that killed me was their use of glassware. They serve beers in the classic American "Shaker" pint glass and serve water in the far superior English Nonic Pint glass. I also saw the bar tender pour a white ale with normal ABV in a stemmed tulip glass.

The shaker pint glasses are kept refrigerated and are too cold in my opinion. I would much rather see them kept at room temp and rinsed in cold water (which they do here). 

All in all, the beer knowledge is not up to par for a place that advertises as a burger joint with a large craft beer selection (30 taps).

The beer service at this establishment was disappointing. To begin with, the first beer I ordered had a noticeable off flavor, specifically a sour taste. To confirm if this issue was widespread, I requested a taste of another similar dark beer, which thankfully did not have the same problem. However, I was disappointed by the fact that the bartender did not take any further action to investigate or address the issue when I sent my first beer back. This lack of attention suggests a lack of knowledge and care when it comes to beer.

Additionally, their choice of glassware was another letdown. They served all their beers in the classic American "Shaker" pint glass, which in my opinion, is not the best choice. Conversely, they served water in the far superior English Nonic Pint glass, which further confused me. I even witnessed the bartender pouring a white ale with a normal alcohol by volume content into a stemmed tulip glass, which was completely mismatched.

Furthermore, the use of refrigerated shaker pint glasses was also a disappointment. In my opinion, it would have been better to keep them at room temperature and rinse them in cold water, which they already do here.

Overall, the lack of beer knowledge and attention to detail in a place that boasts about being a burger joint with an extensive craft beer selection of 30 taps is below the standard I expected.

input:
Not mediocre at all IMHO.  Makes me wonder if Daniel O. went to the same place we did.

This is a great neighborhood byob place that provides welcoming service and excellent food at a reasonable price.  We started going here because numerous South Philly friends recommended it.  This is not foo-foo Italian.  This is not pretentious Italian.  This is "let's go back and work our way through the menu" Italian.  We found the specials to be good choices.  My husband's broccoli rabe and sausage was excellent, as was a grilled romaine salad with bleu cheese and pine nuts.  Both were generous enough to share.  Last time, sausage & figs was a hit.  If you are in the mood for a basic plate of macaronis with red gravy, you won't be disappointed either.  We had a great time with the waitress because my BIL brought a bottle of Great Wall wine from China (that was the 2nd bottle we opened) and that started a whole crazy discussion.  She didn't know us from Adam, but we left there feeling like regulars.

It's a very doable destination if you are on your way to a sporting event at the Linc or the Cit, or to the Spectrum or Wachovia Center.  For those who rely on public transportation, you can get off the subway at Broad & Oregon, then walk back a block to Broad & Porter.  Make a reservation, though because it can be a popular place.  You also want to make sure you have time to have a relaxing meal and make your event in time.
Help me polish this:
In my humble opinion, this place is anything but mediocre. It makes me question if Daniel O. had the same experience as us.

This neighborhood BYOB place is truly exceptional, with its warm service and incredible food that comes at a reasonable price. We were initially drawn to this spot based on the rave recommendations of our friends in South Philly, and it definitely lived up to the hype. Unlike other pretentious Italian restaurants, this place offers an authentic and unpretentious dining experience, where you'll want to keep coming back and trying everything on the menu.

We found the specials to be particularly delightful. My husband absolutely loved the broccoli rabe and sausage dish, and the grilled romaine salad with blue cheese and pine nuts was a flavorful treat. Both dishes were generously portioned, perfect for sharing. On our last visit, the sausage and figs combination was a hit. And if you're craving a classic plate of macaroni with red sauce, they won't disappoint you either.

Our waitress added to the fun experience. When my brother-in-law brought a bottle of Great Wall wine from China (it was the second bottle we opened), it sparked a lively and entertaining discussion. Despite not knowing us, the waitress treated us like regulars and left us with a lasting impression.

Conveniently located, this gem is a great stop if you're on your way to a sporting event at the Linc or the Cit, or if you're heading to the Spectrum or Wachovia Center. Even if you rely on public transportation, it's easily accessible by getting off at the Broad & Oregon subway station, and then walking back one block to Broad & Porter. However, be sure to make a reservation, as it tends to get quite popular. Also, give yourself enough time to enjoy a relaxing meal without rushing to your event.

input:
I must say I'm very disappointed, my two stars are for presentation and prompt delivery. I ordered the rainbow roll, white tuna roll, calamari and chicken lettuce wraps. Where do I begin? ok with the bad. 

I strongly feel that when you are delivering food that should be served cold, you don't put it in a bag with hot food because that equals mushy, warm sushi, which is what I got. The rainbow roll, which normally is topped with raw fish was topped with mushy avocado????? which I ended up peeling off to salvage the sushi. The spicy white tuna roll was very good.

The calamari looked like chicken fingers all the breading was falling off and it was under cooked, I took one bite and tossed it. Now I've had lettuce wraps before but mines came with an actual head of lettuce in a bag and chicken filling in a plate. It was not described this way in the menu at all. All in all I don't think I'll be ordering from here again. I'll stick to Niji's on 5th.
Help me polish this:
I must express my deep disappointment with my recent order. I can only give credit for the presentation and prompt delivery, earning this establishment two stars. I had ordered the rainbow roll, white tuna roll, calamari, and chicken lettuce wraps, but the overall experience was far from satisfactory.

Firstly, I was dismayed that the food items which should have been served cold arrived in the same bag as the hot dishes. This resulted in my sushi becoming mushy and lukewarm, greatly diminishing its quality. The rainbow roll, which typically features raw fish as a topping, was instead topped with mushy avocado. I had to painstakingly remove it in order to salvage the sushi. On a positive note, the spicy white tuna roll was enjoyable.

Additionally, the calamari resembled chicken fingers with its breading falling off, and it was clearly undercooked. After just one bite, I had no choice but to discard it. Furthermore, the presentation of the chicken lettuce wraps was completely different from what was described on the menu. Instead of receiving a plate with chicken filling and a separate bag containing a head of lettuce, everything was combined in a rather confusing manner.

Considering these disappointing aspects, I am afraid I cannot foresee myself ordering from this establishment again. In comparison, I will be sticking to Niji's on 5th where I have had consistently satisfactory experiences.

input:
I came in here the other night for a  post-show snack after seeing a ESO performance at the Winspear. The main reason we chose this location was because it was close to the Winspear, and open late (until 11:30pm on Friday and Saturday). I don't have any strong criticisms of the restaurant. I suppose, if anything, the menu may have seemed a little bit over-priced - at least for what I ordered. I had a Caesar salad with three 'jumbo' shrimp on it, which cost $15. The portion size did not seem to justify the cost and the jumbo shrimp were fairly average in their size, but the flavours were good and the ingredients were fresh. My friend had a soup, which looked and smelled absolutely amazing, and at $6 it didn't seem too unreasonable. She also had the smoked salmon Carpaccio, which looked very appetizing with its thick slices of dark rye bread and generous slices of smoked salmon and capers. The also had a couple of interesting beers on their menu that we were keen to try.

I think if you're going to a show in the area and looking for a spot to get a drink or a snack afterward, this is not a bad option. Their menu at that time of night had an interesting mix of appetizers and desserts that seemed to provide something to suit most tastes.

I'm assuming Normand's Bistro must be connected to the Normand's restaurant which is on Jasper Avenue. Of interest, I have heard that Normand's took over the brunch menu that had formerly been offered at the Glenora Bistro.

I assume that Normand's Bistro is affiliated with the Normand's restaurant located on Jasper Avenue. It's worth noting that I've heard they took over the brunch menu that was previously offered at the Glenora Bistro.

input:
The Sunrise Family Restaurant is an old style diner that has a very small-town, homey feel.   Service is prompt and super friendly.

I had a Monte Cristo sandwich per the waitresses recommendation and I won't lie, it was pretty disappointing.  Take a stack of turkey and a couple thick slices of ham out of their respective industrial packs, microwave them with some swiss cheese on top and serve on limp french toast.  Somebody out there might like it.  I didn't. 

It came with a salad and fries, both of which were good.  The fries were thick steak fries cooked to a perfect golden brown.   

I have a feeling there are some good items on the menu.  I would especially be interested in trying breakfast.  I'll be back.
Help me polish this:
The Sunrise Family Restaurant is a charming, nostalgic diner that can transport you back to a small-town atmosphere. The warm, friendly service is exceptionally quick and attentive.

Based on the waitress's recommendation, I decided to try the Monte Cristo sandwich. Unfortunately, I must admit that it didn't fulfill my expectations. The sandwich consisted of turkey and thick slices of ham, pulled from generic packaging, microwaved with a layer of swiss cheese, and served on slightly stale french toast. While some individuals might enjoy this combination, it didn't satisfy my taste preferences.

To my delight, the meal did come with a side salad and fries, both of which were delightful. The fries were thick steak fries, perfectly cooked to a golden brown, and proved to be a highlight of the meal.

Despite my disappointment with the sandwich, I have faith that the Sunrise Family Restaurant offers other enticing options on their menu. Moreover, I am particularly intrigued by their breakfast selection, and I look forward to returning and exploring more of their offerings.

input:
This is a really fun event for those who enjoy beer in all its forms. The drinks themselves were relatively cheap ($2-4 for a 4 oz. sample. Most were $2, some were $3, and very few were in the $4 range), however the food was really over priced ($6 for a small cup of fancy macaroni and cheese? really?). For the beer lover, however, there is a wide variety of tried and true along with the new kids on the block from local, national and international lines. Also, if you like what you tasted, you can buy it on site, with a Sobeys/Safeway liquor store right on site doing specials on the sampled brews. 

We went VIP for this event, however I don't think it's worth it. What you get: a glass mug instead of a plastic one, a beer and food class ($2 value) and a beer seminar ($2 value). If you do it all, or really value the glass mug, go for it! But for me, who just did the beer and food class, it wasn't worth it. 

My only complaint is for the venue, but for an event that size, you need the space. $16 for parking on top of your entry fee (though I guess most people would cab or Uber it there so you don't have to have a designated driver), and then you have to buy sample tickets on site. It gets quite expensive.

This event is a highly enjoyable experience for beer enthusiasts of all kinds. The drinks themselves are reasonably priced, with 4 oz. samples ranging from $2 to $4. Most samples were $2, a few were $3, and only a handful were on the higher end at $4. On the downside, the food offered at the event is quite overpriced. For instance, a small cup of fancy macaroni and cheese cost a staggering $6. 

For beer lovers, however, this event offers a fantastic selection of tried and true brews, as well as new and upcoming ones from local, national, and international breweries. Moreover, if you find a beer you particularly enjoy, you have the convenience of purchasing it on site, with a Sobeys/Safeway liquor store right there, which often provides specials on the sampled brews. 

Although we opted for the VIP experience, I personally do not believe it was worth the additional cost. The VIP package includes a glass mug instead of a plastic one, a beer and food class (valued at $2), and a beer seminar (also valued at $2). If you highly value the glass mug or plan to participate in all the VIP offerings, it may be worth it for you. However, for someone like me who only attended the beer and food class, it did not justify the additional expense. 

My only complaint lies with the venue, although I understand the need for ample space for an event of this magnitude. Adding insult to injury, parking fees were exorbitant at $16 on top of the entry fee. Nevertheless, I suppose most attendees would opt for a taxi or ride-sharing service like Uber to avoid the need for a designated driver. Additionally, you are required to purchase sample tickets on site, and these can quickly add up, making the overall cost quite steep.

Moreover, what sets Dan apart is his remarkable memory—despite the constant influx of customers, he always remembers my name, making me feel valued and appreciated.

In fact, I am so enamored with Dan's exceptional skills that I exclusively visit Square 1682 on Mondays, ensuring I don't miss the opportunity to be tended to by this master mixologist. On the rare occasion that Dan is not working, I continue on my way, as no one can quite match the level of service and expertise he provides. He truly is one-of-a-kind and has become an integral part of my memorable experiences at this esteemed establishment.

Square 1682 has consistently exceeded my expectations, offering an unparalleled dining experience. From the delicious food and impeccable service to the sophisticated ambiance and Dan's unmatched bartending skills, this establishment holds a special place in my heart, and I have created cherished memories within its exquisite walls.

input: This is a must try, we come here frequent and we are never disappointed. Get there early so you get right in and don't have to wait. Decent selection of coffees, they have french press as well. Menu isn't huge which is nice so you can figure out what you want quickly. Food comes how in a decent time. I seem to always get the same thing (wilburt skillet) everytime I go cause it is amazing. Food just seems so fresh as well, friendly staff. You will leave full and a smile on your face.
Help me polish this: This place is an absolute must-try! We visit frequently and are consistently blown away. Arriving early is key to avoid any waiting time - trust us, it's worth it. They have a decent selection of coffees including the fantastic french press. What we love about their menu is its simplicity, making it easy to decide on what to order. The food always arrives in a timely manner, and we can't resist ordering our favorite, the incredible Wilburt Skillet, every single time. Everything tastes incredibly fresh, and the staff is friendly and attentive. By the end of your visit, you'll leave feeling satisfied and with a huge smile on your face.

input:
I tried to like this place... I really did. So much so that I went back to try it after a less that satisfactory first wax.

Wax 1- I had Despina, I think her name was. I waited a good 15 minutes after my appointment time for her to come and get me from the front. Ironic they have a 9 minute policy that if you don't show they'll cancel/charge you or whatever. Anyway, as for the experience with Despina, she did not speak to me. Like at all. Made me feel super awkward the whole time, and missed a fair few chunks of hair. She didn't ask me anything about myself, didn't tell me where to sit or how she wanted me positioned etc. Luckily I got this one half price as it was my first time at EWC.

Wax 2- I booked 3-4 weeks later with Amy Jo (based on previous Yelp reviews). She was a lot friendlier (literally the only reason why I'm giving this 1 star) BUT way too sloppy. I think it's safe to say this is the worst wax I've ever had. She left half of my hair on right before Valentine's Day! I understand they can't get all the hairs all the time but a lottttt of hair right on top was left clearly visible to my waxer. My apt was at 3.45, I walked out of the building at 3.53. Really. This includes the time spent undressing, redressing, and paying. 8 minutes is not long enough for all of this. It went so quick that when she said she was done I was actually shocked.  
I'm about to go to CVS and get some at home wax strips to finish the job... For $47+ I expect way way more. 

The staff- Another reason why I won't be returning. The ladies at the front desk are generally rude and disinterested in showing any glimpse of good customer service. ALSO, I don't like being asked if I'm going to tip - can't you give me the card machine so I can do it myself rather than make me announce if I would like to tip and how much? 

The hunt for a decent Brazilian wax in Philly continues- someone help me PLEASE!
Help me polish this:
I tried to like this place, truly I did. I even gave it a second chance after a disappointing first wax appointment.

My first experience, I had Despina, or at least I think that was her name. I waited a solid 15 minutes past my appointment time before she finally showed up to get me from the front. It's ironic that they have a policy of canceling or charging you if you're more than 9 minutes late, yet they don't seem to value their clients' time. Beyond the tardiness, Despina didn't speak to me at all, which made the whole experience incredibly awkward. She also missed quite a few patches of hair and provided no guidance on where to sit or how to position myself. Fortunately, since it was my first visit, I received a discounted rate.

I scheduled my next appointment 3-4 weeks later with Amy Jo, based on positive Yelp reviews. She was definitely friendlier than Despina (which is the only reason for the one-star rating), but her technique was far from satisfactory. In fact, I'd say this was the worst wax I've ever had. She left a significant amount of hair untouched, right before Valentine's Day no less! I understand that not all hairs can be removed every time, but she missed so many that were clearly visible to her. To add to the disappointment, my appointment was scheduled for 3:45 pm, but I left the building at 3:53 pm. This includes the time spent undressing, redressing, and paying. Eight minutes simply wasn't enough for everything. The process went so quickly that I was genuinely shocked when she said she was finished. I'm now forced to take matters into my own hands and purchase at-home wax strips from CVS to complete the job. Considering I paid $47 or more for this service, I expect far better results.

Furthermore, the staff at the front desk was another letdown. They generally come across as rude and disinterested in providing decent customer service. Additionally, I find it off-putting to be asked if I'm going to tip. It would be much more preferable if they handed me the card machine so that I can handle it myself, sparing me the obligation to declare whether or not I plan to tip and how much.

With all these negative experiences, my search for a competent Brazilian wax in Philly continues. Please, someone, help me find a better option.

input: Amazing and comfortable atmosphere with extremely unique flavor combinations in the dishes. The Cuban Lamb Frita is a must (add the egg! It's worth it). All of the side items are delicious, you literally can't go wrong. The staff is friendly and they are extremely efficient with the coffee refills. This has quickly become my new regular brunch spot!
Help me polish this: Experience an extraordinary and inviting ambiance complemented by an exceptional fusion of flavors in every dish. The Cuban Lamb Frita, a definite must-try, becomes even more satisfying with the addition of a perfectly cooked egg. Delight in the delectable assortment of side items, as each one is guaranteed to tantalize your taste buds. The staff, known for their friendly demeanor, flawlessly blend their warmth with efficiency when it comes to refilling your coffee, ensuring a seamless dining experience. Undoubtedly, this establishment has swiftly transformed into my go-to brunch destination!

input:
This place is good. For the lofty prices the proportions were very small. However the drinks were cheap and the service was very good. The piano is a nice touch as well. 

The cheesecake is incredible, just get it and don't look back.
Help me polish this:
This place is worth a visit. Although the prices are a bit on the higher side, the portions are quite small. However, the drinks are reasonably priced and the service is excellent. Additionally, the piano adds a nice touch to the ambiance.

The highlight of the menu is undoubtedly the cheesecake. It is absolutely incredible! Don't hesitate to order it and you won't regret it.

input: If you beat the crowd you're in. Small but that's the only negative. Everything I've tried on the menu is AMAZING! They even have vegetarian/vegan items. I always get whatever french toast special they have. I always take people who stay with me for Mardi Gras here for breakfast before we hit the parades.
Help me polish this: If you manage to beat the crowd, you'll be in for a great experience. The only downside is that the place tends to get small and crowded. In fact, whenever friends or guests stay with me during Mardi Gras, I always make it a point to bring them here for breakfast before we head out to enjoy the parades.

input: Butch did a great job. The tour was relaxing, informative but 2 good stops to eat and see the cemetery. I recommend going on this trip the beginning of your stay so you know where to go during your trip. He'a also pretty fun.
Help me polish this: Butch did an outstanding job! The tour was both relaxing and informative, with two fantastic stops to enjoy a meal and visit the cemetery. I highly recommend taking this trip at the beginning of your stay as it provides great insight on the must-visit places. Moreover, Butch's fun nature adds to the overall enjoyable experience.

input: I love this food truck. They have the tastiest street foods like their captain crunch tilapia burrito. Who would've thought of that? The fried fish is so flakey and delicious, paired with fresh cabbage, tomatoes, avocado and Sriracha mayo. I have also tried their katsu and curry chicken which are so rich in flavor. Their Thai tea is also on point! So much to offer from a small food truck. I live in Jersey and I have driven here many times just to get food. They are so friendly and provide great food at a great price.
Help me polish this: I absolutely adore this food truck! Their selection of street foods is simply unmatched. One dish that has particularly captured my taste buds is their captain crunch tilapia burrito - an unexpectedly delicious combination. The fried fish boasts a delicate flakiness that perfectly complements the fresh cabbage, tomatoes, avocado, and Sriracha mayo. Additionally, I've had the pleasure of indulging in their mouthwatering katsu and curry chicken, both bursting with rich flavors. And let's not forget about their Thai tea, which is impeccably brewed. This small food truck has truly surpassed all expectations. Despite living in Jersey, I've made the drive here numerous times solely for their culinary creations. The friendly atmosphere and incredible value for money make this food truck an absolute gem.

input: I was having an bad migraine and felt terrible. When woke up I had a sinus infection and my day was just going awful. I called a few places to try to get a massage in today because I knew indeed it badly. No one had any availability and I stumbled across massage envy on Google and thought to give them a try. Not only were they able to fit me in with the exact specific type I needed, but they also were able to fit my father in at the exact same time. Jen was understanding and nice, she asked me questions and checked up on me constantly. She even showed me some at home techniques I could use. She took her time, obviously did not rush. Carrie, I believe, was the name of the woman who did a foot massage on my father. He was very pleased and recommended I try it sometime. They also informed me about the membership program which not only is very cost-efficient, but also adheres to my busy schedule. I signed up on the spot with no hesitation. Friendly staff, great atmosphere, comfortable building and very calming environment! Would recommended! I feel so much better already and am going back in a month to get a 90 minute massage.
Help me polish this:
I had a terrible migraine and felt absolutely terrible. When I woke up, I discovered I had a sinus infection, making my day even worse. Desperate for relief, I called several places in an attempt to get a massage appointment today. Unfortunately, everyone was fully booked. That's when I came across Massage Envy on Google and decided to give them a shot. To my surprise, not only were they able to accommodate me with the exact type of massage I needed, but they also had availability for my father at the same time.

Jen, the masseuse attending to me, was incredibly understanding and kind. She asked me questions about my condition and continuously checked up on me. She even taught me some at-home techniques that could help alleviate my pain. Unlike many rushed experiences I've had before, Jen clearly took her time and showed a genuine concern for my well-being. On the other hand, Carrie, the masseuse working on my father's foot massage, left him thoroughly pleased and even recommended I try it sometime.

During our visit, the staff enlightened us about their membership program, which not only offers cost-efficient options but also works well with my busy schedule. Impressed with the overall experience, I wasted no time in signing up without any hesitation. The staff members were friendly, and the atmosphere exuded a sense of peace and tranquility. The facility itself was comfortable and the overall environment extremely calming.

I already feel much better, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit in a month for a 90-minute massage. I highly recommend Massage Envy for anyone in need of a rejuvenating experience.

input: This place is good~  The chicken is moist, the skin is crispy, the flavor is nice and smokey, this is the best kind of roast chicken I have tried. The smells (smokey, bbq) is so good and hypnotizing, just make my mouth water.  I got the double chicken family which is 2 whole chickens, literally a bed of fries underneath them, and cole slaw.  It was more than enough to feed a family of four.  The dipping sauces that come with it are also real good, i really like the mustard base one, its kinda mustardy with a chipotle flair, and there is also a green sauce that is like a salsa.  The fries are wedge fries and they make you real full because there are plenty to go around. We had leftovers because the meal was that big.  I would rather eat here than popeyes or kfc, because you get more, its healthier, and you get better service. The owners are real nice and friendly. I will be back because I know I will be craving this chicken.
Help me polish this:
This place is amazing! The chicken is incredibly moist, with a crispy skin that adds the perfect touch. The flavor is absolutely fantastic, with a nice, smoky taste that I can't get enough of. The aroma of the chicken, with its smoky and BBQ notes, is so delicious that it's almost hypnotizing - it makes my mouth water just thinking about it.

I ordered the double chicken family meal, which included two whole chickens, served on a bed of fries, along with a generous portion of coleslaw. It was more than enough to satisfy a family of four. The dipping sauces that accompanied the meal were also a hit - I especially loved the mustard-based one, which had a hint of chipotle and added an extra zing, and there was also a green sauce that resembled a salsa.

The wedge fries were divine and left me feeling happily full. There were plenty of them to go around, so no one went hungry. In fact, we had leftovers because the portion sizes were so generous.

Compared to other fast-food chicken options like Popeyes or KFC, this place is a cut above. Not only do you get more food here, but it's also healthier, and the service is top-notch. The owners are incredibly friendly and welcoming, which adds to the overall experience.

I am already looking forward to my next visit because I know I will be craving their mouthwatering chicken.

input:

Help me polish this:
This is the closest I get to experiencing Japanese cuisine! While I'm not a huge fan of sushi, sashimi or maki, I thoroughly enjoy their rice bowls and tempura. Moreover, the restaurant's popularity is moderate, so you won't have to wait in line for an extensive period.
