The service has always been good, particularly for fast food, and I appreciate being able to stick somewhat to my dietary plan when I dine here. Whether you're in need of a quick lunch or dinner, this place is perfect for those who are pressed for time.

input: I was new to the Westchase area and I was in need of a new dentist.  After reading reviews and the location being on .5 miles from my place I made an appointment.  The entire staff is great.  I've visited with Dr. Creech-Gionis  and Dr. Stern, they both are outstanding.  They make going to the  dentist less painful.  I can honestly say I'm 100% satisfied.
Help me polish this: I was a newcomer to the Westchase area and found myself in need of a new dentist. After thoroughly researching and considering nearby options, I decided to make an appointment at this dental clinic due to its excellent reviews and convenient location just 0.5 miles away from my place. I can confidently state that my experience with this dental clinic has left me completely satisfied.

input:
Went to Amigos on our 40th anniversary citing the great reviews. Near to no atmosphere. Food was bleeeeah and the price was kinda high for what you get. Can't figure why people like their salsa so much as I think the stuff from "NEW YORK CITY!!" is as good and the chips are just the giant bag variety.

Gawd... all I want is some decent Mexican fare here in Boise!! Used to love Gloria's though not nearly as clean as one would like.  $47.00 with drinks and tip though I think one would do much better at one of the taco trucks as far as flavor goes.
Help me polish this:
We decided to celebrate our 40th anniversary at Amigos based on its positive reviews, but unfortunately, the experience fell short. The restaurant lacked any sort of ambiance, and the food was incredibly underwhelming. Additionally, considering the quality of the dishes, the prices seemed quite high. I couldn't understand why people raved about their salsa, as I believe the salsa you can get from any grocery store in "NEW YORK CITY!!" is just as good. Even the chips were nothing special and seemed like the generic bagged variety.

Honestly, all I wanted was some decent Mexican cuisine here in Boise. I used to enjoy Gloria's, although the cleanliness left much to be desired. Our bill came out to $47.00, including drinks and tip, but I truly believe we could have gotten much better flavor at one of the local taco trucks.

input:
Heather was my waitress and a bartender.
Everything I tried was fabulous.
I had tenderloin sliders with the french fries oh my.
God I will be going back here as often as I possibly can

You will not regret trying this place
Help me polish this: Heather served as both my waitress and bartender, and I must say, everything I tried was absolutely fabulous. The tenderloin sliders paired with the perfectly crisp french fries were simply irresistible. I am definitely planning to return here as frequently as possible. Trust me, you won't regret giving this place a try.

input:
The bouncers are awful, but I would be too if I were 4-feet tall and had an infinite amount of pent-up aggression and shielded childhood memories. 

This place stands for everything Reno shouldn't be. Choose LEX only if the sole alternative is being waterboarded during thanksgiving dinner.
Help me polish this:
The bouncers leave much to be desired, but I can understand why. Imagine being only 4 feet tall, harboring an endless reserve of pent-up aggression and safeguarding shielded childhood memories.

This establishment embodies everything that Reno should steer clear of. Opt for LEX solely as a last resort, perhaps on par with enduring a waterboarding session during Thanksgiving dinner.

input:
5 STAR FOOD! 
For sure one of if not the best place to get a sandwich on the beach anywhere between St Pete Beach & Clearwater Beach. All orders cooked to order. Super Size, gourmet servings and great very friendly service from the owner. Artison sandwiches for the price of Subway. Great cook with well seasoned sauces and dips usually. I always go for the daily special. Today was 3 Shrimp taco's for $6.00 The shrimp were cooked perfectly and served on fresh corn tortillas with a Kiwi sauce with some fresh peppers. Just enough spice and fruit with the shrimp. DELICIOUS. I could have had 6 they were so good. Only drawback is this place is walk up with only bench seating outside. Not a problem given the food quality for me personally but some may p[refer to sit at a table. It's on the bench or to go. A great place if you are staying at one of the local hotel to walk to. I hear they will start delivering soon. This is a local favorite for me.
The only reason I did not give 5 stars overall as the seating may be an issue for some.
Help me polish this: 5 STAR FOOD! Without a doubt, this establishment stands out as one of, if not the best, sandwich spot along the stretch between St. Pete Beach and Clearwater Beach. Every order is prepared with precision and care, ensuring a delectable dining experience. The portions are generous, akin to those found in gourmet restaurants, all at an affordable price, reminiscent of Subway. The chef's culinary expertise shines through in their well-seasoned sauces and dips, elevating each bite to new heights. Personally, I always opt for the daily special, and today's offering of 3 Shrimp tacos for a mere $6.00 left me in awe. Cooked to perfection, these tacos were served on fresh corn tortillas, complemented by a zesty Kiwi sauce and a hint of fresh peppers - a harmonious balance of spice and fruitiness that left me craving more. In fact, they were so delicious that I could have easily devoured six. The only minor drawback of this place is its limited seating, consisting solely of bench seating outside. Nevertheless, for me, the exceptional food quality outweighs any seating concerns. Additionally, if you are staying at one of the local hotels, this spot is conveniently within walking distance. Rumor has it that they will soon commence deliveries as well. As a local, this hidden gem has quickly become a personal favorite of mine. Although I cannot award a perfect 5-star rating due to the seating limitations, I wholeheartedly recommend this establishment to any food enthusiast seeking a memorable dining experience.

input: Beautiful modern place, they have a nice view, the only thing is that is close to the train and you may hear it if you are on that side of the building, other than that it's great and has a yolk on the corner!
Help me polish this: Welcome to this beautiful modern place with a delightful view! Be aware, however, that its proximity to the train may result in occasional sounds, which can seemingly be heard if you are positioned on that particular side of the building. Apart from this minor aspect, the place is absolutely fantastic, and it even boasts a charming yolk on the corner!

input: Went in for full set, request long showed picture. Nails were cut short no big deal, the issue came when I pointed out a crooked nail and was told it hadn't been filed, acrylic was put on nail still crooked. It was filed and getting shorter and shorter. This wasn't my first visit however it will be my last.
Help me polish this: I visited the nail salon for a full set, specifically requesting long nails as shown in a picture. Initially, I was not bothered by the fact that my nails were cut shorter than I wanted. However, things took a turn when I noticed that one of my nails was crooked. I pointed it out to the nail technician, who acknowledged that it hadn't been filed properly but proceeded to apply acrylic on the crooked nail anyway. As she began filing the nail to fix the crookedness, it kept getting shorter and shorter. Although I have been to this salon before, this unfortunate experience has convinced me that it will be my last visit.

input:

We loved the Fried Manchego, Hot Cauiliflower, and Camarones! 
This was over the top unique and tasty!!
Help me polish this: Absolutely amazing! Tuesday nights are an absolute must! They have an incredible selection of half-priced tapas, and their Sangria and margaritas are only $5.00. Our personal favorites were the Fried Manchego, Hot Cauliflower, and Camarones. The flavors were out of this world and truly one-of-a-kind.

input: Amazing live Jazz music. No alcohol. No food. Just JAZZ. This place really shows NOLA city culture off. Tickets are $15.
Help me polish this: Experience the pinnacle of live Jazz music in a truly authentic setting. Embrace the soulful melodies and vibrant rhythms without any distractions or frills. Our venue is dedicated solely to the art of Jazz, ensuring an unparalleled musical immersion. Immerse yourself in the unique culture of New Orleans as we showcase the city's rich musical heritage. Join us for an unforgettable evening where Jazz takes center stage. Secure your tickets now for just $15.

input: If you like a quiet  shopping experience without the crowds, this mall is the place for you.
Help me polish this: If you prefer a serene and peaceful shopping environment, devoid of bustling crowds, then this mall is the perfect destination for you.

input:
We had dinner here after a long day at the convention center.  We asked to sit in a quieter area, and they found us a nice table in a side room.  Service was attentive and professional.  Our waiter recommended the aged ribeye steak--"best steak ever."  I didn't think I wanted an entire 18-ounce boneless, so he suggested we split it.  We did--certainly one of the "best steaks ever"--cooked perfectly medium rare and it was plenty for both of us.  Of course, we also had the signature shrimp cocktail (horseradish) and the iceberg lettuce wedge with crumbled bacon (very pancetta-like).   OK, iceberg wedge isn't the most exciting salad, but it's great when done well, which this was.  
   My only disappointment was a wine list that had a very limited choice of medium-priced wines by the bottle, so wine selection took a while.  A small complaint, so I would rate H & I  4.5 stars if possible.
Help me polish this:
We had a delightful dinner here after a long day at the convention center. We kindly requested a quieter area, and they promptly accommodated us by seating us in a lovely table in a side room. The service we received was exceptional - attentive and professional. Our waiter confidently recommended the aged ribeye steak, even going as far as calling it the "best steak ever." Initially hesitant about the 18-ounce boneless portion, he suggested we split it, and we were not disappointed. The steak was cooked to a perfect medium rare, undoubtedly one of the best we've ever had, and it proved to be more than enough for the both of us. To complement our meal, we also indulged in their signature shrimp cocktail with a hint of horseradish and an iceberg lettuce wedge topped with crumbled bacon reminiscent of pancetta. While the iceberg wedge salad may not be the most adventurous option, their execution of it was exceptional.

The only aspect that left me slightly dissatisfied was the limited selection of medium-priced wines available on their wine list, which led to a bit of a delay in choosing our wine. However, this minor setback does not overshadow the outstanding experience we had. If it were possible, I would rate H & I a solid 4.5 stars.

input: The worst Italian food I have ever tasted!!! I'm far from Italian, but I can make a MEAN lasagna & spaghetti myself compared to this place. 1st of all, we waited 45mins patiently w/ a hungry Hubby, 2yr old, 7yr old, & myself. When we finally got seated, the waitress was very polite, but forgetful at times. Didnt drink any alcohol or sodas but the lemonade was very tart & the garlic bread was not-so-fresh...had to request for some fresh bread after my family devoured the 1st basket from starving & waiting for so long. I ordered the stuffed shells & chicken parmagiana. The salad was very tasty; however, they only have Italian dressing...no ranch or anything else. I am not a picky eater & rarely complain, but the stuffed shells & parmagiana chicken tasted HORRIBLE!! The chicken was very bland & the stuffed shells were hard & overbaked. The meranera sauce tasted like it was old or aged too long (if there's ever such a thing, lol). I could not bring myself to eat my entree. I had to send it back. I heard the lady at the table next to ours say the salmon was good, so I figured the salmon might be safe. It was actually very good! I was still very disappointed after this restaurant was referred to me by many. I felt like they got an easy $50 bucks out of me. I would have rathered gone to the olive garden or macaroni grill. If u r looking for an awesome authentic Italian cusine restaurant in Tucson, I highly recommend Contessa off of Ina Rd. The only reason we didn't go there is b/c it was out of the way from where we were going.  It's pretty far from where we live but always worth the drive. Everything is freshly made & u can definite tell the difference! I'm sorry Caruso, but I don't think my family will be coming here ever again!
Help me polish this:
"The worst Italian food I have ever tasted! I may not be Italian myself, but compared to this place, even my homemade lasagna and spaghetti are exceptional. Firstly, we patiently waited for 45 minutes with my hungry husband, 2-year-old, 7-year-old, and myself. Finally, when we were seated, the waitress was polite but forgetful at times. We didn't order any alcohol or sodas, but the lemonade was overly tart and the garlic bread was not fresh. We had to request a fresh basket after my family devoured the first one due to starvation and the long wait. 

I decided to order the stuffed shells and chicken parmigiana. The salad was surprisingly tasty; however, they only had Italian dressing to offer, without any ranch or alternative options. While I am not a picky eater and rarely complain, the stuffed shells and parmigiana chicken were absolutely dreadful! The chicken lacked flavor and the stuffed shells were hard and overbaked. The marinara sauce tasted old or over-aged, if such a thing exists (lol). I couldn't bring myself to eat my entree and had to send it back. 

I overheard a lady at the neighboring table praising the salmon, so I thought it might be a safe option. Thankfully, it turned out to be good! However, this reprieve couldn't salvage my disappointment after this restaurant was recommended to me by many. It felt like they easily pocketed $50 from me. I would have preferred going to Olive Garden or Macaroni Grill instead. If you are seeking an authentic and exceptional Italian cuisine experience in Tucson, I highly recommend Contessa off of Ina Rd. It may be quite a distance from us, but it's always worth the drive. Their food is freshly made, and the difference is noticeable!"

I apologize, Caruso, but I don't believe my family will ever return to your restaurant.

input: I tend to stay away from strip mall bars, that being said my buddy John is a bar back here and raved about it so we decided to give it a try. The food is very good, I will try their pizza next time, they also have a killer craft bar they just added, prices are very reasonable too
Help me polish this: I usually tend to avoid strip mall bars, but my buddy John works as a bar back at this place and he couldn't stop raving about it. input: I had take out from here tonight so this review is solely the food. My first time here even though I live around the corner. Help me polish this: I ordered takeout from this place tonight and wanted to focus solely on reviewing the food. Despite living just around the corner, it was my first time trying this establishment. The greens were delightfully fresh and crispy, the blue cheese dressing was smooth without an overwhelming amount of chunks, and the chicken itself was absolutely delicious. input:
If you are looking to be impressed by French-German dishes in New Orleans, please go to Luke Restaurant, I know I was. 

The restaurant is located in the Central Business District, next to the Hilton and in the former Masonic Temple Building, so there is that historic vibe to the restaurant. The front room is a lot more grand than the back room (where we were seated), but that is offset by views of the open kitchen. 

Apparently they only want to seat people with reservations, so since we did not have one, we were refused seating until 9:15pm (it was 6:45pm) but with a little back and forth, we ended up waiting only 15 minutes before we were seated. However, as we walked through the restaurant to the back room, way too many tables were empty that it made no sense that they acted that way. A lot of tables still remained empty throughout the meal.

I decided to start out my meal with a cocktail. I originally wanted the Mint Julep but they were out so I had the Riverbend (vodka, lemon juice, basil syrup, blueberries & ginger ale) at the recommendation of the server. It was a relatively sweet cocktail, with the ginger ale being the most powering flavor, but you could still taste the alcohol.

My friend choose a regular starter and ordered a cup of the Crawfish Bisque. She ate all of it so I am assuming she liked it, but she did complain of a sour aftertaste.

My boyfriend skipped the appetizers and went straight for the entree. He always seems to find the most basic item on the menu and order it. He had the Luke Burger (bacon, caramelized onions, tomatoes, Swiss cheese) and was raving about it. One thing I can tell you, it was a very good size. 

My friend had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" with lump crab meat, roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausages. She loved it.

I have an obsession with mussels so I had the classic Moules et Frites. Although only having two simply ingredients (garlic & thyme) in the broth, the flavors stood out and the taste was a lot bolder than others I have had with a lot more ingredients. The house-made fries were scrumptious. These are the best kind.

Even with all that food, we still made room for dessert. We first had the Bread Pudding which was delicious but quite sweet. I am also not a fan of over sauced foods.

One wasn't enough so we also ordered the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Creme Brulee. It was superb and not too sweet which is a plus for me. The little cookies on top added nothing to the dessert and if anything could have been left off.

All that good food, I still have to give props to our server. He was amazing and engaging. The front desk soured the mood a little bit a first but he more than made up for it. I couldn't have asked for anyone better.
Help me polish this:
If you are in search of an impressive French-German dining experience in New Orleans, look no further than Luke Restaurant. I was thoroughly impressed myself.

Situated in the Central Business District, right next to the Hilton hotel and housed in the former Masonic Temple Building, Luke Restaurant exudes a historic charm. While the front room carries a grand ambiance, we were seated in the back room, which offers a view of the open kitchen. Despite its less grand setting, the view compensated for it.

It's worth noting that the restaurant prioritizes reservations, and since we didn't have one, we initially faced some resistance in securing a table. However, after a little negotiation, we were accommodated within a mere 15 minutes. Interestingly though, as we passed through the restaurant, I couldn't help but notice several empty tables, casting doubt on their strict reservation policy. In fact, many tables remained vacant throughout our entire meal.

To kickstart our evening, I opted for a cocktail. My initial choice, the Mint Julep, unfortunately, was unavailable, so I decided to try the server's recommendation, the Riverbend, a delightful blend of vodka, lemon juice, basil syrup, blueberries, and ginger ale. It leaned towards the sweeter side, with the ginger ale dominating the flavors, while alcohol undertones still remained discernible.

Meanwhile, my friend chose the Crawfish Bisque as her starter, which she thoroughly enjoyed, finishing her entire serving. However, she did mention detecting a slight sour aftertaste.

Skipping the appetizers altogether, my boyfriend dove straight into his entree, opting for the Luke Burger comprising bacon, caramelized onions, tomatoes, and Swiss cheese. He couldn't stop raving about it, and I must say, it was generously portioned.

For her main course, my friend ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" accompanied by lump crab meat, roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille, and green onion sausages. She couldn't have been happier with her selection.

Being an ardent fan of mussels, I couldn't resist ordering the classic Moules et Frites. Despite the broth consisting of only garlic and thyme, the flavors were pronounced, standing out compared to versions with more complex ingredient combinations. The house-made fries were simply irresistible - the epitome of perfection.

Even after indulging in such a feast, we managed to save some room for dessert. We first savored the Bread Pudding, which proved to be delicious albeit a touch too sweet for my taste. I also prefer less sauced dishes, so this slightly overwhelmed me.

With one dessert not sufficing, we also indulged in the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Creme Brulee, which was exquisitely balanced in sweetness - a definite plus for me. The small cookies on top didn't contribute much and could have been omitted.

Above all, I must commend our server for delivering an exceptional dining experience. He was attentive and engaging, truly enhancing our evening. While our initial encounter with the front desk left a sour note, our server more than made up for it. I couldn't have asked for a better dining companion.

input:

I originally went to get a cleaning/exam but was told I needed several inlays which, of course, weren't covered by insurance and were very expensive. The dental work was done well(no complaints there) but it's very expensive and was possibly unnecessary.
Help me polish this:

However, upon reflection, I realized two things - firstly, watching TV isn't really feasible during dental procedures, and secondly, it's possible that these amenities are offered as a "perk" to offset the high prices charged.

Initially, I had gone in for a routine cleaning and exam, but to my surprise, I was informed that I required several inlays. Unfortunately, these were not covered by insurance, resulting in a hefty expense. While I can't fault the quality of the dental work itself, the cost was exorbitant and there is a lingering concern that these procedures may not have been entirely necessary.

Help me polish this:

input:
I love it!  The reviews were great and I was desperate for good carry out, so we decided to try Pizzaville (is anyone else picturing JT singing - Bring it on down to Pizzaville?).  The prices are a bit high, but the quality of the food is great!  The pizza crust is between a hand tossed and thin crust.  Perfectly crunchy ends and just chewy enough in the middle.  Good quality cheese and tangy tomato sauce. I ordered it with just mushrooms and they put on a lot!   I also asked for heavy sauce.  They put extra sauce on the pizza and even gave me an extra container of sauce in case I needed more. 

I can't decide which was better, the pizza or "breadsticks."  I say "breadsticks" because they were really more like garlic bread strips.  So buttery and garlicy, they were great even without sauce.  I'm ashamed to say I ate nearly the entire order myself.  

The employees are very nice and helpful.  The store is clean. I need to go back and try their lunch buffet.
Help me polish this:
I absolutely love it! After reading the fantastic reviews and being in dire need of good carry out, we made the decision to give Pizzaville a try (anyone else picturing JT singing "Bring it on down to Pizzaville"?). While the prices may be slightly on the higher side, the food quality more than makes up for it! The pizza crust at Pizzaville strikes the perfect balance between hand-tossed and thin crust. It has wonderfully crispy ends and just the right amount of chewiness in the middle. The high-quality cheese and tangy tomato sauce make for a delightful combination. I opted for mushrooms only, and they generously piled them on! I also requested heavy sauce, and they not only added extra sauce to the pizza but even provided an additional container in case I needed more.

Now comes the difficult decision of determining which was better, the pizza or the "breadsticks". I use quotation marks because the so-called "breadsticks" were essentially garlic bread strips. They were incredibly buttery and packed with garlic flavor, so delicious that they didn't even require sauce. I must confess, I devoured nearly the entire order myself – they were that irresistible.

In addition to the scrumptious food, the employees at Pizzaville are incredibly friendly and helpful, and the store itself is clean and inviting. I simply must make a return visit to sample their lunch buffet; I have high hopes it will be just as amazing as their carry out.

input: The service was good and the staff was polite, but the food was bland and lacked flavor. The drinks were ok about what you would expect of a chain restaurant. If you are looking for somewhere to sit Down for a quick lunch this might be your place.

input:
I thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance. The decor was modern and cozy. The lighting was appropriate for dinner but terrible for selfies lol. Our waiter was OK. He seemed to be very hyper and impatient. I almost felt like he was rushing to take care of us instead of genuinely trying to give us an experience. I ordered the Shrimp Breaux Bridge and it was tasty. Nothing to phone home about but it was good. My friend ordered the Balsamic Salmon and it was good as well. It kind of reminded me of an Asian dish. Another friend had the Pesto Crusted Idaho Trout. It was cooked and flavored very nicely. 

I also ordered the Zangria White which is a sangria that was supposed to include strawberries, blueberries and diced apples... and i only got apples. IF there is an item on the menu that contains SEASONAL FRUITS AND VEGGIES ETC.... DISCLOSE SOMEWHERE ON THE MENU THAT THOSE THINGS ARE OUT OF SEASON. It definitely wouldve made a difference in my drink order. But overall the sangria was OK. 

I would go back because Im sure the service is better that what I experienced and I have heard amazing things about the menu.
Help me polish this:
I thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance of the restaurant. The modern and cozy decor created a pleasant atmosphere. However, the lighting was more suitable for dinner than for taking selfies, which was a slight inconvenience. 

Our waiter was okay, although he appeared to be quite hyper and impatient. It felt as though he was rushing to attend to us rather than genuinely focusing on enhancing our dining experience. 

Regarding the food, I ordered the Shrimp Breaux Bridge, which was tasty but didn't particularly stand out. It was good, but not remarkable. My friend opted for the Balsamic Salmon, which was also enjoyable. Interestingly, it had a slight Asian influence in its flavors. Another companion chose the Pesto Crusted Idaho Trout, which was skillfully cooked and brimming with flavor. 

I also decided to try the Zangria White, a sangria advertised to include strawberries, blueberries, and diced apples. Unfortunately, my drink only contained apples, which was disappointing. It would have been helpful if the menu had indicated that certain ingredients, such as seasonal fruits and veggies, were unavailable. This information would have influenced my choice of drink. Nevertheless, the sangria was decent overall. 

Despite the mixed experience, I would be willing to give this restaurant another try. I believe the service may be better than what I encountered, and I have heard rave reviews about the menu.

input:
Despite being a spin-off at the burgers from Rouge, I actually think that the burgers here are, dare I say it, better then flagship restaurants.
Over the last year they keep expanding their burger and toppings options by editing the little placard next to the registers, instead of changing their giant menuboard every time  they decide to add a new cheese or vegetable you can put on the burger.

I've been here a few times, trying the 500 (lettuce, bacon, cheddar, special sauce) delicious, and also making my own combos with their Kobe Beef burger (I think its worth the extra few bucks). I like it with truffle cheese and grilled onions. The brioche bun also really makes these burgers something special.

Their fries are also extremely delicious. As a huge fan of truffle oil, I can never resist getting their truffle oil fries. When they come warm out of the fryer, coated in truffle oil, there is just no better taste known to man.

Most important of all, they are open late on weekends.
Help me polish this:
Despite being a spin-off of Rouge's burgers, I believe that the burgers at this place are, dare I say it, even better than those at the flagship restaurants. What sets them apart is their commitment to continually expanding their burger and toppings options. Instead of changing their giant menu board every time they introduce a new cheese or vegetable, they simply edit the little placard next to the registers. This shows their dedication to providing a wide range of choices for burger enthusiasts.

During my visits here, I have tried the 500 burger - which includes lettuce, bacon, cheddar, and special sauce - and I must say it was delightful. Additionally, I have experimented with creating my own combinations, particularly with their Kobe Beef burger. Though it may cost a little extra, I believe it is worth every penny. I highly recommend pairing it with truffle cheese and grilled onions. To top it all off, the brioche bun they use elevates the overall burger experience and adds a special touch.

In addition to their exceptional burgers, I must give a special mention to their fries. As someone who is a huge fan of truffle oil, I find myself unable to resist their truffle oil fries. Served warm and coated in this aromatic delight, it truly offers a taste that is unrivaled.

Lastly, their late-night weekend hours are a major plus for me. Their commitment to staying open late ensures that even during those late-night cravings, I can still enjoy their fantastic burgers and fries.

In conclusion, despite being a spin-off, this place has managed to surpass its flagship counterparts with its variety of burger choices, the quality of ingredients used, and the overall deliciousness of their offerings. Whether you're a burger aficionado or simply a late-night food enthusiast, this place is a must-try.

input:
I really, really, really like so much about this hotel. For starters, it's BEAUTIFUL!!  Everytime I go to Reno, this is where I stay and I will continue to stay here when I go!!

PRO's:

1. The Spa is amazing! The staff working there are so friendly and helpful.The pools in the spa area are so clean. There were plenty of towels, water, juice, etc. 

2. The rooms were very clean and organized. 

3. The front desk staff was very nice and helpful. We didnt like the location of our room, so they moved us to another location with no problems.

4. They have a little diner that is there open 24 hours and has good food. Granted its a bit expensive, but it's a casino, what do you expect?


CON's:

1. The bathrooms in the hotel rooms didnt have fans, so when you're in the shower it gets so steamy, so fast!

2. We ordered rooms services and we ordered coffee as well, and they didnt bring creamer.
Help me polish this:
I absolutely love this hotel! There are so many things that make it exceptional. Firstly, the hotel itself is stunning, making it my go-to place whenever I visit Reno. I will definitely be staying here every time I come!

Here are some of the great features:

1. The spa is absolutely amazing! The staff working there are incredibly friendly and helpful. Additionally, the pools in the spa area are immaculately clean, and there is always an abundance of towels, water, juice, and more to make your experience even more enjoyable.

2. The rooms are consistently clean and well-organized. You can always count on a comfortable and tidy space to relax in.

3. The front desk staff is always kind and ready to assist you. We had an issue with the location of our room, but they were very understanding and promptly moved us to another location without any hassle.

4. The hotel has a delightful 24-hour diner on site that serves delicious food. While it may be a bit pricey, it's important to remember that it's a casino, so higher prices are to be expected.

However, there are a couple of minor drawbacks to note:

1. The bathrooms in the hotel rooms lack fans, leading to a quick build-up of steam when taking a shower. This can make the bathroom uncomfortably steamy.

2. During a room service order, we requested coffee and unfortunately, they forgot to bring creamer along with it.

Overall, despite these small inconveniences, I cannot recommend this hotel enough. It truly is the perfect place to stay in Reno, constantly providing excellent services.

She has a little turnover and I really like that. The first place that my kids were at in Carson had turn over all the time..... input: First time here and I'm not disappointed. Great seasoning on the seafood. I ordered oysters and their $45 combo and some garlic chicken wings for a family of six. It was more than enough for us. Only thing I can complain about is she messed up on our order.

input:

We walk to the bus stop by our house, the bus takes us directly to the Sparks bus station for a whopping $2 each. No parking, no driving through crowds, and no paying for parking. Winning.

From the bus station, we head immediately to Great Basin to get a large Icky and Bitchin' Berry. Beer is a must for battling these crowds and the large beers are worth the price!

If you have the JA Nugget mobile app, it will tell you where every vendor is and show it on a map. No more mindless wandering looking for your favorite vendor. I don't have a favorite, but go off of recommendations from friends, co-workers, etc.

Some vendors take cards, but we always make sure to bring plenty of cash. 

Be sure to walk through the non-rib vendors too. We got a couple of hats this year, which are nice to have at the event, but are also great beach hats for next year.

Saturday was a whole day affair and required us taking a cab back home. But because there was practically no crowd on Monday, we were able to get a beer, some food, and still use our bus transfer to get back home. Food stops being served at 5:00 pm on Monday and the vendors also start selling off extra food at crazy cheap prices.

input:
Excellent food and bar. Slow service.

A friend and I stopped here during an evening of bar hopping in the CBD. We were seated promptly and given our menus, which are half-French, half-English. Not a big deal for anyone who can read French and/or has been living in Louisiana for a reasonable amount of time, but definitely something tourists should be wary of. I didn't have any alcohol because I was the designated driver, but I can say that their drink menu is extensive, and the bar was packed from the moment we arrived until the moment we left. 

This restaurant's biggest strength is it's food. I tasted their crab bisque, and had Poulet Grand-Mère as my entrée. Both were excellent. The latter arrived in a wide cast-iron bowl, which I'm sure has a more proper name, but was an interesting touch nonetheless.

The service was why I gave this restaurant 4/5 instead of 5/5. Most of the wait staff seemed to be interns from culinary school. The handful we dealt with were very friendly, but would do well to be a little more attentive. For example, the server who brought us our desserts ran off before we could ask for spoons to eat the dessert with. 

In summary, a good dining experience, but I think I would rather continue exploring new restaurants in the area before returning.

In conclusion, it was a pleasant dining experience, but I would prefer to explore other restaurants in the area before considering a return visit.

input:
Came here for Sunday brunch and walked away with a very full belly and a good buzz! 

Their brunch buffet includes tons of seafood, an omelet station, pasta bar, carving station, custom sushi rolls, fresh fruit, salads, and the usually breakfast foods you'd expect at a buffet. I almost forgot dessert...an entire side of the room is dedicated to a table full of desserts AND a chocolate fountain. The brunch price also include bottomless mimosas which were literally bottomless. Our server never let us empty our glasses and  the mimosas were very heavy on the champagne, so we all got a bit tipsy. At least the alcohol let us forget how much weight we gained during this meal.

As if the buffet spread wasn't enough, they also have an a la carte menu with small dishes. The choices included Belgian waffles, french toast, blintzes, Mahi, and a few other savory dishes.  You can order as many of these items as you want, as many times as you want. Our server was sure to remind us of this, she seemed to enjoy watching how gluttonous our table was! 

Unfortunately we were here during Tropical Storm Debby, so we didn't get to enjoy a beautiful view of the bay, Although, being here while the weather was so awful was very cozy with the fireplace and wood interior. Thanks to the weather it wasn't crowded either, so don't write this place off on account of bad weather. 

At $35 a person, the Sunday brunch seems pricey, but if you have no qualms about overeating and overdrinking, you'll definitely get your money's worth.
Help me polish this:
I had an amazing experience at this Sunday brunch. From the moment I walked in, I knew I was in for a treat. The buffet offered a vast array of options, including an omelet station, pasta bar, carving station, and even custom sushi rolls. And let's not forget about the desserts! An entire side of the room was dedicated to a variety of sweet treats, including a captivating chocolate fountain.

But what truly made this brunch stand out was the bottomless mimosas. It's rare to find a place that actually provides limitless refills, and this establishment did not disappoint. The mimosas were expertly crafted, with the perfect amount of champagne, leaving us feeling pleasantly tipsy. The attentive server made sure our glasses were always filled, adding to the overall enjoyable experience.

If the buffet wasn't already enough, they also offered an a la carte menu with delicious small dishes. From Belgian waffles to Mahi, the choices were tempting and satisfying. The server reminded us that we could order as many of these items as we wanted, and her delight at witnessing our indulgence was contagious.

Despite the unfortunate weather conditions due to Tropical Storm Debby, the cozy ambiance, complete with a fireplace and wood interior, made our experience even more special. Additionally, being a less crowded day due to the weather allowed us to fully enjoy and appreciate the dining experience.

Although the Sunday brunch may seem pricey at $35 per person, it is well worth the cost for those who can embrace the joy of overeating and overdrinking. You will leave with a satisfied belly and a memorable experience that is truly worth the investment.

input:
I've been to Mount Laurel's On the Border over 50 times. I used to go to Don Pablo's but I fell in love with On the Border's chips and salsa (their chips are nice and salty, and their salsa is a little spicier).

When I go, 90% of the time I just sit at the bar and drink beer and snack on their chips and salsa. The beer specials are pretty good but could be a little better- weekdays has a happy hour as well as a late night happy hour too.

When I do dine, I often just enjoy a variety of vegetarian sides. Lately, I've grown to enjoy their cheese enchiladas, which I find delicious. Service when dining is usually great.

As for the bartenders, it's really hit-or-miss. Joann is probably my favorite- she's friendly, attentive, funny, and I've really gotten to know her, and I'd give them 5 stars if my experience was with her alone. There is a bartender named Nikki though, and if she's there, I always get the worst service. She barely checks on me/us to see how we're doing, she seems unfriendly, if she actually comes to refill your chips then she will not refill your salsa, she has taken my beer and refilled it without asking (when I was done and trying to leave), and I've had to wait forever to ask her for my check. At least twice, I've had to ask other bartenders to bring my check so that I could finally close out and leave. I'd give them 1 star if my experience was based on her alone.

Overall, good appetizers, cold beer, moderate prices, and usually good service.

input: Delicious food, sub-par service. I stopped into this dessert bar today to grab some dessert and a coffee to-go. While everyone seemed to be very helpful, or at least wanting to be, I'm not sure I received the best possible service. I ordered two slices of cake, one marshmallow chocolate and one cheesecake. Both were DELICIOUS, but it seemed like I waited forever to receive these, and when i did, it was in a cute but inefficient manner. The to-go boxes were stacked one on top of the other, with a loosely tied string around them. While I admire the aesthetics here, I would have much preferred a bag. Though, the worst part of my experience was the barista. I ordered an iced coffee with milk and sugar. First, he put ice in the cup and filled it halfway with coffee. He then asked me to pick and put in my own sugars from a cup of packets as he stated "I wouldn't know what and how much you want, I only drink my coffee black." As I considered this incompetent statement, i expected him to then put more hot coffee in to help the sugar dissolve. But no, he proceeded to fill the rest of the HALF OF THE CUP with milk. And then handing me the drink he told me I'd better stir it to mix the cream and sugar in. Not sure why I'd paid such a high price to practically make my own half-coffee half-mild beverage, I simply smiled and walked away. I ended up throwing out the drink as I could hardly even taste the coffee and I'm not too fond of a lot of milk in my coffee. Nonetheless, the cakes were delicious, and I will be coming back with the hopes that this new business is still in the process of improving itself.

Meatloaf and mashed potatoes were just as I expected; thankfully, no attempt to "fancy them up"; just tasty comfort food.  I asked for French dressing and bleu cheese crumbles on my salad, and they were generous with the cheese.  The salad was cold and fresh and crisp.

The reason I did not give five stars was the service. The first night, we weren't told of specials (ugh, saw them on the way out and would have ordered them!), and my friend's appetizer order was wrong. Drinks were not refilled often enough, and the waitress seemed uninformed about some of the items.  The next night, different waitress. We were one of only two tables, and still waited too long for her to return. She was unable to answer a question about a menu item, as well.

The place is beautiful, and the bathroom was clean and bright.  The menu offers many thoughtfully composed choices. Some of your servers are not up to par.

input:
My son and I went in for burgers after a long day's drive returning him to Nashville for the upcoming semester. We were in need of immediate sustenance after a long fast. What we found was a busy place that actually knew how to operate with a full house. Our need were quickly satisfied with courteous and reasonably priced service. 

Since we were just two, we were quickly seated. We started off with a couple Highland stouts. It was a nice drink and at a reasonable price. Before our entree, we shared a large garden salad. It was fresh and flavorful. The dressing was a bit on the heavy side for a vinaigrette. 

For entrees, I had the Black and Blue burger with fries. The burger was just incredible. It was perfectly cooked. The blue cheese was not overpowering. The bun was soft and fresh. The side of regular fries were crisp and lightly salted. Even better, they went perfectly with the homemade ketchup. I'm not a fan of ketchup, but theirs is very nice since they seem to avoid adding too much sweetness. My son had a basic burger with sweet potato fries. I tried the sweet potato fries and think they might be some of the best I've ever eaten. The burger looked as good as mine and my son concurred. 

The burger was well made and consumed within minutes. No words were spoken as we ate. Always a good sign. We shall return.
Help me polish this:
My son and I decided to grab burgers after a long day of driving back to Nashville for the upcoming semester. We were famished and in need of a quick meal. Luckily, we stumbled upon a bustling restaurant that knew how to handle a full house. Our needs were promptly met with friendly service and reasonable prices.

Since we were a party of two, we were seated promptly. To start off our meal, we enjoyed a couple of refreshing Highland stouts, which were reasonably priced. Before our main course, we decided to share a generous portion of their garden salad. The salad was bursting with freshness and delicious flavors, although the vinaigrette dressing was slightly on the heavier side.

For our entrees, I opted for the Black and Blue burger with a side of fries. The burger was absolutely phenomenal, cooked to perfection. The blue cheese was just right, providing a delightful tang without overpowering the other flavors. The bun was soft and fresh, adding to the overall satisfaction. The basic burger my son chose was equally impressive, accompanied by some delectable sweet potato fries. I couldn't resist trying them, and they turned out to be some of the best I've ever tasted. My son agreed, and satisfaction filled the air as we indulged in our meals.

The burgers were devoured within minutes, with no need for conversation as our taste buds did the talking. It's always a good sign when the food speaks for itself. We have already made up our minds to return to this fantastic establishment in the future.

input: Nothing more to say than this is the BEST donut place ever. I literally wished they shipped their products. When I moved to Florida, I missed it so much. It's only in New Orleans... sad face!
Help me polish this: There's simply no denying it - this is hands down the absolute BEST donut place you'll ever find. I can't even begin to express how much I wish they shipped their delightful treats. Moving to Florida left a gaping donut-shaped void in my life, and I long for the day when I can indulge in their heavenly creations again. Unfortunately, this gem is exclusive to New Orleans... and let's just say, it leaves me with a tinge of sadness!

input: Katie's is a neighborhood restaurant that has existed in one form or another for a few generation.  It's classic New Orleans fare with an Italian-American slant.  Great meatballs.  You'll see all types of classic New Orleans old people dinging before 8pm.   You won't be disappointed if your expectations aren't too high.
Help me polish this: Katie's is a cherished neighborhood restaurant that has stood the test of time, transcending generations. Offering a delightful blend of classic New Orleans cuisine with an Italian-American twist, their menu boasts remarkably delicious meatballs. One can't help but notice the pleasant charm of the establishment, with a lively gathering of longtime New Orleans residents savoring their meals before 8pm. While setting realistic expectations is key, a visit to Katie's will surely leave you satisfied and eager to return.

input: Excellent service! They were super fast, friendly and professional.  This is now my go to place for oil changes
Help me polish this: Exceptional service! They have proven themselves to be remarkably efficient, amiable, and adept. Without a doubt, this establishment has become my preferred destination for oil changes.

input:

input: This place should be on Restaurant Impossible. It's run down, the decor is tacky, beaten up, miss-matched and cheap. It's really dark...probably to hide how dingy it is. Everything was sticky. I ordered a burger medium and got a charred, tasteless hockey puck. My mom and aunt got the baked crab soup, which before we ordered, we misheard each other and called it baked crap soup. It turned out to be a better description. The crab stuffed mushrooms were heavy on the stuff and light on the crab.  The servers were super nice though.
Help me polish this:
This establishment is truly in desperate need of a Restaurant Impossible makeover. The entire place exudes neglect, with its worn-out and tacky decor that appears cheap and entirely mismatched. Its dim lighting seems almost intentional, perhaps as a means to conceal its dinginess. To make matters worse, everything felt sticky, leaving a lingering feeling of uncleanliness.

Regrettably, my experience with the food was equally disappointing. Despite ordering a medium-cooked burger, what I received resembled nothing more than a charred, tasteless hockey puck. Meanwhile, my mom and aunt opted for the baked crab soup, which, due to a slight miscommunication, we humorously referred to as "baked crap soup." Sadly, this description proved to be more accurate than expected. Furthermore, the crab stuffed mushrooms were disappointingly light on the crab and overwhelmingly packed with filler.

Despite the unfortunate circumstances, it is worth noting that the servers were remarkably pleasant and accommodating.

input:
What can I say?  I'm a sucker for new american.  The owner is a very nice gentleman who really enjoys food.  

The service was impeccable and the food was Ridiculously good.  We ordered a mixed berry waffle, huevo rancho, traditional breakfast bagel with grits, and best sandwich with fresh fruits.  

I highly recommend the huevo rancho and best sandwich.  The grits was very good as well. 

If you decide to visit this restaurant, say hi to the owner.  He's a great guy.
Help me polish this:
Let me help you polish that:

I have to admit, I'm a total sucker for new American cuisine. The owner of this restaurant is an absolute gem, a genuinely nice gentleman who has a true passion for food.

The service we received was nothing short of impeccable, and the food? Well, let's just say it was ridiculously good. Our order consisted of a delightful mixed berry waffle, a mouthwatering huevo rancho, a scrumptious traditional breakfast bagel with a side of perfectly cooked grits, and the best sandwich topped off with a refreshing assortment of fresh fruits.

If I had to recommend a couple of must-try dishes, the huevo rancho and the best sandwich would definitely be at the top of my list. The grits were also exceptionally tasty.

Should you find yourself paying a visit to this restaurant, be sure to say hello to the owner. He's an absolute pleasure to interact with and a truly great guy.

input: Great place for happy hour. Oysters were deLISH! My friend and I had 2 dozen and we had some cocktails! The riverbend and champagne au poir we quite tasty. I had a side of fries and she had a side a grits. Best grits I've eaten. Definitely coming back. The server was great too. Just the right amount of attention!
Help me polish this: This place is amazing for happy hour! The oysters were absolutely delicious, we couldn't resist ordering 2 dozen. And of course, we enjoyed some refreshing cocktails as well! The Riverbend and Champagne au Poir were particularly delightful. To go along with our seafood feast, I opted for a side of fries while my friend indulged in a side of grits. Speaking of which, those were hands down the best grits I've ever had! Needless to say, we'll definitely be returning. The server was also fantastic, striking the perfect balance of attentiveness without being overbearing.

input:
The crew at Bella Vista Designs are FABULOUS.  From start to finish, they are professional, conscientious, and innovative (and affordable!).  They never cease to amaze me with their can-do attitude and absolutely gorgeous and creative design. 

The events at Santa Barbara Historical Museum and Goleta Valley Historical Society that I produce attract generous donors and they always say the same thing when they see their work, "Wow!!"  

I can't thank them enough for the hundreds of successful events (and the many magical moments we've seen)!
Help me polish this:
The team at Bella Vista Designs is absolutely outstanding. From beginning to end, they exhibit unmatched professionalism, unwavering attention to detail, and remarkable creativity - all at an affordable price! Their can-do attitude never fails to impress me, and their designs are consistently breathtaking and inventive.

input:
Couldn't say it better than the below poster. Excellent food, service and prices.

Located where Mugshots used to be (RIP), one of my coworkers had been raving about this place, in particular the falafel and of course the very kind owner.

Went with my pre-wife and we shared beef gyro (carved) pita, falafel pita and hummus plate. Everything was extremely fresh (I concur on the crisp lettuce) well seasoned and just plain delicious.  A lot of food as well and complimentary baklava. We took our leftovers home (I wrapped the two remaining bites of my gyro - it's that good)

I highly recommend this place and you'll definitely walk out with a smile. I think this spot is still relatively unknown and I very rarely post reviews. This is a unique spot to Manayunk and I will be referring all of my friends as I really want the restaurant to succeed - because the owner deserves it and of course for my selfish appetite!
Help me polish this:
I couldn't agree more with the previous reviewer. This restaurant truly excels in terms of its food, service, and prices.

Located in the former Mugshots location (may it rest in peace), a coworker of mine had been gushing about this place, especially the falafel and the exceptionally kind owner.

When I visited with my fiancée, we decided to try the beef gyro pita, falafel pita, and the hummus plate, which we shared. Every dish was incredibly fresh (I wholeheartedly agree about the crispy lettuce), well-seasoned, and simply delightful. The portion sizes were generous, and to our delight, we were even treated to complimentary baklava. We ended up taking some leftovers home (I couldn't resist wrapping up the last two bites of my gyro – it was that good).

I highly recommend this restaurant, and I guarantee you'll leave with a smile on your face. Despite being relatively unknown, I rarely post reviews, but this place is worth sharing. It's a gem in Manayunk, and I'll definitely be recommending it to all my friends because the owner deserves all the success, and selfishly, for my own appetite's sake too!

input: Great food and excellent service. Only knock I would give them was they brought out our entrees about 10 minutes after our apps came so we were still eating that, otherwise great experience
Help me polish this: The dining experience was overall fantastic, with a delightful selection of dishes and outstanding service. The only minor drawback was that our entrées were served approximately 10 minutes after we had received our appetizers. Consequently, we were still enjoying our appetizers when our entrées arrived. Nevertheless, this small timing issue did not significantly affect the overall quality of our visit.

input:
This is a very mediocre place.  The location itself is in the same dirty strip mall as Mozzarella Pizza. The inside has that "we don't really care about the looks" feel to it.  It's not dirty, per se.  It just doesn't look very clean.  Everything looks like its falling apart.  It probably gets its business from suburbanites like me craving what we think of as Chinese food.

All that said, the food I had was palatable.  Nothing outstanding or amazing: it was just all right.  I won't recommend against it, but it's nothing that you would think of as that great either.
Help me polish this:
This place is quite mediocre, situated in the same run-down strip mall as Mozzarella Pizza. Inside, there's an evident lack of concern for aesthetics - it's not exactly dirty, but it definitely lacks cleanliness. The whole place seems on the verge of falling apart. It likely thrives on suburbanites like myself who have a craving for what we consider to be Chinese food.

Having said that, the food I had was decently enjoyable. It wasn't exceptional or mind-blowing - just average. While I wouldn't discourage others from trying it, it's not something you'd consider remarkable either.

input: Phenomenal place to eat. I has the Hickory burger, that was so damn delicious!! Will be coming back for sure!!!
Help me polish this: Phenomenal Place to Eat! I had their Hickory burger and it was absolutely incredible! The flavors were out of this world and I can't wait to come back for more. Highly recommended!

input: After having been here, I would say that the food had great flavors for the taste buds and it was a unique experience.  Our server, Brian was no doubt a foodie... I've never seen anyone get so excited about food and discuss the ingredients in such detail with so much passion.  The food really was different and had unbelievable flavor.  Anyone who calls themselves a foodie should try this place.  I'm thinking they would be pleased with this place.  But, the portions were small.  And I really didn't like the interior of the restaurant.  I'm more of a booths girl.  Booths can be classy, you know?  All in all, I would say this was an interesting place and I would come back, but the dishes were too complicated for me to want to come back beyond once a year.  Speaking of timing, the chefs change the menu every year.  And these guys really are good at what they do.  The owners actually own the Red Pony and two other restaurants all on the same street!  And they're all doing well.
Help me polish this:
After experiencing this restaurant, I can confidently say that the food offered an explosion of flavors for the taste buds, making it a truly unique dining experience. Our server, Brian, undoubtedly had a passion for food as evident in his excitement and detailed discussions about the ingredients. The dishes were undeniably distinct and boasted incredible flavors. Anyone who considers themselves a food enthusiast should definitely give this place a try - it is bound to leave them satisfied. 

However, it is worth mentioning that the portions were on the smaller side, and the interior of the restaurant did not appeal to my personal taste. As a fan of booth seating, I believe it can add a touch of class to the dining experience. Despite these minor drawbacks, I find this restaurant intriguing and would consider returning, though perhaps not more than once a year due to the complexity of the dishes. 

Speaking of timing, the chefs constantly refresh the menu on an annual basis, showcasing their expertise and dedication to their craft. It is worth noting that the owners not only own this restaurant but also the Red Pony and two other successful establishments on the same street, highlighting their prowess in the culinary industry.

input:

Family of four for about 30$.  That's a great deal w today's prices. 

If you are looking for a fast, casual Asian option, give this place a try.
Help me polish this:
We have seen significant improvements since our last visit. The quality of service has greatly improved, thanks to a kid named Dillon who provided excellent service. 

The ambiance is very casual, where you can simply order and sit while they bring the food to you.

The food is not only delicious but also offers a wide variety of options. Although it may not be fancy, it is incredibly affordable. Having a family of four dine here for approximately $30 is truly a great deal, especially considering today's prices.

If you are in search of a fast and casual Asian dining option, I highly recommend giving this place a try.

input: Use the yelp app to get on the waiting list, we went on a Saturday morning and it was very busy, but the waiting list was cut down significantly by using the app. The menu is expansive, a lot of options. The cinnamon French toast was very good. The traditional breakfast foods were on par with most breakfast joints, but the extras on the menu can keep you busy for many visits trying new things. The strawberry orange juice was excellent so I recommend trying it. It was a little hot in the restaurant, could have been cooled down a lot for a more comfortable experience. The service was very good. There were two places to pay at the counter which I thought was a nice way to speed up the leaving process.
Help me polish this:
I suggest the following revision:

We decided to use the Yelp app to put our names on the waiting list as we visited the restaurant on a busy Saturday morning. Thanks to the app, the wait time was significantly reduced. The menu offers a wide range of options and we were particularly impressed with the delicious cinnamon French toast. While the traditional breakfast choices were similar to those offered at other breakfast joints, the additional items on the menu provided countless opportunities to explore new flavors during future visits. Don't miss out on trying their refreshing strawberry orange juice, it's truly excellent. The only downside was that the temperature inside the restaurant was a bit too warm, and it would have been more pleasant if it had been cooler. Nonetheless, we were pleased with the prompt and attentive service. Additionally, they had two separate payment counters, which we found to be a thoughtful touch that streamlined the checkout process.

input:

Beer? Need I say more.

Found my new spot. 

Will be back.
Help me polish this:

The waiting area had a big TV and a comfortable plush couch where I could relax. The young lady who checked me in even offered me a choice of water, soda, or a beer. And let's be honest, when they offer beer, what more is there to say?

Not only was the atmosphere great, but I also received a fantastic haircut. The staff consisted of a wonderful group of guys who engaged in lively discussions about current events, sports, and what's happening around town. I knew right then and there that I had found my new go-to spot.

I am definitely planning to return because Shaving Grace exceeded my expectations in every way.

input: Not only was the food excellent, but the people here are beyond nice-and genuine. I had eggs Benedict. The poached eggs were good but the toast they were sitting on was excellent. Help me polish this: Not only was the food excellent, but the people here were exceptionally friendly and genuine. Our fantastic server, Tina, surprised us with a cream pancake to taste test and I must say, it exceeded all expectations. They were so delectable that I didn't even feel the need to use syrup. Truly a stellar experience!

input: Great service. My husband ordered a cheese and bacon burger and I got the crawfish sausage por bo both well made and great tasting.

As for me, I opted for the crawfish sausage po' boy, and it exceeded my expectations. Both dishes were expertly crafted and bursting with incredible flavors.

input: Had a wonderful experience with JT and Ashley Furniture store!! He was helpful even when I had to change my order.

input:
While at Drexel University, I decided to try a new food truck and go for something that wasn't the typical food truck.  My girlfriend and I always noticed this place was crowded around lunch but never knew why.  After being recommended to try it by a friend, we decided to go ahead and order lunch here.  Cucina Zapata is at the end of the food truck row at the center of Drexel University's campus.  The truck has a graffiti style design which can be easily distinguished from the other food trucks here.

I decided to order (2) thai short rib tacos while my girlfriend got the cap'n crunch tilapia burrito.  The food has a good visual appearance which made us more eager to eat it once we got inside the building.  I really enjoyed the thai short rib tacos even though they put hot sauce on it.  They were definitely better than the typical taco bell food and left me with a 5 star review feeling inside.  My girlfriend also really enjoyed her burrito.

Overall, this food truck provides very good food at a good price.  I recommend this place to anyone looking for a good lunch.
Help me polish this:
During my time at Drexel University, I decided to veer away from the typical food truck fare and try something new. Despite always witnessing a crowd around lunchtime, my girlfriend and I were intrigued by Cucina Zapata and unaware of what drew people to it. Upon a friend's recommendation, we finally mustered the courage to satisfy our curiosity at this food truck situated at the end of Drexel University's bustling food truck row. Its vibrant graffiti-style design easily sets it apart from the others.

Eager to explore their menu, I opted for two mouth-watering Thai short rib tacos, while my girlfriend indulged in the unique Cap'n Crunch tilapia burrito. The presentation of the food itself was visually appealing, further amplifying our anticipation as we entered the building. Personally, I found the Thai short rib tacos outstanding, despite the addition of hot sauce. They far surpassed the typical offerings at Taco Bell, leaving me with a satisfied, five-star review-inducing sensation. My girlfriend shared a similar sentiment, thoroughly enjoying her chosen burrito.

In summary, Cucina Zapata offers exceptional food at a reasonable price point. I wholeheartedly recommend this food truck to anyone seeking a delightful lunchtime experience.

input: got my haircut here for the first time Jessie Becker took the damaged ends off. She's so sweet and does only what you ask of her. She's also great with kids. come see this place and come see her.

input: Great ramen! I'm really happy to have found this place! The service and food are both wonderful!

input: First time here. Great bar and restaurant area. Open floor plan with plenty of TV's to watch the game. Attached to their O'Fallon brewery (in Maryland Heights, Missouri, a suburb of St. Louis). They ranked 2nd in the St Louis area last year for volume of beer sold by a micro brewery. Today, I tried the House Special IPA...a wonderful IPA, not too bitter, just right. Look for Troy behind the bar! (The only reason for 4 stars is no desserts....)
Help me polish this:
First time here, and I must say, this place is fantastic! The bar and restaurant area is great, offering an open floor plan that's perfect for watching the game. They even have plenty of TVs scattered around to ensure you don't miss a single moment. What sets this place apart is the fact that it's attached to their O'Fallon brewery, located in Maryland Heights, Missouri, a vibrant suburb of St. Louis.

If you're a beer enthusiast, you're in for a treat. Last year, they ranked an impressive 2nd in the St. Louis area for the volume of beer sold by a microbrewery. Today, I had the pleasure of trying their House Special IPA, and I must say, it was exceptional. This IPA strikes the perfect balance, delivering a wonderful flavor without excessive bitterness. Truly a standout.

Additionally, I highly recommend looking out for Troy behind the bar. He's fantastic at what he does and will make your experience even more enjoyable. The only reason I'm giving it four stars instead of five is the lack of dessert options. This minor downside aside, everything else about this place is outstanding.

input: This is a neighbourhood dive bar on the eastern part of Whyte Avenue.  It's in a strip mall on a one way eastbound side street.  I was there on a Saturday night to check it out. Very average decor with a couple pool tables and a foosball table. It's definitely a younger crowd here.  They had a band and a doorman.  Drinks were reasonable.  A few tv screens.  The wings are always really cheap and come with a carrot and celery stick.  They make pizzas which looked good and cheesy but I did not try. Servers were quite young and pleasant.  The owner gal behind the bar was fine.  I gave it an extra star because I found the previous review a little harsh.
Help me polish this:
This neighbourhood dive bar is located on the eastern part of Whyte Avenue, nestled within a strip mall on a one-way eastbound side street. I visited this establishment on a Saturday night, eager to experience its unique ambiance. The interior was adorned with very average decor, featuring a couple of pool tables and a foosball table. It was immediately apparent that this bar attracts a younger crowd.

Entertainment-wise, they had an energetic band performing, adding to the lively atmosphere. The presence of a doorman further enhanced the security and exclusivity of the venue. The drinks offered were reasonably priced, and several TV screens were scattered throughout the bar, ensuring patrons wouldn't miss any important sporting events or shows.

One noteworthy highlight is the affordable and delicious wings, served with a side of fresh carrot and celery sticks. Additionally, they offer pizzas that appeared enticingly gooey and cheesy, although I did not have the opportunity to indulge in them myself. The servers, although quite young, were pleasant and attentive, providing a positive dining experience.

As for the owner, a gal who manned the bar, I found her to be affable and capable in her role. In light of a previous review being overly critical, I believe it is worth mentioning that I have awarded this establishment an extra star as I feel the criticism does not accurately represent my overall experience.

input:

input: I had an amazingly positive experience here. Dr. Neel and Robin were friendly, knowledgable and exceptionally helpful. input: By far the best breakfast I have had in a while. Huge pancakes. Simple home fries with not all the extras. The owner is super sweet and really generous. Deffinetly a new favorite.

input:

input:
I've been having a terrible time in St Louis finding a decent Chinese place that is within delivery or easy take out range of our house. This time I tried Wei Hong. I told my partner it can't be any worse than the other mediocre places we have been going. I was wrong.
The take out service was fast for a Sat night. We were there within 20 minutes of ordering and it was ready. But the dining room was empty. For a Sat night that should have been a big clue. The rest of the places in the neighborhood were busy.
The steamed dumplings could have been great. The tasted homemade and the filling was good. However, they were so doughy with a really thick wrapper too thick that it detracted from the good filling. Everything else went downhill from there. 
The beef and broccoli was inedible. The beef had an awful weird texture. Like it was boiled and was gelatinous.  The sauce on it had off flavors. We literally scraped it off our plates and threw the whole thing out.  The meat in both the general Tao's chicken and the orange beef also had weird textures. It was mushy and the coating was thick on those as well. The flavors in the sauces would have been fine, but they were gloopy.  The fried rice was fair but nothing memorable.
We won't be going back.

input:
was on an errand-running run and remembered how ashamed i was at the state of my car the last time i looked at it - five minutes earlier, as i entered said vehicle.

saw the sign as i was about to turn into riverside plaza to make my groceries and decided it was time.  got the basic $12 tchoup and even though there were about 5 cars in the vacuum line ahead of me, my car was ready before i was done checking out the waiting area.  iguanas, parrots, ms. pac man ($1 a game?  the price of nostalgia, i guess).  not to mention the windows that look out into the auto wash system - which is really entertainment enough for me.  i'm not picky.

but then my number was up and i went out and inspected the results.  still some bird poop remnants on the hood and a few bugs didn't give up the ghost on the grill...maybe i am picky after all.  

don't get me wrong - it was better than nothing (which was what my car got in terms of washings since mid-january), but i'm missing my favorite car wash right about now.  their regular automatic wash with vacuum and window cleaning (i.e. the tchoup treatment) is $14, true, but those dudes are much more thorough with the elbow grease post-assembly line washing.

but that place is in los angeles, alas.  which is perhaps the best gauge of how pricey this place is: 85% as expensive as l.a., but 66.67% the quality.  worth it?  you do the math.  i'ma try a completely touchless system next time.  i reckon i'll get about the same results, but with no parrots or ms. pac-man.
Help me polish this:
I was in the midst of running errands when I suddenly felt embarrassed by the sorry state of my car, which I had just entered five minutes ago. As I was about to turn into Riverside Plaza to grab groceries, I noticed a sign and decided it was finally time for a car wash. Opting for the basic $12 package, I patiently waited in line behind five other cars at the vacuum station. Surprisingly, my car was finished before I even had a chance to explore the waiting area, which was adorned with iguanas, parrots, and the classic Ms. Pac-Man game (although I must say, $1 per game is quite a nostalgic price). The real entertainment, however, came from observing the auto wash system through the windows. I guess I'm not too hard to please.

When my turn came, I stepped out to inspect the results. To my dismay, there were still remnants of bird poop on the hood and a few persistent bugs on the grill. Perhaps I am more particular than I thought. Don't get me wrong, the car wash was better than nothing, considering my car hadn't received any cleaning since mid-January. However, I couldn't help but long for my favorite car wash back in Los Angeles. For just $14, they provided a thorough automatic wash, complete with vacuuming and window cleaning—the true Tchoup treatment. Comparatively, this place falls short, offering only 66.67% of the quality at 85% of the price. Is it worth it? I'll leave that calculation up to you. Next time, I'll give a completely touchless system a try. I assume the results will be similar, but sadly without the parrots or Ms. Pac-Man.

This is a great late brunch option during the weekends when the big morning rush dies down after 1 pm. Usually there is no wait or 5 minute wait at this time. One big complaint is that they don't have an organized system for seating guests. The servers don't always greet incoming patrons (which should be required Waffle House-style) and they sometimes tell you to seat yourself (which can lead to one or two people taking up tables for 4) or they'll seat you (whenever they get around to talking to you). 

I've ordered a several different dishes at this point and they have varies from ok to awesome. The chicken wings and onion rings are just ok. The wings are either lightly dredged in flour or not at and then fried whole. They aren't really seasoned so the wings are pretty bland. The "onion rings" made of formed, chopped onions that are breaded. The chicken fingers were a bit over battered and dry. The smashwich (or whatever it's called) was pretty good: your choice of breakfast meat with hash browns and eggs in a hoagie roll, but unspectacular. The club sandwich is classic diner fare that is very well executed. The egg and omelette platters are a very good deal and dang tasty. The best thing on the menu is definitely the waffle. It's gently sweet, very crispy and covered in butter. So good!

The service is generally pretty attentive (once you're seated), the restaurant and bathrooms are very clean, the food is a good, tasty value

during this late brunch option. However, one major drawback is their lack of an organized guest seating system. Servers sometimes fail to greet incoming patrons, which should be a requirement similar to Waffle House. This can result in individuals taking up larger tables or delayed seating.

The chicken fingers are over battered and dry. On the other hand, the smashwich—an option with your choice of breakfast meat, hash browns, and eggs in a hoagie roll—is decent but not exceptional. In terms of service, once you are seated, the staff is generally attentive. The restaurant and bathrooms are kept clean, contributing to a pleasant dining experience. Overall, considering the food's taste, value for money, and cleanliness, this late brunch option is definitely worth trying out during weekends when the morning rush has subsided after 1 pm.

Help me polish this:
I would give this place a rating of 5, but I was disappointed with their reuben sandwich. I have a habit of ordering reuben at new places that offer it on their menu, and unfortunately, the rye bread used for this sandwich was not up to par, which was surprising considering that Companion is known for their bread.

On the other hand, my fiancee had a different sandwich (I forgot the name) with chicken, bacon, and avocado on french bread, and it was absolutely amazing!

I also tried their spice chicken soup paired with corn bread, and it was fantastic! The soup was packed with vegetables and chicken, with just the right amount of heat, and the corn bread was large and delicious.

However, I must warn you not to order their chi latte as it was not impressive at all - I would suggest skipping it. 

While the prices were a bit steep, this place is definitely worth visiting for a delightful breakfast or lunch. The staff are friendly and welcoming. Give it a try and let me know your thoughts!

input:
Probably the best thing about Target is that it isn't Wal Mart.

Target is awesome because it has everything from clothes to toys to electronics to makeup. 

I usually stop in here (if I remember) to pick up my makeup, because it's at least $2-3 cheaper than other stores.  They have a great grocery section and their selection of household items (microwaves, etc.) is fantastic.

They are always good about having enough registers open for the number of shoppers in the place, and I rarely have to wait in a line.
Help me polish this: Target stands out as an exceptional retailer, setting itself apart from competitors such as Walmart. This is largely due to Target's wide range of product offerings, including clothing, toys, electronics, and makeup. Unlike other retailers, Target consistently offers competitive prices, making it an ideal destination for cost-conscious shoppers like myself. When it comes to purchasing makeup, Target proves even more enticing as their prices are consistently $2-3 cheaper than other stores. Additionally, Target excels in its grocery section, offering an impressive array of items, and boasts a fantastic selection of household essentials, such as microwaves. One of the hallmarks of a great retail experience is the checkout process, and Target excels in this regard. With sufficient registers open to cater to the number of shoppers present, I seldom find myself waiting in line for an extended period of time.

Help me polish this:
