input:
This is the biggest and best location for HMV in the city. The prices aren't any different from other stores but they do have a larger selection of gifting (figurines,mugs,blankets etc) as well as the largest collection of titles that don't fit into what is new and hot at the moment. Anything that they don't carry can actually be ordered in for you but I have to say staff here are not always the best at phoning customers to let them know when their titles are in so one should definitely keep their number by the phone to check in with them after a week or so.

The biggest selling point for me here besides the selection has to be the staff at the tills. It can get a little busy here but lines are always dealt with quickly and I appreciate that they don't push as hard as other locations to try and sign you up for a pure card. F.Y.I to anybody considering the pure rewards program the redemption items are not that great. It took me about a year of collecting just to accumulate enough points for a true blood key chain and when I got it it was placed in a bubble mailer and not even in it's original packaging. Needless to say when it came time to renew the card I opted out.

Anyways to sum it all up I will say for selection and speedy service these guys get five stars but the prices as well as the sometimes slow ordering process drop it down to a 3. Still worth checking out though if you have been on the hunt at smaller stores for a particular movie or cd.
Help me polish this:
This HMV location is the largest and best in the city. While the prices are similar to other stores, they have an extensive selection of gift items such as figurines, mugs, and blankets. Additionally, they have the largest collection of titles that may not be popular at the moment. If they don't have something in stock, you can place an order with them. However, the staff may not always be proactive in notifying customers when their orders arrive, so it's advisable to keep their number handy and check in after a week or so.

One standout feature for me is the staff at the tills. Despite the store's busyness, they efficiently handle the checkout lines. I appreciate that they don't aggressively push for sign-ups to their pure card program, unlike other locations. On a side note, for anyone considering the pure rewards program, the redemption items are not very impressive. It took me a year of collecting points just to get a true blood keychain, which arrived in a bubble mailer without its original packaging. Consequently, I decided not to renew my card when the time came.

In summary, this HMV location deserves five stars for its selection and speedy service. However, the prices and occasional sluggish ordering process bring it down to a three. Nevertheless, it's worth a visit, especially if you've been searching for a specific movie or CD at smaller stores.

input: Wow is all I have to say. Must try the friend oysters!we ordered that and crawfish bisque and shrimp with grits. All the dishes were delicious. Make sure to make reservation.
Help me polish this: Wow, I cannot express how impressed I am. One must try the phenomenal friend oysters at this place! We also ordered their delicious crawfish bisque and shrimp with grits, both of which exceeded our expectations. It's essential to make a reservation to ensure you don't miss out on this extraordinary dining experience.

input: Was on a mission trying to find the perfect coat for the Holidays. Found my idea of the perfect coat at Burlington but they did not have my size. Went to Target, bought a coat but ended up taking it bath. Was not my dream coat. Next stop Ross. The only coat in my size was a beautiful Bomber style jacket made of pleather. Bought it right before Christmas. Now it's a few days after Christmas and my husband Guy points out to me that the coat is really wrinkled. I go on line and look up every possible hack to get wrinkles out of pleather. They all fail miserably. I just went back to Ross with that coat, no receipt, no tags and asked to speak to the manager. The manager is a young male with dark hair and black framed glasses. I tell him of my plight. He literally says go find what you need, no problem. WOW! You won't believe it, but there was my Camouflage coat, in my size, hanging there waiting for me. Oh the irony! They exchanged my coat and after all that I ended up with my Dream coat after all. Thank you Ross Dress for Less. You will forever be my first choice for now on!
Help me polish this:
I was on a mission to find the perfect coat for the Holidays, and after searching high and low, I finally found my ideal coat at Burlington. However, to my disappointment, they didn't have it in my size. Determined not to give up, I decided to try my luck at Target, where I bought a coat that I thought would suffice. Regrettably, it turned out to be far from my dream coat. 

Refusing to settle for less, I made one last attempt at Ross. There, I stumbled upon a beautiful pleather Bomber style jacket that fit me perfectly. With Christmas just around the corner, I happily purchased it. However, a few days after Christmas, my husband Guy pointed out how incredibly wrinkled the coat was. Desperate to salvage it, I scoured the internet for every possible hack to remove wrinkles from pleather, but all my attempts failed miserably.

Frustrated, I decided to go back to Ross, armed with only the coat and no receipt or tags. I requested to speak to the manager, who happened to be a young man with dark hair and black framed glasses. I poured out my predicament to him, hoping for a miracle. Astonishingly, he simply replied, "Go find what you need, no problem." I was amazed at his willingness to help.

Unbelievably, as if fate had intervened, I found my dream coat, a Camouflage coat, hanging there in my size, waiting for me. The irony was not lost on me. Ross Dress for Less exchanged my coat, completely understanding my situation. In the end, despite all the trials, I finally ended up with my long-desired coat. I am immensely grateful to Ross Dress for Less, and they will forever be my first choice from now on.

input: You honestly can't go wrong here. My favorites are the Udon Noodle Salad (a-ma-zing) and the Crispy Hipcity Ranch (so, so good). Friendly staff, fast service. Oh, they deliver too!
Help me polish this: You really can't go wrong with this place. My personal favorites are the Udon Noodle Salad (absolutely amazing) and the Crispy Hipcity Ranch (incredibly delicious). The staff is friendly and the service is fast. Plus, they even offer delivery!

input: Philadelphia, I love you.  Places like this remind me why.  We sat at the counter and watched the guys make the pizzas.  Our son hates cheese on a pizza and they had one already on the menu for him: The Marinara (oregano, crushed san marzano tomatoes, garlic, olive oil).  It was simple... but delicious. If you like real wood-fired pizzas that char the crust (a little blackened... in a good way), this is the place to go to.  Our other favorite pizza joints that rival this place are Lombardi's (NYC) and Grimaldi's (Brooklyn).  We all had a slice and were shocked at the lovely simplicity of it. Razor thin slices of garlic dotted the fresh tomato sauce.  My husband and I shared the Salsiccia (fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, mozzarella).  Roasted fennel on a pizza?  Brilliant. I cried a little.  No wait... I REALLY cried when we shared this cocktail: The Brooklyn (Dad's Hat rye, Luxardo cherry, white vermouth).  It says it serves one, but they brought it out in a cute little bottle and gave us each a glass...each with a hand- crafted giant square ice cube (hipster-cool) and Luxardo cherries.  Perfection.  We also shared a Rotolo (pizza dough, mortadella, ricotta, pistacchio pesto).  Those are crazy amazing.  I kept saying my husband could eat the rest... then freaking out and going back for another bite. He's lucky I didn't stab him in the hand with a fork to fight over the last bite (to be fair, he was the smart one who ordered it).  I could've eaten several of those and forgotten the pizza (although that was wonderful too!).  We finished with a little dessert... perfect little Italian cookies ("Cookie Jar" - pignoli, almond cookies, chocolate biscotti, pistacchio gnocchi) and I got an Affogato (fiordilatte soft serve with a shot of espresso).  The soft serve is Italian sweet cream... decadent and lovely... with rich espresso in a pretty little Italian mug.  I'm in Heaven here.  I know nothing about Vetri's other restaurants, but I'm checking them out next time I'm in Philadelphia!  By the way... service was great and friendly.  5 stars all around!
Help me polish this:
Philadelphia, I cannot express enough how much I adore you. This city never fails to remind me why I hold it so dear to my heart. Recently, we had the pleasure of visiting a pizza place that left us in awe. As we sat at the counter, our eyes were fixed on the skilled pizza-makers crafting each pie with precision. One particular pizza on the menu caught our attention, especially because it catered perfectly to our son's unusual pizza preferences. The Marinara, a simple combination of oregano, crushed san marzano tomatoes, garlic, and olive oil, was a delightful surprise. True to its wood-fired origins, the crust had a subtle char that added a touch of smokiness, elevating the entire experience. This place, with its mastery of wood-fired pizza, easily rivals our other favorites like Lombardi's in NYC and Grimaldi's in Brooklyn.

We couldn't resist trying more of their tempting creations. We all eagerly savored a slice of their exceptional pizza, adorned with razor-thin slices of garlic delicately dotting the fresh tomato sauce. My husband and I decided to share the Salsiccia, which featured fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, and mozzarella. The brilliant addition of roasted fennel on a pizza brought tears to my eyes (figuratively, of course). 

An unexpected surprise awaited us when we ordered The Brooklyn cocktail. Meant to serve only one, this cocktail arrived in a charming little bottle, accompanied by individual glasses adorned with hand-crafted giant square ice cubes and Luxardo cherries. Each sip was perfection, showcasing the flavors of Dad's Hat rye, Luxardo cherry, and white vermouth in perfect harmony.

The Rotolo caught our attention next. A delightful combination of pizza dough, mortadella, ricotta, and pistachio pesto, these little delights were nothing short of crazy amazing. I must admit, I struggled to share with my husband, finding myself going back for just "one more bite" repeatedly. Keeping my fork from becoming a weapon to claim the last bite was a testament to my love for him (and his good decision in ordering the dish).

We concluded our meal with a small yet satisfying dessert. The Cookie Jar, a delightful assortment of pignoli, almond cookies, chocolate biscotti, and pistachio gnocchi, made our taste buds sing with joy. To accompany it, I indulged in an Affogato, a heavenly combination of fiordilatte soft serve and a shot of espresso. Served in an elegant Italian mug, the richness of the sweet cream blended beautifully with the boldness of the espresso.

I must confess, my knowledge of Vetri's other restaurants is limited. However, after this exceptional experience, I am eager to explore their other establishments during my next visit to Philadelphia. Additionally, I must applaud the service we received at this pizza place. The staff was friendly and attentive, creating a truly enjoyable dining experience. This place deserves a perfect 5-star rating in every aspect.

input:
This a really price store with great clothes. Mostly high end stuff, everything here is designer. 

The workers here are really friendly and not pushy. They will leave you alone if you just want to be left alone, they are never breathing down your neck trying to make a sale. They carry casual clothing but I think it's much better place for suits and dress shirts and fancy clothing. I think this place stands out in West Edmonton Mall in terms of service and dressy clothing for men. They really do everything to make your shopping experience better. 

Be prepared to spend some coin here, although you won't be disappointed.
Help me polish this:
This store is truly a hidden gem, offering an exquisite selection of high-quality clothing at reasonable prices. Specializing in designer wear, you'll find an array of luxury brands that cater to discerning tastes.

What truly sets this store apart is the exceptional customer service. The staff here are exceptionally friendly and never pushy. They understand that some shoppers prefer to browse undisturbed, so they give you the space you need. You won't find them breathing down your neck trying to make a quick sale. This excellent balance of attentiveness and respect for your privacy makes shopping here a delight.

While they do carry casual clothing, their real forte lies in their impressive collection of suits, dress shirts, and formal attire. Whether you're dressing for a special occasion or simply want to elevate your style, this is the place to be. Among the vast offerings in West Edmonton Mall, this store stands out for both its impeccable service and its selection of dressy clothing for men.

It's important to note that shopping here may require a willingness to invest in quality pieces. However, rest assured, the investment will be worth every penny. Once you experience what this store has to offer, you won't be disappointed.

input:
The food was pretty tasty. Nothing outstanding though. It reminds me of any Mediterranean food truck that I've been to. It's a nice late night spot. Definitely hits the spot at the end of the night. To me, the amount of food you get for the price could be improved but I would not say that I feel ripped off. The amount of food you get is fair but I think it'd be easier to justify if you got a little more. 

There's plenty of seating. Despite being near a whole bunch of bar/club scenes, once you're inside it's easy to take a break and have a nice conversation. It is all very clean and well kept. The servers are quick and friendly. When I went there were only two guys working but they weren't busy so it didn't take too long. The entire restaurant is very dimly lit and the atmosphere is a bit of a hodgepodge of things. On one wall there is a mural of outer space and the music that plays seems to have no rhyme or reason to it. 

It's a bit of a strange place but I would definitely go back.
Help me polish this:
The food at this place was decent, although not exceptional. It had a typical Mediterranean food truck taste that I've experienced before. It makes for a nice option for a late-night meal, satisfying cravings after a night out. While I feel that the portion sizes could be better for the price, I can't say that I felt cheated. The amount of food served is fair, but a little more would make it more worthwhile.

This spot offers ample seating, which is surprising given its proximity to various bars and clubs. Once inside, it's a welcoming environment where you can easily take a break and enjoy a pleasant conversation. The restaurant maintains a high level of cleanliness and upkeep, creating a comfortable dining experience. The servers are prompt and friendly. During my visit, only two staff members were working, but they managed to provide quick service as there weren't many customers. The entire place is dimly lit, and the eclectic mix of décor contributes to its quirky ambiance. With a space mural on one wall and a seemingly random selection of music playing, it's an interesting combination.

Overall, despite its peculiar atmosphere, I would definitely consider revisiting this place.

input:
When giving friends from out of town a tour of the French Quarter, one can only expect they want some classic New Orleans dishes. I've been here a couple of times, but they were the ones that wanted to go, due to their lunch special. It's a nice, well know restaurant that offers a 17.00 lunch special that includes a soup or salad, entree, and the option for a 4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. I got the Bloody Mary and it was a great size for the price. It was spicy and hit the spot.
They text message you when your table is ready, so were able to walk around the quarter while we waited. Thank god a lot of restaurants are getting rid of the those buzzers that make you feel like you are under house arrest. 
We sat down to a beautiful table right by the open shutters. The servers, were ok. They were busy, but forgot a couple of things we asked for. It was still a great experience though!
I got the pork chop with red beans and the turtle soup. The turtle soup was one of the best I have had. The pork chop was cooked to perfection and the read beans were seasoned very well. It came with cornbread, but it was very dry. After this lunch at noon, I didn't find myself hungry till it was basically time for bed. It was a very generous portion and well worth the money.

Muriel's is a great way to get a classic, good quality New Orleans meal at a decent price. The location is spectacular, and the history behind the restaurant made for great conversation at the table.
Definitely check it out if you are in the Quarter!
Help me polish this:
When giving friends from out of town a tour of the French Quarter, it's expected that they would want to try some classic New Orleans dishes. I've been to Muriel's a couple of times before, but this time it was my friends who insisted we go, primarily because of their lunch special. Muriel's is a well-known restaurant that offers a $17.00 lunch special, which includes a choice of soup or salad, an entree, and the option for a $4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. I decided to go for the Bloody Mary, and it turned out to be a great deal. The drink was perfectly spicy and really hit the spot.

One thing I really appreciated about Muriel's is that they text you when your table is ready, so we were able to explore the quarter while we waited. It was a relief to see that they don't use those annoying buzzers that make you feel like you're under house arrest. 

Once we were seated, we were lucky enough to get a beautiful table right by the open shutters. The servers, however, were just okay. They seemed quite busy and forgot a couple of things we asked for, but it didn't dampen our overall experience.

For my main course, I ordered the pork chop with red beans and also tried the turtle soup. The turtle soup was hands-down one of the best I've ever had - it had fantastic flavor and was incredibly well-prepared. The pork chop was also cooked to perfection and the red beans were seasoned wonderfully. The only disappointment was the cornbread, which was a little dry. 

After this hearty lunch at noon, I surprisingly didn't find myself feeling hungry until it was almost bedtime. The portions were very generous, and for the price, it was definitely worth it.

I highly recommend Muriel's for anyone looking to experience a classic, high-quality New Orleans meal at an affordable price. The restaurant's location is truly spectacular, and the history behind it made for great conversation at the table. If you're in the French Quarter, make sure to check it out!

input: We stopped here's on the recommendation of our shuttle driver.  The red velvet ice cream is wonderful!! Pieces of cake. Creamy goodness.  Yum!
Help me polish this: We decided to make a stop based on our shuttle driver's recommendation, and boy, were we glad we did! The red velvet ice cream here is absolutely incredible! Indulging in this creamy goodness feels like heaven. The addition of cake pieces takes it to a whole new level of yum!

input:
I ate here for the first time today.  The woman that works behind the counter is really friendly and offered to waive the minimum credit order amount ($7), since I work nearby.

The food itself is pretty average for American-Chinese food.  Nothing great, but not bad either.  My sauce was greasy, but the food in general doesn't seem to be (e.g. fried rice).  They do have some vegetarian options which are of the tofu variety as opposed to fake meat. 

I would go back since they have lunch specials that come with rice and either a drink, soup, or egg roll ($5.75).

EDIT: I got super sick after leaving this review, and I'm 99% sure it was food poisoning.  Will not be returning.
Help me polish this:
I had my first dining experience here today, and I must say, the woman working behind the counter was extremely friendly. She even offered to waive the minimum credit order amount of $7 since I work nearby.

As for the food, it's fairly average for American-Chinese cuisine. It neither wowed me nor disappointed me. Although the sauce I had was a bit greasy, the overall food seemed to be fine, especially dishes like fried rice. Additionally, they have a decent selection of vegetarian options, which are primarily tofu-based rather than using mock meats.

Considering the affordable lunch specials that include rice and a choice of drink, soup, or egg roll for just $5.75, I would definitely consider returning.

However, an update: Unfortunately, I fell ill shortly after leaving this review, and I strongly suspect it was due to food poisoning. Therefore, I will not be revisiting this establishment.

input:
Delicious! 

I wish they took reservations, but my friend and her fiance go there nice and early so that we could snag a seat inside (it was cold out!). 

We ordered the bianco salad ( to share between 2) and the western addition (to share between 4).

I thought the salad was tasty but nothing special, despite the white chocolate shavings. Cute idea, but not enough crunch or pizazz to make the salad seem really fabulous.

The pizza, however, was pretty darn good. We ordered it deep dish to try their special cornmeal crust and were pretty impressed. 
The crust tastes a little bit like cornbread, a little bit like pizza dough, a tiny bit like grease (the good kind) and a lot like YUM!

I don't know if it was the best pizza I've ever had, but it was very good. It would be even better if it were a tad cheaper, and didn't get so crowded! But definitely worth a visit if you're in the area!
Help me polish this:
Delightful! Although it's a shame that they don't take reservations, my friend and her fiance were wise to arrive early, securing us a cozy seat indoors as it was chilly outside.

To start, we opted for the bianco salad to share between the two of us, and the western addition pizza to share amongst the four of us. The salad, while tasty, didn't quite hit the mark for me. Despite the inventive addition of white chocolate shavings, it lacked the desired crunch and pizazz that would have made it truly fabulous.

On the other hand, the pizza truly impressed us. We decided to go for the deep dish option and were pleasantly surprised by their special cornmeal crust. It possessed a distinctive blend of cornbread and pizza dough flavors, with just a hint of delicious grease (the good kind). In short, it was an absolute delight!

While I can't declare it the best pizza I've ever had, it certainly ranks high on my list. Perhaps if it were slightly more affordable and the establishment less crowded, the experience would be even better. Nevertheless, if you happen to be in the area, I highly recommend paying them a visit!

input: A downtown without a bookstore is like a downtown without... I don't know I lost the metaphor. It's just sad is what it is. You need books, you need a place to browse, talk with other book lovers, and listen to book readings. Indy Reads is that place. And it's more than that because all proceeds support a great cause, adult literacy. Most of the books are used so donate a book and pick up a new (used) one. You may be surprised at all the books they have that you didn't even know you wanted. They also have a small selection of new books. If they don't have what you're looking for, you can order it. The one thing I don't really like is that the $1 children's books can be jammed so tightly that it's hard to look through them. The kids books are also arranged by color, which makes it harder for me to distinguish between titles as I glance through. Prices are excellent throughout, and the space is really nice. Check it out!
Help me polish this:
A downtown without a bookstore is like a downtown without a heart. It's a void that leaves us longing for the magic of exploration and community that only books can bring. Thankfully, Indy Reads is here to fill that void and more. Not only does it provide a place to find and discover books, but it also serves as a hub for bibliophiles to connect, exchange ideas, and immerse themselves in the world of literature.

What sets Indy Reads apart is its commitment to supporting a noble cause – adult literacy. By shopping at Indy Reads, you become an advocate for education and empowerment. The majority of the books available are used, allowing for a sustainable cycle of donating and acquiring new (used) treasures. In fact, you might be pleasantly surprised by the vast selection of books they offer – ones you didn't even realize you were missing from your collection. They even have a curated selection of new books for those seeking fresh additions to their libraries.

However, it's important to note that the organization's children's books section could use some improvement. While the $1 price tag is enticing, the books are often crammed together, making it difficult to peruse through them effortlessly. Additionally, arranging them by color can be confusing when trying to quickly identify specific titles. Despite this minor drawback, Indy Reads makes up for it with affordable pricing and a welcoming atmosphere.

Take the opportunity to visit Indy Reads and experience the joy of being surrounded by books. It's a delightful haven where you can lose yourself in fascinating stories, engage in lively discussions with fellow book lovers, and even attend captivating book readings. So come and be part of this vibrant literary community, supporting an important cause while indulging in the pleasures of reading.

input: Wish I would have came on Yelp and read the previous reviews, it would've saved me a lot of time and frustration. I ran in today to see if someone could take a look at my right passenger front wheel. My tire pressure light was on and I noticed a piece of tire was lifted. I go in and he tells me it's a couple hours wait. Ok, I'll give you that I just showed up so the wait thing is to be expected. I ask the guy if I can make an appointment to come back. He says its first come first serve. Really? When I've made appts previously with other Just Tires? Why not just say you don't want my service? Bottom line? Guy was rude and lacked any customer service. Went down the street to Mr. Tire and was in and out with a replaced new tire in half an hour. Oh, and they appeared WAY busier based on the waiting area and cars in the garage.
Help me polish this: I wish I had come across the previous reviews on Yelp before visiting this place. It would have saved me a significant amount of time and frustration. I went there today to have my right passenger front wheel inspected as my tire pressure light was on, and I noticed a portion of the tire was lifted. Upon arrival, I was informed that the wait time would be a couple of hours. While I understand that I didn't have an appointment and the wait is reasonable, I asked if I could schedule an appointment for a later time. Surprisingly, I was told that they operate on a first-come, first-served basis. This deviated from my previous experiences at other Just Tires locations where I was able to schedule appointments. It felt like they simply didn't want my business. The bottom line is that the staff member I interacted with displayed rudeness and a complete lack of customer service skills. As a result, I decided to go to Mr. Tire down the street and was pleasantly surprised at their efficiency. Within half an hour, they had replaced my tire, and their waiting area and garage were visibly busier.

input:
I gave it one star because it doesn't give me an option to give it zero. This place sucks. Where should I start?? Okay, arrived at 7 pm with reservations and was seated in the dungeon. Fine. We ordered queso fundido with chorizo and got a weird looking cheese skillet with tortillas NOT chips. Odd! So had to ask for chips. Should've asked for a trash can. Ed's is huge. If you've ever been on a cruise ship, Ed's has a variety of activity spaces, restaurant, bars and lounges under one roof. 

It's endless entertainment. You could probably float around here for a whole week and never get bored. There is a pool room, video games, bowling, a dance area, restaurants, lounges, a stage and much more around every corner you turn. It's a good place for young kids and birthday parties once you're too old for Chucky Cheese. 

Although I've personally never seen a band here my partner has, and it's not that expensive to see good bands like Ween, Jurassic Five or Interpol. The venue's neither big or small, so Ed's can host lesser known but interesting musicians as they can sell upwards of 600 tickets. So for bands that aren't popular enough to fill the Coliseum, Ed's still helps them establish a presence in E-town.

input:
They used to make an Amiga bowl that had an abundance of shredded grilled chicken on the bottom of a flour tortilla bowl, a layer of rice topped with grilled onions and peppers with a queso sauce drizzeled over the top.
Tonight there was no rice nor any shredded chicken, it had been replaced with chicken crisps. They are the outer parts of a grilled chicken breast with no moisture and very few of them.
Having met the owner in the past and having his wife wait on me I knew something wasn't right.
I explained to the waitress that this dish had changed and wasn't good! She politely offered something else. What to order...if they had modified a basic dish what was next?
To my surprise a male manager came out and "informed" me that this is exactly what they had been serving for 10 years and I must have either special ordered something or was mistaken.
I said this is not what they had served me for the past 5 years and I never had requested a special order before. 
I also asked what they had done to the phenominal soft tacos? They were usually served in a soft warm flour tortilla and had moisture and flavor. Tonight they were stale and crisp and the filing was bland.  Again he informed me I was mistaken while he held my order that had been sent back to the kitchen in front of me.
I apologized and said I didn't wish for anything else, thank you.
Another manager came out a few moments later apologizing and stated that they are unfamiliar with what I had ordered and would "special order" anything I wanted. I declined.
Apparently their cook walked out tonight and they were winging it.
Too bad it was a good place to get a good mexican meal.
Two thumbs down on Poblano's.

I came in with high hopes and left with slight disappointment. 

Our server was super attentive, and very friendly; however I feel like the food was disappointing. Our egg drop soup came out right away at a nice piping hot temperature and when the rest of our food came out it was practically room temperature. 

Feeling adventurous, I had ordered the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts entree with brown rice while he ordered the Sesame Chicken platter. I like the idea of sharing food, but my food was too busy all on its own without adding something else to the mix. The brown rice was cold and very bland while the shrimp was overly sweet and I didn't feel like the candied walnuts and melon balls were complementary flavors.

The chocolate cake we had for dessert was amazing though; 6 layers of chocolate on chocolate. It was so sweet and rich, we ended up sharing a slice.

So to sum up, service was great, dessert was great, but the food needs some work. Sorry PF Changs, I just am not impressed.

One thing I will note (that our server told us) is that they are very big on catering to food allergies (especially gluten).

input:
On a recent trip to Port Richey, I selected Holiday Inn Express for a couple of reasons.  The main reason was the option of two beds (as I was sharing the room with my brother).  The other reasons were:  price, vicinity to my aunt's home and complementary breakfast. 

My family and I typically stay at the Hyatt Place/House when we're traveling.  However, since it was just my brother and I, I figured we'd give Holiday Inn a shot. 

+  The staff were very friendly and helpful.
+  Free wifi.
+  Breakfast was very good, offering both hot and cold entrees. 

-  Sadly, the beds were WAY TOO soft.  It felt as if the mattresses were past their life expectancy.  As a result, I didn't really sleep well for most of my three nights there.
-  The a/c was hit and miss with the lack of reliable thermostat controls. 

There was a pool and hot tub, but since I didn't utilize either, it wouldn't be fair to rate them.  There also a small gym that I didn't use either. 

All in all, it was just ok.  Hyatt has spoiled me.
Help me polish this:
During my recent trip to Port Richey, I opted for Holiday Inn Express for a few reasons. Firstly, I needed a room with two beds as my brother accompanied me. Additionally, the price was reasonable, it was conveniently located near my aunt's place, and they offered a complimentary breakfast.

Normally, my family and I prefer staying at the Hyatt Place/House while traveling. However, since it was just my brother and me, I decided to give Holiday Inn a try.

There were several positives to highlight about my stay. The staff at Holiday Inn Express were extremely friendly and helpful. We also appreciated the fact that they offered free wifi, which was a nice amenity. Moreover, the breakfast provided a good variety of hot and cold options, making it a satisfying start to the day.

However, I do have a couple of criticisms. Firstly, the beds were excessively soft and it seemed like the mattresses were overdue for replacement. Consequently, I struggled to get a comfortable night's sleep during most of my three-night stay. Secondly, the air conditioning was unreliable due to the inconsistent thermostat controls.

Although there were amenities like a pool, hot tub, and small gym available, I didn't have the opportunity to utilize them. Therefore, I cannot provide a fair rating for those facilities.

Overall, I would say my experience at Holiday Inn Express was just average. The excellent service and complimentary amenities were overshadowed by the discomfort caused by the worn-out mattresses and inconsistent air conditioning. Hyatt has certainly set high standards that I have grown accustomed to.

input: The staff wasn't too interested in helping customers, instead focused on the TV in the lobby, flirting with each other and just standing around. I found the food to be ok, not great, not terrible. I'll round up from the 1.5 I give them.

input:

input:
do not eat here. my husband, two friends and i went out for restaurant week to marmont steakhouse on saturday, january 26, 2013; our experience was horrific.  the four of us ordered the crab bisque soup for our first course, it was cold and we sent it back to be reheated.  my second course was the calamari it was bland, fried too hard and rubbery.  finally two ppl from our party ordered the lobster ravioli for an entree.  it was not lobster ravioli but beef. i asked our waiter and one other waiter to please double check with the chef because this is not lobster, i expressed that i have not eaten beef or pork since 1994, and that it would make me ill. they both came back separately and argued that it was in fact lobster. another party of maybe 6 ppl ordered the lobster ravioli, they had the same problem and sent their dishes back to the kitchen too.  the server finally came over after i'd eaten two of the ravioli to apologize for the kitchens error and telling us that was in fact beef. 
i have been in the bathroom all day with diarrhea from the beef ravioli! the staff was very nonchalant about it and offered an insincere apology.
Help me polish this:
"Do not dine at this establishment. My husband, two friends, and I had an absolutely terrible experience at Marmont Steakhouse during restaurant week on Saturday, January 26, 2013. It was a complete nightmare.

To start, all four of us ordered the crab bisque soup as our first course. Shockingly, it arrived at our table cold. We had to send it back to be reheated. Not a promising beginning.

Moving on to the calamari, which was my second course. It was incredibly bland, fried to the point of being overly crispy, and had a rubbery texture. Definitely not the calamari I was expecting.

But the worst part came when two people in our group ordered the lobster ravioli for our main course. To our dismay, what arrived on our plates was not lobster ravioli, but beef. Concerned, I immediately called the attention of our waiter and another staff member, asking them to kindly double-check with the chef. I made it clear that I have abstained from eating beef and pork since 1994 due to dietary restrictions, and consuming it would make me ill. Astonishingly, they both argued vehemently, insisting that it was indeed lobster. 

Our disbelief grew even further when another table, consisting of approximately six people, also ordered the lobster ravioli and encountered the same problem. Their dishes were also sent back to the kitchen. It wasn't until later, after I had already consumed two of the ravioli, that our server finally approached us to apologize for the kitchen's error, admitting that it was, in fact, beef.

The consequences of this mistake have been unbearable. I have been suffering from severe diarrhea all day as a result of consuming the beef ravioli. Despite our distress, the staff displayed a nonchalant attitude and offered an insincere apology that did little to rectify the situation.

I urge you to steer clear of this establishment. They clearly lack proper attention to detail, disregard dietary restrictions, and possess an alarming level of indifference towards the well-being of their patrons."

input:
I went here on a Wednesday night and, though it wasn't busy, there were no open tables without a reservation,  except the tall tables in the bar area. It still seemed to be a very quiet place anyway. 

The location is not attractive, the street is dark and mostly empty at night, but the inside is stylish in a masculine, refined sort of way; dark wood, low light, maps on the walls and prints of watercolors depicting old Missouri scenes. It was a great place for a quiet, intimate dinner. They've got a couple of TVs up above the bar. 

They seemed very well staffed, as if each table had its own server. 

The menu is one page but very intriguing, I had so many questions for our server about "what is this?" and "what is that?" and he was totally nice and knowledgeable about the menu items. He seemed nervous and unsure at first, but he was friendly and made sure to check on us frequently. 

We decided to split 3 small plates and a side dish between the two of us and, honestly, it was a little too much food for just two people. Perhaps we don't have hearty enough appetites.

Their menu is so varied and interesting, it's really all over the map in terms of seasonings and ethnic origins but the main focus seems to be rustic and warming - at least at this time of year. I have a feeling they may change it up from time to time. I'm sure you'll get things here you won't find anywhere else. The prices are very reasonable, considering the planning and good execution of the food. You'd certainly find more expensive, and less original places in Clayton and down town. 

We ordered the smoked trout, the venison hot dogs, the mini monte cristo sandwiches, and the french fries. 

The venison hot dogs and the smoked trout were fantastic and interesting. The french fries were very well made, and the dipping sauces delicious. I was so impressed with these that I was then a bit underwhelmed by the mini monte cristos. Since everything else there seemed to have a unique spin on it, I expected them to do something original here as well, but they were just like any monte cristo you might have. They were very tasty of course, but nothing new. 

With the food plus two draft beers, our total was $52.05 before tip and we were stuffed and satisfied. I applaud them!
Help me polish this:
I visited this restaurant on a quiet Wednesday night and, although it wasn't crowded, finding a table without a reservation was a challenge, except for the tall tables in the bar area. Despite this, the ambiance remained serene.

The location, though unappealing with its dark and mostly empty street, contrasts with the stylish and refined interior. Dark wood, subdued lighting, maps on the walls, and watercolor prints depicting old Missouri scenes create an attractive, masculine vibe. It proved to be a perfect spot for a quiet and intimate dinner, albeit with a couple of televisions positioned above the bar.

The restaurant appeared to have a well-staffed team; it felt as though each table had its dedicated server.

The menu, though concise, intrigued me greatly. I bombarded our server with questions about various items, and he was both knowledgeable and gracious in his responses. While he initially seemed nervous and unsure, he soon warmed up, frequently checking on us throughout the evening.

Since we couldn't decide on a single dish, we opted to share three small plates and a side. Surprisingly, the portion sizes were more generous than anticipated, and it ended up being too much food for just the two of us. Perhaps our appetites were not as hearty as we thought.

The menu boasts a diverse and fascinating selection, offering a mix of seasonings and ethnic influences. The emphasis appeared to be on rustic and comforting fare, especially during this time of year. However, it's likely that they change their offerings periodically. Expect to find unique dishes here that can't be found elsewhere. Considering the thoughtfulness and quality of the food, the prices are remarkably reasonable, especially when compared to more expensive and less innovative establishments in Clayton and downtown.

We ordered the smoked trout, venison hot dogs, mini Monte Cristo sandwiches, and french fries.

The venison hot dogs and smoked trout were both outstanding and intriguing. The french fries were skillfully prepared, and the accompanying dipping sauces were delicious. These dishes left quite an impression, which made me somewhat underwhelmed by the mini Monte Cristos. Given the restaurant's penchant for putting a unique spin on their offerings, I expected some creativity with this dish as well, but they were simply regular Monte Cristo sandwiches. While still tasty, they didn't offer anything new.

Including two draft beers, our bill came to $52.05 before tip, and we left feeling satisfied and pleasantly full. I commend the restaurant for their quality and value.

input:
It is typical Broad Ripple charming spot. Small, trendy and bustling with activity. They do not take reservations. Which is somewhat annoying when you are traveling from another part of town. Whatever, we just had to arrange to arrive earlier than we would have liked to hopefully secure a table, which we did. When we arrived it was quiet and only several tables had guests seated. As our dinner progressed it became more crowded until every seat was filled. Nice lively scene except then you can not hear squat! It made dinner conversation difficult. Boo!!!! I think this could be an easy fix for them. 

Meal/Drinks:  The cocktails were creative and tasted wonderful. Our servers suggestions were pretty spot on as we enjoyed most of her suggestions. 

The guacamole was very good with the exception of the fact that my friend has a nut allergy and we asked to have them left off and of coarse they arrived with them on! They really weren't necessary in my opinion either as I don't think they add much to the dish. The reason I wanted to try this restaurant- The Harvest salad! We all split this as well and it was good. The combination of fruit and root vegetables was delish! The figs were so good and the herbed goat cheese mouse was a highlight on this plate!

Two of us ordered the Veracruz Trigger fish and the other ordered the Serrano Scallops and all of it was wonderful. The white sweet mashed potatoes were interesting! I am glad we tried them. The Veracruz sauce was wonderful and full of flavor. It was a lot of food though. Had we known we would have probably skipped one of the first course selections or split an entree. That'a ok though- lunch for today :)

We also tried the Tostones and Stewed Black Beans. Beans were very good, full of flavor! Tostones seemed very dry but maybe that is what they are supposed to be- this is the first time I have had them. BUT, dipped in the Stewed Black Beans they tasted great!

We passed on dessert as they had no gluten free, dairy free options. Delicia offers many options for restricted diets, which we loved. Just no dessert, which is probably better anyway-we were so full! 

Go, you will not be disappointed. Just go before 7pm on a Friday night to ensure a table.

input:
This makes my 6th or 7th time to Jackson's in the last 2 years and I thought that after tonight's visit they deserved a review. 

I had the panini Reuben.  Panini was amazing. Great use of garlic. Loved the cut of the meat. Not stringy but nicely chinked in thin slices. Cheese was well melted throughout the mix of kraut and meat. Rye Bread was wonderful. Would love to have it as a staple in my house. 

Salad came out same time as sandwich which was not good.

Presentation was a little sloppy. 

Like every other place I have had a panini (except Panera where they do it right), the sandwich was served directly on a plate. Why don't they serve on a napkin? Particularly when they bring the salad out at the same time as the sandwich?  If the sandwich sits for more than a few moments, the bread gets soggy from the steam.  Nothing serious, but for the price, which is a little high, it seems lacking.  While the price is a little high, i think it is justified considering the food and drink quality. 

They have a great selection of wines and beers that are likely to fit any palette.  

Wait staff have always been friendly. But you can tell this is a place where people are expected to hustle. Sometimes short or even distracted the service can be lacking. 

The second time I visited was during a medium lunch rush and the wait time was 15 min to get drinks. My trip tonight it was about 8 min. For a sat night this is not bad. But not great either. My bartenders were awesome and never left me wanting (except for getting my salad with the main course).

Overall a good experience and I will be back.

input:
I went there for a pedicure and gel manicure.  It was my first time and the reviews was what enticed me. I loved loved Young, who did my pedicure.  She was very friendly and has a very positive attitude.  She took her time with my pedicure and was very thorough with the massaging (which was the best part). 

Unfortunately Young didn't do my manicure.   I had a gel manicure that needed to be soaked off.  The owner did my nails.  She first scraped my nails with the cuticle pusher, but when it wasn't coming off fast enough, she used the drill.  I was really worried as I didn't want my nails to be thin.  But I just let her do her thing.  I'm usually not picky so when she was working on my nails I didn't watch what she was doing until I realized after close examination she didn't fully take the old gel polish off.  
Not only that, the polish didn't go on smoothly, there's are noticeable bumps on my nail bed and the sides of my nails weren't even fully covered.  

I am so disappointed.  I love Young, but I don't know if I'll be going back due to my experience with my gel manicure.

However, my gel manicure was not as satisfying. Instead of Young, the owner performed the manicure. She initially scraped my nails with a cuticle pusher, but when that method proved to be too slow, she resorted to using a drill. Although I was concerned about the potential thinning of my nails, I trusted her expertise and allowed her to proceed.

Admittedly, I should have been more attentive to the process, but I only realized after a closer examination that the old gel polish hadn't been completely removed. As someone who is usually not picky, I am extremely disappointed with the outcome. While I highly appreciate Young's skill and service, I am uncertain whether I will return to this salon due to my unsatisfactory experience with the gel manicure.

input:
This is a cool place.  I wonder how many people know that an Ouzaria is?  The ambience here is definitely upbeat - I'd rate it a great place for a group or first date.  They have a couple of semi-secluded tables in the back room that keeps it from getting too loud, but it's not a quiet romantic place.  

We brought my Mother-in-Law, who enjoys good food as long as it's not too weird.  I guess my wife is about the same, now that I think about it.  We tried three tapas plates; a three-cheese sampler, featuring feta, goat cheese and kasseri cheese, greek meatballs and pan-seared scallops.  We liked all three of these dishes.  The scallops were especially good - big and tender.   For tapas, they were pretty big portions, so keep this in mind.  The waitress suggested ordering one thing at a time, but we didn't heed her advice and ordered it all up front.   Two at a time would probably be a good idea.  Along with the tapas, we ordered a traditional Greek salad, which ended up being the lone clunker, surprisingly.  We just didn't like the dressing - too sweet for our tastes.  The gyro meat was fine, though, so maybe we'll just get a gyro next time.   One more thing:  The Spanish granacha (can't remember the label) was excellent for just $6 and a nice pour. 

Okay, now for the belly dancer:  She was cute and a good dancer, but I think this is just something that requires more alcohol on my part.  We did have a few laughs about it, though.  I opted not to get a dollar out to stuff in her skirt or whatever.   Fun but a little awkward. 

I've been to a few other Greek places in town that had better food, but for a night out, Momo's is definitely the choice.  We'll be back.

Help me polish this: If you're in search of authentic Italian food products, look no further than Claudio's. This place is the epitome of old-school Italian culture and family. input:
This hotel was so terrible and I can narrow it down to 4 things:

1. The price: Expect to pay a lot of money from the second you arrive. They charge $35 per person for a round trip shuttle ride to the airport. Our room was roughly $275 a night. It's an incredibly large hotel that offers a nail salon, a Godiva Chocolate store, about 9 restaurants and a few bars. But you'll pay dearly for any of those things - like $2.50 for a small bottle of soda. The hotel is designed to keep you in there and they charge you $15 for a round trip shuttle ride to the downtown Nashville area. 

2. The service: We called the front desk and were on hold for 20 minutes. We went to the front desk and waited in line for an hour. We waited around to ask the concierge questions. And each time we got, "I don't know" as the usual response. The cleaning staff was extraordinarily loud and they actually shouted as they went down the hall at 6:30 a.m.

3. The name: They call this place a resort but that is, by far, a misnomer. This place is a convention hotel, period. It's horrifically loud at all hours of the day because they host about 3 conventions at one time. Our windows faced one of the courtyards and there is music pumping there 24 hours a day. The walls are thin and you can hear *everything* happening in the neighboring rooms. (eww!) If you want to relax at a resort, don't stay here because with all those convention people, loud cleaning staff, 24 hour music and thin walls you will only end up with more stress.

4. The size: It's no joke that you will get lost in this hotel. It's inexplicably large. And when it hits noon, you should already be in one of the few restaurants because they fill up FAST. With several conventions happening at one time, getting a "quick bite" is not possible here. And there's not really any place close by, either. You can walk over to the mall for some fast food but plan enough time for your walk - getting out of the hotel takes at least 5 minutes.

I'm sure glad I was there for a convention and didn't pay out of my own pocket for this ridiculous hotel.
Help me polish this:
This hotel left a lot to be desired, and I can easily pinpoint four major issues:

1. Exorbitant prices: From the moment you arrive, expect to pay a hefty amount. They charge a whopping $35 per person for a round trip shuttle ride to the airport, and the room rate is around $275 per night. Despite offering an array of amenities, such as a nail salon, Godiva Chocolate store, multiple restaurants, and bars, you'll pay a premium for everything - even a small bottle of soda costs $2.50. Furthermore, the hotel charges $15 for a round trip shuttle ride to downtown Nashville, seemingly designed to keep guests confined within its premises.

2. Disappointing service: Our experience with the front desk was frustrating, as we were left on hold for 20 minutes when calling, and waiting in line for an hour at the physical desk. The concierge was equally unhelpful, often responding with a shrug and an "I don't know" to our inquiries. To add to the frustration, the cleaning staff was incredibly loud, shouting as they moved down the hallway as early as 6:30 a.m.

3. Misleading branding: Despite being labeled as a resort, this place is far from it. In reality, it functions primarily as a convention hotel, constantly hosting multiple conventions simultaneously. As a result, it is relentlessly noisy, with music blaring in the courtyards 24/7. The thin walls amplify all the noise from neighboring rooms, which can be quite unpleasant. If you're seeking a peaceful and relaxing resort experience, this is definitely not the place to stay, as the continuous presence of convention-goers, loud cleaning staff, non-stop music, and thin walls only contribute to stress.

4. Overwhelming size: Prepare to get lost in this massive hotel - it's truly bewildering. By noon, the few restaurants within the premises are already filled up, and due to the numerous conventions happening concurrently, grabbing a quick bite is nearly impossible. Moreover, there aren't many dining options in close proximity either. While there is a mall nearby offering fast food, even reaching it from the hotel takes at least 5 minutes, so adequate time must be allocated.

Fortunately, I attended a convention and didn't have to bear the expense of this absurd hotel out of my own pocket.

input:
I waited a long time to finally try this place and I have to say I was let down a bit. I tried the mandatory Dan Dan noodles. They were very flavorful and not too spicy. Nothing mind blowing here just a really good lo mein or spicy pasta dish with virtually no protein more or less. Also had the scallion pancakes. I was just in Chinatown recently at a place I also reviewed (first person from Yelp to do so) and they were way better there. ( I highly recommend you try that place) These were more like quesadillas laying flat where as the other ones jumped off the plate and were so much more crispy and substantial. The last appetizer I had was the Wontons in Chilli oil. These were just not good to me at all and one bite was all I needed. Basically it is steamed Wontons in a bowl with the soup being the chilli oil. Just heavy heavy choking heat with very little substance or taste. Take those same homemade wontons and pan fry them with some chilli peppers and a nice light sauce and you have could a real winner but I digress. Finally we tried the Talapia Medallions . These were fried to perfection but there were some greens mixed in that I could not chew through and had to discard via the old napkin trick which to me is a bit of a deal/star breaker.

The service was very good and the atmosphere very nice but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here again. All I could think about was how much more I prefer Cantonese style where its all about flavors and you can add heat as you like it. I'm sure I could find better authentic Szechuan cuisine that better suits my taste just not here. It feels very commercialized and Americanized. I prefer the hole in the wall places where I am the only caucasian in the place a heck of a lot more.
Help me polish this:
I was disappointed with my long-awaited visit to this place. The mandatory Dan Dan noodles were flavorful but not outstanding. It felt more like a good lo mein or spicy pasta dish rather than an exceptional Szechuan dish with minimal protein. I also tried the scallion pancakes, which were far better at another Chinatown establishment that I recently reviewed on Yelp (I highly recommend you try that place). Unlike the flat and lackluster ones here, the other pancakes were crispy, substantial, and truly appetizing.

I also had the Wontons in Chili oil for an appetizer, but they were a letdown. One bite was enough for me. The steamed wontons were drowned in chili oil, resulting in overwhelming heat that lacked substance and flavor. Pan-frying the homemade wontons with chili peppers and a light sauce would have made a real winner. Moving on, the Talapia Medallions were fried to perfection, but unfortunately, there were some greens mixed in that were impossible to chew through. I had to resort to the old napkin trick to discreetly discard them, which was quite disappointing and somewhat of a deal breaker for me.

While the service was excellent and the atmosphere pleasant, I don't think I would make a special trip to dine here again. I couldn't help but compare it to Cantonese-style cuisine, which focuses more on flavors and allows you to adjust the heat according to your preference. I'm confident I can find a better, more authentic Szechuan experience that suits my taste elsewhere. This place feels too commercialized and Americanized for my liking. I much prefer the charm and authenticity of hole-in-the-wall establishments where I'm often the only Caucasian diner.

You should definitely go there. It's an awesome place. Just make sure to arrive early and wear comfortable, loose pants.

input: Please, this place makes a semi-new menu and raised their prices. input:
This update (and upgrade) to my review of Khyber is long overdue!

I think the most ringing summary is that I have since moved ~1 mile further away from the Khyber, and I still go there just as often.  I have now sampled most of the menu, but the truly excellent Southern barbecue is what usually calls to me.  You can't go wrong whether you pick the brisket, the ribs, the chicken, the pulled pork or a combo of the above.  Their mac and cheese remains my favorite side, and the addition of the very good coleslaw rounds out the experience.

I love the vibe of Kyber.  It usually pretty full, but they usually seem to have a table available for me (Yay!).  It is often loud, but never quite so loud that I wish it were quieter.  The staff is very knowledgeable, and happy to provide beer recommendations and taste tests of drafts.  They Khyber also manages to hit that sweet spot where I never end up being the most or least intoxicated person there!
Help me polish this:
This update (and upgrade) to my review of Khyber is long overdue!

In a nutshell, despite my recent move ~1 mile further away from the Khyber, my frequent visits remain unchanged. Exploring most of their menu, I have come to realize that their Southern barbecue is truly exceptional and always calls to me. Whether you go for the delectable brisket, mouthwatering ribs, flavorful chicken, succulent pulled pork, or a combination of these options, you can't go wrong. The mac and cheese remains my ultimate favorite side dish, and their addition of the fantastic coleslaw perfectly complements the overall experience.

One of the aspects I adore about Khyber is its vibrant atmosphere. Even though it's usually bustling with customers, I've never struggled to find an available table (Yay!). While it tends to be lively, it never reaches a point where I yearn for a quieter setting. The staff is incredibly attentive and knowledgeable, always ready to offer beer recommendations or even provide taste tests of their draft selections. What impresses me further is how Khyber strikes the perfect balance—nobody there seems excessively intoxicated or completely sober, making it a great place to unwind.

input: Great  breads especially the German rye. My favorite breakfast is the poached eggs, cooked perfectly. For lunch, I go for the eggplant panini or  Laurie's salad.
Help me polish this:
I absolutely love indulging in an assortment of bakes, but one of my all-time favorites has to be the delightful German rye. Its distinct flavor and texture make it a remarkable choice for any occasion. 

When it comes to breakfast, there's nothing quite like a plate of perfectly poached eggs to start the day on a delicious note. The combination of a gently cooked egg with its silky yolk oozing out harmoniously pairs with any type of bread, and German rye takes it to another level of satisfaction. 

For a fulfilling lunch, I often find myself gravitating towards the eggplant panini or Laurie's salad. The tantalizing blend of flavors and textures in the panini, with its roasted eggplant, savory fillings, and toasted bread, creates a mouthwatering experience. Alternatively, Laurie's salad offers a refreshing and wholesome option to satisfy your midday cravings. Its vibrant assortment of fresh greens, crisp veggies, and delectable toppings provide a satisfying and nutritious meal. 

Indulging in great breads like the remarkable German rye, complemented by perfectly poached eggs for breakfast or tempting options like the eggplant panini and Laurie's salad for lunch, makes for an exquisite gastronomic experience.

input: Tony's really has surprisingly good Mexican food, which you wouldn't expect to find out here in Chalmette.  It's actually the best Mexican food I've had in Louisiana. input: Love the lamb gyros plate. It's a distance for me to drive, so sometimes I get an extra order to take back home.  The tiramisu is very good too. The dolmas are good but more vinegary than I prefer.  The Greek salad that comes with the entree' is good also.
Help me polish this: I absolutely love the lamb gyros plate at this restaurant. Although it's a bit of a distance for me to drive, I often find myself getting an extra order to take back home because it's just that delicious. Additionally, the tiramisu is simply mouthwatering. However, I must admit that the dolmas are slightly more vinegary than my personal preference. Nevertheless, the Greek salad that accompanies the main course is also quite enjoyable.

input: Love the yum yum club and macaroni salad is awesome too!! Sometimes service could be a little more friendly but besides that I continue to go back because price is right and good tastes great
Help me polish this: I absolutely adore the yum yum club and their macaroni salad is simply amazing! While it would be nice if the service was slightly friendlier, the affordable pricing and superb taste keep me coming back time and time again.

input:
This is my husbands and my first time here in Reno. Wow what a great hotel to stay in for your first time. We had a great room with a spa and the shower had a steam room feature. The hotel also offered many places to eat and relax. The casino was very clean and a joy to be in even if you don't gamble like myself. However I did win 41.00 with a 1.00 slot machine :)  we decided to venture out finally to see Reno. However, we weren't impressed with anything else but our great hotel.  Easy checkout right from the room was a time saver. Well now off to explore Reno some more.
If your considering a hotel that is nice, clean, up to date this is the one.
Help me polish this:
This is my husband's and my first time here in Reno, and wow, what a fantastic hotel to stay in for our first visit. We were thrilled to have a spacious room with a spa, and the shower even had a steam room feature. The hotel has a variety of dining options and plenty of places to unwind and relax. Even though I'm not a gambler, I thoroughly enjoyed the clean and delightful atmosphere of the casino. It's worth mentioning that I actually won $41.00 on a $1.00 slot machine!

When we finally decided to explore Reno, unfortunately, we weren't as impressed with everything else compared to our amazing hotel. Nevertheless, the hassle-free checkout right from our room was a time saver. Now, we're off to further explore Reno.

If you're looking for a nice, clean, and modern hotel, this is the perfect choice.

input: Studying previous  yelp reviews, we decided to take the kids to hibachi and sushi.  This place did not disappoint. The sushi was amazing and the hibachi was awesome. Help me polish this: After thoroughly reviewing past Yelp reviews, we made the decision to bring our kids to a hibachi and sushi restaurant. And let me tell you, this place exceeded all our expectations. The sushi was absolutely phenomenal, captivating our taste buds with every bite. The hibachi experience was equally remarkable and left us in awe. To conclude our outstanding dining adventure, we indulged in the delectable dessert of fried bananas paired with creamy ice cream, further enhancing our overall experience. The service was exceptional, with attentive staff members ensuring our satisfaction throughout the meal. Without a doubt, we will be eagerly returning for more unforgettable dining experiences.

input: I Love it here. The pizza is fantastic,  and the staff is very friendly. It's a great place to hang out with friends and family.
Help me polish this: I absolutely adore this place! The pizza here is simply phenomenal, leaving my taste buds in a state of pure bliss. Moreover, the staff goes above and beyond, emanating such friendliness and warmth that it adds an extra layer of delight to the entire experience. It's an absolute haven to gather with loved ones, creating cherished memories and fostering a sense of togetherness.

input: Went here the other day with some friends for a bite and a drink. Service was great as where the drinks ;) Will definitely be back!
Help me polish this: I recently went to this place with some friends for a meal and drinks. The service was excellent, and the drinks were amazing! I had such a great experience that I'm definitely planning to return again in the future.

input: This place was on my list for all of the great reviews. The lamb was very flavorful, but the garlic Naan is just frozen from Trader Joe's. Also, the lamb was fairly expensive for the amount you get. Lastly, despite saying they take American Express at the door, the owner would not accept Amex. I will likely not return.
Help me polish this: This place had been highly recommended to me due to its great reviews. The lamb was indeed packed with flavor; however, the garlic Naan turned out to be disappointingly frozen from Trader Joe's. Additionally, the lamb dish seemed quite pricey considering the portion size. To add to my disappointment, despite the establishment displaying a sign indicating they accept American Express, the owner refused to honor it. Regrettably, I do not anticipate revisiting this establishment in the future.

input:
This little unassuming shop is tucked away in a strip mall full of furniture stores. Had it not been for Yelp, I would never have known it was here. Now, I won't be taking a trip to Brentwood without stopping for a scoop!

The flavors are quite varied and innovative. I had pumpkin and some sort of whipped cream cheese flavor--both were divine--which when mixed tasted just like pumpkin pie! The owner, Michael, is absolutely a sweetheart and is generous with the samples and the recommendations, and he's always coming up with new flavors to whip up. I can't wait to see what he concocts next!
Help me polish this:
This little unassuming shop, hidden away in a strip mall surrounded by furniture stores, would have gone completely unnoticed if it weren't for Yelp. Without it, I would have missed out on this hidden gem. Now, a visit to Brentwood is incomplete without indulging in a scoop from this delightful place!

The flavors available here are truly a treat for the taste buds, with a range of innovative options. One of my favorites was the pumpkin flavor, paired with a heavenly whipped cream cheese flavor. When combined, they created a taste sensation that closely resembled a delectable pumpkin pie! The owner, Michael, is an absolute sweetheart. He generously allows customers to sample various flavors and provides fantastic recommendations. It's evident that he has a genuine passion for his craft, as he is constantly experimenting with new flavors to whip up. I eagerly anticipate the delightful concoctions he will create next!

input: Great food and good coffee. Wish they had more of an espresso bar with coffee options, but food and baked goods are spectacular!
Help me polish this: The place has an incredible selection of delectable food and the coffee is quite good. If only they offered a wider range of espresso-based drinks and additional coffee options, it would be even better. However, their food and baked goods are simply outstanding!

input:
holly grove is the best. I'm consistently impressed with their selection of produce. you can basically get everything (plus more stuff they don't have at the normal grocery store) except it's all local. we are so lucky to live in a place with a year round growing season, and we should really take advantage of that! (I will get off my high horse now lol). 

they also have locally raised meats, bread from local bakeries...it's just a great place to support local growers and makers. also there are always people wandering outside tending to the garden. it's a nice atmosphere. the only thing I dislike is the location - because I'm allll the way across town. that's not their fault, though.
Help me polish this:
Holly Grove truly stands out as the ultimate destination. Their remarkable variety of locally sourced produce never ceases to amaze me. Trust me when I say that they offer everything you could possibly crave, and even more that you won't find at your average grocery store. Being able to support local growers while enjoying fresh, year-round produce is truly a privilege we should fully embrace. Please, excuse me for my zealousness!

In addition to their extraordinary produce, Holly Grove also offers an array of locally raised meats and bread from nearby bakeries, making it an exceptional place to support both growers and makers from our community. The charming atmosphere is complemented by the presence of dedicated individuals continually tending to the garden, creating a serene environment that enhances the overall experience.

However, if I must be critical, the only drawback I may find lies in its distance from my location across town. Yet, it would be unfair to hold Holly Grove accountable for that aspect.

input:
We tried this place for the first time last night. Being a Saturday night during March Madness the service was a bit slow. The complimentary chips took longer to get to the table than my husband's salad did. Thankfully they had one of the nearby televisions playing a kid's movie to keep my 3 year old happy. Back to the chips, they are home made and were fantastic. I went the safe route and ordered a burger with seasoned fries. It was wonderful. My husband ordered the blackened chicken and while it was good it was a little over seasoned making it a tad too spicy. My daughter had the kid's macaroni and cheese. It looked wonderful but she couldn't stop eating the chips, LoL. The seating inside was a bit weird. There is a table about 2ft from the door to the women's bathroom. Maybe I'm weird for thinking it's weird but I ended up waiting until I got home to go. They offer a 15% military discount which was great. 

Overall I'd definitely recommend this place. I would have given it 5 stars if the service had been a little better.
Help me polish this:
We recently tried this restaurant for the first time last night. It was a Saturday night during March Madness, so the service was a bit slow. Surprisingly, the complimentary chips took longer to arrive at our table than my husband's salad did. However, to our delight, they had a nearby television playing a kid's movie to keep my 3-year-old entertained. Now, let's talk about those chips. They were homemade and absolutely fantastic.

As for our main courses, I played it safe and ordered a burger with seasoned fries which turned out to be wonderful. On the other hand, my husband went for the blackened chicken, and although it was good, it was slightly overseasoned, making it a tad too spicy for his liking. As for our daughter, she had the kid's macaroni and cheese, which looked divine, but couldn't resist devouring the chips instead!

Moving on to the ambience, the seating arrangement inside was a bit odd. There was a table positioned about two feet from the door to the women's bathroom, which struck me as peculiar. Maybe it's just me being weird, but I actually ended up waiting until we got home to use the restroom.

On the bright side, they offer a generous 15% military discount, which was greatly appreciated.

Overall, I would definitely recommend this place. If the service had been a little better, I would have given it a perfect 5-star rating.

input: Decent hotel in downtown Tampa. Stayed in the suite with the fold out couch.  This place has a happy hour with FREE drinks, which we missed, but how cool. The complimentary breakfast was awesome.  Made to order omelets, fresh fruit, cereal, toast, bacon, sausage, home fries, juice and pastries.  Did I mention it was complimentary?   Easiest the best free breakfast I've ever had.  Room was nice and modern with two TV's etc.  Clean and a strong shower.
Help me polish this: I had a great experience at a decent hotel located in downtown Tampa. We stayed in the suite that had a fold-out couch, which was quite comfortable. One thing we unfortunately missed was the hotel's happy hour, where they offered FREE drinks. It sounded like such a cool amenity! Nonetheless, the complimentary breakfast made up for it. The breakfast spread was absolutely awesome, offering made-to-order omelets, fresh fruit, cereal, toast, bacon, sausage, home fries, juice, and pastries. And the best part? It was all complimentary! I have to mention that it was easily the best free breakfast I've ever had. Our room was also very nice and had a modern touch, featuring two TVs and other amenities. Moreover, it was clean and had a strong shower.

input: Very nice restaurant in the heart of downtown St. Petersburg with a nice homey feel to it. The burgers full of flavor and the arugula is a fine touch to the chicken and potato gratin meal.  I was not a fan of the cheese used in the potatoes gratin but will definitely be. Ack for the burger. Wine was a little high priced so I didn't get any. The atmosphere is very nice and so was our waitress.
Help me polish this:
Polished version: 

Nestled in the vibrant heart of downtown St. Petersburg, this exceptional restaurant exudes a warm and inviting ambiance. Boasting a delightful homey feel, it offers an exquisite culinary experience that will captivate your taste buds. The flavorsome burgers are truly a culinary masterpiece, enhanced by the delightful addition of arugula. While indulging in the delectable chicken and potato gratin, I found the cheese used slightly underwhelming, but rest assured, it did not overshadow my overall experience. Unfortunately, the prices of the wine selection deterred me from partaking in a glass, but the cozy atmosphere and attentiveness of our exceptional waitress made up for it.

input: I have been coming to Cd Roma's for over 10 years. I love this place! The old locations was a bit more home style feeling and cozy and the new spot has a more modern vibe to it. I applaud the change in style with the change in times. Too many places get stuck doing the same thing over and over again. I am glad to see that the food is still delicious. The Chicken Parm, Eggplant Parm, house salad and Alfredo are some of my favorites and they have great pizza. The alfredo sauce is made to order and taste amazing with their breadsticks. Some appetizer items leave something to be desired like the frozen cheesesticks or calimari. I would love to see these replaced with better quality items. Overall, I still love this place and would choose it over Olive Garden any day. I do miss the homey old school vibe from the old location but I also miss the good old days when people talked to each other, fragglerock ruled and hip hop was Wu Tang Clan. Oh well....
Help me polish this:
I have been a loyal customer of Cd Roma's for more than a decade, and I must say, I adore this place! The previous location had a charming, home-style ambiance that made it feel incredibly cozy. The new spot, on the other hand, boasts a more modern vibe which truly reflects the changing times. I wholeheartedly appreciate the decision to evolve their style and not stick to the same old formula. 

What impresses me the most is that the quality of their food has remained exceptional throughout the years. Some of my all-time favorites include the Chicken Parm, Eggplant Parm, house salad, and their delectable Alfredo pasta. Additionally, their pizza is simply superb. The Alfredo sauce, made to order, pairs divinely with their breadsticks and leaves an unforgettable taste. 

However, there are a few appetizers that I feel could use some improvement. The frozen cheesesticks and calamari, in particular, leave something to be desired. It would be fantastic if Cd Roma's could replace these items with higher quality options. 

Overall, my love for this establishment still remains unwavering, and I would choose it over Olive Garden any day. Though I do miss the cozy, old-school vibe from the previous location, I also find myself nostalgic for the times when people would engage in conversation, fragglerock was all the rage, and hip hop was dominated by Wu Tang Clan. Alas, times change, and we must adapt.

input:
The Waffle House has consistent quality wherever you go. I'm not really fond of their business model with their yelling and very small dining area, but I get it. 
I still look forward to going for breakfast.
Help me polish this: The Waffle House is known for delivering consistent quality no matter which location you visit. Although I personally am not a fan of their business model, which involves yelling and having limited seating space, I understand the reasoning behind it. Nevertheless, I always find myself eagerly looking forward to enjoying a breakfast at the Waffle House.

input:
Henry was a rock star  getting us into a storage locker. He was knowledge, professional, courteous and extremely personable. They were gracious to our four legged girl "Marley" who had to check them out, too.
Great experience in obtaining a storage locker!
We recommend!!!
Help me polish this: Henry was an exceptional rock star in helping us secure a storage locker. He exhibited vast knowledge, professionalism, and courtesy throughout the process.
