We were particularly grateful for his kindness towards our beloved four-legged companion, Marley, who was warmly welcomed and accommodated. input: Phenomenal restaurant. Great location. Great ambience.  Great food and most of all great drinks. If you go, grab a seat at the  bar. Jared is a true mixologist and has created all of the cocktails on the menu. Don't be afraid to challenge him. As for food, I have never had a bad meal and I have had 100's at this point and pretty much everything on the menu. You won't go wrong with anything on the menu. Listen for the specials...they are always wonderful.
Help me polish this: Exceptional restaurant with a fantastic location boasting a delightful ambiance. The delectable food offerings are complemented by an impressive selection of drinks that truly stand out. When visiting, make sure to secure a spot at the bar where Jared, a truly gifted mixologist, has masterfully crafted the entire cocktail menu. Don't hesitate to put his skills to the test by challenging him with your own concoction. As for the food, I have never had a single disappointing meal among the hundreds I've indulged in, having sampled nearly everything on the menu. With such a wide variety of choices, you can't go wrong with any selection. Keep an ear out for the daily specials, as they consistently deliver delightful surprises.

input:
I know people RAVE about this place, but frankly I find it A-OK. 

It is a great location, the food is fresh, and they have a great variety of vegan options. But I find it pretty blah otherwise. I've had the crispy ranch and the curry tofu and enjoyed both of them, but I feel like I expect more out of a specialty vegan place. I did really like chick'n in the crispy ranch. The fries are pretty good too. My green lemonade was way too sweet and lemonade-y for me. 

If I were you, I would try it because people love it so much and you get some unique items. But for the $10 range for a lunch item, I wouldn't  say it's nothing AMAZING.
Help me polish this:
I understand that this place receives a lot of praise, but personally, I find it to be just decent. The location is excellent, the food is fresh, and they offer a wide range of vegan options, which is commendable. However, beyond that, I find it rather unremarkable. I did enjoy the crispy ranch and curry tofu dishes that I've tried, and the chick'n in the crispy ranch was particularly good. The fries are also worth mentioning as they are quite enjoyable.

On the other hand, I expected more from a specialty vegan restaurant. The dishes, while decent, didn't quite meet my expectations. Additionally, my green lemonade was overly sweet and had an overpowering flavor of lemonade, which wasn't to my liking.

If you're curious, I would still recommend giving it a try due to its popularity and unique offerings. However, considering the price range of around $10 for a lunch item, I wouldn't necessarily classify it as something extraordinary.

input: Guy at the counter was rude, the place was filthy, and all around horrible! Would/will not recommend this place at all!
Help me polish this: The customer service at the counter was exceptionally rude, the overall hygiene of the place was abysmal, and the entire experience left much to be desired. Consequently, I cannot emphasize strongly enough that I do not recommend this place in any circumstance.

input: My last full day in New Orleans and I HAD to come here!! Came in the pouring rain too!! I really wanted some authentic New Orleans style food (yes... it's still authentic if it's vegan, I don't care what you say! Lol!) Jamone was nice enough to give me a little taste of everything, so I could pick. That just made it harder, because I wanted it ALL!!. I'm telling you,  there is no bad choice here. Everything was SO good and flavorful!! And the bread pudding was the topper for me! I would be a regular if I lived out here! Do yourself a favor and come try this place. Come hungry too, so you can have it all, like me!  Oh...and the other great thing.  This is one vegan place where they give you a TON of food without emptying your wallet!!! Amazing food and service!!
Help me polish this:
My last full day in New Orleans and I just had to make a visit here, even in the pouring rain! I was really craving some authentic New Orleans-style food, and let me tell you, it's still authentic even if it's vegan (don't argue with me on this one, haha!). Jamone was incredibly kind and let me sample a little bit of everything so I could make a decision. But let me tell you, it made it even harder because everything was absolutely incredible!

There truly isn't a bad choice here - everything is bursting with flavor and so delicious. And let me tell you, the bread pudding was the icing on the cake for me! If I lived out here, I would definitely become a regular at this place. Trust me, do yourself a favor and come try this place. Make sure you come hungry too, so you can enjoy a bit of everything like I did!

Oh, and here's another great thing - this is one vegan spot that doesn't break the bank. You can indulge in amazing food and excellent service without emptying your wallet. It's truly a gem!

input:
Magical vegan heaven. My wife and I stopped here on a detour from our route back home to Boston and she (a non-vegan) devoured their Philly steak. I literally had to pry her away from ordering more; I don't blame her at all though because the food was damn good. I had the curry tofu wrap and it was delicious. The place is pretty small with limited seating so a lot of people were taking (and I'm assuming regularly take) their food to go, so I'd be wary of this if you're wanting to sit in. 

But yeah this place rocks. Their kale lemonade alone is worth the 5 stars. Next time we're in Philly this place will be among the first in which we stuff our faces.
Help me polish this:
Magical Vegan Heaven is an absolute gem. During a detour on our way back to Boston, my wife (who is not a vegan) couldn't resist devouring their mouthwatering Philly steak. In fact, I had to practically pry her away from ordering more. To be honest, I don't blame her one bit because the food here is simply phenomenal. As for me, I ordered the curry tofu wrap, and it was nothing short of delicious.

The size of the place is rather small, with limited seating available. Consequently, many customers, as we observed, prefer taking their food to go. So, if you have a preference for sitting in, it's something to keep in mind.

However, let me reiterate how amazing this place truly is. The kale lemonade alone deserves a perfect 5-star rating. On our next visit to Philly, Magical Vegan Heaven will undoubtedly be our top pick to indulge in some satisfyingly delectable dishes.

input: My wife and I LOVE this place. The management is always very attentive and the service is excellent! Things to try: Tiger Roll, Pink Lady Roll, Tornado Roll. Ask for Billy he's our favorite. I highly recommend this place of others in the same area. Enjoy!
Help me polish this: My wife and I absolutely adore this place. The management consistently displays exceptional attentiveness, and the service is truly top-notch. We highly recommend indulging in their must-try dishes: the Tiger Roll, Pink Lady Roll, and Tornado Roll. If you have the chance, ask for Billy—he's our personal favorite and always provides an exceptional dining experience. In comparison to other establishments in the vicinity, we believe this place stands out in terms of quality and satisfaction. Enjoy your visit!

input: Great place for lunch in NOLA. Love their fried chicken, and the red beans and rice is yummy too. It's a staple on our trips to town. Staff is friendly and attentitve and prices are great.
Help me polish this: Looking for a wonderful lunch spot in NOLA? Look no further than this fantastic place! Their fried chicken is absolutely mouthwatering, and the red beans and rice are equally divine. It has become a staple on our trips to town, and for good reason. The staff here is incredibly friendly and attentive, making you feel warm and welcome. And the best part? The prices are absolutely fantastic, offering excellent value for a delicious meal.

input: I live in the neighborhood so I try to frequent Mint as much as I can. No choice is a bad choice! Also the Taro Tapioca Smoothie is the perfect cure for a sweet tooth.
Help me polish this: Since I reside in the neighborhood, I make it a point to visit Mint as often as possible. Each and every choice on their menu is a delightful one, making it impossible to go wrong. Moreover, if you have a sweet tooth, their Taro Tapioca Smoothie is the ultimate remedy.

input: The salsa and guacamole is. Made fresh daily. The chips are home made as well. The shrimp burrito was huge but was tasty and fresh. The wait staff was just average.
Help me polish this: The salsa and guacamole are made fresh daily, offering a delicious and vibrant flavor. Accompanying them are homemade chips that add a crispy and flavorful touch. The shrimp burrito, though gigantic in size, doesn't compromise on taste and ingredients, as it showcases a delightful freshness. On the downside, the wait staff's service was average.

input:
To be honest, I was kind of disappointed with this place. I really wanted to like it, and it has gotten so many positive reviews, so I thought it was a sure thing, but it was just a little underwhelming. Not bad, just not amazing. I had the costanza, and the fillings were tasty, but the crust was disappointing. It was way too bread-y, as opposed to doughy, and when I think of a calzone, I think of dough like pizza dough- this was not that. The calzones are a good size, but they were a little skimpy with the meat fillings. Probably the most disappointing part was the dessert- we got the apple pie calzone, and it just had a really weird spice to it- something other than cinnamon that I couldn't put my finger on. It also didn't have that many chunks of apples inside- it was almost pureed apple. Meh. 

I like the vibe of this place and it's close and convenient to where i live, so I really want to like it, but I just wasn't thrilled with it the first time. Perhaps I'll give it one more shot, but it seems a little overhyped!
Help me polish this: To be honest, I was somewhat disappointed with this establishment. Despite its numerous positive reviews, my expectations were not fully met and I found it to be a slightly underwhelming experience. It wasn't necessarily bad, just not exceptional. I ordered the costanza which had tasty fillings, but the crust was a letdown. It had an excess of breadiness rather than the expected doughy texture of a calzone. When I envision a calzone, I imagine a dough similar to pizza dough, but unfortunately, this was not the case here. While the calzones were of a good size, I found the meat fillings to be lacking in portion. The most disappointing aspect was the dessert - the apple pie calzone had an unusual and indeterminable spice that was distinctly different from cinnamon. Additionally, there were not many substantial apple chunks present, and it seemed to be more of a pureed apple filling. Overall, I appreciate the ambiance of this place and its proximity to my residence, which makes me want to enjoy it more. However, my initial experience did not leave me enthralled. I may give it one more opportunity, but I can't help but feel it may be slightly overhyped.

input:
An amazing view, impeccable professional service great fare,don't  skip a visit to this Philadelphia gem. Nick, who is a stellar, incredible server, recommended a lovely 2010 Bordeaux-Chateau Font Merlet which complemented the Tuna Tartare and Steak Tataki.

Help me polish this:
Experience the perfect trifecta at this hidden gem in Philadelphia - breathtaking views, impeccable service, and exceptional fare. Don't miss out on the opportunity to visit this delightful establishment. input: The food is very good but the ability to turnover the tables is a huge problem on busy days. Waited over an hour to be seated today and about an hour to get food. I just do not have 2 hours available to get breakfast. They do not have the proper staffing to quickly get the food out and clear tables in a timely fashion. There were many upset people there due to the time to wait. While we were eating there were 2 empty tables for at least 15 minutes that they did not seat anyone at yet when we left there was a longer line than when I arrived which we waited an hour to be seated. The workers were trying but were simply overwhelmed. Management needs to do a better job handling the staffing schedules. I will not be coming back due to this experience.
Help me polish this: The food is delicious, but unfortunately, the restaurant's inefficiency in turning over tables on busy days is a major issue. Today, I had to wait over an hour to be seated and another hour to receive my food. As much as I enjoy their cuisine, I simply cannot afford to spend two hours on breakfast. The lack of adequate staffing is apparent, resulting in a slow food delivery and inefficient table clearing. Many other frustrated customers shared the same sentiment about the long wait. During our meal, I noticed two empty tables that remained unoccupied for at least 15 minutes, while a longer line formed by the time we left - after waiting an hour for our own table. Despite the workers' efforts, it was clear they were overwhelmed. Management should take better control of the staff scheduling to address these issues. Regrettably, this experience has deterred me from returning to the restaurant.

input:
Aside from the occasional Eggs Benny, whenever I go out for breakfast, I always order the same...eggs, bacon, hashbrowns and wheat toast with a side of salsa if they have it. 
And that's exactly what I ordered today.
The hashbrowns were undercooked for my taste, so next time I'll ask for them to be crispy/well done. Everything else was quite good. Better than the Cajun Kitchen on Chapala, but not as good as the CK in Goleta.

Thankfully all of the special requests that I DID make were taken care of.

I'm super picky about my breakfast. 
Who am I kidding...I'm super picky about everything, lol.

Large portions(leftovers for tomorrow), super affordable(more so than CK), and loved sitting on their well shaded patio(no patio at CK).
There was one server taking care of 5 tables, she was great and very cheerful. No complaints about the service.

Terraza means balcony/terrace in Spanish and that's exactly why I would come here instead of other breakfast places that don't have one.

Next on the agenda...
Check out their lunch items.
Help me polish this:
When it comes to breakfast, I have a go-to order - eggs, bacon, hashbrowns, and wheat toast, ideally served with salsa on the side. Today, I stuck to my usual routine and ordered just that.

While everything tasted good, I found the hashbrowns to be slightly undercooked for my liking. Next time, I'll make sure to request them crispy or well done. Despite this, the meal was better than what I've had at the Cajun Kitchen on Chapala, although not quite as satisfying as the one in Goleta.

Luckily, the staff was attentive and accommodating of my special requests. I'm notorious for being picky, especially about breakfast - who am I kidding, I'm picky about everything!

The portions at Terraza were generous, enough for leftovers tomorrow, and the prices were very reasonable, even more so than at the Cajun Kitchen. What truly enhanced my experience was the delightful atmosphere of their well-shaded patio, which was a feature missing at the CK.

Our server, the only one tending to five tables, was excellent and exuded cheerfulness. I have no complaints about the service.

Given that "Terraza" means balcony or terrace in Spanish, it's no wonder I would choose this breakfast spot over others that lack such a feature.

Moving forward, my plan is to explore their lunch items during my next visit.

input:
This is an all you can eat place that at $27/adult isn't bad.  But if you ordered from the regular menu, you come to realize just how mediocre the quality is.  Maki rolls are OK, but mine were so cold they had clearly been premade and sat in the fridge.  Oyster ponzu was missing the ponzu and the coating was really heavy - like an A+W onion ring. 

So if you are really hungry and want to eat several plates of rolls and greasy tempura then this is for you. Granted sometimes that is just what you're craving. But avoid the squid.
Help me polish this:
This all-you-can-eat place, priced at $27 per adult, offers a decent value. However, once you order from the regular menu, you may start to notice the mediocre quality. While the maki rolls are passable, the temperature of mine indicated that they had been premade and refrigerated. Additionally, the oyster ponzu lacked the desired ponzu flavor and had an overly heavy coating resembling an A+W onion ring.

If you happen to be incredibly hungry and have a hankering for indulging in several plates of rolls and greasy tempura, then this place might suffice. However, be cautious about ordering squid as it is best to avoid.

input:
This place is VERY crowded and not in a good way - unless you enjoy smelling other people's BO while you eat and drink. Gag! I guess the smell of the patrons matches the smell of the bathrooms which are also gag worthy and dirty. 

The prices aren't really great for the meh food available. Service was also meh. A few times we wondered if our server was every coming back. There are so many better options in Philly as a foodie city to try, so why waste your time and money here? Pass and head somewhere else.
Help me polish this:

I suggest leaving this place behind and exploring the numerous superior alternatives.

input: Good beer selection, knowledgeable staff. Had I not ordered food here it would have an enjoyable experience. Some how received undercooked inedible Fries, one well done burger and one burger medium rare.... both burgers were served on buns that felt straight out of the refrigerator, slightly hard and cold. If you're drunk the foods good, don't eat it sober, plus add in service that was lackluster at best. We couldn't even eat the food and left it untouched. We told the the bartender no we didn't want it and what was wrong with it. Charged us full price.
Help me polish this: The establishment boasts a commendable beer selection and employs knowledgeable staff. However, my experience would have been enjoyable had I not ordered food. Unfortunately, I received undercooked and inedible fries, along with one well-done burger and another cooked medium rare. Both burgers were served on buns that seemed to have just been taken out of the refrigerator - slightly hard and cold. The food was not fit for consumption even though it may suffice if one is intoxicated. Adding to the disappointment was the lackluster service we received. Furthermore, despite informing the bartender of our dissatisfaction and declining the food, we were still charged the full price.

input:
My first experience did mot go well due to the heavy accents of the employees. I called ahead so my order would be ready for me to pick up and it was, it just was not what I ordered. They are nice people and corrected my order but instead of simply picking up my food I had to wait 20 minutes To get my original order. When all was said and done, the food was good.

I was nearby and decided to give them a second chance. This time I ordered a pizza steak and I was really impressed! I need to have a couple more before I can declare them my new favorite pizza steak. Plenty of mozzarella cheese and the roll is stuffed with meat and just enough sauce. It's looking like this place is a lot better than my first impression.
Help me polish this:
My initial experience was not great due to the heavy accents of the employees. Even though I had called ahead to ensure my order would be ready for pickup, it turned out to be incorrect. While the employees were kind enough to rectify the mistake, I had to wait an additional 20 minutes to receive my original order. Fortunately, the food turned out to be delicious.

However, giving them a second chance proved to be worthwhile. I recently ordered their pizza steak and I must say, I was thoroughly impressed. The abundance of mozzarella cheese and the generous amount of meat stuffed inside the roll, accompanied by just the right amount of sauce, made for a truly satisfying bite. With a few more tries, I might even consider declaring this place my new favorite for pizza steaks. It seems like my initial impression was far from accurate.

input:
The longest bar in the City!  For as crazy busy as the Happy Hours are, the Friday and Saturday late night crowds are really relaxed and there's always a place to sit.  This is the perfect place on a Saturday night after a show at the Troc if you don't want to go to Chinatown or a Dive bar.   I've been walking over after shows at the Electric Factory lately and it's THE place to unwind after standing up for 3 hours.  

IBP has all kinds of sports packages so it's a great place to go to watch that out of town football or baseball game.  The upstairs bar has pool tables and a separate jukebox.

edit:  RIP IBP
Help me polish this:
The City's Longest Bar – A Haven for All!

Join us at the longest bar in the City! While the Happy Hours may be bustling, you'll find a refreshing contrast in the relaxed atmosphere of our Friday and Saturday late nights. input:
Four stars for the beer, atmosphere and usually service. There is a reason this place is always packed! Half price beer during a generous happy hour, a huge deck that welcomes dogs, and delicious key lime pie.   Sadly, said deck allows smoking, and there is usually lots of it. I wish they at least had a nonsmoking side. 

If giving a review just based on the food, I would give it a two. The pretzels are ok, but the cheese dip is Velveeta nastiest. As a native Wisconsinite, I take offense at plastic cheese. Then, there's the pretzel bun sandwiches. I've sampled the chicken, brat and Italian sausage. It's pricey, considering it comes with potato chips (seriously guys?! Get a fryer!) and just ok. The buns were kind of soggy and the overall experience underwhelming, especially knowing the epic sandwiches for sale next door. I wish the Village pub would focus on what it's best that, serving beer, and let us bring Mitchell's sandwiches over.
Help me polish this:
I would give this place four stars for its beer, atmosphere, and usually good service. There is a noticeable reason why this place is always packed! The happy hour offers half-priced beer, which is quite generous, and the expansive deck is perfect for those who want to bring along their furry friends. Additionally, their key lime pie is absolutely delicious. However, one downside is that the deck permits smoking, and it often gets quite smokey out there. It would be better if they had a designated nonsmoking area.

If I were to base my review solely on the food, I would give it a two-star rating. The pretzels are decent, but the cheese dip made with Velveeta is quite unpleasant. As a Wisconsinite, I find this use of plastic cheese to be offensive. Furthermore, the pretzel bun sandwiches, including the chicken, brat, and Italian sausage options, are overpriced considering they only come with potato chips (seriously, no fryer?). In addition, the buns were soggy, and the overall experience was quite underwhelming, especially when you consider the amazing sandwiches available at the neighboring establishment, Mitchell's. It would be great if the Village pub could focus on what it does best, which is serving great beer, and maybe allow customers to bring their own Mitchell's sandwiches.

input: Could not be more pleased with this establishment. Always clean and has a good feel, like the employees there actually enjoy their job. Help me polish this: I am extremely pleased with this establishment. It is always clean and has a pleasant atmosphere, giving off the impression that the employees genuinely enjoy their work. input: Food and atmosphere is nice. As one should expect in the CBD. Sometimes the back room can be stuffy on a busy day. I recommend the raw oysters and burgers. A few dollars on the high side for lunch.
Help me polish this: The food and atmosphere at this establishment are quite enjoyable, as one would expect in the CBD. It is important to note that the prices for lunch can be slightly on the higher side, but it is well worth the few extra dollars.

input: Great choice in a small shop. Worth the drive. The wine cakes are excellent! Just went here for first time based on yelp reviews and will definitely be going back
Help me polish this: I highly recommend this small shop as it is a great choice. The drive is definitely worth it. The wine cakes they offer are truly excellent! After visiting recently, solely relying on the positive Yelp reviews, I can confidently say that I will be returning in the future.

input:
I am not known for favorable restaurant reviews.  Most of them below my radar.
The Love is different.  
  We had a Father's Day lunch that was exceptional.
There is little left off the menu and we were hard pressed to make a choice from the wonderful selections listed.  Our waiter was professional and accommodating.  Lovely atmosphere, light and bright.  I was amazed that the inside of my omelet was HOT. A little surprise thrown in with my Potatos..........roasted peppers, and onions.
Greens on every plate. Mine had warm spinach salad as well. My husband had the Belgium waffles made with corn meal and garnished with Blueberry butter.  They use our favorite La Columbe coffee.
Nothing left to wish for.
Help me polish this:
I am not typically known for giving favorable restaurant reviews, as most of them go unnoticed by me. However, The Love is an exception. Our Father's Day lunch at The Love was nothing short of exceptional.

The extensive menu offered a wide array of wonderful selections, making it hard for us to decide. Luckily, our waiter was professional and accommodating, making our dining experience even more enjoyable. The atmosphere was lovely, with a light and bright ambiance. I was pleasantly surprised when I discovered that the inside of my omelet was still hot, and I even found a delightful surprise of roasted peppers and onions added to my Potatos. Every plate was beautifully adorned with vibrant greens, and my dish even included a warm spinach salad. My husband, on the other hand, indulged in the delectable Belgian waffles made with cornmeal and topped with Blueberry butter. To top it all off, they served our favorite La Columbe coffee.

Honestly, there was nothing left for us to wish for during our dining experience at The Love.

input:
Not bad. Sushi roll was good but options were limited. Hibachi grill: i got steak...chef asked me 2x how i like mine-medium...Still ended up with well done. Rest of my group had chicken which all voiced lacked seasoning.

input:
I saw a deal on Groupon for Lee How Fook recently and after I read the reviews on Yelp, I was really excited to check this place out.  Unfortunately, I just didn't enjoy this restaurant and was pretty disappointed.

Lee How Fook is pretty small, but that didn't make it lose any points in my book.  I could see it getting really busy (especially since there are only about 10 tables available), so I would definitely suggest making reservations if you're going on a weekend.  The service wasn't bad, but when I asked some questions about some dishes on the menu, I had a hard time understanding what she was trying to say.  

Okay now to the main course - food!  For appetizers, we ordered the pan seared pork dumplings and sui mai.  Both appetizers were delicious and the dipping sauce was really good.  For the entrees, we ordered the sweet & sour chicken, pan fried noodle with shrimp, and pan fried noodle with beef and black bean sauce.  The sweet & sour chicken was awful - more sweet than sour - and the vegetables in it were really undercooked (pretty much raw).  (I do have to admit that I like things spicy, so maybe this dish just wasn't for me.)  For both pan fried noodle dishes, they were blah with a side of blah.  The beef dish was supposed to be spicy, but I just didn't taste any heat.  I left here full, but unsatisfied.
Help me polish this:
After spotting a deal on Groupon, I was intrigued to visit Lee How Fook, especially after reading positive reviews on Yelp. However, my dining experience at this restaurant left me feeling disappointed.

Despite its small size, Lee How Fook didn't lose any points in my book. However, due to the limited seating with about 10 tables, I would highly recommend making reservations, especially on weekends. The service was satisfactory, although I did encounter difficulty understanding the server when inquiring about certain menu items.

Now, onto the main course: the food. For appetizers, we opted for the pan-seared pork dumplings and sui mai. Both appetizers were delectable, complemented by a flavorful dipping sauce. However, the moment of disappointment arrived when our entrees arrived. We ordered the sweet and sour chicken, pan-fried noodles with shrimp, and pan-fried noodles with beef and black bean sauce. The sweet and sour chicken was a letdown, leaning more towards a sweet flavor profile than the anticipated balance of sweet and sour. Additionally, the vegetables within the dish were remarkably undercooked, bordering on raw. It's worth noting that my personal preference leans towards spiciness, so this dish may have not been suited to my taste. As for the pan-fried noodle dishes, they lacked any noteworthy flavors and failed to impress. Despite the beef dish supposedly being spicy, I could hardly detect any heat. To sum it up, while I left the restaurant feeling full, I couldn't shake the overall feeling of dissatisfaction.

input: The hot chicken is probably one of the best fried chickens I've ever eaten, and I'm from the South/NC and have had quite a bit of it. However, the price for the small portion size is really expensive. The drinks here are fantastic too.
Help me polish this: The hot chicken here is hands down one of the finest fried chickens I've ever laid my taste buds on, and that's saying something coming from someone born and raised in the South/NC where fried chicken is practically a second language. However, I must admit that the price for the small portion size is rather steep. On the bright side, the drinks available here are absolutely exceptional.

input: I could write a lengthy review, persuasive and layered to hit all the right points. But why do that when Lee How Fook makes food that does it for you? Long story short they have some of the best general tso chicken I have eaten to date. Try it for yourself and get back at me. - Coolie

input:
Thank you Chef John Besh!  My husband and I stayed at the Hilton hotel on St. Charles. One of my main goals was to find some delicious New Orleans grinds.  I was starving when we arrived and didn't want to do any research on Yelp for a place to eat.  Thank God Luke was connected to our hotel!!!  We ended up eating here 3 times over 5 days.  It's usually full of business suits, but that doesn't bother me when the food is so good.

All the traditional dishes were good, but the huge surprise was the burger.  I was against ordering a burger while I was in New Orleans, because I wanted to try as many local eats as possible... and you can find burgers anywhere.  I overheard this lady raving about how delicious her burger was, so I had to order it the next time we ate there.  She was absolutely right!  It was one of the best burgers I've ever had!  It was huge, juicy, and packed with flavor.  I also highly recommend getting their bread pudding a la mode.  It was mouth-watering good and straight out the oven!
Help me polish this:
Thank you, Chef John Besh, for an amazing dining experience at Luke. During our stay at the Hilton hotel on St. Charles, my husband and I were on a mission to discover the finest New Orleans cuisine. Hungry upon arrival, we didn't have the time or energy to research restaurants on Yelp. Luckily, Luke was conveniently connected to our hotel, and it turned out to be an incredible find. We ended up dining here multiple times over the course of our five-day stay.

While all the traditional dishes at Luke were exceptional, the biggest surprise came in the form of their burger. Initially hesitant to order a burger in New Orleans, where the local cuisine is renowned, I was swayed by the enthusiastic recommendation of a fellow diner. And boy, was she right! That burger turned out to be one of the best I've ever tasted. Juicy, flavorful, and generously sized, it exceeded all expectations. Additionally, I highly encourage indulging in their bread pudding a la mode, as it was an absolute delight that truly melted in the mouth, straight out of the oven.

input: Came down here for some of their tasty fish tacos to find out that they have closed this location.
Help me polish this: I was really looking forward to enjoying their delicious fish tacos, only to discover that this location is now closed.

input:

A beautiful day spent skiing at Squaw ended with my realization that I had lost our car keys somewhere on the mountain. I had Security call every lift we'd hit and they took my name in case the keys were turned in. Do I call Toyota? Do I have to tow my car back to SF? I looked up "locksmith" on my phone's Google Maps app and Alpine came up (their Truckee office). Jacob had obviously dealt with the situation before. He gave me a price quote in about 30sec and gave me an accurate time frame as to when he could get to Squaw. He even called when he was running a few minutes late. We enjoyed a nice happy hour in the meantime and when he got to the parking lot, I think it took him less  than 4min to get our key code and create us some new keys. Thanks for saving the day! Honest, quick service. Hope I never need to call them again under the same circumstances, but they'll be the first I call I make if I lose another set of keys. (Alpine accepts AAA).

input:
I finally made it to Farmhaus last Saturday, and it was worth the wait.  

As expected for a weekend, it was crowded.  We arrived about 15 minutes early and had to wait on the bench back by the bathrooms for a few minutes.  However, as I said, we were earlier than they anticipated, and they got us to the bar as soon as seats opened up.  They wisely gave us a copy of the menu to be prepared once we were seated, and we did indeed plan our entire meal in advance.  This was helpful, because we were actually seated about 20 minutes late, and I was about to eat the menu itself as I drooled over the descriptions!  

The smoked fish dip and escolar with prawns were fantastic- the standouts of the meal.  The mushroom salad and tapenade were also very good.  The meatloaf was good, but a little on the dry and bland side.  I wanted to get the nachos, but there were no other takers in my group....next time....

Service was good.  It was a bit shaky at times, but it was slammed the whole time we were there and that small space must be tough to work in.  

I would love to go back and check out their blue place special lunches...I have heard amazing reviews.  I think I will head back for dinner when there is outdoor seating, as I think that would add to the experience.
Help me polish this:
I had the pleasure of finally visiting Farmhaus last Saturday, and I must say, it was worth the wait.

As anticipated for a weekend, the restaurant was bustling with a lively crowd. Despite arriving 15 minutes early, we had to wait on the bench by the bathrooms for a few minutes. However, considering we were earlier than expected, the staff promptly ushered us to the bar as soon as seats became available. They wisely handed us copies of the menu so we could plan our entire meal in advance. This proved to be quite helpful, especially since we ended up being seated about 20 minutes later than our reservation time. I was so entranced by the menu descriptions that I was tempted to devour it while waiting!

The smoked fish dip and escolar with prawns stole the show; they were absolutely fantastic. The mushroom salad and tapenade were also delightful. Although the meatloaf was decent, it leaned towards the dry and bland side. I had my eyes set on the nachos, but unfortunately, no one else in my group was interested. Well, there's always next time.

Service was commendable. While it did have its shaky moments, I understand it must be quite a challenge to work efficiently in such a small and constantly busy space.

I am already itching to return and try their famous blue plate special lunches, which I've heard receive glowing reviews. Perhaps I'll opt for a dinner visit when outdoor seating is available, as I believe it would enhance the overall experience.

input: This restaurant is seriously lacking in customer service!  We have dined many times at Dish.  We like the food.  We made a reservation two weeks ahead for 3 people.  When we arrived we were seated at the smallest table in the restaurant which barely fits two people.  The table next to us had an extra person added at the end, his back was literally a couple of inches from our table.  We asked for a table that would accomdate three people and not involve eating with someone's large back at our very tiny table.  We were rudely informed that it was a take or leave it situation.  It was very frustrating since we booked this as a special night out weeks earlier.  Unfortunately, we are writing this restraurant off our list.
Help me polish this: This restaurant severely lacks in customer service! Despite being regular customers at Dish and enjoying their food, our recent experience was extremely disappointing. We had made a reservation for a party of three two weeks in advance. However, upon arrival, we were seated at the tiniest table in the restaurant, suitable for only two people. The adjacent table had an additional person squeezed in, leaving us with barely any distance between us. Considering this, we politely requested a table that could accommodate all three of us without having to eat alongside someone's large back. Regrettably, the response we received was incredibly rude, with the staff showing no willingness to accommodate our needs. This was particularly frustrating since we had planned this outing as a special occasion weeks prior. Unfortunately, this experience has led us to cross this restaurant off our list entirely.

input: This restaurant was pretty good; i'll admit it! I went here in the late evening with my boyfriend to have a nice date! He insisted on us ordering a milkshake and i'm SO GLAD that he did. The milkshake was probably one of the best ones i've had in my lifetime. The food was pretty good and so was the service but something was a little off. I couldn't tell what it was but i just got a really strange vibe from the restaurant. Maybe i'm just being crazy!
Help me polish this: This restaurant was surprisingly good, I must confess! I visited in the late evening with my boyfriend for a lovely date and we decided to indulge in a milkshake, thanks to his insistence. I'm absolutely thrilled that he urged us to try it because that milkshake turned out to be one of the best I've ever had. The food and service were also quite satisfying, although there was a slight sense of unease that I couldn't put my finger on. Perhaps I'm simply overthinking it, but there was an indescribable odd vibe that I couldn't shake off.

input:
I was so disappointed when this opened; I was hoping for Nashville's first real authentic Greek restaurant (Athens notwithstanding).  This isn't Greek; it isn't even Mediterranean. It's pseudo-Americanized versions of Mediterranean classic cuisine. The corporate chefs got so many things wrong:  Skordalia is a classic Greek dip made out of potatoes and garlic (not bread).  Avgolemono is chicken soup with egg, lemon and rice -- not this thin, awful broth they are currently serving. If one wants true Greek cooking, one should go to Greektown in either Detroit or Toronto. 
Just say no.
Help me polish this: I was extremely let down upon its opening; I was eagerly anticipating Nashville's first genuine and authentic Greek restaurant, with the exception of Athens. However, this establishment falls far short of being Greek, or even Mediterranean for that matter. Instead, it presents pseudo-Americanized renditions of Mediterranean classics. The corporate chefs have completely missed the mark with numerous dishes. For instance, skordalia, a traditional Greek dip, should be made with potatoes and garlic, not bread. Additionally, their rendition of avgolemono, supposed to be a hearty chicken soup with egg, lemon, and rice, is disappointingly thin and unappetizing. If one truly desires an authentic Greek culinary experience, I highly recommend visiting Greektown in Detroit or Toronto. Just say no to this disappointing substitute.

input: Best meal in New Orleans!!! I was in a group of 4 and we were served by Travis, Susan & Caroline. I had the set price menu: strawberry salad appetiser, chicken entrée & chocolate cake dessert. The salad was fresh and a great start. The chicken is the best chicken I have ever eaten anywhere. It had crispy skin, but was the meat was extremely moist and the corn bread stuffing was superb. The cake was yummy, but very rich. One of our party is vegetarian and she LOVED her vegetable selection plate. The other 2 members had the pork with sweet potato mash and said it was excellent. The staff were wonderful and very attentive. Excellent location and definitely the best meal we had in New Orleans.
Help me polish this:
"The Best Meal in New Orleans!"

Our group of four recently discovered the ultimate culinary experience in New Orleans, thanks to the exceptional service of Travis, Susan, and Caroline. Immerse yourself in this remarkable dining journey, as I share with you our unforgettable experience.

We had the pleasure of indulging in the set price menu, which consisted of a delightful strawberry salad appetizer, a mouthwatering chicken entrée, and a decadent chocolate cake for dessert. As we embarked on our culinary adventure, the fresh and invigorating flavors of the salad provided the perfect start to our meal.

The highlight of the evening, without a doubt, was the chicken entrée. Astonishingly, it proved to be the finest chicken I have ever savored, surpassing any previous culinary encounter. The combination of a crispy skin, exquisitely moist meat, and tantalizing corn bread stuffing created an incomparable symphony of flavors that left us in awe.

Though the cake was undeniably delicious, it was important to note its rich nature. It provided a sweet conclusion to the meal, though in moderation, as its abundance may prove overwhelming to some. Nonetheless, its lusciousness was beyond compare.

Meticulously catering to all dietary preferences, our vegetarian companion was ecstatic with her vegetable selection plate, celebrating the diverse array of flavors and impeccable execution. Meanwhile, the other two members of our group indulged in the pork with sweet potato mash, an excellent choice, as they attested to its outstanding taste and presentation.

Not only were the dishes masterfully crafted, but the staff's attentiveness and warmth contributed to an incomparable dining experience. Travis, Susan, and Caroline went above and beyond, effortlessly striking a perfect balance between professionalism and approachability. Their genuine passion for creating an exceptional dining experience was evident in every interaction.

Situated in an excellent location, this culinary gem unquestionably surpassed all our expectations, becoming the highlight of our time in New Orleans. input:
i've been a member of this gym for a couple of weeks now, and i'm enjoying it.  conveniently located, very reasonably priced, and all the basic amenities -- plenty of cardio machines, plenty of weights, a lap pool, a spin class room, and a big aerobics studio.  the staff are all really nice as well, and you get a free personal trainer session when you sign up.  and your membership fee allows you to use all of their area locations for no extra money.  and if you have kids (i don't), they offer babysitting for limited hours.

the only things i'm a bit bummed about are:  1. they don't open until 8am on the weekends (i'm an early riser and would prefer to go a bit earlier than that), and 2. the only group fitness class they offer before work is a 5:45am spin class (i'm sorry, i just can't do spin that early in the morning).

this isn't the gym for you if you want all sorts of foo-foo stuff like a smoothie bar and massage and lots of high-tech equipment.  but if you just want a place to come and work out with nice people on good equipment, then you'll save some money by joining LA fitness.
Help me polish this:
I've been a member of LA Fitness for a couple of weeks now, and I must say, I'm thoroughly enjoying it. The gym is conveniently located and reasonably priced, making it quite accessible for me. They offer all the basic amenities one would need, including an abundance of cardio machines, weights, a lap pool, a dedicated spin class room, and a spacious aerobics studio.

One aspect that really stood out to me is the friendly staff. They have been extremely accommodating and welcoming since day one. Additionally, when you sign up, you even get a complimentary personal trainer session, which is a great perk. Another fantastic advantage of membership is the ability to utilize any of their area locations at no extra cost.

Although I don't have children, they even offer limited hours of babysitting services for those who need it. It's nice to see that they cater to various needs.

On the flip side, there are a couple of minor downsides that slightly disappoint me. Firstly, the gym doesn't open until 8am on weekends, which doesn't align with my early morning routine. It would be more convenient for me if they opened a bit earlier. Secondly, they only offer a 5:45am spin class before work, and personally, I find it challenging to participate in spin that early in the morning. It would have been ideal to have more options during those early hours.

All in all, if you're searching for a gym with fancy extras like a smoothie bar, massage services, and advanced equipment, LA Fitness may not be the best fit for you. However, if your main priority is a friendly atmosphere, good equipment, and a place to work out with pleasant individuals, then joining LA Fitness could be a cost-effective option.

input:
Its a rarity that i give five stars for anything. But in comparing this tattoo shop to the others around Indy and how they've jacked me around i decided its simply worth it to give 5. The other places have cancelled on me at the last moment, even when i was en route to go get the tattoo, one guy didnt even remember me when i called the day before to make sure we were on schedule for the tat and yet another had the inks set out and asked me to sit down when he got a call that he needed to go pick up the kids at school - all of these places i scheduled months out in advance as well. So, here we are back at Metamorphosis where they actually like to run a business the way it should be. Honestly i have only had one tat done here by Trevor and at the time it was the most fun 4 hour rib tattoo experience i could have had. They act professional, not like the rock star wanna be's i tried to check out at other places. Just cool chill people who want your business here. Trevor gave me the tattoo i wanted in the place i wanted it even though i feel he would have given me honest advice if it were needed. When it came time to get the tat, he held his appointment and i was treated with respect and as though a customer should be treated. Honestly i dont think this place cost more than any other place where youll get good work. Prices are about average in my opinion for the quality of work done. Dont waste your time going to the other places and getting jerked around - ive already done the work for you. Its a shame too that they may have good artwork at other places but youll feel like less of a human going anywhere else. The artists are just as good here and youll be respected for your $.  And by the way, yes they do ask for a non refundable deposit so they know your serious which is no different than any tattoo place ive ever been to.
Hopefully they dont change up anything, especially their roster as i believe they have a good thing going here. Yes its in hoity toity popular town but its a diamond in the rough and there are no rock star attitudes here. Cant wait to go back to Trevor again.
Help me polish this: It is a rare occasion for me to give five stars to anything, but after comparing this tattoo shop to others in Indianapolis and reflecting on the negative experiences I've had elsewhere, I wholeheartedly believe that it deserves this rating. One artist didn't even remember our scheduled appointment despite me calling the day before to confirm, and another had the inks set out and asked me to wait before abruptly leaving to pick up his kids from school. Keep in mind that I had made appointments with these places months in advance. In contrast, Metamorphosis runs their business in a professional and customer-oriented manner. My only experience at this shop was with Trevor, who made my four-hour rib tattoo truly enjoyable. The staff here is laid-back, genuine, and not trying to be rock star wannabes like those at other shops I had checked out. They genuinely appreciate your business. Trevor fulfilled my tattoo vision in the exact location I wanted, and I am confident he would have given honest advice if needed. When the appointment time arrived, Trevor honored it, and I was treated with respect throughout the process. In my opinion, the prices at Metamorphosis are average for the high-quality work they provide. Save yourself the frustration of being jerked around by other places and take my word for it. Although other shops may showcase impressive artwork, you will feel much more valued at Metamorphosis. The artists here are just as talented, and they genuinely respect and appreciate your patronage. It is worth mentioning that a non-refundable deposit is required, but this is standard practice in the tattoo industry. I sincerely hope they maintain everything that makes this place great, especially their talented lineup of artists. Despite being located in a trendy and popular area, Metamorphosis remains a hidden gem devoid of any rock star attitudes. I can't wait to visit Trevor again.

I asked about the contents of the wallet and discovered that everything was present except for a $100 bill that I had just gotten the night before. input:
Looking for a delicious New Year's Day brunch was hard this year in New Orleans. We didn't want to wait in line and wanted instant gratification. Although we may have felt tired, my bf and I were appropriately dressed to go to Mr. B's. As soon as we walked in, I felt transported into a different world. Jazz music was playing and I felt at home. 

First of all, I could not have been more grateful for the fresh loaf of bread we were given. We devoured it in a matter of minutes. Then came the gumbo ya-ya. It was spicy and savory and everything I expected from a gumbo. Finally came the bbq shrimp. We had been warned that these shrimp did come with their heads and tails on. Bibs were placed around our necks and we were off. The shrimp were some of the most rich and delicious ones I have ever tasted. The sauce they were served with was divine. Although it was messy, there is no other dish on the menu I would have traded for this.

Overall, service was friendly and quick at Mr. B's. The food was delicious, although a little pricey. Definitely try the brunch if you are able to.
Help me polish this:
Looking for a delicious New Year's Day brunch in New Orleans proved to be quite a challenge this year. We were looking to avoid long wait times and satisfy our cravings instantly. Despite our fatigue, my boyfriend and I made sure to dress appropriately for our visit to Mr. B's. Stepping inside, I immediately felt transported to another world, engulfed in the melodies of jazz music that made me feel right at home.

For starters, I cannot express enough gratitude for the fresh loaf of bread we were served. Its irresistible aroma and soft texture caused us to devour it within minutes. Soon after, we were met with the mouthwatering gumbo ya-ya we had been eagerly anticipating. Each spoonful was a perfect balance of spiciness and savory flavors, meeting all the expectations we had for a gumbo. And then, the moment we had been warned about arrived—the barbecue shrimp, complete with heads and tails. We were provided with bibs to protect our attire before indulging in these incredibly flavorful and succulent shrimp. The accompanying sauce truly was divine, making the messy experience entirely worth it. There is no doubt in my mind that I wouldn't trade this dish for any other on the menu.

In terms of service, we were impressed by the friendly and efficient staff at Mr. B's. As for the prices, though slightly steep, the delectable food more than makes up for it. If the opportunity presents itself, I highly recommend giving their brunch a try for an unforgettable dining experience.

input:
Nice Steakhouse in St. Louis. We went here for a client dinner and was pleasantly surprised. You get a nice view of the arch on the way in to the restaurant as well. 

The Apps were OK. We ended up getting the Carmine's trio (crab cakes, scallops and toasted ravioli). Crab cakes were above average. The scallops were a little saccharine for my tastes but the ravioli was good; and let's face it...one doesn't come to St. Louis for the scallops. Thankfully the filet mignon was exceptional. It was the perfect size, not too salty and rare just like I had requested. 

This was partnered with an above average wine list to make a great night out.
Help me polish this:
The steakhouse in St. Louis that we visited for a client dinner turned out to be a pleasant surprise. Furthermore, on the way to the restaurant, we were treated to a nice view of the arch.

As for the appetizers, they were decent. We opted for the Carmine's trio, which consisted of crab cakes, scallops, and toasted ravioli. The crab cakes surpassed expectations and were above average. However, the scallops were a tad too sweet for my palate. Nonetheless, the ravioli was enjoyable, and let's be honest, one doesn't visit St. Louis specifically for the scallops. Fortunately, the filet mignon stole the spotlight, as it was truly exceptional. Perfectly sized, not overly seasoned, and cooked to the rareness I had requested.

To complement our dining experience, the restaurant offered an impressive wine list that exceeded expectations. It truly enhanced our overall evening and made it a memorable outing.

input: Three from my office had lunch delivered from San Antonio Taco today.  It was our first time from there.  The food did not live up to the reviews. input:
