The only complaints I have is with the produce (which is expected considering it is COUSIN'S after all) and the hours (like many others have said, they have awful and inconvenient hours post-5pm).

That being said, I can get most essentials here and for much cheaper than anywhere else. 

This is only a two minute bike ride from my apartment so there's no reason not to shop here. Matter of fact, I'm headed there tomorrow.

When it's too cold or you're feeling to cheap to go to Trader Joe's, Cousin's is the place to head to.
Help me polish this:
Cousin's is the go-to place in North Philly. Personally, I would choose this establishment any day over Fresh Grocer. However, I do have a couple of complaints. As expected, the produce section is not the best (though that is to be expected when shopping at COUSIN'S). Additionally, the hours are quite inconvenient, especially after 5pm, echoing the sentiment of many others.

Having said that, Cousin's is still the best option for getting most of your essentials at a much cheaper price compared to other stores. Its close proximity to my apartment, just a two-minute bike ride away, makes it the most convenient choice. In fact, I am planning to make a trip there tomorrow.

For those days when the weather is too cold or when you're trying to save some money, Cousin's is the perfect alternative to Trader Joe's.

input:
I've been here twice now and sampled a bunch of what they have to offer - I feel like what you order will really dictate how much you like this place.  i.e. they do some things great and other things just so-so.

The two things I will surely go back for more of is the Sausage and Pepper Pizza (capitalized - because I mean business) and some sort of puff pastry that has a white cream in the middle - I'm sure it has a name but it escapes me.  The pizza was perfectly flavored and the sausage/peppers had a nice kick to it.  Im sure it would make for great leftovers but unfortunately (fortunately?) for me it was gone well before it found the refrigerator.  The cream puff cream was just awesome - couldn't pin-point the flavor (vanilla?) but I would prefer it to top every dessert I get from this point forward.

I also got a bunch of the other sweets (salted brownie, blondie, red velvet crumb-cake) and a few bagels.  All were good, but not great.  Was pleasantly surprised by the wheat everything bagels - whole wheat bagels usually suck.

What I didn't really like was the pepperoni pizza.  It was pretty bland for my liking - in complete contrast to the sausage and pepper pizza - and the pepperoni was pretty sparse. I also didn't like being told 25 minutes, showing up in 25 minutes and then standing there for 25 minutes waiting for the pizza.  The small shop + no chairs = awkwardly standing there for almost a half hour.  

Since it's close to me and has so many tasty looking treats yet to try - I'll surely be back.  Hopefully I'll get more 'great' than 'so-so'.
Help me polish this:
I've visited this place twice now and have tried a variety of dishes. I must say that your experience here greatly depends on what you order. Some items are excellent while others are just average.

Without a doubt, I would highly recommend the Sausage and Pepper Pizza - it's simply amazing. The flavors are spot on, and the sausage and peppers give it a nice spicy kick. I regret not having any leftovers because it was so delicious. Additionally, there's a puff pastry with a luscious white cream filling that I couldn't get enough of. I can't recall its name, but it was absolutely fantastic. I wish I could have that cream on top of any dessert I consume in the future.

I also tried various other sweets like the salted brownie, blondie, and red velvet crumb-cake, as well as a few bagels. While they were good, they didn't reach the level of greatness. However, I was pleasantly surprised by the wheat everything bagels as I usually find whole wheat bagels to be disappointing.

Unfortunately, I wasn't a fan of the pepperoni pizza here. It lacked flavor compared to the outstanding Sausage and Pepper Pizza, and the amount of pepperoni was quite sparse. Another downside was the waiting time. I was told it would take 25 minutes, so I arrived promptly, but ended up standing awkwardly for another 25 minutes in the small shop with no chairs.

Despite these minor setbacks, I will definitely return to this place since it is conveniently located near me and has many enticing treats left for me to try. Hopefully, on my next visit, I'll have more "great" experiences rather than just "so-so."

input:
It is an actual speakeasy! Very cool and chill place. The ambience is classy but the vibe of the place is casual. Highly recommend if you just want to have good cocktails/drinks with good music. 
Warning: They literally serve one dish of appetizer (which is not that tasty). Don't go empty stomach and with expectation of good food (or any food). As I mentioned, it is true to its speakeasy status.
Help me polish this:
This place is a true speakeasy, offering a cool and laid-back atmosphere. The ambiance exudes class, while maintaining a casual vibe. I highly recommend this spot if you simply want to enjoy fantastic cocktails or drinks accompanied by great music.

However, I must give you a heads up that the food options are quite limited. They only serve one appetizer dish, but it may not be to your taste. It's best not to arrive hungry or with high expectations regarding the food. Just keep in mind that this place stays true to its speakeasy style.

input: Spent way too much money to get actually spoiled food delivered to us. Ordered a huge order, over 50% of it was incorrect. Will never return to this location.
Help me polish this: We were extremely disappointed with the recent delivery experience we had. Despite spending a significant amount of money, the food we received was spoiled. Moreover, to make matters worse, our order was filled with numerous mistakes, with over 50% of it being incorrect. This has left us deeply dissatisfied, and as a result, we will not be returning to this location in the future.

input: This is actually a 3 1/2 star review for me. Only because everything that I wanted they did not have or weren't willing to do. Firstly, I came here specifically for the chicken slider because from the picture it showed that you can get it on a biscuit and when I told the lady taking my order, she said they don't do that -__-. Then I wanted that buttermilk bites and they weren't available, however, my brother ordered the brown buttered cream sundae and got the buttermilk bites in that!! Oh yes, and the glazed donuts are so thick and dry. I liked the sliders I had though: fried chicken, beef belly and catfish(okay). And the sundae is pretty tasty. Good for a first try but not to continue coming.
Help me polish this: This is a 3 1/2 star review for me. The main reason for this rating is that the restaurant did not have the items I specifically wanted and were not willing to accommodate my requests. Firstly, I was disappointed when I asked for the chicken slider on a biscuit, as shown in the picture, and was informed that they did not offer that option. This was frustrating. Additionally, I had my heart set on trying the buttermilk bites, but unfortunately, they were not available. However, I was surprised to see that my brother's order, the brown buttered cream sundae, included the buttermilk bites. This inconsistency was confusing. On a positive note, I did enjoy the sliders I tried, particularly the fried chicken, beef belly, and catfish options. The sundae was also quite tasty. Overall, it was a decent first try, but I probably won't be returning due to the lack of availability and inconsistency.

input: A short walk from my apartment I was told about a small, welcoming cafe very popular for breakfast and brunch. It did not disappoint! I had a salmon scramble with egg whites the first time i went. The second time i went i got the tofu with brown rice breakfast plate. Both meals were great!! And i was seated quickly
Help me polish this: Just a short stroll away from my apartment, I had heard rave reviews about a small, cozy cafe that was known for its delightful breakfast and brunch menu. And let me tell you, it lived up to the hype! On my first visit, I decided to indulge myself with a scrumptious salmon scramble made with fluffy egg whites. The flavors were absolutely delightful! Encouraged by my first experience, I returned to the cafe a second time and opted for their tantalizing tofu with brown rice breakfast plate. Once again, I was not disappointed! The meals were exceptional, and what made the experience even better was the swift seating. The hospitality of this charming cafe was truly remarkable.

input: Went for Dinner at 6pm on a Friday and expect it to be packed, luckily for us, it wasn't. The staff is very friendly and the atmosphere is straight out of Magnolia Journal. The food was pretty dang good and drinks are too. The only reason I left off a star was the fact it took a little while to get our cocktails and our appetizer came at the same time as our food. But, they're new and I've been in hospitality before, so I get it!
Help me polish this: I went for dinner at 6 pm on a Friday expecting it to be packed, but fortunately, it wasn't. The staff was incredibly friendly, and the atmosphere had a charming and cozy vibe reminiscent of the Magnolia Journal. To my delight, the food turned out to be quite delicious, and the drinks were equally enjoyable. I deducted one star from my rating, however, due to the slight delay in receiving our cocktails and the fact that our appetizer arrived simultaneously with our main course. Nevertheless, I understand that they are a new establishment, and having worked in hospitality myself, these minor hiccups are forgivable.

input: This is a great quiet place to eat very 1960's business style.  You can have the food of Tony's or eat off the bar menu.  I had the Risotto which was excellent.  Other people at the table had the special, linguine with shrimp and lobster, and strip steak.  Everyone loved their meals.  Of course the service here is fantastic.  They are not overbearing but attentive as well.
Help me polish this: This establishment offers a wonderful ambiance reminiscent of the tranquility and sophistication of 1960's business settings. It provides the option to indulge in the delightful cuisine from Tony's renowned menu, or savor the delectable offerings available on the bar menu. Personally, I thoroughly enjoyed their exquisite Risotto, which was prepared to perfection. The individuals accompanying me at the table opted for the daily special, which consisted of linguine adorned with succulent shrimp and lobster, as well as the mouthwatering strip steak. Without exception, everyone raved about their meals, undoubtedly savoring every bite. The impeccable service at this establishment is truly noteworthy - it strikes the perfect balance between attentiveness and giving guests ample space.

input: My go to place for sushi rolls! Their rolls are huge and the service is excellent. My favorite is heat attack appetizer( korean style jalapeno poppers) sapporo roll and honey roll. They also have a section of deepfried rolls on the menu! Their food always look so  fresh and appetizing. Great presentation. Try the spicy sashimi bowl if you wanna try something new!
Help me polish this: My absolute favorite spot for sushi rolls! Not only are their rolls absolutely massive, but the service is top-notch as well. I highly recommend trying their delightful Heat Attack appetizer, which features Korean-style jalapeno poppers. The Sapporo Roll and Honey Roll are my personal go-tos, bursting with incredible flavors. And you can't miss their unique deep-fried rolls, prominently displayed on the menu. Their food always looks incredibly fresh and appetizing, presented in such an eye-catching way. If you're feeling adventurous, I urge you to give their Spicy Sashimi Bowl a try - it's a truly unique experience!

input:
Ok. I am not the type to complain, but I have been here twice and both times I have had terrible service at the bar. The first bartender served me but acted as if I was bothering him.  This second time, with a completely different bartender mind you, it was worse. I am not dressed like a street person or anything, and I am not pan-handling. But you would think that I was the way he acted. First, I sit at the bar and I am waiting for service. So, the bartender walks by me, pours a glass a water, turns in front of me, puts the water down, gives me some stupid half-grin then walks off. Not one audible word of greeting or a grunt passed between his lips. Then, he gets a menu, drops that down and walks off again! Not a sound. Is it me, but when a customer enters an eating establishment, shouldn't they be greeted in some manner?  Not looked at like "why are you here. I have better things to do"?  I am not looking for a royal salute or anything. Just "Hey man, what can I get ya?"  or something to that affect.   Anyway, I start to look at the drink and food menus. Then, a group of anywhere from 10-15 people come in behind me and say, to what looked like a manager, "We don't want to eat, is it ok if we just have a few drinks at the bar?". The manager says "Sure." The guy then says, "Can we get few beers down here"? (paraphrasing). The bartender says "Sure!" and proceed to service this group, one-by-one, as they order drinks. Ok, fine technically, I was looking at the menu when this started. But still, he walked back and forth, right in front of me, for about 10-12 minutes. Not once did he say, "Hey, just shout and I will get you something", or "Hey man, just give me a few minutes and I will be right with you". Nothing!  It was obvious it was a big group, but I mean, he gave no acknowledgement to the fact that I was sitting there waiting! 

Long story short - after this 10-12 minutes of waiting, I just walked out and went somewhere else. Now this place has about 4\5 stars with around 500 reviews. So, I guess people like it. But their bartenders are as unfriendly as I have ever encountered.  Maybe if you get a table it's different.
Help me polish this:
Okay, so I'm not usually one to complain, but I've had an unpleasant experience at this bar twice now. Both times, the service was terrible. The first bartender seemed bothered by my presence and barely acknowledged me. It was even worse this second time, with a different bartender. I want to clarify that I was dressed appropriately and not causing any trouble, but the bartender treated me as if I didn't belong there. 

I sat at the bar, waiting for service. The bartender passed by me, poured a glass of water, placed it in front of me without a word, and walked away with a half-hearted grin. No greeting, no acknowledgement whatsoever. Then, he grabbed a menu, dropped it in front of me, and walked off again, still without saying a word. Isn't it customary for customers to be greeted when they enter an eating establishment? I shouldn't feel like I'm bothering the staff just by being there. 

As I started looking at the menus, a group of 10-15 people entered behind me and asked the manager if they could have a few drinks at the bar without dining. The manager agreed, and the bartender immediately began serving the group, one by one, without any hesitation. I understand I was still looking at the menu at that point, but the bartender continuously passed by me for about 10-12 minutes, completely ignoring my presence. He didn't even offer a simple "I'll be right with you" or acknowledge that I was waiting. 

In the end, I decided to walk out and find another place to go. Despite this establishment having a high rating with hundreds of positive reviews, I couldn't ignore the unfriendliness of their bartenders. Perhaps the experience would have been different if I had chosen to sit at a table instead.

input:
Love it here

The atmosphere is great the options are more than average and the lunch bento boxes are great.  If you have the opportunity always try the boba as well.

Those complaining are just picky and should go back to eating at home.  

Try their beef braised soup as it is hearty and delicious.
Help me polish this:
I absolutely love it here! The atmosphere is superb and the variety of options available is beyond average. The lunch bento boxes are simply fantastic, and I highly recommend trying them. If you get the chance, don't miss out on their boba drinks too — they are truly worth experiencing.

As for those who complain, they seem to be overly picky and might be better off dining at home instead.

One dish you must definitely try is their beef braised soup. It's incredibly hearty and delightfully delicious.

input: Beautiful decor, great atmosphere, amazing food! My husband and I were thinking how it's NY prices but better quality than most we have had at this price point. He had udon noodles and I had a few rolls (Spicy Salmon is a must!) Flavors were great- not too strong but tasteful! :) We enjoyed our experience!
Help me polish this: The restaurant's beautiful decor, great atmosphere, and amazing food left a lasting impression on my husband and me. Despite the prices being similar to those in New York, the quality surpassed our expectations. My husband indulged in the udon noodles, while I savored a selection of rolls, with the Spicy Salmon being an absolute must-try! The flavors were perfectly balanced, not overpowering but still delightfully tasteful. Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed our dining experience!

input: Hotel is lovely. The front desk staff is extremely friendly and helpful. We were lucky enough to get a room away from the club so we had no problem sleeping. If you are looking for quiet stay somewhere else if you looking for fun this is perfect!
Help me polish this: The hotel is absolutely delightful. The front desk staff is exceptionally friendly and eager to assist. We were fortunate to be assigned a room away from the club, which ensured a peaceful night's sleep. However, if tranquility is what you seek, it may be more suitable to consider an alternative option. This hotel is an ideal choice for those seeking a vibrant and lively atmosphere.

input: I loved loved loved the pizza here. I returned and got their gnocchi and it was amazing as well. Really fresh ingredients nice variety on the menu. Really felt like a small family restaurant in Europe. Best pizza in middle Tennessee.
Help me polish this: I absolutely adored the pizza at this place, I mean, I loved loved loved it! I decided to come back again and this time I ordered their gnocchi, and let me tell you, it was mind-blowing. The ingredients were incredibly fresh, and the menu had a nice variety of options to choose from. The atmosphere gave off a cozy vibe, reminiscent of a small family restaurant in Europe. Without a doubt, hands down, this is the best pizza in middle Tennessee.

input: For a $16 haircut, I was expecting an OK-looking trim (all I really needed was some damage control - just someone to lop off my split ends and maybe add a few layers).  What I got was a very professionally looking haircut that works well with my face shape and made my hair a lot healthier and happier.  My expectations were far exceeded - and it definitely surpassed my last 'professional' hair salon experience.  Plus, the shampoo smelled amazing and the girl was really thorough.  I wish I had brought more cash to tip her!!!  The only thing you should keep in mind before going is time.  I had to wait an extra half an hour and it was the longest haircut I've ever had.  I would much rather have the student take the time to make sure it looks good, however, than have someone do a half-ass job.  I think it's important that the school has a series of steps and checklists their students have to go through to ensure they are giving you the best experience possible.  Just make sure you have a decent block of time in your schedule to relax in the chair!
Help me polish this:
I was pleasantly surprised with my $16 haircut experience. Initially, I was only expecting a basic trim to fix my split ends and maybe add some layers. However, I received a professionally executed haircut that perfectly complemented my face shape and significantly improved the health and appearance of my hair. It definitely exceeded my expectations and surpassed my previous salon visits, which claimed to be professional. 

Furthermore, the shampoo used during the process had an amazing scent, and the stylist was extremely diligent. I regret not having brought more cash to tip her generously. 

The only aspect to consider before going is the time commitment. I had to wait an additional half hour, resulting in the longest haircut I've ever had. Nevertheless, I believe it's crucial for the student to invest the necessary time to ensure a satisfactory outcome rather than rush through the process. It gives me confidence to know that the school institutes a series of steps and checklists to guarantee the best possible experience for their clients. Just be sure to allocate a decent block of time in your schedule to fully relax in the chair.

input: My daughter was married at the Presidio Chapel in May, 2015. The wedding was magical and we were all treated really well by Rain Longo(she coordinates special events in the Chapel). She was very patient, supportive and enthusiastic. The chapel itself made for an outstanding and very authentic venue. My daughter and bridesmaids were able to get ready in a beautiful adjoining room. The rental of the Chapel included use for 6 hours and it was very affordable. Thanks to all for making this special day so perfect. Thanks!!!!
Help me polish this:
My daughter's wedding at the Presidio Chapel in May 2015 was truly magical. The entire experience was made even more memorable thanks to the exceptional service provided by Rain Longo, who expertly coordinated all the special events at the Chapel. Rain demonstrated great patience, support, and enthusiasm throughout the planning process. 

The Chapel itself served as an outstanding and authentic venue, creating a truly unique atmosphere for the wedding. In addition, the beautiful adjoining room provided a perfect space for my daughter and her bridesmaids to get ready. 

One aspect that made the Chapel an excellent choice was the affordability of the rental. With a generous six-hour timeframe included, we felt that we received great value for the price. 

I would like to express my sincere gratitude to everyone involved in making this day so perfect. Your dedication and hard work contributed greatly to the success of the wedding. Thank you again for creating such wonderful memories.

input:
I'm not a regular waxer, but went in for a pre-vacation treat. The wax specialist Miriam was prompt and knew what she was doing. She spent much of our hour together telling me why my regular shaving is bad and waxing is good, and seriously marketing the EWC products to me. 
Brows and lower legs were done well. Underarms were left with a decent number of stray hairs which she told me I could tweeze out later. Little bits of wax were left on my skin here and there. Overall I felt like I did not walk out of there ready to hit the beach.
Help me polish this:
I'm not an avid waxer myself, but I decided to treat myself to a pre-vacation wax. Miriam, the wax specialist, was prompt and clearly experienced. Throughout our session, she took time to explain the drawbacks of regular shaving and the benefits of waxing, all while promoting EWC products.

The shaping of my brows and the waxing of my lower legs were done well. However, I noticed that there were still a noticeable amount of stray hairs left in my underarm area, which Miriam suggested I could tweeze out later. Additionally, I found remnants of wax on my skin in some areas. The overall outcome left me feeling less prepared for the beach than I had hoped for.

input:
The food was very good. The reason for the three stars is the noise level. I was with three other people in a corner table and we had to shout to hear each other. If the restaurant could work on the noise level, it would absolutely get more stars. The pad see ew got great reviews from the person who ordered it. I got The King and I (veg/chicken/shrimp stir fry) and it was excellent. Nice heat and curry flavor. The pad thai was a bit sweet I thought, but the person who ordered it really liked it.

Portion sizes are not enormous. We had some leftovers but also didn't come in starving.

Good service, very attentive. The noise level was the only negative.
Help me polish this: The food at this restaurant was delicious. However, I gave it three stars due to the high noise level. I was seated at a corner table with three other people, and we had to shout in order to hear each other. If the restaurant could address the noise issue, it would definitely receive a higher rating. One person in our group highly recommended the pad see ew, which received great reviews. I personally had The King and I (a stir fry with vegetables, chicken, and shrimp), and it was excellent. The dish had a nice level of heat and a flavorful curry taste. Although, I found the pad thai to be a bit too sweet, the person who ordered it really enjoyed it. The portion sizes were moderate, allowing us to have some leftovers without feeling overly full. The service was good, with attentive staff. Overall, the only negative aspect was the noise level.

input:
***Please note that if you lose something valuable you may not get it back. The person who may clean the vehicle may be a thief. I left in the car my radar detector complete with a case not logged in to their lost and found. When I check in my rental on 12/21 and returned 01/02/2018 to visit the counter they told me nothing was found. They also told me that for something with a case go missing was very unlikely. Yet they found nothing. Hmmm, I wonder how it can go missing when it was the only place I left it? I filed a lost ticket with them; Reference Number: 4355421, Reported: 12/21/2017.

They may think their employees may be honest but my $300 radar detector is nowhere to be found at their location. So? Yes, one of their employee's stole it. 

I'm a fan of the concept of picking your car. As someone who has been using the same rental place in St. Louis Airport for 8 months and counting. I can tell you they do lousy job at cleaning the cars. I'm always finding plastic bottles underneath the back seats.

I'm also finding a lot un-wiped of front seat and dashboard areas full of sticky substances. The cars are never fully clean as someone who rents from them weekly.

This location does a shitty job of making cars ready for travel. As someone who has access to the execute cars due to the amount of travel I do. They fail to meet some simple travel requirements you expect when you rent. 

Next time you rent look underneath the seats in the passenger areas and you may find plastic bottle under them.

I would love for them to review the cameras and see who cleaned the car so they can fire them on the day I returned the rental! I brought them thousand of dollars and I do expect a refund for the stolen item.
Help me polish this:
***Please note that there is a possibility of not recovering lost valuable items. It is important to consider that the person responsible for cleaning the vehicle may potentially be a thief. In my case, I had left my radar detector, along with its case, inside the car without registering it in their lost and found system. When I checked in my rental on 12/21 and returned on 01/02/2018 to inquire at the counter, I was informed that nothing had been found. Despite being told that it was unlikely for an item with a case to go missing, no trace of my radar detector was discovered. This raises questions about how it could have vanished when the car was the only place I left it. I filed a lost ticket with them, providing the reference number: 4355421, and reported the incident on 12/21/2017.

Although the rental company may believe their employees to be trustworthy, my $300 radar detector cannot be located at their facility, leading me to surmise that one of their employees may have stolen it.

As a patron of this particular rental company at St. Louis Airport for the past 8 months, I have noticed a lackadaisical approach to cleaning the cars. Plastic bottles are consistently discovered underneath the back seats, and the front seat and dashboard areas are often left with sticky substances. The cars are never thoroughly cleaned, which is disappointing for someone like myself who rents from them on a weekly basis.

Inadequate preparation of the vehicles for travel seems to be a recurring issue at this location. Given the amount of travel I undertake and my access to executive vehicles, I anticipate certain basic travel requirements to be fulfilled when I rent a car.

I encourage future renters to inspect the passenger areas underneath the seats, where you may find plastic bottles left behind.

It would be greatly appreciated if the rental company reviewed their surveillance footage to determine who cleaned the car on the day of my return, potentially leading to the dismissal of the responsible individual. Considering the significant amount of money I have brought to their business, I expect a refund for the stolen item as a reasonable resolution.

input: This place is so great. I love the laid back atmosphere. Walked right in with our dog and were seating on the cozy wrap around porch outside. We ate here the last morning of our trip and it was the perfect ending. I stayed full long enough to get me through and 8 hour car ride home! I had the bananas foster French toast which was amazing but super rich. I couldn't eat it all because of the portion size and richness. My fiancé opted for the healthier choice of a vegetable omelet which was delicious as well. I can't wait to come back here and try something else on the menu. I will definitely try one of their famous juices next time.
Help me polish this:
This place is absolutely amazing. I am enamored by the laid-back atmosphere it offers. As soon as we walked in with our furry friend, we were promptly seated on the cozy wrap-around porch outside. It was the perfect spot to enjoy our last morning of the trip, and it left us feeling fully satisfied for the upcoming 8-hour car ride home!

I opted for the bananas foster French toast, and it was beyond incredible. However, I must admit it was incredibly rich and the portion size was quite generous. I couldn't finish it all, but that didn't take away from how much I enjoyed it. On the other hand, my fiancé made a healthier choice with the vegetable omelet, and it was equally delicious.

Looking forward to returning to this gem and exploring more options on their enticing menu. Next time, I am definitely going to sample one of their famous juices for a refreshing twist.

input: The food here is delicious and the portions are amazing for the price.  The girl who works behind the counter is an absolute sweetheart.  Always smiling and happy.   I wish I worked closer so I could come more often.
Help me polish this: The food at this place is simply delectable, and the portion sizes offered at such an affordable price are truly incredible. Moreover, the girl who diligently attends to customers behind the counter is an absolute gem. Her constant cheerful demeanor and radiant smile never fail to brighten up my day. If only my workplace were closer, I would happily become a regular here.

input: Nice scenery of nature. Great trail for running, walking, hiking and biking. Plenty of places to sit for a short break along the way.
Help me polish this: Experience the breathtaking beauty of nature with its stunning scenery. Immerse yourself in the great outdoors through a trail that is perfect for running, walking, hiking, and biking. This trail not only offers an invigorating workout, but also provides numerous idyllic spots to pause and take a well-deserved break amidst serene surroundings.

input: Really truly slow service.  Not the waitress. The kitchen. 40 min to get a pasta and salad.  Recommended if you want to really drag that date out.
Help me polish this: Exceptionally sluggish service, and I don't just mean our waiter. The kitchen was painfully slow, taking a whopping 40 minutes to serve a simple pasta and salad. If you're looking to elongate your date to the extreme, this place comes highly recommended.

input: This place is wonderful! Obviously the chips, salsa and beans are yummy, but get the guacamole too! The chimichanga bites are fantastic, whatever the sauce is that comes with them is super good! For dinner, the street tacos are amazing, so are the enchiladas. They don't have a full bar, but you can still get a real margarita, and they pack a punch! They make them at their other location and bring them over, which is clever, because this location doesn't yet have its liquor license. Overall 4 out 5 stars because it's a good Mexican restaurant, but 5 stars is reserved for my most favorites only. Close second though, and we love that it's right downtown. Oh, and the service... very good! We usually always have the same server, and she is very nice and attentive.
Help me polish this: This place is absolutely wonderful! Not only are the chips, salsa, and beans delicious, but you have to try the guacamole too! The chimichanga bites are simply fantastic, and the accompanying sauce is incredibly flavorful. When it comes to dinner, both the street tacos and enchiladas are amazing. Although they don't have a full bar, you can still enjoy a real margarita that really packs a punch! The clever idea of making them at their other location and bringing them over is pretty impressive, especially since this location hasn't obtained its liquor license yet. I would give this restaurant 4 out of 5 stars because it's undeniably a great Mexican restaurant, although I reserve 5 stars for my absolute favorites. Nonetheless, it's a close second and the fact that it's conveniently located downtown is a major plus. Oh, and let's not forget about the service... it's really top-notch! We typically have the same server every time we visit, and she is incredibly friendly and attentive.

input: Holy _____! Good rolls. Great service. Good prices. Lots of healthy options. Try the sushi. It worth every penny!
Help me polish this: Holy Mackerel! Incredible rolls, exceptional service, unbeatable prices, and an abundance of healthy options. Don't miss out on their heavenly sushi—it's worth every single penny!

input: We had an excellent lunch here. The food was great and the service was fantastic. Great Gumbo Ya Ya, great BBQ shrimp, delicious crab cakes. Everything we tried was good. I highly recommend this place.
Help me polish this: We had an outstanding lunch at this place. The food was remarkable, and the service was exceptional. The Gumbo Ya Ya and BBQ shrimp were both outstanding, and the crab cakes were absolutely delicious. Every dish we tried exceeded our expectations. We cannot recommend this place highly enough.

input:

input: As a fan of the late night kabab, shwarma or gyro in nyc, I made a stop through Ali ba ba's on one occasion and ended up here again near the end of the trip as it hits the spot! Help me polish this: As a passionate enthusiast of late night kabab, shwarma, or gyro in NYC, I found myself making a pit stop at Ali ba ba's during one of my visits to New Orleans. To my delight, I ended up returning to this joint towards the end of my trip as it truly hits the spot! The gyros here are larger in size compared to the ones I typically get in NYC, although they do come at a higher price of $6. I suppose the increased cost can be attributed to the limited demand (resulting in shorter lines) and the locals' preference for po boys over gyros. While it's a pity that they only offer rooster sauce as hot sauce, which leaves something to be desired, the quality of their gyros surpasses that of the nearby $5 dollar slices or the slightly pricier lucky dogs found on the corner. Despite occasionally experiencing slow service, Ali ba ba's remains my top choice for a satisfying gyro fix in NOLA.

input:

The mashed taters were creamy with a slight hint of garlic. Mmmm.

I preferred my husband's halibut over my tuna. The tuna was good, but the halibut had more flavor, IMO.

Can't wait to go back again. Yum yum yum.

input:
I purchased a used 09 Rav4 from Glanzmann Subaru last month. Coming from TN, I chose to purchase this vehicle from Glanzmann due to its limited availability and attractive price. I communicated with sales on numerous occasions before committing to purchase from Glanzmann nearly 1000 miles from home.

The process was overall quite simple, though I felt we could have gotten alot more done regarding interstate complications prior to completing travel plans to purchase the vehicle. My only actual complaint stems from the vehicle's description. As an out of state buyer, I was at the mercy of the sales team to accurately describe and depict any conditional issues that might be of interest to a prospective buyer. Unfortunately, none of the issues with this vehicle were highlighted, depicted, described, or otherwise demonstrated throughout the entire sales process. I even asked the sales agent to, while on the phone, inspect the vehicle and describe any possible imperfection so that I could have no surprises upon arrival. I spent several hundred dollars in travel expenses to collect this vehicle, only to discover there were a number of aesthetic defects that deserved attention (large dents, cracked paint, cuts in leather). I had limited time and opportunity to react to these conditional flaws and purchased the vehicle - I had already flown from Nashville to Philadelphia! 

This is obviously a small family-owned dealership. I expected a considerably more honest and direct interaction and was disappointed with the outcome. The automobile is a fine machine, but the defects certainly take away from the value. Mr. Jeff Glanzmann, I implore you to make honesty your #1 policy.  I had the opportunity to purchase the same vehicle, with honestly similar defects, from a dealership in Atlanta for the same price. I opted to purchase yours, incurring not-insignificant travel expenses, because of it's immaculate description.

input:
My girlfriends and I ate at the Creole House for dinner. Our decision to dine here was largely based on the fact that it was pouring raining and this restaurant is next door to our hotel. We started with the bacon garlic oysters and jumbo buffalo wings. The bacon garlic oysters were average, at best. The oysters were overpowered by the cheese and bacon, which was disappointing. The buffalo wings were pretty good and seasoned well. For entrees, we ordered: 1) jumbalaya pasta, 2) blackened red fish and 3) canal street red fish. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite (would not order again). The blackened red fish was just okay and the skimpy side of sautéed veggies (spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms) were VERY salty (would order again as a LAST resort). The canal street red fish wasn't great but my friend would order it again. Her biggest complaint was that it had very little garlic sauce. We also ordered paddle boat drinks, which tasted good but were more juice vs alcohol (had to order an extra shot).

So, overall, we were underwhelmed with the food, making it a solid 3 stars. On a positive note, our server, Alexander, was great...very hospitable and tried his best to make sure we were satisfied.
Help me polish this:
My girlfriends and I decided to have dinner at the Creole House, mainly because it was conveniently located right next to our hotel and it was pouring rain outside. To start off our meal, we opted for the bacon garlic oysters and jumbo buffalo wings. Unfortunately, the bacon garlic oysters were just average. The flavors of the cheese and bacon overpowered the oysters, which was quite disappointing. On the other hand, the buffalo wings were tasty and well-seasoned.

Moving on to our main courses, we ordered three dishes: the jumbalaya pasta, the blackened red fish, and the canal street red fish. Regrettably, the jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite dish of the evening. We wouldn't order it again. The blackened red fish was decent, but the accompanying sautéed veggies (spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms) were excessively salty. We would only consider ordering it again as a last resort. As for the canal street red fish, although it didn't impress us, one of my friends mentioned that she would still order it again despite its lack of garlic sauce.

In addition to our food, we also tried the paddle boat drinks. While they tasted good, we felt that they were more juice than alcohol, so we ended up ordering an extra shot to enhance the drink.

Overall, our dining experience was underwhelming, leading us to rate our visit at a solid 3 stars. However, we should highlight that our server, Alexander, was exceptional. He provided excellent service, was incredibly hospitable, and made every effort to ensure our satisfaction.

input:
Okay, don't jump on me for this, but its partially my fault because I held them to such high expectations (due to the hype and anticipation of them opening up here) before actually eating at this location. I read so much about it on Facebook and the likes......so reading and seeing the yummy pics; well I just knew it would be all that.....untill yesterday.....

Me and my bf Vince went to BlackFinn for Sunday lunch yesterday. The atmosphere was cool and it was really nice inside. The staff was pleasant as well, so I'm thinking "hum...I like...". We ordered  a couple of mojitos and we also had another drink, which was okay.  Time to order; I ordered the Cuban sandwich, hold the mustard, and add mayo instead....with Black Finn fries and my bf ordered the Prime Rib sandwich with au jus and the same fries.  We got our order, which took a bit of time but it was okay. Everything looked so yummy and I knew they were going to meet my expectations. Now mind ya, my bf put off going to BlackFinn since they day they opened and I've been on him to go here. So anyway, the fries were a bit salty, but good. I had a choice of two dipping sauces, which I believe were ranch and barbeque. Delicious! I bit into the sandwich and what did I taste? A mouth full of mustard!!! Eeewww!! Okay, did I not say "hold the mustard"? So lo and behold, my food had to be returned while my bf ate his food. His beef about his sandwich (no pun intended) was that there was more bread than meat. I looked at it and I noticed the same thing. Also, the au jus was a bit low as well and wasn't enough for the sandwich.  So I'm like the little old lady from the back-in-the-day commercials saying "Where's the beef?" LOL. Wow! 

Finally, after he finishes his sandwich, my food finally comes out and guess what? They left the swiss cheese off the sandwich. WTF! Okay, so at this point I'm like "forget it, just take it back." How many times must I send my sandwich back to get it right? Now I must say that the manager on duty was accommodating and she took care of the check and apolgized for the errors. So for her professionalism and the fact that the staff was very polite, I give them two stars. Will I go back....yes I will give them another chance to redeem themselves, but all in my ear is my bf saying that there must have been a reason why he hesitated to come here and this is why.  Oh well......

input:
I have to start out by saying, why do those who like hookah not know about this place?! It was such a wonderful experience! Please hear me out!

My mission on this review is to get the word out! A friend and I went spur of the moment and I'm glad we did. From the outside of the building you wouldn't know it was a hookah bar (except the giant sign of course lol). The moment you open that giant wooden door, the decor and paint color gives it that authentic look. Warm yellow paint with evil eyes and giant metal wall lamps with cutouts shining red surrounding all the walls.
When you go up a few steps there's a gift shop, a table, and the register. They ask you to take a seat upstairs and they follow you shortly after. (There's even another upstairs that I barely peaked at).
This is the amazing part: cushions on the floor with giant metal mandala tables!!!! It was so authentic I could barely handle my excitement. They have a menu with drinks, food and hookah. Water was only a dollar which was amazing because hookah bars are usually pretty pricy.
We smoked "sex on the beach" flavored shisha. It was smooth! Very smooth! We even brought bubbles for the trip to have a little fun :)
What I like about this place compared to other loud hookah bars is that it wasn't even close to being hectic. I felt like I should have whispered at first, but after awhile I was more comfortable. Only one other couple was there and they were very nice to talk to as well. The older man and the young guy was extremely nice. The younger dude checked in on us and was sociable which was really kinda nice but not overbearing.

If you are seeking a laid-back, serene, and relaxing hookah bar experience, this establishment undoubtedly deserves a top spot on your list.

input:
3.50 stars.  

Gabby's wasn't open.  I knew that.  Neither was Rotier's.  But my handy Yelp app had assured me that Fido's was open.  Imagine the disappointment when I realized there was a very real possibility that no burgers would happen on this trip down to the Deep South.  Would I really have to wait two more weeks when I would find solace in East Texas?   

"We can try Burger up," I mentioned.  

"Why don't you just call them?" hissed the appropriately nicknamed Viper.  

True.  We didn't have to keep driving around aimlessly.  So I call Burger Up, and a very pleasant, sweet voice assures me they are indeed open.  

Viper: "What was her name?  She sounded hot."
  
Me: "Paige."

Viper: "Yeah, she's definitely hot.  Have you ever met an unattractive Paige?"

Me: "Good point.  At least we have that going for us."

Paige was indeed attractive, but this review isn't about a photogenic individual who happens to work at Burger Up.  It's about what ended up being a visit to our fourth choice for burgers in Nashville.  

Burger Up follows a national trend towards upscale burgers.  My particular order consisted of a medium rare patty served with aged cheddar, Benton's bacon (very good), and ketchup served on an artisan bun.  Basically, it was a gussied up bacon cheeseburger, but it was a rather tasty one.  My major complaint is that I wish the actual meat itself exhibited more flavor.  Having said that, the burger was cooked properly and the flavors worked well together.  I ordered some wilted spinach on the side (mediocre) and truffle fries.  Let's talk about those truffle fries for a bit.  I know more people are apparently into the sweet potato fries here, but I think they are missing the boat.  Burger Up's truffle tries have pleasant aroma, taste great, and are the perfect texture for soaking up oil.  If you are on a diet, it is true you should skip these delightful fries.  But if that were the case, why are you at a burger joint in the first place?  Seriously, if you get nothing else out of my review, please do yourself a favor and order the truffle fries.  

Burger Up also boast an interesting beer menu with semi-obscure breweries from the Deep South included in the list.  I tried a pecan-infused amber from Mississippi - not bad.  I could imagine Burger Up could be a decent place to drink for a bit after eating.  

If I attended Vanderbilt, I would probably go here on a moderately frequent basis.  If you want a change from the dive bar hamburger, Burger Up is a decent change of pace.

input: Very cute place with a great selection of loose leaf teas and other tea paraphernalia. The drinks and sweets are delicious and creative. Great relaxing ambience. As a tea lover, I loved reading the books about tea that the owner had. The owner is very nice and is very knowledgeable and passionate about tea. I would love to come back again!
Help me polish this: This charming establishment offers an exceptional variety of loose leaf teas and a delightful array of tea accessories. The delectable drinks and creative sweets tantalize the taste buds in the most delightful way. The ambient atmosphere is perfect for relaxation, making it an absolute haven for tea enthusiasts. As a tea lover myself, I thoroughly enjoyed perusing the collection of tea-themed books curated by the passionate owner. Their deep knowledge and devotion to tea were truly inspiring. Without a doubt, I cannot wait to return to this enchanting place!

input: Great food and service. The antipasto was by far the best that I have ever had.  The pasta is all fresh and full of flavor. The Fisherman's stew was loaded with great tender fish in a saffron sauce.
Help me polish this: Exceptional food and service. The antipasto surpassed any I have ever tasted, leaving me utterly impressed. Each pasta dish was crafted with fresh ingredients and bursting with delicious flavors. The Fisherman's stew stood out with its abundance of tender fish swimming in a delectable saffron sauce.

input: Muriel's is a great stop in NOLA. The goat cheese and shrimp crepes are by far the best food I ate in the city (perhaps anywhere ever) and the rest of the meal lived up to the appetizer. Service is great, venue is quintessential French Quarter. It's a little distracting to see ghost tours outside the window at dinner- but the food is so delicious, you won't mind the audience. Rumor has it that Muriel's is haunted, but the only thing other worldly I encountered was the cuisine.
Help me polish this: Muriel's in NOLA is a must-visit spot. Without a doubt, the goat cheese and shrimp crepes there are the most incredible dish I have ever tasted, not just in the city, but possibly anywhere. And let me tell you, the rest of the meal definitely lives up to the expectations set by this phenomenal appetizer. The service at Muriel's is exceptional, and the venue itself perfectly embodies the charm of the French Quarter. Though the occasional distraction of ghost tours passing by the window during dinner can be a tad unsettling, the delectable food makes it easy to overlook. While there may be rumors of hauntings at Muriel's, the only otherworldly experience you'll have is with the outstanding cuisine.

input: Went to this Taco Bell last night.  It was 1 30 and it said 30 minutes to close.  All the lights were on.  We backed up and forward twice and no one would wait on us.  We gave up and pulled up young man was at window closing  register.  Taco Bell was happy to serve us.
Help me polish this: Last night, my friends and I visited Taco Bell. It was around 1:30 AM, and the sign indicated that there were still 30 minutes until closing time. Despite the lights being on, we couldn't get anyone to assist us when we pulled up to the drive-thru. Frustrated, we decided to give up and began to reverse our car. However, just as we were about to leave, a young man appeared at the window, closing the register. Surprisingly, he was more than willing to take our order, and Taco Bell ended up serving us with a smile.

input: Cute place to eat at. Ate breakfast here and was dissappointed after seeing such good reviews. Breakfast menu is very limited. The omlet was just OK.  Biscuit didnt have much flavor to it. We were able to be seated really quick (during the week) but i imagine it getting really crowded during the weekends.
Help me polish this: This place was touted as a cute dining spot, but unfortunately, my breakfast experience here left me quite disappointed. Despite the positive reviews, the breakfast menu was surprisingly limited. The omelet I ordered was mediocre at best, lacking any outstanding qualities. The biscuit I tried was rather bland and lacked flavor. On the bright side, we were promptly seated, possibly due to it being a weekday. However, considering the crowd that can be expected on weekends, I can imagine that securing a table might be quite challenging.

input:
Probably the most expensive game in town. But totally worth it for me. I upgraded myself to the executive locker rooms because that gives me zero excuses for why I can't go to the gym before work or after if I am going out later that night. I always have my makeup, hair stuff, etc in my locker. Just getting back to the gym after a long absence due to health issues so I'm taking it slow. I've seen one or two machines that are not quite working right but the facility as a whole is pretty sharp & welcoming. You have tons of options of what to do classes wise, equipment wise...
My only 2 down sides are that I wish they were open a little later on weekends, but that's just me moving slowly on my time off. I wish there was a bit more ritation with the class schedule. There are classes I'd like to take but they always run mid day, never really early, after work or weekends. So no option to try them. I'm sure it's an instructor issue so not likely something that will change. Overall I'm super happy that I joined.
Help me polish this:
The gym I recently joined is probably the most expensive one in town, but it's definitely worth the cost for me. I upgraded to the executive locker rooms, which eliminates any excuses for me to skip my workout before or after work, even if I have plans later in the evening. With all my makeup, hair products, and other essentials stored in my locker, I'm always prepared. 

After dealing with health issues for a while, I am slowly getting back into my fitness routine, and the gym provides a supportive environment for that. Although I've noticed a few machines that are not functioning properly, I find the overall facility to be well-maintained and inviting. There are countless options for classes and equipment, allowing me to diversify my workouts. 

However, there are two downsides I've experienced. Firstly, I wish the gym had longer weekend hours as I tend to move at a slower pace during my days off. Secondly, I would appreciate more flexibility in the class schedule. Many of the classes I'm interested in only run during midday hours, making it impossible for me to try them out due to work and weekend commitments. I suspect this issue lies with the instructors and is unlikely to change. 

Despite these minor inconveniences, I am extremely satisfied with my decision to join this gym.

input:

Help me polish this:

input: Not to bad. I sat at the bar and the bartender was awesome. The lunch menu here is very decent and the beer is ice cold.  I usually come during lunch when it isn't to congested. So, to get consistent service,  go when it isn't to congested. I will definitely go back?
Help me polish this: Not too bad. I had a great time sitting at the bar, and the bartender was awesome. The lunch menu here is quite decent, and the beer is always served ice-cold. I usually prefer coming during lunch hours when it's not too crowded, as it allows for more consistent service. I will definitely be coming back!

input: The only knock on this place is that they didn't have all the pools open during Memorial Day weekend. Other than that the hotel provides a very friendly environment that's good for adults and families as well plenty of places to eat inside the resort and the atrium was amazing and really fun to explore. Little far from town but a good middle point between music row and the airport. Hotel staff was top notch and the place was clean while still having that old charm. I'd stay here again in a heart beat next time I visit Nashville.
Help me polish this: The only downside to this place was that not all the pools were open during Memorial Day weekend. However, the hotel offers a welcoming environment that caters to both adults and families. Additionally, there are plenty of dining options within the resort and the atrium is a captivating and enjoyable area to explore. Despite being slightly distant from town, it is conveniently situated between music row and the airport. The hotel staff is exceptional and the premises are well-maintained, with a charming vintage appeal. Without hesitation, I would choose to stay here again on my next visit to Nashville.

input:
Great treat to beat the heat! I stopped in during the Manayunk Arts Festival yesterday to get a cold refreshing treat and I was very pleased with the service and the quality of the fresh frozen yogurt and toppings.

It is a self service fro-yo establishment with countless options of flavors and toppings. I enjoyed the toasted coconut yogurt and topped it with rainbow sprinkles, fresh strawberries, blueberries and raspberries. The fruit was very refreshing but it was hard to select what to put on it because everything looked so yummy. If you are a chocolate lover there are plenty of candy toppings to add to your fro-yo too. 

If you are not sure what flavor you will enjoy best you can sample them with small paper cups that so you don't have to find out if you like the flavor or not after you already purchase! 

Another plus is that the establishment is kept very clean and it still looks as new as it did when it first opening on Main Street just a couple of years ago!
Help me polish this:
Cool down with a refreshing treat at the Manayunk Arts Festival! I stopped by yesterday and was delighted by the exceptional service and the high-quality fresh frozen yogurt and toppings available.

This self-service fro-yo establishment offers a wide array of flavors and toppings to choose from. I savored the delightful toasted coconut yogurt adorned with rainbow sprinkles, fresh strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries. The fruit added a refreshing burst to the treat, and I must admit, it was quite challenging to determine which toppings to select, as everything looked irresistibly delicious. For those with a penchant for chocolate, there are also numerous candy toppings to enhance your fro-yo experience.

A bonus feature of this establishment is the opportunity to sample different flavors before making your decision. They provide small paper cups for sampling, ensuring you don't have to regret your purchase later if a flavor doesn't suit your taste buds.

Additionally, the establishment is impeccably maintained and still appears as immaculate as it did when it first opened on Main Street a few years ago.

input: I think the trendiness of this chain, in general, has sort of faded and what you have left is the basis of this chain, which is over-priced food of a questionable quality. I wouldn't call it bad, but it's a whole lot of fried food and most of the breadings, whether it's fried pickles or okra or calamari or shrimp, are the same across all of that. The batter is fine, but it gets wearing. The coconut shrimp and hush puppies were definitely overcooked, which was kind of disappointing. Coke Zero on tap, but the mix could be better. For the price, it is also worth nothing there is a ton of food here, definitely quantity over quality. Décor is pretty cool and this is parked right along the Boise river, though it's a bit tucked away and has to be more or less sought out...probably worth hitting at least once, but there are far better local places that are more worthy of attention.
Help me polish this: In my opinion, the trendiness of this chain has noticeably declined, leaving behind the core concept of overpriced food that raises questions about its quality. It wouldn't be fair to label it as terrible, but the majority of their offerings consist of fried food with similar breading. While the batter is decent, it becomes monotonous after a while. Unfortunately, the coconut shrimp and hush puppies were both overcooked, which was quite underwhelming. They have Coke Zero on tap, but the drink could use some improvement in terms of taste. Moreover, considering the price, it's important to note that the quantity of food here outweighs its quality. On a positive note, the establishment boasts an appealing decor and is located alongside the beautiful Boise river, albeit slightly tucked away and requiring effort to find. It might be worth trying out at least once, but there are certainly superior local establishments deserving of more attention.

input:
There are bars you can still smoke in?! Yuck. Sorry smokers (I used to be one so I get it) but yuck. The stink of smoke in my hair woke me up in the middle of the night after stopping in here and was so bad I had to get up to wash it before I could get back to sleep. That's not good.

Definitely a dive, this bar is very dim and smokey. The bartender was friendly and came to take my order as soon as I walked up to the bar. The bloody mary I ordered wasn't that great or strong, though.  That's not good either.
Help me polish this:
Are there still bars where smoking is allowed? Ugh, that's disgusting. I apologize to any smokers (I used to be one myself, so I understand), but it's just unpleasant. The smell of smoke in my hair actually woke me up in the middle of the night after visiting this place, and it was so awful that I had to get up and wash it before I could go back to sleep. That's definitely not a good experience.

This bar is undeniably a dive. It's incredibly dim and filled with smoke. On the plus side, the bartender was friendly and promptly took my order as soon as I approached the bar. Unfortunately, the bloody mary I ordered was not up to par, lacking in taste and strength. That's another disappointment.

input: Got there mid-morning today, the early rush was over. Two tables were full, each with three people. The family in one of the tables had just walked in ahead of me, so they were being attended to first. Still, I was immediately welcomed, and in a couple of minutes a friendly lady brought the breakfast menu and asked if I wanted coffee. A cup appeared a few moments later, and was kept full throughout my visit. Radio playing golden oldies from the 70s, my kind of music. The ham omelet with home fries and toast arrive a few minutes later, worth waiting for. Done just right and kept me filled for hours. A friendly family restaurant where you feel welcome and appreciated, just north of Gulfport.
Help me polish this: I arrived at the restaurant mid-morning today, after the early rush had subsided. Two tables were occupied, each seating three people. Upon my arrival, I noticed that a family had just walked in before me, so naturally, they were being attended to first. However, I was warmly welcomed and within moments, a friendly lady brought me the breakfast menu and offered me coffee. Shortly after, a cup of coffee appeared before me, and throughout my visit, it was consistently refilled. The radio played nostalgic golden oldies from the 70s, which happened to be my preferred music genre. After a short wait, my ham omelet with home fries and toast arrived, and it was definitely worth the wait. The dish was perfectly cooked and kept me satisfied for the remainder of the morning. Overall, this restaurant exuded a friendly and welcoming atmosphere, making me feel appreciated as a customer. It is conveniently located just north of Gulfport.

input: This place is so lovely. It has everything!! Amazing wine selection, hookah's, Lebanese food which I think is the best in the city.
Help me polish this: This place is absolutely enchanting. It truly has everything one could ask for. From an incredible wine selection to a delightful array of hookah flavors, this place is a haven for those seeking to indulge. Moreover, the Lebanese food offered here is undoubtedly the finest in the entire city.

input: This was recommended by a colleague who is local in the area. A group of us from work decided to go and give it a try.  As soon as we sat down, Chris, took care of us.  He was patient, understanding and extremely knowledgeable of the menu.  Well, our entire party enjoyed every part of the evening while at Red Mess!  From the chips & salsa to the drinks to each of our entrees ... just absolutely DELICIOUS!
Help me polish this:
This restaurant came highly recommended by a colleague who is local to the area. A group of us from work decided to give it a try, and we were not disappointed. From the moment we sat down, our server Chris took excellent care of us. He was patient, understanding, and had an impressive knowledge of the menu.

Our entire party had an incredible evening at Red Mess. Every aspect of our meal, from the chips and salsa to the drinks and entrees, was absolutely delicious.

input: This is my 3rd time and 3rd location at a Brick House across the country. This is by far one of the few chain restaurants I will regularly and happily eat at. The food is very unique and every selection is a good choice. This particular location I received better than average service. Will come back when back in town.
Help me polish this: This is my third visit to a Brick House location across the country, and I must say it is one of the few chain restaurants I genuinely enjoy and frequently dine at. The food here is truly exceptional, with each menu item offering a delightful and distinctive experience. During my recent visit to this specific location, I was pleasantly surprised by the above-average level of service I received. I will definitely make it a point to return here whenever I find myself back in town.

input: So... This place is the sh*t. By far the classiest spot on the block, Siam is nudging STL standards up and up. The sashimi:  top grade. The outdoor patio: perfect to enjoy a beer/conversation off the dance floor. The music: something for everyone -- and the last couple nights I've been, the guest dj's we're KILLING some deep house grooves that rival NYC and Miami.  The best thing, though, may be the crowd: a solid mix that don't need labels, don't want pretense, just want a solid, quality night out.  F*ck yeah, Siam!
Help me polish this:
This place is absolutely fantastic. Hands down the classiest establishment in the area, Siam is taking the standards in STL to new heights. The sashimi here is truly top-notch, of the highest quality. Additionally, the outdoor patio provides the perfect setting to enjoy a beer and engage in a conversation away from the bustling dance floor. The music selection is diverse, catering to everyone's preferences, and lately, the guest DJs have been absolutely killing it with their deep house grooves that can rival those found in NYC and Miami.

However, the best aspect of Siam has got to be the crowd it attracts. It's a wonderful blend of individuals who refuse to conform to stereotypes and simply crave a genuine, high-quality night out. This place doesn't need labels or pretentiousness, it offers an all-around exceptional experience. Siam, you truly rock!

input:
Worn down signs intrigue me.  I had biked passed 16th Street Seafood a ton of times, always wondering what was going on inside.  Now I know the answer, and the answer is- not much. At least in terms of decor. There is a gumball machine, 2 empty candy machines, plus a counter to order at and that's pretty much it. Also absent was the plethora of seafood over ice you would hope to see at a place specializing in seafood. There were some frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs- but not else. Still, I threw caution to the winds of Tasker Street and put in an order.

I didn't want to go for fried seafood, so the sandwiches and platters were out.

I got a large order of mussels in butter and garlic sauce ($9.50). Mussels are one of those things I like making at home, but it is way too hot for that right now. . My main complaint is that the order came with an unacceptable amount of closed shells - 9!   It was still a good sized order with a big piece of bread to dip in the unexpectedly spicy, broth. As the place is to-go only- they know how to wrap up messy seafood orders, nothing was spilled.

Remember when I said I didn't want anything fried, well that's not ever actually true. So I ended up sneaking in 2 fried shrimps. Not bad, but not worth $1.25 each.
Help me polish this:
Worn down signs never fail to capture my curiosity. Every time I biked past 16th Street Seafood, I found myself yearning to uncover its hidden secrets. Finally, the opportunity arose, and I discovered that, unfortunately, there wasn't much to behold inside, at least not in terms of decor. The unassuming interior consisted of a gumball machine, two vacant candy dispensers, and a simple counter for placing orders. Disappointingly, the abundance of seafood displayed on ice, which one would expect from a specialized seafood joint, was conspicuously absent. Instead, the offerings consisted of frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs. Nevertheless, undeterred by the lackluster atmosphere, I decided to take a leap of faith and place an order.

With a desire to steer clear of fried seafood, I disregarded the enticing options of sandwiches and platters. Instead, I opted for a generous serving of mussels in a tantalizing butter and garlic sauce, priced at $9.50. Although I frequently prepare mussels in the comfort of my own home, the scorching weather discouraged such culinary endeavors. My only gripe with the order was the disappointing number of closed shells - a mere nine. However, the portion size was commendable, accompanied by a substantial piece of bread to dip into the unexpectedly fiery broth. As the establishment only offered take-out service, they had mastered the art of packaging messy seafood orders, ensuring nothing was spilled in transit.

Now, if you recall, I initially claimed that I did not crave anything fried. Yet, as fate would have it, I succumbed to temptation and surreptitiously added two fried shrimps to my order. They were passable, but regrettably not worth the steep price of $1.25 each.

input:
we had a groupon and so we went - great lobsters (although they were out of a few sizes this evening) but they were delicious and our waitress Jessica was very attending and nice - made some good suggestions.

not fancy but good lobster.
Help me polish this: We decided to take advantage of a Groupon deal and visit a restaurant that offered great lobsters.
