input: Great little upscale but not overpriced cafe. Lots of options, but needs a lox bagel sandwich. :) One of my preferred places to lunch with someone.
Help me polish this: Come and experience the charm of this hidden gem - a fantastic little upscale café that strikes the perfect balance between quality and affordability. With an extensive menu offering a wide array of options, there's something to satisfy every craving. However, no visit would be complete without trying their irresistible lox bagel sandwich. It's the go-to spot for me when I want to enjoy a delightful lunch with someone special.

input:
Animo juice is the best find in Haddonfield (after the Hadrosaurus, of course!)

I stop at Animo every time I go to Jersey to visit my family; or do I visit my family every time I stop at Animo?  Debatable.

Animo started with juice.  Not frozen juices with sorbet & yogurt added.  Real juice.  

Their menu has expanded & they now call themselves "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar!"  The burrito menu features 10 burritos, all under $10, f my favorite the "Haight & Ashbury" is stuffed with rice, beans, meat/roasted veggies, cheese, lettuce, tomato, guacamole & sour cream.

Not that hungry, have a 'petito', a small version of the burrito, averaging $5.  Porky & Petunia - the name is as cute as the petito is yummy:  shredded lettuce, pulled pork & pineapple salsa.  

A breakfast petito & Animo MD juice destroy any hangover.  The MD is juiced greens, carrot, orange, apple, kiwi, banana & spirolina.   My BF loves the Chilly Palmer:  Acai, apple, banana, yogurt & flax seed.  

For a happy belly add or substitute the perfectly cooked quinoa to any dish.  The Border Salad is a perfect example: lettuce, guac, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, cilantro lime vin, & sub quinoa for meat.   

Fiber-full signature juices, frozen whipped bananas, sliced fresh wheat grass (cheaper than Jameson!) & yogurt/granola bowls!  

The city's juice bars have something to learn from Animo.
Help me polish this:
Animo Juice is undoubtedly the ultimate discovery in Haddonfield, surpassed only by the iconic Hadrosaurus!

Whenever I pay a visit to Jersey to see my family, a stop at Animo is an absolute must. Or is it the other way around? It's up for debate.

Animo's roots lie in the world of juice. Genuine, authentic juice. None of those frozen concoctions with sorbet and yogurt thrown in. Just pure juice.

However, since their humble beginnings, their menu has flourished, leading them to rebrand themselves as "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar!" You'll find a selection of 10 delectable burritos, all priced under $10. My personal favorite is the "Haight & Ashbury," packed with rice, beans, your choice of meat or roasted veggies, cheese, lettuce, tomato, guacamole, and sour cream.

Feeling slightly less famished? Grab yourself a 'petito,' a smaller version of their signature burritos, averaging at $5. I highly recommend the "Porky & Petunia," not only for its adorable name but also for its mouthwatering combination of shredded lettuce, pulled pork, and pineapple salsa.

For those mornings when a hangover needs to be vanquished, an Animo MD juice paired with a breakfast petito works wonders. The MD juice is a blend of rejuvenating greens, carrots, oranges, apples, kiwis, bananas, and spirolina. Meanwhile, my significant other raves about the Chilly Palmer: a refreshing blend of acai, apples, bananas, yogurt, and flax seed.

To truly satisfy your taste buds, consider adding or substituting perfectly cooked quinoa to any dish. The Border Salad is a prime example, featuring a delightful mix of lettuce, guacamole, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, cilantro lime vinaigrette, and the option to trade in meat for quinoa.

As if that wasn't enough, Animo also offers fiber-rich signature juices, frozen whipped bananas, slices of fresh wheatgrass (far more affordable than a shot of Jameson!), and delectable yogurt and granola bowls.

In conclusion, the city's juice bars could learn a thing or two from the remarkable experience that Animo Juice provides.

input: Had a very memorable birthday in SB and was so happy to have Wine Edventures be my gift! Sean picked us up Saturday morning and was super friendly (funny, too). It was just my husband and I along with a group of 10 - who happened to be all guys, having a bachelor party! Haha, so that was pretty funny. We stopped at 3 wineries and 1 brewery. Sean explained where we were as we were driving around and also gave us lessons at the tastings. He provided us with bottled water and souvenir wine glasses. We had lunch at the 2nd vineyard of the day, which was very good - choice of sandwich and a pasta salad side with chips and a cookie (the cookies are awesome). It was a fun day and I'd highly recommend this adventure to anyone looking for a fun day in the SB area.
Help me polish this:
I had an absolutely unforgettable birthday experience in Santa Barbara, and I couldn't have been happier with Wine Edventures as my gift! Sean, our guide, picked us up on Saturday morning and immediately made us feel at ease with his friendliness and sense of humor. It was just my husband and I, along with a group of 10 guys who were having a bachelor party - it made for quite the amusing mix!

Throughout the day, Sean expertly navigated us to three incredible wineries and one brewery. As we drove from place to place, he provided interesting insights about the area and its winemaking history. At each tasting, he took the time to teach us about the wines we were sampling, making the experience even more enjoyable.

We were provided with bottled water to stay hydrated and got to take home souvenir wine glasses as mementos of our adventure. Additionally, Sean arranged for our lunch to be served at the second vineyard of the day, and it was absolutely delicious. We had the choice of a mouthwatering sandwich and a delightful pasta salad as a side, accompanied by chips and an irresistible cookie. Believe me, those cookies were out of this world!

Overall, it was an incredibly fun-filled day, and I can't recommend this Wine Edventures experience enough to anyone seeking a fantastic time in the Santa Barbara area.

input:
This is my favorite in Delaware.  The menu is simple and perfectly executed.  Rolls are reasonably priced, artfully made and are PACKED with fish!  I do believe they use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, but the color, texture, taste and smell are perfect.  Easily the best spicy tuna I have ever had.  I think the secret is the kewpie mayo along w/ the right amount of sriracha and sichimi powder.  Frankly, I can't get enough of this place and have at times, eaten it every day for lunch for weeks.  I've gone as far as to pick it up for dinner AFTER having had it for lunch. Their introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been great!

The Sushiman, YC Park is amazing to watch.  I've seen him skin a cucumber with a sword-like sushi knife in no time flat, in a single ribbon and then continue to shave it into a nori thin sheet for his tuna naruto roll roll.  The temaki are as big as a carnival iced cream cone.  You can barely finish one of them, there is so much fish in there.  The nigiri are beautiful.  Uniform pieces of fresh fish, perfectly perched on the best sushi rice I've ever had (just the right amount of vinegar and sugar).

Skip the newly opened Kooma.  Save Mikimotos for a night out, but go to Tokyo for lunch!  The owners are lovely, so support them in this tough economy.  If you must eat sushi, eat it here!

Why not 5 stars?  I have to save it for places that serve the local fresh fish, plucked out of the water that morning.  Let me know if you find a place that does!
Help me polish this:
Here's a polished version of the text:

"This place in Delaware is hands down my favorite. The menu is simple yet flawlessly executed. The rolls are reasonably priced, beautifully crafted, and generously packed with fish. Although they may use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, the color, texture, taste, and aroma are beyond perfect. Their spicy tuna roll is, without a doubt, the best I've ever had. I believe the secret lies in the combination of kewpie mayo, just the right amount of sriracha, and sichimi powder. Frankly, I'm obsessed with this place and have even had it for lunch every day for weeks. I've gone as far as picking it up for dinner after having it for lunch. Their introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been a fantastic addition as well!

Watching the Sushiman, YC Park, is a true delight. I've witnessed him effortlessly skinning a cucumber with a sword-like sushi knife, creating a single ribbon, and then skillfully transforming it into a thin nori sheet for his tuna naruto roll. The temaki rolls are massive, equivalent to a carnival ice cream cone. It's almost impossible to finish one due to the abundance of fish stuffed inside. The nigiri pieces are a sight to behold. Every carefully prepared slice of fresh fish sits perfectly atop the most exquisite sushi rice I've ever tasted, with just the right balance of vinegar and sugar.

I recommend skipping the newly opened Kooma and saving Mikimotos for a special night out. However, when it comes to lunchtime sushi, Tokyo is the place to be! The owners are delightful, and it's crucial to support them in this challenging economy. If you have a craving for sushi, this is the place to satisfy it!

Why not 5 stars? Well, that honor is reserved for places that serve locally sourced, freshly caught fish straight from the water that morning. Let me know if you come across a place like that!"

input: So I'm super confused as to why everyone rags on this place. They're super nice, quick, and cheap.  People have complained about their chicken fingers being dry but I have no clue what they're talking about. They're great and their honey mustard is delicious. I've had salads from there too and they give you lots of veggies which I love. Their fries are delish as well and I love that they give you cole slaw with the chicken finger platter. All and all, I love that this place is literally a few steps away from my apartment and that they have decent food. I also don't understand the greasy spoon comments... you do realize it's a pizza joint right? You aren't going there for the ambiance, more for the cheap food.
Help me polish this: I am confused as to why there are so many negative comments about this place. In my experience, the staff has been incredibly friendly and efficient, and the prices are reasonable. Some people have complained about their chicken fingers being dry, but personally, I find them to be delicious. Their honey mustard sauce is also fantastic. Additionally, I have tried their salads and they are packed with fresh vegetables, which I really appreciate. The fries are also tasty, and I love that they include cole slaw with the chicken finger platter. Overall, I am delighted to have this place just a few steps away from my apartment. It offers decent food at affordable prices. Moreover, I don't understand the criticisms about it being a greasy spoon. It is a pizza joint after all; the emphasis is not on the ambiance but on providing inexpensive food.

input: Great cheesesteak! Friendly and fast service. Lazo's really made my day.

input: Ambience OK, too bad stuck in a mall in New Hope.  They were very understaffed (which thankfully they kept apologizing for) so there service was definitely slow, however very very pleasant.  We definitely felt it was worth the wait!  Vegetable Samosas were delicious, chicken were slightly dry.  I ordered chicken tikka masala which was so flavorful and rich and my husband had the chicken tagine...amazing!  Has the feeling of a place where "you get what you get and you don't get upset" but when you get it, it is really out of this world!  Loved the mix of cuisines, just enough choices on the menu.  Restaurant is BYOB so we were unprepared, but we will be back!
Help me polish this: The ambience was alright, albeit unfortunate to be stuck in a mall in New Hope. The restaurant was clearly understaffed, leading to slow service. However, the staff made up for it with their pleasant demeanor and consistent apologies. Despite the wait, we found the experience to be worthwhile. The Vegetable Samosas were delicious, but the chicken dishes were slightly dry. My order of chicken tikka masala was exceptionally flavorful and rich, while my husband's choice of the chicken tagine left us amazed. There was a sense of acceptance that "you get what you get and you don't get upset," but when the food finally arrived, it was truly extraordinary. We adored the blend of cuisines and the menu offered just enough choices. It's worth noting that the restaurant operates on a BYOB policy, catching us off guard, but we will definitely return prepared next time!

input: This is the cutest mom/pop local, high-quality ice cream joint in all of Tucson! Delicious... But definitely a bit pricey ($4.50 for a regular single scoop)- hence the 4 stars as opposed to 5.

input: I definitely won't be coming back here. Long story short, I scheduled an appointment online to have the transmission and differential fluid changed on my pilot. I arrived on time, and I was told it would take approximately 2 hours for completion, I also said I wanted an oil change, but " full synthetic". He said it would be $20 more, I said okay. When it was finally done and I was ready to check out, my advisor (Brandon) give me the total cost, which was double than what I expected and paid for in the past. I asked him what was all done, he said, "they completed a transmission flush instead of the regular drain and refill". I told him that's not what I wanted or asked for. He went on to say "it was good for the car and whatever", like I'm some kind of idiot. First of all Honda doesn't recommend doing a transmission flush and secondly, its almost triple what you would normally pay for a standard transmission fluid change. On top of that they didn't even do a full synthetic oil change it was just a blend. I didn't have time to argue with him because I was already late for an appointment, but I have the email showing what I originally asked for, so I'll be calling my bank soon.
Help me polish this:

input: We love, love M.L. Rose! I am a huge beer fan and the flights are so fun to choose and try. I love the neighborhood hangout feel, not too hipster, not too old....just right! We always have awesome service too. My hang up can be the food. Wings not quite crispy enough, burgers not cooked to taste, spinach artichoke dip just meh. The steak and Gouda was flat out gross - big fatty slab of undercooked steak on bread. We were told it is leaving the menu, but they should have removed it long ago. And no visit from the manager when the sandwich was returned, which was a little underwhelming. We will be back, we are big fans, but please get your kitchen together so I can have my fav burger in town cooked just right :-)
Help me polish this:
We absolutely adore M.L. Rose! As a passionate beer enthusiast, I can't get enough of their fantastic flight options. It's always a blast deciding which ones to try. What sets M.L. Rose apart is its cozy neighborhood ambiance – not overly hipster, not too old-fashioned – just the perfect balance. Additionally, the service has consistently impressed us, always going above and beyond.

However, I must admit that the food sometimes falls short. While the wings are delicious, they could use a bit more crispiness to reach perfection. Similarly, the burgers don't always live up to my taste, sometimes not cooked to my desired level. The spinach artichoke dip has left me feeling underwhelmed at times; it's just not as flavorful as I'd hoped. I must say, though, the steak and Gouda dish was exceptionally disappointing. It consisted of an undercooked, fatty steak placed on bread, and I was taken aback by the unappetizing presentation. Although it's supposedly being removed from the menu – a decision that should've been made much earlier – the lack of attention from the manager when the dish was returned was rather underwhelming.

Despite these food-related setbacks, my enthusiasm for M.L. Rose remains unwavering. We will definitely return because we truly are loyal fans. However, I do hope that the kitchen can address these issues, especially with preparing my favorite burger in town to perfection.

input:
We went on a non typical day, school year mid week, so we had the luxury of being only a handful of people there  Therefore, my review may not be representative of a typical visit. 
Arrived at opening and found the off season price within reason. Bathrooms and water park were immaculate. The lifeguards were attentive and friendly. 
A star was lost because I found the water and air temp to be a tad too cold. The park was smaller then other indoor water parks I've been to. Only two big slides, one group slide, a couple of younger kids areas, lazy river and a simulated surf area. They would periodically close the big slides in order to open the surf area, for lack of staffing. A minor annoyance since that is why we were there. 
I can see how people  would be upset paying more and sharing the park with hundreds of others. But I think if your timing is right, you could have an enjoyable afternoon.
We did save money by using our AAA card. Could have saved more as it was my sons birthday month, but I didn't have proof on me.
Help me polish this:
We had the opportunity to visit the water park on a non-typical day, during the school year mid-week, so it's important to note that my review may not fully reflect a typical visit. Nonetheless, our experience was quite enjoyable.

Upon arrival at the opening, we were pleased to find that the off-season price was reasonable. The cleanliness of the bathrooms and water park area was impressive, and the lifeguards were attentive and friendly.

I deducted one star from my rating due to the slightly cold water and air temperature. Additionally, the park was smaller compared to other indoor water parks I've visited. It featured only two big slides, one group slide, a couple of areas for younger kids, a lazy river, and a simulated surf area. Occasionally, the management would close the big slides to allocate staffing to the surf area, which was a minor inconvenience since surfing was one of the main reasons we chose to visit.

I can understand how some people might be disappointed if they paid more and had to share the park with hundreds of others. However, with good timing, one can have an enjoyable afternoon without the crowds.

On a positive note, we were able to save some money by using our AAA card. Although we could have saved even more as it was my son's birthday month, unfortunately, I did not have the necessary proof with me at the time.

Overall, despite a few minor drawbacks, our visit to the water park was pleasant, and I believe others can have a similar experience if they plan accordingly.

input:
I normally wouldn't think Greek food for brunch or lunch; I'm way more of a traditional American-style brunch kind of guy.  But when my friends suggested to meet them here for brunch this past weekend, I trusted their better judgement.  In the end, I'm glad I did.  This cozy Center City spot not only serves an amazing (and dare I say, a contender for the best) brunch in Philly, the staff really make you feel at home.  They really know how to wow their patrons: fresh food, delightful presentation, and so many delicious sounding choices it's hard to choose which dish you want from their one page menu for mains.

Their specialty, and they're not shy to tell you, is the Cyprus Breakfast.  It's a mediterranean twist on the classic combination of eggs, meat, and starch.  The plate comes out with two sunny-side up eggs, fried in olive oil and garnished with fresh parsely.  It's served alongside a grilled slice of lounza (Greek ham), two pieces of salty, crisp fried halloumi, warm bread, and tomato, cucumber, and onion salad.  The menu also features a spread of other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern specialities: Avgolemono, Moussaka, Pastitsio, Shaksouka, and Malohwa to name a few.  They even serve Greek Coffee and Frappes!

The service may be a little over-attentive in an attempt to make you feel more than welcome, but it's much appreciated, especially when other restaurants fail to put as much effort into the service as they do the food.  One other tip: reservations are highly recommended, if not required.  Because of Kanella's small space, getting a table at brunch is nearly impossible if you're not on the list.  But if you can score seats here for brunch, then expect nothing less than a stellar way to start your weekend morning (or recover from last night's activities).  Can't wait to come back and try out the dinner menu.
Help me polish this:
I wouldn't normally consider Greek food for brunch or lunch as I'm usually more of a traditional American-style brunch kind of guy. However, when my friends suggested meeting here for brunch this past weekend, I trusted their judgement and I'm so glad I did. Their specialty, and they're quite open about it, is the Cyprus Breakfast, a Mediterranean twist on the classic combination of eggs, meat, and starch. The plate arrives with two perfectly cooked sunny-side up eggs, fried in olive oil and garnished with fresh parsley. It's accompanied by a grilled slice of lounza (Greek ham), two pieces of salty, crispy fried halloumi, warm bread, and a refreshing tomato, cucumber, and onion salad. Moreover, the menu also features a range of other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern specialties such as Avgolemono, Moussaka, Pastitsio, Shaksouka, and Malohwa. They even serve Greek Coffee and Frappes!

The service can be a bit over-attentive, as the staff goes above and beyond to ensure you feel more than welcome. However, I find this level of attentiveness to be highly appreciated, especially when compared to other restaurants that might not prioritize service as much as the quality of the food. One important tip: it is highly recommended, if not required, to make reservations. Nevertheless, if you manage to get seats here for brunch, you can expect nothing less than an exceptional way to start your weekend morning (or recover from last night's activities). input: This place gets two stars from me only because the gravy fries were good. Their sandwiches are awful. Thick slabs of badly sliced, tough, dry meat....gross. The positive reviews you may come across are likely from locals who haven't had the opportunity to try superior options. The last time I was at the salon, Christopher, Leah and I had a blast reminiscing about '80s fashion!  I can't remember a time when I enjoyed going to the hair salon (which is probably because I never have!).

input:
Nice, old school space with a long bar. It reminded me of some places I've been out west, which might be a little strange in the heart of Philadelphia. 

Not too loud at all - conversations were easy and a lot of the patrons were doing just that. There's a jukebox, so maybe it cranks up later in the evening. We were there pretty early. 

Great service from several people working behind the bar. 

Several beers on tap including a local CCCCC IPA, which was solid. Not many wines, though.

Small menu but very good food. The elote (corn) is quite good, as was the cucumber(?) salad. But the brat plate was the star. Wonderful brat, German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel and a hot salsa/relish. Best brat plate ever. Served on a cool wood board.

Prohibition is located in or near a somewhat dicey neighborhood, at least to this non-resident's eye. I may very well be wrong about that. We had to walk a trashy, pissy street past what seemed like skid row coming from the hotel on Race St. If it was later at night we might have chosen not to walk back.
Help me polish this:
The space at Prohibition is reminiscent of old school establishments with a long bar, giving off a charming and nostalgic vibe. It's a bit unusual to find such a place in the heart of Philadelphia, but it adds to its unique appeal.

Despite its potential for being noisy, the atmosphere was surprisingly calm and conducive to easy conversations. Many of the patrons were engaged in relaxed chitchat, making for a pleasant ambiance. Although there's a jukebox, which could potentially crank up the volume later in the evening, we visited early enough to enjoy a peaceful experience.

The bar staff provided excellent service, with multiple individuals attending to our needs promptly and attentively.

Their range of beers on tap includes a delicious local CCCCC IPA, which I found to be quite satisfying. However, I should note that their wine selection is somewhat limited.

While the menu may not be extensive, the quality of the food is exceptional. The elote (corn) and the cucumber salad stood out as particularly delicious options. However, the true highlight was the brat plate, consisting of a delectable bratwurst, German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel, and a hot salsa/relish. Served on a stylish wooden board, this brat plate is easily the best I've ever had.

It's important to mention that Prohibition is located in or near a neighborhood that may appear questionable, especially for those unfamiliar with the area. From our experience, walking along Race St. towards the hotel, we encountered some unsightly and unpleasant surroundings that resembled a skid row. Given the circumstances, we might reconsider walking back to the hotel late at night.

input:
We  heard that Fresh Market was open and since we just got back from vaca we thought we would try it.  First of all, accolades to the staff they could not have been more helpful.  Especially Thomas in the meat section.  For these two things I would give them a five.  However, it does downhill from this point on:  ordered one pound of swiss cheese, after standing there waiting for about 5 minutes, and no one else was on line, the unfriendly clerk waited on us. The imported swiss cheese that we ordered was so poorly cut that in two days we had one clump of swiss cheese, rather than many slices.  I bought ricotta cheese for Easter and went to open it, and it was bad, although it was dated 3/28.  The tomatoes on the vine that I bought on Friday were bad by Sunday.  I have found their prices very high, selection, poor and at this point it is just not worth it. I also bought two pound cakes and their were not up to par.  Very dry and tasteless.. Overall a very disappointing shopping trip 
There is plenty of convenient parking and the store was immaculate, but it is not for me.  The final straw was that I asked for extra cash for Easter gifts, the clerk at the register said there was a $150 limit, the ATM terminal said $100 and the "manager" said $50...I thought they should get their act together.  Best to stay with Weaver's Way... or Whole Foods or Wegmann's.
Help me polish this:
We had heard that Fresh Market was open and decided to give it a try, as we had just returned from vacation. First and foremost, the staff deserves accolades as they were extremely helpful, especially Thomas in the meat section. For their excellent service, I would give them a five-star rating. However, our experience went downhill from there.

We ordered one pound of Swiss cheese, and after waiting for about 5 minutes (with no one else in line), an unfriendly clerk finally served us. Unfortunately, the imported Swiss cheese we received was poorly cut, resulting in one clump instead of individual slices. Additionally, we purchased ricotta cheese for Easter, but it turned out to be bad despite having a 3/28 expiration date. The tomatoes on the vine that we bought on Friday also went bad by Sunday. 

Furthermore, we found their prices to be very high and the selection poor. Overall, the quality did not justify the cost. We also bought two pound cakes, which were disappointingly dry and tasteless. It was an overall disappointing shopping trip.

On a positive note, there was ample convenient parking available, and the store itself was impeccably clean. However, based on our experience, Fresh Market is not a store that I would personally recommend. The final straw was when we asked for extra cash for Easter gifts, only to receive conflicting information from the clerk at the register, the ATM terminal, and the so-called "manager". This lack of consistency made it clear that the store needs to improve its communication and organization. It is best to stick with Weaver's Way, Whole Foods, or Wegmann's for a more satisfactory shopping experience.

input:
I heard this ice cream parlour opened last summer, so upon my first trip home (sometime during the fall) I hustled over to try it. Since Friendly's closed a few years ago, Warminster has sorely needed a new ice cream place (DQ was our last one standing for quite some time). 

Much to my dismay, the Big Scoop had already closed for the season. I marked it in my calendar go return in March, when it reopened. Upon my next trip home in the spring, I was disappointed to see that I was just a few days early for their reopening, and would have to wait until my return in April.

After much anticipation, I made it to Big Scoop last weekend with my sister (who has been before). I was shocked to see what a range of products they serve - hot dogs, funnel cake, onion rings, pizza, you name it! I was tempted at the prospect of waffles and ice cream, but I wasn't that hungry so I settled for a scoop of chocolate chip cookie with hot fudge and whipped cream. The generous scoop of ice cream was tasty and packed with globs of cookie dough! I also tasted the birthday cake, which I enjoyed very much. 

The service was quick, and the shop crowded quickly. The interior was nicely remodeled and looks clean and family friendly. The man who helped me was extremely courteous and seemed to be doing most of the work. 

Especially given the lack of competition around here, the Big Scoop gets an easy four stars!

This is another one of those anytime coffee shops. You can come get some work done, people watch, or just grab a drink to go. Either way, its open early and late.

For the quarter, its "off the beaten path" but in the busy area the locals hang out, and on the way to Fenchmen where everyone goes for good local music, Jazz, et al. 

They have food, not the cheapest, or local, but its better for you than the greasy, salty, fatty foods. Just make sure your service number is visible I got distracted hid my number, and had to stop the guy looking.  

Service varies. Since its a busy sidewalk, people stop in for that pick me up before work or party. One minute there is a like 12 long, and the barista is running ragged, the next its dead. 

Sometimes I'll sit for over an hour working or catching up on email. I'll order something every so often, and its no big deal for me to queue myself if they get busy. After all it helps those stopping in for a quick drink.

p.s. I love there tall cookies

oh and how many coffee shops can you get a shot in your coffee! That's right, its not a bar, but its New Orleans.

Although the food offered here isn't the most affordable or locally sourced, it is a healthier alternative to the usual greasy, salty, and fatty options. Just ensure your service number is visible as I once got distracted and had to search for the staff member who was looking for me.

By the way, their tall cookies are absolutely delightful!

And let's not forget about the unique feature of this coffee shop – where else can you find a shot in your coffee? Although it's not a bar, this establishment embodies the spirit of New Orleans.

All I wanted was to pay for my food and take it home. 

To make matters worse, during my most recent visit tonight, I handed them two twenty-dollar bills for a bill amounting to $27. When I arrived home, I discovered that not only was the food incorrect, but my warm dish was served cold and the sushi was not what I had ordered. This disappointing experience has led me to the decision that I will no longer be patronizing this establishment.

input: Their pizza is pretty good, service is usually cool inside. But today I ordered a delivery for the first time, the driver was very insulting to me. When I open my door she asked me about a car across the street with a guy in the driver's seat. I replied "I don't know," she said "cus I don't wanna be set up to get robbed". Mind you I already paid with my visa when I ordered, her behavior made me feel awkward as if I had done something wrong. I gave her the tip I had in my hand and said thank you, hoping that maybe if I remain polite she'll stop thinking so negative I just wanted some pizza not to be judged because of my surroundings or to be stereotyped.
Help me polish this: Their pizza is consistently delicious, and the service inside the restaurant has always been pleasant. However, my first experience with their delivery service left a bitter taste in my mouth. Upon opening my door to the driver, she immediately asked about a car parked across the street with a man in the driver's seat. Confused, I honestly replied, "I don't know." Without missing a beat, she retorted, "I don't wanna be set up to get robbed." I was taken aback by her comment, considering I had already paid for my order with my Visa when I placed it. Her behavior left me feeling uncomfortable and as if I had done something wrong. Despite this, I handed her the tip I had prepared and politely thanked her, hoping that my kindness would dissuade her from such negative assumptions. All I wanted was some pizza, not to be judged based on my surroundings or to be subjected to stereotypes.

input:
First time here and I have to say it's pretty good! The bake shop fits well with the fishtown environment and it's very clean and welcoming inside. The display of beautiful cakes let's you know you have top quality bakers there. 

I got a few items to share such as a Burbon Pecan cookie, chocolate chip cookie, vanilla cupcake with buttercream icing, and a vanilla cupcake with raspberry icing. 

I had a taste of the Burbon Pecan Cookie. It was not too sweet and you get nice bites of pecan; a nice hot coffee is a perfect compliment.The cupcakes were good (cake wise) but, not a huge fan of the icings. The cake itself was sweet and moist. 

Didn't get to try the Chocolate chip cookie but the concensus was that it's delicious. 

I would definitely come back and I have taken a big interest in having Cake Life make a custom order!
Help me polish this:
First time here and I must say, it's truly delightful! The bake shop seamlessly blends with the vibrant fishtown environment and exudes a refreshing cleanliness and warmth inside. The exquisite display of cakes serves as a testament to the exceptional talent of the bakers.

During my visit, I indulged in a few treats, including a delectable Burbon Pecan cookie, an enticing chocolate chip cookie, and two varieties of vanilla cupcakes adorned with buttercream and raspberry icing respectively.

The Burbon Pecan Cookie was a delightful blend of flavors, with the perfect balance of sweetness and the delightful crunch of pecans. It paired magnificently with a steaming hot coffee. The cupcakes, while impeccably moist and sweet, left me slightly less impressed with the icings. 

Although I regrettably did not sample the Chocolate chip cookie myself, the unanimous agreement among others was that it offered sheer deliciousness.

Without a doubt, I will be returning for more delightful experiences and have developed a profound interest in placing a custom order at Cake Life!

input:
Went here last Thursday and arrived early enough to take advantage of their $5 domestic pitchers during hh which includes mich golden light, my fave! It did take the server about 10-15 minutes to even notice we were there, but after that service was just fine. 

Started off with the wings which were delicious, although the bf was certain it was not actually a pound of wings which they claim on their menu.

I ordered the gyro and fries which were surprisingly really good! Gyro meat was tasty and the fries were awesome! Bf had the French onion soup and potato skins which he said were good as well.

We stayed for rock n roll bingo (which I guess is every Thursday, and free!) and we had a blast. They also have a pool table and darts in the back which we played while waiting for bingo to start.

We will definitely be back!
Help me polish this:
I went to this place last Thursday and arrived early enough to take advantage of their happy hour deal with $5 domestic pitchers, which includes my favorite, Michelob Golden Light! The only downside was that it took the server about 10-15 minutes to notice us, but after that, the service was just fine. 

To start, we ordered the wings, which were absolutely delicious. However, my boyfriend was skeptical about it being a full pound of wings as stated on the menu. 

For my main course, I decided to try the gyro and fries, and I was pleasantly surprised by how good they were! The gyro meat was flavorful and the fries were fantastic. My boyfriend had the French onion soup and potato skins, and he said they were also quite tasty.

We stayed for rock n roll bingo, which apparently happens every Thursday and is free! We had a blast playing pool and darts in the back while waiting for bingo to start.

Overall, we had a great experience and will definitely be returning!

input: Johnny Tucci and his crew are the absolute best videographers, hands down. They are professional, prompt, and extremely talented. They made our wedding footage look like a movie production and brought everyone to tears that watched it. My advice is that if you are going to splurge in one area for your special day, spend it on a videographer. They do not disappoint.
Help me polish this: Johnny Tucci and his crew truly stand out as the absolute best videographers, without a doubt. Their level of professionalism, punctuality, and exceptional talent is unmatched. Our wedding footage was transformed into a breathtaking movie production that moved everyone who watched it, bringing tears to their eyes. If you're considering splurging on one aspect of your special day, my strong recommendation is to invest in a videographer. Trust me, Johnny Tucci and his team will not disappoint.

input:
One of the absolute best places to see a game in the entire country!

Get there early or if it's a blowout, stroll around the park. There are tons of interesting places to eat & drink (including a rooftop bar). Tickets are still amazingly reasonable even after all the success the Phils have had in recent years particularly when compared to the NY parks.

I used to go more often before the team became so prominent (right after the park opened), and I sat all over the joint. Not really anywhere I wouldn't recommend. The outfied is a great option. 

After starting with a 17 game pack many years ago & then buying season tix a few years back (which my company still has), the staff was great about recommending sections that would avoid direct sunlight , etc. (3rd base field level is awesome).

If you are visiting or considering a trip, don't buy the negative publicity about the Philly fans. The crowds are great. Sure, you have idiots and maniacs like you do at any park and for any professional sporting event, but they are by far the minority and Citizens Bank Park is policed pretty well for nonsense. 

I was once with a group of guys & we stood out in one of the open standing areas between 3rd base & the left field wall the whole night. At one point a very nice officer politely asked us not to curse because there were families around. We we were far from out of control, and we all thought that was pretty cool... so we had fun with some occasional lighthearted banter with the officer for the rest of the night.

Don't expect to be sheltered with your kids like you would be in your own living room, but there's no teens running onto the field getting tazed every night nor are there drunk idiots throwing up on people. 

It's a great atmosphere, a wonderful park & still a very fun team to watch.
Help me polish this:
One of the absolute best places in the entire country to see a game is at Citizens Bank Park! Whether you arrive early or if it's a blowout, you can take a leisurely stroll around the park and explore all it has to offer. With numerous interesting places to eat and drink, including a rooftop bar, there is something for everyone.

Despite the Philadelphia Phillies' recent success, ticket prices remain surprisingly reasonable compared to the parks in New York. I used to attend games more frequently when the team wasn't as prominent, right after the park opened, and I sat in various sections. Honestly, there isn't a bad seat in the house. However, watching the game from the outfield is a fantastic option.

Having started with a 17 game pack many years ago and eventually purchasing season tickets through my company, I've had the pleasure of receiving great recommendations from the staff. They were always mindful of finding sections that provided shade and ensured a comfortable viewing experience. Personally, I highly recommend the third base field level for an awesome vantage point.

If you're planning a trip to Citizens Bank Park or considering visiting, don't let the negative publicity about Philly fans deter you. The crowd atmosphere is fantastic. While every park has a few rowdy individuals, they are definitely the minority here. Citizens Bank Park is well-policed to prevent any nonsense.

I recall an incident when my friends and I were standing in one of the open areas between third base and the left field wall for an entire game. A friendly police officer politely asked us to refrain from using profanity due to families being present. We were far from out of control and found the officer's request rather cool. From then on, we engaged in lighthearted banter with the officer for the remainder of the night, having a great time.

While you shouldn't expect the same level of sheltering for your kids as you would have in your own living room, you can rest assured that there are no rowdy teens running onto the field or drunken idiots causing a scene. Citizens Bank Park offers a fantastic atmosphere, a beautiful park, and a reliably enjoyable team to watch.

input: I love Cosi but this Cosi is going down hill fast. I always get a signature salad and lately they are made wrong and no dressing at all. How hard is it to make their own signature salad!? It's practically what they are known for!!! So angry.
Help me polish this: I used to adore Cosi, but sadly, it seems to be deteriorating rapidly. Every time I order my beloved signature salad lately, it's been prepared incorrectly or without any dressing at all. I mean, come on, making their own signature salad should be a piece of cake for them! It's practically their specialty! I can't help but feel frustrated and disappointed.

input: OMG!! what a disappointment today was, I have been so excited to see Rembrandt's reopen after a few months of remodel, what I was thinking is that the new owners would want to do more restorations of this Beautiful, Cozy, old Church, maybe try to find more space to add Tables, but NO, I walked into a Modern, Cold, Hospital Coffee Shop, the Charm is gone, so so disappointed and sad, we all love the Charm of Eagle, but it seems to be fading fast, Please People talk to all the other Eagle Shop Owners when your visiting them especially the old Original Buildings to keep Eagle's charm and quaintness and restore these Beautiful Buildings.
Help me polish this: Oh my goodness! Today was such a huge disappointment. I had been eagerly anticipating the reopening of Rembrandt's after its remodel for months. I had high hopes that the new owners would prioritize restoring the beautiful, cozy, old Church and maybe even find ways to add more tables. But boy, was I wrong! When I walked in, I was greeted by a cold, modern coffee shop that resembled a hospital rather than the charming place it once was. I cannot express how disappointed and sad I am. Eagle used to be filled with so much charm, but it feels like it's fading away rapidly. I implore everyone, when you visit other shops in Eagle, especially those housed in the original, historic buildings, please talk to the owners and encourage them to preserve Eagle's charm and quaintness. Let's all come together and restore these beautiful buildings to their former glory.

input:
The service was lacking. The waiters and waitresses don't know the menu and when you ask for certain things to be brought to your table, it's constantly forgotten. The food is visually appealing but some of the most awkward and distasteful food I've ever had. The waffles are stale, the biscuits are hard as rock and their chorizo is not real chorizo.

The only thing this place has going for it is the atmosphere and their alcohol selection.
Help me polish this:
The overall service was quite disappointing. The waitstaff appeared to be unaware of the menu, and multiple requests made to bring specific items to our table were consistently forgotten. Although the food had a visually appealing presentation, its taste and quality left much to be desired. The waffles were noticeably stale, the biscuits were as hard as rocks, and the supposed chorizo did not meet the expectations of genuine chorizo.

However, it is worth noting that the atmosphere of the place is pleasant, and they do boast an impressive selection of alcoholic beverages.

input:
This restaurant is a nice place to go and sit down to have something to eat. I've ate just about everything they have on the menu and I'd say their burgers are great. Although their pizza is a bit on the tough side I still manage to eat the crust too. 

Very comfortable dining room area as well!
Help me polish this:
This restaurant offers a pleasant atmosphere where you can enjoy a relaxing meal. I have tried nearly every item on their menu and personally, I highly recommend their delicious burgers. However, I must say that their pizza tends to be a little bit tougher than expected, although I still find it enjoyable, including the crust.

Additionally, the dining room area is exceptionally comfortable, enhancing the overall dining experience.

input: We live in the neighborhood and have eaten here many times. I feel as if this restaurant is going downhill. This time we were there for dinner early on a Sunday. The bathrooms were filthy. There are 2 and one was not usable due to all of the paper towels that had been put into the toilet (there was no toilet paper). The other one was usable but also no toilet paper. Our server, Ashley, was not interested in providing any semblance of customer service...RUDE! We had a simple question about the beers on special and she became quite defensive. My daughter spilled her drink, which I realize is a pain in the ass for the restaurant and server (although we were outside so it wasn't that big a deal). We apologized profusely but she didn't even try to hide her annoyance. Finally, the chicken quesadilla should have been labeled the gristle quesadilla....more fat than actual meat...yuck. We love the proximity of this place to where we live and it was great in the past but not anymore...will likely not return...not with so many better quality restaurants in Northern Liberties and Fishtown.
Help me polish this:
We are residents of this neighborhood and have dined at this establishment numerous times. However, it saddens me to say that we have noticed a decline in the overall quality of this restaurant. During our recent visit, which took place on a Sunday evening, we were disappointed to find the bathrooms in an unsanitary condition. One of the restrooms was rendered unusable due to an excessive amount of paper towels stuffed into the toilet, and the other restroom also lacked toilet paper.

Furthermore, our server, Ashley, left much to be desired in terms of customer service. When we inquired about the beers on special, she responded defensively and seemed disinterested in providing assistance. To add to our disappointment, my daughter accidentally spilled her drink. While we understand that this can be an inconvenience for both the restaurant and the server, Ashley made no effort to conceal her annoyance, despite our sincere apologies.

Lastly, the chicken quesadilla we ordered was a major letdown. It was more gristle than actual meat, leaving an unpleasant taste in our mouths. While we appreciate the convenience of this restaurant's location, it is evident that the quality we previously enjoyed has diminished. Considering the abundance of higher-quality dining options in Northern Liberties and Fishtown, it is unlikely that we will return to this establishment.

input: Pretty average bar/restaurant with the menu offerings you can expect from a place like this. The food was OK, and the service was excellent.
Help me polish this: Welcome to a charming bar/restaurant that embodies an average yet comfortable dining experience, offering exactly what you would anticipate from such a place. While the menu boasts familiar offerings, don't expect any groundbreaking culinary creations. The food here is perfectly satisfactory, yet may not leave a lasting impression on your taste buds. However, where this establishment truly shines is in its exceptional service. The attentive and friendly staff go above and beyond, ensuring that your visit is made truly memorable.

input: We came here based on the recommendation we received and from the street it doesn't look like much. But when you sit down and you scan the menu you will come to realize that this place serves nothing but home-cooked comfort food. We had the BLT and it was packed full of flavor, they didn't scrimp on the bacon and the vegetables for very fresh. With the sandwiches came some of the best french fries that we've had, and some of the best coleslaw that I've had in the state of Florida. We took a couple of pies home and they were delicious. We will definitely come back.
Help me polish this: We came here based on a recommendation and, from the outside, the place didn't look like much. However, once we sat down and took a look at the menu, we quickly realized that this restaurant specializes in nothing but comforting, homemade food. We decided to try their BLT, and it was bursting with flavor. The generous amount of bacon and fresh vegetables made it an absolute delight. Accompanying the sandwiches were the most incredible French fries we've ever had and a coleslaw that easily ranks among the best in the state of Florida. We couldn't resist taking a couple of pies home, and they were absolutely delicious. Needless to say, we will definitely be returning in the future.

input: I was greated by a nice friendly staff. There wasnt a long wait for my food. I ordered a chicken bacon croissant with chipolte sauce. They cut it in half as requested and was served in maybe only 20 seconds after the time it took to cook. Food taste great
Help me polish this: I was warmly greeted by a friendly staff, who made my dining experience enjoyable. The wait time for my food was impressively short and I was promptly served. I ordered a delicious chicken bacon croissant with chipotle sauce, which was prepared exactly as I had requested - cut in half. In no more than 20 seconds after cooking, my meal was served. The taste of the food was excellent, adding to my overall satisfaction with the experience.

input: Excellent food! I am a Thai food junkie, and have travelled to Thailand and throughout Southeast Asia several times. There is ok Thai food in Nashville and then there is Great Thai food. This place was GREAT! The decor is a little dated but who cares...I was there for the food, which is fabulous!!!
Help me polish this: Outstanding Cuisine! Being a Thai food enthusiast, I have extensively explored Thailand and other Southeast Asian countries. While Nashville boasts decent Thai food options, this particular establishment stands out as truly exceptional. Though the decor may be slightly outdated, it pales in comparison to the exquisite flavors that await you. The food here is simply divine!

input: This place is absolutely fantastic. I honesty really don't even like sweets and am not all that into donuts but this place will make you a believer. The apple fritter is amazingly delicious and you can't go wrong with a chocolate long john. Don't even bother with any other donut shops in stl.
Help me polish this: This place is truly outstanding. Honestly, I'm not usually a fan of sweets or particularly fond of donuts, but this place has completely changed my opinion. Their apple fritter is an absolute delight, unbelievably delicious. And you can't go wrong with their chocolate long john either – it's a definite winner. Trust me, there's no need to waste your time on other donut shops in STL.

input: Of all the restaurants we tried in New Orleans, this was by far our favorite. I had both lunch and dinner on two separate occasions. The service was wonderful, the ambiance is cozy but alive. Make sure to call ahead and get a reservation over the phone if opentable looks booked. Their lunch special spicy fried chicken is a must have! If you are a party of two or three, ask for the corner booth by the window. Best table in the house.
Help me polish this:
Out of all the restaurants we tried in New Orleans, this particular one stood out as our absolute favorite. We had the pleasure of dining here for both lunch and dinner on separate occasions, and we were consistently impressed. The service provided by the staff was exceptional, ensuring that our dining experience was nothing short of wonderful. Upon entering, we immediately felt a cozy yet vibrant ambiance that added to the overall charm of the place.

If you plan on visiting, it is advisable to call ahead and secure a reservation over the phone, especially if opentable shows no availability. This popular spot tends to fill up quickly. Trust me, it's worth it. Oh, and don't miss out on their lunch special – the spicy fried chicken is an absolute must-try! Trust me, your taste buds will thank you.

For those dining in smaller groups of two or three, I highly recommend requesting the corner booth by the window. This coveted spot offers the best view and gives you the feeling of being in the most sought-after seat in the entire restaurant.

Overall, this restaurant exceeded our expectations in every way. From the exceptional service to the delectable food and delightful ambiance, it truly stands out among the rest. Without a doubt, choosing this place will leave you with a memorable and delicious dining experience.

input:
City Parkの近くにある激安かき氷屋さん。シェーブドアイスっていったほうがいいね！
特に夏のニューオーリンズはジメジメして暑いから、公園に行った後にここでかき氷とか最高だと思う！

味の種類は半端なく多いです！50以上はあったはず！
そしてなんといっても安い！ぼくは一番安いチョイスのレギュラーかき氷のスモールを頼みましたが、スモールでも結構十分だと思います。そして値段はたったの$1.50. 安い！！

トッピングをしても５ドル以上はいかないはず。
夏のうだる暑さには、最高のチョイスだと思います！
Help me polish this:
Here is the polished version:

There's a super affordable shaved ice shop near City Park. It's better to call it shaved ice instead of snow cones! Especially in the humid and hot New Orleans summers, I think it's the best to have shaved ice here after visiting the park!

They have an incredible variety of flavors! There must have been over 50 options! And the best part is, it's really cheap! I opted for the smallest size, the regular small shaved ice, and it was still plenty. And the price? Just $1.50. It's so affordable!!

Even with toppings, it shouldn't cost more than $5. I believe it's the perfect choice for the scorching summer heat!

input: Mr. X has amazing flavor and overall a pretty friendly staff. The wait time for carry out is on average about 20 minutes, which is way better than a 45 minute wait at chain pizzerias. I get the hand-tossed crust comparable to traditional NY style pizza, and has excellent flavor and texture!
Help me polish this: Mr. X offers an exceptional culinary experience with its incredible flavor and exceptionally friendly staff. Unlike chain pizzerias with an average wait time of 45 minutes for carry out, Mr. X ensures your order is ready in just about 20 minutes. Their hand-tossed crust, reminiscent of the traditional NY style pizza, delivers a delightful combination of flavors, texture, and quality.

input:
First time being here.  It was a nice place but empty.  Had one old man sitting in there, then us two 40 somethings, then another old man.  That was it.   We came during happy hour, basically waiting for Snake and Jakes to open up so we came here to kill some time.  

Beer selection was nice, Magic Hat, Fat Tire, Blue Moon, etc.  Prices were ok too.

Lotsa dark woods and a few TVs and a lonely but attractive bartender that was very nice.  

Nothing bad to say about this place other than it was kinda dead.  It was very clean looking and nicely decorated, just kinda boring.
Help me polish this:
First time being here, and I must say, it was a pleasant place despite being relatively empty. Upon arrival, we noticed only one elderly gentleman seated at the bar, the two of us in our forties, and another older man. It was happy hour, and we were simply killing time until Snake and Jakes opened up, so we decided to spend some time here.

The beer selection caught our attention with its enticing options, including Magic Hat, Fat Tire, Blue Moon, and more. Additionally, the prices were reasonable.

The interior featured an abundance of dark woods, a few TVs, and a lone yet attractive bartender who provided exceptional service.

Overall, I can't complain about this place except for the lack of liveliness. It boasted a clean and tasteful decor, but unfortunately, it lacked excitement.

input:
i dont know what has happened to the in store service in this place!  We have been down here for a few weeks now and have been here 6 times.Only once was the order completed without a screw up!

Today 2 tall decaf coffees took close to 20 minutes.By then our bagels were cold.First i was told the decaf was "brewing' and then i was told there was something 'wrong" with the brewer? After 15 minutes i was offered a decaf americano.
Before we left i politely told a fellow behind the counter the service was abominable and he said 'well we can only store 2 vente size decafs at a time? HUH? I asked if the management knew about this and he just shrugged.
Clearly this staff has never been trained to make it right for the customer.No apology.No coupon.Just a convoluted story.
 
Amazing how you can have numerous people running around a store but you cant get the simplest order straight My next visit to a Starbucks will certainly not be this one.
Help me polish this:
I am highly dissatisfied with the in-store service at this place. We have been here for a few weeks now and have visited six times, but only once did we receive our order without any mistakes.

Today, it took nearly 20 minutes to receive two tall decaf coffees. By the time they arrived, our bagels were already cold. Initially, I was informed that the decaf was "brewing," but later I was told that there was something wrong with the brewer. After 15 minutes of waiting, I was offered a decaf americano instead.

Before leaving, I politely voiced my concerns to a staff member behind the counter. However, the response I received was shocking. I was told that they could only store two vente size decafs at a time. This left me puzzled. I inquired if the management was aware of this issue, but the staff member simply shrugged.

It is apparent that this staff has never been properly trained in providing satisfactory service to customers. No apology was offered, and no coupon was given to make up for the poor experience. It is astonishing how a store can have so many staff members, and yet, fail to fulfill even the simplest order. I can confidently say that I will not be visiting this particular Starbucks again.

input:
As a double date with a good long lost friend for a relaxing evening dinner, we were surprised in early august to not get reservations until 8. 
So we arrived an hour early and had drinks in the lobby while the piano man played beautifully. The bartender was a bit slow at first but kept us well tended. 
Our table in the corner against the glass was ready early and we enjoyed watching the rays chase fish around the bay as the sun set.  
I started with the tasty crab and corn chowder but was a bit disappointed with al dente potatoes in the bowl. 
Wife ordered the scallops which were superb as was my crab stuffed grouper. But my rice was also inadequately cooked. 
Creve brûlée was excellent as was Tim's attentive service. 
Worth going again, but they need to get all the parts of the dishes correct to get 5 stars.
Help me polish this:
As we embarked on a double date with a dear long-lost friend, seeking a relaxing evening dinner, we were taken aback in early August when we discovered that reservations were unavailable until 8 o'clock. Despite this setback, we decided to make the most of our time and arrived an hour early, taking solace in the soothing ambiance of the lobby while the talented piano man entranced us with his music. Although the bartender initially seemed a bit sluggish, he eventually warmed up to us and provided us with excellent service throughout the night.

Fortunately, our table in the corner, adjacent to the glass windows, was prepared ahead of schedule, allowing us to relish in the breathtaking sight of the sun bidding the day farewell as the rays danced around the bay, playfully chasing fish beneath the shimmering surface.

For starters, I opted for the delectable crab and corn chowder, which offered a burst of flavors, although I couldn't help but feel slightly disappointed with the al dente potatoes that accompanied it. On the other hand, my wife's scallops were nothing short of extraordinary, while my choice of the crab stuffed grouper left me thoroughly satisfied. However, I couldn't overlook the fact that the rice served alongside the dish was undercooked, slightly diminishing the overall experience.

Concluding our meal on a sweet note, the creve brûlée proved to be a highlight, surpassing expectations with its impeccable taste and delightful texture. Additionally, Tim, our attentive server, contributed to our enjoyable dining experience.

While this establishment certainly warrants a return visit, achieving a perfect five-star rating will necessitate the meticulous attention to detail required to ensure that every component of the dishes is executed flawlessly.

input: My wife and I visited this hidden gem today and were not let down. The shop was clean, bright, colorful, and comfortable. We were able to sample all the flavors, listen to the story of how they came about, and walked off with many bags of deliciousness. The owners there were so kind. They took the time to understand exactly what kind of foods we enjoy to match us up with the perfect popcorn. Definitely coming back soon!
Help me polish this:
My wife and I discovered an absolute hidden gem today, and it certainly did not disappoint. From the moment we stepped into this quaint shop, we were captivated by its cleanliness, vibrant ambiance, and cozy atmosphere. The array of colors and tasteful decor instantly uplifted our spirits.

One of the highlights of our visit was the opportunity to sample every single flavor they offered. Listening to the captivating story behind each creation made the experience even more delightful. We ended up leaving with numerous bags of sheer deliciousness, eagerly awaiting the moment we could indulge in their irresistible popcorn again.

The owners of this establishment deserve special appreciation for their kindness and hospitality. Not only did they warmly welcome us, but they also dedicated their time to truly understand our preferred flavor profiles. As a result, they skillfully matched us with the perfect popcorn choices that perfectly aligned with our tastes.

Needless to say, we are already looking forward to returning to this remarkable place very soon. Its unique charm, coupled with the genuine care provided by the owners, creates an experience that is simply unparalleled.

input: A really cute new coffee shop in town. We stopped here in the morning to get a much needed caffeine break. Who's warm day so we opted to get an iced coffee. We had many options on the type of milk and sweetener is available. They had limited food items available being mostly donuts this morning. We opted for a piece of the vegan banana bread to share. Iced coffee came out quickly and are banana bread and we went outside to sit with and realize there is no area connected to this restaurant for outdoor seating. The restaurant next-door however was not yet open so we sat at one of their tables thinking no one would mind. It would be nice if the coffee house itself had its own outdoor seating. Are iced coffee was very good and hit the spot. The vegan banana bread was good but seemed very dense to me. I'll be back another time to try some more of the fancy coffee they have available here. I'm hoping that they will add to the food menu as well as a try to not eat donuts most days. Maybe a breakfast sandwich or some other option than a pastry would be good.
Help me polish this:
A charming new coffee shop just opened up in town, and we couldn't resist stopping by for a much-needed caffeine break this morning. Since it was a warm day, we decided to indulge in some refreshing iced coffee. To our delight, there were plenty of options for milk and sweeteners. However, the food selection was quite limited, consisting mostly of donuts. Regardless, we decided to share a piece of their vegan banana bread, which was tasty but a tad dense.

Once our iced coffees were prepared promptly, we ventured outside to find that the coffee shop lacked its own outdoor seating area. Since the neighboring restaurant was still closed, we took a seat at one of their tables, assuming no one would mind. Nevertheless, it would be great if the coffee house had its own designated outdoor seating for customers' convenience.

All in all, our iced coffees hit the spot, and we thoroughly enjoyed them. Next time, I plan on returning to explore their extensive selection of fancy coffees. Perhaps they could consider expanding their food menu as well, offering alternatives to donuts like breakfast sandwiches or other delectable options.

input:

input: I have been here numerous times for brunch, dinner and take out during lunch time hours. Staff is always friendly and the food is delicious.

input: Do not waste your time and money on this place. The "food" is what you might expect from a small town Chi-Chi's.

input:
Cozy and family friendly restaurant. I came here for a private engagement party, where the bride and groom to be had arranged for special menus and baked all of their desserts. There were a few booth tables reserved for presents, wine, and desserts. No room for side tables like in an actual special events space.

The wait staff was nice. From the limited menu, I picked the Penne Fellini, which has prosciutto di parma, peas, onions, and light cream sauce. The whole dish was literally this pasta swimming in sauce. It may have had a light cream flavor, but it was ladled heavily onto the pasta. I didn't have a desire to consume an entire meal of this, so I ended up not finishing.

It was a fun celebration, and we were really there for the friends and family, not the food. Oh, and we also had the bruschetta and salad, neither of which was very memorable. I wouldn't be thrilled to come back here, but I think it's awesome that they turned the whole restaurant into a venue for such a special occasion!

Polished Version:

The wait staff was attentive and friendly throughout the event. I opted for the Penne Fellini from the limited menu, which consisted of prosciutto di Parma, peas, onions, and a light cream sauce. While the food didn't make a lasting impression, the celebration itself was a joyful experience shared with friends and family. It should be noted that the bruschetta and salad we had were also unremarkable. Although I don't feel particularly inclined to visit this restaurant again, I cannot overlook the fact that the establishment transformed itself into a special venue for such a significant occasion—an admirable feat in itself!

input:
This place is the epitome of a great hole in the wall find.  From  the  70s vintage floral upholstery  to the back entrance off the alley, it undersells it self and sets you up for a great surprise.  The food is good -- not fancy, not at all pretentious - but good. 

A group from work made the trek on the coldest day of the year and we were rewarded for our efforts -- the chicken hot pot was the best example this dish I have ever had.  The seafood dish with shrimp, scallops and squid was very generous for the price of about $10. The beef in black bean sauce was nice and spicy.  

I will certainly return, but only with adventurous companions.
Help me polish this:
This place is the epitome of a hidden gem. With its vintage floral upholstery from the 70s and a back entrance off the alley, it's unassuming and surprises you in the best possible way. The food is not fancy or pretentious, but it's undeniably good.

A group of us from work decided to brave the coldest day of the year and our efforts paid off. The chicken hot pot we ordered was the epitome of this dish - it was the best I've ever had. The seafood dish, packed with shrimp, scallops, and squid, was incredibly generous for its affordable price of about $10. The beef in black bean sauce had just the right amount of spice.

I'm definitely coming back to this place, but I'll make sure to bring along adventurous companions who appreciate hidden gems like this one.

input:

input:
FOOD REVIEW

If you're looking for quality meal that is quick and affordable, the Fountain has you covered. The menu isn't extensive, but it's got a good amount of inexpensive sandwiches, salads, and soups.  

Their Cuban Sandwich ($10 w/ side) was pretty excellent.  The bread wasn't the traditional panini-style, but a French baguette...it was still great and had a little crispness to it.  All the main ingredients (meat, mustard, pickles, cheese) were in good balance.  As a Florida boy who loves his Cuban sandwiches, I would definitely recommend this.

I also tried a bit of their Royal Grille, a grilled-chese sandwich with several cheeses, as well as apple slices, on whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 w/ side, extra to add ham/turkey).  It was damn good and hit the grilled cheese craving just right.  A side salad was also done well.

For my side, I chose their "spicy carrots" which sounded unique.  It consists of sliced raw carrots that have been marinated in a tangy dressing with crushed red pepper, served in a cup. The carrots were cold and crisp and the flavors were fantastic.  The spice was just enough to be pleasant.  I would definitely get these again.

Our food came out super quick and our service was great.  I'm looking forward to trying a couple more items and bumping this up to 5 stars.
Help me polish this:
Food Review: The Fountain

If you're in need of a quick and affordable meal without compromising on quality, look no further than The Fountain. Although their menu isn't extensive, they offer a range of delicious and inexpensive sandwiches, salads, and soups.

One standout item I tried was their Cuban Sandwich ($10 with a side). While the bread was not the typical panini-style bread, opting for a French baguette instead, it still delivered a delightful crispness. The combination of meat, mustard, pickles, and cheese was well-balanced, making this a definite recommendation especially for fellow Cuban sandwich enthusiasts.

I also had the pleasure of sampling their Royal Grille, a grilled cheese sandwich made with a variety of cheeses, apple slices, all neatly placed between whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 with a side, and extra to add ham/turkey). It satisfactorily satisfied my grilled cheese craving, delivering a delightful blend of flavors. The side salad accompanying it was equally well-prepared.

For my chosen side dish, I opted for their "spicy carrots," a unique option that intrigued me. Served in a cup, these sliced raw carrots had been marinated in a tangy dressing with crushed red pepper. The carrots were refreshingly cold and crisp, with fantastic flavors that perfectly balanced the pleasant spice level. I would certainly order these again.

Not only was our food served promptly, but the service we received was outstanding. I'm excited to return and try a few more items, as this experience has certainly left me eager to award The Fountain a well-deserved 5 stars.

input:
Burger Up is, by far, one of our favorite restaurants in the Nashville area.  It has a cool hipster vibe, without being annoying :)  The burgers are outstanding, and there are endless options, whether you prefer beef, chicken, seafood, or veggie!  I would recommend the Woodstock - the Jack Daniels Maple Ketchup is out of this world, and Benton's bacon is always delicious.  Upgrade to the truffle fries; they're to die for.  Or, if you're a vegetarian, the troyathalon is a great option.  Filling, with great texture and flavor.  As far as drinks go, 12 South Lemonade.

The customer service is also great.  They've always been attentive, but not "on top of you", and they're very knowledgable about their food.  Parking can be a bit difficult at certain times of the day, but it's worth a short walk if necessary.

I would definitely recommend checking it out!
Help me polish this:
I highly recommend Burger Up as one of the best restaurants in the Nashville area. With its cool and hipster vibe, it manages to create a trendy atmosphere without being overwhelming. The burgers they offer are truly exceptional, and the variety of options is endless, catering to all preferences, whether you crave beef, chicken, seafood, or a veggie option. Personally, I can't get enough of the Woodstock burger, featuring the heavenly Jack Daniels Maple Ketchup and the always delicious Benton's bacon. Pro tip: don't miss out on upgrading to their truffle fries - they're absolutely irresistible. Even if you're a vegetarian, the troyathalon burger is an amazing choice, packed with filling ingredients and bursting with fantastic textures and flavors. To wash it all down, I highly recommend trying their 12 South Lemonade.

Not only is the food outstanding, but the customer service is also top-notch. The staff is attentive without being overbearing, and their knowledge about the menu is impressive. Keep in mind that parking can be a bit challenging at times, especially during peak hours, but rest assured, even if it means a short walk, it's well worth it.

Don't miss the chance to experience Burger Up - I promise it won't disappoint!

input:

I knew I couldn't eat the full-course meal so we decided to get cheese fondue and one of their entrees. Cheese fondue was delicious. If I go next time, I would probably just get the cheese fondue. =]

And the entree we had.. was some chicken, meat, shrimp, mushrooms, etc. We decided to go with oil instead of broth because that's what our waitress suggested and I didn't really like it. I think I will try the broth next time if I do and see if I like it any better. Except the mushroom with stuffing, others were ok.

We had this private booth which was very romantic and nice. I think this place would be good for people who want privacy and have plenty of time for dinner. We stayed there for 2&1/2 hours excluding the waiting time.

input:
Great Mexican BYOB! I went to Las Cazuelas for the first time for my birthday.  We had a wonderful time.  I was looking for a fun and festive place to go with friends.  This was the perfect choice. We brought our own bottle of tequila, and they made tasty margaritas for the table.  Those were a big hit with my friends, and a cool twist for a Mexican BYOB.  The restaurant is cute.  Plus, the food here is delicious. 

I'm surprised this place doesn't have higher reviews on Yelp, because it far exceeded my expectations... 

The guacamole appetizer was fresh and yummy.  I ordered the shrimp entree with rice and vegetables, and asked for it spicy.  My entrée had an attractive presentation on the plate (i.e. looked classy), and was delicious, well seasoned, and very fresh. On my suggestion, my partner ordered one of their mole sauce dishes (i.e. a sauce usually made from unsweetened chocolate and pureed pumpkin seeds), and it was tasty too. 

I should also note that the waitress was very attentive.  When I placed my order, I explained to her that I have mild lactose intolerance and can't eat much butter or cream (but am okay with cheese), so she had the chef cook the veggies in olive oil, rather than butter.  Thanks for being so cool about accommodating that request!  

The prices are extremely reasonable for fancy and unusual Mexican food, and I love the fact they're a BYOB.  The chef serves creative and inspired cuisine, which has a traditional flair and style to it.  In other words: Don't come here for regular tacos or burritos.  Come here for a fun foodie experience at a reasonable price, and bring tequila for the perk of BYOB Margaritas!
Help me polish this:
Las Cazuelas is a fantastic spot for a memorable Mexican BYOB experience. I celebrated my birthday there recently and it exceeded all expectations. The ambiance of the restaurant is delightful, providing a fun and festive atmosphere that was perfect for celebrating with friends. 

One unique aspect of Las Cazuelas is their BYOB policy. We brought our own bottle of tequila and to our delight, they crafted some truly delicious margaritas for the table. This was a hit among my friends and added an exciting twist to our dining experience. 

The food at Las Cazuelas is simply divine. Despite being surprised by the restaurant's relatively low Yelp reviews, the cuisine far exceeded my expectations. The guacamole appetizer was made with fresh, flavorful ingredients and was absolutely delightful. 

For my main course, I opted for the shrimp entree with rice and vegetables, requesting it to be prepared spicy. The presentation of the dish was elegant and the flavors were impressively well-balanced. The shrimp was cooked to perfection, the dish expertly seasoned, and the ingredients incredibly fresh. At my suggestion, my partner tried one of their mole sauce dishes, which was a tasty revelation.

Additionally, the attentive service provided by the waitress was notable. She was accommodating of my dietary needs, taking the time to understand my mild lactose intolerance. As a result, the chef prepared the vegetables using olive oil instead of butter. This level of consideration and care demonstrated their commitment to customer satisfaction.

Notably, Las Cazuelas offers extremely reasonable prices for their exceptional Mexican cuisine. Here, you won't find your ordinary tacos or burritos. Rather, the chef serves up creative, inspired Mexican dishes with a traditional flair. It's a must-visit for foodies seeking a unique and enjoyable dining experience that won't break the bank. And of course, don't forget to bring your own tequila for the added perk of BYOB margaritas!
